lines.text: एवं दत्तात्रेयमुखाद्‌ जगत्तत्त्वं निशम्य तु ।
पप्रच्छ भार्गवो भूयः संदेहकलिलान्तरः ॥ १ ॥
evaṁ dattātreyamukhād jagattattvaṁ niśamya tu ।
papraccha bhārgavo bhūyaḥ sandehakalilāntaraḥ ॥ 1 ॥

evam — thus, dattātreya-mukhāt — from the mouth of Dattatreya, jagat-tattvam — the nature of the world, niśamya — having heard, tu — indeed, papraccha — asked, bhārgavaḥ — Bhargava, bhūyaḥ — again, sandeha-kalila-antaraḥ — with a heart full of doubts.
Thus, having heard the nature of the world from Dattatreya, Bhargava asked again with a heart full of doubts.
भगवन्‌ संश्रुतं प्रोक्तं भवता जागतं ननु ।
यथा ब्रवीषि भगवंस्तत्तथैव न चाऽन्यथा ॥ २ ॥
bhagavan saṁśrutaṁ proktaṁ bhavatā jāgataṁ nanu ।
yathā bravīṣi bhagavan tat tathaiva na ca anyathā ॥ 2 ॥

bhagavan — O Lord, saṁśrutam — well heard, proktam — said, bhavatā — by you, jāgatam — about the world, nanu — indeed, yathā — as, bravīṣi — you say, bhagavan — O Lord, tat — that, tathaiva — just so, na — not, ca — and, anyathā — otherwise.
O Lord, what you have said about the world is well heard. Indeed, as you say, it is just so and not otherwise.
तथापि कुत एतद्धि भाति सत्यात्मकं सदा ।
कुतो वाऽन्यैर्बुद्धिमद्भिः सत्यत्वेन विनिश्चितम्‌ ॥ ३ ॥
tathāpi kuta etad dhi bhāti satyātmakaṁ sadā ।
kuto vā anyaiḥ buddhimadbhiḥ satyatvena viniścitam ॥ 3 ॥

tathā api — even so, kutaḥ — from where, etat — this, hi — indeed, bhāti — shines, satyātmakam — as truth, sadā — always, kutaḥ — from where, vā — or, anyaiḥ — by others, buddhimadbhiḥ — by the wise, satyatvena — as truth, viniścitam — determined.
Even so, from where does this world always shine as truth? Or from where is it determined as truth by other wise ones?
त्वत्तः श्रुतं चापि भूयो भाति मे सत्यवत्‌ कुतः ।
ब्रूह्येतत्‌ कृपया नाथ यथा नश्येदयं भ्रमः ॥ ४ ॥
tvattaḥ śrutaṁ ca api bhūyo bhāti me satyavat kutaḥ ।
brūhi etat kṛpayā nātha yathā naśyed ayaṁ bhramaḥ ॥ 4 ॥

tvattaḥ — from you, śrutam — heard, ca api — and also, bhūyaḥ — again, bhāti — appears, me — to me, satyavat — as truth, kutaḥ — from where, brūhi — tell, etat — this, kṛpayā — with kindness, nātha — O Lord, yathā — so that, naśyet — may be destroyed, ayaṁ — this, bhramaḥ — delusion.
From you I have heard and it still appears to me as truth again. Tell this with kindness, O Lord, so that this delusion may be destroyed.
इत्यापृष्टो भार्गवेण दत्तात्रेयो महाशयः ।
जगत्सत्यभ्रान्तिमूलं प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमे ॥ ५ ॥
ity āpṛṣṭo bhārgaveṇa dattātreyo mahāśayaḥ ।
jagatsatya-bhrānti-mūlaṁ pravaktum upacakrame ॥ 5 ॥

iti — thus, āpṛṣṭaḥ — asked, bhārgaveṇa — by Bhargava, dattātreyaḥ — Dattatreya, mahāśayaḥ — the great sage, jagat-satya-bhrānti-mūlam — the root of the delusion of the world's reality, pravaktum — to speak, upacakrame — began.
Thus asked by Bhargava, the great sage Dattatreya began to speak about the root of the delusion of the world's reality.
शृणु राम जगद्‌भ्रान्तेर्मूलमेतत्‌ सनातनम्‌ ।
वस्त्वविद्यापूर्वकं यद्‌ दृढभावनमेव तत्‌ ॥ ६ ॥
śṛṇu rāma jagadbhrānter mūlam etat sanātanam ।
vastu-avidyā-pūrvakaṁ yad dṛḍha-bhāvanam eva tat ॥ 6 ॥

śṛṇu — listen, rāma — O Rama, jagat-bhrānteḥ — of the world's delusion, mūlam — the root, etat — this, sanātanam — eternal, vastu — thing, avidyā-pūrvakam — based on ignorance, yat — which, dṛḍha-bhāvanam — firm belief, eva — indeed, tat — that.
Listen, O Rama, the root of the world's delusion is this eternal thing, based on ignorance and firm belief.
पश्यात्मानमविज्ञाय स्वात्मबुद्धिं शरीरके ।
क्व मांसरुधिरास्थीनि क्व चिदात्मातिनिर्मलः ॥ ७ ॥
paśya ātmānam avijñāya sva-ātma-buddhiṁ śarīrake ।
kva māṁsa-rudhira-asthīni kva cit ātmā ati-nirmalaḥ ॥ 7 ॥

paśya — see, ātmānam — the self, avijñāya — not knowing, sva-ātma-buddhim — self-awareness, śarīrake — in the body, kva — where, māṁsa — flesh, rudhira — blood, asthīni — bones, kva — where, cit — consciousness, ātmā — self, ati-nirmalaḥ — very pure.
See, not knowing the self and having self-awareness in the body, where is the flesh, blood, and bones, and where is the very pure self?
केवलं भावनादाढर्याच्चिदात्मा देहकोऽभवत्‌ ।
ज्ञातेऽप्यात्मनि चिद्रूपे भूयो भ्रान्तिः शरीरके ॥ ८ ॥
kevalaṁ bhāvanā-dāḍharyāt cit-ātmā dehakaḥ abhavat ।
jñāte api ātmani cit-rūpe bhūyaḥ bhrāntiḥ śarīrake ॥ 8 ॥

kevalam — only, bhāvanā-dāḍharyāt — due to firm belief, cit-ātmā — consciousness-self, dehakaḥ — as body, abhavat — became, jñāte — even after knowing, api — also, ātmani — in the self, cit-rūpe — as consciousness, bhūyaḥ — again, bhrāntiḥ — delusion, śarīrake — in the body.
Only due to firm belief, the consciousness-self became the body. Even after knowing the self as consciousness, the delusion of the body arises again.
एवमेव भावनया सत्यं भाति जगत्‌ खलु ।
विपरीतं भावयन्‌ वै दृढभ्रान्तिं निवर्तयेत्‌ ॥ ९ ॥
evam eva bhāvanayā satyaṁ bhāti jagat khalu ।
viparītaṁ bhāvayan vai dṛḍha-bhrāntiṁ nivartayet ॥ 9 ॥

evam — thus, eva — indeed, bhāvanayā — by belief, satyam — as truth, bhāti — appears, jagat — world, khalu — indeed, viparītam — opposite, bhāvayan — thinking, vai — indeed, dṛḍha-bhrāntim — firm delusion, nivartayet — removes.
Thus, by belief, the world appears as truth. By thinking the opposite, one can remove the firm delusion.
यो यथा भावयेदेतज्जगत्तस्य तथा भवेत्‌ ।
योगिनां धारणाध्यानैः पश्य तद्रूपसङ्गतिम्‌ ॥ १० ॥
yo yathā bhāvayet etat jagat tasya tathā bhavet ।
yogināṁ dhāraṇā-dhyānaiḥ paśya tad-rūpa-saṅgatim ॥ 10 ॥

yaḥ — who, yathā — as, bhāvayet — believes, etat — this, jagat — world, tasya — for him, tathā — so, bhavet — it becomes, yoginām — of yogis, dhāraṇā-dhyānaiḥ — by concentration and meditation, paśya — see, tad-rūpa-saṅgatim — union with that form.
Whoever believes in this world in such a way, for him, it becomes so. See the union with that form through the concentration and meditation of yogis.
अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि पुरावृत्तं महाद्भुतम्‌ ।
अस्ति वङ्गे सुन्दराख्यं पुरं परमपावनम्‌ ॥ ११ ॥
atra te vartayiṣyāmi purāvṛttaṁ mahādbhutam ।
asti vaṅge sundarākhyam puraṁ parama-pāvanam ॥ 11 ॥

atra — here, te — to you, vartayiṣyāmi — I will tell, purāvṛttam — ancient story, mahādbhutam — very wonderful, asti — there is, vaṅge — in Bengal, sundara-ākhyam — named Sundara, puraṁ — city, parama-pāvanam — very sacred.
Here I will tell you a very wonderful ancient story. There is a very sacred city named Sundara in Bengal.
तत्रासीन्नृपतिर्धीमान्‌ सुषेण इति विश्रुतः ।
तस्य भ्राता महासेनो यवीयान्‌ प्रियकृत्‌ सदा ॥ १२ ॥
tatrāsīn nṛpatir dhīmān suṣeṇa iti viśrutaḥ ।
tasya bhrātā mahāseno yavīyān priyakṛt sadā ॥ 12 ॥

tatra — there, āsīt — was, nṛpatiḥ — king, dhīmān — wise, suṣeṇaḥ — named Sushena, iti — thus, viśrutaḥ — known, tasya — his, bhrātā — brother, mahāsenaḥ — named Mahasena, yavīyān — younger, priyakṛt — always kind, sadā — always.
There was a wise king named Sushena, known thus. His younger brother, named Mahasena, was always kind and loving.
शशास राज्यं नृपतिर्धर्मतः सर्वसम्मतः ।
कदाचिदश्वमेधैः सोऽयजद्‌ देवं महेश्वरम्‌ ॥ १३ ॥
śaśāsa rājyaṁ nṛpatiḥ dharmataḥ sarva-sammataḥ ।
kadācit aśvamedhaiḥ saḥ ayajad devaṁ maheśvaram ॥ 13 ॥

śaśāsa — ruled, rājyam — kingdom, nṛpatiḥ — king, dharmataḥ — righteously, sarva-sammataḥ — accepted by all, kadācit — once, aśvamedhaiḥ — with horse sacrifices, saḥ — he, ayajat — worshipped, devam — god, maheśvaram — Maheshvara.
The king ruled the kingdom righteously and was accepted by all. Once, he worshipped the god Maheshvara with horse sacrifices.
तत्र राजकुमारास्तु महाबलपराक्रमाः ।
महत्या सेनया यज्ञाऽश्वं सर्वे ह्यनुसंययुः ॥ १४ ॥
tatra rājaputrās tu mahābala-parākramāḥ ।
mahatyā senayā yajña-aśvaṁ sarve hy anusaṁyayuḥ ॥ 14 ॥

tatra — there, rājaputrāḥ — princes, tu — indeed, mahābala-parākramāḥ — with great strength and valor, mahatyā — great, senayā — army, yajña-aśvam — sacrificial horse, sarve — all, hi — indeed, anusaṁyayuḥ — followed.
There, the princes, with great strength and valor, followed the sacrificial horse with a great army.
अश्वस्य रोधकान्‌ सर्वान्‌ विजित्य बलिनो बलात्‌ ।
ययुरैरावतीतीरमन्वश्वं नृपतेः सुताः ॥ १५ ॥
aśvasya rodhakān sarvān vijitya balino balāt ।
yayur airāvatī-tīram anvaśvaṁ nṛpateḥ sutāḥ ॥ 15 ॥

aśvasya — of the horse, rodhakān — obstructors, sarvān — all, vijitya — having conquered, balinaḥ — strong, balāt — by force, yayuḥ — went, airāvatī-tīram — to the bank of the Iravati, anv-aśvam — following the horse, nṛpateḥ — of the king, sutāḥ — sons.
Having conquered all the obstructors of the horse by force, the strong sons of the king went to the bank of the Iravati, following the horse.
ददृशुस्तत्र राजर्षि तङ्गणाख्यं तपोनिधिम्‌ ।
बलोद्धता अवज्ञाय तमसङ्गम्य ते ययुः ॥ १६ ॥
dadṛśuḥ tatra rājarṣi taṅgaṇākhyaṁ tapo-nidhim ।
baloddhatā avajñāya tam asaṅgamya te yayuḥ ॥ 16 ॥

dadṛśuḥ — saw, tatra — there, rājarṣi — royal sage, taṅgaṇa-ākhyam — named Tangana, tapo-nidhim — treasure of penance, bala-uddhatāḥ — arrogant with strength, avajñāya — disrespecting, tam — him, asaṅgamya — ignoring, te — they, yayuḥ — went.
There they saw the royal sage named Tangana, a treasure of penance. Arrogant with strength, they disrespected and ignored him and went on.
तद्वीक्ष्य तङ्गणसुतः पित्रवज्ञां रुषान्वितः ।
जग्राहाश्वं यज्ञियं तं राजपुत्रान्‌ हि भर्त्सयन्‌ ॥ १७ ॥
tad vīkṣya taṅgaṇa-sutaḥ pitṛ-avajñāṁ ruṣānvitaḥ ।
jagrāha aśvaṁ yajñiyam taṁ rājaputrān hi bhartsayan ॥ 17 ॥

tat vīkṣya — seeing that, taṅgaṇa-sutaḥ — son of Tangana, pitṛ-avajñām — disrespect to his father, ruṣā-anvitaḥ — filled with anger, jagrāha — seized, aśvam — the horse, yajñiyam — sacrificial, tam — that, rājaputrān — princes, hi — indeed, bhartsayan — rebuking.
Seeing that, the son of Tangana, filled with anger at the disrespect to his father, seized the sacrificial horse, rebuking the princes.
अथ राजकुमारास्ते रुरुधुः सर्वतो हि तम्‌ ।
तावत्तङ्गणपुत्रोऽपि गण्डशैलं पुरः स्थितम्‌ ॥ १८ ॥
atha rājaputrās te rurudhuḥ sarvataḥ hi tam ।
tāvat taṅgaṇa-putraḥ api gaṇḍa-śailam puraḥ sthitam ॥ 18 ॥

atha — then, rājaputrāḥ — the princes, te — they, rurudhuḥ — surrounded, sarvataḥ — from all sides, hi — indeed, tam — him, tāvat — meanwhile, taṅgaṇa-putraḥ — son of Tangana, api — also, gaṇḍa-śailam — the rocky hill, puraḥ sthitam — standing before.
Then the princes surrounded him from all sides. Meanwhile, the son of Tangana entered the rocky hill standing before.
विवेशाश्वं समादाय पश्यत्सु राजसूनुषु ।
साश्वं शिलाविलीनं तं दृष्ट्वा राजकुमारकाः ॥ १९ ॥
viveśa aśvam samādāya paśyatsu rāj-sūnuṣu ।
sa-aśvam śilā-vilīnam tam dṛṣṭvā rāja-kumārakāḥ ॥ 19 ॥

viveśa — entered, aśvam — the horse, samādāya — taking along, paśyatsu — in the presence of, rāja-sūnuṣu — the princes, sa-aśvam — with the horse, śilā-vilīnam — merged into the rock, tam — that, dṛṣṭvā — seeing, rāja-kumārakāḥ — the princes.
Taking the horse along, he entered the rock in the presence of the princes. Seeing him merged into the rock with the horse, the princes...
विभिदुर्गण्डशैलं तं शस्त्रैरुच्चावचैः पृथक्‌ ।
चूर्णिताद्‌ गण्डशैलात्‌ स महत्या सेनया वृतः ॥ २० ॥
vibhidhuḥ gaṇḍa-śailam tam śastraiḥ uccāvacaiḥ pṛthak ।
cūrṇitāt gaṇḍa-śailāt sa mahatyā senayā vṛtaḥ ॥ 20 ॥

vibhidhuḥ — shattered, gaṇḍa-śailam — the rocky hill, tam — that, śastraiḥ — with weapons, uccāvacaiḥ — of various kinds, pṛthak — separately, cūrṇitāt — from the shattered, gaṇḍa-śailāt — rocky hill, saḥ — he, mahatyā — with a great, senayā — army, vṛtaḥ — surrounded.
...shattered the rocky hill with various kinds of weapons. From the shattered rocky hill, he emerged, surrounded by a great army.
निर्गत्य तङ्गणसुतो जिगाय युधि तान्‌ क्षणात्‌ ।
निहत्य सेनां सौषेणीं बद्ध्वा राजकुमारकान्‌ ॥ २१ ॥
nirgatya taṅgaṇa-suto jigāya yudhi tān kṣaṇāt ।
nihatya senāṁ sauṣeṇīṁ baddhvā rāja-kumārakān ॥ 21 ॥

nirgatya — emerging, taṅgaṇa-sutaḥ — son of Tangana, jigāya — defeated, yudhi — in battle, tān — them, kṣaṇāt — instantly, nihatya — having killed, senām — the army, sauṣeṇīm — of Sushena, baddhvā — having bound, rāja-kumārakān — the princes.
Emerging, the son of Tangana instantly defeated them in battle. Having killed Sushena's army, he bound the princes.
प्रविवेश गण्डशैलं भूयस्तङ्गणसम्भवः ।
अथ सेनाभटाः शिष्टा गत्वा राज्ञे न्यवेदयन्‌ ॥ २२ ॥
praviveśa gaṇḍa-śailaṁ bhūyas taṅgaṇa-sambhavaḥ ।
atha senā-bhaṭāḥ śiṣṭā gatvā rājñe nyavedayan ॥ 22 ॥

praviveśa — entered, gaṇḍa-śailam — the rocky hill, bhūyaḥ — again, taṅgaṇa-sambhavaḥ — son of Tangana, atha — then, senā-bhaṭāḥ — soldiers, śiṣṭāḥ — remaining, gatvā — going, rājñe — to the king, nyavedayan — reported.
The son of Tangana entered the rocky hill again. Then the remaining soldiers went to the king and reported.
साश्वराजकुमाराणां हरणं गण्डशैलके ।
सुषेणो विस्मितोऽत्यन्तमुवाचावरजं स्वकम्‌ ॥ २३ ॥
sāśva-rāja-kumārāṇāṁ haraṇaṁ gaṇḍa-śailake ।
suṣeṇo vismito’tyantam uvācāvarajaṁ svakam ॥ 23 ॥

sāśva — with the horse, rāja-kumārāṇām — of the princes, haraṇam — capture, gaṇḍa-śailake — in the rocky hill, suṣeṇaḥ — Sushena, vismitaḥ — astonished, atyantam — extremely, uvāca — said, avarajaṁ — younger brother, svakam — his own.
The capture of the princes with the horse in the rocky hill astonished Sushena, who then said to his younger brother.
वत्साशु गच्छ तं देशं यत्रास्ते तङ्गणो मुनिः ।
तपस्विनोऽचिन्त्यवीर्या अजेया देवमानुषैः ॥ २४ ॥
vatsāśu gaccha taṁ deśaṁ yatrāste taṅgaṇo muniḥ ।
tapasvino’cintya-vīryā ajeyā deva-mānuṣaiḥ ॥ 24 ॥

vatsa — dear, āśu — quickly, gaccha — go, taṁ deśaṁ — to that place, yatra — where, āste — resides, taṅgaṇaḥ muniḥ — sage Tangana, tapasvinaḥ — ascetics, acintya-vīryāḥ — of unimaginable strength, ajeyāḥ — invincible, deva-mānuṣaiḥ — by gods and humans.
Dear, quickly go to the place where sage Tangana resides. Ascetics are of unimaginable strength and invincible by gods and humans.
तं प्रसाद्य सुतानश्वं चासाद्यायाहि सत्वरम्‌ ।
न कालोऽतिव्रजेदेष वसन्तो यज्ञसम्मतः ॥ २५ ॥
taṁ prasādya sutān aśvaṁ ca āsādya āyāhi satvaram ।
na kālo’tivrajet eṣa vasanto yajña-sammataḥ ॥ 25 ॥

taṁ — him, prasādya — appeasing, sutān — sons, aśvam — horse, ca — and, āsādya — retrieving, āyāhi — come, satvaram — quickly, na kālaḥ — time, ativrajet — should not pass, eṣaḥ — this, vasantaḥ — spring, yajña-sammataḥ — approved for the sacrifice.
Appease him, retrieve the sons and the horse, and come quickly. Time should not pass; this spring is approved for the sacrifice.
अभिमानो न कर्तव्यस्तपस्विषु कदाचन ।
क्रुद्धास्तपस्विनो लोकान्‌ भस्मीकुर्युः क्षणेन वै ॥ २६ ॥
abhimāno na kartavyaḥ tapasviṣu kadācana ।
kruddhās tapasvino lokān bhasmī-kuryuḥ kṣaṇena vai ॥ 26 ॥

abhimānaḥ — arrogance, na kartavyaḥ — should not be shown, tapasviṣu — towards ascetics, kadācana — ever, kruddhāḥ — angry, tapasvinaḥ — ascetics, lokān — worlds, bhasmī-kuryuḥ — can burn to ashes, kṣaṇena — in an instant, vai — indeed.
Never show arrogance towards ascetics. Angry ascetics can burn worlds to ashes in an instant.
अतः प्रसादनपरो भूत्वा स्वार्थं प्रसाधय ।
इत्यादिष्टो महासेनस्तं देशं शीघ्रमाययौ ॥ २७ ॥

एवं राज्ञाऽनुयुक्तोऽथ तङ्गणः प्राह भूपतिम्‌ ॥ ५३ ॥
kathaṁ gaṇḍa-śaila-garbhe saṁsthitās tat samīraya ।
evaṁ rājñā anuyuktaḥ atha taṅgaṇaḥ prāha bhūpatim ॥ 53 ॥

How were they situated in the mountain cave? Tell me that." Thus asked by the king, then Tangana said to the king.
शृणु राजन्‌ प्रवक्ष्यामि पुराऽहं पृथिवीपतिः ।
समुद्रवलयां पृथ्वीमन्वशासं चिरं खलु ॥ ५४ ॥
śṛṇu rājan pravakṣyāmi purā ahaṁ pṛthivī-patiḥ ।
samudra-valayāṁ pṛthvīm anvaśāsaṁ ciraṁ khalu ॥ 54 ॥

śṛṇu — listen, rājan — O king, pravakṣyāmi — I will tell, purā — once, aham — I, pṛthivī-patiḥ — lord of the earth, samudra-valayām — ocean-bounded, pṛthvīm — earth, anvaśāsaṁ — ruled, ciraṁ — for a long time, khalu — indeed.
Listen, O king, I will tell you. Once, I was the lord of the earth, ruling the ocean-bounded earth for a long time.

mahādeva-prasādena jñātvā citim adhi-īśvarīm ।
tripurāṁ loka-saṁsthānaṁ nīrasaṁ vimṛśan tataḥ ॥ 55 ॥

mahādeva-prasādena — by the grace of Mahadeva, jñātvā — knowing, citim — consciousness, adhi-īśvarīm — supreme, tripurām — Tripura, loka-saṁsthānam — world, nīrasam — devoid of essence, vimṛśan — pondering, tataḥ — then.
By the grace of Mahadeva, knowing the supreme consciousness, Tripura, and pondering on the world as devoid of essence, then.

Disillusioned with worldly affairs, leaving the kingdom to my sons, I then entered this forest, and my faithful wife followed me.
तस्याभितप्यतो मेऽद्य ययुरर्बुदवत्सराः ।
भार्यापि मत्सेवनेन परां सिद्धिमुपागता ॥ ५७ ॥
tasyābhitapyataḥ me adya yayuḥ arbuda-vatsarāḥ ।
bhāryā api mat-sevanena parāṁ siddhim upāgatā ॥ 57 ॥

By my effortful meditation, now, after years, fruits of it have come. My wife also attained supreme perfection by serving me.

समाधावेव कामार्त्तमानसाऽभूत्ततस्तु सा ॥ ५८ ॥
kadācid atha bhāvya-artha-gauravān me priyā satī ।

Once, then, due to the importance of future matters, my faithful beloved, in her meditation, with a mind tormented by desire, became then.

असहन्ती कामवेगं भावयामास मद्रतिम्‌ ॥ ५९ ॥
māṁ dṛṣṭvā ratim icchantī samādhi-sthaṁ sthira-antaram ।
asahantī kāma-vegaṁ bhāvayām āsa mad-ratim ॥ 59 ॥

māṁ — me, dṛṣṭvā — seeing, ratim — pleasure, icchantī — desiring, samādhi-stham — in meditation, sthira-antaram — steady within, asahantī — unable to bear, kāma-vegam — the force of desire, bhāvayām āsa — thought of, mad-ratim — pleasure with me.
Seeing me in meditation, steady within, she desiring pleasure, unable to bear the force of desire, she thought of pleasure with me.

दधार गर्भं सुषुवे पुत्रमेनं पुरः स्थितम्‌ ॥ ६० ॥
gāḍha-bhāvanayā prāpya sambhogaṁ tu mayā saha ।
dadhāra garbhaṁ suṣuve putram enam puraḥ sthitam ॥ 60 ॥

With intense thought, attaining union with me, she bore pregnancy and gave birth to this son standing before.

putraṁ nyasya mad-utsaṅge māṁ samādheḥ prabodhya ca ।
dehaṁ bhūteṣu sākṛtya para-vyoma-ātmatāṁ yayau ॥ 61 ॥

putraṁ — son, nyasya — placing, mad-utsaṅge — on my lap, māṁ — me, samādheḥ — from meditation, prabodhya — awakening, ca — and, dehaṁ — body, bhūteṣu — to elements, sākṛtya — returning, para-vyoma-ātmatāṁ — to the supreme sky, yayau — went.
Placing the son on my lap, awakening me from meditation, she returned her body to the elements and went to the supreme sky.
अथ दृष्ट्वोत्सङ्ग एनं ज्ञात्वा तस्या गतिं पराम्‌ ।
दयाक्रान्तमना जातस्तेनायं वर्द्धितो मया ॥ ६२ ॥
atha dṛṣṭvotsāṅga enaṁ jñātvā tasyā gatiṁ parām ।
dayā-ākrānta-manā jātas tenāyaṁ varddhito mayā ॥ 62 ॥

atha — then, dṛṣṭvā — seeing, utsaṅga — on the lap, enaṁ — him, jñātvā — knowing, tasyā — her, gatiṁ — state, parām — supreme, dayā-ākrānta-manā — with a compassionate mind, jātaḥ — became, tena — by him, ayaṁ — this, varddhitaḥ — raised, mayā — by me.
Then, seeing him on the lap and knowing her supreme state, with a compassionate mind, I raised him.
श्रुत्वा कदाचिन्मत्तोऽयं राज्यशास्तिं पुरा कृताम्‌ ।
राज्यशासनकामोऽभूत्‌ प्रार्थयामास मामनु ॥ ६३ ॥
śrutvā kadācin matto'yaṁ rājya-śāstiṁ purā kṛtām ।
rājya-śāsana-kāmo'bhūt prārthayām āsa mām anu ॥ 63 ॥

śrutvā — hearing, kadācin — once, mattaḥ — from me, ayaṁ — he, rājya-śāstiṁ — governance, purā — formerly, kṛtām — done, rājya-śāsana-kāmaḥ — desirous of governance, abhūt — became, prārthayām āsa — requested, mām — me, anu — to follow.
Once, hearing from me about the governance I had done formerly, he became desirous of governance and requested me.

tato mad-upadeśena prāpya yoga-ṛddhim uttamām ।

tataḥ — then, mad-upadeśena — by my instruction, prāpya — attaining, yoga-ṛddhim — supreme yogic power, uttamām — excellent, nirmāya — creating, bhāvanā-yogāt — by the power of imagination, lokam — world, asmin — in this, mahāśmani — great stone.
Then, by my instruction, attaining the supreme yogic power, he created a world in this great stone by the power of imagination.

samudra-valayāṁ pṛthvīṁ śāsti nityaṁ sutās tvayam ।
tal-loke'aśvaḥ sutā rājño niruddhās te hi mocitāḥ ॥ 65 ॥

samudra-valayāṁ — ocean-bounded, pṛthvīṁ — earth, śāsti — rules, nityam — always, sutaḥ — son, tvayam — this, tal-loke — in that world, aśvaḥ — horse, sutā — sons, rājñaḥ — king's, niruddhāḥ — confined, te — they, hi — indeed, mocitāḥ — released.
This son always rules the ocean-bounded earth. In that world, the king's sons and horse, were confined, they have indeed been now released.

इति श्रुत्वा मुनिवचो भूयः पप्रच्छ भूपतिः ॥ ६६ ॥
ity etat te samākhyātaṁ gaṇḍa-śaile'varodhanam ।
iti śrutvā muni-vaco bhūyaḥ papraccha bhūpatiḥ ॥ 66 ॥

iti — thus, etat — this, te — to you, samākhyātam — explained, gaṇḍa-śaile — in the mountain, avarodhanam — confinement, iti — thus, śrutvā — hearing, muni-vaco — sage's words, bhūyaḥ — again, papraccha — asked, bhūpatiḥ — king.
Thus, I have explained to you the confinement in the mountain. Hearing the sage's words, the king again asked.

śrutaṁ tvad-uktam etad vai mahā-ścarya-karaṁ param ।
taṁ lokaṁ draṣṭum icchāmi kṛpayā me pradarśaya ॥ 67 ॥

śrutam — heard, tvad-uktam — what you said, etat — this, vai — indeed, mahā-ścarya-karam — very wonderful, param — supreme, tam — that, lokam — world, draṣṭum — to see, icchāmi — I wish, kṛpayā — kindly, me — to me, pradarśaya — show.
I have heard what you said, very wonderful indeed. I wish to see that supreme world. Kindly show it to me.
इति सम्प्रार्थितो राज्ञा मुनिः पुत्रं समादिशत्‌ ।
वत्सास्मै दर्शय स्वीयं लोकं सर्वं यथेप्सितम्‌ ॥ ६८ ॥
iti samprārthito rājñā muniḥ putraṁ samādiśat ।
vatsā'smai darśaya svīyaṁ lokaṁ sarvaṁ yathepsitam ॥ 68 ॥

iti — thus, samprārthitaḥ — requested, rājñā — by the king, muniḥ — sage, putram — son, samādiśat — instructed, vatsa — dear, asmai — to him, darśaya — show, svīyaṁ — own, lokam — world, sarvam — all, yathepsitam — as desired.
Thus requested by the king, the sage instructed his son, "Dear, show him your entire world as desired."

अथ तं तङ्गणसुतः समासाद्य नृपं ययौ ॥ ६९ ॥
ity uktvā taṅgaṇo bhūyaḥ praviśa samāhitim ।
atha taṁ taṅgaṇa-sutaḥ samāsādya nṛpaṁ yayau ॥ 69 ॥

iti — thus, uktvā — having said, taṅgaṇaḥ — Tangana, bhūyaḥ — again, praviśa — entered, samāhitim — meditation, atha — then, tam — him, taṅgaṇa-sutaḥ — Tangana's son, samāsādya — approaching, nṛpam — the king, yayau — went.
Having said thus, Tangana again entered meditation. Then, Tangana's son approached the king and went.

प्रवेष्टुं नाशकद्‌ भूप आह्वयन्तं मुनेः सुतम्‌ ॥ ७० ॥
gaṇḍa-śailaṁ prati tataḥ prāviśan muni-dārakaḥ ।
praveṣṭuṁ nāśakad bhūpa āhvayantaṁ muneḥ sutam ॥ 70 ॥

gaṇḍa-śailam — mountain, prati — towards, tataḥ — then, prāviśan — entered, muni-dārakaḥ — sage's son, praveṣṭum — to enter, na — not, aśakad — could, bhūpa — king, āhvayantaṁ — calling, muneḥ sutam — sage's son.
Then, the sage's son entered the mountain. The king could not enter, calling the sage's son.

अथ भूयो विनिष्कम्य प्राह भूपं मुनेः सुतः ॥ ७१ ॥
so'pi gaṇḍa-śilāntaḥ-stho rājānaṁ samupāhvayat ।
atha bhūyo viniṣkamya prāha bhūpaṁ muneḥ sutaḥ ॥ 71 ॥

saḥ — he, api — also, gaṇḍa-śilāntaḥ-sthaḥ — inside the mountain, rājānam — king, samupāhvayat — called, atha — then, bhūyaḥ — again, viniṣkamya — coming out, prāha — said, bhūpam — to the king, muneḥ sutaḥ — sage's son.
He, inside the mountain, called the king. Then, coming out again, the sage's son said to the king.

अयोगाद्‌ गण्डशैलोऽयं घनः सप्रतिघोऽभवत्‌ ॥ ७२ ॥
nūpaiṣa lokaḥ te'sādhyaḥ praveṣṭuṁ khalvayoginaḥ ।
ayogād gaṇḍa-śailo'yaṁ ghanaḥ saprati-gho'bhavat ॥ 72 ॥

nu — indeed, eṣaḥ — this, lokaḥ — world, te — for you, asādhyaḥ — impossible, praveṣṭum — to enter, khalu — indeed, ayoginaḥ — for non-yogi, ayogāt — due to lack of yoga, gaṇḍa-śailaḥ — mountain, ayam — this, ghanaḥ — solid, saprati-ghaḥ — with resistance, abhavat — became.
Indeed, this world is impossible for you, a non-yogi, to enter. Due to lack of yoga, this mountain became solid with resistance.
नेतव्यस्त्वं सर्वथैव पितुर्वचनगौरवात्‌ ।
तदत्र देहं विन्यस्य कोटरे तृणसंवृते ॥ ७३ ॥
netavyas tvaṁ sarvathaiva pitur vacana-gauravāt ।
tad atra dehaṁ vinyasya koṭare tṛṇa-saṁvṛte ॥ 73 ॥

Certainly, you are to be led due to respect for my father's words. Therefore, place your body here in this cave covered with grass.

इत्युक्तः प्राह नृपतिरशक्तो देहनिर्गमे ॥ ७४ ॥
mano-mātra-śarīraḥ san śailaṁ viśa mayā saha ।
ity uktaḥ prāha nṛpatir aśakto deha-nirgame ॥ 74 ॥

mano-mātra-śarīraḥ — with a mind-only body, san — being, śailam — mountain, viśa — enter, mayā saha — with me, iti uktaḥ — thus spoken, prāha — said, nṛpatiḥ — king, aśaktaḥ — unable, deha-nirgame — to leave the body.
Having only a mental body, enter the mountain with me. Thus addressed, the king, unable to leave the body, said.

kathaṁ mune deham imam utsṛjāmi samīraya ।

kathaṁ — how, mune — O sage, deham — body, imam — this, utsṛjāmi — can I leave, samīraya — explain, utsṛjāmi — if I leave, yadi — if, balāt — forcefully, nāśam — destruction, eṣyāmi — I will attain, sarvathā — certainly.
O sage, how shall I leave this body? Explain. If I leave it by force, I will completely come to destruction.
एवं वदन्तं नृपतिं प्रहस्याह मुनेः सुतः ।

evaṁ vadantaṁ nṛpatiṁ prahasya āha muneḥ sutaḥ ।
aho yogānabhijño'si cāstu netre nimīlya ॥ 76 ॥

evaṁ — thus, vadantam — speaking, nṛpatim — to the king, prahasya — smiling, āha — said, muneḥ sutaḥ — sage's son, aho — oh, yogānabhijñaḥ — ignorant of yoga, asi — you are, ca — indeed, astu — be it, netre — eyes, nimīlya — closing.
Thus speaking, the sage's son smiled and said to the king, "Oh, you are ignorant of yoga. Indeed, be it so, close your eyes."

ity uktvā mīlita-akṣaṁ taṁ praviśya nimiṣa-ardhataḥ ।
ākṛṣya talliṅga-tanuṁ kṣiptvā śvabhre ca tat-tanum ॥ 77 ॥

iti — thus, uktvā — having said, mīlita-akṣam — with closed eyes, tam — him, praviśya — entering, nimiṣa-ardhataḥ — in a moment, ākṛṣya — pulling, talliṅga-tanum — that subtle body, kṣiptvā — throwing, śvabhre — into a pit, ca — and, tat-tanum — that body.
Having said this, with his eyes closed, entering the king in a moment, pulling his subtle body and throwing the physical body into a pit.

yoga-sāmarthyataḥ śaile niviśya nṛpa-saṁyutaḥ ।
suṣuptaṁ deha-vaikalyāt sva-saṅkalpa-uttha-dehake ॥ 78 ॥

yoga-sāmarthyataḥ — by the power of yoga, śaile — in the mountain, niviśya — entering, nṛpa-saṁyutaḥ — with the king, suṣuptaṁ — asleep, deha-vaikalyāt — due to the body's absence, sva-saṅkalpa-uttha-dehake — with the mind-created body.
By the power of yoga, entering the mountain with the king, being asleep due to the body's absence, only with the mind-created body.

गृहीतं मुनिनाऽपश्यत्‌ स्वं महागगने तदा ॥ ७९ ॥
saṁyojya bodhayām āsa prabuddho nṛpatis tadā ।
gṛhītaṁ muninā'paśyat svaṁ mahā-gagane tadā ॥ 79 ॥

saṁyojya — placing, bodhayām āsa — awakened, prabuddhaḥ — awakened, nṛpatiḥ — king, tadā — then, gṛhītam — taken, muninā — by the sage, apaśyat — saw, svaṁ — his own, mahā-gagane — in the great sky, tadā — then.
Placing and awakening, the king then saw himself taken by the sage in the great sky.
ऊर्ध्वं विष्वक्‌ च संपश्यन्‌ नभो भीममनन्तकम्‌ ।
भीतः प्राह मुनेः पुत्रं मुने मां न परित्यज ॥ ८० ॥
ūrdhvaṁ viṣvak ca saṁpaśyan nabho bhīmam anantakam ।
bhītaḥ prāha muneḥ putraṁ mune māṁ na parityaja ॥ 80 ॥

ūrdhvam — upward, viṣvak — all around, ca — and, saṁpaśyan — seeing, nabhaḥ — sky, bhīmam — fearful, anantakam — infinite, bhītaḥ — afraid, prāha — said, muneḥ putram — to the sage's son, mune — O sage, māṁ — me, na — not, parityaja — leave.
Seeing upward and all around the fearful, infinite sky, afraid, he said to the sage's son, "O sage, do not leave me."
परित्यक्तो विनश्यामि पतिष्येऽहं निराश्रये ।
इति भीतं नृपं दृष्ट्वा प्रहस्याह मूनेः सुतः ॥ ८१ ॥
parityakto vinaśyāmi patiṣye'haṁ nirāśraye ।
iti bhītaṁ nṛpaṁ dṛṣṭvā prahasyāha muneḥ sutaḥ ॥ 81 ॥

parityaktaḥ — abandoned, vinaśyāmi — I will perish, patiṣye — I will fall, ahaṁ — I, nirāśraye — without support, iti — thus, bhītam — frightened, nṛpam — king, dṛṣṭvā — seeing, prahasya — smiling, āha — said, muneḥ sutaḥ — sage's son.
I will perish if abandoned; I will fall without support. Seeing the frightened king, the sage's son smiled and said:
परित्यज भयं भूप नोत्सृजामि निशामय ।
एनं शैलान्तरस्थानं लोकं धैर्येण सर्वतः ॥ ८२ ॥
parityaja bhayaṁ bhūpa notsṛjāmi niśāmaya ।
enaṁ śailāntarasthānaṁ lokaṁ dhairyeṇa sarvataḥ ॥ 82 ॥

parityaja — abandon, bhayam — fear, bhūpa — O king, na utsṛjāmi — I will not leave you, niśāmaya — observe, enam — this, śaila-antara-sthānaṁ — inner mountain place, lokam — world, dhairyeṇa — with courage, sarvataḥ — completely.
Abandon your fear, O king; I will not leave you. Observe this inner mountain world with courage.
अथ धैर्यं समालम्ब्य नृपः समवलोकयत्‌ ।
अधो दूरे सनक्षत्रमभ्रमन्धतमोवृतम्‌ ॥ ८३ ॥
atha dhairyaṁ samālambya nṛpaḥ samavalokayata ।
adho dūre sanakṣatram abhram andhatamo-vṛtam ॥ 83 ॥

atha — then, dhairyam — courage, samālambya — taking, nṛpaḥ — king, samavalokayata — observed, adhaḥ — below, dūre — at a distance, sa-nakṣatram — with stars, abhram — sky, andha-tamaḥ-vṛtam — covered in deep darkness.
Then, taking courage, the king observed below at a distance, the sky with stars, covered in deep darkness.
प्रविश्य तं देशमपि ततोऽधस्तात्‌ प्रपश्यत ।
चन्द्रमण्डलमास्फीतं तत्रागत्य जडीकृतः ॥ ८४ ॥
praviśya taṁ deśam api tato'dhastāt prapaśyata ।
candra-maṇḍalam āspītaṁ tatrāgatya jaḍīkṛtaḥ ॥ 84 ॥

praviśya — entering, tam — that, deśam — place, api — also, tataḥ — then, adhastāt — below, prapaśyata — observed, candra-maṇḍalam — moon's orbit, āspītam — vast, tatra — there, āgatya — coming, jaḍīkṛtaḥ — immobilized.
Entering that place, he then observed below, the vast moon's orbit. Coming there, he was immobilized.
चन्द्रमण्डलशीतेन मुनिपुत्रेण रक्षितः ।
अथ प्राप्य सूर्यलोकं तत्करैरभितापितः ॥ ८५ ॥
candra-maṇḍala-śītena muni-putreṇa rakṣitaḥ ।
atha prāpya sūrya-lokaṁ tat-karair abhitāpitaḥ ॥ 85 ॥

candra-maṇḍala-śītena — by the coolness of the moon's orbit, muni-putreṇa — by the sage's son, rakṣitaḥ — protected, atha — then, prāpya — reaching, sūrya-lokaṁ — sun's world, tat-karaiḥ — by its rays, abhitāpitaḥ — heated.
Protected by the coolness of the moon's orbit and the sage's son, he then reached the sun's world, heated by its rays.
मुनिपुत्रेण योगेन शिशिरीकृतदेहकः ।
अपश्यल्लोकमखिलं स्वर्लोकप्रतिबिम्बवत्‌ ॥ ८६ ॥
muni-putreṇa yogena śiśirī-kṛta-dehakaḥ ।
apaśyal lokam akhilaṁ svar-loka-pratibimba-vat ॥ 86 ॥

muni-putreṇa — by the sage's son, yogena — by yoga, śiśirī-kṛta-dehakaḥ — body cooled, apaśyat — observed, lokam — world, akhilam — entire, svar-loka-pratibimba-vat — like a reflection of the heavenly world.
Cooled by the sage's son through yoga, he observed the entire world, like a reflection of the heavenly world.
अथ शृङ्गे हेमगिरेर्मुनिना सह संस्थितः ।
मुनिप्रदर्शितं सर्वमपश्यत्‌ पृथिवीपतिः ॥ ८७ ॥
atha śṛṅge hema-girer muninā saha saṁsthitaḥ ।
muni-pradarśitaṁ sarvam apaśyat pṛthivī-patiḥ ॥ 87 ॥

atha — then, śṛṅge — on the peak, hema-gireḥ — of the golden mountain, muninā — with the sage, saha — together, saṁsthitaḥ — standing, muni-pradarśitam — shown by the sage, sarvam — all, apaśyat — observed, pṛthivī-patiḥ — king.
Then, standing on the peak of the golden mountain with the sage, the king observed all shown by the sage.
दूरान्तरावलोकाय मुनिदत्तशुभेक्षणः ।
अपश्यद्वलयात्मानं लोकालोकाख्यपर्वतम्‌ ॥ ८८ ॥
dūrāntarāvalokāya muni-datta-śubhekṣaṇaḥ ।
apaśyat valayātmānaṁ lokāloka-ākhya-parvatam ॥ 88 ॥

dūra-antara-avalokāya — for seeing distant places, muni-datta-śubha-īkṣaṇaḥ — blessed with divine sight by the sage, apaśyat — observed, valaya-ātmānam — circular, lokāloka-ākhya-parvatam — mountain named Lokāloka.
Blessed with divine sight by the sage to see distant places, he observed the circular mountain named Lokāloka.
तद्बहिर्ध्वान्तसन्दोहमन्तः सौवर्णमेदिनीम्‌ ।
समुद्रान्‌ सप्तद्वीपांश्च नदीगिरिसमाकुलान्‌ ॥ ८९ ॥
tad-bahir-dhvānta-sandoham antaḥ sauvarṇa-medīnīm ।
samudrān sapta-dvīpāṁś ca nadī-giri-samākulān ॥ 89 ॥

tad-bahiḥ — outside it, dhvānta-sandoham — masses of darkness, antaḥ — inside, sauvarṇa-medīnīm — golden land, samudrān — oceans, sapta-dvīpān — seven islands, ca — and, nadī-giri-samākulān — filled with rivers and mountains.
Outside it, masses of darkness; inside, a golden land with oceans, seven islands, filled with rivers and mountains.
भुवनान्यपि सर्वाणि चेन्द्राद्यान्‌ विबुधोत्तमान्‌ ।
दैत्यान्‌ मनुष्यान्‌ रक्षांसि यक्षकिंपुरुषादिकान्‌ ॥ ९० ॥
bhuvanāny api sarvāṇi cendrādyān vibudhottamān ।
daityān manuṣyān rakṣāṁsi yakṣa-kimpuruṣādikān ॥ 90 ॥

bhuvanāni — worlds, api — also, sarvāṇi — all, ca — and, indra-ādyān — starting with Indra, vibudha-uttamān — best of the wise, daityān — demons, manuṣyān — humans, rakṣāṁsi — demons, yakṣa-kimpuruṣa-ādikān — Yakshas, Kinnaras, and others.
He observed all worlds, starting with Indra, the best of the wise, demons, humans, Rakshasas, Yakshas, Kinnaras, and others.
तत्रापश्यत्‌ सत्यलोके वैकुण्ठे राजते नगे ।
मुनिपुत्रं स्वमात्मानं ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवात्मना ॥ ९१ ॥
tatrāpaśyat satya-loke vaikuṇṭhe rājate nage ।
muni-putraṁ svam ātmānaṁ brahma-viṣṇu-śivātmanā ॥ 91 ॥

tatra — there, apaśyat — observed, satya-loke — in Satya-loka, vaikuṇṭhe — in Vaikuntha, rājate nage — in the silver mountain, muni-putram — sage's son, svam ātmānam — himself, brahma-viṣṇu-śiva-ātmanā — as Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva.
There, he observed in Satya-loka, in Vaikuntha, in the silver mountain, the sage's son and himself as Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva.
विभज्य संस्थितं सर्वलोकसृष्टयादिहेतवे ।
अथाऽपश्यद्‌ भूविभागे कृत्वा रूपान्तरं तथा ॥ ९२ ॥
vibhajya saṁsthitaṁ sarva-loka-sṛṣṭyādi-hetave ।
athāpaśyat bhū-vibhāge kṛtvā rūpāntaraṁ tathā ॥ 92 ॥

vibhajya — divided, saṁsthitaṁ — existing, sarva-loka-sṛṣṭi-ādi-hetave — for the creation of all worlds, atha — then, apaśyat — observed, bhū-vibhāge — in the division of the earth, kṛtvā — having made, rūpa-antaraṁ — different forms, tathā — likewise.
Divided, existing for the creation of all worlds, then he observed in the division of the earth, having made different forms, likewise.
प्रशासनपरो भूमेः सार्वभौमत्वमास्थितः ।
एवं मुनिकुमारस्य दृष्ट्वा योगर्द्धिमुत्तमाम्‌ ॥ ९३ ॥
praśāsana-paro bhūmeḥ sārvabhaumatvam āsthitaḥ ।
evaṁ muni-kumārasya dṛṣṭvā yoga-ṛddhim uttamām ॥ 93 ॥

praśāsana-paraḥ — dedicated to administration, bhūmeḥ — of the earth, sārvabhaumatvam — universal sovereignty, āsthitaḥ — assumed, evaṁ — thus, muni-kumārasya — of the sage's son, dṛṣṭvā — seeing, yoga-ṛddhim — the power of yoga, uttamām — supreme.
Dedicated to the administration of the earth, assuming universal sovereignty, thus seeing the supreme power of yoga of the sage's son.
विस्मितोऽभून्महासेनस्ततः प्राह मुनेः सुतः ।
राजन्नेतल्लोकजातं पश्यतः काल अत्यगात्‌ ॥ ९४ ॥
vismito'bhūn mahāsenas tataḥ prāha muneḥ sutaḥ ।
rājann etal loka-jātaṁ paśyataḥ kāla atyagāt ॥ 94 ॥

vismitaḥ abhūt — was astonished, mahāsenaḥ — Mahasena, tataḥ — then, prāha — said, muneḥ sutaḥ — sage's son, rājan — O king, etal — this, loka-jātam — world creation, paśyataḥ — while seeing, kālaḥ atyagāt — time has passed.
Mahasena was astonished and then the sage's son said, "O king, while you were seeing this world creation, time has passed."
अर्बुदानां द्वादशकमितोऽप्यत्र दिनात्मकः ।
गच्छावो बाह्यलोकं तं यत्रास्ते जनको मम ॥ ९५ ॥
arbudānāṁ dvādaśakam ito'py atra dinātmakaḥ ।
gacchāvo bāhya-lokaṁ taṁ yatrāste janako mama ॥ 95 ॥

arbudānāṁ — of crores, dvādaśakam — twelve, itaḥ api atra — there also, dinātmakaḥ — days, gacchāvaḥ — let us go, bāhya-lokam — to the outer world, tam — that, yatra — where, āste — resides, janakaḥ mama — my father.
"Twelve crores of days have passed there also; let us go to the outer world where my father resides."
इत्युकत्वा भूभृता तेन सह भूयः खमाप्लुतः ।
पूर्ववत्‌ तद्गण्डशैलान्निर्गत्याभ्याययौ बहिः ॥ ९६ ॥
ityuktvā bhūbhṛtā tena saha bhūyaḥ kham āplutaḥ ।
pūrvavat tad-gaṇḍa-śailāt nirgatya abhyāyayau bahiḥ ॥ 96 ॥

iti uktvā — thus saying, bhūbhṛtā — by the king, tena saha — with him, bhūyaḥ — again, kham āplutaḥ — rose into the sky, pūrvavat — as before, tad-gaṇḍa-śailāt — from that mountain, nirgatya — emerging, abhyāyayau — reached, bahiḥ — outside.
Thus saying, the king rose into the sky with him again, emerging from that mountain as before, and reached the outside.

colophon.en: Thus ends the twelfth chapter named "Observing the World of Gandhashaila" in the revered Knowledge Section of Tripura Rahasya.

lines.text: मुनिपुत्रः पुनः शैलाद्‌ महासेनं विनिर्गमे ।
विधाय मूर्च्छितं लिङ्गदेहं संस्कारमात्रकम्‌ ॥ १ ॥
muniputraḥ punaḥ śailād mahāsenaṁ vinirgame ।
vidhāya mūrcchitaṁ liṅga-dehaṁ saṁskāra-mātrakam ॥ 1 ॥

muniputraḥ — sage's son, punaḥ — again, śailāt — from the mountain, mahāsenam — Mahasena, vinirgame — at the exit, vidhāya — having made, mūrcchitam — unconscious, liṅga-deham — subtle body, saṁskāra-mātrakam — consisting of impressions.
The sage's son, again at the exit from the mountain, made Mahasena unconscious with the subtle body consisting of impressions.
समादाय विनिर्गत्य प्राक्षिपत्तच्छरीरके ।
उत्थापयामास तु तं जीर्णदेहसुसङ्गतम्‌ ॥ २ ॥
samādāya vinirgatyaprākṣipat tac-charīrake ।
utthāpayāmāsa tu taṁ jīrṇa-deha-susaṅgatam ॥ 2 ॥

samādāya — taking, vinirgatyā — after exiting, prākṣipat — placed, tac-charīrake — into that body, utthāpayāmāsa — revived, tu — indeed, tam — him, jīrṇa-deha-susaṅgatam — well-fitting the worn-out body.
Taking him out, he placed him into that body and revived him, fitting him well into the worn-out body.
अथोत्थितो महासेनो बाह्यलोकं समीक्ष्य तु ।
भुवं जनांस्तरून्‌ स्त्रोतोह्रदादींश्चापि नूतनान्‌ ॥ ३ ॥
athotthito mahāseno bāhya-lokaṁ samīkṣya tu ।
bhuvaṁ janāṁs tarūn srotah-radādīṁś ca api nūtanān ॥ 3 ॥

atha — then, utthitaḥ — risen, mahāsenaḥ — Mahasena, bāhya-lokam — external world, samīkṣya — observing, tu — indeed, bhuvam — land, janān — people, tarūn — trees, srotah-radādīn — streams and ponds, ca api — and also, nūtanān — new.
Then, Mahasena, risen, observed the external world, the land, people, trees, streams, and ponds, all new.
बभूव विस्मितोऽत्यन्तं पप्रच्छ मुनिनन्दनम्‌ ।
कतमो वै महाभाग ! लोकोऽयं मे प्रदर्शितः ॥ ४ ॥
babhūva vismito'tyantaṁ papraccha muni-nandanam ।
katamo vai mahābhāga! loko'yaṁ me pradarśitaḥ ॥ 4 ॥

babhūva — became, vismitaḥ — astonished, atyantam — greatly, papraccha — asked, muni-nandanam — sage's son, katamaḥ — which, vai — indeed, mahābhāga — O great one, lokaḥ — world, ayam — this, me — to me, pradarśitaḥ — shown.
Greatly astonished, he asked the sage's son, "Which world is this, O great one, that you have shown to me?"
पुरादृष्टादपूर्वोऽयं समाचक्ष्वैतदद्‌भुतम्‌ ।
इत्यापुष्टो मुनिसुतो महासेनमुवाच ह ॥ ५ ॥
purādṛṣṭād apūrvo'yaṁ samācakṣvaitad adbhutam ।
ityāpuṣṭo muni-suto mahāsenam uvāca ha ॥ 5 ॥

purā-dṛṣṭāt — from the previously seen, apūrvaḥ — unprecedented, ayam — this, samācakṣva — explain, etad — this, adbhutam — wonderful, iti — thus, āpuṣṭaḥ — asked, muni-sutaḥ — sage's son, mahāsenam — Mahasena, uvāca — said, ha — indeed.
"Explain this unprecedented, wonderful world," asked Mahasena. The sage's son said to him:
शृणु राजन्नयं लोकः पूर्वं योऽस्माभिरास्थितः ।
स एव चिरकालेन परिणामान्तरं गतः ॥ ६ ॥
śṛṇu rājan nayaṁ lokaḥ pūrvaṁ yo'smābhir āsthitaḥ ।
sa eva cirakālena pariṇāmāntaraṁ gataḥ ॥ 6 ॥

śṛṇu — listen, rājan — O king, ayam — this, lokaḥ — world, pūrvam — before, yaḥ — which, asmābhiḥ — by us, āsthitaḥ — inhabited, saḥ — that, eva — indeed, cirakālena — over a long time, pariṇāma-antaram — transformation, gataḥ — underwent.
"Listen, O king, this world, which we inhabited before, has indeed undergone a transformation over a long time."
शैललोकगतानां नो दिनमेकं यदत्यगात्‌ ।
तावतैवात्र कालेन द्वादशार्बुदवत्सराः ॥ ७ ॥
śaila-loka-gatānāṁ no dinam ekaṁ yad atyagāt ।
tāvataivātra kālena dvādaśārbudavat-sarāḥ ॥ 7 ॥

śaila-loka-gatānām — in the mountain world, no — our, dinam ekam — one day, yad — which, atyagāt — passed, tāvata — that much, eva — indeed, atra — here, kālena — in time, dvādaśa-arbuda-vat-sarāḥ — twelve crores of years.
"One day in the mountain world, for us, indeed, here corresponds to twelve crores of years in time."
अतिक्रान्ता अतो लोकस्त्वयं रूपान्तरं गतः ।
भिन्नां व्यवहृतिं पश्य भाषां चापि समन्ततः ॥ ८ ॥
atikrāntā ato lokaḥ tvayaṁ rūpāntaraṁ gataḥ ।
bhinnāṁ vyavahṛtiṁ paśya bhāṣāṁ cāpi samantataḥ ॥ 8 ॥

atikrāntā — passed, ataḥ — thus, lokaḥ — world, ayam — this, rūpāntaram — different form, gataḥ — attained, bhinnām — different, vyavahṛtim — customs, paśya — see, bhāṣām — language, ca api — and also, samantataḥ — everywhere.
"Thus, this world has passed and attained a different form. See the different customs and languages everywhere."
एवमेव जनानां तु कालेन भिद्यते स्थितिः ।
एवं मया तु बहुधा दृष्टा भिन्ना जगत्स्थितिः ॥ ९ ॥
evameva janānāṁ tu kālena bhidyate sthitiḥ ।
evaṁ mayā tu bahudhā dṛṣṭā bhinnā jagat-sthitiḥ ॥ 9 ॥

evam-eva — in the same way, janānām — of people, tu — indeed, kālena — with time, bhidyate — changes, sthitiḥ — condition, evam — thus, mayā — by me, tu — indeed, bahudhā — in many ways, dṛṣṭā — seen, bhinnā — different, jagat-sthitiḥ — world conditions.
"In the same way, people's conditions change with time. Thus, I have seen many different world conditions."
पश्यैष मे स भगवान्‌ समाहितमतिः पिता ।
सोऽयं देशो यत्र पूर्व त्वया मे संस्तुतः पिता ॥ १० ॥
paśyaiṣa me sa bhagavān samāhita-matiḥ pitā ।
so'yaṁ deśo yatra pūrva tvayā me saṁstutaḥ pitā ॥ 10 ॥

राजन्‌ विमृश कस्त्वं वै कान्‌ विनष्टान्‌ प्रशोचसि ।
देहस्त्वं देहभिन्नो वा देहः संघातरूपकः ॥ ३७ ॥
rājan vimṛśa kas tvaṁ vai kān vinaṣṭān praśocasi ।
dehas tvaṁ deha-bhinno vā dehaḥ saṅghāta-rūpakaḥ ॥ 37 ॥

rājan — O king, vimṛśa — consider, kaḥ — who, tvam — you, vai — indeed, kān — whom, vinaṣṭān — lost, praśocasi — lament, dehaḥ — body, tvam — you, deha-bhinnaḥ — separate from the body, vā — or, dehaḥ — body, saṅghāta-rūpakaḥ — conglomerate form.
"O king, consider who you are, and whom you lament as lost. Are you the body, separate from the body, or the body in conglomerate form?"
संघातस्यैकदेशस्य वा नाशान्नाश उच्यते ।
प्रतिक्षणं त्वेकदेशनाशो देहस्य भावितः ॥ ३८ ॥
saṅghātasyaika-deśasya vā nāśān nāśa ucyate ।
prati-kṣaṇaṁ tv eka-deśa-nāśo dehasya bhāvitaḥ ॥ 38 ॥

saṅghātasya — of the conglomerate, eka-deśasya — of one part, vā — or, nāśāt — by destruction, nāśaḥ — destruction, ucyate — is called, prati-kṣaṇam — every moment, tu — indeed, eka-deśa-nāśaḥ — part-by-part destruction, dehasya — of the body, bhāvitaḥ — considered.
"The destruction of one part of a conglomerate is called destruction. Every moment, the body undergoes part-by-part destruction."
मूत्रोच्चारश्लेष्मनखकेशादेः सन्ततं क्षयः ।
सर्वात्मना तु संघातनाशो नहि विभाव्यते ॥ ३९ ॥
mūtroccāra-śleṣma-nakha-keśādeḥ santataṁ kṣayaḥ ।
sarvātmanā tu saṅghāta-nāśo nahi vibhāvyate ॥ 39 ॥

mūtra-ucchāra-śleṣma-nakha-keśa-ādeḥ — of urine, excretion, mucus, nails, hair, etc., santataṁ — continually, kṣayaḥ — decline, sarvātmanā — altogether, tu — indeed, saṅghāta-nāśaḥ — destruction of the conglomerate, nahi — not, vibhāvyate — observed.
"The decline of urine, excretion, mucus, nails, hair, etc., continually occurs. Indeed, the complete destruction of the conglomerate is not observed."
भ्रात्रादेस्तव देहांश: स्यात्‌ पृथिव्यादिषु स्फुटम्‌ ।
अन्ततो देहगगनमविनाश्यस्ति केवलम्‌ ॥ ४० ॥
bhrātrādes tava dehāṁśaḥ syāt pṛthivyādiṣu sphuṭam ।
antato deha-gaganam avināśy asti kevalam ॥ 40 ॥

bhrātrādeḥ — of your brother, etc., tava — your, dehāṁśaḥ — part of the body, syāt — is, pṛthivyādiṣu — in the elements like earth, etc., sphuṭam — clearly, antataḥ — ultimately, deha-gaganam — the body-space, avināśyaḥ — indestructible, asti — is, kevalam — only.
"A part of your brother's body is clearly in the elements like earth, etc. Ultimately, the body-space is only indestructible."
न त्वं देहः किन्तु देही मद्देह इति भाषसे ।
यथा मद्वस्त्रमित्येवं स देहस्त्वं कथं वद ॥ ४१ ॥
na tvaṁ dehaḥ kintu dehī mad-deha iti bhāṣase ।
yathā mad-vastram ity evaṁ sa dehas tvaṁ kathaṁ vada ॥ 41 ॥

na — not, tvam — you, dehaḥ — body, kintu — but, dehī — possessor of the body, mad-dehaḥ — my body, iti — thus, bhāṣase — you say, yathā — just as, mad-vastram — my garment, iti — thus, evam — in this way, saḥ — that, dehaḥ — body, tvam — you, katham — how, vada — say.
"You are not the body, but the possessor of the body. Just as you say 'my body,' similarly, how can you be the body?"
यदि त्वं देहभिन्नोऽसि सम्बन्धः कोऽन्यदेहकेः ।
यथा भ्रात्रादिवासोभिर्नास्ति सम्बन्धलेशकः ॥ ४२ ॥
yadi tvaṁ deha-bhinno'si sambandhaḥ ko'nyadehakaiḥ ।
yathā bhrātrādi-vāsobhir nāsti sambandha-leśakaḥ ॥ 42 ॥

yadi — if, tvam — you, deha-bhinnaḥ — separate from the body, asi — are, sambandhaḥ — relationship, kaḥ — what, anya-dehakaiḥ — with other bodies, yathā — just as, bhrātṛ-ādi-vāsobhiḥ — with garments like those of brothers, nāsti — does not exist, sambandha-leśakaḥ — any connection.
"If you are separate from the body, what connection do you have with other bodies? Just as there is no relationship with the garments of brothers."
अविशेषात्तच्छरीरैर्विनष्टैस्ते कथं शुचा ।
मच्छरीरं मदक्षाणि मत्प्राणो मन्मनस्त्विति ॥ ४३ ॥
aviśeṣāt tac-charīraiḥ vinaṣṭais te kathaṁ śucā ।
mac-charīraṁ mad-akṣāṇi mat-prāṇo man-manastv iti ॥ 43 ॥

aviśeṣāt — due to non-difference, tat-charīraiḥ — with those bodies, vinaṣṭaiḥ — destroyed, te — your, katham — how, śucā — lament, mac-charīraṁ — my body, mad-akṣāṇi — my senses, mat-prāṇaḥ — my life, mat-manas — my mind, tvam — you, iti — thus.
"How can you lament the destroyed bodies due to non-difference? My body, my senses, my life, my mind, thus you are."
वदन्‌ भवान्‌ किंस्वरूपो वद मे पृच्छते नृप ।
एवमुक्तो महासेनो मुहूर्तं सुविचाये तु ॥ ४४ ॥
vadan bhavān kiṁ svarūpo vada me pṛcchate nṛpa ।
evam-ukto mahāseno muhūrtaṁ suvichāya tu ॥ 44 ॥

vadan — saying, bhavān — you, kim — what, svarūpaḥ — essence, vada — tell, me — to me, pṛcchate — asking, nṛpa — king, evam-uktaḥ — thus addressed, mahāsenaḥ — Mahasena, muhūrtam — for a moment, suvichāya — deeply reflecting, tu — indeed.
"O king, tell me your true essence," he said to Mahasena. Addressed thus, Mahasena deeply reflected for a moment.
अप्राप्यान्तं मुनेः प्रश्ने प्राह दीनतरस्ततः ।
न जाने भगवन्‌ कोऽहमिति सर्वात्मनाप्यहम्‌ ॥ ४५ ॥
aprāpyāntaṁ muneḥ praśne prāha dīnataras tataḥ ।
na jāne bhagavan ko'ham iti sarvātmana py aham ॥ 45 ॥

aprāpya — without reaching, antaṁ — end, muneḥ — sage's, praśne — question, prāha — said, dīnataraḥ — very distressed, tataḥ — then, na — not, jāne — I know, bhagavan — O lord, kaḥ — who, aham — I, iti — thus, sarvātmana — completely, api — indeed, aham — I.
Unable to answer the sage's question, very distressed, Mahasena said, "O lord, I do not know who I am completely."
स्वभावतस्तु शोचामि कारणं तत्र नाविदम्‌ ।
प्रपन्नस्त्वामहं दीनः किमिदं भगवन्‌ वद ॥ ४६ ॥
svabhāvatas tu śocāmi kāraṇaṁ tatra nāvidam ।
prapannas tvām ahaṁ dīnaḥ kim idaṁ bhagavan vada ॥ 46 ॥

svabhāvataḥ — naturally, tu — but, śocāmi — I lament, kāraṇam — reason, tatra — there, na avidam — I do not know, prapannaḥ — surrendered, tvām — to you, aham — I, dīnaḥ — distressed, kim — what, idam — this, bhagavan — O lord, vada — tell.
"Naturally, I lament without knowing the reason. I have surrendered to you, O lord, distressed. Tell me what this is."
सर्वे शोचन्ति यत्‌ कस्मिन्नपि बन्धौ मृते सति ।
न स्वात्मानं विजानन्ति नान्यं शोचन्ति चैव हि ॥ ४७ ॥
sarve śocanti yat kasminn api bandhau mṛte sati ।
na svātmānaṁ vijānanti nānyaṁ śocanti caiva hi ॥ 47 ॥

sarve — all, śocanti — lament, yat — for, kasmin api — any, bandhau — relative, mṛte — dead, sati — being, na — not, svātmānam — their self, vijānanti — they know, na anyaṁ — not others, śocanti — lament, ca — and, eva — indeed, hi — certainly.
"All lament for any dead relative. They do not know their self and certainly do not lament for others."
एतन्मे ब्रूहि भगवन्‌ शिष्याय तव वै स्फुटम्‌ ।
इति पृष्टो मुनिसुतो महासेनमथाब्रवीत्‌ ॥ ४८ ॥
etan me brūhi bhagavan śiṣyāya tava vai sphuṭam ।
iti pṛṣṭo muni-suto mahāsenam athābravīt ॥ 48 ॥

etan — this, me — to me, brūhi — tell, bhagavan — O lord, śiṣyāya — to your disciple, tava — your, vai — indeed, sphuṭam — clearly, iti — thus, pṛṣṭaḥ — asked, muni-sutaḥ — sage's son, mahāsenam — to Mahasena, atha — then, abravīt — said.
"O lord, tell this clearly to your disciple," Mahasena asked. Then the sage's son spoke to Mahasena.
राजन्‌ शृणु महादेव्या मायया मोहिता जनाः ।
स्वात्मानमविदित्वैव व्यर्थ शोचन्ति सर्वदा ॥ ४९ ॥
rājan śṛṇu mahādevyā māyayā mohitā janāḥ ।
svātmānam aviditvaiva vyartha śocanti sarvadā ॥ 49 ॥

rājan — O king, śṛṇu — listen, mahādevyā — by Mahadevi, māyayā — by illusion, mohitāḥ — deluded, janāḥ — people, svātmānam — their self, aviditvā — not knowing, eva — indeed, vyartha — uselessly, śocanti — they lament, sarvadā — always.
"O king, listen. Deluded by Mahadevi's illusion, people always lament uselessly without knowing their self."
यावन्न विदितं स्वात्मसत्तत्वं तावदेव वै ।
जनाः शोचन्ति विज्ञाय भूयः शोचन्ति न क्वचित्‌ ॥ ५० ॥
yāvan na viditaṁ svātma-sattattvaṁ tāvad eva vai ।
janāḥ śocanti vijñāya bhūyaḥ śocanti na kvacit ॥ 50 ॥

yāvat — until, na — not, viditam — known, svātma-sat-tattvam — true essence of self, tāvat — until then, eva — indeed, vai — certainly, janāḥ — people, śocanti — lament, vijñāya — knowing, bhūyaḥ — again, śocanti — lament, na — not, kvacit — anywhere.
"Until the true essence of the self is known, people certainly lament. Knowing it, they do not lament anywhere again."
यथा निद्रामोहितात्मा स्वमविज्ञाय शोचति ।
ऐन्द्रजालिकमन्त्रोत्थमायया मोहितो नरः ॥ ५१ ॥
yathā nidrā-mohitātmā svam avijñāya śocati ।
aindra-jālika-mantra-utthamāyayā mohito naraḥ ॥ 51 ॥

yathā — just as, nidrā-mohita-ātmā — self deluded by sleep, svam — self, avijñāya — not knowing, śocati — laments, aindra-jālika-mantra-uttham — created by a magician's spell, māyayā — by illusion, mohitaḥ — deluded, naraḥ — man.
"Just as oneself deluded by sleep laments without knowing itself, a man deluded by a magician's spell laments by illusion."
तत्प्रकल्पितसर्पादिभीत्या यद्वद्धि शोचति ।
तथैव मायया मुग्धः स्वमज्ञात्वा प्रशोचति ॥ ५२ ॥
tat-prakalpita-sarpa-ādi-bhītyā yad vad dhi śocati ।
tathaiva māyayā mugdhaḥ svam ajñātvā praśocati ॥ 52 ॥

tat-prakalpita — created by that, sarpa-ādi — snake, bhītyā — by fear, yadvat — as, hi — indeed, śocati — laments, tathā — thus, eva — indeed, māyayā — by illusion, mugdhaḥ — deluded, svam — self, ajñātvā — not knowing, praśocati — laments.
"Just as one laments by the fear of a snake created by illusion, thus, deluded by illusion, one laments without knowing oneself."
यथा स्वप्नात्‌ प्रबुद्धो वा ज्ञातैन्द्रजालिकागमः ।
न शोचति क्वचिच्चान्यान्‌ शुचायुक्तान्‌ हसत्यपि ॥ ५३ ॥
yathā svapnāt prabuddho vā jñātā-indra-jālika-āgamaḥ ।
na śocati kvacit ca anyān śucā-yuktān hasati api ॥ 53 ॥

yathā — just as, svapnāt — from a dream, prabuddhaḥ — awakened, vā — or, jñātā — known, indra-jālika-āgamaḥ — magician's spell, na — not, śocati — laments, kvacit — anywhere, ca — and, anyān — others, śucā-yuktān — in grief, hasati — laughs, api — also.
"Just as one awakened from a dream or knowing a magician's spell does not lament anywhere and laughs at others in grief."
एवं स्वात्मविदो मायामुक्ताः शोचन्ति न क्वचित्‌ ।
शोचतस्त्वादृशान्‌ मायामूढान्‌ प्रविहसन्ति च ॥ ५४ ॥
evaṁ svātma-vido māyā-muktāḥ śocanti na kvacit ।
śocatāḥ tvā-adṛśān māyā-mūḍhān pravihasanti ca ॥ 54 ॥

evaṁ — thus, svātma-vidaḥ — knowers of the self, māyā-muktāḥ — freed from illusion, śocanti — lament, na kvacit — not anywhere, śocatāḥ — those who lament, tvā-adṛśān — like you, māyā-mūḍhān — deluded by illusion, pravihasanti — laugh, ca — and.
"Thus, knowers of the self, freed from illusion, do not lament anywhere and laugh at those like you deluded by illusion."
तत्‌ त्वं विज्ञायात्मतत्त्वं मायामुत्तीर्य दुर्गमाम्‌ ।
जहि शोकं महाबाहो मोहोत्थं सद्विमर्शनात्‌ ॥ ५५॥
tat tvaṁ vijñāya ātma-tattvaṁ māyām uttīrya durgamām ।
jahi śokaṁ mahābāho mohotthaṁ sad-vimarśanāt ॥ 55 ॥

tat — that, tvam — you, vijñāya — knowing, ātma-tattvam — true essence of self, māyām — illusion, uttīrya — crossing, durgamām — difficult, jahi — destroy, śokam — grief, mahābāho — O mighty-armed, mohottham — arising from delusion, sad-vimarśanāt — from true reflection.
"Knowing the true essence of the self, crossing the difficult illusion, destroy grief arising from delusion through true reflection, O mighty-armed one."
इत्युक्तः पुनरप्याह महासेनो मुनोश्वरम्‌ ।
भगवन्‌ यस्त्वया प्रोक्तो दृष्टान्तो विषमः स हि ॥ ५६॥
ityuktaḥ punarapyāha mahāseno munīśvaram ।
bhagavan yastvayā prokto dṛṣṭānto viṣamaḥ sa hi ॥ 56 ॥

iti — thus, uktaḥ — addressed, punaḥ api — again, āha — said, mahāsenaḥ — Mahasena, munīśvaram — to the sage, bhagavan — O lord, yaḥ — which, tvayā — by you, proktaḥ — stated, dṛṣṭāntaḥ — example, viṣamaḥ — difficult, saḥ — that, hi — indeed.
Thus addressed, Mahasena again said to the sage, "O lord, the example you stated is indeed difficult."
स्वाप्नो वा मायिको वापि शून्यात्मा भासते परम्‌ ।
अयं जाग्रत्प्रपञ्चस्तु सत्यः सर्वार्थसाधकः ॥ ५७ ॥
svāpno vā māyiko vāpi śūnyātmā bhāsate param ।
ayaṁ jāgrat-prapañcas tu satyaḥ sarvārtha-sādhakaḥ ॥ 57 ॥

svāpnaḥ — dream, vā — or, māyikaḥ — illusory, vā api — or even, śūnya-ātmā — having a void nature, bhāsate — appears, param — perfectly, ayam — this, jāgrat-prapañcaḥ — waking world, tu — but, satyaḥ — real, sarva-artha-sādhakaḥ — fulfilling all purposes.
"The dream or illusory world appears to have a void nature, but this waking world is real and fulfills all purposes."
अबाधितः स्थिरश्चापि कथं स्वाप्नसमो भवेत्‌ ।
इत्युक्तः पुनराचख्यौ मुनिपुत्रोऽतिबुद्धिमान्‌ ॥ ५८ ॥
abādhitaḥ sthiraś cāpi kathaṁ svāpna-samo bhavet ।
ityuktaḥ punarācakhyau muni-putro'ti-buddhimān ॥ 58 ॥

abādhitaḥ — uncontradicted, sthiraḥ — stable, ca api — and also, katham — how, svāpna-samaḥ — like a dream, bhavet — be, iti — thus, uktaḥ — addressed, punaḥ — again, ācakhyau — explained, muni-putraḥ — sage's son, ati-buddhimān — very wise.
"How can the uncontradicted and stable waking world be like a dream?" Thus addressed, the very wise sage's son again explained.
शृणु राजन्‌ यत्त्वयोक्तं दृष्टान्तो विषमस्त्विति ।
एष मोहो द्वितीयस्ते स्वप्ने स्वाप्नस्य यादृशः ॥ ५९ ॥
śṛṇu rājan yat tvayoktaṁ dṛṣṭānto viṣamas tv iti ।
eṣa moho dvitīyas te svapne svāpnasya yādṛśaḥ ॥ 59 ॥

śṛṇu — listen, rājan — O king, yat — what, tvayā — by you, uktaṁ — stated, dṛṣṭāntaḥ — example, viṣamaḥ — difficult, tu — indeed, iti — thus, eṣaḥ — this, mohaḥ — delusion, dvitīyaḥ — second, te — your, svapne — in a dream, svāpnasya — of the dream, yādṛśaḥ — as.
"Listen, O king, to what you stated, that the example is difficult. This is your second delusion, like a dream within a dream."
स्वाप्नवृक्षोऽपि तत्काले कि न साधयते हितम्‌ ।
पान्थानां किं न हरति तापं छायाप्रदानतः ॥ ६० ॥
svāpna-vṛkṣo'pi tat kāle ki na sādhayate hitam ।
pānthānāṁ ki na harati tāpaṁ chāyā-pradānataḥ ॥ 60 ॥

svāpna-vṛkṣaḥ — dream tree, api — even, tat kāle — at that time, kim — does not, na sādhayate — accomplish, hitam — benefit, pānthānāṁ — for travelers, kim — does not, na harati — remove, tāpam — heat, chāyā-pradānataḥ — by providing shade.
"Does not even a dream tree at that time provide benefit to travelers and remove their heat by providing shade?"
फलाद्यैः स्वाप्नमर्त्यादीन्न तर्पयति किं वद ।
स्वप्ने क्व बाधितः स्वाप्नः कवास्थिरश्चोपलक्षितः ॥ ६१ ॥
phalādyaiḥ svāpna-martyādīn na tarpayati kiṁ vada ।
svapne kva bādhitaḥ svāpnaḥ kava-sthiraś copalakṣitaḥ ॥ 61 ॥

phalādyaiḥ — by fruits and others, svāpna-martyādīn — dream and mortal beings, na — not, tarpayati — satisfies, kiṁ — why, vada — speak, svapne — in a dream, kva — where, bādhitaḥ — obstructed, svāpnaḥ — dream-like, kava-sthiraḥ — stable, ca — and, upalakṣitaḥ — observed.
"Does the dream satisfy the dream and mortal beings by fruits and others? Where is the obstruction in the dream, and how is it observed as stable?"
अखिलं बाधितं जाग्रद्दशायामिति चेच्छृणु ।
जाग्रत्प्रपञ्चोऽपि सर्वः सुषुप्तौ किं न बाधितः ॥ ६२ ॥
akhilaṁ bādhitaṁ jāgrad-daśāyām iti cechṛṇu ।
jāgrat-prapañco'pi sarvaḥ suṣuptau kiṁ na bādhitaḥ ॥ 62 ॥

akhilaṁ — entire, bādhitaṁ — obstructed, jāgrad-daśāyām — in the waking state, iti — thus, cet — if, śṛṇu — listen, jāgrat-prapañcaḥ — waking world, api — also, sarvaḥ — entire, suṣuptau — in deep sleep, kiṁ na — is not, bādhitaḥ — obstructed.
"If you say the entire dream is obstructed in the waking state, listen: is not the entire waking world obstructed in deep sleep?"
न बाधितः परदिनेऽप्यनुवृत्तेस्तथेति चेत्‌ ।
स्वाप्नस्यापि परदिने नानुवृत्तिः क्व वा वद ॥ ६३ ॥
na bādhitaḥ paradine'py anuvṛtteḥ tatheti cet ।
svāpnasya api paradine nānuvṛttiḥ kva vā vada ॥ 63 ॥

na — not, bādhitaḥ — obstructed, paradine — next day, api — also, anuvṛtteḥ — continuation, tathā — thus, iti — so, cet — if, svāpnasya — of the dream, api — also, paradine — next day, na — not, anuvṛttiḥ — continuation, kva — where, vā — or, vada — speak.
"If you say it is not obstructed the next day due to continuation, then where is the continuation of the dream the next day?"
नानुवृत्तिर्भाति स्वप्ने इति चेन्नृपते शृणु ।
जाग्रत्यपि क्वानुवृत्तिभासो नव्यावभासके ॥ ६४ ॥
nānu-vṛttiḥ bhāti svapne iti cet nṛpate śṛṇu ।
jāgrati api kva anuvṛtti-bhāsaḥ navya-avabhāsake ॥ 64 ॥

na anuvṛttiḥ — no continuation, bhāti — appears, svapne — in a dream, iti — thus, cet — if, nṛpate — O king, śṛṇu — listen, jāgrati — in waking, api — also, kva — where, anuvṛtti-bhāsaḥ — appearance of continuation, navya-avabhāsake — in the new experience.
"If you say there is no continuation in the dream, O king, listen: where is the appearance of continuation in the new experience in waking?"
नव्येऽनुवृत्त्यभानेऽपि भात्यन्यत्रेति चेच्छृणु ।
तथा स्वप्नेऽपि भात्येवानुवृत्तिः स्थिरभासने ॥ ६५ ॥
navye anuvṛtti-abhāne api bhāti anyatra iti cet śṛṇu ।
tathā svapne api bhāti eva anuvṛttiḥ sthira-bhāsane ॥ 65 ॥

navye — in new, anuvṛtti-abhāne — in non-continuation, api — also, bhāti — appears, anyatra — elsewhere, iti — thus, cet — if, śṛṇu — listen, tathā — thus, svapne — in the dream, api — also, bhāti — appears, eva — indeed, anuvṛttiḥ — continuation, sthira-bhāsane — in stable appearance.
"If you say the continuation appears elsewhere in the new experience, listen: thus, in the dream, too, the continuation appears indeed in the stable appearance."
मृषानुवृत्तिस्तत्रेति चेज्जाग्रत्यपि सा तथा ।
सुक्ष्मबुद्धया विमृश तद्वस्तु जाग्रति संस्थितम्‌ ॥ ६६ ॥
mṛṣā-anuvṛttiḥ tatra iti cet jāgrati api sā tathā ।
sūkṣma-buddhyā vimṛśa tad vastu jāgrati saṁsthitam ॥ 66 ॥

mṛṣā-anuvṛttiḥ — false continuation, tatra — there, iti — thus, cet — if, jāgrati — in waking, api — also, sā — that, tathā — thus, sūkṣma-buddhyā — with subtle intellect, vimṛśa — consider, tat — that, vastu — thing, jāgrati — in waking, saṁsthitam — established.
"If you say there is false continuation in the dream, thus, in waking, too, it is so. Consider with a subtle intellect that thing established in waking."
देहवृक्षनदीदीपादिकं क्षणविभेदितम्‌ ।
कथं तदनुवृत्तिर्वै भवेदवितथात्मिका ॥ ६७ ॥
deha-vṛkṣa-nadī-dīpa-ādikaṁ kṣaṇa-vibheditam ।
kathaṁ tat anuvṛttiḥ vai bhavet avitathā-ātmikā ॥ 67 ॥

"The body, tree, river, lamp, and so on are momentarily different. How can that continuation indeed be of true essence?"

रूपमस्ति सर्वदैव निर्झरैर्भेदितात्मनाम्‌ ॥ ६८ ॥
acalānām api nahi dvitīya-kṣaṇa-saṅgatam ।
rūpam asti sarvadā eva nirjharaiḥ bhedita-ātmanām ॥ 68 ॥

acalānām — of immovable things, api — even, nahi — not, dvitīya-kṣaṇa-saṅgatam — connected to the next moment, rūpam — form, asti — is, sarvadā — always, eva — indeed, nirjharaiḥ — by streams, bhedita-ātmanām — fragmented essence.
"Even immovable things are not connected to the next moment; their form is always fragmented by streams."
मूषकैरुपदीकाभिः सूकरैर्निर्झरादिभिः ।
सर्वतस्तु विभिद्यन्ते पर्वताः सर्वदैव हि ॥ ६९ ॥
mūṣakaiḥ upadīkābhiḥ sūkaraiḥ nirjharādibhiḥ ।
sarvataḥ tu vibhidyante parvatāḥ sarvadā eva hi ॥ 69 ॥

mūṣakaiḥ — by mice, upadīkābhiḥ — by insects, sūkaraiḥ — by boars, nirjharādibhiḥ — by streams and others, sarvataḥ — from all sides, tu — indeed, vibhidyante — fragmented, parvatāḥ — mountains, sarvadā — always, eva — indeed, hi — certainly.
"Mountains are always fragmented by mice, insects, boars, streams, and others from all sides."
पर्वताम्बुधिभूमुख्या अप्येवं क्षणभेदिनः ।
अथ ते सम्प्रवक्षयामि पश्य सूक्ष्मधिया नृप ॥ ७० ॥
parvata-ambudhi-bhū-mukhyā api evaṁ kṣaṇa-bhedinaḥ ।
atha te sampravakṣayāmi paśya sūkṣma-dhiyā nṛpa ॥ 70 ॥

"Mountains, oceans, and the earth even are momentarily changing. Now I will explain to you; observe with a subtle intellect, O king."

अपरिच्छिन्नाऽनुवृत्तिः कार्येष्वत्यन्तदुर्लभा ॥ ७१ ॥
paricchinna-anuvṛttiḥ hi sama-iva svāpna-jāgratoḥ ।
aparicchinnā-anuvṛttiḥ kāryeṣu atyanta-durlabhā ॥ 71 ॥

"The limited continuation in dreams and waking is indeed the same, while the unlimited continuation in actions is extremely rare."

इति चेत्‌ कारणं रूपं पृथिव्यादिमयं किल ॥ ७२ ॥
anuvṛttiḥ kāraṇena rūpeṇa asti hi sarvadā ।
iti cet kāraṇaṁ rūpaṁ pṛthivy-ādi-mayaṁ kila ॥ 72 ॥

anuvṛttiḥ — continuation, kāraṇena — by cause, rūpeṇa — in form, asti — is, hi — indeed, sarvadā — always, iti — thus, cet — if, kāraṇaṁ — cause, rūpaṁ — form, pṛthivy-ādi-mayaṁ — consisting of earth and others, kila — certainly.
"Continuation always exists by cause and form. If so, the cause is certainly consisting of earth and others."
तच्चानुवृत्तं स्वप्नेऽपि पृथिन्यादेर्हि भासनात्‌ ।
अथ स्वाप्नस्य बाधो हि जाग्रति ह्यनुभूयते ॥ ७३ ॥
tat ca anuvṛttaṁ svapne api pṛthivī-ādeḥ hi bhāsanāt ।
atha svāpnasya bādhaḥ hi jāgrati hi anubhūyate ॥ 73 ॥

tat — that, ca — and, anuvṛttaṁ — continued, svapne — in dream, api — also, pṛthivī-ādeḥ — of earth and others, hi — indeed, bhāsanāt — due to appearance, atha — now, svāpnasya — of the dream, bādhaḥ — obstruction, hi — indeed, jāgrati — in waking, hi — indeed, anubhūyate — experienced.
"That continuation is also observed in the dream due to the appearance of earth and others. Now, the obstruction of the dream is experienced in waking."
न जागरस्य बाधस्तु भासते कस्यचित्‌ क्वचित्‌ ।
इति चेच्छृणु वक्ष्यामि बाधो ह्यनवभासनम्‌ ॥ ७४ ॥
na jāgarasya bādhaḥ tu bhāsate kasyacit kvacit ।
iti cet śṛṇu vakṣyāmi bādhaḥ hi anavabhāsanam ॥ 74 ॥

na — not, jāgarasya — of waking, bādhaḥ — obstruction, tu — indeed, bhāsate — appears, kasyacit — to anyone, kvacit — anywhere, iti — thus, cet — if, śṛṇu — listen, vakṣyāmi — I will explain, bādhaḥ — obstruction, hi — indeed, anavabhāsanam — non-appearance.
"The obstruction of waking does not appear to anyone anywhere. If so, listen, I will explain: obstruction is indeed non-appearance."
सुषुप्तौ सर्वजगतोऽप्यनुभूतं ह्यभासनम्‌ ।
अथ बाधो ह्यप्रमाणदर्शनं चेत्तदा शृणु ॥ ७५ ॥
suṣuptau sarva-jagataḥ api anubhūtaṁ hi abhāsanam ।
atha bādhaḥ hi apramāṇa-darśanaṁ cet tadā śṛṇu ॥ 75 ॥

suṣuptau — in deep sleep, sarva-jagataḥ — of the entire world, api — also, anubhūtaṁ — experienced, hi — indeed, abhāsanam — non-appearance, atha — now, bādhaḥ — obstruction, hi — indeed, apramāṇa-darśanam — absence of perception, cet — if, tadā — then, śṛṇu — listen.
"In deep sleep, the non-appearance of the entire world is experienced. Now, if obstruction is indeed the absence of perception, then listen."
अप्रमाणदृशिर्नास्ति भ्रान्तानां त्वादृशां खलु ।
ज्ञातविज्ञेयतत्त्वानामप्रमाणदुशिः स्फुटा ॥ ७६ ॥
apramāṇa-dṛśiḥ na asti bhrāntānāṁ tu ādr̥śāṁ khalu ।
jñāta-vijñeya-tattvānām apramāṇa-duśiḥ sphuṭā ॥ 76 ॥

"The absence of perception does not exist for the deluded like you, indeed. For those who know the truth, the absence of perception is clear."
तस्मादिदं दृश्यजालं स्वाप्नदृश्यसमस्थिति ।
दीर्घकालोऽपि च स्वप्ने भासते निर्विशेषतः ॥ ७७ ॥
tasmād idaṁ dṛśya-jālaṁ svāpna-dṛśya-samasthiti ।
dīrgha-kālaḥ api ca svapne bhāsate nirviśeṣataḥ ॥ 77 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, idaṁ — this, dṛśya-jālaṁ — network of perceptions, svāpna-dṛśya-sama-sthiti — same state as dream perception, dīrgha-kālaḥ — long duration, api — also, ca — and, svapne — in the dream, bhāsate — appears, nirviśeṣataḥ — without distinction.
"Therefore, this network of perceptions is in the same state as dream perception. A long duration appears in the dream without distinction."

स्वाप्नभावस्तेन तुल्यो जाग्रद्भावोऽपि सर्वशः ॥ ७८ ॥
tasmāt abādhitaḥ hi artha-kriyā-kārī sthiraḥ api ca ।
svāpna-bhāvaḥ tena tulyo jāgrad-bhāvaḥ api sarvaśaḥ ॥ 78 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, abādhitaḥ — unobstructed, hi — indeed, artha-kriyā-kārī — functioning, sthiraḥ — stable, api — also, ca — and, svāpna-bhāvaḥ — dream state, tena — by that, tulyo — similar, jāgrad-bhāvaḥ — waking state, api — also, sarvaśaḥ — in every way.
"Therefore, the unobstructed, functioning, and stable dream state is similar to the waking state in every way."

स्वप्नेऽपि जागरत्वं तु गृहीतं तद्वदेव हि ॥ ७९ ॥
yathā jāgrati jāgrat-tvaṁ gṛhītaṁ jāgare sphuṭam ।
svapne api jāgrat-tvaṁ tu gṛhītaṁ tad-vat eva hi ॥ 79 ॥

yathā — as, jāgrati — in waking, jāgrat-tvaṁ — waking state, gṛhītaṁ — grasped, jāgare — in waking, sphuṭam — clearly, svapne — in the dream, api — also, jāgrat-tvaṁ — waking state, tu — indeed, gṛhītaṁ — grasped, tad-vat — like that, eva — indeed, hi — indeed.
"As the waking state is clearly grasped in waking, the waking state is also grasped in the dream like that."
एवं स्थिते कुतो राजन्‌ विशेषः स्वप्नजाग्रतोः ।
तत्स्वाप्नान्निजबन्धूंस्त्वं नहि शोचसि वै कुतः ॥ ८० ॥
evaṁ sthite kuto rājan viśeṣaḥ svapna-jāgratoḥ ।
tat svāpnān nija-bandhūn tvaṁ nahi śocasi vai kutaḥ ॥ 80 ॥

evaṁ — thus, sthite — established, kutaḥ — where, rājan — O king, viśeṣaḥ — distinction, svapna-jāgratoḥ — between dream and waking, tat — then, svāpnān — dream, nija-bandhūn — own relatives, tvaṁ — you, nahi — not, śocasi — you grieve, vai — indeed, kutaḥ — why.
"Thus established, where is the distinction, O king, between dream and waking? Then, why do you not grieve for your own relatives in the dream?"

शून्यताभावनेनापि शून्यं निष्प्रतिघं भवेत्‌ ॥ ८१ ॥
kevalaṁ bhāvanā-mātrāt satyatā jagati sthitā ।
śūnyatā-bhāvanena api śūnyaṁ niṣpratiṣṭhaṁ bhavet ॥ 81 ॥

kevalam — only, bhāvanā-mātrāt — by mere thought, satyatā — reality, jagati — in the world, sthitā — established, śūnyatā-bhāvanena — by thought of emptiness, api — also, śūnyam — emptiness, niṣpratiṣṭhaṁ — without resistance, bhavet — becomes.
"In this world, reality is established by mere thought. By thinking of emptiness, it also becomes emptiness without resistance."

भवेत्तदात्मभावेन सत्यमेतद्‌ महीपते ॥ ८२ ॥
bhāvanā hyapramāṇatva-vaidhuryeṇa sthirīkṛtā ।
bhavet tadātma-bhāvena satyam etad mahīpate ॥ 82 ॥

bhāvanā — thought, hi — indeed, apramāṇatva-vaidhuryeṇa — by absence of validation, sthirīkṛtā — stabilized, bhavet — becomes, tad-ātma-bhāvena — by its own nature, satyam — truth, etad — this, mahīpate — O king.
"Indeed, thought stabilized by the absence of validation becomes the truth by its own nature, O king."
निदर्शनं त्वत्र चेदं मज्जगद्‌ दृष्टमेव ते ।
इमं शैलं परिक्रम्य चैहि पश्याव सम्प्रति ॥ ८३ ॥
nidarśanaṁ tvatra cedaṁ maj-jagad dṛṣṭam eva te ।
imaṁ śailaṁ parikramya ca ehi paśyāva samprati ॥ 83 ॥

"Indeed, if you have seen my world as an example here, after circumambulating this mountain, come, and we shall see it now."

परिक्रम्य गण्डशैलं राज्ञा सह समेत्य तु ॥ ८४ ॥
ity uktvā nṛpatiṁ haste gṛhītvā paricakrame ।
parikramya gaṇḍa-śailaṁ rājñā saha sametya tu ॥ 84 ॥

iti — thus, uktvā — having said, nṛpatim — the king, haste — by hand, gṛhītvā — taking, paricakrame — circumambulated, parikramya — having circumambulated, gaṇḍa-śailam — the mountain, rājñā — with the king, saha — together, sametya — arriving, tu — indeed.
Thus having said, he took the king by hand and circumambulated the mountain, arriving there together with the king.
पुनः प्राह महासेनं मेधावी मुनिनन्दनः ।
राजन्‌ दृष्ट एष शैलः पादगव्यूतिमात्रकः ॥ ८५ ॥
punaḥ prāha mahāsenaṁ medhāvī muni-nandanaḥ ।
rājan dṛṣṭa eṣa śailaḥ pāda-gavyūti-mātrakaḥ ॥ 85 ॥

punaḥ — again, prāha — spoke, mahāsenam — to Mahāsena, medhāvī — the wise one, muni-nandanaḥ — the sage’s son, rājan — O king, dṛṣṭaḥ — seen, eṣaḥ — this, śailaḥ — mountain, pāda-gavyūti-mātrakaḥ — extending a couple of miles.
Again, the wise son of the sage spoke to Mahāsena: “O king, see this mountain extending a couple of miles.”
दृष्ट एवास्य गर्भे ते लोकः सुविततः स्फुटः ।
एष जाग्रदुत स्वप्नः सत्यो मिथ्यात्मकोऽपि वा ॥ ८६ ॥
dṛṣṭa evāsya garbhe te lokaḥ suvitataḥ sphuṭaḥ ।
eṣa jāgrad uta svapnaḥ satyo mithyātmako'pi vā ॥ 86 ॥

dṛṣṭaḥ — seen, eva — indeed, asya — in its, garbhe — womb, te — your, lokaḥ — world, suvitataḥ — widely, sphuṭaḥ — clear, eṣaḥ — this, jāgrat — waking, uta — or, svapnaḥ — dream, satyaḥ — true, mithyātmakaḥ — false, api — also, vā — or.
"Indeed, seen in its womb, your world is widely and clearly displayed. Is this waking or a dream, true or false?"
शैललोके यद्‌ दिनैकं तदत्र द्वादशार्बुदाः ।
वत्सरास्त्वनुभूतास्ते सत्यासत्ये विवेचय ॥ ८७ ॥
śaila-loke yad dinaikaṁ tad atra dvādaśārbudāḥ ।
vatsarās tv anubhūtās te satyā-satye vivecaya ॥ 87 ॥

śaila-loke — in the mountain world, yat — that which, dinaikam — one day, tad — that, atra — here, dvādaśa-arbudāḥ — twelve million years, vatsarāḥ — years, tu — indeed, anubhūtāḥ — experienced, te — you, satyā-asatye — true or false, vivecaya — discern.
"In the mountain world, one day is here experienced as twelve million years. Discern whether this is true or false."
विवेचनं नास्य भवेत्‌ स्वप्नयोर्भिन्नयोरिव ।
अस्मादेतद्विद्धि जगद्‌ भावनामात्रसारकम्‌ ॥ ८८ ॥
vivecanaṁ nāsya bhavet svapnayor bhinnayor iva ।
asmād etad viddhi jagad bhāvanā-mātra-sārakam ॥ 88 ॥

vivecanam — distinction, na — not, asya — of this, bhavet — is, svapnayoḥ — between dreams, bhinnayoḥ — different, iva — like, asmāt — from this, etad — this, viddhi — know, jagat — world, bhāvanā-mātra-sārakam — essence of thought alone.
"There is no distinction between this and different dreams. From this, know that the essence of the world is thought alone."
अभाव्यमानं चैतत्तु लीयेत क्षणमात्रतः।
तस्माच्छोकं जहि नृपावेत्य स्वाप्नसमं जगत्‌ ॥ ८९ ॥
abhāvyamānaṁ caitat tu līyeta kṣaṇa-mātrataḥ ।
tasmāc chokaṁ jahi nṛpāv etya svāpna-samaṁ jagat ॥ 89 ॥

abhāvyamānam — unreal, ca — and, etat — this, tu — indeed, līyeta — dissolves, kṣaṇa-mātrataḥ — in a moment, tasmāt — therefore, śokam — grief, jahi — abandon, nṛpa — O king, avetya — understanding, svāpna-samam — like a dream, jagat — the world.
"This unreal world dissolves in a moment. Therefore, abandon grief, O king, understanding that the world is like a dream."
स्वाप्नचित्रभित्तिभूतं स्वात्मानं संविदात्मकम्‌ ।
दर्पणप्रतिमं मत्वा संस्थितोऽसि यथा तथा ॥ ९० ॥
svāpna-citra-bhitti-bhūtaṁ svātmānaṁ saṁvid-ātmakam ।
darpaṇa-pratimaṁ matvā saṁsthito'si yathā tathā ॥ 90 ॥

svāpna-citra-bhitti-bhūtam — dream-picture-wall-like, svātmānam — self, saṁvid-ātmakam — consciousness, darpaṇa-pratimam — mirror-like reflection, matvā — considering, saṁsthitaḥ asi — you are situated, yathā — as, tathā — so.
"Considering yourself as a dream-picture on the wall, consciousness in essence, a reflection like in a mirror, so you are situated."
जाग्रच्चित्रदर्पणं चावेह्यात्मानं चिदात्मकम्‌ ।
परमानन्दितस्वान्तो भव शीघ्रं महीपते ॥ ९१ ॥
jāgrat-citra-darpaṇaṁ cāvehy ātmānaṁ cid-ātmakam ।
paramānandita-svānto bhava śīghraṁ mahīpate ॥ 91 ॥

jāgrat-citra-darpaṇam — waking-picture-mirror, ca — and, avehi — know, ātmānam — self, cid-ātmakam — consciousness in essence, paramānandita-svāntaḥ — supremely blissful in heart, bhava — become, śīghram — quickly, mahīpate — O king.
"Know the waking state as a picture in a mirror, and yourself as consciousness in essence. Become supremely blissful in heart quickly, O king."

colophon.dev: इति श्रीत्रिपुरारहस्ये ज्ञानखण्डे शैललोकदर्शनं नाम त्रयोदशोऽध्यायः ॥
colophon.en: Thus ends the thirteenth chapter named "Observing the World of Shailaloka" in the revered Knowledge Section of Tripura Rahasya.thout resistance."

lines.text: इत्याकर्ण्य मुनिवचो विचार्य शुभया धिया ।
जगत्स्थिति स्वाप्नसमां ज्ञात्वा शोकं जहौ द्रुतम्‌ ॥ १ ॥
ityākarṇya muni-vaco vicārya śubhayā dhiyā ।
jagat-sthiti svāpna-samāṁ jñātvā śokaṁ jahau drutam ॥ 1 ॥

iti — thus, ākarṇya — hearing, muni-vaco — the sage's words, vicārya — considering, śubhayā — auspicious, dhiyā — with intellect, jagat-sthiti — the world's state, svāpna-samām — like a dream, jñātvā — knowing, śokam — sorrow, jahau — abandoned, drutam — quickly.
Hearing the sage's words and considering with an auspicious intellect, he quickly abandoned sorrow, knowing the world's state to be like a dream.
धैर्यमालम्ब्य निःशोको भूयोऽपृच्छन्मुनेः सुतम्‌ ।
मुनिपुत्र महाबुद्धे त्वं परावरदर्शनः ॥ २ ॥
dhairyam ālambya niḥśoko bhūyo'pṛcchan muneḥ sutam ।
muniputra mahābuddhe tvaṁ parāvara-darśanaḥ ॥ 2 ॥

dhairyam — courage, ālambya — taking hold of, niḥśokaḥ — free from sorrow, bhūyaḥ — again, apṛcchan — asked, muneḥ — of the sage, sutam — son, muniputra — son of the sage, mahābuddhe — great intelligence, tvam — you, parāvara-darśanaḥ — seer of the past and future.
Taking hold of courage and free from sorrow, he again asked the sage's son: “O son of the sage, of great intelligence, seer of the past and future.”
न तेऽप्यविदितं किञ्चिन्मन्ये स्यादिति लेशतः ।
पृच्छामि यदहं तन्मे कृपया वक्तुमर्हसि ॥ ३ ॥
na te'py aviditaṁ kiñcin manye syād iti leśataḥ ।
pṛcchāmi yad ahaṁ tan me kṛpayā vaktum arhasi ॥ 3 ॥

na — not, te — to you, api — even, aviditam — unknown, kiñcit — anything, manye — I think, syāt — there is, iti — thus, leśataḥ — even slightly, pṛcchāmi — I ask, yat — what, aham — I, tat — that, me — to me, kṛpayā — kindly, vaktum — to tell, arhasi — you should.
"I think there is nothing unknown to you, even slightly. I ask you, kindly tell me what I inquire about."
भावनाप्रभवं ह्येतत्‌ सर्वं वदसि तत्‌ कथम्‌ ।
मया भूयो भावितं च न बहिः सर्वथा भवेत्‌ ॥ ४ ॥
bhāvanā-prabhavaṁ hy etat sarvaṁ vadasi tat katham ।
mayā bhūyo bhāvitaṁ ca na bahiḥ sarvathā bhavet ॥ 4 ॥

bhāvanā-prabhavam — arising from thought, hi — indeed, etat — this, sarvam — all, vadasi — you say, tat — that, katham — how, mayā — by me, bhūyo — further, bhāvitaṁ — contemplated, ca — and, na — not, bahiḥ — outside, sarvathā — in any way, bhavet — become.
"You say all this arises from thought. How then does what I further contemplate not become external in any way?"
त्वया तु भावनासिद्धया शैले लोकः प्रकल्पितः ।
अथापि देशः कालश्च युगपद्‌ विविधः कथम्‌ ॥ ५ ॥
tvayā tu bhāvanā-siddhayā śaile lokaḥ prakalpitaḥ ।
athāpi deśaḥ kālaś ca yugapad vividhaḥ katham ॥ 5 ॥

tvayā — by you, tu — but, bhāvanā-siddhayā — perfected by thought, śaile — in the mountain, lokaḥ — world, prakalpitaḥ — created, atha api — but also, deśaḥ — place, kālaḥ — time, ca — and, yugapad — simultaneously, vividhaḥ — diverse, katham — how.
"You created the world in the mountain perfected by thought, but also how can place and time be diverse simultaneously?"
तत्रासत्यमन्यतरत्‌ कतमं तन्ममेरय ।
इति पृष्टो मुनिसुतः प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमे ॥ ६ ॥
tatra asatyam anyatarat katamaṁ tan me meraya ।
iti pṛṣṭo muni-sutaḥ pravaktum upacakrame ॥ 6 ॥

tatra — there, asatyam — untrue, anyatarat — one of the two, katamam — which, tat — that, me — to me, meraya — reveal, iti — thus, pṛṣṭaḥ — asked, muni-sutaḥ — the sage's son, pravaktum — to explain, upacakrame — began.
"Which of the two there is untrue? Reveal that to me. Thus asked, the sage's son began to explain."
सङ्कल्पो भावना प्रोक्ता सिद्धाऽसिद्धेति सा द्विधा ।
सिद्धिर्विकल्पाऽसम्भेदो विकल्पस्त्वेकनिष्ठितेः ॥ ७ ॥
saṅkalpo bhāvanā proktā siddhā-asiddheti sā dvidhā ।
siddhir vikalpa-asambhedo vikalpas tv ekaniṣṭhiteḥ ॥ 7 ॥

saṅkalpaḥ — intention, bhāvanā — thought, proktā — said, siddhā-asiddhā — accomplished or unaccomplished, iti — thus, sā — it, dvidhā — twofold, siddhiḥ — accomplishment, vikalpa-asambhedaḥ — absence of alternatives, vikalpaḥ — alternative, tu — but, ekaniṣṭhiteḥ — of fixed purpose.
"Intention and thought are said to be twofold: accomplished or unaccomplished. Accomplishment is the absence of alternatives, but unaccomplishment is due to fixed purpose on an alternative."
ब्रह्मभावनया पश्य जातं जगदिदं ननु ।
एतत्‌ सर्वैः सत्यरूपं भावितं सुदृढत्वतः ॥ ८ ॥
brahma-bhāvanayā paśya jātaṁ jagad idaṁ nanu ।
etat sarvaiḥ satya-rūpaṁ bhāvitaṁ sudṛḍhatvataḥ ॥ 8 ॥

brahma-bhāvanayā — by thought of Brahman, paśya — see, jātam — born, jagat — world, idam — this, nanu — indeed, etat — this, sarvaiḥ — by all, satya-rūpam — as real, bhāvitaṁ — thought, sudṛḍhatvataḥ — firmly.
"See this world, born by thought of Brahman. Indeed, this is thought by all as real, firmly."
तथा स्वसङ्कल्पभवे नास्ति कस्यापि भावना ।
विकल्पसम्भेद एषोऽसिद्धा तस्माद्विभावना ॥ ९ ॥
tathā sva-saṅkalpa-bhave nāsti kasyāpi bhāvanā ।
vikalpa-sambheda eṣo'siddhā tasmād vibhāvanā ॥ 9 ॥

tathā — similarly, sva-saṅkalpa-bhave — in one's own intention, na — not, asti — is, kasyāpi — of anyone, bhāvanā — thought, vikalpa-sambhedaḥ — alternative division, eṣaḥ — this, asiddhā — unaccomplished, tasmāt — therefore, vibhāvanā — diverse thought.
"Similarly, in one's own intention, there is no thought by anyone. This division of alternatives leads to unaccomplishment; therefore, it is diverse thought."
भावनायाः सिद्धिरत्र बहुधा संस्थिता भवेत्‌ ।
जन्मना मणिना तद्वदौषधेन च योगतः ॥ १० ॥
bhāvanāyāḥ siddhir atra bahudhā saṁsthitā bhavet ।
janmanā maṇinā tadvad auṣadhena ca yogataḥ ॥ 10 ॥

bhāvanāyāḥ — of thought, siddhiḥ — accomplishment, atra — here, bahudhā — in many ways, saṁsthitā — established, bhavet — is, janmanā — by birth, maṇinā — by gem, tadvat — similarly, auṣadhena — by herb, ca — and, yogataḥ — by yoga.
"The accomplishment of thought is established here in many ways: by birth, by gem, similarly by herb, and by yoga."
तपसा मन्त्रसिद्धया च वरेण च भवेन्नृप ।
जन्मना ब्रह्मणः सा वै मणिना यक्षरक्षसाम्‌ ॥ ११ ॥
tapasā mantra-siddhayā ca vareṇa ca bhaven nṛpa ।
janmanā brahmaṇaḥ sā vai maṇinā yakṣa-rakṣasām ॥ 11 ॥

tapasā — by austerity, mantra-siddhayā — by mantra accomplishment, ca — and, vareṇa — by boon, ca — also, bhavet — is, nṛpa — O king, janmanā — by birth, brahmaṇaḥ — in Brahmanas, sā — that, vai — indeed, maṇinā — by gem, yakṣa-rakṣasām — in Yakshas and Rakshasas.
"By austerity, by mantra accomplishment, and by boon, O king, it is indeed by birth in Brahmanas, by gem in Yakshas and Rakshasas."
औषधेन तु देवानां योगिनां योगतो भवेत्‌ ।
तपसा तापसानां सा मान्त्रिकाणां तु मन्त्रतः ॥ १२ ॥
auṣadhena tu devānāṁ yogināṁ yogato bhavet ।
tapasā tāpasānāṁ sā māntrikāṇāṁ tu mantrataḥ ॥ 12 ॥

auṣadhena — by herb, tu — but, devānām — of gods, yoginām — of yogis, yogataḥ — by yoga, bhavet — is, tapasā — by austerity, tāpasānām — of ascetics, sā — that, māntrikāṇām — of those with mantras, tu — but, mantrataḥ — by mantra.
"But by herb, in gods, by yoga, of yogis, it is by austerity of ascetics, and by mantra of those with mantras."
विश्वकर्ममुखानां च वरप्राप्त्या हि साऽभवत्‌ ।
सङ्कल्पितं तथा भाव्यं पूर्वविस्मरणे सति ॥ १३ ॥
viśvakarma-mukhānāṁ ca vara-prāptyā hi sābhavat ।
saṅkalpitaṁ tathā bhāvyaṁ pūrva-vismaraṇe sati ॥ 13 ॥

viśvakarma-mukhānām — of Vishvakarma and others, ca — and, vara-prāptyā — by boon attainment, hi — indeed, sā — that, abhavat — became, saṅkalpitam — intended, tathā — similarly, bhāvyaṁ — to be thought, pūrva-vismaraṇe — in previous forgetting, sati — being.
"Of Vishvakarma and others, by boon attainment, it indeed became intended, similarly to be thought accomplished, by forgetting the past."
स्थिरं तावद्भवत्येव यावत्‌ पूर्वं नहि स्मरेत्‌ ।
एवमेव निर्विकल्पभावना यदि सुस्थिरा ॥ १४ ॥
sthiraṁ tāvad bhavaty eva yāvat pūrvaṁ nahi smaret ।
evam eva nirvikalpa-bhāvanā yadi susthirā ॥ 14 ॥

sthiraṁ — stable, tāvat — then, bhavati — becomes, eva — indeed, yāvat — until, pūrvam — previous, nahi — not, smaret — remembers, evam — thus, eva — indeed, nirvikalpa-bhāvanā — non-dual thought, yadi — if, susthirā — stable.
"Then the thought becomes stable, indeed until the previous is not remembered. Thus, indeed, non-dual thought if stable."
अनिच्छया विकल्पस्य यावत्‌ सम्भेदनं नहि ।
तावत्‌ सा भावना सिद्धा साधयेद्वै महाफलम्‌ ॥ १५ ॥
anicchayā vikalpasya yāvat sambhedanaṁ nahi ।
tāvat sā bhāvanā siddhā sādhayed vai mahāphalam ॥ 15 ॥

anicchayā — without desire, vikalpasya — of alternative, yāvat — until, sambhedanam — division, nahi — not, tāvat — then, sā — that, bhāvanā — thought, siddhā — accomplished, sādhayet — achieves, vai — indeed, mahāphalam — great result.
"Without desire, until it is not divided by alternatives, then that thought, indeed is accomplished, and achieves a great result."
सम्भेदात्तु विकल्पेन न सिद्धा तव भावना ।
भावनां साधय क्षिप्रं यदि स्त्रष्टुं समीहसि ॥ १६ ॥
sambhedāt tu vikalpena na siddhā tava bhāvanā ।
bhāvanāṁ sādhaya kṣipraṁ yadi sraṣṭuṁ samīhasi ॥ 16 ॥
