sambhedāt — from division, tu — but, vikalpena — by alternative, na — not, siddhā — accomplished, tava — your, bhāvanā — thought, bhāvanām — thought, sādhaya — accomplish, kṣipram — quickly, yadi — if, sraṣṭum — to create, samīhasi — you desire.
"From division, due to alternatives, your thought is not accomplished. Accomplish the thought quickly if you desire to create."
शृणु राजन्‌ देशकालद्वैविध्यं वदतो मम ।
अव्युत्पन्नोऽसि लोकस्य व्यवहारे ततस्तव ॥ १७ ॥
śṛṇu rājan deśa-kāla-dvaividhyaṁ vadataḥ mama ।
avyutpanno'si lokasya vyavahāre tatas tava ॥ 17 ॥

śṛṇu — listen, rājan — O king, deśa-kāla-dvaividhyam — duality of place and time, vadataḥ — speaking, mama — my, avyutpannaḥ — unaffected, asi — you are, lokasya — of the world, vyavahāre — transactions, tataḥ — therefore, tava — your.
"Listen, O king, to my speaking of the duality of place and time, You see, you are unaffected by the world's transactions, therefore…"
एतच्चित्रं भासते वै शृणु सम्यग्‌ ब्रवीमि ते ।
जगद्भावस्वभावोऽयं विविधत्वेन भासनम्‌ ॥ १८ ॥
etat citraṁ bhāsate vai śṛṇu samyag bravīmi te ।
jagad-bhāva-svabhāvo'yaṁ vividhatvena bhāsanam ॥ 18 ॥

etat — this, citram — picture, bhāsate — appears, vai — indeed, śṛṇu — listen, samyak — properly, bravīmi — I speak, te — to you, jagad-bhāva-svabhāvaḥ — nature of the world's being, ayam — this, vividhatvena — by diversity, bhāsanam — appearing.
"This picture of the world appears indeed. Listen properly as I speak to you. This nature of the world's being which appears by diversity."
एक एव हि सूर्यस्य प्रकाशो द्विविधः स्थितः ।
दिवान्धानामन्धकार इतरेषां तु भासकः ॥ १९ ॥
eka eva hi sūryasya prakāśo dvividhaḥ sthitaḥ ।
divāndhānām andhakāra itareṣāṁ tu bhāsakaḥ ॥ 19 ॥

ekaḥ — one, eva — indeed, hi — certainly, sūryasya — of the sun, prakāśaḥ — light, dvividhaḥ — twofold, sthitaḥ — existing, divāndhānām — to the day-blind, andhakāraḥ — darkness, itareṣām — to others, tu — but, bhāsakaḥ — illuminating.
"Indeed, the light of the sun exists as twofold: to the day-blind, it is darkness; but to others, it is illuminating."
जलं मनुष्यपश्वादेः श्वासस्य प्रतिरोधकम्‌ ।
मत्स्यादीनां बहिः श्वासप्रतिरोधो जले नहि ॥ २० ॥
jalaṁ manuṣya-paśv-ādeḥ śvāsasya pratirodhakam ।
matsyādīnāṁ bahiḥ śvāsa-pratirodho jale nahi ॥ 20 ॥

jalaṁ — water, manuṣya-paśu-ādeḥ — of humans and animals, śvāsasya — of breath, pratirodhakam — obstructing, matsya-ādīnām — of fish and others, bahiḥ — outside, śvāsa-pratirodhaḥ — breath obstruction, jale — in water, nahi — not.
"Water obstructs the breath of humans and animals, but for fish and others, there is no breath obstruction in water."
अग्निर्दहति मर्त्यादींस्तं भक्षयति तित्तिरिः ।
वह्निर्नश्यति तोयेन स जले ज्वलति क्वचित्‌ ॥ २१ ॥
agnir dahati martyādīṁs taṁ bhakṣayati tittiriḥ ।
vahnir naśyati toyena sa jale jvalati kvacit ॥ 21 ॥

agnīḥ — fire, dahati — burns, martyādīn — mortals and others, taṁ — that, bhakṣayati — devours, tittiriḥ — water-bird, vahniḥ — fire, naśyati — extinguished, toyena — by water, saḥ — that, jale — in water, jvalati — burns, kvacit — sometimes.
"Fire burns mortals and others, but the water-bird devours that. Fire is extinguished by water, yet it sometimes burns in water."
एवं सर्वे जागतास्तु भावा द्वैरूप्यतः स्थिताः ।
एवं सेन्द्रियवृत्तान्तास्त्वन्ये केऽपि निरिन्द्रियाः ॥ २२ ॥
evaṁ sarve jāgatāstu bhāvā dvairūpyataḥ sthitāḥ ।
evaṁ sendriya-vṛttāntās tv anye ke'pi nirindriyāḥ ॥ 22 ॥

evaṁ — thus, sarve — all, jāgatāḥ — in the world, bhāvāḥ — entities, dvairūpyataḥ — in dual forms, sthitāḥ — existing, evaṁ — thus, sendriya-vṛttāntāḥ — with sensory functions, tu — but, anye — others, ke api — some, nirindriyāḥ — without senses.
"Thus, all entities in the world exist in dual forms. Similarly, some have sensory functions, while others are without senses."
स्वभावतो विरुद्धा वै शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ।
अत्रोपपत्तिं वक्ष्यामि समाहितमनाः शृणु ॥ २३ ॥
svabhāvato viruddhā vai śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ ।
atro papattiṁ vakṣyāmi samāhita-manāḥ śṛṇu ॥ 23 ॥

svabhāvataḥ — by nature, viruddhāḥ — contradictory, vai — indeed, śataśaḥ — in hundreds, atha — also, sahasraśaḥ — in thousands, atra — here, upapattim — explanation, vakṣyāmi — I will explain, samāhita-manāḥ — attentive mind, śṛṇu — listen.
"Indeed, by nature, there are hundreds and thousands of contradictions. Here, I will explain this with an attentive mind, listen."
एते हि चाक्षुषा भावाश्चक्षुर्विकृतिमात्रकाः ।
न चाक्षुषादंशतोऽन्यद्‌ दृश्यमस्ति क्वचिद्‌ बहिः ॥ २४ ॥
ete hi cākṣuṣā bhāvāś cakṣur-vikṛti-mātrakāḥ ।
na cākṣuṣād aṁśato'nyad dṛśyam asti kvacid bahiḥ ॥ 24 ॥

ete — these, hi — indeed, cākṣuṣā — of the eye, bhāvāḥ — objects, cakṣur-vikṛti-mātrakāḥ — mere modifications of the eye, na — not, cākṣuṣāt — from the eye, aṁśataḥ — in part, anyat — other, dṛśyam — visible, asti — is, kvacit — anywhere, bahiḥ — outside.
"These objects, indeed, are mere modifications of the eye. There is nothing else visible anywhere outside of the eye."
यथा पित्तप्रदुष्टाक्षो बहिः पीतं प्रपश्यति ।
यथा तैमिरिकोऽन्यस्तु पश्यत्येकं द्विधा स्थितम्‌ ॥ २५ ॥
yathā pitta-praduṣṭākṣo bahiḥ pītaṁ prapaśyati ।
yathā taimiriko'nyas tu paśyaty ekaṁ dvidhā sthitam ॥ 25 ॥

yathā — as, pitta-praduṣṭa-akṣaḥ — one with jaundiced eyes, bahiḥ — outside, pītam — yellow, prapaśyati — sees, yathā — as, taimirikaḥ — one with cataract, anyaḥ — another, tu — but, paśyati — sees, ekam — one, dvidhā — in two, sthitam — existing.
"As one with jaundiced eyes sees everything as yellow, and another with cataract sees one thing as two."
एवं विचित्रदुष्टाक्षाः पश्यन्ति विविधं जगत्‌ ।
अस्ति पूर्वसमुद्रस्य मध्ये कारण्डकाह्वयः ॥ २६ ॥
evaṁ vicitra-duṣṭākṣāḥ paśyanti vividhaṁ jagat ।
asti pūrva-samudrasya madhye kāraṇḍakāhvayaḥ ॥ 26 ॥

evaṁ — thus, vicitra-duṣṭa-akṣāḥ — with different defective eyes, paśyanti — see, vividham — various, jagat — world, asti — there is, pūrva-samudrasya — of the eastern sea, madhye — in the middle, kāraṇḍaka-āhvayaḥ — named Karandaka.
"Thus, those with different defective eyes see the world in various ways. There is a place named Karandaka in the middle of the eastern sea."
द्वीपस्तत्र जना भावान्‌ रक्तान्‌ पश्यन्ति वै सदा ।
एवं रमणकद्वीपे सदा पश्यन्ति वै जनाः ॥ २७ ॥
dvīpas tatra janā bhāvān raktān paśyanti vai sadā ।
evaṁ ramaṇaka-dvīpe sadā paśyanti vai janāḥ ॥ 27 ॥

dvīpaḥ — island, tatra — there, janāḥ — people, bhāvān — objects, raktān — red, paśyanti — see, vai — indeed, sadā — always, evaṁ — thus, ramaṇaka-dvīpe — in the island of Ramanaka, sadā — always, paśyanti — see, vai — indeed, janāḥ — people.
"There, on the island, people always see objects as red. Similarly, people always see things in the island of Ramanaka."
व्यत्यस्तमूर्ध्वाधरतो निखिलं भावमण्डलम्‌ ।
एवमन्येषु द्वीपेषु विविधं भावमण्डलम्‌ ॥ २८ ॥
vyatyasta-mūrdhvādharato nikhilaṁ bhāva-maṇḍalam ।
evam anyeṣu dvīpeṣu vividhaṁ bhāva-maṇḍalam ॥ 28 ॥

vyatyasta — reversed, mūrdhva-adharataḥ — from top to bottom, nikhilam — entire, bhāva-maṇḍalam — realm of objects, evam — thus, anyeṣu — in other, dvīpeṣu — islands, vividham — various, bhāva-maṇḍalam — realm of objects.
"The entire realm of objects is reversed from top to bottom. Thus, in other islands, the realm of objects is various."
जना नेत्रस्वभावेन पश्यन्ति खलु सर्वदा ।
तत्र तेषामन्यथा तु दृश्यते यदि कुत्रचित्‌ ॥ २९ ॥
janā netra-svabhāvena paśyanti khalu sarvadā ।
tatra teṣām anyathā tu dṛśyate yadi kutracit ॥ 29 ॥

janāḥ — people, netra-svabhāvena — by the nature of the eyes, paśyanti — see, khalu — indeed, sarvadā — always, tatra — there, teṣām — their, anyathā — otherwise, tu — but, dṛśyate — seen, yadi — if, kutracit — somewhere.
"People always see according to the nature of their eyes. There, if anything is seen otherwise, somewhere."
नेत्रं सुसाध्यौषधेन पश्यन्ति प्राग्वदेव हि ।
अतस्तु चक्षुषा यावद्‌ दृश्यते जगतीतले ॥ ३० ॥
netraṁ susādhya-auṣadhena paśyanti prāg-vad eva hi ।
ataḥ tu cakṣuṣā yāvad dṛśyate jagatītale ॥ 30 ॥

netram — eye, susādhya-auṣadhena — by effective medicine, paśyanti — see, prāk-vat — as before, eva — indeed, hi — certainly, ataḥ — thus, tu — but, cakṣuṣā — by the eye, yāvat — as far as, dṛśyate — is seen, jagatītale — on the surface of the earth.
"By effective medicine, the eyes see as before. Thus, whatever is seen on the surface of the earth is seen by the eye."
तावद्‌ भवेच्चाक्षुषोंऽशः पीतवत्‌ पित्तचक्षुषः ।
एवं घ्राणादीन्द्रियाणामंशा गन्धादयोऽपि हि ॥ ३१ ॥
tāvad bhavec cākṣuṣo'ṁśaḥ pīta-vat pitta-cakṣuṣaḥ ।
evaṁ ghrāṇādīndriyāṇām aṁśā gandhādayo'pi hi ॥ 31 ॥

tāvat — as long as, bhavet — is, cākṣuṣaḥ — of the eye, aṁśaḥ — part, pīta-vat — like yellow, pitta-cakṣuṣaḥ — jaundiced eye, evaṁ — thus, ghrāṇa-ādīndriyāṇām — of the sense organs like smell, aṁśāḥ — parts, gandha-ādayaḥ — like smell, api — also, hi — certainly.
"As long as the part of the eye is like yellow, due to jaundiced eyes, similarly the parts of the sense organs like smell and others are too, certainly."
मानसाश्च मनोमात्रास्तथैवाखिलजागताः ।
क्रमोऽप्यक्षस्वभावोत्थ स्ततः किञ्चिद्‌ बहिर्नहि ॥ ३२ ॥
mānasāś ca mano-mātrās tathaivākhila-jāgatāḥ ।
kramaḥ api akṣa-svabhāva-otthaḥ tataḥ kiñcid bahiḥ nahi ॥ 32 ॥

mānasāḥ — mental, ca — and, mano-mātrāḥ — mere mind, tathā — thus, eva — indeed, akhila-jāgatāḥ — entire world, kramaḥ — order, api — also, akṣa-svabhāva-otthaḥ — arising from the nature of the senses, tataḥ — from that, kiñcit — anything, bahiḥ — outside, nahi — not.
"Mental and mere mind is, thus indeed the entire world. The order we see also arises from the nature of the senses, from that, nothing is outside."
शृणु राजन्‌ बहिरिति यल्लोके भाति केवलम्‌ ।
तदाद्यं सर्वजगतां जगच्चित्रस्य भित्तिवत्‌ ॥ ३३ ॥
śṛṇu rājan bahir iti yad loke bhāti kevalam ।
tad ādyaṁ sarva-jagatāṁ jagac-citrasya bhittivat ॥ 33 ॥

śṛṇu — listen, rājan — O king, bahiḥ — outside, iti — thus, yat — which, loke — in the world, bhāti — appears, kevalam — merely, tat — that, ādyaṁ — original, sarva-jagatām — of all worlds, jagat-citrasya — of the world picture, bhittivat — like a canvas.
"Listen, O king, that which appears merely outside in the world, that original nature of all worlds, is like the canvas of the world picture."
तस्य बाह्यस्य वक्तव्यमपादानं ध्रुवं ननु ।
शरीरं स्यादपादानं नेतरद्‌ भवितुं क्षमम्‌ ॥ ३४ ॥
tasya bāhyasya vaktavyam apādānaṁ dhruvaṁ nanu ।
śarīraṁ syād apādānaṁ netarat bhavituṁ kṣamam ॥ 34 ॥

tasya — of that, bāhyasya — external, vaktavyam — to be stated, apādānam — support, dhruvam — certainly, nanu — indeed, śarīram — body, syāt — is, apādānam — support, na itarat — not otherwise, bhavituṁ — to be, kṣamam — capable.
"Certainly, the support of that external, to be stated, is indeed the body. It is the support, otherwise this world is not capable."
तस्यापि बहिराभासाद पादानं कथं नु तत्‌ ।
पर्वताद्‌ बहिरित्युक्ते पर्वतो न बहिर्भवेत्‌ ॥ ३५ ॥
tasyāpi bahir ābhāsād apādānaṁ kathaṁ nu tat ।
parvatād bahiḥ iti ukte parvato na bahiḥ bhavet ॥ 35 ॥

tasya api — of that also, bahir — outside, ābhāsāt — appearance, apādānam — support, kathaṁ — what, nu — indeed, tat — that, parvatāt — from the mountain, bahiḥ — outside, iti — thus, ukte — stated, parvataḥ — mountain, na — not, bahiḥ — outside, bhavet — would be.
"What indeed is the support of that appearance outside? When stated as the mountain is outside, the mountain is not actually outside."
यथा घटो भासते हि बहिस्तद्वच्छरीरकम्‌ ।
भासकाद्‌ बहिरित्येवं वक्तुं वापि न सम्भवेत्‌ ॥ ३६ ॥
yathā ghaṭo bhāsate hi bahis tadvat śarīrakam ।
bhāsakāt bahiḥ iti evaṁ vaktuṁ vā api na sambhavet ॥ 36 ॥

yathā — as, ghaṭaḥ — pot, bhāsate — appears, hi — indeed, bahiḥ — outside, tadvat — likewise, śarīrakam — body, bhāsakāt — from the illuminator, bahiḥ — outside, iti — thus, evam — so, vaktum — to state, vā api — or also, na sambhavet — would not be possible.
"As the pot appears outside, so likewise the body. It is not possible to state as outside from the perspective of the illuminator."
दीपसूर्यालोकबहिर्गतानां नहि भासनम्‌ ।
अतस्तु भासकस्यान्तर्भास्यमस्तीति युज्यते ॥ ३७ ॥
dīpa-sūrya-āloka-bahir-gatānāṁ nahi bhāsanam ।
ataḥ tu bhāsakasya antarbhasyam asti iti yujyate ॥ 37 ॥

dīpa-sūrya-āloka-bahir-gatānām — of the lamp and sun's light going outside, nahi — not, bhāsanam — illumination, ataḥ — therefore, tu — but, bhāsakasya — of the illuminator, antar-bhāsyam — internal illumination, asti — is, iti — thus, yujyate — justified.
"The illumination of the lamp and sun's light from outside is not justified. Therefore, the internal illumination of the illuminator is thus only justified."
भासकं तु न देहादिर्भास्यत्वात्‌ पर्वतादिवत्‌ ।
न सर्वथा यत्तु भास्यं भासकं तद्धि युज्यते ॥ ३८ ॥
bhāsakaṁ tu na dehādir bhāsyatvāt parvatādivat ।
na sarvathā yat tu bhāsyam bhāsakaṁ taddhi yujyate ॥ 38 ॥

bhāsakam — illuminator, tu — but, na — not, deha-ādiḥ — body and others, bhāsyatvāt — being illuminated, parvatā-divat — like mountain and others, na — not, sarvathā — in any way, yat — which, tu — but, bhāsyam — illuminated, bhāsakam — illuminator, tat — that, hi — indeed, yujyate — justified.
"The illuminator is not the body and others, as they are being illuminated like the mountain and others. The illuminator is not in any way the illuminated, indeed that is justified."
भासकस्यापि भास्यत्वे भासकस्यानवस्थितिः ।
स्वस्यैव भासकत्वं च भास्यत्वं नहि युज्यते ॥ ३९ ॥
bhāsakasya api bhāsyatve bhāsakasya anavasthitiḥ ।
svasya eva bhāsakatvaṁ ca bhāsyatvaṁ nahi yujyate ॥ 39 ॥

bhāsakasya — of the illuminator, api — also, bhāsyatve — if being illuminated, bhāsakasya — of the illuminator, anavasthitiḥ — instability, svasya — of oneself, eva — indeed, bhāsakatvam — being illuminator, ca — and, bhāsyatvam — being illuminated, nahi — not, yujyate — justified.
"If the illuminator is also being illuminated, there is instability of the illuminator. Indeed, oneself being the illuminator and being illuminated is not justified."
अतस्तु भासकं शुद्धं भासकैकस्वरूपकम्‌ ।
तच्च भारूपमेवेह पुर्णमेकरसात्मकम्‌ ॥ ४० ॥
ataḥ tu bhāsakam śuddham bhāsakaika-svarūpakam ।
tac ca bhārūpam eva iha purnam eka-rasa-ātmakam ॥ 40 ॥

ataḥ — therefore, tu — but, bhāsakam — illuminator, śuddham — pure, bhāsaka-eka-svarūpakam — having the sole nature of illuminator, tat — that, ca — and, bhārūpam — the essence of light, eva — indeed, iha — here, purnam — complete, eka-rasa-ātmakam — of a single essence.
"Therefore, the illuminator is pure, having the sole nature of the illuminator. That, indeed, is the essence of light here, complete and of a single essence."
तेन व्याप्ता देशकाला भासनात्तस्य पूर्णता ।
अभारूपस्य चाभानाद्‌ भारूपैकरसं हि तत्‌ ॥ ४१ ॥
tena vyāptā deśakālā bhāsanāt tasya pūrṇatā ।
abhārūpasya ca abhānāt bhārūpaikarasaṁ hi tat ॥ 41 ॥

tena — by that, vyāptā — pervaded, deśakālā — space and time, bhāsanāt — due to illumination, tasya — its, pūrṇatā — completeness, abhārūpasya — of the non-essence, ca — and, abhānāt — absence, bhārūpaikarasaṁ — essence of light, hi — indeed, tat — that.
"By that, space and time are pervaded, due to its illumination. Its completeness is the essence of light, as the non-essence is absent anywhere."
अन्तर्बहिर्वा यत्‌ किञ्चिद्‌ भारूपोदरसंस्थितम्‌ ।
अतस्तन्नापादानं स्यात्‌ शृङ्गस्येव हि पर्वतः ॥ ४२ ॥
antarbahir vā yat kiñcid bhārūpodarasaṁsthitam ।
ataḥ tat na apādānaṁ syāt śṛṅgasya eva hi parvataḥ ॥ 42 ॥

antarbahir — inside or outside, vā — or, yat — whatever, kiñcid — anything, bhārūpodara-saṁsthitam — situated within the essence of light, ataḥ — therefore, tat — that, na — not, apādānam — support, syāt — would be, śṛṅgasya — of the peak, eva — indeed, hi — certainly, parvataḥ — mountain.
"Whether inside or outside, whatever is situated within the essence of light, therefore, that would not be the support, just as the mountain is not the peak."
एवंविधं हि भारूपं ग्रस्तसर्वप्रपञ्चकम्‌ ।
भाति स्वतन्त्रतः स्वस्मिन्‌ सर्वत्रापि च सर्वदा ॥ ४३ ॥
evaṁvidham hi bhārūpam grasta-sarva-prapañcakam ।
bhāti svatantrataḥ svasmin sarvatra api ca sarvadā ॥ 43 ॥

evaṁvidham — in this way, hi — indeed, bhārūpam — essence of light, grasta-sarva-prapañcakam — engulfing all phenomena, bhāti — shines, svatantrataḥ — independently, svasmin — in itself, sarvatra — everywhere, api — also, ca — and, sarvadā — always.
"In this way, the essence of light, engulfing all phenomena, shines independently in itself, everywhere and always."
एतत्‌ परा चितिः प्रोक्ता त्रिपुरा परमेश्वरी ।
ब्रह्मेत्याहुर्वेदविदो विष्णुं वैष्णवसत्तमाः ॥ ४४ ॥
etat parā citiḥ proktā tripurā parameśvarī ।
brahma iti āhuḥ veda-vidaḥ viṣṇuṁ vaiṣṇava-sattamāḥ ॥ 44 ॥

etat — this, parā — supreme, citiḥ — consciousness, proktā — is called, tripurā — Tripura, parameśvarī — supreme goddess, brahma — Brahman, iti — thus, āhuḥ — say, veda-vidaḥ — knowers of the Vedas, viṣṇuṁ — Vishnu, vaiṣṇava-sattamāḥ — best of the Vaishnavas.
"This supreme consciousness is called Tripura, the supreme goddess. The knowers of the Vedas call it Brahman, and the best of the Vaishnavas call it Vishnu."
शिवं शैवोत्तमाः प्राहुः शक्ति शक्तिपरायणाः ।
एतद्रूपादृते किञ्चिद्‌ यदि ब्रूयुस्तदल्पकम्‌ ॥ ४५ ॥
śivaṁ śaiva-uttamāḥ prāhuḥ śakti śakti-parāyaṇāḥ ।
etat-rūpāt ṛte kiñcid yadi brūyuḥ tat alpakam ॥ 45 ॥

śivam — Shiva, śaiva-uttamāḥ — best of the Shaivas, prāhuḥ — call, śakti — Shakti, śakti-parāyaṇāḥ — devoted to Shakti, etat-rūpāt — apart from this form, ṛte — without, kiñcid — anything, yadi — if, brūyuḥ — say, tat — that, alpakam — insignificant.
"The best of the Shaivas call it Shiva, and those devoted to Shakti call it Shakti. Anything said apart from this form is insignificant."
तया व्याप्तं तु चिच्छक्त्या दर्पणप्रतिबिम्बवत्‌ ।
तस्य भास्यकृतं भासकत्वं च न स्वतः स्थितम्‌ ॥ ४६ ॥
tayā vyāptaṁ tu cit-śaktyā darpaṇa-pratibimba-vat ।
tasya bhāsyakṛtaṁ bhāsakatvaṁ ca na svataḥ sthitam ॥ 46 ॥

tayā — by that, vyāptam — pervaded, tu — indeed, cit-śaktyā — by the power of consciousness, darpaṇa-pratibimba-vat — like the reflection in a mirror, tasya — of that, bhāsyakṛtam — caused by the illuminated, bhāsakatvam — illumination, ca — and, na — not, svataḥ sthitam — existing by itself.
"Indeed, pervaded by the power of consciousness, like the reflection in a mirror, its illumination is caused by the illuminated and the illuminated does not exist by itself."
भास्यं तु भाननिर्मग्नमादर्शे नगरादिवत्‌ ।
दर्पणे नगरं यद्वद्‌ दर्पणान्नातिरिच्यते ॥ ४७ ॥
bhāsyam tu bhāna-nirmagnam ādarśe nagara-divat ।
darpaṇe nagaraṁ yadvat darpaṇāt na atiricyate ॥ 47 ॥

bhāsyam — the illuminated, tu — indeed, bhāna-nirmagnam — submerged in light, ādarśe — in a mirror, nagara-divat — like a city, darpaṇe — in the mirror, nagaram — city, yadvat — as, darpaṇāt — from the mirror, na — not, atiricyate — differs.
"Indeed, the illuminated is submerged in light, like a city in a mirror. As the city in the mirror does not differ from the mirror."
तथा चिति जगद्‌ भाति यत्तन्नैवातिरिच्यते ।
दर्पणात्मनि सम्पूर्णे निबिडे चैकरूपिणि ॥ ४८ ॥
tathā citi jagat bhāti yat tat na eva atiricyate ।
darpaṇa-ātmani sampūrṇe nibiḍe ca eka-rūpiṇi ॥ 48 ॥

tathā — likewise, citi — consciousness, jagat — world, bhāti — shines, yat — which, tat — that, na — not, eva — indeed, atiricyate — differs, darpaṇa-ātmani — in the mirror self, sampūrṇe — complete, nibiḍe — compact, ca — and, eka-rūpiṇi — of single form.
"Likewise, the world shines in consciousness and does not differ from it, just as the complete, compact, single-form mirror self."
यथा हि भिन्नं नगरं सर्वथा नोपपद्यते ।
तथा पूर्णे सुनिबिडे चैकरूपे चिदात्मनि ॥ ४९ ॥
yathā hi bhinnaṁ nagaraṁ sarvathā na upapadyate ।
tathā pūrṇe sunibiḍe ca eka-rūpe cidātmani ॥ 49 ॥

yathā — as, hi — indeed, bhinnam — separate, nagaram — city, sarvathā — in every way, na upapadyate — does not make sense, tathā — likewise, pūrṇe — complete, sunibiḍe — compact, ca — and, eka-rūpe — single form, cid-ātmani — in the conscious self.
"As a separate city in a mirror in every way does not make sense, likewise, is the complete, compact, single-form conscious self."
जगत्‌ सर्वात्मना नैव ह्युपपत्तिं समश्नुते ।
आकाशस्त्ववकाशात्मा शून्यरूपत्वहेतुतः ॥ ५० ॥
jagat sarvātmanā na eva hi upapattiṁ samaśnute ।
ākāśaḥ tu avakāśa-ātmā śūnya-rūpatva-hetutaḥ ॥ 50 ॥

jagat — world, sarvātmanā — in every way, na — not, eva — indeed, hi — certainly, upapattiṁ — coherence, samaśnute — attains, ākāśaḥ — space, tu — but, avakāśa-ātmā — of the nature of space, śūnya-rūpatva-hetutaḥ — due to the nature of emptiness.
"The world does not attain coherence of self in every way, but self like space, due to its nature of emptiness, does."
द्वैतं जगत्‌ प्रसहते सर्वत्रैव हि सर्वदा ।
सती चितिरशून्यात्मरूपिण्येकरसा कथम्‌ ॥ ५१ ॥
dvaitaṁ jagat prasahate sarvatra eva hi sarvadā ।
satī citiḥ aśūnya-ātma-rūpiṇī eka-rasā katham ॥ 51 ॥

dvaitam — duality, jagat — world, prasahate — tolerates, sarvatra — everywhere, eva — indeed, hi — certainly, sarvadā — always, satī — existing, citiḥ — consciousness, aśūnya-ātma-rūpiṇī — of non-empty nature, eka-rasā — single essence, katham — how.
"The world always tolerates duality everywhere, but how can the existing consciousness, of non-empty nature and single essence, do so?"
द्वितीयलेशं प्रसहेदादर्शात्मवदञ्जसा ।
तस्मादादर्शवत्‌ संवित्‌ स्वातन्त्र्यभरवैभवात्‌ ॥ ५२ ॥
dvitīya-leśaṁ prasahēt ādarśa-ātma-vat añjasā ।
tasmāt ādarśa-vat saṁvit svātantrya-bhara-vaibhavāt ॥ 52 ॥

dvitīya-leśam — a second part, prasahēt — could tolerate, ādarśa-ātma-vat — like the nature of a mirror, añjasā — directly, tasmāt — therefore, ādarśa-vat — like a mirror, saṁvit — consciousness, svātantrya-bhara-vaibhavāt — due to the grandeur of independence.
"A second part, i.e., the world could be tolerated directly, like the nature of a mirror. Therefore, consciousness, like a mirror, possible due to the grandeur of independence."
भासयेदद्वितीये स्वे रूपे सर्वं चराचरम्‌ ।
निमित्तोपादानहीनं द्वितीयमतिचित्रितम्‌ ॥ ५३ ॥
bhāsayēt advitīye sve rūpe sarvaṁ cara-acaram ।
nimitta-upādāna-hīnaṁ dvitīyam ati-citritam ॥ 53 ॥

bhāsayēt — would illuminate, advitīye — in the secondless, sve — in its own, rūpe — form, sarvam — all, cara-acaram — moving and non-moving, nimitta-upādāna-hīnam — devoid of cause and effect, dvitīyam — second, ati-citritam — highly vivid.
"It would illuminate all moving and non-moving forms in the secondless, in its own form, devoid of cause and effect, highly vivid."
यथाऽनेकरूपविधे भासमानेऽपि दर्पणे ।
एकत्वं भासते स्पष्टमविशेषाददूषितम्‌ ॥ ५४ ॥
yathā aneka-rūpa-vidhe bhāsamāne api darpaṇe ।
ekatvam bhāsate spaṣṭam aviśeṣāt adūṣitam ॥ 54 ॥

yathā — as, aneka-rūpa-vidhe — in manifold forms, bhāsamāne — shining, api — even, darpaṇe — in a mirror, ekatvam — oneness, bhāsate — shines, spaṣṭam — clearly, aviśeṣāt — without distinction, adūṣitam — untainted.
"As manifold forms shine in a mirror, even then, oneness shines clearly, without distinction, untainted."
तथा विचित्रे जगति भासमानेऽप्यनेकधा ।
अनुसन्धानसंसिद्धमेकं दोषविवर्ज्जितम्‌ ॥ ५५ ॥
tathā vicitre jagati bhāsamāne api anekadhā ।
anusandhāna-saṁsiddham ekam doṣa-vivarjitam ॥ 55 ॥

tathā — likewise, vicitre — varied, jagati — world, bhāsamāne — shining, api — even, anekadhā — manifold, anusandhāna-saṁsiddham — perfected by investigation, ekam — one, doṣa-vivarjitam — devoid of faults.
"Likewise, in the varied world, even as manifold forms shine, one perfected by investigation remains, devoid of faults."
राजन्‌ स्वात्मनि सम्पश्य मनोराज्यदशास्थितिम्‌ ।
अनेकवैचित्र्यवपुरपि चैतन्यमात्रकम्‌ ॥ ५६ ॥
rājan sva-ātmani sampaśya mano-rājya-daśā-sthitim ।
aneka-vaicitrya-vapuḥ api caitanya-mātrakam ॥ 56 ॥

rājan — O king, sva-ātmani — in your self, sampaśya — behold, mano-rājya-daśā-sthitim — state of the kingdom of mind, aneka-vaicitrya-vapuḥ — manifold varied forms, api — even, caitanya-mātrakam — pure consciousness.
"O king, behold in your self the state of the kingdom of mind, manifold varied forms, even pure consciousness."
सुष्टौ वा प्रलये वापि निर्विकल्पैव सा चितिः ।
प्रतिबिम्बस्य भावे वाप्यभावे वेव दर्पणः ॥ ५७ ॥
suṣṭau vā pralaye vā api nirvikalpa iva sā citiḥ ।
pratibimbasya bhāve vā api abhāve iva darpaṇaḥ ॥ 57 ॥

suṣṭau — in creation, vā — or, pralaye — in dissolution, vā api — or even, nirvikalpa iva — like the undifferentiated, sā — that, citiḥ — consciousness, pratibimbasya — of the reflection, bhāve — in presence, vā api — or even, abhāve — in absence, iva — like, darpaṇaḥ — mirror.
"In creation or in dissolution, that consciousness is like the undifferentiated, in presence or absence of the reflection, like a mirror."
एवंविधैकरूपापि चितिः स्वातन्त्र्यहेतुतः ।
स्वान्तर्विभासयेद्‌ बाह्यमादर्शे गगनं यथा ॥ ५८ ॥
evaṁvidha-eka-rūpā api citiḥ svātantrya-hetutaḥ ।
svāntar-vibhāsayet bāhyam ādarśe gaganaṁ yathā ॥ 58 ॥

evaṁvidha-eka-rūpā api — even in this single form, citiḥ — consciousness, svātantrya-hetutaḥ — due to the cause of independence, svāntar-vibhāsayet — illuminates within, bāhyam — external, ādarśe — in the mirror, gaganaṁ yathā — like the sky.
"Even in this single form, consciousness, due to the cause of independence, illuminates within, like the sky in a mirror."
एषा हि प्रथमा सुष्टिरविद्या तम उच्यते ।
पूर्णस्यांशेनेव भानं बाह्याभासनमुच्यते ॥ ५९ ॥
eṣā hi prathamā suṣṭiḥ avidyā tama ucyate ।
pūrṇasya aṁśena iva bhānaṁ bāhya-ābhāsanam ucyate ॥ 59 ॥

eṣā — this, hi — indeed, prathamā — first, suṣṭiḥ — establishment, avidyā — ignorance, tama — darkness, ucyate — is called, pūrṇasya — of the complete, aṁśena — by a part, iva — as if, bhānaṁ — illumination, bāhya-ābhāsanam — external appearance, ucyate — is called.
"This first establishment is called ignorance, darkness, due to this, it appears as if it is a part of the complete, as if illumination is called the external appearance."
पूर्णाहम्भावविच्छेदादनहम्भावरूपता ।
एषैवाव्यक्तमित्युक्ता जडशक्तिश्च कथ्यते ॥ ६० ॥
pūrṇa-aham-bhāva-viccheda-at aham-bhāva-rūpatā ।
eṣā eva avyaktam iti uktā jaḍa-śaktiḥ ca kathyate ॥ 60 ॥

pūrṇa-aham-bhāva-viccheda — from the division of the complete I-feeling, aham-bhāva-rūpatā — the form of the I-feeling, eṣā — this, eva — indeed, avyaktam — unmanifest, iti — thus, uktā — is called, jaḍa-śaktiḥ — inert power, ca — and, kathyate — is described.
"From the division of the complete I-feeling, this form of the I-feeling is indeed called the unmanifest, and is described as the inert power (causing ignorance)."
या चितिश्चात्र विच्छिन्नाभासिनी बहिरात्मनः ।
शिवतत्त्वमिति प्रोक्ता शक्तिस्तद्भासनं भवेत्‌ ॥ ६१ ॥
yā citiḥ ca atra vicchinnā-abhāsinī bahiḥ ātmanaḥ ।
śiva-tattvam iti proktā śaktiḥ tad bhāsanam bhavet ॥ 61 ॥

yā — which, citiḥ — consciousness, ca — and, atra — here, vicchinnā — fragmented, abhāsinī — manifesting, bahiḥ — externally, ātmanaḥ — of the self, śiva-tattvam — Shiva principle, iti — thus, proktā — said, śaktiḥ — power, tad — that, bhāsanam — illumination, bhavet — is.
"Which consciousness, here manifesting externally in a fragmented manner, is said to be the Shiva principle. That power is its illumination."
बहीरूपं महाशून्यं कल्पितं यत्तदेव तु ।
अहम्भावाच्छादनेन सदाशिवमयं स्मृतम्‌ ॥ ६२ ॥
bahī-rūpaṁ mahā-śūnyaṁ kalpitaṁ yat tad eva tu ।
aham-bhāva-ācchādanena sadā-śiva-mayaṁ smṛtam ॥ 62 ॥

bahī-rūpam — external form, mahā-śūnyam — great void, kalpitam — imagined, yat — which, tad eva — that indeed, tu — but, aham-bhāva-ācchādanena — by the covering of the I-feeling, sadā-śiva-mayam — filled with Shiva always, smṛtam — is remembered.
"The external form is imagined as the great void, indeed, filled by the covering of the I-feeling, is remembered as always filled with Shiva."
तदेव जाड्यमुख्यत्वे ईश्वराख्यं प्रचक्षते ।
अनयोः संवेदनं तु भेदाभेदविमर्शनम्‌ ॥ ६३ ॥
tad eva jāḍya-mukhya-tve īśvara-ākhyam pracakṣate ।
anayoḥ saṁvedanaṁ tu bheda-abheda-vimarśanam ॥ 63 ॥

tad eva — that indeed, jāḍya-mukhya-tve — in the primary state of inertia, īśvara-ākhyam — called Ishvara, pracakṣate — is considered, anayoḥ — of these two, saṁvedanam — consciousness, tu — but, bheda-abheda-vimarśanam — examination of distinction and non-distinction.
"That indeed, in the primary state of inertia, is considered as called Ishvara. But the consciousness of these two (Jiva & Ishvara) is the examination of distinction and non-distinction."
शुद्धविद्येति सम्प्रोक्तमेतावच्छुद्धमुच्यते ।
भेदशक्तेरप्ररूढया चाभेदात्मावभासनात्‌ ॥ ६४ ॥
śuddha-vidyā iti samproktam etāvat śuddham ucyate ।
bheda-śakteḥ aprarūḍhayā ca abheda-ātma-avabhāsanāt ॥ 64 ॥

śuddha-vidyā — pure knowledge, iti — thus, samproktam — is called, etāvat — this much, śuddham — pure, ucyate — is said, bheda-śakteḥ — of the power of distinction, aprarūḍhayā — not fully grown, ca — and, abheda-ātma-avabhāsanāt — from the illumination of the non-distinct self.
"Thus, this much is called pure knowledge, said to be pure, due to the power of distinction not fully grown and due to the illumination of the non-distinct self."
अथ चित्स्वातन्त्र्यभरात्‌ प्ररूढे भेदभावने ।
जडशक्तिर्धर्मिभावं चितिर्धर्मात्मतां ययौ ॥ ६५ ॥
atha cit-svātantrya-bharāt prarūḍhe bheda-bhāvane ।
jaḍa-śaktiḥ dharmi-bhāvam citiḥ dharma-ātmatām yayau ॥ 65 ॥

atha — then, cit-svātantrya-bharāt — due to the fullness of consciousness's independence, prarūḍhe — fully grown, bheda-bhāvane — in the feeling of distinction, jaḍa-śaktiḥ — inert power, dharmi-bhāvam — state of possessing attributes, citiḥ — consciousness, dharma-ātmatām — state of being the essence of attributes, yayau — attained.

"Then, due to the fullness of consciousness's independence, in the fully grown feeling of distinction, the inert power attained the state of possessing attributes, and consciousness attained the state of being the essence of attributes."
तदा सा जडशक्तिस्तु मायातत्त्वं प्रचक्षते ।
माया विभेदबुद्धिस्तु भेदप्रचुरभावनात्‌ ॥ ६६ ॥
tadā sā jaḍa-śaktiḥ tu māyā-tattvaṁ pracakṣate ।
māyā vibheda-buddhiḥ tu bheda-pracura-bhāvanāt ॥ 66 ॥

tadā — then, sā — that, jaḍa-śaktiḥ — inert power, tu — but, māyā-tattvaṁ — principle of illusion, pracakṣate — is considered, māyā — illusion, vibheda-buddhiḥ — the intellect of distinction, tu — but, bheda-pracura-bhāvanāt — due to the abundance of distinction feeling.
"Then, that inert power is considered the principle of illusion, but the intellect of distinction is due to the abundance of the feeling of distinction."
भेदप्रचुरसंवीता चितिः सङ्कुचितात्मिका ।
पञ्चकञ्चुकसंव्याप्ता पुरुषत्वं प्रपद्यते ॥ ६७ ॥
bheda-pracura-saṁvītā citiḥ saṅkucita-ātmikā ।
pañca-kañcuka-saṁvyāptā puruṣatvaṁ prapadyate ॥ 67 ॥

bheda-pracura-saṁvītā — enveloped by the abundance of distinction, citiḥ — consciousness, saṅkucita-ātmikā — contracted in nature, pañca-kañcuka-saṁvyāptā — enveloped by the five sheaths, puruṣatvaṁ — state of the individual soul, prapadyate — attains.
"Enveloped by the abundance of distinction, consciousness, contracted in nature, enveloped by the five sheaths, attains the state of the individual soul."
कलाविद्यारागकालनियतिः पञ्चकञ्चुकम्‌ ।
कला किञ्चित्कर्तृता स्याद्विद्या किञ्चिज्ज्ञता भवेत्‌ ॥ ६८ ॥
kalā-vidyā-rāga-kāla-niyatiḥ pañca-kañcukaṁ ।
kalā kiñcit-kartrtā syāt vidyā kiñcit-jñatā bhavet ॥ 68 ॥

kalā — power of action, vidyā — power of knowledge, rāga — attachment, kāla — time, niyatiḥ — destiny, pañca-kañcukaṁ — five sheaths, kalā — power of action, kiñcit-kartrtā — limited doership, syāt — would be, vidyā — power of knowledge, kiñcit-jñatā — limited knowledge, bhavet — would be.

"The five sheaths are the power of action, power of knowledge, attachment, time, and destiny. The power of action results in limited doership, and the power of knowledge results in limited knowledge."
रागस्तृष्णा परिच्छित्तिरायुषा काल उच्यते ।
नियतिः परतन्त्रत्वमेतैर्युक्तस्तु पूरुषः ॥ ६९ ॥
rāgaḥ tṛṣṇā paricchittiḥ āyuṣā kālaḥ ucyate ।
niyatiḥ paratantratvam etaiḥ yuktaḥ tu pūruṣaḥ ॥ 69 ॥

rāgaḥ — attachment, tṛṣṇā — thirst, paricchittiḥ — limitation, āyuṣā — by lifespan, kālaḥ — time, ucyate — is called, niyatiḥ — destiny, paratantratvam — subservience, etaiḥ — by these, yuktaḥ — endowed, tu — but, pūruṣaḥ — individual soul.
"Attachment is called thirst, limitation is due to lifespan, and time is called destiny. Endowed with these, the individual soul becomes subservient."
चितिशक्तिमधिष्ठाय विचित्रानादिकर्मणाम्‌ ।
जनानां वासनापिण्डः स्थितः प्रकृतिरुच्यते ॥ ७० ॥
citi-śaktiṁ adhiṣṭhāya vicitra-anādi-karmaṇām ।
janānāṁ vāsanā-piṇḍaḥ sthitaḥ prakṛtiḥ ucyate ॥ 70 ॥

citi-śaktiṁ — consciousness power, adhiṣṭhāya — presiding over, vicitra — various, anādi-karmaṇām — beginningless actions, janānāṁ — of people, vāsanā-piṇḍaḥ — aggregate of tendencies, sthitaḥ — established, prakṛtiḥ — nature, ucyate — is called.
"Presiding over by the power of consciousness, various beginningless actions of people, the aggregate of tendencies, established, is called nature."
फलं तु त्रिविधं यस्मात्‌ कर्मणां सा त्रिरूपिणी ।
अस्या अवस्थाभेदो हि चित्तमित्यभिधीयते ॥ ७१॥
phalaṁ tu trividhaṁ yasmāt karmaṇāṁ sā tri-rūpiṇī ।
asyāḥ avasthā-bhedaḥ hi cittam iti abhidhīyate ॥ 71 ॥

phalaṁ — result, tu — but, trividhaṁ — threefold, yasmāt — because, karmaṇāṁ — of actions, sā — she, tri-rūpiṇī — of three forms, asyāḥ — of this, avasthā-bhedaḥ — state difference, hi — indeed, cittam — mind, iti — thus, abhidhīyate — is called.
"The result of actions is threefold because she (nature) has three forms. The difference in states is indeed called the mind."
सुषुप्तौ प्रकृतिर्ज्ञेया तदन्ते चित्तमुच्यते ।
वासनापिण्डसहिता चितिश्चित्तमुदीरितम्‌ ॥ ७२॥
suṣuptau prakṛtiḥ jñeyā tad-ante cittam ucyate ।
vāsanā-piṇḍa-sahitā citiḥ cittam udīritam ॥ 72 ॥

suṣuptau — in deep sleep, prakṛtiḥ — nature, jñeyā — should be known, tad-ante — after that, cittam — mind, ucyate — is called, vāsanā-piṇḍa-sahitā — with the aggregate of tendencies, citiḥ — consciousness, cittam — mind, udīritam — is said.
"In deep sleep, one’s nature should be known. After that, it is called the mind. Consciousness with the aggregate of tendencies is said to be the mind."
अव्यक्तमेतदेवोक्तं वासनापिण्डभावतः ।
पुरुषाणां विभेदेन चित्तं बहुविधं भवेत्‌ ॥ ७३ ॥
avyaktam etad eva uktam vāsanā-piṇḍa-bhāvataḥ ।
puruṣāṇāṁ vibhedena cittam bahuvidhaṁ bhavet ॥ 73 ॥

avyaktam — unmanifest, etad — this, eva — indeed, uktam — is said, vāsanā-piṇḍa-bhāvataḥ — due to the state of the aggregate of tendencies, puruṣāṇāṁ — of individuals, vibhedena — by distinction, cittam — mind, bahuvidhaṁ — various, bhavet — becomes.
"This unmanifest is indeed said to be due to the state of the aggregate of tendencies. By the distinction of individuals, the mind becomes various."
जीवानामविभेदेन सुषुप्तावेकधा हि तत्‌ ।
प्रकृतित्वं समायाति तदन्ते चित्ततामियात्‌ ॥ ७४ ॥
jīvānām avibhedena suṣuptau ekadhā hi tat ।
prakṛtitvaṁ samāyāti tad-ante cittatām iyāt ॥ 74 ॥

jīvānām — of beings, avibhedena — without distinction, suṣuptau — in deep sleep, ekadhā — one, hi — indeed, tat — that, prakṛtitvaṁ — nature, samāyāti — attains, tad-ante — after that, cittatām — state of mind, iyāt — goes.
"Without distinction, that one state of beings in deep sleep indeed attains true nature. After that, it goes into the state of mind."
एतदेव पुमान्‌ प्रोक्तश्चितिप्राधान्यहेतुना ।
अव्यक्तप्राधान्यतस्तु चित्तप्रकृतितामियात्‌ ॥ ७५ ॥
etad eva pumān proktaḥ citi-prādhānya-hetunā ।
avyakta-prādhānyataḥ tu citta-prakṛtitām iyāt ॥ 75 ॥

etad — this, eva — indeed, pumān — person, proktaḥ — is said, citi-prādhānya-hetunā — due to the predominance of consciousness, avyakta-prādhānyataḥ — due to the predominance of the unmanifest, tu — but, citta-prakṛtitām — state of mind and nature, iyāt — goes.
"This person is indeed said to be due to the predominance of consciousness. But due to the predominance of the unmanifest, it goes into the state of mind and nature."
क्रियाभेदात्‌ तत्‌ त्रिविधमन्तःकरणमुच्यते ।
अहङ्कारबुद्धिमनोरूपेण नृपसत्तम ॥ ७६ ॥
kriyā-bhedāt tat tri-vidham antaḥkaraṇam ucyate ।
ahaṅkāra-buddhi-mano-rūpeṇa nṛpa-sattama ॥ 76 ॥

kriyā-bhedāt — due to the distinction of actions, tat — that, tri-vidham — threefold, antaḥkaraṇam — inner instrument, ucyate — is called, ahaṅkāra — ego, buddhi — intellect, manaḥ — mind, rūpeṇa — in the form of, nṛpa-sattama — O best of kings.
"Due to the distinction of actions, that inner instrument is called threefold: ego, intellect, and mind, O best of kings."
ज्ञानकर्मेन्द्रियाणां तु पञ्चकं स्यात्ततः पृथक्‌ ।
शब्दादिगगनादीनि भूतानि स्थूलसूक्ष्मतः ॥ ७७ ॥
jñāna-karma-indriyāṇāṁ tu pañcakaṁ syāt tataḥ pṛthak ।
śabda-ādi-gagana-ādīni bhūtāni sthūla-sūkṣmataḥ ॥ 77 ॥

jñāna-karma-indriyāṇāṁ — of the knowledge and action senses, tu — but, pañcakaṁ — fivefold, syāt — would be, tataḥ — from that, pṛthak — separately, śabda-ādi — sound etc., gagana-ādīni — sky etc., bhūtāni — elements, sthūla-sūkṣmataḥ — gross and subtle.
"Of the knowledge and action senses, fivefold they would become. From that, separately, the elements are sound, sky, etc., both gross and subtle are born"
एवं सा परमा संविद्‌ बाह्याभासप्रपूर्वकम्‌ ।
क्रीडां करोति सुष्ट्यादिक्रमेण सर्वसाक्षिणी ॥ ७८ ॥
evaṁ sā paramā saṁvid bāhya-ābhāsa-pra-pūrvakam ।
krīḍāṁ karoti suṣṭi-ādi-krameṇa sarva-sākṣiṇī ॥ 78 ॥

evaṁ — thus, sā — she, paramā saṁvid — supreme consciousness, bāhya-ābhāsa-pra-pūrvakam — external appearance as a precursor, krīḍāṁ — play, karoti — performs, suṣṭi-ādi-krameṇa — in the order of creation, etc., sarva-sākṣiṇī — witnessing all.
"Thus, the supreme consciousness, with the external appearance as a precursor, performs play in the order of creation, etc., witnessing all."
तत्राद्यया श्रीत्रिपुराशक्त्या सृष्टौ प्रभावितः ।
हिरण्यगर्भो यो ब्रह्मा तस्यैतद्‌ भावनोत्थितम्‌ ॥ ७९ ॥
tatra ādyayā śrī-tripura-śaktyā sṛṣṭau prabhāvitaḥ ।
hiraṇyagarbho yo brahmā tasya etad bhāvana-utthitam ॥ 79 ॥

tatra — there, ādyayā — by the primordial, śrī-tripura-śaktyā — Tripura's power, sṛṣṭau — in creation, prabhāvitaḥ — influenced, hiraṇyagarbhaḥ — Hiraṇyagarbha, yaḥ — who, brahmā — Brahmā, tasya — of him, etad — this, bhāvana-utthitam — arising from contemplation.
"There, influenced by the primordial power of Tripura in creation, Hiraṇyagarbha, who is Brahmā, arises from this contemplation."
जगत्तत्र तु या संवित्‌ त्वमहंरूपभासिनी ।
सा परैव हि चिच्छक्तिस्तद्भेदो न तु विद्यते ॥ ८० ॥
jagat tatra tu yā saṁvit tvam-ahaṁ-rūpa-bhāsinī ।
sā para-eva hi cit-śaktiḥ tad-bhedaḥ na tu vidyate ॥ 80 ॥

jagat — world, tatra — there, tu — but, yā — which, saṁvit — consciousness, tvam-ahaṁ-rūpa-bhāsinī — manifesting as "you" and "I", sā — she, para — supreme, eva — indeed, hi — certainly, cit-śaktiḥ — power of consciousness, tad-bhedaḥ — distinction of that, na — not, tu — but, vidyate — exists.
"There, but the consciousness which manifests as 'you' and 'I', she is indeed the supreme power of consciousness. There is no distinction of that."
भेदस्त्वौपाधिको भाति ह्युपाधिर्ब्रह्यभावितः ।
तद्भावनोपसंहारे नास्ति भेदस्य भासनम्‌ ॥ ८१ ॥
bhedas tu aupādhikaḥ bhāti hi upādhiḥ brahya-bhāvitaḥ ।
tad-bhāvana-upasaṁhāre nāsti bhedasya bhāsanam ॥ 81 ॥

bhedaḥ — distinction, tu — but, aupādhikaḥ — due to limitations, bhāti — appears, hi — indeed, upādhiḥ — limitation, brahya-bhāvitaḥ — contemplated in Brahman, tad-bhāvana-upasaṁhāre — in the cessation of that contemplation, na — not, asti — exists, bhedasya — of distinction, bhāsanam — appearance.
"The distinction appears due to limitations, indeed contemplated in Brahman. In the cessation of that contemplation, the appearance of distinction does not exist."
चितो या भावनाशक्तिर्मायया ते समावृता ।
तदावरणहाने तु तव सा सिद्धिमेष्यति ॥ ८२ ॥
cito yā bhāvanā-śaktiḥ māyayā te samāvṛtā ।
tad-āvaraṇa-hāne tu tava sā siddhim eṣyati ॥ 82 ॥

citaḥ — of consciousness, yā — which, bhāvanā-śaktiḥ — power of contemplation, māyayā — by illusion, te — of you, samāvṛtā — covered, tad-āvaraṇa-hāne — in the removal of that covering, tu — but, tava — of you, sā — that, siddhim — success, eṣyati — will attain.
"The power of contemplation of consciousness, covered by illusion, but in the removal of that covering, you will attain success."
देशः कालोऽथवा किञ्चिद्‌ यथा येन विभावितम्‌ ।
तथा तत्तत्र भासेत दीर्घसूक्ष्मत्वभेदतः ॥ ८३ ॥
deśaḥ kālaḥ atha vā kiñcid yathā yena vibhāvitaṁ ।
tathā tat tatra bhāseta dīrgha-sūkṣmatva-bhedataḥ ॥ 83 ॥

deśaḥ — place, kālaḥ — time, atha vā — or, kiñcit — something, yathā — as, yena — by whom, vibhāvitaṁ — contemplated, tathā — thus, tat — that, tatra — there, bhāseta — would appear, dīrgha-sūkṣmatva-bhedataḥ — due to the difference in extent and subtlety.
"Place, time, or something, are defined as contemplated by whom, thus it would appear there due to the difference in extent and subtlety."
मयैकदिनरूपेण भावितं तद्‌ दिनैककम्‌ ।
ब्रह्मणा तावदेवात्र द्वादशाऽर्बुदरूपतः ॥ ८४ ॥
mayā eka-dina-rūpeṇa bhāvitaṁ tad dina-ekakam ।
brahmaṇā tāvad eva atra dvādaśa-arbuda-rūpataḥ ॥ 84 ॥

mayā — by me, eka-dina-rūpeṇa — in the form of one day, bhāvitaṁ — contemplated, tad — that, dina-ekakam — one day, brahmaṇā — by Brahma, tāvat — so much, eva — indeed, atra — here, dvādaśa-arbuda-rūpataḥ — in the form of twelve billion years.
"Contemplated by me as one day, that one day is indeed here, in the form of twelve billion years by Brahma."
भावितं तेनैवमेतच्चिरशीघ्रत्वभासनम्‌ ।
ब्रह्मणा निर्मिते शैले पादगव्यूतिसम्मितेः ॥ ८५ ॥
bhāvitaṁ tena evam etac cira-śīghratva-bhāsanam ।
brahmaṇā nirmiti-śaile pāda-gavyūti-sammiteḥ ॥ 85 ॥

bhāvitaṁ — contemplated, tena — by him, evam — thus, etat — this, cira-śīghratva-bhāsanam — appearance of long and short duration, brahmaṇā — by Brahma, nirmiti-śaile — in the created mountain, pāda-gavyūti-sammiteḥ — measured by a span and a gavyūti (distance of two miles).
"Thus contemplated by him, this appearance of difference of long and short duration, in the created mountain by Brahma, measured by a span and a gavyūti."
मयाऽनन्तप्रदेशस्य भावितत्वादनन्तता ।
एवं च द्वयमप्यत्र सत्यं चासत्यमेव च ॥ ८६ ॥
mayā ananta-pradeśasya bhāvitatvāt anantatā ।
evaṁ ca dvayam api atra satyaṁ ca asatyam eva ca ॥ 86 ॥

mayā — by me, ananta-pradeśasya — of infinite region, bhāvitatvāt — due to contemplation, anantatā — infiniteness, evaṁ — thus, ca — and, dvayam — both, api — also, atra — here, satyam — true, ca — and, asatyam — false, eva — indeed, ca — and.
"But by me, due to contemplation of the infinite region in the mountain, thus both are here, true and false indeed."
त्वमप्यन्तः क्रोशमितं देशं कालं कलात्मकम्‌ ।
विभाव्य भूयस्तत्रैव भावयानन्तयोजनम्‌ ॥ ८७ ॥
tvam api antaḥ krośa-mitaṁ deśaṁ kālaṁ kalātmakam ।
vibhāvya bhūyas tatra eva bhāvaya ananta-yojanam ॥ 87 ॥

tvam — you, api — also, antaḥ — within, krośa-mitaṁ — measured by a krosha (two miles), deśaṁ — place, kālaṁ — time, kalātmakam — formed of moments, vibhāvya — contemplating, bhūyas — further, tatra — there, eva — indeed, bhāvaya — contemplate, ananta-yojanam — infinite yojanas.
"You also, within, contemplating a place measured by a krosha, and time formed of moments, can further contemplate there indeed, infinite yojanas."
असंख्यकालमपि च भासेद्‌ यावद्धि भावनम्‌ ।
तस्माद्‌ भावनमात्रात्मरूपमेतज्जगद्‌ बहिः ॥ ८८ ॥
asaṅkhya-kālam api ca bhāset yāvat hi bhāvanam ।
tasmād bhāvana-mātra-ātma-rūpam etat jagat bahiḥ ॥ 88 ॥

asaṅkhya-kālam — innumerable time, api — also, ca — and, bhāset — appears, yāvat — as long as, hi — indeed, bhāvanam — contemplation, tasmāt — therefore, bhāvana-mātra-ātma-rūpam — the form of mere contemplation, etat — this, jagat — world, bahiḥ — external.
"Innumerable time also appears as long as contemplation does. Therefore, this external world is the form of mere contemplation."
चिदात्मरूपेऽव्यक्ते वै भासते मनुजाधिप ।
तस्माद्‌ बाह्यात्मकाव्यक्तभित्तौ चित्रमयं जगत्‌ ॥ ८९ ॥
cid-ātma-rūpe avyaktaṁ vai bhāsate manuja-adhipa ।
tasmād bāhya-ātmakā avyakta-bhittau citra-mayaṁ jagat ॥ 89 ॥

cid-ātma-rūpe — in the form of consciousness, avyaktaṁ — unmanifest, vai — indeed, bhāsate — appears, manuja-adhipa — O lord of men, tasmāt — therefore, bāhya-ātmakā — of the external self, avyakta-bhittau — on the unmanifest background, citra-mayaṁ — full of images, jagat — world.
"In the form of consciousness, the unmanifest appears, O lord of men. Therefore, the world, full of images, is on the unmanifest background of the external self."
अव्यक्तभित्तिमात्रं स्यात्‌ सा स्वभित्तिचिदात्मिका ।
अत एव चिराद्‌ गम्यो दूरदेशोऽपि योगिनः ॥ ९० ॥
avyakta-bhitti-mātraṁ syāt sā sva-bhitti-cid-ātmikā ।
ata eva cirād gamyaḥ dūra-deśaḥ api yoginaḥ ॥ 90 ॥

avyakta-bhitti-mātraṁ — mere unmanifest background, syāt — would be, sā — she, sva-bhitti-cid-ātmikā — own consciousness as the background, ataḥ — therefore, eva — indeed, cirāt — after a long time, gamyaḥ — attainable, dūra-deśaḥ — distant place, api — also, yoginaḥ — for a yogi.
"She would be the mere unmanifest background, with her own consciousness as the background. Therefore, even a distant place is attainable for a yogi or a long time also."
क्षणेन गत्वा पश्यन्ति करामलकवद्‌ ध्रुवम्‌ ।
तस्माद्‌ दूरं समीपं वा चिरं शीघ्रमथापि वा ॥ ९१ ॥
kṣaṇena gatvā paśyanti kara-āmalaka-vat dhruvam ।
tasmāt dūraṁ samīpaṁ vā ciraṁ śīghram atha api vā ॥ 91 ॥

kṣaṇena — in a moment, gatvā — having gone, paśyanti — they see, kara-āmalaka-vat — like a fruit in the palm, dhruvam — certainly, tasmāt — therefore, dūram — far, samīpam — near, vā — or, ciram — long, śīghram — quickly, atha api — or also, vā — or.
"In a moment, they see it like a fruit in the palm, certainly. Therefore, whether far or near, long time or quickly."
भावनामात्रसंसिद्धं चिद्दर्पणसमाश्रितम्‌ ।
निश्चित्यैवं त्यज भ्रान्तिं शुद्धचिद्भावनक्रमात्‌ ॥ ९२ ॥
bhāvana-mātra-saṁsiddhaṁ cid-darpaṇa-samāśritam ।
niścitya evaṁ tyaja bhrāntiṁ śuddha-cit-bhāvana-kramāt ॥ 92 ॥

bhāvana-mātra-saṁsiddhaṁ — perfected by mere contemplation, cit-darpaṇa-samāśritam — based on the mirror of consciousness, niścitya — having ascertained, evaṁ — thus, tyaja — abandon, bhrāntim — delusion, śuddha-cit-bhāvana-kramāt — by the method of pure consciousness contemplation.
"Perfected by mere contemplation, based on the mirror of consciousness, having ascertained thus, abandon delusion by the method of pure consciousness contemplation."
ततस्त्वमप्यहमिव स्वतन्त्रस्तु भविष्यसि ।
इति श्रुत्वा मुनिसुतवचनं मुनिसत्तमः ॥ ९३ ॥
tatas tvam api aham iva sva-tantraḥ tu bhaviṣyasi ।
iti śrutvā muni-suta-vacanaṁ muni-sattamaḥ ॥ 93 ॥

tataḥ — then, tvam — you, api — also, aham — I, iva — like, sva-tantraḥ — independent, tu — but, bhaviṣyasi — will become, iti — thus, śrutvā — having heard, muni-suta-vacanam — the words of the sage's son, muni-sattamaḥ — the best of sages.
"Then you, like me, will become independent. Thus, having heard the words of the sage's son, the best of sages."
परित्यज्याखिलभ्रान्तिं ज्ञातज्ञेयः शुभाशयः ।
समाध्यभ्यासयोगेन संसाध्य निजभावनाम्‌ ॥ ९४ ॥
parityajya akhila-bhrāntiṁ jñāta-jñeyaḥ śubha-āśayaḥ ।
samādhi-abhyāsa-yogena saṁsādhya nija-bhāvanām ॥ 94 ॥

parityajya — having abandoned, akhila-bhrāntim — all delusion, jñāta-jñeyaḥ — knower of the knowable, śubha-āśayaḥ — of auspicious disposition, samādhi-abhyāsa-yogena — by the practice of meditation, saṁsādhya — having perfected, nija-bhāvanām — one's own contemplation.
"Then he, having abandoned all delusion, the knower of the knowable, of auspicious disposition, by the practice of meditation, having perfected one's own contemplation."
स्वातन्त्र्यमधिगम्याथ चिरकालं विहृत्य तु ।
देहाभासमथोन्मूल्य महागगनसंश्रयः ॥ ९५ ॥
sva-tantryam adhigamya atha cira-kālaṁ vihṛtya tu ।
deha-ābhāsam atha un-mūlya mahā-gagana-saṁśrayaḥ ॥ 95 ॥

sva-tantryam — independence, adhigamya — having attained, atha — then, cira-kālam — for a long time, vihṛtya — having enjoyed, tu — but, deha-ābhāsam — the appearance of the body, atha — then, un-mūlya — having uprooted, mahā-gagana-saṁśrayaḥ — refuge in the great sky.
"Having attained independence, then for a long time having enjoyed, but then uprooting the appearance of the body, taking refuge in the great sky."
निर्वाणं परमं प्राप्तो महासेनोऽपि भार्गव ।
एवं जगत्‌ सत्यभावभावनामात्रहेतुतः ॥ ९६ ॥
nirvāṇaṁ paramaṁ prāpto mahāsenaḥ api bhārgava ।
evaṁ jagat satya-bhāva-bhāvanā-mātra-hetutaḥ ॥ 96 ॥

nirvāṇam — liberation, paramam — supreme, prāptaḥ — attained, mahāsenaḥ — Mahāsena, api — also, bhārgava — O descendant of Bhrigu, evaṁ — thus, jagat — world, satya-bhāva-bhāvanā-mātra-hetutaḥ — true due to the cause of mere contemplation of existence.
"Mahāsena also attained supreme liberation, O descendant of Bhrigu. Thus, the world is true due to the cause of mere contemplation of existence."
भाति सत्यात्मरूपेण विमृशैतद्‌ भृगूद्वह ।
विचारेण शमं यायाद्‌ भ्रान्तिस्ते चित्तसंश्रया ॥ ९७ ॥
bhāti satya-ātma-rūpeṇa vimṛśa etat bhṛgu-udvaha ।
vicāreṇa śamaṁ yāyāt bhrāntiḥ te citta-saṁśrayā ॥ 97 ॥

bhāti — shines, satya-ātma-rūpeṇa — in the form of true self, vimṛśa — consider, etat — this, bhṛgu-udvaha — O best of Bhrigus, vicāreṇa — by reflection, śamam — peace, yāyāt — would attain, bhrāntiḥ — delusion, te — your, citta-saṁśrayā — resting in the mind.
"Consider this, O best of Bhrigus, the world shines in the form of the true self. By reflection, your delusion, resting in the mind, would attain peace."

colophon.dev: इति श्रीत्रिपुरारहस्ये ज्ञानखण्डे शैललोकाख्यानं नाम चतुर्दशोऽध्यायः ॥
colophon.en: Thus ends the fourteenth chapter named "The Story of Shailaloka" in the revered Knowledge Section of Tripura Rahasya.

lines.text: इति श्रुत्वा शैललोकाख्यानमत्यद्भुतं तदा ।
भूयोऽत्यन्तं विस्मितोऽभूद्‌ रामो भृगुकुलोद्वहः ॥ १ ॥
iti śrutvā śaila-loka-ākhyānam atyadbhutam tadā ।
bhūyaḥ atyantaṁ vismitaḥ abhūt rāmaḥ bhṛgu-kula-udvahaḥ ॥ 1 ॥

iti — thus, śrutvā — having heard, śaila-loka-ākhyānam — the story of the mountain world, atyadbhutam — very wonderful, tadā — then, bhūyaḥ — again, atyantam — extremely, vismitaḥ — astonished, abhūt — became, rāmaḥ — Rama, bhṛgu-kula-udvahaḥ — the best of the Bhrigu lineage.
"Thus, having heard the very wonderful story of the mountain world, Rama, the best of the Bhrigu lineage, was again extremely astonished."
विमृश्य गुरुणा प्रोक्तं बुद्धया निश्चित्य शुद्धया ।
दत्तात्रेयं पुनर्गत्वा नत्वा पप्रच्छ सादरम्‌ ॥ २ ॥
vimṛśya guruṇā proktam buddhyā niścitya śuddhayā ।
dattātreyaṁ punar gatvā natvā papraccha sādarām ॥ 2 ॥

vimṛśya — reflecting, guruṇā — by the guru, proktam — said, buddhyā — with intellect, niścitya — ascertaining, śuddhayā — pure, dattātreyaṁ — to Dattatreya, punaḥ — again, gatvā — having gone, natvā — bowing, papraccha — asked, sādarām — with respect.
"Reflecting on what was said by the guru, with pure intellect, ascertaining, he again went to Dattatreya, bowed, and respectfully asked."
भगवन्‌ यत्त्वया प्रोक्तमाख्यानैर्विविधैस्तु तत्‌ ।
तत्र सारमियज्ज्ञातं मयाऽत्यन्तं विचारतः ॥ ३ ॥
bhagavan yat tvayā proktam ākhyānaiḥ vividhaiḥ tu tat ।
tatra sāram iyat jñātam mayā atyantam vicārataḥ ॥ 3 ॥

bhagavan — O Lord, yat — which, tvayā — by you, proktam — said, ākhyānaiḥ — stories, vividhaiḥ — various, tu — but, tat — that, tatra — there, sāram — essence, iyat — this much, jñātam — known, mayā — by me, atyantam — thoroughly, vicārataḥ — considering.
"O Lord, what you said through various stories, I have thoroughly considered and known this much essence."
संवेदनं सत्यमेकं संवेद्यं तत्र कल्पितम्‌ ।
आदर्शनगरप्रख्यं मृषैव प्रविभावितम्‌ ॥ ४ ॥
saṁvedanam satyam ekaṁ saṁvedyam tatra kalpitam ।
ādarśa-nagara-prakhyaṁ mṛṣā eva pravibhāvitaṁ ॥ 4 ॥

saṁvedanam — consciousness, satyam — true, ekam — one, saṁvedyam — object of consciousness, tatra — there, kalpitam — imagined, ādarśa-nagara-prakhyam — like a city in a mirror, mṛṣā — false, eva — indeed, pravibhāvitaṁ — considered.
"Consciousness is the one truth, and the object of consciousness is imagined there, like a city in a mirror, indeed considered false."
सा चितिः परमा शक्तिः संविद्रूपा महेश्वरी ।
स्वात्मभित्तौ जगच्चित्रमव्यक्तादिप्रभेदितम्‌ ॥ ५ ॥
sā citiḥ paramā śaktiḥ saṁvid-rūpā maheśvarī ।
sva-ātma-bhittau jagat-citram avyakta-ādi-prabheditam ॥ 5 ॥

sā — she, citiḥ — consciousness, paramā — supreme, śaktiḥ — power, saṁvid-rūpā — in the form of knowledge, maheśvarī — the great goddess, sva-ātma-bhittau — on her own self as the background, jagat-citram — the picture of the world, avyakta-ādi-prabheditam — differentiated from the unmanifest, etc.

"She, consciousness, is the supreme power, in the form of knowledge, the great goddess, who projects the picture of the world on her own self as the background, differentiated from the unmanifest, etc."
भासयेत्‌ स्वातन्त्र्यमात्राद्‌ निरुपादानहेतुकम्‌ ।
एतावत्तु मया ज्ञातं विचार्यं सूक्षमया धिया ॥ ६ ॥
bhāsayet svātantrya-mātrāt nirupādāna-hetukam ।
etāvat tu mayā jñātam vicārya sūkṣma-yā dhiyā ॥ 6 ॥

bhāsayet — manifests, svātantrya-mātrāt — due to mere independence, nirupādāna-hetukam — without any cause, etāvat — this much, tu — but, mayā — by me, jñātam — known, vicārya — considering, sūkṣma-yā dhiyā — with subtle intellect.
"Manifests due to mere independence, without any cause. This much I have known, considering with subtle intellect."
किन्त्वेवंविधसंवित्तिर्वेद्यवन्ध्या निरूपिता ।
उपलब्धुमशक्यैव सवेद्यायाः सदा स्थिते ॥ ७ ॥
kintu evaṁ-vidha-saṁvittiḥ vedya-vandhyā nirūpitā ।
upalabdhum aśakyā eva sa-vedyāyāḥ sadā sthite ॥ 7 ॥

kintu — but, evaṁ-vidha-saṁvittiḥ — such consciousness, vedya-vandhyā — barren of the object of knowledge, nirūpitā — described, upalabdhum — to attain, aśakyā — impossible, eva — indeed, sa-vedyāyāḥ — with the object of knowledge, sadā sthite — always present.
"But such consciousness, described as barren of the object of knowledge, is indeed impossible to attain, as the object of knowledge is always present."
वेद्यं विना तु संवित्तेः कथं स्यादुपलम्भनम्‌ ।
उपलम्भं विना तस्याः पुरुषार्थो न विद्यते ॥ ८ ॥
vedyam vinā tu saṁvitteḥ kathaṁ syāt upalambhanam ।
upalambhaṁ vinā tasyāḥ puruṣārthaḥ na vidyate ॥ 8 ॥

vedyam — object of knowledge, vinā — without, tu — but, saṁvitteḥ — of consciousness, kathaṁ — how, syāt — can be, upalambhanam — perception, upalambham — perception, vinā — without, tasyāḥ — of that, puruṣārthaḥ — purpose, na vidyate — does not exist.
"Without the object of knowledge, how can there be perception of consciousness? Without perception, there is no purpose for it."
पुरुषार्थोऽपि मोक्षः स्यात्‌ स वा किंविध उच्यते ।
विज्ञाने सति मोक्षः स्यान्मुक्ते व्यवहृतिः कथम्‌ ॥ ९ ॥
puruṣārthaḥ api mokṣaḥ syāt sa vā kim-vidhaḥ ucyate ।
vijñāne sati mokṣaḥ syāt mukte vyavahṛtiḥ katham ॥ 9 ॥

puruṣārthaḥ — purpose, api — also, mokṣaḥ — liberation, syāt — would be, sa — it, vā — or, kim-vidhaḥ — of what kind, ucyate — is said, vijñāne — in knowledge, sati — being, mokṣaḥ — liberation, syāt — would be, mukte — in liberation, vyavahṛtiḥ — activity, katham — how.
"Purpose, even liberation, how would it be? Of what kind is it said? With knowledge being, liberation would be, but in liberation, how is activity?"
ज्ञानिनोऽपि च दृश्यन्ते व्यवहारपरायणाः ।
कथं तेषां हि संवेद्यमुक्तं संवेदनं स्थितम्‌ ॥ १० ॥
jñāninaḥ api ca dṛśyante vyavahāra-parāyaṇāḥ ।
kathaṁ teṣāṁ hi saṁvedyam uktaṁ saṁvedanam sthitam ॥ 10 ॥

jñāninaḥ — knowers, api — also, ca — and, dṛśyante — are seen, vyavahāra-parāyaṇāḥ — devoted to activity, katham — how, teṣām — their, hi — indeed, saṁvedyam — object of consciousness, uktam — said, saṁvedanam — consciousness, sthitam — established.
"Knowers are seen devoted to activity. How indeed is their object of consciousness said to be established in consciousness?"
स्थितायां शुद्धसंवित्तौ व्यवहारः कथं भवेत्‌ ।
विज्ञानमेकरूपं वै मोक्षोऽप्येकः फलं भवेत्‌ ॥ ११ ॥
sthitāyāṁ śuddha-saṁvittau vyavahāraḥ katham bhavet ।
vijñānam eka-rūpam vai mokṣaḥ api ekaḥ phalam bhavet ॥ 11 ॥

sthitāyām — being established, śuddha-saṁvittau — in pure consciousness, vyavahāraḥ — activity, katham — how, bhavet — can be, vijñānam — knowledge, eka-rūpam — of one form, vai — indeed, mokṣaḥ — liberation, api — also, ekaḥ — one, phalam — result, bhavet — would be.
"Being established in pure consciousness, how can there be activity? Knowledge being of one form, liberation would indeed be one result."
तत्कथं ज्ञानिनां भेदः स्थितौ लोके हि दुश्यते ।
केचित्‌ कर्म प्रकुर्वन्ति काले सच्छास्त्रचोदितम्‌ ॥ १२ ॥
tat katham jñānināṁ bhedaḥ sthitau loke hi dṛśyate ।
kecit karma prakurvanti kāle sat-śāstra-coditam ॥ 12 ॥

tat — that, katham — how, jñāninām — of the knowers, bhedaḥ — difference, sthitau — in state, loke — in the world, hi — indeed, dṛśyate — is seen, kecit — some, karma — action, prakurvanti — perform, kāle — in time, sat-śāstra-coditam — as per the true scriptures.
"How is the difference in state of the knowers seen in the world? Some perform actions as per the true scriptures in time."
केचित्‌ समाराधयन्ति देवतां भिन्नवर्त्मभिः ।
केचित्‌ समाधिपरमाः संहृतेन्द्रियमण्डलाः ॥ १३ ॥
kecit samārādhayanti devatāṁ bhinna-vartmabhiḥ ।
kecit samādhi-paramāḥ saṁhṛta-indriya-maṇḍalāḥ ॥ 13 ॥

kecit — some, samārādhayanti — worship, devatām — deities, bhinna-vartmabhiḥ — by different paths, kecit — some, samādhi-paramāḥ — devoted to meditation, saṁhṛta-indriya-maṇḍalāḥ — with controlled senses.
"Some worship deities by different paths, while some are devoted to meditation with controlled senses."
केचित्तपः प्रकुर्वन्ति देहेन्द्रियविशोषणम्‌ ।
केचिच्छिष्यान्‌ बोधयन्ति पृथक्प्रवचनैः स्फुटम्‌ ॥ १४ ॥
kecit tapaḥ prakurvanti deha-indriya-viśoṣaṇam ।
kecit śiṣyān bodhayanti pṛthak-pravacanaiḥ sphuṭam ॥ 14 ॥

kecit — some, tapaḥ — austerity, prakurvanti — perform, deha-indriya-viśoṣaṇam — drying up the body and senses, kecit — some, śiṣyān — disciples, bodhayanti — enlighten, pṛthak-pravacanaiḥ — by separate discourses, sphuṭam — clearly.
"Some perform austerities drying up the body and senses, while some enlighten disciples by separate discourses clearly."
केचिद्राज्यं प्रशासन्ति दण्डनीत्युक्तवर्त्मना ।
केचित्‌ प्रवादं कुर्वन्ति सदस्यु प्रतिवादिभिः ॥ १५ ॥
kecit rājyaṁ praśāsanti daṇḍa-nīti-ukta-vartmanā ।
kecit pravādaṁ kurvanti sadasyu prati-vādibhiḥ ॥ 15 ॥

kecit — some, rājyaṁ — kingdom, praśāsanti — govern, daṇḍa-nīti-ukta-vartmanā — by the path of the law of punishment, kecit — some, pravādam — debate, kurvanti — do, sadasyu — in assemblies, prati-vādibhiḥ — with opponents.
"Some govern kingdoms by the path of the law of punishment, while some debate in assemblies with opponents."
केचिच्छास्त्राणि विविधान्यजस्त्रं रचयन्ति वै ।
अन्ये केवलमुग्धत्वमावहन्ति सदैव हि ॥ १६ ॥
kecit śāstrāṇi vividhāni ajasraṁ racayanti vai ।
anye kevalam ugdhatvam āvahanti sadaiva hi ॥ 16 ॥

kecit — some, śāstrāṇi — scriptures, vividhāni — various, ajasraṁ — constantly, racayanti — compose, vai — indeed, anye — others, kevalam — merely, ugdhatvam — foolishness, āvahanti — bring, sadaiva — always, hi — indeed.
"Some constantly compose various scriptures, while others merely always bring foolishness."
केऽपि लोकविगर्ह्यां तु वृत्तिं नित्यमिहास्थिताः ।
त इमे ज्ञानिन इति प्रथिता भूरिशोचनैः ॥ १७ ॥
ke api loka-vigarhyāṁ tu vṛttiṁ nityam iha āsthitāḥ ।
ta ime jñānina iti prathitā bhūri-śocanaiḥ ॥ 17 ॥

ke api — some, loka-vigarhyām — condemned by the world, tu — but, vṛttim — livelihood, nityam — always, iha — here, āsthitāḥ — engaged, ta — they, ime — these, jñāninaḥ — knowers, iti — thus, prathitāḥ — famous, bhūri-śocanaiḥ — much criticized.
"Some are always engaged in livelihoods condemned by the world, yet these knowers are thus famous and much criticized."
तत्कथं साधनफलाभेदेऽपि स्थितिभिन्नता ।
किमेते समविज्ञानास्तारतम्यमुताश्रिताः ॥ १८ ॥
tat katham sādhana-phala-abhede api sthiti-bhinnatā ।
kim ete sama-vijñānāḥ tāratamyam uta āśritāḥ ॥ 18 ॥

tat — that, katham — how, sādhana-phala-abhede — in the absence of difference in practice and result, api — also, sthiti-bhinnatā — difference in state, kim — whether, ete — these, sama-vijñānāḥ — of equal knowledge, tāratamyam — difference, uta — or, āśritāḥ — resorted to.
"How is there a difference in state despite the absence of difference in practice and result? Are these knowers of equal knowledge, or have they resorted to difference?"
एतत्सर्वमशेषेण प्रवक्तुं मे समर्हसि ।
शिष्येऽनन्यशरण्ये ते निसर्गसदयं मनः ॥ १९ ॥
etat sarvam aśeṣeṇa pravaktum me samarhasi ।
śiṣye ananya-śaraṇye te nisarga-sadayaṁ manaḥ ॥ 19 ॥

etat — this, sarvam — all, aśeṣeṇa — completely, pravaktum — to explain, me — to me, samarhasi — you are able, śiṣye — disciple, ananya-śaraṇye — with no other refuge, te — your, nisarga-sadayaṁ — naturally compassionate, manaḥ — mind.
"You are able to explain all this to me completely. I, your disciple, have no other refuge, and your mind is naturally compassionate."
इत्यत्रिसूनुरापृष्टो भार्गवेण प्रसन्नधीः ।
मत्वा योग्यं प्रश्नजातं प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमे ॥ २० ॥
iti atri-sūnuḥ āpṛṣṭaḥ bhārgaveṇa prasanna-dhīḥ ।
matvā yogyaṁ praśna-jātaṁ pravaktum upacakrame ॥ 20 ॥

iti — thus, atri-sūnuḥ — Atri's son (Dattatreya), āpṛṣṭaḥ — asked, bhārgaveṇa — by Bhargava, prasanna-dhīḥ — with a clear mind, matvā — considering, yogyaṁ — appropriate, praśna-jātaṁ — series of questions, pravaktum — to explain, upacakrame — began.
"Thus, Atri's son (Dattatreya), asked by Bhargava with a clear mind, considering the series of questions appropriate, began to explain."
राम बुद्धिमतां श्रेष्ठ नूनं स्पृशसि तत्पदम्‌ ।
सद्विमर्शपरो यस्त्वमतो ज्ञातुं प्रभावितः ॥ २१ ॥
rāma buddhimatāṁ śreṣṭha nūnaṁ spṛśasi tat-padam ।
sad-vimarśa-paraḥ yaḥ tvam ataḥ jñātuṁ prabhāvitaḥ ॥ 21 ॥

rāma — O Rāma, buddhimatām — among the wise, śreṣṭha — best, nūnaṁ — certainly, spṛśasi — you reach, tat-padam — that state, sad-vimarśa-paraḥ — devoted to good reflection, yaḥ — who, tvam — you, ataḥ — therefore, jñātuṁ — to know, prabhāvitaḥ — endowed.
"O Rāma, best among the wise, you certainly will reach that state, being devoted to good reflection, therefore you are endowed to know."
एतदेव हि तच्छक्तिपातो यत्सद्विमर्शनम्‌ ।
भगवच्छक्तिपातेन विना कः श्रेय आप्नुयात्‌ ॥ २२ ॥
etad-eva hi tac-chakti-pāto yat-sad-vimarśanam ।
bhagavat-śakti-pātena vinā kaḥ śreya āpnuyāt ॥ 22 ॥

etat-eva — this indeed, hi — indeed, tat-śakti-pātaḥ — that grace, yat-sad-vimarśanam — which is good reflection, bhagavat-śakti-pātena — by divine grace, vinā — without, kaḥ — who, śreyaḥ — auspiciousness, āpnuyāt — attains.
"This indeed is that grace, which is good reflection; without divine grace, who attains auspiciousness?"
कृत्यमात्मदेवताया जानीह्येतावदेव हि ।
यत्‌ सद्विमर्शनं नित्यं वर्धयेत्‌ सुप्रसादिता ॥ २३ ॥
kṛtyam-ātmadevatāyā jānīhy-etāvad-eva hi ।
yat-sad-vimarśanam nityaṁ vardhayet suprasāditā ॥ 23 ॥

kṛtyam — duty, ātma-devatāyāḥ — of one's own deity, jānīhi — know, etāvat — this much, eva — indeed, hi — indeed, yat — which, sad-vimarśanam — good reflection, nityam — always, vardhayet — increases, suprasāditā — well pleased.
"Know this much as the duty of one's own deity; good reflection always increases when well pleased."
यत्‌ त्वया विदितं तत्तु तादृक्‌ सत्यं नहीतरत्‌ ।
किन्तु तत्‌ तादृशमपि त्वयोक्तं परचिद्वपुः ॥ २४ ॥
yat tvayā viditaṁ tat tu tādṛk satyam na hi itarat ।
kintu tat tādṛśam api tvayoktaṁ para-cid-vapuḥ ॥ 24 ॥

yat — which, tvayā — by you, viditam — known, tat — that, tu — indeed, tādṛk — such, satyam — true, na — not, hi — indeed, itarat — otherwise, kintu — but, tat — that, tādṛśam — such, api — even, tvayā — by you, uktam — spoken, para-cid-vapuḥ — transcendental consciousness body.
"What you have known is indeed true; it is not otherwise. But even that which is spoken by you, the transcendental consciousness body."
न ते सुविदितं राम यत एवं वदस्यतः ।
ताटस्थ्येन तु यो यावद्वेद तावन्न वेद वै ॥ २५ ॥
na te suviditam rāma yat evaṁ vadasyataḥ ।
tāṭasthyena tu yaḥ yāvat veda tāvat na veda vai ॥ 25 ॥

na — not, te — by you, suviditam — well known, rāma — O Rāma, yat — what, evam — thus, vadasyataḥ — speaking, tāṭasthyena — with detachment, tu — but, yaḥ — who, yāvat — as long as, veda — knows, tāvat — so long, na veda vai — indeed does not know.
"What you have spoken is not well known by you, O Rāma. But as long as one knows with detachment (from experience), indeed, he does not know."
यतः सा विदिता सम्यक्‌ ताटस्थ्यमुपशामयेत्‌ ।
तटस्थसंवेदनं तु स्वप्नसंवेदनोपमम्‌ ॥ २६ ॥
yataḥ sā viditā samyak tāṭasthyam-upaśāmayet ।
taṭastha-saṁvedanam tu svapna-saṁvedana-upamam ॥ 26 ॥

yataḥ — because, sā — that, viditā — known, samyak — properly, tāṭasthyam — detachment, upaśāmayet — dispels, taṭastha-saṁvedanam — detached knowledge, tu — but, svapna-saṁvedana-upamam — like dream knowledge.
"Because when that is properly known, it dispels detachment. But detached knowledge is like dream knowledge."
यथा स्वप्तनिधिप्राप्तिः पुरुषाणां निरर्थिका ।
तथा तटस्थविज्ञानममुख्यफलदं भवेत्‌ ॥ २७ ॥
yathā svapna-nidhi-prāptiḥ puruṣāṇāṁ nirarthikā ।
tathā taṭastha-vijñānam amukhya-phala-daṁ bhavet ॥ 27 ॥

yathā — as, svapna-nidhi-prāptiḥ — dream treasure attainment, puruṣāṇām — for people, nirarthikā — useless, tathā — thus, taṭastha-vijñānam — detached knowledge, amukhya-phala-dam — giving non-primary results, bhavet — would be.
"As dream treasure attainment is useless for people, thus detached knowledge would give non-primary results."
अत्र ते कथयिष्यामि प्राग्वृत्तमतिशोभनम्‌ ।
पुरा विदेहेषु कश्चिदासीद्‌ राजा सुधार्मिकः ॥ २८ ॥
atra te kathayiṣyāmi prāg-vṛttam atiśobhanam ।
purā videheṣu kaścid āsīd rājā su-dhārmikaḥ ॥ 28 ॥

atra — here, te — to you, kathayiṣyāmi — I will tell, prāg-vṛttam — ancient event, atiśobhanam — very wonderful, purā — formerly, videheṣu — in Videha, kaścit — some, āsīd — was, rājā — king, su-dhārmikaḥ — very righteous.
"Here I will tell you a very wonderful ancient event. Formerly, in Videha, there was a very righteous king."
वृद्धप्रज्ञो हि जनकः प्रविज्ञातपरावरः ।
स कदाचित्‌ स्वात्मदेवीमीजे क्रतुभिरुत्तमैः ॥ २९ ॥
vṛddha-prajño hi janakaḥ pravijñāta-para-avaraḥ ।
sa kadācit svātma-devīm īje kratu-bhiḥ uttamaiḥ ॥ 29 ॥

vṛddha-prajñaḥ — wise elder, hi — indeed, janakaḥ — Janaka, pravijñāta-para-avaraḥ — well versed in higher and lower knowledge, saḥ — he, kadācit — once, svātma-devīm — his own deity, īje — worshipped, kratu-bhiḥ — with rituals, uttamaiḥ — supreme.
"Janaka, the wise elder, well versed in higher and lower knowledge, once worshipped his own deity with supreme rituals."
तत्राजग्मुर्ब्राह्मणाद्या विद्यावन्तस्तपस्विनः ।
कलाभिज्ञा वैदिकाश्च यज्वानश्चापि सत्रिणः ॥ ३० ॥
tatra ājagmuḥ brāhmaṇa-ādyā vidyāvantaḥ tapasvinaḥ ।
kalā-abhi-jñāḥ vaidikāḥ ca yajvānaḥ ca api satriṇaḥ ॥ 30 ॥

tatra — there, ājagmuḥ — came, brāhmaṇa-ādyāḥ — Brāhmaṇas and others, vidyāvantaḥ — learned, tapasvinaḥ — ascetics, kalā-abhi-jñāḥ — skilled in arts, vaidikāḥ — Vedic scholars, ca — and, yajvānaḥ — ritualists, ca — and, api — also, satriṇaḥ — possessors of sacrifices.
"There came Brāhmaṇas and others, learned ascetics, skilled in arts, Vedic scholars, ritualists, and possessors of sacrifices."
तत्काल एव वरुणो यष्टुं समुपचक्रमे ।
तेनोपहूता विप्राद्या न ययुस्तत्र भूरिशः ॥ ३१ ॥
tat-kāla eva varuṇaḥ yaṣṭuṁ samupacakrame ।
tena upahūtā vipra-ādyā na yayuḥ tatra bhūriśaḥ ॥ 31 ॥

tat-kāla — at that time, eva — indeed, varuṇaḥ — Varuṇa, yaṣṭum — to sacrifice, samupacakrame — began, tena — by him, upahūtāḥ — invited, vipra-ādyāḥ — Brāhmaṇas and others, na — not, yayuḥ — went, tatra — there, bhūriśaḥ — many.
"At that time, sacrifice to Varuṇa started, and many invited Brāhmaṇas and others did not go there."
जनके ह्यभिसंप्रीताः पूजितास्तेन तर्पिताः ।
अथाजगाम वरुणदायादो बौद्धसम्पदा ॥ ३२ ॥
janake hi abhisampṛtāḥ pūjitāḥ tena tarpitaḥ ।
atha ājagāma varuṇa-dāyādaḥ bauddha-sampadā ॥ 32 ॥

janake — by Janaka, hi — indeed, abhisampṛtāḥ — pleased, pūjitāḥ — honored, tena — by him, tarpitaḥ — satisfied, atha — then, ājagāma — came, varuṇa-dāyādaḥ — Varuṇa's son, bauddha-sampadā — with Buddhist wealth.
"Indeed, pleased by Janaka, honored and satisfied by him, then came Varuṇa's son with Buddhist wealth."
विप्रवेषधरो नेतुं ब्राह्मणान्‌ कूटवर्त्मना ।
आसाद्य यज्ञसदनं नृपं संयोज्य चाशिषा ॥ ३३ ॥
vipra-veṣa-dharaḥ netuṁ brāhmaṇān kūṭa-vartmanā ।
āsādya yajña-sadanaṁ nṛpaṁ saṁyojya ca āśiṣā ॥ 33 ॥

vipra-veṣa-dharaḥ — in the guise of a Brāhmaṇa, netum — to lead, brāhmaṇān — Brāhmaṇas, kūṭa-vartmanā — by deceit, āsādya — reaching, yajña-sadanam — sacrificial hall, nṛpam — king, saṁyojya — uniting, ca — and, āśiṣā — with blessings.
"In the guise of a Brāhmaṇa, to lead Brāhmaṇas by deceit, reaching the sacrificial hall, uniting the king with blessings."
आक्षिपत्तत्र सभ्यांस्तु शृण्वता च सभासदाम्‌ ।
राजंस्ते यज्ञसदनमत्यन्तं नैव शोभते ॥ ३४ ॥
ākṣipat tatra sabhyān tu śṛṇvatā ca sabhā-sadām ।
rājan te yajña-sadanam atyantaṁ naiva śobhate ॥ 34 ॥

ākṣipat — reproached, tatra — there, sabhyān — the members, tu — but, śṛṇvatā — listening, ca — and, sabhā-sadām — assembly members, rājan — O King, te — your, yajña-sadanam — sacrificial hall, atyantam — greatly, na — not, eva — indeed, śobhate — shines.
"He reproached the members there, while the assembly members listened. 'O King, your sacrificial hall does not shine greatly.'"
कमलाकरवत्‌ काककङ्कवृन्दस्य सञ्चयात्‌ ।
सभा विद्वत्समुदयैः शोभिनी शोभतेतराम्‌ ॥ ३५ ॥
kamalākara-vat kāka-kaṅka-vṛndasya sañcayāt ।
sabhā vidvat-samudayaiḥ śobhinī śobhate-tarām ॥ 35 ॥

kamalākara-vat — like a lotus pond, kāka-kaṅka-vṛndasya — of crows and cranes, sañcayāt — due to assembly, sabhā — assembly, vidvat-samudayaiḥ — with learned gatherings, śobhinī — shining, śobhate-tarām — shines greatly.
"Like a lotus pond filled with crows and cranes, the assembly shines greatly with learned gatherings."
शारदं हंससङ्घातैः सपद्मं तु सरो यथा ।
तदत्र विद्याविशदं न पश्याम्येकमप्यलम्‌ ॥ ३६ ॥
śāradaṁ haṁsa-saṅghātaiḥ sa-padmaṁ tu saro yathā ।
tat atra vidyā-viśadam na paśyāmi ekam api alam ॥ 36 ॥

śāradaṁ — autumnal, haṁsa-saṅghātaiḥ — with flocks of swans, sa-padmaṁ — with lotuses, tu — indeed, saraḥ — lake, yathā — as, tat — that, atra — here, vidyā-viśadam — clear knowledge, na paśyāmi — I do not see, ekam api — even one, alam — sufficiently.
"As an autumnal lake with flocks of swans and lotuses, here I do not see even one clear knowledge sufficiently."
स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि नात्र मे संस्थितिर्भवेत्‌ ।
कथं सभामिमां मूर्खप्रचुरां संविशाम्यहम्‌ ॥ ३७ ॥
svasti te astu gamiṣyāmi na atra me saṁsthitir bhavet। kathaṁ sabhām imāṁ mūrkha-pracurāṁ saṁviśāmi aham॥37॥

svasti te astu — may it be well with you, gamiṣyāmi — I will go, na — not, atra — here, me — my, saṁsthitih bhavet — stay will be, katham — how, sabhām imām — this assembly, mūrkha-pracurām — filled with fools, saṁviśāmi — I enter, aham — I.
"May it be well with you; I will go. My stay here will not be. How can I enter this assembly filled with fools?"
एवं वारुणिना प्रोक्ताः सभ्याश्चुक्रुधुरञ्जसा ।
किमरे द्विजबन्धो त्वमधिक्षिपसि सर्वत: ॥ ३८ ॥
evaṁ vāruṇinā proktāḥ sabhyāḥ cukrudhuḥ añjasā ।
kim are dvija-bandho tvam adhikṣipasi sarvataḥ ॥ 38 ॥

evam — thus, vāruṇinā — by Varuṇa's son, proktāḥ — addressed, sabhyāḥ — the members, cukrudhuḥ — became angry, añjasā — immediately, kim — why, are — O, dvija-bandho — O relative of Brāhmaṇas, tvam — you, adhikṣipasi — insult, sarvataḥ — everywhere.
"Thus addressed by Varuṇa's son, the members immediately became angry. 'Why, O relative of Brāhmaṇas, do you insult everyone?'"
केयं तवेदृशी विद्या यया सर्वे वयं जिताः ।
वृथा कत्थसि दुर्बुद्धे जित्वाऽस्मांस्त्वं गमिष्यसि ॥ ३९ ॥
ka iyam tava edṛśī vidyā yayā sarve vayaṁ jitāḥ ।
vṛthā katthasi durbuddhe jitvā asmān tvaṁ gamiṣyasi ॥ 39 ॥

kaḥ — what, iyam — this, tava — your, edṛśī — such, vidyā — knowledge, yayā — by which, sarve — all, vayam — we, jitāḥ — conquered, vṛthā — uselessly, katthasi — you boast, durbuddhe — O foolish one, jitvā — conquering, asmān — us, tvam — you, gamiṣyasi — will go.
"What is this knowledge of yours by which you have conquered all of us? Uselessly you boast, O foolish one; having conquered us, you will go."
प्रायो भूलोकसंस्थाना विद्वांसः सङ्गताः खलु ।
किं त्वं भूलोकमेवाद्य जेतुमिच्छसि दुर्मते ॥ ४० ॥
prāyaḥ bhūloka-saṁsthānā vidvāṁsaḥ saṅgatāḥ khalu ।
kim tvam bhūloka-meva adya jetum icchasi durmate ॥ 40 ॥

prāyaḥ — mostly, bhūloka-saṁsthānāḥ — situated in the earthly realm, vidvāṁsaḥ — scholars, saṅgatāḥ — assembled, khalu — indeed, kim — why, tvam — you, bhūloka-meva — only the earthly realm, adya — today, jetum — to conquer, icchasi — wish, durmate — O evil-minded one.
"Mostly, scholars situated in the earthly realm have indeed assembled. Why, O evil-minded one, do you wish to conquer only the earthly realm today?"
ब्रूहि का ते भवेद्विद्या ययाऽस्मान्‌ जेतुमिच्छसि ।
इत्युक्तवत्सु सभ्येषु वारुणिः पुनराह तान्‌ ॥ ४१ ॥
brūhi kā te bhavet vidyā yayā asmān jetum icchasi ।
iti uktavatsu sabhyeṣu vāruṇiḥ punaḥ āha tān ॥ 41 ॥

brūhi — tell, kā — what, te — your, bhavet — is, vidyā — knowledge, yayā — by which, asmān — us, jetum — to conquer, icchasi — you desire, iti — thus, uktavatsu — when said, sabhyeṣu — by the members, vāruṇiḥ — Varuṇa's son, punaḥ — again, āha — said, tān — to them.
"Tell, what is your knowledge by which you desire to conquer us?" Thus, when the members said this, Varuṇa's son again said to them.
समयेन विजेष्यामि सर्वान्‌ वः क्षणमात्रतः ।
अहं जितो भवद्भिस्तु समुद्रे स्यां निमज्जितः ॥ ४२ ॥
samayena vijeṣyāmi sarvān vaḥ kṣaṇa-mātrataḥ ।
ahaṁ jitaḥ bhavadbhiḥ tu samudre syām nimajjitaḥ ॥ 42 ॥

samayena — by agreement, vijeṣyāmi — I will conquer, sarvān — all, vaḥ — you, kṣaṇa-mātrataḥ — in a moment, ahaṁ — I, jitaḥ — conquered, bhavadbhiḥ — by you, tu — but, samudre — in the ocean, syām — shall be, nimajjitaḥ — submerged.
"By agreement, I will conquer all of you in a moment. If I am conquered by you, I shall be submerged in the ocean."
युष्मास्वहं मज्जयामि जितं जितमथापि वा ।
उपेत्यैवं तु समयं विवदन्तु मया सहं ॥ ४३ ॥
yuṣmāsu ahaṁ majjayāmi jitaṁ jitam atha api vā ।
upetya evaṁ tu samayaṁ vivadantu mayā sahaṁ ॥ 43 ॥

yuṣmāsu — in you, ahaṁ — I, majjayāmi — will submerge, jitam — conquered, jitam — conquered, atha — or, api — also, vā — either, upetya — approaching, evaṁ — thus, tu — but, samayaṁ — agreement, vivadantu — let argue, mayā — with me, saham — together.
"I will submerge you if conquered, or be submerged if I conquer. Approaching thus, let us argue by this agreement."
इत्युक्ताः सम्मतिं चक्रुः सभ्या वादाय तेन तु ।
विवादं चक्रुरत्यन्तं तेन वारुणिना द्विजाः ॥ ४४ ॥
iti uktāḥ sammatim cakruḥ sabhyāḥ vādaya tena tu ।
vivādaṁ cakruḥ atyantam tena vāruṇinā dvijāḥ ॥ 44 ॥

iti — thus, uktāḥ — said, sammatim — agreement, cakruḥ — made, sabhyāḥ — the members, vādaya — to argue, tena — by him, tu — but, vivādam — argument, cakruḥ — did, atyantam — intensely, tena — by him, vāruṇinā — by Varuṇa's son, dvijāḥ — the Brāhmaṇas.
"Thus said, the members agreed to argue with him. The Brāhmaṇas intensely argued with Varuṇa's son."
जिजेगाय वारुणिर्विप्रान्‌ वितण्डाजल्पवर्त्मना ।
सिन्धौ निमज्जिता विप्राः शतशोऽथ सहस्त्रशः ॥ ४५ ॥
jijegāya vāruṇiḥ viprān vitaṇḍā-jalpa-vartmanā ।
sindhau nimajjitāḥ viprāḥ śataśaḥ atha sahastraśaḥ ॥ 45 ॥

jijegāya — conquered, vāruṇiḥ — Varuṇa's son, viprān — Brāhmaṇas, vitaṇḍā-jalpa-vartmanā — by deceitful arguments, sindhau — in the ocean, nimajjitāḥ — submerged, viprāḥ — Brāhmaṇas, śataśaḥ — by hundreds, atha — and, sahastraśaḥ — by thousands.
"Varuṇa's son conquered the Brāhmaṇas by deceitful arguments, submerging hundreds and thousands of Brāhmaṇas in the ocean."
निमज्जितास्तु ये विप्रा दूतैस्तैर्वारुणैर्हृताः ।
वारुणं यज्ञमासाद्य मुमुदुः पूजिता भृशम्‌ ॥ ४६ ॥
nimajjitāḥ tu ye viprāḥ dūtaiḥ taiḥ vāruṇaiḥ hṛtāḥ ।
vāruṇam yajñam āsādya mumuduḥ pūjitāḥ bhṛśam ॥ 46 ॥

nimajjitāḥ — submerged, tu — but, ye — those, viprāḥ — Brāhmaṇas, dūtaiḥ — by the messengers, taiḥ — by them, vāruṇaiḥ — of Varuṇa, hṛtāḥ — taken, vāruṇam — Varuṇa's, yajñam — sacrifice, āsādya — approaching, mumuduḥ — rejoiced, pūjitāḥ — honored, bhṛśam — greatly.
"The Brāhmaṇas who were submerged were taken by Varuṇa's messengers. Approaching Varuṇa's sacrifice, they rejoiced, greatly honored."
मज्जितं पितरं श्रुत्वा कहोलं तत्सुतस्ततः ।
अष्टावक्रः समागत्य ज्ञानवैतण्ड्यजल्पकः ॥ ४७ ॥
majjitam pitaraṁ śrutvā kaholam tat-sutaḥ tataḥ ।
aṣṭāvakraḥ samāgatya jñāna-vaitaṇḍya-jalpakaḥ ॥ 47 ॥

majjitam — submerged, pitaraṁ — father, śrutvā — hearing, kaholam — Kahola, tat-sutaḥ — his son, tataḥ — then, aṣṭāvakraḥ — Aṣṭāvakra, samāgatya — arriving, jñāna-vaitaṇḍya-jalpakaḥ — one skilled in disputation and knowledge.
"Hearing that his father Kahola was submerged, then his son Aṣṭāvakra, skilled in disputation and knowledge, arrived."
विजित्य वारूणिं सिन्धावादिदेश निमज्जने ।
अथ प्रकाशमापन्नो वारुणिर्द्विजमुख्यकान्‌ ॥ ४८ ॥
vijitya vāruṇiṁ sindhau ādiśa nimajjane ।
atha prakāśam āpannaḥ vāruṇiḥ dvija-mukhyakān ॥ 48 ॥

vijitya — conquering, vāruṇim — Varuṇa's son, sindhau — in the ocean, ādiśa — commanded, nimajjane — in submersion, atha — then, prakāśam — clearly, āpannaḥ — becoming, vāruṇiḥ — Varuṇa's son, dvija-mukhyakān — the foremost Brāhmaṇas.
"Conquering Varuṇa's son, he commanded him to be submerged in the ocean. Then Varuṇa's son clearly summoned the foremost Brāhmaṇas."
समानयत्‌ स्वलोकस्थानष्टावक्रेण निर्जितः ।
अथागतेषु विप्रेषु कहोलतनयो भृशम्‌ ॥ ४९ ॥
samānayat sva-loka-sthān aṣṭāvakreṇa nirjitaḥ ।
atha āgateṣu vipreṣu kahola-tanayaḥ bhṛśam ॥ 49 ॥

samānayat — brought, sva-loka-sthān — from his own world, aṣṭāvakreṇa — by Aṣṭāvakra, nirjitaḥ — conquered, atha — then, āgateṣu — when arrived, vipreṣu — Brāhmaṇas, kahola-tanayaḥ — Kahola's son, bhṛśam — greatly.
"He brought them from his own world, having been conquered by Aṣṭāvakra. Then, when the Brāhmaṇas arrived, Kahola's son greatly."
विप्रान्‌ विमोचितान्‌ सर्वानत्यवर्तत दर्पतः ।
अष्टावक्रेण विमता विप्राः खेदमुपागताः ॥ ५० ॥
viprān vimocitān sarvān atyavartata darpataḥ ।
aṣṭāvakreṇa vimatāḥ viprāḥ khedam upāgatāḥ ॥ 50 ॥

viprān — the Brāhmaṇas, vimocitān — freed, sarvān — all, atyavartata — surpassed, darpataḥ — with pride, aṣṭāvakreṇa — by Aṣṭāvakra, vimatāḥ — defeated, viprāḥ — Brāhmaṇas, khedam — sorrow, upāgatāḥ — came.
"Freed all the Brāhmaṇas, he was surpassed with pride. Defeated by Aṣṭāvakra, the Brāhmaṇas came in sorrow."
तत्काल आगतां काञ्चित्‌ तापसीं शरणं ययुः ।
तान्‌ समाश्वास्य विप्रान्‌ सा काषायाम्बरवासिनी ॥ ५१ ॥
tatkāla āgatām kāñcit tāpasīṁ śaraṇaṁ yayuḥ ।
tān samāśvāsya viprān sā kāṣāya-ambara-vāsinī ॥ 51 ॥

tatkāla — at that time, āgatām — arrived, kāñcit — some, tāpasīm — ascetic woman, śaraṇam — refuge, yayuḥ — they took, tān — them, samāśvāsya — consoling, viprān — the Brāhmaṇas, sā — she, kāṣāya-ambara-vāsinī — wearing ochre robes.
"At that time, they took refuge in an ascetic woman who arrived. Consoling them, the Brāhmaṇas, she, wearing ochre robes."
जटिला नित्यतरुणी मनोहरवपुर्धरा ।
सभामुपेत्य प्रोवाच नृपेणाभिसुपूजिता ॥ ५२ ॥
jaṭilā nitya-taruṇī manohara-vapur-dharā ।
sabhām upetya provāca nṛpeṇa abhisu-pūjitā ॥ 52 ॥

jaṭilā — with matted hair, nitya-taruṇī — ever young, manohara-vapur-dharā — possessing a beautiful form, sabhām — assembly, upetya — approaching, provāca — spoke, nṛpeṇa — by the king, abhisu-pūjitā — highly honored.
"With matted hair, ever young, possessing a beautiful form, approaching the assembly, she spoke, highly honored by the king."
कहोलसुत वत्स त्वमत्यन्तं बुद्धिमानसि ।
त्वया विमोचिता विप्रा वादे निर्जित्य वारुणिम्‌ ॥ ५३ ॥
kahola-suta vatsa tvam atyantaṁ buddhimān asi ।
tvayā vimocitā viprā vāde nirjitya vāruṇim ॥ 53 ॥

kahola-suta — son of Kahola, vatsa — dear, tvam — you, atyantaṁ — greatly, buddhimān asi — are wise, tvayā — by you, vimocitāḥ — freed, viprāḥ — Brāhmaṇas, vāde — in argument, nirjitya — having conquered, vāruṇim — Varuṇa's son.
"Son of Kahola, dear, you are greatly wise. The Brāhmaṇas were freed by you, having conquered Varuṇa's son in argument."
अहं पृच्छामि किञ्चित्वां वद हित्वा सुकैतवम्‌ ।
यत्पदं विदितं सर्वामृतत्वप्रतिपादकम्‌ ॥ ५४ ॥
ahaṁ pṛcchāmi kiñcit tvāṁ vada hitvā su-kaitavam ।
yat-padaṁ viditaṁ sarva-amṛtatva-pratipādakam ॥ 54 ॥

aham — I, pṛcchāmi — ask, kiñcit — something, tvām — you, vada — tell, hitvā — leaving, su-kaitavam — deceit, yat-padam — which position, viditam — known, sarva — all, amṛtatva-pratipādakam — leading to immortality.
"I ask you something, tell without deceit, which position, when known, leads to immortality for all."
यत्पदे विदिते सर्वसन्देहः प्रलयं व्रजेत्‌ ।
अविज्ञातं न किञ्चित्‌ स्यादाशास्यं वा न किञ्चन ॥ ५५ ॥
yat-pade vidite sarva-sandehaḥ pralayaṁ vrajet ।
avijñātaṁ na kiñcit syāt āśāsyaṁ vā na kiñcana ॥ 55 ॥

yat-pade — which position, vidite — known, sarva-sandehaḥ — all doubts, pralayaṁ vrajet — dissolve, avijñātam — unknown, na kiñcit — nothing, syāt — would be, āśāsyaṁ vā — desirable, na kiñcana — nothing.
"In which position, when known, all doubts dissolve, nothing remains unknown, and nothing is desirable."
अवेद्यं विदितं तच्चेद्‌ वद मामुप सत्वरम्‌ ।
तापस्यैवं समापृष्टः कहोलतनयोऽब्रवीत्‌ ॥ ५६ ॥
avedyaṁ viditaṁ tat ced vada mām upa satvaram ।
