tāpasya evaṁ samāpṛṣṭaḥ kahola-tanayaḥ abravīt ॥ 56 ॥

avedyaṁ — unknown, viditam — known, tat — that, ced — if, vada — tell, mām — me, upa — to, satvaram — immediately, tāpasya — by the ascetic woman, evaṁ — thus, samāpṛṣṭaḥ — asked, kahola-tanayaḥ — Kahola's son, abravīt — said.
"If you know the unknown, tell me immediately." Thus asked by the ascetic woman, Kahola's son said.
विदितं तत्पदं भूयो वच्मि तापसि संशृणु ।
न मे ह्यविदितं लोके ह्यस्ति किञ्चित्‌ कियत्त्विदम्‌ ॥ ५७ ॥
viditaṁ tat-padaṁ bhūyaḥ vacmi tāpasi saṁśṛṇu ।

आदर्शनगरप्रख्यं तदेतत्परमं पदम्‌ ॥ ६० ॥

नाशास्यं वा भवेत्‌ किञ्चिदेवं प्रविदिते परे ॥ ६२ ॥

"Until then, he does not obtain the necklace on the neck, even with subtle investigation. Thus, O sage's son, realize the self and its own nature."
भूयोऽतिनिपुणोऽप्यन्तरात्मानमनुदाहरेत्‌ ।
यावत्‌ तावद्‌ बहिः कुत्र कथं तद्विदितं भवेत्‌ ॥ ८४ ॥
bhūyo'tinipuṇo'py antar-ātmānam anudāharet ।
yāvat tāvad bahiḥ kutra kathaṁ tadviditaṁ bhavet ॥ 84 ॥

bhūyaḥ — again, ati-nipuṇaḥ — very skilled, api — even, antar-ātmānam — inner self, anudāharet — realizes, yāvat — as long as, tāvat — until then, bahiḥ — outside, kutra — where, katham — how, tat-viditam — that known, bhavet — be.
"Even if very skilled, until one realizes the inner self, how can one know it from outside?"
यथा हि दीपो विषयान्‌ प्रकाशयति सर्वतः ।
स्वयं प्रकाश्यतां नैति क्वचिद्दीपस्य कस्यचित्‌ ॥ ८५ ॥
yathā hi dīpo viṣayān prakāśayati sarvataḥ ।
svayaṁ prakāśyatāṁ naiti kvacid dīpasya kasyacit ॥ 85 ॥

yathā — as, hi — indeed, dīpaḥ — a lamp, viṣayān — objects, prakāśayati — illuminates, sarvataḥ — everywhere, svayam — itself, prakāśyatām — illumination, na — not, eti — goes, kvacit — anywhere, dīpasya — of a lamp, kasyacit — of anyone.
"As a lamp illuminates objects everywhere, but does not illuminate itself anywhere."
प्रकाशते स्वयं चैवानपेक्ष्यान्यं प्रकाशकम्‌ ।
एवं सूर्यादयः सर्वे प्रकाशकतया स्थिताः ॥ ८६ ॥
prakāśate svayaṁ caiva anapekṣya anyaṁ prakāśakam ।
evaṁ sūryādayaḥ sarve prakāśakatayā sthitāḥ ॥ 86 ॥

prakāśate — illuminates, svayam — itself, ca — also, eva — indeed, anapekṣya — without depending, anyam — another, prakāśakam — illuminator, evam — thus, sūrya-ādayaḥ — the sun and others, sarve — all, prakāśakatayā — as illuminators, sthitāḥ — situated.
"Thus, the sun and others illuminate themselves without depending on another illuminator, all are situated as illuminators."
एवं च किं दीपमुखा अप्रकाश्यत्वहेतुतः ।
न सन्ति न प्रकाशन्त इति वक्तुं हि युज्यते ॥ ८७ ॥
evaṁ ca kiṁ dīpa-mukhā aprakāśyatva-hetutaḥ ।
na santi na prakāśanta iti vaktuṁ hi yujyate ॥ 87 ॥

evam — thus, ca — and, kim — what, dīpa-mukhāḥ — lamps, aprakāśyatva-hetutaḥ — due to non-illumination, na santi — do not exist, na prakāśanta — do not illuminate, iti — thus, vaktum — to say, hi — indeed, yujyate — appropriate.
"And thus, what about lamps, due to non-illumination, do not exist or illuminate, it is appropriate to say."
एवं प्रकाश्यभूतेषु सत्सु दीपमुखेषु वै ।
अत्यन्तमप्रकाश्यं यच्चित्तत्वं तत्कुतो वद ॥ ८८ ॥
evaṁ prakāśya-bhūteṣu satsu dīpa-mukheṣu vai ।
atyantaṁ aprakāśyaṁ yat citta-tattvaṁ tat kuto vada ॥ 88 ॥

evam — thus, prakāśya-bhūteṣu — illuminating objects, satsu — existing, dīpa-mukheṣu — in lamps, vai — indeed, atyantam — absolutely, aprakāśyam — non-illuminating, yat — what, citta-tattvam — the nature of consciousness, tat — that, kuto — how, vada — say.
"Thus, with illuminating objects existing in lamps, absolutely non-illuminating, how do you say that is the nature of consciousness?"
असंवेद्यं प्रकाशेत चेत्यत्र विचिकित्सितम्‌ ।
तस्मात्‌ त्वमन्तर्मुखया दृष्ट्या सम्यग्‌ विचारय ॥ ८९ ॥
asaṁvedyaṁ prakāśeta cetyatra vicikitsitam ।
tasmāt tvam antarmukhayā dṛṣṭyā samyag vicāraya ॥ 89 ॥

asaṁvedyam — not perceivable, prakāśeta — illuminates, cet — if, atra — here, vicikitsitam — doubtful, tasmāt — therefore, tvam — you, antarmukhayā — inward-facing, dṛṣṭyā — with vision, samyak — properly, vicāraya — consider.
"If it illuminates without being perceivable, that is doubtful; therefore, you consider all this properly with an inward-facing vision."
चिच्छक्तिरेषा परमा त्रिपुरा सर्वसंश्रया ।
सर्वावभासिनी कुत्र कदा वा न प्रकाशते ॥ ९० ॥
cicchaktireṣā paramā tripurā sarvasaṁśrayā ।
sarvāvabhāsinī kutra kadā vā na prakāśate ॥ 90 ॥

cit-śaktiḥ — consciousness power, eṣā — this, paramā — supreme, tripurā — Tripura, sarva-saṁśrayā — all-encompassing, sarva-avabhāsinī — all-illuminating, kutra — where, kadā — when, vā — or, na — not, prakāśate — shines.
"This supreme consciousness power, Tripura, all-encompassing, all-illuminating, where and when does it not shine?"
यदा सा न प्रकाशेत प्रकाशेत तदा नु किम्‌ ।
अप्रकाशेनापि सैव चितिशक्तिः प्रकाशते ॥ ९१ ॥
yadā sā na prakāśeta prakāśeta tadā nu kim ।
aprakāśenāpi saiva citiśaktiḥ prakāśate ॥ 91 ॥

yadā — when, sā — it, na — not, prakāśeta — shines, prakāśeta — shines, tadā — then, nu — indeed, kim — what, aprakāśena — by non-illumination, api — also, sā — it, eva — indeed, citiśaktiḥ — consciousness power, prakāśate — shines.
"When it does not shine, then what indeed? By non-illumination also, the consciousness power shines."
अप्रकाशो यथा भाति सा न भायात्‌ कथं वद ।
भाति चेत्‌ सा कथं भाति विमृशैतत्‌ सुसूक्ष्मतः ॥ ९२ ॥
aprakāśo yathā bhāti sā na bhāyāt kathaṁ vada ।
bhāti cet sā kathaṁ bhāti vimṛśaitat susūkṣmataḥ ॥ 92 ॥

aprakāśaḥ — non-illumination, yathā — how, bhāti — appears, sā — it, na — not, bhāyāt — shines, kathaṁ — how, vada — tell, bhāti — shines, cet — if, sā — it, kathaṁ — how, bhāti — shines, vimṛśa — consider, etat — this, susūkṣmataḥ — with subtlety.
"How does non-illumination appear? How does it not shine, tell me. If it shines, how does it shine? Consider this with subtlety."
अत्र सर्वे न पश्यन्ति कुशला अपि पण्डिताः ।
अनन्तर्दृष्टयस्तेन मोहिताः संसरन्ति च ॥ ९३ ॥
atra sarve na paśyanti kuśalā api paṇḍitāḥ ।
anantardṛṣṭayastena mohitāḥ saṁsaranti ca ॥ 93 ॥

atra — here, sarve — all, na — not, paśyanti — see, kuśalāḥ — skillful, api — even, paṇḍitāḥ — scholars, an-antar-dṛṣṭayaḥ — without inner vision, tena — by this, mohitāḥ — deluded, saṁsaranti — wander, ca — and.
"Here, all, even skillful scholars do not see. Without inner vision, deluded by this, they wander."
यावद्‌ दृष्टिः प्रवृत्तिं तु न परित्यज्य तिष्ठति ।
तावदन्तर्दृष्टितापि न स्यादेव कथञ्चन ॥ ९४ ॥
yāvad dṛṣṭiḥ pravṛttiṁ tu na parityajya tiṣṭhati ।
tāvad antar-dṛṣṭitāpi na syādeva kathañcana ॥ 94 ॥

yāvat — as long as, dṛṣṭiḥ — vision, pravṛttiṁ — activity, tu — but, na — not, parityajya — renouncing, tiṣṭhati — remains, tāvat — so long, antar-dṛṣṭitā — inner vision, api — even, na syāt — does not exist, eva — indeed, kathañcana — in any way.
"As long as vision does not remain by renouncing activity, so long, inner vision does not exist in any way."
यावन्नान्तर्दृष्टिमेति तावत्तां न प्रपश्यति ।
अन्तर्दृष्टिर्निरीहा स्यात्‌ सेहायाः सा कथं भवेत्‌ ॥ ९५ ॥
yāvannāntardṛṣṭimeti tāvattāṁ na prapaśyati ।
antardṛṣṭirnirīhā syāt sehayāḥ sā kathaṁ bhavet ॥ 95 ॥

yāvat — as long as, na — not, antar-dṛṣṭim — inner vision, eti — attains, tāvat — so long, tāṁ — that, na prapaśyati — does not see, antar-dṛṣṭiḥ — inner vision, nirīhā — desireless, syāt — should be, sehayāḥ — with effort, sā — that, kathaṁ — how, bhavet — can be.
"As long as one does not attain inner vision, so long, one does not see it. Inner vision should be desireless, how can that be with effort?"
परिहृत्य तु तां सम्यक्‌ स्वभावमुपसंश्रय ।
क्षणं स्वं भावमाश्रित्य निर्विमर्शस्ततः परम्‌ ॥ ९६ ॥
parihṛtya tu tāṁ samyak svabhāvamupasaṁśraya ।
kṣaṇaṁ svaṁ bhāvamāśritya nirvimarśas tataḥ param ॥ 96 ॥

parihṛtya — abandoning, tu — but, tāṁ — that, samyak — properly, svabhāvam — own nature, upasaṁśraya — resort to, kṣaṇam — for a moment, svaṁ bhāvam — own essence, āśritya — relying, nirvimarśaḥ — without deliberation, tataḥ — then, param — beyond.
"Abandoning that properly, resort to your own nature. For a moment, relying on your own essence, without deliberation, then beyond."
विमृश्य स्मरणद्वारा ततो वेत्सि समस्तकम्‌ ।
असंवेद्यं सुवेद्यं च तदेवं तत्त्वमुच्यते ॥ ९७ ॥
vimṛśya smaraṇadvārā tato vetsi samastakam ।
asaṁvedyaṁ suvedyaṁ ca tad evaṁ tattvam ucyate ॥ 97 ॥

vimṛśya — considering, smaraṇa-dvārā — through memory, tataḥ — then, vetsi — you know, samastakam — everything, asaṁvedyam — unknowable, suvedyam — well-known, ca — and, tat — that, evam — thus, tattvam — truth, ucyate — is said.
"Considering through memory, then you know everything, unknowable and well-known, that is said to be the truth."
विदित्वैवमवेद्यं च प्राप्नुयादमृतां स्थितिम्‌ ।
एतत्तेऽभिहितं सर्व मुनिपुत्र नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ ९८ ॥
viditvaivam avedyaṁ ca prāpnuyād amṛtāṁ sthitim ।
etat te'bhihitaṁ sarva muni-putra namo'stu te ॥ 98 ॥

viditvā — knowing, evam — thus, avedyam — unknowable, ca — and, prāpnuyāt — one may attain, amṛtām sthitim — immortal state, etat — this, te — to you, abhihitam — spoken, sarvam — all, muni-putra — O sage's son, namaḥ astu — salutations be, te — to you.
"Knowing thus the unknowable, one may attain the immortal state. This is all spoken to you, O sage's son, salutations be to you."
व्रजाम्यहं त्वया चैतन्न विज्ञातं सकृच्छ्रुतेः ।
बोधयिष्यति त्वामेष राजा बुद्धिमतां वरः ॥ ९९ ॥
vrajāmy ahaṁ tvayā caitanna vijñātaṁ sakṛt śruteḥ ।
bodhayiṣyati tvāmeṣa rājā buddhimatāṁ varaḥ ॥ 99 ॥

vrajāmi — I go, aham — I, tvayā — by you, ca — and, etat — this, na — not, vijñātam — known, sakṛt — once, śruteḥ — by hearing, bodhayiṣyati — will enlighten, tvām — you, eṣaḥ — this, rājā — king, buddhimatāṁ varaḥ — best among the wise.
"I go, as this is not known by you through once hearing. This king, the best among the wise, will enlighten you."
पृच्छ भूयः संशयं ते सर्वं छेत्स्यति वै नृपः ।
इत्युक्त्वा पूजिता राज्ञा प्रणता च सभासदैः ॥ १०० ॥
pṛccha bhūyaḥ saṁśayaṁ te sarvaṁ chetsyati vai nṛpaḥ ।
ity uktvā pūjitā rājñā praṇatā ca sabhāsadaiḥ ॥ 100 ॥

pṛccha — ask, bhūyaḥ — again, saṁśayam — doubt, te — your, sarvam — all, chetsyati — will clear, vai — indeed, nṛpaḥ — king, iti — thus, uktvā — having said, pūjitā — honored, rājñā — by the king, praṇatā — bowed, ca — and, sabhāsadaiḥ — by the assembly.
"Ask again your doubts, the king will clear them all. Having said this, she was honored by the king and bowed by the assembly."
वातनुन्नाभ्रलेखेव क्षणादन्तर्द्धिमाययौ ।
एतत्‌ तेऽभिहितं राम वेदनप्रक्रियात्मनः ॥ १०१ ॥
vāta-nunna-abhralekha-iva kṣaṇāt antardhim āyayau ।
etat te abhihitaṁ rāma vedana-prakriyā-ātmanaḥ ॥ 101 ॥

vāta — wind, nunna — driven, abhralekha — cloud streak, iva — like, kṣaṇāt — in a moment, antardhim — disappearance, āyayau — came, etat — this, te — to you, abhihitaṁ — explained, rāma — O Rama, vedana — perception, prakriyā — process, ātmanaḥ — of the self
Like a cloud streak driven by the wind, she disappeared in a moment. This is explained to you, O Rama, the process of perception of the self.

colophon.en: Thus ends the fifteenth chapter named "Ashtavakra" in the revered Knowledge Section of Tripura Rahasya.

lines.text: शृत्वैतद्‌ भार्गवो रामः प्राप्य विस्मयमान्तरे ।
भूयः पप्रच्छात्रिसूनुमवितृप्तः कथाश्रुतेः ॥ १ ॥
śṛtvaitad bhārgavo rāmaḥ prāpya vismayamāntare ।
bhūyaḥ papracchātrisūnumavitṛptaḥ kathāśruteḥ ॥ 1 ॥

śṛtva — having heard, etad — this, bhārgavaḥ — Bhargava, rāmaḥ — Rama, prāpya — having experienced, vismaya — wonder, antare — within, bhūyaḥ — again, papraccha — asked, atri-sūnum — Atri's son, avitṛptaḥ — unsatisfied, kathā-śruteḥ — by hearing the story.
Having heard this, Rama, the son of Bhargava, experienced wonder within and asked Atri's son again, unsatisfied by hearing the story.
भगवन्नद्भुतं ह्येतच्छ्रुतं वृत्तं पुरातनम्‌ ।
भूयः पप्रच्छ राजानमष्टावक्रो महामुनिः ॥ २ ॥
bhagavannadbhutaṁ hyetacchrutaṁ vṛttaṁ purātanam ।
bhūyaḥ papraccha rājānamaṣṭāvakro mahāmuniḥ ॥ 2 ॥

bhagavan — O Lord, adbhutam — wonderful, hi — indeed, etat — this, śrutam — heard, vṛttam — event, purātanam — ancient, bhūyaḥ — again, papraccha — asked, rājānam — king, aṣṭāvakraḥ — Ashtavakra, mahāmuniḥ — great sage.
O Lord, this ancient event heard is indeed wonderful. The great sage Ashtavakra again asked the king.
यद्राजा प्रत्युवाचैनं तच्च मे वद सर्वशः ।
अहोऽद्भुतं समाख्यानं न क्वचिच्च मया श्रुतम्‌ ॥ ३ ॥
yadrājā pratyuvācainaṁ tacca me vada sarvaśaḥ ।
aho'dbhutaṁ samākhyānaṁ na kvacicc mayā śrutam ॥ 3 ॥

yat — what, rājā — the king, pratyuvāca — replied, enam — to him, tat — that, ca — and, me — to me, vada — tell, sarvaśaḥ — completely, aho — oh, adbhutam — wonderful, samākhyānam — story, na kvacit — never, mayā — by me, śrutam — heard.
What the king replied to him, tell that to me completely. Oh, this wonderful story I have never heard.
विज्ञानवृत्तसर्वस्वं दयया वद मे गुरो ।
इत्येवमनुयुक्तोऽथ दत्तात्रेयो महामुनिः ॥ ४ ॥
vijñānavṛttasarvasvaṁ dayayā vada me guro ।
ityevamanu yukto'tha dattātreyo mahāmuniḥ ॥ 4 ॥

vijñāna-vṛtta-sarvasvam — all about knowledge and action, dayayā — with compassion, vada — tell, me — to me, guro — O Guru, iti — thus, evam — in this way, anu yuktaḥ — asked, atha — then, dattātreyaḥ — Dattatreya, mahāmuniḥ — great sage.
O Guru, with compassion, tell me all about knowledge and action. Thus asked, the great sage Dattatreya then...
भार्गवाय समाचख्यौ कथां परमपावनीम्‌ ।
शृणु भार्गव यत्‌ प्रोक्तं जनकेन महात्मना ॥ ५ ॥
bhārgavāya samācakhyau kathāṁ paramapāvanīm ।
śṛṇu bhārgava yat proktaṁ janakena mahātmanā ॥ 5 ॥

bhārgavāya — to Bhargava, samācakhyau — narrated, kathām — story, parama-pāvanīm — supremely purifying, śṛṇu — listen, bhārgava — O Bhargava, yat — what, proktam — spoken, janakena — by Janaka, mahātmanā — the great soul.
Narrated to Bhargava a supremely purifying story. Listen, O Bhargava, to what was spoken by the great soul Janaka.
निर्गतायां तु तापस्यामष्टावक्रो मुनेः सुतः ।
संवृतो बहुभिर्विप्रैः समेत्य नृपपुङ्गवम्‌ ॥ ६ ॥
nirgatāyāṁ tu tāpasyāmaṣṭāvakro muneḥ sutaḥ ।
saṁvṛto bahubhir vipraiḥ sametya nṛpapuṅgavam ॥ 6 ॥

nirgatāyām — when she had departed, tu — but, tāpasyām — ascetic woman, aṣṭāvakraḥ — Ashtavakra, muneḥ sutaḥ — the son of the sage, saṁvṛtaḥ — surrounded, bahubhiḥ — by many, vipraiḥ — sages, sametya — having met, nṛpa-puṅgavam — the foremost of kings.
When the ascetic woman had departed, Ashtavakra, the sage's son, surrounded by many sages, met the foremost of kings.
पप्रच्छ यत्तु तापस्या संक्षिप्योक्तं महार्थकम्‌ ।
तदुच्यमानं तु मया सम्यक्‌ शृणु समाहितः ॥ ७ ॥
papraccha yattu tāpasyā saṁkṣipyoktaṁ mahārthakam ।
taducyamānaṁ tu mayā samyak śṛṇu samāhitaḥ ॥ 7 ॥

papraccha — asked, yat — what, tu — but, tāpasyā — ascetic woman, saṁkṣipya — briefly, uktam — spoken, mahārthakam — significant, tat — that, ucyamānam — being said, tu — but, mayā — by me, samyak — properly, śṛṇu — listen, samāhitaḥ — attentively.
He asked what the ascetic woman briefly spoke, which was significant. That being said by me, listen properly and attentively.
राजन्‌ विदेहाधिपते तापस्योक्तं तु यत्तया ।
तदहं नाविदं सम्यक्‌ संक्षेपोक्तत्वहेतुतः ॥ ८ ॥
rājan videhādhipate tāpasyoktaṁ tu yattayā ।
tadahaṁ nāvidaṁ samyak saṁkṣepoktatvahetutaḥ ॥ 8 ॥

rājan — O King, videhādhipate — lord of Videha, tāpasyā — ascetic woman, uktam — said, tu — but, yat — what, tayā — by her, tat — that, aham — I, na avidam — did not know, samyak — properly, saṁkṣepa-uktatva-hetutaḥ — due to the brevity of the statement.
O King, lord of Videha, what the ascetic woman said, I did not know properly due to the brevity of the statement.
कथं विद्यामवेद्यं तत्‌ समाचक्ष्व दयानिधे ।
एवं जनक आपृष्टः प्राह तं विस्मयन्निव ॥ ९ ॥
kathaṁ vidyāmavedyaṁ tat samācakṣva dayānidhe ।
evaṁ janaka āpṛṣṭaḥ prāha taṁ vismayanniva ॥ 9 ॥

anirūpyaṁ kevalaṁ tad avedyam api sarvathā ॥ 13 ॥

The difference in form indeed appears in the knowable side. See the knowable separately by intellect without form.
बिम्बानुकृतिरादर्शो यद्वत्‌ तद्वदियं चितिः ।
दृश्याकारधृतेर्नानारूपतां प्रतिपद्यते ॥ २० ॥
bimbānukṛtirādarśo yadvat tadvadiyaṁ citiḥ ।
dṛśyākāra-dhṛter nānā-rūpatāṁ pratipadyate ॥ 20 ॥

evaṁ vittir iyaṁ vedyā vedyavyāvṛttarūpataḥ ।

Thus, this knowledge is knowable in a form distinct from the knowable. But by nature, that knowledge is not knowable and is all-pervading.

yata etad vedituḥ syād rūpaṁ tasmān na vedyate ।
vimṛśāṣṭāvakra rūpaṁ nijam evaṁvidhaṁ sphuṭam ॥ 22 ॥

na tvaṁ śarīraṁ prāṇo vā mano vāpy asthiratvataḥ ।

This supreme consciousness remains without transcending the ego-mind, therefore, you, O Aṣṭāvakra, are the knower of all in essence.

paśya pratyāvṛtta-cakṣuḥ svātmānaṁ kevalāṁ citim ।

See with the turned inward vision your own pure consciousness. Those with the highest intellect see their own self indeed at the instruction time.

Its turning inward is also said, listen, O learned one. The unturned inward vision indeed does not see anything.

didūkṣuś cakṣuṣā kiñcit tad anyebhyo hy aśeṣataḥ ।

tadā — then, tat — that, bhāsate — shines, spaṣṭam — clearly, na anyadā — not otherwise, tu — but, kadācana — at any time, anyadā — otherwise, tu — but, purovṛtti — outward-oriented, na — not, spaṣṭam — clearly, bhāsate — shines, kvacit — at any time.
Then that shines clearly, but not otherwise at any time. Otherwise, the outward-oriented vision does not shine clearly at any time.

Thus indeed, with the mind, the perception of happiness and sorrow would be. With the unturned inward mind, one is not able to know anything.

tasmāt tad ekaparata parāvṛttiś ca cakṣuṣaḥ ।

tasmāt — therefore, tad — that, ekaparata — singular focus, parāvṛttiḥ — turning inward, ca — and, cakṣuṣaḥ — of the vision, pratyāvṛttam — turned inward, manaḥ — mind, śuddham — pure, nija-rūpa-avabhāsakam — reflecting the own form.
Therefore, that singular focus and turning inward of the vision, the turned inward mind, is pure, reflecting its own form.
अत्र ते सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणु तन्नियतान्तरः ।
अगोचरश्चेदात्मासौ मनसा गोचरोऽपि च ॥ ३४ ॥
atra te saṁpravakṣyāmi śṛṇu tan niyatāntaraḥ ।
agocaraś ced ātmāsau manasā gocaro 'pi ca ॥ 34 ॥

atra — here, te — to you, saṁpravakṣyāmi — I will explain, śṛṇu — listen, tat — that, niyata-antaraḥ — specific distinction, agocaraḥ — beyond the senses, cet — if, ātmā — self, asau — that, manasā — with mind, gocaraḥ — within the senses, api — also, ca — and.
Here I will explain to you, listen, that specific distinction. If that self is beyond the senses, it is also within the senses with the mind.

mano-gocaratā bāhye dvi-prakāreṇa saṁsthitā ॥ 35 ॥

atra — here, muhyanti — are confused, bahavaḥ — many, śruti-āgama-vivecakāḥ — those who distinguish Vedic scriptures, mano-gocaratā — mind's scope, bāhye — externally, dvi-prakāreṇa — in two ways, saṁsthitā — situated.

आद्यान्येभ्यः परावृत्तिः परा तत्परता भवेत्‌ ।
अन्येभ्यस्तु परावृत्तिमात्रेऽपि मनसः सति ॥ ३६ ॥
ādya-anye-bhyaḥ parāvṛttiḥ parā tat-paratā bhavet ।

ādya — first, anye-bhyaḥ — from others, parāvṛttiḥ — turning inward, parā — superior, tat-paratā — focused on that, bhavet — would be, anye-bhyaḥ — from others, tu — but, parāvṛtti-mātre — mere turning inward, api — even, manasaḥ — of the mind, sati — being.

sarvāśrayaṁ sarvagatam api taiḥ chāditam yataḥ ।
ataḥ tebhyah parāvṛtti-mātreṇaiva vibhāsate ॥ 43 ॥

evaṁ citiḥ sarvagatā sarvāśrayatayā sthitā ।

Thus, consciousness, pervading and supporting all, is situated at all times, fully complete in the mind, like space, O twice-born.

tasmād anya-parāvṛtti-mātra manasa iṣyate ।
paśya vipra citiḥ kutra kadā na asti avabhāsinī ॥ 45 ॥

Therefore, mere turning inward from others of the mind is desired. See, O wise one, where and when consciousness is not shining.

yadā yatra ca sā nāsti na yadā na api yatra ca ।
tasmāt cid-ātma-avabhāse manasaḥ anya-parāvṛtiḥ ॥ 46 ॥

yadā — when, yatra — where, ca — and, sā — it, nāsti — is not, na — not, yadā — when, na api — nor, yatra — where, ca — and, tasmāt — therefore, cid-ātma-avabhāse — in the shining of the self-consciousness, manasaḥ — of the mind, anya-parāvṛtiḥ — turning inward from others.
When and where it is not, nor when and where it is, therefore, in the shining of the self-consciousness, by the mind's turning inward from others.
केवलापेक्षिता नैवाभिमुख्यं नूतनं क्वचित्‌ ।
आभिमुख्याभावहेतोरेवाऽवेद्यत्वमिष्यते ॥ ४७ ॥
kevalā-pekṣitā naiva-ābhimukhyaṁ nūtanaṁ kvacit ।
ābhimukhya-abhāva-hetor eva-avedyatvam iṣyate ॥ 47 ॥

kevalā-pekṣitā — absolute dependency, na eva — not indeed, ābhimukhyaṁ — facing, nūtanaṁ — new, kvacit — anywhere, ābhimukhya-abhāva-hetoḥ — due to the lack of facing, eva — indeed, avedyatvam — unperceived, iṣyate — is considered.
It is not merely dependent on some, nor is it entirely new at times. Indeed, due to the absence of dependence, it is said to be unknowable.
अत एव शुद्धमनोवेद्यं तत्तत्वमुच्यते ।
अन्येभ्यस्तु परावृत्तिरेव शुद्धिर्हि मानसी ॥ ४८ ॥
ata eva śuddha-mano-vedyaṁ tat-tattvam ucyate ।
anye-bhyaḥ tu parāvṛttiḥ eva śuddhiḥ hi mānasī ॥ 48 ॥

ataḥ eva — therefore indeed, śuddha-mano-vedyaṁ — pure mind perceived, tat-tattvam — that reality, ucyate — is said, anye-bhyaḥ — from others, tu — but, parāvṛttiḥ — turning inward, eva — indeed, śuddhiḥ — purity, hi — indeed, mānasī — mental.
Therefore indeed, pure mind perceived is said to be that reality. But from others, indeed, turning inward is mental purity.
एतदेव परं तत्त्वज्ञाने साधनमुच्यते ।
यावन्नहि मनः शुद्धं तावज्ज्ञानं कथं भवेत्‌ ॥ ४९ ॥
etad eva paraṁ tattva-jñāne sādhanam ucyate ।
yāvat na hi manaḥ śuddhaṁ tāvat jñānaṁ kathaṁ bhavet ॥ 49 ॥

etad — this, eva — indeed, paraṁ — supreme, tattva-jñāne — in the knowledge of reality, sādhanam — means, ucyate — is said, yāvat — as long as, na — not, hi — indeed, manaḥ — mind, śuddhaṁ — pure, tāvat — then, jñānaṁ — knowledge, kathaṁ — how, bhavet — would be.
This indeed is said to be the supreme means in the knowledge of reality. As long as the mind is not pure, then how would knowledge be?

śuddhe manasi vai jñānaṁ kathaṁ vā na bhavet dhruvam ।
upakṣīṇaṁ sarvam atra sādhanam tasya śodhane ॥ 50 ॥

śuddhe — pure, manasi — mind, vai — indeed, jñānaṁ — knowledge, kathaṁ — how, vā — or, na — not, bhavet — would be, dhruvam — surely, upakṣīṇaṁ — diminished, sarvam — all, atra — here, sādhanam — means, tasya — its, śodhane — purification.
When the mind is pure, how would knowledge surely not be? All the means here are for its purification.
कर्म वोपासनं वापि वैराग्यादिकमेव वा ।
मनसः शोधने एव विनियुक्तं न चान्यथा ॥ ५१ ॥
karma vā upāsanam vā api vairāgyādikam eva vā ।
manasaḥ śodhane eva viniyuktaṁ na ca anyathā ॥ 51 ॥

karma — action, vā — or, upāsanam — worship, vā — or, api — even, vairāgyādikam — dispassion, eva — indeed, vā — or, manasaḥ — of the mind, śodhane — purification, eva — indeed, viniyuktaṁ — engaged, na ca — and not, anyathā — otherwise.
Action, worship, even dispassion, are engaged indeed for the purification of the mind, and not otherwise.

tasmāt śuddhena manasā bhāsate tat paraṁ vapuḥ ।
iti rājñā iritaṁ śrutvā tu aṣṭāvakraḥ punar jagau ॥ 52 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, śuddhena — with pure, manasā — mind, bhāsate — shines, tat — that, paraṁ — supreme, vapuḥ — form, iti — thus, rājñā — by the king, iritaṁ — said, śrutvā — hearing, tu — but, aṣṭāvakraḥ — Aṣṭāvakra, punar — again, jagau — spoke.
Therefore, with a pure mind, that supreme form shines. Thus, hearing what was said by the king, Aṣṭāvakra again spoke.

केवला चेत्‌ सा परा चिद्‌ मनसा प्रविभासते ॥ ५३ ॥
rājan tvayā uktam anye-bhyaḥ parāvṛttiḥ hi mānasī ।
kevalā cet sā parā cit manasā pravibhāsate ॥ 53 ॥

rājan — O king, tvayā — by you, uktam — said, anye-bhyaḥ — from others, parāvṛttiḥ — turning inward, hi — indeed, mānasī — mental, kevalā — alone, cet — if, sā — that, parā — supreme, cit — consciousness, manasā — with the mind, pravibhāsate — shines.
O king, you said, turning inward from others is indeed mental. If that alone is supreme, consciousness shines with the mind.
तत्‌ सुषुप्तौ विभासेत परावृत्तं मनस्तदा ।
ततः किं साधनैरन्यैः सुप्तिमात्रात्‌ कृतार्थता ॥ ५४ ॥
tat suṣuptau vibhāset parāvṛttaṁ manaḥ tadā ।
tataḥ kiṁ sādhanaiḥ anyaiḥ supti-mātrāt kṛtārthatā ॥ 54 ॥

tat — that, suṣuptau — in deep sleep, vibhāset — would shine, parāvṛttaṁ — turned inward, manaḥ — mind, tadā — then, tataḥ — then, kiṁ — what, sādhanaiḥ — with means, anyaiḥ — other, supti-mātrāt — from mere sleep, kṛtārthatā — accomplishment.
If that turned inward mind would shine in deep sleep, then what is the use of other means? Is accomplishment done from mere sleep?
इति पर्यनुयुक्तोऽथ विप्रेणोवाच भूपतिः ।
समाहितः शृणु ब्रह्मन्‌ समाधानं वदामि ते ॥ ५५ ॥
iti paryanu yuktaḥ atha vipreṇa uvāca bhūpatiḥ ।
samāhitaḥ śṛṇu brahman samādhānaṁ vadāmi te ॥ 55 ॥

iti — thus, paryanu yuktaḥ — addressed, atha — then, vipreṇa — by the sage, uvāca — said, bhūpatiḥ — the king, samāhitaḥ — composed, śṛṇu — hear, brahman — O sage, samādhānaṁ — resolution, vadāmi — I speak, te — to you.
Thus addressed by the sage, the king then said, "Hear, O sage, composed, I speak the resolution to you."

लीनं मनस्त्वं चाप्यस्य कथं तामवभासयेत्‌ ॥ ५६ ॥
satyaṁ suṣuptau manasaḥ parāvṛttiḥ tu sarvathā ।
līnaṁ manaḥ tvam ca api asya kathaṁ tām avabhāsayet ॥ 56 ॥

satyaṁ — truly, suṣuptau — in deep sleep, manasaḥ — of the mind, parāvṛttiḥ — turning inward, tu — indeed, sarvathā — completely, līnaṁ — dissolved, manaḥ — mind, tvam — you, ca — and, api — also, asya — of it, kathaṁ — how, tām — it, avabhāsayet — would shine.
Truly, in deep sleep, the mind's turning inward is complete. It is a dissolved mind, and you also, now how would it shine?
कज्जलेन समालिप्ते दर्पणे गगनं नहि ।
अन्येभ्यस्तु परावृत्तिमात्रेण भासते क्वचित्‌ ॥ ५७ ॥
kajjaleṇa samālipte darpaṇe gaganaṁ nahi ।
anye-bhyaḥ tu parāvṛtti-mātreṇa bhāsate kvacit ॥ 57 ॥

kajjaleṇa — with ink, samālipte — covered, darpaṇe — mirror, gaganaṁ — sky, nahi — not, anye-bhyaḥ — from others, tu — but, parāvṛtti-mātreṇa — by mere turning inward, bhāsate — shines, kvacit — sometimes.
When the mirror is covered with ink, the sky does not shine in the mirror. But sometimes, by mere turning inward from others, it shines.

evaṁ vilipte manasi nidrayā anya-parāvṛteḥ ।
ayogyatvād eva mano bhāsayet na citiṁ kvacit ॥ 58 ॥

evaṁ — thus, vilipte — covered, manasi — mind, nidrayā — by sleep, anya-parāvṛteḥ — turned inward from others, ayogyatvād — due to unsuitability, eva — indeed, mano — mind, bhāsayet — shines, na — not, citiṁ — consciousness, kvacit — anywhere.
Thus, when the mind is covered by sleep, turned inward from others, due to unsuitability, the mind does not shine consciousness anywhere.
अन्यथा लोष्टकुड्यादेरपि भायात्‌ कुतो न सा ।
तस्माद्योग्येन मनसा शुद्धेन भासते हि सा ॥ ५९ ॥
anyathā loṣṭa-kuḍya-ādeḥ api bhāyāt kuto na sā ।
tasmād yogyena manasā śuddhena bhāsate hi sā ॥ 59 ॥

anyathā — otherwise, loṣṭa-kuḍya-ādeḥ — of clod, wall, etc., api — even, bhāyāt — would shine, kuto na — why not, sā — it, tasmāt — therefore, yogyena — suitable, manasā — with mind, śuddhena — pure, bhāsate — shines, hi — indeed, sā — it.
In other times, why wouldn't it shine even on clod, wall, etc.? Therefore, it indeed shines with a suitable, pure mind.
अतः सद्योजातशिशोर्भासते नहि किञ्चन ।
अथापि शृणु वक्ष्यामि मषीलिप्ते हि दर्पणे ॥ ६० ॥
ataḥ sadyojāta-śiśoḥ bhāsate nahi kiñcana ।
athāpi śṛṇu vakṣyāmi maṣī-lipte hi darpaṇe ॥ 60 ॥

ataḥ — therefore, sadyojāta-śiśoḥ — of a newborn child, bhāsate — shines, nahi — not, kiñcana — anything, athāpi — even then, śṛṇu — listen, vakṣyāmi — I will explain, maṣī-lipte — covered with ink, hi — indeed, darpaṇe — in the mirror.
Therefore, it is similar to as nothing shines for a newborn child. Even then, listen, I will explain, what happens when the mirror is covered with ink.

संश्लेषान्न विलक्ष्येत स्वभावस्यानपोहनात्‌ ॥ ६१ ॥
alakṣitaṁ ca api maṣīpratibimbanam asti vai ।
saṁśleṣān na vilakṣyeta svabhāvasya anapohanāt ॥ 61 ॥

alakṣitaṁ — unseen, ca — and, api — even, maṣīpratibimbanam — ink reflection, asti — exists, vai — indeed, saṁśleṣāt — due to blending, na — not, vilakṣyeta — distinguished, svabhāvasya — of nature, anapohanāt — due to non-removal.
Even when it is covered with ink, the reflection exists unseen, indeed. Due to blending, it is not distinguished from its nature, due to non-removal of ink.
तथा मनः सुषुप्तिस्थं संश्लिष्टं निद्रयैव हि ।
अतोऽन्येभ्यः परावृत्तेरभावाद्‌ भासयेन्न ताम्‌ ॥ ६२ ॥
tathā manaḥ suṣupti-sthaṁ saṁśliṣṭaṁ nidrayā eva hi ।
ato anyebhyaḥ parāvṛtteḥ abhāvāt bhāsayet na tām ॥ 62 ॥

tathā — similarly, manaḥ — the mind, suṣupti-sthaṁ — situated in deep sleep, saṁśliṣṭaṁ — blended, nidrayā — by sleep, eva — indeed, hi — surely, ataḥ — therefore, anyebhyaḥ — from others, parāvṛtteḥ — turning away, abhāvāt — due to absence, bhāsayet — shines, na — not, tām — it.
Similarly, the mind situated in deep sleep is blended by sleep. Therefore, due to the absence of turning away from others, blended with sleep, it does not shine.
अतो निद्रास्मृतिरपि व्युत्थितस्य हि सम्भवेत्‌ ।
मूढतापि च या तस्यां दशायामनुभूयते ॥ ६३ ॥
ato nidrā-smṛtiḥ api vyutthitasya hi saṁbhavet ।
mūḍhatā api ca yā tasyāṁ daśāyām anubhūyate ॥ 63 ॥

ato — therefore, nidrā-smṛtiḥ — memory of sleep, api — even, vyutthitasya — of one who has arisen, hi — indeed, saṁbhavet — occurs, mūḍhatā — confusion, api — also, ca — and, yā — which, tasyāṁ — in that, daśāyām — state, anubhūyate — is experienced.
Therefore, note that the memory of sleep occurs even for one who has arisen. Observe the confusion experienced in that state.
तत्ते सम्यक्‌ प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणु सम्यक्‌ समाहितः ।
मनसस्तु द्विधाऽवस्था प्रकाशामर्शभेदतः ॥ ६४ ॥
tat te samyak pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu samyak samāhitaḥ ।
manasas tu dvidhā avasthā prakāśa-āmarśa-bhedataḥ ॥ 64 ॥

tat — that, te — to you, samyak — correctly, pravakṣyāmi — I will explain, śṛṇu — listen, samyak — properly, samāhitaḥ — composed, manasaḥ — of the mind, tu — indeed, dvidhā — two-fold, avasthā — state, prakāśa-āmarśa-bhedataḥ — by the distinction of illumination and reflection.
I will explain that to you correctly. Listen properly, composed. The mind has two states, distinguished by illumination and reflection.
बहिरर्थेषु विश्रान्तिर्या प्रकाशः स उच्यते ।
यस्तद्विचारः स्वस्मिन्‌ वै स विमर्श उदाहृतः ॥ ६५ ॥
bahir-artheṣu viśrāntiḥ yā prakāśaḥ sa ucyate।
yaḥ tad-vicāraḥ svasmin vai sa vimarśaḥ udāhṛtaḥ ॥ 65 ॥

bahir-artheṣu — in external objects, viśrāntiḥ — rest, yā — which, prakāśaḥ — illumination, saḥ — that, ucyate — is called, yaḥ — which, tad-vicāraḥ — reflection on that, svasmin — in oneself, vai — indeed, saḥ — that, vimarśaḥ — reflection, udāhṛtaḥ — is mentioned.
The rest in external objects is called illumination. The reflection on that in oneself is indeed mentioned as reflection.
प्रकाशो निर्विकल्पः स्याद्‌ वस्तूनामविभेदतः ।
विमर्शः शब्दसम्भेदाद्‌ विभेदात्‌ सविकल्पकः ॥ ६६ ॥
prakāśaḥ nirvikalpaḥ syād vastūnām avibhedataḥ ।
vimarśaḥ śabda-sambhedāt vibhedāt savikalpakaḥ ॥ 66 ॥

prakāśaḥ — illumination, nirvikalpaḥ — non-conceptual, syāt — would be, vastūnām — of objects, avibhedataḥ — due to non-distinction, vimarśaḥ — reflection, śabda-sambhedāt — due to word distinction, vibhedāt — due to distinction, savikalpakaḥ — conceptual.
Illumination would be non-conceptual due to non-distinction of objects. Reflection is conceptual due to word distinction and distinction.
अयमेवंविध इति शब्दसम्भेदवर्जितः ।
वस्तुदर्शनरूपोऽसौ प्रकाशो निर्विकल्पकः ॥ ६७ ॥
ayam evaṁ-vidha iti śabda-sambheda-varjitaḥ ।
vastu-darśana-rūpaḥ asau prakāśaḥ nirvikalpakaḥ ॥ 67 ॥

ayam — this, evaṁ-vidha — of this kind, iti — thus, śabda-sambheda-varjitaḥ — devoid of word distinction, vastu-darśana-rūpaḥ — of the form of object perception, asau — that, prakāśaḥ — illumination, nirvikalpakaḥ — non-conceptual.
This kind, thus devoid of word distinction, of the form of object perception, that illumination is non-conceptual.
अयमेवंविध इति वस्तुदर्शनमूलकः ।
शब्दसन्भिन्नरूपोऽसौ विचारात्मावभासनः ॥ ६८ ॥
ayam evaṁ-vidha iti vastu-darśana-mūlakaḥ ।
śabda-sambhinna-rūpaḥ asau vicāra-ātma-avabhāsanaḥ ॥ 68 ॥

ayam — this, evaṁ-vidha — of this kind, iti — thus, vastu-darśana-mūlakaḥ — based on object perception, śabda-sambhinna-rūpaḥ — of the form distinguished by words, asau — that, vicāra-ātma-avabhāsanaḥ — reflection's self-illumination.
This kind, thus based on object perception, of the form distinguished by words, that reflection's self-illumination.
आन्तरोऽभिनवोऽन्यो वा विमर्श इति कीर्तितः ।
तत्र योऽभिनवाभासः स प्रोक्तोऽनुभवात्मकः ॥ ६९ ॥
āntaraḥ abhinavaḥ anyaḥ vā vimarśa iti kīrtitaḥ ।
tatra yaḥ abhinava-ābhāsaḥ saḥ proktaḥ anubhava-ātmakaḥ ॥ 69 ॥

āntaraḥ — internal, abhinavaḥ — new, anyaḥ — another, vā — or, vimarśaḥ — reflection, iti — thus, kīrtitaḥ — mentioned, tatra — therein, yaḥ — which, abhinava-ābhāsaḥ — new appearance, saḥ — that, proktaḥ — said, anubhava-ātmakaḥ — experiential.
Internal, new, or another, is mentioned as reflection. Therein, the new appearance is said to be experiential.
अन्यः स्मृत्यनुसन्धानात्मकः संस्कारसम्भवः ।
एवं मनो द्विप्रकारशक्तियुक्तं सदा स्थितम्‌ ॥ ७० ॥
anyaḥ smṛti-anusandhāna-ātmakaḥ saṁskāra-sambhavaḥ ।
evaṁ manaḥ dvi-prakāra-śakti-yuktaṁ sadā sthitam ॥ 70 ॥

anyaḥ — another, smṛti-anusandhāna-ātmakaḥ — of the nature of memory and investigation, saṁskāra-sambhavaḥ — arising from impressions, evaṁ — thus, manaḥ — mind, dvi-prakāra-śakti-yuktaṁ — endowed with two kinds of power, sadā — always, sthitam — situated.
Another is of the nature of memory and investigation, arising from impressions. Thus, the mind, endowed with two kinds of power, is always situated.
निद्राप्रकाशरूपाऽसौ सुषुप्तिश्चिरसंस्थिता ।
जागसमर्शबहुला चेत्यमूढदशोच्यते ॥ ७१ ॥
nidrā-prakāśa-rūpā asau suṣuptiḥ cira-saṁsthitā ।
jāga-saṁmarśa-bahulā cetya-mūḍha-daśā ucyate ॥ 71 ॥

nidrā-prakāśa-rūpā — of the form of sleep and illumination, asau — that, suṣuptiḥ — deep sleep, cira-saṁsthitā — long-standing, jāga-saṁmarśa-bahulā — full of waking reflection, ca — and, iti — thus, amūḍha-daśā — non-deluded state, ucyate — is called.
That deep sleep, of the form of sleep and illumination, long-standing, full of waking reflection, is called the non-deluded state.
प्रकाशनिबिडा यस्मात्‌ सुषुप्तिर्मूढतात्मिका ।
अत एव हि दीपादेः प्रकाशनिबिडत्वतः ॥ ७२ ॥
prakāśa-nibiḍā yasmāt suṣuptiḥ mūḍhatā-ātmikā ।
ataḥ eva hi dīpa-ādeḥ prakāśa-nibiḍatvataḥ ॥ 72 ॥

prakāśa-nibiḍā — dense with illumination, yasmāt — because, suṣuptiḥ — deep sleep, mūḍhatā-ātmikā — of the nature of confusion, ataḥ — therefore, eva — indeed, hi — surely, dīpa-ādeḥ — like a lamp, prakāśa-nibiḍatvataḥ — due to density of illumination.
Because deep sleep is dense with illumination and of the nature of confusion, therefore, indeed, it is like a lamp due to the density of illumination.
निश्चिता मूढता सर्वैर्विद्वद्भिरपि सर्वथा ।
निद्रा प्रथमजाऽव्यक्तं महाशून्यमिहोच्यते ॥ ७३ ॥
niścitā mūḍhatā sarvaiḥ vidvadbhiḥ api sarvathā ।
nidrā prathama-jā avyaktam mahā-śūnyam iha ucyate ॥ 73 ॥

niścitā — determined, mūḍhatā — confusion, sarvaiḥ — by all, vidvadbhiḥ — by the wise, api — also, sarvathā — in every way, nidrā — sleep, prathama-jā — first-born, avyaktam — unmanifest, mahā-śūnyam — great void, iha — here, ucyate — is called.
Determined as confusion by all, even by the wise in every way, sleep is called the first-born, unmanifest, great void here.
नास्ति सामान्यपदवी सुषुप्तिस्तत्प्रकाशनम्‌ ।
वस्तुदर्शनकालेऽपि जाग्रत्येवंविधं मनः ॥ ७४ ॥
nāsti sāmānya-padavī suṣuptiḥ tat-prakāśanam ।
vastu-darśana-kāle api jāgrati evaṁ-vidhaṁ manaḥ ॥ 74 ॥

nāsti — there is not, sāmānya-padavī — common state, suṣuptiḥ — deep sleep, tat-prakāśanam — its illumination, vastu-darśana-kāle — during object perception, api — even, jāgrati — in waking, evaṁ-vidhaṁ — of this kind, manaḥ — mind.
There is no common state of deep sleep. Its illumination, during object perception, even in waking, the mind is of this kind.
किन्तूत्तरक्षणोद्‌भूतविकल्पौघैस्तिरोहितम्‌ ।
सुषुप्तावव्यक्तशक्तिप्रकाशनिबिडत्वतः ॥ ७५ ॥
kintu uttara-kṣaṇa-udbhūta-vikalpa-aughaiḥ tirohitam ।
suṣuptau avyakta-śakti-prakāśa-nibiḍatvataḥ ॥ 75 ॥

kintu — but, uttara-kṣaṇa-udbhūta — arisen in the next moment, vikalpa-aughaiḥ — by the flood of concepts, tirohitam — hidden, suṣuptau — in deep sleep, avyakta-śakti — unmanifest power, prakāśa-nibiḍatvataḥ — due to density of illumination.
But hidden by the flood of concepts arising in the next moment, in deep sleep, due to the density of illumination of unmanifest power.
मनो विलीनमित्येवं विविञ्चन्ति विवेचकाः ।
वस्तुदर्शनकालेऽपि चैवं लीनं मनो भवेत्‌ ॥ ७६ ॥
mano vilīnam iti evaṁ viciṁcanti vivecakāḥ ।
vastu-darśana-kāle api ca evaṁ līnaṁ manaḥ bhavet ॥ 76 ॥

mano — mind, vilīnam — dissolved, iti — thus, evaṁ — in this way, viciṁcanti — discern, vivecakāḥ — the discerning ones, vastu-darśana-kāle — during object perception, api — even, ca — and, evaṁ — thus, līnaṁ — dissolved, manaḥ — mind, bhavet — becomes.
Thus, the discerning ones discern the mind as dissolved. During object perception, even thus, the mind becomes dissolved.
शृणु ब्रह्मन्‌ रहस्यं ते वक्ष्यामि स्वानुभूतितः ।
यत्र मुह्यन्ति विद्वांसोऽप्यतिसूक्ष्मविवेचकाः ॥ ७७ ॥
śṛṇu brahman rahasyaṁ te vakṣyāmi sva-anubhūtitaḥ ।
yatra muhyanti vidvāṁsaḥ api ati-sūkṣma-vivecakāḥ ॥ 77 ॥

śṛṇu — listen, brahman — O sage, rahasyaṁ — secret, te — to you, vakṣyāmi — I will explain, sva-anubhūtitaḥ — from my own experience, yatra — where, muhyanti — get confused, vidvāṁsaḥ — the wise, api — even, ati-sūkṣma-vivecakāḥ — highly subtle discerners.
Listen, O sage, I will explain to you the secret from my own experience, where even the wise and highly subtle discerners get confused.
निर्विकल्पसमाधिश्च सुषुप्तिर्वस्तुदर्शनम्‌ ।
त्रयमेतच्चैकविधं प्रकाशनिबिडत्वतः ॥ ७८ ॥
nirvikalpa-samādhiḥ ca suṣuptiḥ vastu-darśanam ।
trayam etat ca ekavidhaṁ prakāśa-nibiḍatvataḥ ॥ 78 ॥

nirvikalpa-samādhiḥ — non-conceptual absorption, ca — and, suṣuptiḥ — deep sleep, vastu-darśanam — object perception, trayam — trio, etat — this, ca — and, ekavidhaṁ — one kind, prakāśa-nibiḍatvataḥ — due to density of illumination.
Non-conceptual absorption, deep sleep, and object perception, this trio is of one kind due to the density of illumination.
विमर्शभेदाद्‌ भेदो हि लक्ष्यते व्यावहारिकैः ।
तत्र हेतुर्भास्यभेदादित्येव प्रविनिश्चयः ॥ ७९ ॥
vimarśa-bhedāt bhedaḥ hi lakṣyate vyāvahārikaiḥ ।
tatra hetuḥ bhāsya-bhedāt iti eva praviniścayaḥ ॥ 79 ॥

vimarśa-bhedāt — due to difference in reflection, bhedaḥ — distinction, hi — indeed, lakṣyate — is observed, vyāvahārikaiḥ — by practitioners, tatra — there, hetuḥ — cause, bhāsya-bhedāt — due to difference in objects, iti — thus, eva — indeed, praviniścayaḥ — determination.
Due to the difference in reflection, distinction is observed by practitioners. The cause there is determined to be the difference in objects.
समाधौ केवलचितिः सुप्तावव्यक्तमेव च ।
दर्शने भिन्नभासो हि भास्यमेवं त्रिधा स्थितम्‌ ॥ ८० ॥
samādhau kevala-citiḥ suptau avyaktam eva ca ।
darśane bhinna-bhāsaḥ hi bhāsyam evaṁ tridhā sthitam ॥ 80 ॥

samādhau — in absorption, kevala-citiḥ — pure consciousness, suptau — in sleep, avyaktam — unmanifest, eva — indeed, ca — and, darśane — in perception, bhinna-bhāsaḥ — differentiated appearance, hi — indeed, bhāsyam — object, evaṁ — thus, tridhā — threefold, sthitam — situated.
In absorption, pure consciousness; in sleep, unmanifest; and in perception, differentiated appearance. Thus, the object is situated in a threefold manner.
भास्यभेदेऽपि भासस्तु केवलं निर्विकल्पकः ।
अतः प्रकाशनिबिड इत्येव संप्रचक्षते ॥ ८१ ॥
bhāsyabhede api bhāsaḥ tu kevalaṁ nirvikalpakaḥ ।
ataḥ prakāśa-nibiḍa iti eva saṁpracakṣate ॥ 81 ॥

bhāsyabhede — despite differences in the objects, api — even, bhāsaḥ — illumination, tu — indeed, kevalaṁ — only, nirvikalpakaḥ — non-conceptual, ataḥ — therefore, prakāśa-nibiḍaḥ — dense illumination, iti — thus, eva — indeed, saṁpracakṣate — is called.
Despite differences in the objects, the illumination is only non-conceptual. Therefore, it is called dense illumination.
समाधिश्च सुषुप्तिश्च चिरकालभवत्वतः ।
अनन्तरं स्पष्टतया सर्वैरपि विमृश्यते ॥ ८२ ॥
samādhiḥ ca suṣuptiḥ ca cira-kāla-bhavatvataḥ ।
anantaraṁ spaṣṭatayā sarvaiḥ api vimṛśyate ॥ 82 ॥

samādhiḥ — absorption, ca — and, suṣuptiḥ — deep sleep, ca — and, cira-kāla-bhavatvataḥ — due to long duration, anantaraṁ — subsequently, spaṣṭatayā — clearly, sarvaiḥ — by all, api — even, vimṛśyate — is discerned.
Absorption and deep sleep, due to their long duration, are subsequently clearly discerned by all.
क्षणिकत्वाद्‌ दर्शनं तु स्पष्टं नहि विमृश्यते ।
एवं समाधिः सुप्तिश्च क्षणिका न विमृश्यते ॥ ८३ ॥
kṣaṇikatvāt darśanaṁ tu spaṣṭaṁ nahi vimṛśyate ।
evaṁ samādhiḥ suptiḥ ca kṣaṇikā na vimṛśyate ॥ 83 ॥

kṣaṇikatvāt — due to momentariness, darśanaṁ — perception, tu — indeed, spaṣṭaṁ — clearly, nahi — not, vimṛśyate — is discerned, evaṁ — thus, samādhiḥ — absorption, suptiḥ — sleep, ca — and, kṣaṇikā — momentary, na — not, vimṛśyate — is discerned.
Due to momentariness, perception is not clearly discerned. Thus, absorption and sleep, being momentary, are not discerned.
सुषुप्तिः क्षणिका तद्वत्‌ समाधिरपि विद्यते ।
सुषुप्तिर्लक्ष्यते सूक्ष्मदृग्भिः परिचयात्‌ खलु ॥ ८४ ॥
suṣuptiḥ kṣaṇikā tadvat samādhiḥ api vidyate ।
suṣuptiḥ lakṣyate sūkṣma-dṛgbhiḥ paricayāt khalu ॥ 84 ॥

suṣuptiḥ — deep sleep, kṣaṇikā — momentary, tadvat — likewise, samādhiḥ — absorption, api — also, vidyate — exists, suṣuptiḥ — deep sleep, lakṣyate — is observed, sūkṣma-dṛgbhiḥ — by those with subtle vision, paricayāt — due to familiarity, khalu — indeed.
Deep sleep is momentary; likewise, absorption also exists. Deep sleep is observed by those with subtle vision, due to familiarity, indeed.
समाधिस्त्वपरिचयात्‌ सूक्ष्मो नहि विमृश्यते ।
सर्वेषां प्राणिनां ब्रह्मन्‌ व्यवहारदशास्वपि ॥ ८५ ॥
samādhiḥ tu aparicayāt sūkṣmaḥ nahi vimṛśyate ।
sarveṣāṁ prāṇināṁ brahman vyavahāra-daśāsu api ॥ 85 ॥

samādhiḥ — absorption, tu — indeed, aparicayāt — due to unfamiliarity, sūkṣmaḥ — subtle, nahi — not, vimṛśyate — is discerned, sarveṣāṁ — of all, prāṇināṁ — beings, brahman — O sage, vyavahāra-daśāsu — in states of activity, api — even.
Absorption, indeed, due to unfamiliarity, is not discerned as subtle by all beings, O sage, even in states of activity.
सूक्ष्माः समाधयः सन्ति चाव्युत्पत्त्या विभान्ति नो ।
जाग्रत्यविमृशिर्या स्यात्‌ स समाधिरूदीरितः ॥ ८६ ॥
sūkṣmāḥ samādhayaḥ santi ca avyutpattyā vibhānti no ।
jāgrati avimṛśiḥ yā syāt sa samādhiḥ udīritaḥ ॥ 86 ॥

sūkṣmāḥ — subtle, samādhayaḥ — absorptions, santi — are, ca — and, avyutpattyā — due to lack of cultivation, vibhānti — appear, no — not, jāgrati — in waking, avimṛśiḥ — non-reflection, yā — which, syāt — is, sa — that, samādhiḥ — absorption, udīritaḥ — is stated.
Subtle absorptions are present but do not appear due to lack of cultivation. In waking, the non-reflection which is, is stated as absorption.
विमर्शाभावमात्रं तु समाधिरभिधीयते ।
सुषुप्तौ दर्शने चापि समाधित्वमतः स्थितम्‌ ॥ ८७ ॥
vimarśa-abhāva-mātraṁ tu samādhiḥ abhidhīyate ।
suṣuptau darśane ca api samādhitvam ataḥ sthitam ॥ 87 ॥

vimarśa-abhāva-mātraṁ — mere absence of reflection, tu — indeed, samādhiḥ — absorption, abhidhīyate — is called, suṣuptau — in deep sleep, darśane — in perception, ca — and, api — also, samādhitvam — state of absorption, ataḥ — thus, sthitam — is situated.
The mere absence of reflection is called absorption. Thus, the state of absorption is situated in deep sleep and in perception.
किन्तु मुख्यसमाधित्वमनयोर्नहि विद्यते ।
भेदामर्शनसंस्कारगर्भितत्वान्न मुख्यता ॥ ८८ ॥
kintu mukhya-samādhitvam anayoḥ nahi vidyate ।
bheda-amarśana-saṁskāra-garbhitatvāt na mukhyatā ॥ 88 ॥

kintu — but, mukhya-samādhitvam — primary absorption, anayoḥ — of these two, nahi — not, vidyate — is found, bheda-amarśana — absence of distinction, saṁskāra-garbhitatvāt — due to being imbued with impressions, na — not, mukhyatā — primacy.
But primary absorption is not found in these two. Due to being imbued with impressions of absence of distinction, there is no primacy.
दर्शनं जाग्रति भवेदविमर्शनरूपकम्‌ ।
तथापि ते प्रवक्ष्यामि मुनिपुत्रादराच्छृणु ॥ ८९ ॥
darśanaṁ jāgrati bhavet avimarśana-rūpakam ।
tathā api te pravakṣyāmi muni-putra ādarāt śṛṇu ॥ 89 ॥

darśanaṁ — perception, jāgrati — in waking, bhavet — becomes, avimarśana-rūpakam — of the nature of non-reflection, tathā api — yet, te — to you, pravakṣyāmi — I will explain, muni-putra — O sage's son, ādarāt — with respect, śṛṇu — listen.
Perception in waking becomes of the nature of non-reflection. Yet, I will explain to you, O sage's son, with respect. Listen.
अव्यक्तं यत्प्रथमजं नास्ति सामान्यकं हि तत्‌ ।
नास्तीत्येव हि तद्भानमत्यन्ताभावरूपकम्‌ ॥ ९० ॥
avyaktaṁ yat prathama-jaṁ nāsti sāmānya-kaṁ hi tat ।
nāsti iti eva hi tat-bhānam atyanta-abhāva-rūpakam ॥ 90 ॥

avyaktaṁ — unmanifest, yat — which, prathama-jam — first-born, nāsti — is not, sāmānya-kam — common, hi — indeed, tat — that, nāsti iti — it does not exist, eva — indeed, hi — surely, tat-bhānam — its perception, atyanta-abhāva-rūpakam — of the nature of absolute non-existence.
The unmanifest, which is first-born, is not common. Indeed, its perception as "it does not exist" is of the nature of absolute non-existence.
एषा सुषुप्तिरित्युक्ता जडशक्तिर्भवेच्चितः ।
दर्शने भासमानं च नास्त्याभासपदं यतः ॥ ९१ ॥
eṣā suṣuptiḥ iti uktā jaḍa-śaktiḥ bhavet cittaḥ ।
darśane bhāsamānaṁ ca nāsti ābhāsa-padaṁ yataḥ ॥ 91 ॥

eṣā — this, suṣuptiḥ — deep sleep, iti — thus, uktā — is said, jaḍa-śaktiḥ — inert power, bhavet — becomes, cittaḥ — of consciousness, darśane — in perception, bhāsamānam — appearing, ca — and, nāsti — is not, ābhāsa-padam — state of appearance, yataḥ — because.
This deep sleep is thus said to be the inert power of consciousness. In perception, appearing, it does not reach the state of appearance.
अतः सुषुप्तिरेव स्याज्जडदर्शनसङ्गता ।
समाधौ भासमाना या चितिः सा ब्रह्मरूपिणी ॥ ९२ ॥
ataḥ suṣuptiḥ eva syāt jaḍa-darśana-saṅgatā ।
samādhau bhāsamānā yā citiḥ sā brahma-rūpiṇī ॥ 92 ॥

ataḥ — therefore, suṣuptiḥ — deep sleep, eva — indeed, syāt — is, jaḍa-darśana-saṅgatā — associated with inert perception, samādhau — in absorption, bhāsamānā — appearing, yā — which, citiḥ — consciousness, sā — it, brahma-rūpiṇī — of the nature of Brahman.
Therefore, deep sleep is indeed associated with inert perception. In absorption, the consciousness that appears is of the nature of Brahman.
भक्षिणी कालदेशानां नास्त्याभासविनाशिनी ।
सर्वथाऽस्तिमयो देवी सुषुप्तिः सा कथं भवेत्‌ ॥ ९३ ॥
bhakṣiṇī kāla-deśānāṁ nāsti-ābhāsa-vināśinī ।
sarvathā-asti-mayaḥ devī suṣuptiḥ sā kathaṁ bhavet ॥ 93 ॥

bhakṣiṇī — devouring, kāla-deśānāṁ — of time and space, nāsti-ābhāsa-vināśinī — destroyer of non-existence appearance, sarvathā — completely, asti-mayaḥ — made of existence, devī — goddess, suṣuptiḥ — deep sleep, sā — that, kathaṁ — how, bhavet — can be.
Devouring time and space, destroyer of the appearance of non-existence, completely made of existence, how can that goddess be deep sleep?
तस्मात्‌ सुषुप्तिमात्रेण न भवेद्धि कृतार्थता ।
बोधयामास जनक इत्यष्टावक्रमुक्तिभिः ॥ ९४ ॥
tasmāt suṣupti-mātreṇa na bhavet hi kṛtārthatā ।
bodhayāmāsa janaka iti aṣṭāvakra-muktibhiḥ ॥ 94 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, suṣupti-mātreṇa — by mere deep sleep, na — not, bhavet — becomes, hi — indeed, kṛtārthatā — fulfillment, bodhayāmāsa — enlightened, janaka — Janaka, iti — thus, aṣṭāvakra — Ashtavakra, muktibhiḥ — by words.
Therefore, mere deep sleep does not become fulfillment. Janaka thus enlightened Ashtavakra with these words.

colophon.en: Thus ends the sixteenth chapter named "Ashtavakra" in the revered Knowledge Section of Tripura Rahasya.

lines.text: श्रुत्वैवं जनकेनोक्तमष्टावक्रः पुनर्नुपम्‌ ।
पप्रच्छ यत्तद्वदामि शृणु भार्गव यत्नतः ॥ १ ॥
śrutvā evaṁ janakena uktam aṣṭāvakraḥ punar nṛpam ।
papraccha yat tad vadāmi śṛṇu bhārgava yatnataḥ ॥ 1 ॥

śrutvā — having heard, evaṁ — thus, janakena — by Janaka, uktam — said, aṣṭāvakraḥ — Ashtavakra, punaḥ — again, nṛpam — to the king, papraccha — asked, yat — which, tad — that, vadāmi — I will tell, śṛṇu — listen, bhārgava — O descendant of Bhrigu, yatnataḥ — attentively.
Having heard thus from Janaka, Ashtavakra again asked the king. What he asked, I will tell you. Listen attentively, O descendant of Bhrigu.
राजन्‌ यदुक्तं भवता व्यवहारदशास्वपि ।
सूक्ष्माः समाधयः सन्तीत्येवं तन्मे वद स्फुटम्‌ ॥ २ ॥
rājan yad uktam bhavatā vyavahāra-daśāsu api ।
sūkṣmāḥ samādhayaḥ santi iti evaṁ tan me vada sphuṭam ॥ 2 ॥

rājan — O king, yad — which, uktam — said, bhavatā — by you, vyavahāra-daśāsu — in states of activity, api — even, sūkṣmāḥ — subtle, samādhayaḥ — absorptions, santi — are, iti — thus, evaṁ — indeed, tat — that, me — to me, vada — tell, sphuṭam — clearly.
O king, you said that even in states of activity, there are subtle absorptions. Thus, tell me that clearly.
दशासु कासु ते सन्ति निर्विकल्पचिदात्मकाः ।
एवं तेनानुयुक्तोऽथ प्राह राजा महाशयः ॥ ३ ॥
daśāsu kāsu te santi nirvikalpa-cid-ātmakāḥ ।
evaṁ tena anuyuktaḥ atha prāha rājā mahāśayaḥ ॥ 3 ॥

daśāsu — in the states, kāsu — in which, te — they, santi — are, nirvikalpa-cid-ātmakāḥ — of non-conceptual consciousness, evaṁ — thus, tena — by him, anuyuktaḥ — asked, atha — then, prāha — said, rājā — the king, mahāśayaḥ — the great soul.
In which states are those absorptions of non-conceptual consciousness? Thus asked by him, the great king then said.
शृणु ब्रह्मन्‌ प्रवक्ष्यामि व्यवहारे समाधयः ।
प्रियया सम्परिष्वक्तो नव्यया प्रथमं यदा ॥ ४ ॥
śṛṇu brahman pravakṣyāmi vyavahāre samādhayaḥ ।
priyayā sampariṣvaktaḥ navyayā prathamaṁ yadā ॥ 4 ॥

śṛṇu — listen, brahman — O sage, pravakṣyāmi — I will explain, vyavahāre — in activities, samādhayaḥ — absorptions, priyayā — by the beloved, sampariṣvaktaḥ — embraced, navyayā — newly, prathamaṁ — first, yadā — when.
Listen, O sage, I will explain the absorptions in activities. When first embraced by the beloved, newly.
तदा न वेद बाह्यं वाऽप्यान्तरं वा क्षणं नरः ।
तिष्ठेन्न निद्रयाक्रान्तः स समाधिरुदीरितः ॥ ५ ॥
tadā na veda bāhyaṁ vā api āntaraṁ vā kṣaṇaṁ naraḥ ।
tiṣṭhenna nidrayā ākrāntaḥ sa samādhiḥ udīritaḥ ॥ 5 ॥

tadā — then, na — not, veda — knows, bāhyaṁ — external, vā — or, api — even, āntaraṁ — internal, vā — or, kṣaṇaṁ — for a moment, naraḥ — man, tiṣṭhet — remains, na — not, nidrayā — by sleep, ākrāntaḥ — overpowered, saḥ — that, samādhiḥ — absorption, udīritaḥ — is called.
Then, the man does not know the external or internal for a moment. He remains not overpowered by sleep. That is called absorption.
यच्चिराद्वाञ्छितं किञ्चिदलभ्यत्वेन निश्चितम्‌ ।
अकस्मात्तस्य संप्राप्तिर्यदा भवति वै मुने ॥ ६ ॥
yaccirād vāñchitaṁ kiñcid alabhyatvena niścitam ।
akasmat tasya saṁprāptiḥ yadā bhavati vai mune ॥ 6 ॥

yad — which, cirāt — after a long time, vāñchitam — desired, kiñcid — something, alabhyatvena — as unattainable, niścitam — determined, akasmat — suddenly, tasya — its, saṁprāptiḥ — attainment, yadā — when, bhavati — happens, vai — indeed, mune — O sage.
When something long desired, determined as unattainable, is suddenly attained, O sage.
तदा न वेद बाह्यं वाऽप्यान्तरं वा क्षणं नरः ।
तिष्ठेन्न निद्रयाक्रान्तः स समाधिरुदीरितः ॥ ७ ॥
tadā na veda bāhyaṁ vā api āntaraṁ vā kṣaṇaṁ naraḥ ।
tiṣṭhenna nidrayā ākrāntaḥ sa samādhiḥ udīritaḥ ॥ 7 ॥

tadā — then, na — not, veda — knows, bāhyaṁ — external, vā — or, api — even, āntaraṁ — internal, vā — or, kṣaṇaṁ — for a moment, naraḥ — man, tiṣṭhet — remains, na — not, nidrayā — by sleep, ākrāntaḥ — overpowered, saḥ — that, samādhiḥ — absorption, udīritaḥ — is called.
Then, the man does not know the external or internal for a moment. He remains not overpowered by sleep. That is called absorption.
अतर्कितं व्रजन्‌ क्वापि निर्भयो हृष्टमानसः ।
अकस्माद्यदि सम्पश्येद्‌ व्याघ्रादि मृत्युसम्मितम्‌ ॥ ८ ॥
atarkitaṁ vrajan kvāpi nirbhayaḥ hṛṣṭa-mānasaḥ ।
akasmat yadi sampaśyed vyāghra-ādi mṛtyu-sammitam ॥ 8 ॥

atarkitam — unexpectedly, vrajan — going, kvāpi — somewhere, nirbhayaḥ — fearless, hṛṣṭa-mānasaḥ — with a delighted mind, akasmat — suddenly, yadi — if, sampaśyet — sees, vyāghra-ādi — tiger, etc., mṛtyu-sammitam — death-like.
Unexpectedly going somewhere, fearless with a delighted mind, if suddenly sees a tiger, etc., like death.
तदा न वेद बाह्यं वाऽप्यान्तरं वा क्षणं नरः ।
तिष्ठेन्न निद्रयाक्रान्तः स समाधिरुदीरितः ॥ ९ ॥
tadā na veda bāhyaṁ vā api āntaraṁ vā kṣaṇaṁ naraḥ ।
tiṣṭhenna nidrayā ākrāntaḥ sa samādhiḥ udīritaḥ ॥ 9 ॥

tadā — then, na — not, veda — knows, bāhyaṁ — external, vā — or, api — even, āntaraṁ — internal, vā — or, kṣaṇaṁ — for a moment, naraḥ — man, tiṣṭhet — remains, na — not, nidrayā — by sleep, ākrāntaḥ — overpowered, saḥ — that, samādhiḥ — absorption, udīritaḥ — is called.
Then, the man does not know the external or internal for a moment. He remains not overpowered by sleep. That is called absorption.
अतिप्रियं स्वपुत्रादि विभुं च गृहकर्मणि ।
अरोगिणं यदाऽकस्मात्‌ संशृणोति मृतं किल ॥ १० ॥
atipriyaṁ svaputra-ādi vibhum ca gṛha-karmaṇi ।
arogiṇaṁ yadā akasmat saṁśṛṇoti mṛtaṁ kila ॥ 10 ॥

atipriyam — very dear, svaputra-ādi — one's own son, etc., vibhum — the lord, ca — and, gṛha-karmaṇi — in household duties, arogiṇam — healthy, yadā — when, akasmat — suddenly, saṁśṛṇoti — hears, mṛtam — dead, kila — indeed.
When very dear, one's own son, etc., the lord in household duties, suddenly hears as dead, indeed.
तदा न वेद बाह्यं वाऽप्यान्तरं वा क्षणं नरः ।
तिष्ठेन्न निद्रयाक्रान्तः स समाधिरुदीरितः ॥ ११ ॥
tadā na veda bāhyaṁ vā api āntaraṁ vā kṣaṇaṁ naraḥ ।
tiṣṭhet na nidrayā ākrāntaḥ saḥ samādhiḥ udīritaḥ ॥ 11 ॥

tadā — then, na — not, veda — knows, bāhyaṁ — external, vā — or, api — even, āntaraṁ — internal, vā — or, kṣaṇaṁ — for a moment, naraḥ — man, tiṣṭhet — remains, na — not, nidrayā — by sleep, ākrāntaḥ — overpowered, saḥ — that, samādhiḥ — absorption, udīritaḥ — is called.
Then, the man does not know the external or internal for a moment. He remains not overpowered by sleep. That is called absorption.
अथान्यथापि वक्ष्यामि समाधेः सम्भवं शृणु ।
जाग्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्तीनां मध्ये सन्ति समाधयः ॥ १२ ॥
atha anyathā api vakṣyāmi samādheḥ sambhavam śṛṇu ।
jāgrat-svapna-suṣuptīnām madhye santi samādhayaḥ ॥ 12 ॥

atha — now, anyathā — otherwise, api — also, vakṣyāmi — I will tell, samādheḥ — of absorption, sambhavam — origin, śṛṇu — listen, jāgrat-svapna-suṣuptīnām — of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, madhye — in between, santi — there are, samādhayaḥ — absorptions.
Now, I will also tell otherwise the origin of absorption. Listen, there are absorptions in between waking, dreaming, and deep sleep.
दूरे किञ्चित्‌ पश्यतस्तु बुद्धया चैकाग्रया मुने ।
मनो दीर्घात्मतां याति जलूकेव तृणालिषु ॥ १३ ॥
dūre kiñcit paśyataḥ tu buddhyā ca ekāgrayā mune ।
mano dīrghātmatāṁ yāti jalūkeva tṛṇāliṣu ॥ 13 ॥

dūre — at a distance, kiñcit — something, paśyataḥ — seeing, tu — but, buddhyā — by the intellect, ca — and, ekāgrayā — one-pointed, mune — O sage, manaḥ — mind, dīrghātmatāṁ — elongated state, yāti — goes, jalūkā — leech, iva — like, tṛṇa-āliṣu — in the blades of grass.
Seeing something at a distance with a one-pointed intellect, O sage, the mind goes into an elongated state like a leech on the blades of grass.
देहे देहाभासमयं भावे भावात्मकं तथा ।
मध्ये तत्निर्विकल्पाख्यं मनो लक्षय सर्वदा ॥ १४ ॥
dehe dehābhāsamayaṁ bhāve bhāvātmakaṁ tathā ।
madhye tat nirvikalpa-ākhyam manaḥ lakṣaya sarvadā ॥ 14 ॥

dehe — in the body, deha-ābhāsa-mayam — consisting of the appearance of the body, bhāve — in the state, bhāva-ātmakam — consisting of feeling, tathā — likewise, madhye — in between, tat — that, nirvikalpa-ākhyam — called non-conceptual, manaḥ — mind, lakṣaya — observe, sarvadā — always.
In the body, consisting of the appearance of the body, and in the state of feeling, likewise, in between, observe the mind always in the state called non-conceptual.
बहुना किमिहोक्तेन शृणु सूक्ष्मविमर्शन ।
व्यवहारे न कस्यापि ज्ञानमेकं तु भासते ॥ १५ ॥
bahunā kim iha uktena śṛṇu sūkṣma-vimarśana ।
vyavahāre na kasya api jñānam ekaṁ tu bhāsate ॥ 15 ॥

bahunā — with many words, kim — what, iha — here, uktena — by speaking, śṛṇu — listen, sūkṣma-vimarśana — subtle examiner, vyavahāre — in activities, na — not, kasya api — of anyone, jñānam — knowledge, ekam — one, tu — but, bhāsate — shines.
What is the use of many words here? Listen, O subtle examiner, in activities, the knowledge of anyone does not shine as one.
खण्डज्ञानसमूहात्मा व्यवहारोऽयमाततः ।
अत एव वर्णयन्ति तैर्थिकाः सर्व एव हि ॥ १६ ॥
khaṇḍa-jñāna-samūha-ātmā vyavahāraḥ ayam ātaḥ ।
ata eva varṇayanti tairthikāḥ sarva eva hi ॥ 16 ॥

khaṇḍa-jñāna — fragmented knowledge, samūha-ātmā — consisting of groups, vyavahāraḥ — activity, ayam — this, ātaḥ — therefore, ataḥ — therefore, eva — indeed, varṇayanti — describe, tairthikāḥ — philosophers, sarva — all, eva — indeed, hi — surely.
This activity consists of fragmented knowledge and groups. Therefore, all philosophers indeed describe it as such.
आत्मानं बुद्धिमपि वा क्षणभेदविभेदितम्‌ ।
तदन्तरक्षणौघेषु निर्विकल्पदशा स्थिता ॥ १७ ॥
ātmānaṁ buddhim api vā kṣaṇa-bheda-vibheditam ।
tad-antara-kṣaṇa-ogheṣu nirvikalpa-daśā sthitā ॥ 17 ॥

ātmānam — self, buddhim — intellect, api — also, vā — or, kṣaṇa-bheda-vibheditam — divided by moments, tad-antara-kṣaṇa-ogheṣu — in the stream of those moments, nirvikalpa-daśā — state of non-conceptuality, sthitā — stands.
The self or intellect, divided by moments, stands in the state of non-conceptuality in the stream of those moments.
कहोलात्मज जानीहि जानतां तु प्रतिक्षणम्‌ ।
समाधिरस्ति चान्यस्य समाधिः शशशृङ्गवत्‌ ॥ १८ ॥
kahola-ātmaja jānīhi jānatāṁ tu prati-kṣaṇam ।
samādhiḥ asti ca anyasya samādhiḥ śaśa-śṛṅga-vat ॥ 18 ॥

kahola-ātmaja — son of Kahola, jānīhi — know, jānatām — of the knowers, tu — indeed, prati-kṣaṇam — every moment, samādhiḥ — absorption, asti — there is, ca — and, anyasya — of another, samādhiḥ — absorption, śaśa-śṛṅga-vat — like the horn of a rabbit.
O son of Kahola, know that for the knowers, there is absorption every moment. For another, absorption is like the horn of a rabbit.
जनकोक्तमिति श्रुत्वा भूयः पप्रच्छ स द्विजः ।
राजन्नेवं व्यवहृतौ समाधिर्निर्विकल्पकः ॥ १९ ॥
janaka-uktam iti śrutvā bhūyaḥ papraccha saḥ dvijaḥ ।
rājan evaṁ vyavahṛtau samādhiḥ nirvikalpakaḥ ॥ 19 ॥

janaka-uktam — said by Janaka, iti — thus, śrutvā — having heard, bhūyaḥ — again, papraccha — asked, saḥ — he, dvijaḥ — the sage, rājan — O king, evaṁ — thus, vyavahṛtau — in activity, samādhiḥ — absorption, nirvikalpakaḥ — non-conceptual.
Having heard thus said by Janaka, the sage again asked, "O king, is absorption non-conceptual in activity?"
सर्वेषामस्ति यदि चेत्तत्‌ कुतः संसृतिर्भवेत्‌ ।
सृषुप्तौ दर्शने चापि जडाव्यक्तविभासतः ॥ २० ॥
sarveṣām asti yadi cet tat kutaḥ saṁsṛtiḥ bhavet ।
suṣuptau darśane ca api jaḍa-avyakta-vibhāsataḥ ॥ 20 ॥

sarveṣām — for everyone, asti — there is, yadi — if, cet — thus, tat — that, kutaḥ — how, saṁsṛtiḥ — transmigration, bhavet — would be, suṣuptau — in deep sleep, darśane — in perception, ca — and, api — also, jaḍa-avyakta-vibhāsataḥ — appearing inert and indistinct.
If that is for everyone, how would there be transmigration? In deep sleep and perception, appearing inert and indistinct.
पुरुषार्थासाधनत्वं समाधिस्त्वविकल्पकः ।
शुद्धसंविद्विभातात्मा तद्‌ भूयः संसृतिः कथम्‌ ॥ २१ ॥
puruṣārthāsādhanatvaṁ samādhis tu avikalpakaḥ ।
śuddha-saṁvid-vibhātātmā tad bhūyaḥ saṁsṛtiḥ katham ॥ 21 ॥

puruṣārthāsādhanatvam — the accomplishment of human goals, samādhiḥ — absorption, tu — indeed, avikalpakaḥ — non-conceptual, śuddha-saṁvid — pure consciousness, vibhāta-ātmā — shining self, tad — that, bhūyaḥ — again, saṁsṛtiḥ — transmigration, katham — how.
The accomplishment of human goals is indeed through non-conceptual absorption, where the pure consciousness shines as the self. How then can there be transmigration again?
एतदेव हि विज्ञानमज्ञानकुलनाशनम्‌ ।
निर्विकल्पसमाध्याख्यं यन्निःश्रेयसकारणम्‌ ॥ २२ ॥
etad eva hi vijñānam ajñāna-kula-nāśanam ।
nirvikalpa-samādhi-ākhyam yan niḥśreyasa-kāraṇam ॥ 22 ॥

etad — this, eva — indeed, hi — surely, vijñānam — knowledge, ajñāna-kula-nāśanam — destroyer of the family of ignorance, nirvikalpa-samādhi-ākhyam — called non-conceptual absorption, yat — which, niḥśreyasa-kāraṇam — cause of the highest good.
This knowledge is indeed the destroyer of the family of ignorance, called non-conceptual absorption, which is the cause of the highest good.
एतन्मे शंस राजेन्द्र सर्वसंशयनाशनम्‌ ।
इत्यापृष्टो महीपालः प्राह तं मुनिपुङ्गवम्‌ ॥ २३ ॥
etan me śaṁsa rājendra sarva-saṁśaya-nāśanam ।
ityāpṛṣṭo mahīpālaḥ prāha taṁ muni-puṅgavam ॥ 23 ॥

etan — this, me — to me, śaṁsa — tell, rājendra — O king, sarva-saṁśaya-nāśanam — destroyer of all doubts, iti — thus, āpṛṣṭaḥ — asked, mahīpālaḥ — the king, prāha — said, tam — to him, muni-puṅgavam — sage.
"O king, tell me this, the destroyer of all doubts," thus asked, the king said to the sage.
शृणु ब्रह्मन्‌ प्रवक्ष्यामि रहस्यं परमं त्विदम्‌ ।
अज्ञानात्‌ संसृतिरियं प्रवृत्ताऽनादिकालतः ॥ २४ ॥
śṛṇu brahman pravakṣyāmi rahasyam paramam tv idam ।
ajñānāt saṁsṛtir iyaṁ pravṛttā anādi-kālataḥ ॥ 24 ॥

śṛṇu — listen, brahman — O sage, pravakṣyāmi — I will tell, rahasyam — secret, paramam — supreme, tu — indeed, idam — this, ajñānāt — from ignorance, saṁsṛtiḥ — transmigration, iyam — this, pravṛttā — has arisen, anādi-kālataḥ — from beginningless time.
Listen, O sage, I will tell you this supreme secret. From ignorance, this transmigration has arisen from beginningless time.
सुखःदुखावभासानां प्रवाहात्मतया स्थिता ।
स्वप्नवत्‌ सन्तता सर्वैः सर्वदा ह्यनुभूयते ॥ २५ ॥
sukha-duḥkha-avabhāsānāṁ pravāha-ātmatayā sthitā ।
svapna-vat santatā sarvaiḥ sarvadā hi anubhūyate ॥ 25 ॥

sukha-duḥkha-avabhāsānām — of appearances of pleasure and pain, pravāha-ātmatayā — by the nature of flow, sthitā — established, svapna-vat — like a dream, santatā — continuity, sarvaiḥ — by all, sarvadā — always, hi — indeed, anubhūyate — is experienced.
The appearances of pleasure and pain are established by the nature of flow, like a dream, continuously experienced by all, always.
निवृत्तिस्तस्य तु ज्ञानादेवेति प्रविभावितम्‌ ।
तज्ज्ञानं संविकल्पं स्यादज्ञानस्य प्रबाधनम्‌ ॥ २६ ॥
nivṛttiḥ tasya tu jñānāt eva iti pravibhāvitaṁ ।
tat jñānaṁ savikalpaṁ syād ajñānasya prabādhanam ॥ 26 ॥

nivṛttiḥ — cessation, tasya — of that, tu — indeed, jñānāt — from knowledge, eva — alone, iti — thus, pravibhāvitaṁ — is understood, tat — that, jñānam — knowledge, savikalpam — conceptual, syāt — may be, ajñānasya — of ignorance, prabādhanam — removal.
The cessation of that is understood to be from knowledge alone. That knowledge may be conceptual, which removes ignorance.
निर्विकल्पकविज्ञानादज्ञानं न निवर्तते ।
निर्विकल्पकविज्ञानं केनचिन्न विरुद्ध्यते ॥ २७ ॥
nirvikalpaka-vijñānāt ajñānaṁ na nivartate ।
nirvikalpaka-vijñānaṁ kenacit na virudhyate ॥ 27 ॥

nirvikalpaka-vijñānāt — from non-conceptual knowledge, ajñānam — ignorance, na — not, nivartate — is removed, nirvikalpaka-vijñānam — non-conceptual knowledge, kenacit — by anyone, na — not, virudhyate — opposed.
Ignorance is not removed by non-conceptual knowledge alone. Non-conceptual knowledge is not opposed by anyone.
निर्विकल्पकविज्ञानं सविकल्पसमाश्रयम्‌ ।
विचित्रचित्राभासानां भित्तिवत्‌ सुव्यवस्थितम्‌ ॥ २८ ॥
nirvikalpaka-vijñānam savikalpa-samāśrayam ।
vicitra-citrābhāsānām bhittivat suvyavasthitam ॥ 28 ॥

nirvikalpaka-vijñānam — non-conceptual knowledge, savikalpa-samāśrayam — supported by conceptual, vicitra-citrābhāsānām — of varied appearances, bhittivat — like a wall, suvyavasthitam — well-established.
Together, non-conceptual knowledge, supported by conceptual, is well-established like a wall for varied appearances.
निर्विकल्पं ज्ञानमिति केवलं ज्ञानमुच्यते ।
तत्रैव हि विकल्पानामुल्लेखात्‌ सविकल्पकम्‌ ॥ २९ ॥
nirvikalpam jñānam iti kevalam jñānam ucyate ।
tatra eva hi vikalpānām ullekhāt savikalpakam ॥ 29 ॥

nirvikalpam — non-conceptual, jñānam — knowledge, iti — thus, kevalam — alone, jñānam — knowledge, ucyate — is called, tatra — there, eva — indeed, hi — surely, vikalpānām — of concepts, ullekhāt — due to mentioning, savikalpakam — conceptual.
Non-conceptual knowledge alone is called knowledge. Indeed, due to the mentioning of concepts, it becomes conceptual.
अज्ञानं सविकल्पाख्यज्ञानमेव न चेतरत्‌ ।
तदनेकविधं कार्यकारणात्मतया स्थितम्‌ ॥ ३० ॥
ajñānam savikalpa-ākhyam jñānam eva na cet arat ।
tat aneka-vidham kārya-kāraṇātmatayā sthitam ॥ 30 ॥

ajñānam — ignorance, savikalpa-ākhyam — known as conceptual, jñānam — knowledge, eva — indeed, na — not, cet — if, arat — otherwise, tat — that, aneka-vidham — of various kinds, kārya-kāraṇa-ātmatayā — as cause and effect, sthitam — established.
Ignorance, known as conceptual knowledge, is indeed not otherwise. That is established as various kinds of cause and effect.
कारणं स्वात्मपूर्णत्वाख्यातिरूपमुदीरितम्‌ ।
चिदात्मा पूर्ण एव स्यादवच्छेदविवर्जनात्‌ ॥ ३१ ॥
kāraṇaṁ sva-ātma-pūrṇatva-ākhyāti-rūpam udīritam ।
cid-ātmā pūrṇa eva syāt avaccheda-vivarjanāt ॥ 31 ॥

kāraṇam — cause, sva-ātma-pūrṇatva-ākhyāti-rūpam — known as the fullness of one's own self, udīritam — declared, cid-ātmā — conscious self, pūrṇa — complete, eva — indeed, syāt — may be, avaccheda-vivarjanāt — due to the absence of limitation.
The cause is declared to be known as the fullness of one's own self. The conscious self may indeed be complete due to the absence of limitation.
अवच्छेदनहेतूनां कलादीनां हि साधकः ।
तथाविधात्मनः ख्यातिरपूर्णत्वेन या स्थिता ॥ ३२ ॥
avaccheda-nahetūnāṁ kalādīnāṁ hi sādhakaḥ ।
tathāvidha-ātmanaḥ khyātir apūrṇatvena yā sthitā ॥ 32 ॥

avaccheda-nahetūnāṁ — of the absence of limitation, kalādīnāṁ — of parts and so forth, hi — indeed, sādhakaḥ — adept, tathāvidha-ātmanaḥ — of such a self, khyātir — knowledge, apūrṇatvena — as incompleteness, yā — which, sthitā — is established.
The adept is indeed of the absence of limitation of parts and so forth. The knowledge of such a self is established as incompleteness.
अत्राधुनाऽस्मीतिरूपा मूलाज्ञानं हि सा भवेत्‌ ।
तस्यैव पल्लवप्रायं देहात्मत्वादिभासनम्‌ ॥ ३३ ॥
atra adhunā asmi-iti-rūpā mūla-ajñānaṁ hi sā bhavet ।
tasyāḥ eva pallava-prāyaṁ deha-ātmatva-ādi-bhāsanam ॥ 33 ॥

atra — here, adhunā — now, asmi-iti-rūpā — in the form of 'I am', mūla-ajñānam — root ignorance, hi — indeed, sā — that, bhavet — may be, tasyāḥ — of that, eva — indeed, pallava-prāyaṁ — in the form of a sprout, deha-ātmatva-ādi-bhāsanam — appearance of body-self and so forth.
Here now, in the form of 'I am', that root ignorance may indeed be. The appearance of body-self and so forth is in the form of a sprout of that.
अज्ञानस्य निवृत्त्यन्तं संसारो न निवर्तते ।
पूर्णात्मविज्ञानमृते त्वज्ञानं न निवर्तते ॥ ३४ ॥
ajñānasya nivṛtti-antaṁ saṁsāraḥ na nivartate ।
pūrṇa-ātma-vijñāna-mṛte tu ajñānaṁ na nivartate ॥ 34 ॥

ajñānasya — of ignorance, nivṛtti-antam — cessation, saṁsāraḥ — transmigration, na — not, nivartate — ceases, pūrṇa-ātma-vijñāna-mṛte — without complete self-knowledge, tu — indeed, ajñānam — ignorance, na — not, nivartate — ceases.
The cessation of ignorance does not lead to the end of transmigration. Indeed, ignorance does not cease without complete self-knowledge.
तच्च पूर्णात्मविज्ञानं द्विविधं सुव्यवस्थितम्‌ ।
परोक्षमपरोक्षं च परोक्षं गुरुशास्त्रतः ॥ ३५ ॥
tat ca pūrṇa-ātma-vijñānaṁ dvividham suvyavasthitam ।
parokṣam aparokṣaṁ ca parokṣaṁ guru-śāstrataḥ ॥ 35 ॥

tat — that, ca — and, pūrṇa-ātma-vijñānaṁ — complete self-knowledge, dvividham — of two kinds, suvyavasthitam — well-established, parokṣam — indirect, aparokṣam — direct, ca — and, parokṣam — indirect, guru-śāstrataḥ — from teacher and scripture.
That complete self-knowledge is well-established as of two kinds: indirect and direct. The indirect comes from teacher and scripture.
तत्‌ साक्षात्‌ पुरुषार्थस्य न कारणमिति स्थितम्‌ ।
यादृशं ते भवेज्ज्ञानं शास्त्रश्रुतिसमुद्भवम्‌ ॥ ३६ ॥
tat sākṣāt puruṣārthasya na kāraṇam iti sthitam ।
yādṛśaṁ te bhavet jñānam śāstra-śruti-samudbhavam ॥ 36 ॥

tat — that, sākṣāt — directly, puruṣārthasya — of human goals, na — not, kāraṇam — cause, iti — thus, sthitam — established, yādṛśam — as, te — your, bhavet — may be, jñānam — knowledge, śāstra-śruti-samudbhavam — arising from scripture and hearing.
It is established that direct knowledge is not the cause of human goals. Your knowledge may be as arising from scripture and hearing.
श्रद्धामात्राभ्युपगतं फलदं न प्रचक्षते ।
अपरोक्षं हि विज्ञानं समाधिपरिपाकजम्‌ ॥ ३७ ॥
śraddhā-mātra-abhyupagatam phaladam na pracakṣate ।
aparokṣam hi vijñānam samādhi-paripākajam ॥ 37 ॥

śraddhā-mātra-abhyupagatam — obtained merely by faith, phaladam — yielding fruit, na — not, pracakṣate — is said, aparokṣam — direct, hi — indeed, vijñānam — knowledge, samādhi-paripākajam — arising from the maturation of absorption.
Knowledge obtained merely by faith is not said to yield fruit. Direct knowledge indeed arises from the maturation of absorption.
सप्रपञ्चाज्ञाननाराक्षमं शुभफलावहम् ।
समाधिर्ज्ञानपूर्वस्तु विज्ञानं जनयेत्‌ खलु ॥ ३८ ॥
sa-prapañca-ajñāna-nārākṣamam śubha-phalāvaham ।
samādhiḥ jñāna-pūrvah tu vijñānam janayet khalu ॥ 38 ॥

sa-prapañca-ajñāna-nārākṣamam — not obstructed by ignorance with elaboration, śubha-phalāvaham — yielding auspicious fruit, samādhiḥ — absorption, jñāna-pūrvah — preceded by knowledge, tu — indeed, vijñānam — knowledge, janayet — produces, khalu — certainly.
Absorption, not obstructed by ignorance with elaboration, certainly yields auspicious fruit. Absorption preceded by knowledge indeed produces knowledge.
तस्मादज्ञानिनां नार्थ: समाधौ सम्भवत्यपि ।
यथाऽविदितमाणिक्यः पश्यन्‌ कोशगृहे मणिम्‌ ॥ ३९ ॥
tasmāt ajñānināṁ na arthaḥ samādhau sambhavati api ।
yathā aviditam āṇikyaḥ paśyan kośa-gṛhe maṇim ॥ 39 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, ajñāninām — of the ignorant, na arthaḥ — no benefit, samādhau — in absorption, sambhavati — arises, api — also, yathā — as, aviditam — unknown, āṇikyaḥ — ruby, paśyan — seeing, kośa-gṛhe — in a box, maṇim — gem.
Therefore, no benefit arises in absorption for the ignorant, just as seeing an unknown ruby in a box.
न जानाति यथाऽन्यस्तु श्रुतज्ञातमणिः क्वचित्‌ ।
दृष्ट्वा प्रत्यभिजानाति तत्परो मणिमञ्जसा ॥ ४० ॥
na jānāti yathā anyas tu śruta-jñāta-maṇiḥ kvacit ।
dṛṣṭvā pratyabhijānāti tat-paraḥ maṇim añjasā ॥ 40 ॥

na jānāti — does not know, yathā — as, anyas — another, tu — but, śruta-jñāta-maṇiḥ — a gem known by hearing, kvacit — somewhere, dṛṣṭvā — having seen, pratyabhijānāti — recognizes, tat-paraḥ — devoted to that, maṇim — gem, añjasā — immediately.
Just as another person, having seen a gem known by hearing somewhere, immediately recognizes it.
अतत्परः श्रुतमपि भूयः पश्यन्‌ मणिं क्वचित्‌ ।
न विजानाति तदिह ब्रह्मन्‌ सुनिपुणोऽपि सन्‌ ॥ ४१ ॥
atatparaḥ śrutam api bhūyaḥ paśyan maṇiṁ kvacit ।
na vijānāti tad iha brahman sunipuṇo api san ॥ 41 ॥

atatparaḥ — not devoted, śrutam — heard, api — even, bhūyaḥ — again, paśyan — seeing, maṇim — gem, kvacit — somewhere, na — not, vijānāti — knows, tad — that, iha — here, brahman — O sage, sunipuṇo api san — even if very skilled.
Even if one is very skilled, if not devoted, one may see a gem somewhere again and again without recognizing it, O sage.
तथा मूढा न विन्दन्ति फलं विज्ञानसंश्रयम्‌ ।
अज्ञातत्वात्‌ पण्डितास्तु श्रुतज्ञानयुता अपि ॥ ४२ ॥
tathā mūḍhā na vindanti phalaṁ vijñāna-saṁśrayam ।
ajñātatvāt paṇḍitās tu śruta-jñāna-yutā api ॥ 42 ॥

tathā — similarly, mūḍhāḥ — deluded ones, na vindanti — do not find, phalam — fruit, vijñāna-saṁśrayam — based on knowledge, ajñātatvāt — due to ignorance, paṇḍitāḥ tu — but the learned, śruta-jñāna-yutāḥ api — even if endowed with heard knowledge.
Similarly, deluded ones do not find the fruit based on knowledge. Even the learned, if ignorant, do not recognize it.
अतत्परत्वहेतोस्तु न विजानन्ति सर्वथा ।
यथा हि तारकां पश्यन्नपि जानाति न क्वचित्‌ ॥ ४३ ॥
atatparatva-hetos tu na vijānanti sarvathā ।
yathā hi tārakāṁ paśyan api jānāti na kvacit ॥ 43 ॥

atatparatva-hetos tu — due to the reason of not being devoted, na vijānanti — do not know, sarvathā — at all, yathā hi — just as, tārakām — star, paśyan — seeing, api — even, jānāti — knows, na — not, kvacit — anywhere.
Due to not being devoted, they do not recognize at all, just as one does not recognize a star even when seeing it.
मूढः श्रुतज्ञानहीनः श्रुतज्ञानयुतोऽपि वै ।
पश्यन्नपि च नो वेत्ति तत्परत्वविवर्जनात्‌ ॥ ४४ ॥
mūḍhaḥ śruta-jñāna-hīnaḥ śruta-jñāna-yuto api vai ।
paśyan api ca no vetti tatparatva-vivarjanāt ॥ 44 ॥

mūḍhaḥ — deluded, śruta-jñāna-hīnaḥ — devoid of heard knowledge, śruta-jñāna-yutaḥ api — even if endowed with heard knowledge, vai — indeed, paśyan api — even if seeing, ca — and, na — not, vetti — knows, tatparatva-vivarjanāt — due to the absence of devotion.
The deluded, devoid of heard knowledge, even if endowed with it, indeed, do not recognize even if they see, due to the absence of devotion.
यस्तु श्रुत्वा शुक्रतारां दिगाकारादिलक्षणैः ।
मया ज्ञेयं सर्वथेति तत्परो बुद्धिमान्‌ नरः ॥ ४५ ॥
yaḥ tu śrutvā śukratārāṁ dig-ākāra-ādi-lakṣaṇaiḥ ।
mayā jñeyaṁ sarvathā iti tatparaḥ buddhimān naraḥ ॥ 45 ॥

yaḥ tu — one who, śrutvā — having heard, śukratārām — Venus star, dig-ākāra-ādi-lakṣaṇaiḥ — by the characteristics of direction and form, mayā — by me, jñeyam — to be known, sarvathā — in every way, iti — thus, tatparaḥ — devoted to that, buddhimān naraḥ — wise man.
One who, having heard about the Venus star by the characteristics of direction and form, determines that it should be known by them in every way, is a wise man devoted to that.
एकाग्रमानसः पश्यन्‌ प्रत्यभिज्ञास्यति स्फुटम्‌ ।
एवमज्ञानतो मूढाश्चान्ये तात्पर्यवर्जनात्‌ ॥ ४६ ॥
ekāgra-mānasaḥ paśyan pratyabhijñāsyati sphuṭam ।
evam ajñānato mūḍhāḥ ca anye tatparya-varjanāt ॥ 46 ॥

ekāgra-mānasaḥ — with a focused mind, paśyan — seeing, pratyabhijñāsyati — will recognize, sphuṭam — clearly, evam — thus, ajñānataḥ — due to ignorance, mūḍhāḥ — deluded ones, ca — and, anye — others, tatparya-varjanāt — due to the lack of devotion.
With a focused mind, one will recognize it clearly. Thus, due to ignorance and lack of devotion, the deluded ones do not recognize it.
न विजानन्ति स्वात्मानं ब्रह्मन्‌ सत्सु समाधिषु ।
भिक्षामटति दुर्दैवाद्‌ यथा वै विस्मृताकरः ॥ ४७ ॥
na vijānanti sva-ātmānaṁ brahman satsu samādhiṣu ।
bhikṣām aṭati durdaivāt yathā vai vismṛta-ākaraḥ ॥ 47 ॥

na vijānanti — do not recognize, sva-ātmānam — their own self, brahman — O sage, satsu — in the presence, samādhiṣu — of absorptions, bhikṣām — alms, aṭati — wanders, durdaivāt — due to bad luck, yathā — just as, vai — indeed, vismṛta-ākaraḥ — one who has forgotten his treasure.
They do not recognize their own self in the presence of absorptions, O sage, wandering for alms due to bad luck, just as one who has forgotten his treasure.
तस्मादेता दशाः सर्वाः समाधीनां निरर्थर्थिकाः ।
अत एव शिशूनां हि सर्वदा निर्विकल्पकम्‌ ॥ ४८ ॥
tasmād etā daśāḥ sarvāḥ samādhīnām nirartharthikāḥ ।
ata eva śiśūnām hi sarvadā nirvikalpakaṁ ॥ 48 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, etāḥ — these, daśāḥ — states, sarvāḥ — all, samādhīnām — of absorptions, nirartharthikāḥ — purposeless, ataḥ — therefore, eva — indeed, śiśūnām — of children, hi — indeed, sarvadā — always, nirvikalpakaṁ — non-conceptual.
Therefore, all these states of absorptions are purposeless. Indeed, for children, the non-conceptual state is always present.
न फलं साधयेद्‌ ब्रह्मन्‌ अज्ञानस्यानिवृत्तितः ।
प्रत्यभिज्ञात्मकं यत्तु ज्ञानं स्यात्‌ सविकल्पकम्‌ ॥ ४९ ॥
na phalaṁ sādhayet brahman ajñānasya anivṛttitaḥ ।
pratyabhijñātmakaṁ yat tu jñānaṁ syāt savikalpakam ॥ 49 ॥

na phalam — no fruit, sādhayet — yields, brahman — O sage, ajñānasya — of ignorance, anivṛttitaḥ — from the non-removal, pratyabhijñātmakaṁ — based on recognition, yat — which, tu — indeed, jñānam — knowledge, syāt — may be, savikalpakam — conceptual.
No fruit is yielded from the non-removal of ignorance, O sage. Knowledge, which is based on recognition, may be conceptual.
तदेव संसारमूलमज्ञानं विनिवर्तयेत्‌ ।
अनेकजन्मसु कृतैः सन्तुष्टा स्वात्मदेवता ॥ ५० ॥
tad eva saṁsāra-mūlam ajñānam vinivartayet ।
aneka-janmasu kṛtaiḥ santuṣṭā sva-ātma-devatā ॥ 50 ॥

tat — that, eva — indeed, saṁsāra-mūlam — root of transmigration, ajñānam — ignorance, vinivartayet — removes, aneka-janmasu — in many births, kṛtaiḥ — by acts, santuṣṭā — pleased, sva-ātma-devatā — self-deity.
That indeed removes the ignorance, the root of transmigration. Pleased by acts in many births, the self-deity becomes satisfied.
यदा तदा मुमुक्षुत्वं नान्यदा कल्पकोटिभिः ।
चेतनत्वं जन्मवत्सु परमं दुर्लभं भवेत्‌ ॥ ५१ ॥
yadā tadā mumukṣutvaṁ na anyadā kalpa-koṭibhiḥ ।
cetanatvaṁ janmavatsu paramaṁ durlabhaṁ bhavet ॥ 51 ॥

yadā — when, tadā — then, mumukṣutvaṁ — desire for liberation, na anyadā — not otherwise, kalpa-koṭibhiḥ — in millions of ages, cetanatvaṁ — awareness, janmavatsu — in births, paramam — supreme, durlabham — rare, bhavet — may be.
Then the desire for liberation arises, it does not arise otherwise, even in millions of ages. Awareness in births is supremely rare.
सुदुर्लभं तेष्वपि च मानुषं जन्म सर्वथा ।
तत्रापि सूक्ष्मबुद्धित्वमत्यन्तं हि सुदुर्लभम्‌ ॥ ५२ ॥
sudurlabhaṁ teṣu api ca mānuṣaṁ janma sarvathā ।
tatra api sūkṣma-buddhitvam atyantaṁ hi sudurlabham ॥ 52 ॥

sudurlabham — very rare, teṣu api — among them, ca — and, mānuṣaṁ janma — human birth, sarvathā — in every way, tatra api — even there, sūkṣma-buddhitvam — subtle intellect, atyantam — extremely, hi — indeed, sudurlabham — very rare.
Very rare among them, indeed, is human birth in every way. Even there, subtle intellect is extremely rare.
पश्य ब्रह्मन्‌ स्थावराणां शतांशेनापि सम्मितम्‌ ।
न दृश्यते जङ्गमं वै तेषामपि शतांशतः ॥ ५३ ॥
paśya brahman sthāvarāṇāṁ śatāṁśena api sammitam ।
na dṛśyate jaṅgamaṁ vai teṣām api śatāṁśataḥ ॥ 53 ॥

paśya — see, brahman — O sage, sthāvarāṇām — among the immobile, śatāṁśena api — even a hundredth part, sammitam — considered, na dṛśyate — is not seen, jaṅgamaṁ — mobile beings, vai — indeed, teṣām api — among them, śatāṁśataḥ — a hundredth part.
See, O sage, among the immobile beings, even a hundredth part is considered. Indeed, among them, the mobile beings are not seen as even a hundredth part.
समं नास्ति मनुष्यत्वं तत्रापि परिभावय ।
पशुतुल्याः प्रदृश्यन्ते मनुष्याणां हि कोटयः ॥ ५४ ॥
samaṁ na asti manuṣyatvaṁ tatra api paribhāvaya ।
paśu-tulyāḥ pradṛśyante manuṣyāṇāṁ hi koṭayaḥ ॥ 54 ॥

samaṁ — equal, na asti — there is not, manuṣyatvaṁ — humanity, tatra api — even there, paribhāvaya — consider, paśu-tulyāḥ — like animals, pradṛśyante — are seen, manuṣyāṇām — among humans, hi — indeed, koṭayaḥ — millions.
There is no equal humanity, even there, consider. Millions of humans are seen like animals.
ये न जानन्ति सदसत्‌ पुण्यं वा पापमेव वा ।
अन्येऽपि कोटिशो मर्त्याः प्रवृत्ताः कामनापराः ॥ ५५ ॥
ye na jānanti sad-asat puṇyaṁ vā pāpam eva vā ।
anye api koṭiśo martyāḥ pravṛttāḥ kāmanā-parāḥ ॥ 55 ॥

ye — those who, na jānanti — do not know, sat-asat — good and bad, puṇyam vā — virtue or, pāpam eva vā — or sin, anye api — others also, koṭiśaḥ — by millions, martyāḥ — mortals, pravṛttāḥ — engaged, kāmanā-parāḥ — engrossed in desires.
Those who do not know good and bad, virtue or sin, others also, millions of mortals, are engaged and engrossed in desires.
गतागतं रोचयन्ते पाण्डित्याभासगर्विताः ।
एवंविधजनानां तु केऽप्यन्ये बुद्धिमद्विधाः ॥ ५६ ॥
gatāgamaṁ rocayante pāṇḍitya-ābhāsa-garvitāḥ ।
evaṁvidha-janānāṁ tu ke api anye buddhimat-vidhāḥ ॥ 56 ॥

gatāgamaṁ — coming and going, rocayante — delight in, pāṇḍitya-ābhāsa-garvitāḥ — proud of the semblance of wisdom, evaṁvidha-janānām — among such people, tu — but, ke api — some, anye — others, buddhimat-vidhāḥ — wise ones.
Delighting in the coming and going, proud of the semblance of wisdom, among such people, but some are wise ones.
मालिन्यशेषचित्तास्तेऽप्यद्वैतपदनास्तिकाः ।
भगवन्माययाच्छन्नमद्वैतं परमं पदम्‌ ॥ ५७ ॥
mālīnyaśeṣa-cittāḥ te api advaita-pada-nāstikāḥ ।
bhagavan-māyayā ācchannam advaitam paramaṁ padam ॥ 57 ॥

mālīnyaśeṣa-cittāḥ — with minds full of impurity, te api — they also, advaita-pada-nāstikāḥ — disbelievers in the non-dual state, bhagavan-māyayā — by the divine illusion, ācchannam — covered, advaitam — non-dual, paramam padam — supreme state.
With minds full of impurity, they also are disbelievers in the non-dual state. Covered by the divine illusion, they do not perceive the non-dual supreme state.
कथं सर्वैः समासाद्यं मायान्धैर्मन्दभाग्यकैः ।
मायान्धानां तत्पदं तु न बुद्धि मुपरोहति ॥ ५८ ॥
kathaṁ sarvaiḥ samāsādyaṁ māyā-andhaiḥ manda-bhāgyakaiḥ ।
māyā-andhānāṁ tat-padaṁ tu na buddhiṁ uparohati ॥ 58 ॥
