kathaṁ — how, sarvaiḥ — by all, samāsādyaṁ — to be attained, māyā-andhaiḥ — by those blinded by illusion, manda-bhāgyakaiḥ — by the unfortunate, māyā-andhānāṁ — of those blinded by illusion, tat-padam — that state, tu — indeed, na — not, buddhiṁ — intellect, uparohati — ascends.
How can that state be attained by all, by those blinded by illusion, by the unfortunate? Indeed, the intellect of those blinded by illusion does not ascend to that state.
अन्ये दुर्भागधेयास्ते बुद्ध्यारूढमपीह ये ।
वृथाभिनिविशा भूयोऽपह्नुवन्ति कुकल्पनैः ॥ ५९ ॥
anye durbhāga-dheyāḥ te buddhi-ārūḍham api iha ye ।
vṛthā-abhiniviśā bhūyaḥ apahnu-vanti ku-kalpanaiḥ ॥ 59 ॥

anye — others, durbhāga-dheyāḥ — with bad fortune, te — they, buddhi-ārūḍham api — even if intellectually advanced, iha — here, ye — who, vṛthā-abhiniviśāḥ — with false notions, bhūyaḥ — again, apahnu-vanti — deny, ku-kalpanaiḥ — by wrong imaginations.
Others, with bad fortune, even if intellectually advanced, here, who with false notions, again are denied by wrong imaginations.
अहो भगवती माया पश्यन्तोऽपि महत्पदम्‌ ।
चिन्तामणिं हस्तगतं त्यजन्ति हि कुकल्पनैः ॥ ६० ॥
aho bhagavatī māyā paśyantaḥ api mahat-padam ।
cintāmaṇiṁ hasta-gatam tyajanti hi ku-kalpanaiḥ ॥ 60 ॥

aho — alas, bhagavatī — divine, māyā — illusion, paśyantaḥ api — even seeing, mahat-padam — great state, cintāmaṇim — wish-fulfilling gem, hasta-gatam — in hand, tyajanti — abandon, hi — indeed, ku-kalpanaiḥ — by wrong imaginations.
Alas, the divine illusion, even seeing the great state, the wish-fulfilling gem in hand, they abandon indeed by wrong imaginations.
येषां समाराधनेन तुष्टा सा स्वात्मदेवता ।
ते मायया विनिर्मुक्ताः सुतर्काः श्रद्धया युताः ॥ ६१ ॥
yeṣāṁ samārādhanena tuṣṭā sā svātma-devatā ।
te māyayā vinirmuktāḥ sutarkāḥ śraddhayā yutāḥ ॥ 61 ॥

yeṣāṁ — whose, samārādhanena — by the worship, tuṣṭā — pleased, sā — she, svātma-devatā — self-deity, te — they, māyayā — by illusion, vinirmuktāḥ — liberated, sutarkāḥ — with good reasoning, śraddhayā — with faith, yutāḥ — endowed.
Those whose self-deity is pleased by worship, they are liberated from illusion, endowed with good reasoning and faith.
पराद्वये समाश्वस्ताः प्राप्नुवन्ति परं पदम्‌ ।
तत्क्रमं तेऽभिधास्यामि ब्रह्मन्‌ संशृणु संयतः ॥ ६२ ॥
parādvaye samāśvastāḥ prāpnuvanti paraṁ padam ।
tatkramaṁ te’bhidhāsyāmi brahman saṁśṛṇu saṁyataḥ ॥ 62 ॥

parādvaye — in non-duality, samāśvastāḥ — established, prāpnuvanti — attain, paraṁ padam — the supreme state, tatkramam — the sequence, te — to you, abhidhāsyāmi — I will explain, brahman — O sage, saṁśṛṇu — listen, saṁyataḥ — attentively.
Established in non-duality, they attain the supreme state. I will explain the sequence to you, O sage, listen attentively.
अनन्तजन्मसुकृतैर्देवताभक्तिराप्यते ।
तया संराध्य सुचिरं तत्प्रसादात्ततः परम्‌ ॥ ६३ ॥
ananta-janma-sukṛtaiḥ devatā-bhaktiḥ āpyate ।
tayā saṁrādhya suciraṁ tat-prasādāt tataḥ param ॥ 63 ॥

ananta-janma-sukṛtaiḥ — by the merits of countless births, devatā-bhaktiḥ — devotion to the deity, āpyate — is obtained, tayā — by that, saṁrādhya — worshipping, suciram — for a long time, tat-prasādāt — by that grace, tataḥ param — thereafter.
Devotion to the deity is obtained by the merits of countless births. Worshipping for a long time, by that grace, thereafter.
वैरस्यं भोगवृन्देषु तत्परत्वं च प्राप्नुयात्‌ ।
वैराग्यतत्परत्वाभ्यां श्रद्धया चापि सङ्गतः ॥ ६४ ॥
vairasyaṁ bhoga-vṛndeṣu tat-paratvaṁ ca prāpnuyāt ।
vairāgya-tat-paratvābhyāṁ śraddhayā ca api saṁgataḥ ॥ 64 ॥

vairasyam — disinterest, bhoga-vṛndeṣu — in the objects of enjoyment, tat-paratvam — devotion to that, ca — and, prāpnuyāt — attains, vairāgya-tat-paratvābhyām — through dispassion and devotion, śraddhayā — with faith, ca — and, api — also, saṁgataḥ — associated.
Attains disinterest in the objects of enjoyment and devotion to that, through dispassion and devotion, and associated with faith.
सद्गुरु प्राप्य तत्प्रोक्त्या वेत्त्यद्वैतं परं पदम्‌ ।
एतज्ज्ञानं परोक्षं वै ह्यस्त्यद्वैतमितीह यत्‌ ॥ ६५ ॥
sadguru prāpya tat-proktyā vetty-advaitaṁ paraṁ padam ।
etad-jñānaṁ parokṣaṁ vai hy-asty-advaitam itīha yat ॥ 65 ॥

sadguru — true guru, prāpya — having attained, tat-proktyā — by his instruction, vetti — knows, advaitam — non-duality, paraṁ padam — supreme state, etad-jñānam — this knowledge, parokṣam — indirect, vai — indeed, hi — certainly, asti-advaitam — non-duality exists, iti — thus, iha — here, yat — which.
Having attained the true guru, by his instruction, one knows non-duality, the supreme state. This knowledge is indeed indirect, for non-duality exists thus here.
ततो विचारयेत्‌ सम्यगद्वैतं स्वात्मदैवतम्‌ ।
उपपाद्य सुतर्कैस्तु संशयांस्तेन नाशयेत्‌ ॥ ६६ ॥
tato vicārayet samyag advaitaṁ svātma-daivatam ।
upapādya sutarkaiḥ tu saṁśayān tena nāśayet ॥ 66 ॥

tataḥ — then, vicārayet — contemplate, samyak — properly, advaitam — non-duality, svātma-daivatam — self-deity, upapādya — by establishing, sutarkaiḥ — with sound reasoning, tu — and, saṁśayān — doubts, tena — by that, nāśayet — dispels.
Then, properly contemplate non-duality, the self-deity, by establishing with sound reasoning and dispelling doubts.
अथ निश्चितमात्माख्यतत्त्वमद्वयमादरात्‌ ।
अनुध्यायेदाऽपरोक्षं हठवृत्त्यापि यत्नतः ॥ ६७ ॥
atha niścitam ātma-ākhya-tattvam-advayam-ādarāt ।
anudhyāyet aparokṣaṁ haṭha-vṛttyā api yatnataḥ ॥ 67 ॥

atha — then, niścitam — firmly established, ātma-ākhya — called the self, tattvam — principle, advayam — non-dual, ādarāt — with respect, anudhyāyet — meditate, aparokṣam — directly, haṭha-vṛttyā — with determination, api — also, yatnataḥ — with effort.
Then, having firmly established the principle of the self, non-dual, with respect, meditate directly with determination and effort.
ततो विकल्पविषयीकृत्य ध्यातं परं पदम्‌ ।
संसारमूलमज्ञानं नाशयेन्नात्र संशयः ॥ ६८ ॥
tato vikalpa-viṣayīkṛtya dhyātaṁ paraṁ padam ।
saṁsāra-mūlam-ajñānaṁ nāśayet na atra saṁśayaḥ ॥ 68 ॥

tataḥ — then, vikalpa-viṣayīkṛtya — making the object of meditation, dhyātam — meditated, paraṁ padam — supreme state, saṁsāra-mūlam — the root of transmigration, ajñānam — ignorance, nāśayet — destroys, na atra — no, saṁśayaḥ — doubt.
Then, making the supreme state the object of meditation, destroys ignorance, the root of transmigration, no doubt about it.
पक्वध्याने निर्विकल्पे समाध्याख्ये परं पदम्‌ ।
आसाद्य पश्चात्‌ संस्मृत्य प्रत्यभिज्ञानवान्‌ भवेत्‌ ॥ ६९ ॥
pakva-dhyāne nirvikalpe samādhyākhye paraṁ padam ।
āsādya paścāt saṁsmṛtya pratyabhijñānavān bhavet ॥ 69 ॥

pakva-dhyāne — in mature meditation, nirvikalpe — in non-dual, samādhyākhye — called samadhi, paraṁ padam — supreme state, āsādya — having attained, paścāt — then, saṁsmṛtya — recalling, pratyabhijñānavān — with recognition, bhavet — becomes.
In mature meditation, in non-dual samadhi, called the supreme state, having attained, then recalling, becomes recognizing.
सोऽद्वैतात्माऽहमस्मीति त्वपरोक्षविकल्पतः ।
संसारमूलमज्ञानं साङ्गं नाशयति द्रुतम्‌ ॥ ७० ॥
so advaitātmā aham asmi iti tu aparokṣa-vikalpataḥ ।
saṁsāra-mūlam ajñānaṁ sāṅgaṁ nāśayati drutam ॥ 70 ॥

saḥ — he, advaita-ātmā — non-dual self, aham — I, asmi — am, iti — thus, tu — but, aparokṣa-vikalpataḥ — by direct thought, saṁsāra-mūlam — the root of transmigration, ajñānam — ignorance, sāṅgaṁ — with parts, nāśayati — destroys, drutam — quickly.
He, the non-dual self, thinking "I am," directly destroys the root of transmigration, ignorance, with parts, quickly.
ध्यानस्य परिपाको हि विकल्पपरिवर्जनम्‌ ।
विकल्पो विविधख्यातिरेकधा निर्विकल्पकः ॥ ७१ ॥
dhyānasya paripāko hi vikalpa-parivarjanam ।
vikalpaḥ vividha-khyātiḥ ekadhā nirvikalpakaḥ ॥ 71 ॥

dhyānasya — of meditation, paripākaḥ — maturity, hi — indeed, vikalpa-parivarjanam — renunciation of thoughts, vikalpaḥ — thought, vividha-khyātiḥ — various perceptions, ekadhā — one way, nirvikalpakaḥ — non-dual.
The maturity of meditation is indeed the renunciation of thoughts; thought is various perceptions, but in one way, non-dual.
अन्यानुल्लेखमात्रेण विकल्पो वर्जितो भवेत्‌ ।
विकल्पे वर्जिते पश्चान्निर्विकल्पं स्वतः स्थितम्‌ ॥ ७२ ॥
anyā-anullekha-mātreṇa vikalpaḥ varjito bhavet ।
vikalpe varjite paścāt nirvikalpaṁ svataḥ sthitam ॥ 72 ॥

anyā-anullekha-mātreṇa — by not even mentioning others, vikalpaḥ — thought, varjitaḥ bhavet — is renounced, vikalpe — when thought, varjite — is renounced, paścāt — thereafter, nirvikalpaṁ — non-dual, svataḥ — naturally, sthitam — established.
By not even mentioning others, thought is renounced; when thought is renounced, thereafter non-dual is naturally established.
चित्रे विमृष्टे यद्वत्तु शुद्धा भित्तिर्हि संस्थिता ।
सम्पादनं शुद्धभित्तेश्चित्रसम्मार्ष्टिरेव हि ॥ ७३ ॥
citre vimṛṣṭe yadvat tu śuddhā bhittiḥ hi saṁsthitā ।
sampādanaṁ śuddha-bhitteḥ citra-sammārṣṭiḥ eva hi ॥ 73 ॥

citre — in the painting, vimṛṣṭe — when cleansed, yadvat — as, tu — but, śuddhā bhittiḥ — pure wall, hi — indeed, saṁsthitā — remains, sampādanaṁ — the making, śuddha-bhitteḥ — of the pure wall, citra-sammārṣṭiḥ — cleaning the painting, eva hi — indeed.
As in the painting, when cleansed, the pure wall remains, indeed the making of the pure wall is cleaning the painting, indeed.
एवं विकल्पस्यापोहे निर्विकल्पं मनः स्वतः ।
निर्विकल्पात्मसम्पत्तिर्विकल्पत्याग एव हि ॥ ७४ ॥
evaṁ vikalpasya apohena nirvikalpaṁ manaḥ svataḥ ।
nirvikalpa-ātma-sampattiḥ vikalpa-tyāga eva hi ॥ 74 ॥

evaṁ — thus, vikalpasya — of thought, apohena — by removal, nirvikalpaṁ — non-dual, manaḥ — mind, svataḥ — naturally, nirvikalpa-ātma-sampattiḥ — non-dual self attainment, vikalpa-tyāgaḥ — renunciation of thought, eva hi — indeed.
Thus, by the removal of thought, the mind is naturally non-dual; non-dual self-attainment is indeed the renunciation of thought.
नातोऽधिकं किञ्चिदस्ति पदं प्राप्यं हि पावनम्‌ ।
अत्र मुह्यन्ति विबुधा अपि मायामहित्वतः ॥ ७५ ॥
na ataḥ adhikaṁ kiñcit asti padaṁ prāpyaṁ hi pāvanam ।
atra muhyanti vibudhāḥ api māyā-mahitvataḥ ॥ 75 ॥

na — not, ataḥ — than this, adhikaṁ — higher, kiñcit — anything, asti — is, padaṁ — state, prāpyaṁ — to be attained, hi — indeed, pāvanam — pure, atra — here, muhyanti — are deluded, vibudhāḥ — wise ones, api — also, māyā-mahitvataḥ — by the power of illusion.
There is no higher state to be attained than this pure state; even wise ones are deluded here by the power of illusion.
सुबुद्धानां क्षणेनैव पदमेतद्धि लक्षितम्‌ ।
त्रिधाऽधिकारिणो ब्रह्मन्‌ उत्तमाधममध्यमाः ॥ ७६ ॥
su-buddhānāṁ kṣaṇena eva padam etad hi lakṣitam ।
tridhā-adhikāriṇaḥ brahman uttama-adhama-madhyamāḥ ॥ 76 ॥

su-buddhānāṁ — of the wise, kṣaṇena — in a moment, eva — indeed, padam — state, etat — this, hi — indeed, lakṣitam — perceived, tridhā-adhikāriṇaḥ — three types of qualified ones, brahman — O sage, uttama — highest, adhama — lowest, madhyamāḥ — middle.
The wise perceive this state in a moment, indeed; O sage, there are three types of qualified ones: highest, lowest, and middle.
उत्तमाः सकृदादेशकाले बुद्ध्यन्ति तत्पदम्‌ ।
विचारो ध्यानमपि च श्रुतिकालसमं भवेत्‌ ॥ ७७ ॥
uttamāḥ sakṛt-ādiśa-kāle budhyanti tat-padam ।
vicāraḥ dhyānam api ca śruti-kāla-samam bhavet ॥ 77 ॥

uttamāḥ — the highest, sakṛt-ādiśa-kāle — at the first instruction, budhyanti — understand, tat-padam — that state, vicāraḥ — contemplation, dhyānam — meditation, api — also, ca — and, śruti-kāla-samam — at the same time as hearing, bhavet — it happens.
The highest understand that state at the first instruction; contemplation and meditation also happen at the same time as hearing.
उत्तमानां नहि क्लेशः प्राप्तौ तस्य पदस्य हि ।
अहं पुरा निदाघस्य रात्रौ ज्योत्स्नासुमण्डिते ॥ ७८ ॥
uttamānāṁ nahi kleśaḥ prāptau tasya padasya hi ।
ahaṁ purā nidāghasya rātrau jyotsnā-su-maṇḍite ॥ 78 ॥

uttamānāṁ — for the highest, nahi — indeed not, kleśaḥ — effort, prāptau — in attaining, tasya padasya — that state, hi — indeed, ahaṁ — I, purā — once, nidāghasya — in the summer, rātrau — at night, jyotsnā-su-maṇḍite — adorned with moonlight.
For the highest, indeed, there is no effort in attaining that state; once, in the summer night adorned with moonlight.
प्रियया सम्परिष्वक्तो विकसद्वाटिकाङ्गणे ।
पराद्धर्यशयनासीनो मदिरामदघूर्णितः ॥ ७९ ॥
priyāyāṁ sampariṣvaktaḥ vikasad-vāṭikā-aṅgaṇe ।
parāddharya-śayanā-asīnaḥ madirā-mada-ghūrṇitaḥ ॥ 79 ॥
priyāyām — by the beloved, sampariṣvaktaḥ — embraced, vikasad-vāṭikā-aṅgaṇe — in a blooming garden, parāddharya-śayana — luxurious bed, āsīnaḥ — seated, madirā-mada-ghūrṇitaḥ — intoxicated by wine.
Embraced by the beloved, seated in a blooming garden on a luxurious bed, intoxicated by wine.
अश्रौषं खे सिद्धगणवचनं मधुपेशलम्‌ ।
अद्वैततत्त्वाश्रितं वै तत्काले ह्यविदं पदम्‌ ॥ ८० ॥
aśrauṣaṁ khe siddha-gaṇa-vacanaṁ madhu-peśalam ।
advaita-tattva-āśritaṁ vai tat-kāle hi avindaṁ padam ॥ 80 ॥

aśrauṣam — I heard, khe — in the sky, siddha-gaṇa-vacanam — the words of a group of siddhas, madhu-peśalam — sweet as honey, advaita-tattva-āśritam — referring to the principle of non-duality, vai — indeed, tat-kāle — at that time, hi — certainly, avindam — realized, padam — the state.
I heard in the sky the sweet words of a group of siddhas, referring to the principle of non-duality, and realized that state at that time.
विज्ञातं तद्विचारेण ध्यानेनापि तदैव हि ।
एवमर्धमुहूर्तेन ज्ञात्वा तत्पावनं पदम्‌ ॥ ८१ ॥
vijñātaṁ tad-vicāreṇa dhyānena api tadaiva hi ।
evam ardha-muhūrtena jñātvā tat pāvanaṁ padam ॥ 81 ॥

vijñātaṁ — realized, tad — that, vicāreṇa — through contemplation, dhyānena — through meditation, api — also, tadaiva — at that very moment, hi — indeed, evam — thus, ardha-muhūrtena — in half a moment, jñātvā — having realized, tat — that, pāvanaṁ — pure, padam — state.
Realized through contemplation and meditation at that very moment; thus, in half a moment, having realized that pure state.
मुहूर्तमभवं भूयस्तत्समाहितमानसः ।
परमानन्दवाराशिपरिमग्नो ह्यशेषतः ॥ ८२ ॥
muhūrtam abhavaṁ bhūyas tat samāhita-mānasaḥ ।
paramānanda-vārāśi-parimagnaḥ hi aśeṣataḥ ॥ 82 ॥

muhūrtam — for a moment, abhavam — I became, bhūyas — more, tat — that, samāhita-mānasaḥ — with a concentrated mind, paramānanda — supreme bliss, vārāśi — ocean, parimagnaḥ — immersed, hi — indeed, aśeṣataḥ — completely.
For a moment, I became more with a concentrated mind, completely immersed in the ocean of supreme bliss.
अथ स्मृतिं समासाद्य विचारपरमोऽभवम्‌ ।
अहोऽद्भुतपदं ह्येतदानन्दामृतनिर्भरम्‌ ॥ ८३ ॥
atha smṛtiṁ samāsādya vicāra-paramaḥ abhavam ।
aho adbhuta-padaṁ hi etad ānanda-amṛta-nirbharam ॥ 83 ॥

atha — then, smṛtim — memory, samāsādya — having attained, vicāra-paramaḥ — engrossed in contemplation, abhavam — I became, aho — oh, adbhuta-padam — wonderful state, hi — indeed, etad — this, ānanda-amṛta-nirbharam — filled with bliss and nectar.
Then, having attained memory, I became engrossed in contemplation; oh, this wonderful state is indeed filled with bliss and nectar.
अपूर्वमासादितं मे भूयस्तत्‌ संविशाम्यहम्‌ ।
नैतस्य लेशमात्रं स्यादैन्द्रदिसुखमप्यलम्‌ ॥ ८४ ॥
apūrvam āsāditaṁ me bhūyas tat saṁviśāmi aham ।
na etasya leśa-mātraṁ syād aindra-di-sukham api alam ॥ 84 ॥

apūrvam — unprecedented, āsāditam — attained, me — by me, bhūyas — again, tat — that, saṁviśāmi — I enter, aham — I, na — not, etasya — of this, leśa-mātram — even a fraction, syāt — would be, aindra-di-sukham — the happiness of Indra and others, api — even, alam — sufficient.
Having attained this unprecedented state again, I enter it; not even a fraction of the happiness of Indra and others would be sufficient in that state.
आब्रह्म सुखमेतस्य लेशतोऽपि न सम्मितम्‌ ।
अद्यावधि व्यर्थ एष कालो मे ह्यतिवाहितः ॥ ८५ ॥
ābrahma sukham etasya leśataḥ api na sammitam ।
adya-avadhi vyartha eṣa kālo me hi atīvhitaḥ ॥ 85 ॥

ābrahma — up to Brahma, sukham — happiness, etasya — of this, leśataḥ — even in a fraction, api — even, na — not, sammitam — comparable, adya-avadhi — until today, vyarthaḥ — wasted, eṣaḥ — this, kālaḥ — time, me — by me, hi — indeed, atīvhitaḥ — passed.
The happiness of this state, even in a fraction, is not comparable up to Brahma; until today, indeed, I have wasted this time.
अविदित्वा स्वं निधानं चिन्तामणिगणान्वितम्‌ ।
यथा भिक्षामटति वै मुष्टिपिष्टप्रलिप्सया ॥ ८६ ॥
aviditvā svaṁ nidhānaṁ cintāmaṇi-gaṇa-anvitam ।
yathā bhikṣām aṭati vai muṣṭi-piṣṭa-pralipsayā ॥ 86 ॥

aviditvā — without knowing, svaṁ — own, nidhānam — treasure, cintāmaṇi-gaṇa-anvitam — adorned with wish-fulfilling gems, yathā — as, bhikṣām — alms, aṭati — wanders, vai — indeed, muṣṭi-piṣṭa-pralipsayā — seeking flour in a fist.
Without knowing one's own treasure adorned with wish-fulfilling gems, one wanders for alms, indeed, seeking flour in a fist.
अहो लोकास्तथा स्वात्मानन्दाज्ञानविमोहिताः ।
बाह्यं सुखं लेशमात्रं प्राप्नुवन्ति महाश्रमैः ॥ ८७ ॥
aho lokāḥ tathā sva-ātma-ānanda-ajñāna-vimohitāḥ ।
bāhyaṁ sukhaṁ leśa-mātraṁ prāpnuvanti mahā-śramaiḥ ॥ 87 ॥

aho — alas, lokāḥ — people, tathā — thus, sva-ātma-ānanda — own self-bliss, ajñāna — ignorance, vimohitāḥ — deluded, bāhyaṁ — external, sukham — happiness, leśa-mātram — a fraction, prāpnuvanti — attain, mahā-śramaiḥ — with great effort.
Alas, people, deluded by ignorance of their own self-bliss, attain external happiness, only a fraction, with great effort.
तदलं मे वृथा बाह्यसुखलेशपरिश्रमात्‌ ।
अनन्तानन्दसन्दोहतत्परः स्यां हि सर्वदा ॥ ८८॥
tad alam me vṛthā bāhya-sukha-leśa-pariśramāt ।
ananta-ānanda-sandoha-tat-paraḥ syām hi sarvadā ॥ 88 ॥

tad — that, alam — enough, me — for me, vṛthā — in vain, bāhya-sukha-leśa-pariśramāt — from efforts for external happiness, ananta-ānanda-sandoha — infinite bliss, tat-paraḥ — devoted to that, syām — I would be, hi — indeed, sarvadā — always.
Enough of this vain effort for external happiness; I would indeed always be devoted to the infinite bliss.
अलमेतेन बाह्येन व्यवहारेण मे किमु ।
पिष्टपेषणकल्पेन चोपालम्भपदेन वै ॥ ८९ ॥
alam etena bāhyena vyavahāreṇa me kimu ।
piṣṭa-peṣaṇa-kalpena ca upālambha-padena vai ॥ 89 ॥

alam — enough, etena — with this, bāhyena — external, vyavahāreṇa — activity, me — for me, kimu — what, piṣṭa-peṣaṇa-kalpena — like grinding flour, ca — and, upālambha-padena — with reproof, vai — indeed.
Enough of this external activity for me; like grinding flour and reproof, indeed.
तानि भोज्यानि तान्येव माल्यानि शयनानि च ।
भूषणानि विचित्राणि योषित्सम्भोगकाश्च ते ॥ ९० ॥
tāni bhojyāni tāni eva mālyāni śayanāni ca ।
bhūṣaṇāni vicitrāṇi yoṣit-sambhoga-kāśca te ॥ 90 ॥

tāni — those, bhojyāni — foods, tāni eva — those indeed, mālyāni — garlands, śayanāni ca — and beds, bhūṣaṇāni — ornaments, vicitrāṇi — varied, yoṣit-sambhoga-kāḥ — pleasures with women, ca — and, te — they.
Those foods, those indeed, garlands, and beds, varied ornaments, and pleasures with women.
चिरपर्युषितप्रायाण्यपि संसेव्यते पुनः ।
गतानुगतिकत्वान्मे जुगुप्सा नहि जायते ॥ ९१ ॥
cira-paryuṣita-prāyāṇi api saṁsevyate punaḥ ।
gatānugatikatvāt me jugupsā na hi jāyate ॥ 91 ॥

cira-paryuṣita-prāyāṇi — mostly long stale, api — even, saṁsevyate — are enjoyed, punaḥ — again, gatānugatikatvāt — by following others, me — my, jugupsā — disgust, na hi — not indeed, jāyate — arises.
Mostly long stale, yet enjoyed again, following others, my disgust indeed does not arise.
इति निश्चित्य भूयोऽहं यावदन्तर्मुखोद्यतः ।
तावदन्यो विमर्शो मां सुशुभः प्रत्युपस्थितः ॥ ९२ ॥
iti niścitya bhūyaḥ aham yāvat antarmukha-udyataḥ ।
tāvat anyaḥ vimarśaḥ māṁ suśubhaḥ pratyupasthitaḥ ॥ 92 ॥

iti — thus, niścitya — deciding, bhūyaḥ — again, aham — I, yāvat — as much as, antarmukha-udyataḥ — turned inward, tāvat — then, anyaḥ — another, vimarśaḥ — contemplation, māṁ — me, suśubhaḥ — auspicious, pratyupasthitaḥ — approached.
Thus deciding, as much as I turned inward again, then another auspicious contemplation approached me.
अहो मे चित्तमोहोऽयं किं मामेवमुपस्थितः ।
आनन्दपरिपूर्णात्मा स एवाहं स्थितोऽपि सन्‌ ॥ ९३ ॥
aho me citta-mohaḥ ayaṁ kiṁ mām evam upasthitaḥ ।
ānanda-paripūrṇa-ātmā sa eva aham sthitaḥ api san ॥ 93 ॥

aho — oh, me — my, citta-mohaḥ — delusion of mind, ayaṁ — this, kiṁ — why, mām — to me, evam — thus, upasthitaḥ — approached, ānanda-paripūrṇa-ātmā — blissfully complete self, saḥ — he, eva — indeed, aham — I, sthitaḥ — established, api — even, san — being.
Oh, this delusion of mind, why has it approached me? Even being blissfully complete self, I am indeed always established.
भूयः किं कर्तुमिच्छामि प्राप्तव्यं वाऽपि किं मया ।
किमप्राप्तं मया कुत्र कदा वा प्राप्यते कथम्‌ ॥ ९४ ॥
bhūyaḥ kiṁ kartum icchāmi prāptavyaṁ vā api kiṁ mayā ।
kim aprāptaṁ mayā kutra kadā vā prāpyate katham ॥ 94 ॥

bhūyaḥ — again, kiṁ — what, kartum — to do, icchāmi — I wish, prāptavyam — to be obtained, vā api — or also, kiṁ — what, mayā — by me, kim — what, aprāptam — not obtained, mayā — by me, kutra — where, kadā — when, vā — or, prāpyate — is attained, katham — how.
What do I wish to do again? What is there to be obtained by me? What have I not obtained, where, when, or how is it attained?
अप्राप्तस्यापि सम्प्राप्तिः कथं सत्या हि सम्भवेत्‌ ।
अहोऽनन्तचिदानन्दरूपे मे स्यात्‌ कथं क्रिया ॥ ९५ ॥
aprāptasya api samprāptiḥ kathaṁ satyā hi saṁbhavet ।
aho ananta-cid-ānanda-rūpe me syāt kathaṁ kriyā ॥ 95 ॥

aprāptasya — of the unachieved, api — also, samprāptiḥ — achievement, kathaṁ — how, satyā — true, hi — indeed, saṁbhavet — could be, aho — oh, ananta — infinite, cid — consciousness, ānanda — bliss, rūpe — in the form, me — of me, syāt — could be, kathaṁ — how, kriyā — action.
How could the achievement of the unachieved be true? Oh, how could there be action in my form of infinite consciousness and bliss?
देहेन्द्रियान्तःकरणान्यपि स्वाप्नसमानि वै ।
ममैव तानि सर्वाणि त्वखण्डैकचिदात्मनः ॥ ९६ ॥
deha-indriya-antaḥ-karaṇāni api svāpna-samāni vai ।
mamaiʾva tāni sarvāṇi tv akhaṇḍa-eka-cid-ātmanaḥ ॥ 96 ॥

deha — body, indriya — senses, antaḥ-karaṇāni — inner faculties, api — even, svāpna-samāni — like a dream, vai — indeed, mama — my, eva — only, tāni — they, sarvāṇi — all, tu — indeed, akhaṇḍa — indivisible, eka — one, cid-ātmanaḥ — consciousness-self.
The body, senses, and inner faculties are indeed like a dream; all these are indeed mine, of the indivisible one consciousness-self.
तत्रैकमन्तःकरणं निरुद्धयापि च किं भवेत्‌ ।
अन्यान्यप्यनिरुद्धानि मनांसि च ममैव हि ॥ ९७ ॥
tatra ekam antaḥ-karaṇaṁ niruddhyā api ca kiṁ bhavet ।
anyāni api aniruddhāni manāṁsi ca mamaiva hi ॥ 97 ॥

tatra — there, ekam — one, antaḥ-karaṇam — inner faculty, niruddhyā — by restraining, api — even, ca — and, kiṁ bhavet — what would be, anyāni — others, api — even, aniruddhāni — unrestrained, manāṁsi — minds, ca — and, mama — my, eva — indeed, hi — indeed.
What would happen if one inner faculty is restrained? Even if others are unrestrained, they are indeed my minds.
तथा चैकस्य मनसो निरोधे मम किं भवेत्‌ ।
निरुद्धान्यनिरुद्धानि मनांसि मयि भान्त्यलम्‌ ॥ ९८ ॥
tathā ca ekasya manasaḥ nirodhe mama kiṁ bhavet ।
niruddhāni aniruddhāni manāṁsi mayi bhānti alam ॥ 98 ॥

tathā — thus, ca — and, ekasya — of one, manasaḥ — mind, nirodhe — in restraint, mama — of me, kiṁ bhavet — what would happen, niruddhāni — restrained, aniruddhāni — unrestrained, manāṁsi — minds, mayi — in me, bhānti — shine, alam — completely.
Thus, if one mind is restrained, what would happen to me? Restrained and unrestrained minds completely shine in me.
निरोधे सर्वमनसामपि मे न निरोधनम्‌ ।
महाकाशात्‌ सुवितते कुतो मयि निरोधनम्‌ ॥ ९९ ॥
nirodhe sarva-manasām api me na nirodhanam ।
mahākāśāt suvitate kuto mayi nirodhanam ॥ 99 ॥

nirodhe — in the restraint, sarva-manasaām — of all minds, api — even, me — my, na — not, nirodhanam — restraint, mahākāśāt — from vast space, suvitate — extensive, kuto — where, mayi — in me, nirodhanam — restraint.
In the restraint of all minds, there is no restraint for me; from the vast and extensive space, where is the restraint in me?
एवं पुर्णानन्दरूपे समाधिः स्यात्‌ कथं मयि ।
चिदानन्दप्रपूर्णस्य पूर्णस्य गगनादपि ॥ १०० ॥
evaṁ pūrṇa-ānanda-rūpe samādhiḥ syāt kathaṁ mayi ।
cid-ānanda-pūrṇasya pūrṇasya gaganād api ॥ 100 ॥

evaṁ — thus, pūrṇa-ānanda-rūpe — in the form of complete bliss, samādhiḥ — absorption, syāt — could be, kathaṁ — how, mayi — in me, cid-ānanda-pūrṇasya — filled with consciousness-bliss, pūrṇasya — complete, gaganāt api — even than the sky.
Thus, how could absorption (samadhi) be in me, filled with complete consciousness-bliss, more complete than the sky?
मम क्रिया कथं का स्याद्ययापि स्तः शुभाशुभे ।
अनन्तेषु शरीरात्माभासेषु मन्महित्वतः ॥ १०१ ॥
mama kriyā kathaṁ kā syād yayā api staḥ śubhāśubhe ।
ananteṣu śarīra-ātma-ābhāseṣu man-mahitvataḥ ॥ 101 ॥

mama — my, kriyā — action, kathaṁ — how, kā — what, syād — could be, yayā — by which, api — even, staḥ — are, śubhāśubhe — good and bad, ananteṣu — in infinite, śarīra-ātma-ābhāseṣu — body-self appearances, man-mahitvataḥ — due to my greatness.
How could there be any action for me, by which good and bad even exist, in the infinite body-self appearances due to my greatness?
क्रियाभासावभासेन तदभावेन वाऽपि किम्‌ ।
कर्तव्यं वाऽप्यकर्तव्यं मम नास्त्यपि लेशतः ॥ १०२ ॥
kriyā-ābhāsa-ābhāsena tad-abhāvena vā api kim ।
kartavyaṁ vā api akartavyaṁ mama na asti api leśataḥ ॥ 102 ॥

kriyā-ābhāsa-ābhāsena — by the appearance of action, tad-abhāvena — by the absence of that, vā api — or even, kim — what, kartavyam — to be done, vā api — or also, akartavyam — not to be done, mama — mine, na asti — there is not, api — even, leśataḥ — in the least.
What is to be done or not to be done by the appearance or absence of action? There is not even the least to be done or not to be done by me.
तस्मान्निरोधने किं स्यादहमानन्दनिर्भरः ।
समाधावसमाधौ वा सत्यपूर्णस्वभावकः ॥ १०३ ॥
tasmāt nirodhane kiṁ syād aham-ānanda-nirbharaḥ ।
samādhau asamādhau vā satya-pūrṇa-svabhāvakaḥ ॥ 103 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, nirodhane — in restraint, kiṁ syād — what would be, aham — I, ānanda-nirbharaḥ — full of bliss, samādhau — in absorption, asamādhau vā — or not in absorption, satya-pūrṇa-svabhāvakaḥ — of true complete nature.
Therefore, what would be in restraint for me, full of bliss, whether in absorption or not, of true complete nature?
यस्यां क्रियायां देहोऽयं स्थितस्तत्रैव तिष्ठतु ।
इत्यहं सर्वथा स्वस्थः सुमहानन्दमन्दिरः ॥ १०४ ॥
yasyāṁ kriyāyāṁ dehaḥ ayaṁ sthitaḥ tatra eva tiṣṭhatu ।
iti aham sarvathā svasthaḥ su-mahānanda-mandiraḥ ॥ 104 ॥

yasyām — in which, kriyāyām — action, dehaḥ — body, ayaṁ — this, sthitaḥ — established, tatra eva — there itself, tiṣṭhatu — let it remain, iti — thus, aham — I, sarvathā — in every way, svasthaḥ — serene, su-mahānanda-mandiraḥ — abode of great bliss.
In whichever action this body is established, let it remain there itself; thus, I am serene in every way, an abode of great bliss.
अनस्तमितभारूपोऽहं सुपूर्णो निरञ्जनः ।
उत्तमाधिकृतस्यैवं स्थितिर्मे सम्प्रकीर्तिता ॥ १०५ ॥
anastamita-bhā-rūpaḥ aham supūrṇaḥ nirañjanaḥ ।
uttama-adhikṛtasya evaṁ sthitiḥ me samprakīrtitā ॥ 105 ॥

anastamita-bhā-rūpaḥ — of unending radiance form, aham — I, supūrṇaḥ — completely full, nirañjanaḥ — stainless, uttama-adhikṛtasya — of the highest state, evaṁ — thus, sthitiḥ — state, me — my, samprakīrtitā — declared.
Of unending radiance form, I am completely full and stainless; thus, this is my declared state of the highest.
अधमानामनेकैस्तु जन्मभिर्ज्ञानजं फलम्‌ ।
मध्यमानां तु क्रमतः श्रवणं च विचारणम्‌ ॥ १०६ ॥
adhamānām anekaiḥ tu janmabhiḥ jñāna-jam phalam ।
madhyamānām tu kramataḥ śravaṇaṁ ca vicāraṇam ॥ 106 ॥

adhamānām — of the inferior, anekaiḥ — many, tu — but, janmabhiḥ — births, jñāna-jam — born of knowledge, phalam — fruit, madhyamānām — of the middle, tu — but, kramataḥ — gradually, śravaṇam — hearing, ca — and, vicāraṇam — contemplation.
For the inferior, the fruit born of knowledge comes after many births; for the middle, it comes gradually through hearing and contemplation.
अनुध्यानं च भवति ततो ज्ञानं प्रजायते ।
विज्ञानफलसंयुक्तः समाधिर्दुर्लभो भवेत्‌ ॥ १०७ ॥
anudhyānaṁ ca bhavati tato jñānaṁ prajāyate ।
vijñāna-phala-saṁyuktaḥ samādhiḥ durlabhaḥ bhavet ॥ 107 ॥

anudhyānam — meditation, ca — and, bhavati — becomes, tataḥ — then, jñānam — knowledge, prajāyate — arises, vijñāna-phala-saṁyuktaḥ — joined with the fruit of realization, samādhiḥ — absorption, durlabhaḥ — rare, bhavet — becomes.
Meditation becomes, then knowledge arises; absorption joined with the fruit of realization becomes rare.
विज्ञानफलहीनेन किं समाधिशतेन वा ।
तस्माद्विज्ञानहीनैस्तैः फलं नास्ति समाधिभिः ॥ १०८ ॥
vijñāna-phala-hīnena kiṁ samādhi-śatena vā ।
tasmāt vijñāna-hīnaḥ taiḥ phalaṁ na asti samādhibhiḥ ॥ 108 ॥

vijñāna-phala-hīnena — without the fruit of realization, kiṁ — what, samādhi-śatena — with hundreds of absorptions, vā — or, tasmāt — therefore, vijñāna-hīnaḥ — devoid of realization, taiḥ — by them, phalaṁ — fruit, na asti — is not, samādhibhiḥ — by absorptions.
What is the use of hundreds of absorptions without the fruit of realization? Therefore, devoid of realization, there is no fruit by those absorptions.
लोकेऽपि गच्छन्‌ मार्गेषु निर्विकल्पप्रकाशितान्‌ ।
भावानविज्ञाय तेषामज्ञानं न निवर्तते ॥ १०९ ॥
loke api gacchan mārgeṣu nirvikalpa-prakāśitān ।
bhāvān avijñāya teṣām ajñānaṁ na nivartate ॥ 109 ॥

loke — in the world, api — even, gacchan — going, mārgeṣu — in the paths, nirvikalpa-prakāśitān — illuminated by non-dual awareness, bhāvān — objects, avijñāya — not knowing, teṣām — their, ajñānam — ignorance, na nivartate — does not end.
Even going in the world, in the paths illuminated by non-dual awareness, not knowing the objects, their ignorance does not end.
निर्विकल्पाख्यविज्ञानं ज्ञानमात्रं निजं वपुः ।
तत्‌ सर्वदा भासमानमप्यभातविधं ननु ॥ ११० ॥
nirvikalpa-ākhya-vijñānaṁ jñāna-mātraṁ nijaṁ vapuḥ ।
tat sarvadā bhāsamānam api abhāta-vidhaṁ nanu ॥ 110 ॥

nirvikalpa-ākhya-vijñānam — realization known as non-dual, jñāna-mātram — pure knowledge, nijaṁ vapuḥ — own form, tat — that, sarvadā — always, bhāsamānam — shining, api — even, abhāta-vidham — not perceived, nanu — indeed.
Realization known as non-dual, pure knowledge, own form, that always shines, indeed, even if not perceived.
विकल्पाच्छादनादेव विकल्पानां व्यपोहने ।
भासमानमेव भूयो भातकल्पमपूर्वतः ॥ १११ ॥
vikalpa-ācchādanāt eva vikalpānāṁ vyapohane ।
bhāsamānam eva bhūyaḥ bhāta-kalpam apūrva-taḥ ॥ 111 ॥

vikalpa-ācchādanāt — by the covering of conceptions, eva — indeed, vikalpānāṁ — of conceptions, vyapohane — in the removal, bhāsamānam — shining, eva — indeed, bhūyaḥ — more, bhāta-kalpam — appearing, apūrva-taḥ — unprecedented.
By the covering of conceptions, indeed, in the removal of conceptions, the shining appears more, unprecedentedly.
ज्ञानज्ञेयाविभेदेन त्वज्ञातं ज्ञातमुच्यते ।
एवमेष भवेदात्मविज्ञानक्रम उत्तमः ॥ ११२ ॥
jñāna-jñeya-avibhedena tu ajñātaṁ jñātam ucyate ।
evaṁ eṣa bhavet ātma-vijñāna-krama uttamaḥ ॥ 112 ॥

jñāna-jñeya-avibhedena — by the non-difference of knowledge and known, tu — but, ajñātaṁ — unknown, jñātam — known, ucyate — is said, evaṁ — thus, eṣa — this, bhavet — becomes, ātma-vijñāna-krama — the order of self-realization, uttamaḥ — highest.
By the non-difference of knowledge and the known, the unknown is said to be known; thus, this becomes the highest order of self-realization.
ब्रह्यन्नेवं श्रुतं भूयो विचार्य ज्ञातुमर्हसि ।
अथ विज्ञायात्मतत्त्वं कृतार्थस्त्वं भविष्यसि ॥ ११३ ॥
brahman evaṁ śrutaṁ bhūyaḥ vicārya jñātum arhasi ।
atha vijñāya ātma-tattvaṁ kṛtārthaḥ tvaṁ bhaviṣyasi ॥ 113 ॥

brahman — O Brahmin, evaṁ — thus, śrutam — heard, bhūyaḥ — again, vicārya — contemplating, jñātum arhasi — you should know, atha — then, vijñāya — knowing, ātma-tattvam — self-principle, kṛtārthaḥ — accomplished, tvaṁ — you, bhaviṣyasi — will become.
O Brahmin, thus heard, contemplating again, you should know; then, knowing the self-principle, you will become accomplished.
जनकेनैवमादिष्टस्त्वष्टावक्रो महामुनिः ।
पूजितस्त्वभ्यनुज्ञातो गत्वा स्वं स्थानमादरात्‌ ॥ ११४ ॥
janakena evam ādiṣṭaḥ aṣṭāvakraḥ mahāmuniḥ ।
pūjitaḥ tu abhyanujñātaḥ gatvā svaṁ sthānam ādarāt ॥ 114 ॥

janakena — by Janaka, evam — thus, ādiṣṭaḥ — instructed, aṣṭāvakraḥ — Aṣṭāvakra, mahāmuniḥ — great sage, pūjitaḥ — honored, tu — then, abhyanujñātaḥ — permitted, gatvā — going, svaṁ sthānam — own place, ādarāt — respectfully.
Thus instructed by Janaka, the great sage Aṣṭāvakra, honored and permitted, respectfully returned to his own place.
विचारानुध्यानपूर्वं विज्ञाय परमं पदम्‌ ।
विधूय सर्वसन्देहान्‌ जीवन्मुक्तोऽभवद्‌ द्रुतम्‌ ॥ ११५ ॥
vicāra-anudhāna-pūrvaṁ vijñāya paramaṁ padam ।
vidhūya sarva-sandehān jīvan-muktaḥ abhavat drutam ॥ 115 ॥

vicāra-anudhāna-pūrvaṁ — through contemplation and meditation, vijñāya — realizing, paramaṁ padam — supreme state, vidhūya — removing, sarva-sandehān — all doubts, jīvan-muktaḥ — liberated while living, abhavat — became, drutam — quickly.
Through contemplation and meditation, realizing the supreme state, removing all doubts, he quickly became liberated while living.

colophon.en: Thus ends the seventeenth chapter named "Ashtavakra" in the revered Knowledge Section of Tripura Rahasya.

lines.text: भार्गवैवं हि सा संविद्‌ वेद्यवन्ध्या निरूपिता ।
उपलब्धिदशास्तस्या बहुधा संश्रुता ननु ॥ १ ॥
bhārgavaivaṁ hi sā saṁvid vedyavandhyā nirūpitā ।
upalabdhidaśāstasyā bahudhā saṁśrutā nanu ॥ 1 ॥

bhārgava — O Bhārgava, evaṁ — thus, hi — indeed, sā — that, saṁvid — consciousness, vedyavandhyā — without an object, nirūpitā — described, upalabdhi-daśā — states of realization, tasyāḥ — of that, bahudhā — in many ways, saṁśrutā — heard, nanu — indeed.
O Bhārgava, thus indeed that consciousness is described as objectless. The states of its realization are heard in many ways, indeed.
अव्युत्पत्त्या न जानन्ति जना मायाविमोहिताः ।
सा दशा भाव्यते सूक्ष्मदृशैव नान्यथा क्वचित्‌ ॥ २ ॥
avyutpattyā na jānanti janā māyā-vimohitāḥ ।
sā daśā bhāvyate sūkṣmadṛśā eva na anyathā kvacit ॥ 2 ॥

avyutpattyā — by lack of discernment, na jānanti — do not know, janā — people, māyā-vimohitāḥ — deluded by illusion, sā daśā — that state, bhāvyate — is realized, sūkṣma-dṛśā — by subtle vision, eva — indeed, na anyathā — not otherwise, kvacit — anywhere.
People deluded by illusion do not know due to lack of discernment. That state is realized by subtle vision, indeed, not otherwise, anywhere.
किं बहूक्तेन ते राम शृणु सारं ब्रवीम्यहम्‌ ।
मनसा वेद्यते वेद्यं मनसोऽतो न वेद्यता ॥ ३ ॥
kiṁ bahūktena te rāma śṛṇu sāraṁ bravīmyaham ।
manasā vedyate vedyaṁ manasaḥ ato na vedyatā ॥ 3 ॥

kiṁ bahūktena — what use is much talking, te — to you, rāma — O Rāma, śṛṇu — listen, sāraṁ — essence, bravīmi — I speak, aham — I, manasā — by mind, vedyate — is known, vedyaṁ — the object, manasaḥ — of the mind, ato — therefore, na vedyatā — not known.
What use is much talking to you, O Rāma? Listen, I speak the essence. The object is known by the mind; therefore, the mind is not known.
तथा च वेद्यनिर्मुक्तं मनोऽप्यस्तीति सम्भवेत्‌ ।
तन्मनो वेद्यनिर्मुक्ता वित्तिरित्यभिधीयते ॥ ४ ॥
tathā ca vedya-nirmuktaṁ mano api asti iti sambhavet ।
tan mano vedya-nirmuktā vittiḥ iti abhidhīyate ॥ 4 ॥

tathā — thus, ca — and, vedya-nirmuktaṁ — free from object, mano — mind, api — also, asti — is, iti — thus, sambhavet — it could be, tat — that, mano — mind, vedya-nirmuktā — free from object, vittiḥ — awareness, iti — thus, abhidhīyate — is called.
Thus, the mind also, free from objects, could be. That mind, free from objects, is called awareness.
उपलब्धिस्वरूपत्वाद्विदितैव हि सा सदा ।
अन्योपलब्ध्यपेक्षायामान्ध्यं स्यादनवस्थितेः ॥ ५ ॥
upalabdhi-svarūpatvāt viditā eva hi sā sadā ।
anya-upalabdhi-apekṣāyām āndhyaṁ syāt anavasthiteḥ ॥ 5 ॥

upalabdhi-svarūpatvāt — by the nature of realization, viditā — known, eva — indeed, hi — indeed, sā — that, sadā — always, anya-upalabdhi-apekṣāyām — in dependence on other realization, āndhyaṁ — blindness, syāt — would be, anavasthiteḥ — from instability.
By the nature of realization, that is always known indeed. Dependence on other realizations would be blindness from instability.
कञ्चिद्भावं हि संपश्यन्न भासि किमु भार्गव ।
न भासि चेन्न त्वमसि ततः प्रश्नस्तु ते कथम्‌ ॥ ६ ॥
kañcid bhāvaṁ hi saṁpaśyan na bhāsi kimu bhārgava ।
na bhāsi cet na tvam asi tataḥ praśnaḥ tu te katham ॥ 6 ॥

kañcid — any, bhāvaṁ — object, hi — indeed, saṁpaśyan — seeing, na bhāsi — do not shine, kimu — how, bhārgava — O Bhārgava, na bhāsi — do not shine, cet — if, na tvam asi — you are not, tataḥ — then, praśnaḥ — question, tu — indeed, te — your, katham — how.
O Bhārgava, how do you see any object, yet do not shine? If you do not shine, then how is your question?
अहो स्वयं खपुष्पात्मा सन्‌ कथं हितमिच्छसि ।
कथं तवात्मानमहं साधयामि विभावय ॥ ७ ॥
aho svayaṁ kha-puṣpa-ātmā san kathaṁ hitam icchasi ।
kathaṁ tava ātmānam aham sādhayāmi vibhāvaya ॥ 7 ॥

aho — oh, svayaṁ — yourself, kha-puṣpa-ātmā — like a sky-flower, san — being, kathaṁ — how, hitam — benefit, icchasi — you desire, kathaṁ — how, tava — your, ātmānam — self, aham — I, sādhayāmi — help, vibhāvaya — reflect.
Oh, being like a sky-flower, how do you desire benefit? How can I help your self? Reflect on this.
सामान्येन विभान्तं मां न जानामि विशेषतः ।
इति चेद्‌ राम सामान्यमेव ते रूपमव्ययम्‌ ॥ ८ ॥
sāmānyena vibhāntaṁ māṁ na jānāmi viśeṣataḥ ।
iti cet rāma sāmānyam eva te rūpam avyayam ॥ 8 ॥

sāmānyena — generally, vibhāntaṁ — shining, māṁ — me, na jānāmi — I do not know, viśeṣataḥ — specifically, iti — thus, cet — if, rāma — O Rāma, sāmānyam — general, eva — indeed, te — your, rūpam — form, avyayam — unchanging.
If you say you do not know me generally shining specifically, O Rāma, indeed your form is general and unchanging.
विशेषलेशरहितमेतावद्धयेव ते वपुः ।
अहो जानन्नपि पुनरलं मुह्यसि वै वृथा ॥ ९ ॥
viśeṣa-leśa-rahitam etāvat eva te vapuḥ ।
aho jānann api punar alaṁ muhyasi vai vṛthā ॥ 9 ॥

viśeṣa-leśa-rahitam — without a trace of specificity, etāvat — this much, eva — indeed, te — your, vapuḥ — form, aho — oh, jānann api — knowing even, punaḥ — again, alaṁ — very much, muhyasi — you are confused, vai — indeed, vṛthā — in vain.
Without a trace of specificity, this much indeed is your form. Oh, knowing even, you are very much confused again in vain.
भासकं सर्वमपि च विशेषविषयं भवेत्‌ ।
अतः सामान्यरूपस्त्वं विभासि स्वत एव हि ॥ १० ॥
bhāsakaṁ sarvam api ca viśeṣa-viṣayaṁ bhavet ।
ataḥ sāmānya-rūpaḥ tvaṁ vibhāsi svataḥ eva hi ॥ 10 ॥

bhāsakaṁ — illuminator, sarvam api — everything even, ca — and, viśeṣa-viṣayaṁ — specific object, bhavet — may be, ataḥ — therefore, sāmānya-rūpaḥ — general form, tvaṁ — you, vibhāsi — shine, svataḥ — by yourself, eva — indeed, hi — indeed.
The illuminator of everything even may be a specific object; therefore, by yourself, you shine as a general form, indeed.
शरीराद्यात्मना भासि चेच्छृणु प्रब्रवीमि ते ।
शरीरात्मतया भासि सङ्कल्पेनैव नान्यथा ॥ ११ ॥
śarīra-ādya-ātmanā bhāsi cet śṛṇu prabravīmi te ।
śarīra-ātmatayā bhāsi saṅkalpena eva na anyathā ॥ 11 ॥

śarīra-ādya-ātmanā — by body, etc., as self, bhāsi — you shine, cet — if, śṛṇu — listen, prabravīmi — I tell, te — to you, śarīra-ātmatayā — as the body-self, bhāsi — you shine, saṅkalpena — by conception, eva — indeed, na anyathā — not otherwise.
If you shine by body, etc., as self, listen, I tell you: you shine as the body-self by conception, indeed, not otherwise.
विभावय सूक्ष्मदृशा सङ्कल्पेऽन्यस्य देहतः ।
भाति किं तव देहत्वं देहस्तच्चापि ते भवेत्‌ ॥ १२ ॥
vibhāvaya sūkṣma-dṛśā saṅkalpe anyasya dehataḥ ।
bhāti kiṁ tava dehatvaṁ dehaḥ tat ca api te bhavet ॥ 12 ॥

vibhāvaya — consider, sūkṣma-dṛśā — with subtle vision, saṅkalpe — in the conception, anyasya — of another, dehataḥ — as body, bhāti — appears, kiṁ — whether, tava — your, dehatvam — bodiness, dehaḥ — body, tat — that, ca — and, api — also, te — your, bhavet — becomes.
Consider with subtle vision, in the conception of another as body, whether it appears as your bodiness; and that body also becomes yours.
एवं सङ्कल्प्यते यद्यच्छरीरं तत्तदेव हि ।
तेन सर्वमयस्त्वं स्याः कथं देहात्ममात्रकः ॥ १३ ॥
evaṁ saṅkalpyate yat yat śarīraṁ tat tat eva hi ।
tena sarvamayaḥ tvaṁ syāḥ kathaṁ deha-ātma-mātrakaḥ ॥ 13 ॥

evaṁ — thus, saṅkalpyate — is conceived, yat yat — whatever, śarīraṁ — body, tat tat — that indeed, eva — indeed, hi — indeed, tena — by that, sarvamayaḥ — all-pervading, tvaṁ — you, syāḥ — would be, kathaṁ — how, deha-ātma-mātrakaḥ — body-self only.
Thus, whatever body is conceived, that indeed becomes yours; by that, you would be all-pervading. How could you be only the body-self?
तस्माद्‌ दृश्यं तव वपुर्नहि स्याद्वयभिचारतः ।
तस्माद्‌ दृड्॰मात्ररूपोऽसि न दृग्‌ दृश्या कदाचन ॥ १४ ॥
tasmād dṛśyaṁ tava vapuḥ na hi syāt vayabhi-cārataḥ ।
tasmād dṛg-mātra-rūpaḥ asi na dṛk dṛśyā kadācana ॥ 14 ॥

tasmād — therefore, dṛśyaṁ — visible, tava — your, vapuḥ — form, na hi — indeed not, syāt — would be, vayabhi-cārataḥ — by variation, tasmād — therefore, dṛg-mātra-rūpaḥ — of the form of pure seeing, asi — you are, na dṛk — not the seer, dṛśyā — seen, kadācana — ever.
Therefore, your visible form would not be by variation. Therefore, you are of the form of pure seeing, not ever the seer or seen.
सा स्वप्रभा दृश्यरूपविशेषलेशवर्जिता ।
देहदेशकालभेदचित्रवैचित्र्यचित्रिता ॥ १५ ॥
sā svaprabhā dṛśya-rūpa-viśeṣa-leśa-varjitā ।
Deha-deśa-kāla-bheda-citra-vaicitrya-citritā ॥ 15 ॥

sā — that, svaprabhā — self-luminous, dṛśya-rūpa — seen form, viśeṣa-leśa — trace of distinction, varjitā — devoid, deha-deśa-kāla-bheda — body, place, time, difference, citra-vaicitrya-citritā — filled with manifold diversity.
That self-luminous form, devoid of any trace of distinction, is filled with manifold diversity of body, place, time, and differences.
तस्मात्‌ सङ्कल्पमात्रस्य वर्जनात्‌ परतः स्थितम्‌ ।
शेषं शुद्धचिते रूपं स्वात्मानमुपलक्षय ॥ १६ ॥
tasmāt saṅkalpa-mātrasya varjanāt parataḥ sthitam ।
śeṣaṁ śuddha-cite rūpaṁ svātmānam upalakṣaya ॥ 16 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, saṅkalpa-mātrasya — of conception alone, varjanāt — by abandoning, parataḥ — beyond, sthitam — situated, śeṣaṁ — remaining, śuddha-cite — in pure consciousness, rūpaṁ — form, svātmānam — own self, upalakṣaya — perceive.
Therefore, by abandoning conception alone, perceive the form of your own self, remaining beyond, situated in pure consciousness.
एवं सकृल्लक्षिते तु यत्‌ स्थितं तदलक्षणात्‌ ।
अज्ञानं सर्वसंसारकारणं तद्‌ विलीयते ॥ १७ ॥
evaṁ sakṛt lakṣite tu yat sthitam tat alakṣaṇāt ।
ajñānaṁ sarva-saṁsāra-kāraṇaṁ tad vilīyate ॥ 17 ॥

evaṁ — thus, sakṛt — once, lakṣite — perceived, tu — indeed, yat — that which, sthitam — situated, tat — that, alakṣaṇāt — without attribute, ajñānaṁ — ignorance, sarva-saṁsāra-kāraṇaṁ — cause of all transmigration, tad — that, vilīyate — dissolves.
Thus, once perceived, that which is situated without attribute, that ignorance, the cause of all transmigration, dissolves.
न मोक्षो नभसः पृष्ठे न पाताले न भूतले ।
सङ्कल्पवर्जनाच्छुद्धस्वरूपस्य प्रथैव सः ॥ १८ ॥
na mokṣo nabhasaḥ pṛṣṭhe na pātāle na bhūtale ।
saṅkalpa-varjanāt śuddha-svarūpasya prathaiva saḥ ॥ 18 ॥

na mokṣaḥ — not liberation, nabhasaḥ pṛṣṭhe — in the sky's back, na pātāle — not in the netherworld, na bhūtale — not on the earth, saṅkalpa-varjanāt — by abandoning conception, śuddha-svarūpasya — of the pure self, prathā — manifestation, eva — indeed, saḥ — that.
Liberation is not in the sky, netherworld, or on earth; it is indeed the manifestation of the pure self by abandoning conception.
स स्वरूपात्मकत्वात्तु नाप्राप्तः स्यात्‌ कदाचन ।
केवलं मोहमात्रस्य निरासेन कृतार्थता ॥ १९ ॥
sa svarūpa-ātmakatvāt tu na aprāptaḥ syāt kadācana ।
kevalaṁ moha-mātrasya nirāsena kṛtārthatā ॥ 19 ॥

saḥ — that, svarūpa-ātmakatvāt — by being the self-nature, tu — but, na aprāptaḥ — not unattained, syāt — would be, kadācana — ever, kevalaṁ — only, moha-mātrasya — of mere delusion, nirāsena — by removal, kṛtārthatā — fulfillment.
That is never unattained by being the self-nature; only by the removal of mere delusion is fulfillment.
अन्यो मोक्षो न सम्भाव्यः कृतकत्वाद्विनाश्यतः ।
स्वरूपादतिरिक्तश्चेच्छशशृङ्गसमो हि सः ॥ २० ॥
anyaḥ mokṣaḥ na sambhāvyaḥ kṛtakatvāt vināśyataḥ ।
svarūpāt atiriktaḥ cet śaśa-śṛṅga-samaḥ hi saḥ ॥ 20 ॥

anyaḥ — another, mokṣaḥ — liberation, na sambhāvyaḥ — not conceivable, kṛtakatvāt — due to being created, vināśyataḥ — perishable, svarūpāt — from the self-nature, atiriktaḥ — separate, cet — if, śaśa-śṛṅga-samaḥ — like a hare's horn, hi — indeed, saḥ — that.
Another liberation, separate from the self-nature, is not conceivable, as it would be perishable due to being created; indeed, it would be like a hare's horn.
स्वरूपं सर्वत: पूर्णमन्यो मोक्षः क्व सम्भवेत्‌ ।
स्वरूपे सम्भवन्‌ मोक्षो दर्पणप्रतिबिम्बवत्‌ ॥ २१ ॥
svarūpaṁ sarvataḥ pūrṇam anyo mokṣaḥ kva sambhavet ।
svarūpe sambhavan mokṣaḥ darpaṇa-pratibimba-vat ॥ 21 ॥

svarūpaṁ — own nature, sarvataḥ — completely, pūrṇam — full, anyaḥ — another, mokṣaḥ — liberation, kva — where, sambhavet — can happen, svarūpe — in own nature, sambhavan — arising, mokṣaḥ — liberation, darpaṇa-pratibimba-vat — like a reflection in a mirror.
The own nature being completely full, where can another liberation happen? Liberation arising in one's own nature is like a reflection in a mirror.
लोकेऽपि बन्धविगमादृते मोक्षो न भावितः ।
विगमोऽभाव एव स्यात्‌ सत्योऽभावात्मकः कथम्‌ ॥ २२ ॥
loke api bandha-vigamātṛte mokṣo na bhāvitaḥ ।
vigamaḥ abhāva eva syāt satyaḥ abhāva-ātmakaḥ katham ॥ 22 ॥

loke — in the world, api — even, bandha-vigama-ātṛte — without the disappearance of bondage, mokṣaḥ — liberation, na bhāvitaḥ — not conceived, vigamaḥ — disappearance, abhāva — non-existence, eva — indeed, syāt — would be, satyaḥ — real, abhāva-ātmakaḥ — of the nature of non-existence, katham — how.
Even in the world, liberation without the disappearance of bondage is not conceived. The disappearance would indeed be non-existence; how can the real be of the nature of non-existence?
भावाभावात्मकं वस्तु नहि सम्भवति क्वचित्‌ ।
तथा च स्वाप्नभावाश्च भावाभावोभयात्मकाः ॥ २३ ॥
bhāva-abhāva-ātmakaṁ vastu nahi sambhavati kvacit ।
tathā ca svāpna-bhāvāḥ ca bhāva-abhāva-ubhaya-ātmakāḥ ॥ 23 ॥

bhāva-abhāva-ātmakam — of the nature of existence and non-existence, vastu — entity, nahi — not, sambhavati — possible, kvacit — anywhere, tathā — thus, ca — and, svāpna-bhāvāḥ — dream states, ca — and, bhāva-abhāva-ubhaya-ātmakāḥ — of the nature of both existence and non-existence.
An entity of the nature of existence and non-existence is not possible anywhere. Thus, dream states are of the nature of both existence and non-existence.
सत्याः स्युर्बाधहेतोस्ते त्वसत्या इति चेच्छृणु ।
बाधोऽभावप्रत्ययः स्यात्‌ प्रत्ययाभावकालिकः ॥ २४ ॥
satyāḥ syuḥ bādha-hetuḥ te tu asatyāḥ iti cet śṛṇu ।
bādhaḥ abhāva-pratyayaḥ syāt pratyaya-abhāva-kālikaḥ ॥ 24 ॥

satyāḥ — real, syuḥ — would be, bādha-hetuḥ — cause of negation, te — they, tu — indeed, asatyāḥ — unreal, iti — thus, cet — if, śṛṇu — listen, bādhaḥ — negation, abhāva-pratyayaḥ — notion of non-existence, syāt — would be, pratyaya-abhāva-kālikaḥ — in the time of the notion's absence.
If they are real, the cause of negation would indeed make them unreal. Listen: negation is the notion of non-existence, which occurs in the absence of the notion.
यस्यैवं बाधयोगः स्यात्‌ सोऽसत्यो नहि चेतरः ।
अस्ति सर्वस्य दृश्यस्य बाधोऽप्रत्ययकालिकः ॥ २५ ॥
yasya evaṁ bādha-yogaḥ syāt saḥ asatyaḥ nahi ca itaraḥ ।
asti sarvasya dṛśyasya bādhaḥ apratyaya-kālikaḥ ॥ 25 ॥

yasya — whose, evam — thus, bādha-yogaḥ — association with negation, syāt — would be, saḥ — that, asatyaḥ — unreal, nahi — indeed not, ca — and, itaraḥ — otherwise, asti — exists, sarvasya — of all, dṛśyasya — of the visible, bādhaḥ — negation, apratyaya-kālikaḥ — in the absence of the notion.
That which is associated with negation is unreal, indeed not otherwise. Negation exists for all visible things in the absence of the notion.
तस्मादसत्यमेव स्याद्‌ भावाभावात्मना स्थितम्‌ ।
यस्याभावस्पर्शलेशः कदाचित्‌ कुत्रचिन्नहि ॥ २६ ॥
tasmāt asatyam eva syāt bhāva-abhāva-ātmanā sthitam ।
yasya abhāva-sparśa-leśaḥ kadācit kutracit na hi ॥ 26 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, asatyam — unreal, eva — indeed, syāt — would be, bhāva-abhāva-ātmanā — of the nature of existence and non-existence, sthitam — established, yasya — whose, abhāva-sparśa-leśaḥ — touch of non-existence, kadācit — at any time, kutracit — anywhere, na hi — indeed not.
Therefore, it would indeed be unreal, established as the nature of existence and non-existence, whose touch of non-existence is never anywhere.
एवंविधं तु चित्तत्त्वं सत्यं सर्वात्मना स्थितम्‌ ।
तस्माद्विभिन्नमोक्षस्तु न सत्यः स्यात्‌ कथञ्चन ॥ २७ ॥
evaṁ-vidham tu citta-tattvam satyam sarva-ātmanā sthitam ।
tasmāt vibhinna-mokṣaḥ tu na satyaḥ syāt kathañcana ॥ 27 ॥

evaṁ-vidham — thus, citta-tattvam — nature of consciousness, satyam — true, sarva-ātmanā — in all respects, sthitam — established, tasmāt — therefore, vibhinna-mokṣaḥ — separate liberation, tu — indeed, na — not, satyaḥ — true, syāt — would be, kathañcana — at all.
Thus, the nature of consciousness, true in all respects, is established. Therefore, separate liberation would not be true at all.
मोक्षः पूर्णस्वरूपस्य सकृत्‌ प्रथनमुच्यते ।
चेत्यवर्जनमात्रेण चितिः पूर्णा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ २८ ॥
mokṣaḥ pūrṇa-svarūpasya sakṛt prathanaṁ ucyate ।
cetya-varjanamātreṇa citiḥ pūrṇā prakīrtitā ॥ 28 ॥

mokṣaḥ — liberation, pūrṇa-svarūpasya — of the complete self, sakṛt — once, prathanaṁ — manifestation, ucyate — is said, cetya-varjanamātreṇa — by mere abandonment of objects, citiḥ — consciousness, pūrṇā — full, prakīrtitā — is proclaimed.
Liberation of the complete self is said to be its own manifestation. By mere abandonment of objects, consciousness is proclaimed as full.
चेत्याभासनमेवास्याश्चितेः सङ्कोचनं भवेत्‌ ।
चेत्याभाने चितिः पूर्णा परिच्छेदविवर्जनात्‌ ॥ २९ ॥
cetya-ābhāsanam eva asyaḥ citeḥ saṅkocanaṁ bhavet ।
cetya-ābhāne citiḥ pūrṇā pariccheda-vivarjanāt ॥ 29 ॥

cetya-ābhāsanam — manifestation of objects, eva — indeed, asyaḥ — of this, citeḥ — of consciousness, saṅkocanaṁ — contraction, bhavet — would be, cetya-ābhāne — in the absence of objects, citiḥ — consciousness, pūrṇā — full, pariccheda-vivarjanāt — by the absence of limitation.
The manifestation of objects indeed is the contraction of consciousness. In the absence of objects, consciousness is full by the absence of limitation.
कालादिभिः परिच्छेदो यदि तस्या निरूप्यते ।
अचेतितः परिच्छेदश्चेतितो वा भवेद्‌ वद ॥ ३० ॥
kālādibhiḥ paricchedaḥ yadi tasyā nirūpyate ।
acetitaḥ paricchedaḥ cetito vā bhavet vada ॥ 30 ॥

kālādibhiḥ — by time, etc., paricchedaḥ — limitation, yadi — if, tasyāḥ — of that, nirūpyate — is defined, acetitaḥ — by the non-conscious, paricchedaḥ — limitation, cetitaḥ — by the conscious, vā — or, bhavet — would be, vada — tell.
If limitation by time, etc., is defined for that, tell whether the limitation would be by the non-conscious or by the conscious.
अचेतने ह्यसिद्धः स्याच्चेतने सैव व्यापिका ।
लोके कालपरिच्छिन्नो भावो यः कोऽपि भावितः ॥ ३१ ॥
acetane hi asiddhaḥ syāt cetane saiva vyāpikā ।
loke kāla-paricchinnaḥ bhāvaḥ yaḥ kaḥ api bhāvitaḥ ॥ 31 ॥

acetane — by the non-conscious, hi — indeed, asiddhaḥ — unreal, syāt — would be, cetane — by the conscious, saiva — that indeed, vyāpikā — pervasive, loke — in the world, kāla-paricchinnaḥ — limited by time, bhāvaḥ — entity, yaḥ kaḥ api — any, bhāvitaḥ — conceived.
By the non-conscious, indeed, it would be unreal; by the conscious, that indeed is pervasive. In the world, any entity conceived as limited by time.
भावकालौ परिच्चेद्यपरिच्छेदकतां गतौ ।
चिता व्याप्तौ भवेतां वै यदा तर्हि तथाविधौ ॥ ३२ ॥
bhāva-kālau pariccheda-aparicchedakatāṁ gatau ।
citā vyāptau bhavetāṁ vai yadā tarhi tathā-vidhau ॥ 32 ॥

bhāva-kālau — entity and time, pariccheda-aparicchedakatāṁ — state of being limited and unlimited, gatau — attained, citā — consciousness, vyāptau — pervasive, bhavetām — would be, vai — indeed, yadā — when, tarhi — then, tathā-vidhau — such.
When entity and time attain the state of being limited and unlimited, then consciousness indeed would be pervasive in such.
अव्याप्तौ तु चिता यर्हि कथं सिद्धयेत्‌ परिच्छिदिः ।
चितेर्बहिर्यदा चेत्यमस्ति तत्‌ स्यात्‌ परिच्छिदिः ॥ ३३ ॥
avyāptau tu citā yarhi kathaṁ siddhayet paricchidiḥ ।
citeḥ bahiḥ yadā cetyaṁ asti tat syāt paricchidiḥ ॥ 33 ॥

avyāptau — in non-pervasiveness, tu — indeed, citā — consciousness, yarhi — when, kathaṁ — how, siddhayet — would be established, paricchidiḥ — limitation, citeḥ — of consciousness, bahiḥ — outside, yadā — when, cetyaṁ — object, asti — is, tat — that, syāt — would be, paricchidiḥ — limitation.
When consciousness is not pervasive, how would limitation be established? When an object is outside of consciousness, that would be limitation.
चितेर्बहिश्चेत्यसिद्धिः सर्वथा नोपपद्यते ।
यो बहिः स कथं सिद्धयेच्चितिसम्बन्धवर्जितः ॥ ३४ ॥
citeḥ bahiḥ cetya-siddhiḥ sarvathā na upapadyate ।
yo bahiḥ sa kathaṁ siddhayet citi-sambandha-varjitaḥ ॥ 34 ॥

citeḥ — of consciousness, bahiḥ — outside, cetya-siddhiḥ — establishment of objects, sarvathā — in any way, na — not, upapadyate — appropriate, yaḥ — who, bahiḥ — outside, saḥ — that, kathaṁ — how, siddhayet — would be established, citi-sambandha-varjitaḥ — devoid of connection with consciousness.
The establishment of objects outside of consciousness is not appropriate in any way. How would that which is outside be established, devoid of connection with consciousness?
सम्बन्धोऽपि नैकदेशः स्यादसिद्धस्तथेतरः ।
तत्सम्बन्धांशमात्रस्य भानादन्यन्न सिद्धयति ॥ ३५ ॥
sambandhaḥ api na eka-deśaḥ syāt asiddhaḥ tathā itaraḥ ।
tat-sambandha-aṁśa-mātrasya bhānāt anyat na siddhayati ॥ 35 ॥

sambandhaḥ — connection, api — even, na — not, eka-deśaḥ — partial, syāt — would be, asiddhaḥ — unreal, tathā — thus, itaraḥ — otherwise, tat-sambandha-aṁśa-mātrasya — mere connection with that part, bhānāt — from appearance, anyat — other, na — not, siddhayati — established.
Even connection would not be partial; otherwise, it would be unreal. Mere connection with that part, from appearance, other is not established.
अतो बहिः पदार्थोऽपि चितिनिर्मग्न इष्यताम्‌ ।
एवं च सर्वात्मनैव मग्नं चेत्यमपीष्यताम्‌ ॥ ३६ ॥
ataḥ bahiḥ padārthaḥ api citi-nirmagna iṣyatām ।
evaṁ ca sarva-ātmanā eva magnaṁ cetyaṁ api iṣyatām ॥ 36 ॥

ataḥ — therefore, bahiḥ — outside, padārthaḥ — object, api — even, citi-nirmagna — immersed in consciousness, iṣyatām — should be considered, evaṁ — thus, ca — and, sarva-ātmanā — in all respects, eva — indeed, magnaṁ — immersed, cetyaṁ — object, api — also, iṣyatām — should be considered.
Therefore, the object outside should be considered immersed in consciousness. Thus, in all respects, the object indeed should be considered immersed.
कथं स्वान्तर्विनिर्मग्नं स्वपरिच्छेदकं भवेत्‌ ।
चेत्यमेवंविधं राम विचारय युयुक्तितः ॥ ३७ ॥
kathaṁ sva-antar-vinir-magnaṁ sva-pariccheda-kaṁ bhavet ।
cetyaṁ evaṁ-vidhaṁ rāma vicāraya yuyuktitaḥ ॥ 37 ॥

kathaṁ — how, sva-antar — own interior, vinir-magnaṁ — completely immersed, sva-pariccheda-kaṁ — self-limiting, bhavet — would be, cetyaṁ — object, evaṁ-vidham — such, rāma — O Rama, vicāraya — consider, yuyuktitaḥ — logically.
How would the object, completely immersed in its own interior, be self-limiting? O Rama, consider logically such an object.
चितेरन्तर्भासमानं प्रतिबिम्बात्मकं भवेत्‌ ।
न भावोदरगो भावो भवन्‌ लोके सुदृश्यते ॥ ३८ ॥
citeḥ antar-bhāsamānaṁ prati-bimba-ātmakaṁ bhavet ।
na bhāva-udara-gaḥ bhāvaḥ bhavan loke su-dṛśyate ॥ 38 ॥

citeḥ — of consciousness, antar — interior, bhāsamānaṁ — appearing, prati-bimba-ātmakaṁ — reflection-like, bhavet — would be, na — not, bhāva-udara-gaḥ — within the interior of the object, bhāvaḥ — object, bhavan — being, loke — in the world, su-dṛśyate — clearly seen.
The object appearing within consciousness would be like a reflection. The object within the interior of the object is not clearly seen in the world.
भावानां स्याद्धि साङ्कर्यं तथा चेद्‌ राम सर्वतः ।
बहिःपदार्थस्ते प्रोक्तो भ्रममूलो हि सर्वथा ॥ ३९ ॥
bhāvānāṁ syāt hi sāṅkaryaṁ tathā cet rāma sarvataḥ ।
bahiḥ-padārthaḥ te proktaḥ bhrama-mūlaḥ hi sarvathā ॥ 39 ॥

bhāvānāṁ — of objects, syāt — would be, hi — indeed, sāṅkaryaṁ — mixture, tathā — thus, cet — if, rāma — O Rama, sarvataḥ — in all respects, bahiḥ-padārthaḥ — external object, te — by you, proktaḥ — stated, bhrama-mūlaḥ — based on illusion, hi — indeed, sarvathā — in all respects.
If the objects indeed would be mixed, O Rama, in all respects, the external object stated by you is indeed based on illusion.
तदाश्रयाणां भावानां कथं स्यात्‌ सत्यता वद ।
चितिस्वरूपः स्वात्मैव तत्तद्भावात्मना सदा ॥ ४० ॥
tad-āśrayāṇāṁ bhāvānāṁ kathaṁ syāt satyatā vada ।
citi-svarūpaḥ sva-ātmā eva tat-tat-bhāva-ātmanā sadā ॥ 40 ॥

tad-āśrayāṇāṁ — dependent on that, bhāvānāṁ — of objects, kathaṁ — how, syāt — would be, satyatā — reality, vada — tell, citi-svarūpaḥ — of the nature of consciousness, sva-ātmā — own self, eva — indeed, tat-tat-bhāva-ātmanā — as the essence of those objects, sadā — always.
Tell, how would the reality of objects dependent on that be? The nature of consciousness, indeed one's own self, is always as the essence of those objects.
भासते स्वाच्छन्द्यशक्त्या नाधिकं विद्यते क्वचित्‌ ।
इति वाक्यं समाकर्ण्य पुनः पप्रच्छ भार्गवः ॥ ४१ ॥
bhāsate svācchandya-śaktyā nādhikaṁ vidyate kvacit ।
iti vākyaṁ samākarṇya punaḥ papraccha bhārgavaḥ ॥ 41 ॥

bhāsate — it appears, svācchandya-śaktyā — by its own free power, na — not, adhikam — more, vidyate — is, kvacit — anywhere, iti — thus, vākyaṁ — statement, samākarṇya — hearing, punaḥ — again, papraccha — asked, bhārgavaḥ — Bhārgava.
It appears by its own free power, and nothing more exists anywhere. Hearing this statement, Bhārgava asked again.
भगवन्‌ भवता प्रोक्तं दुर्घटं प्रतिभाति मे ।
शुद्धा चितिर्विचित्रैका भासत इत्यसम्भवात्‌ ॥ ४२ ॥
bhagavan bhavatā proktaṁ durghaṭaṁ pratibhāti me ।
śuddhā citir vicitraikā bhāsata ity-asambhavāt ॥ 42 ॥

bhagavan — O Lord, bhavatā — by you, proktaṁ — said, durghaṭaṁ — difficult, pratibhāti — appears, me — to me, śuddhā — pure, citiḥ — consciousness, vicitraikā — as varied one, bhāsata — appears, iti — thus, asambhavāt — because of impossibility.
O Lord, what you said appears difficult to me. The pure consciousness appearing as varied is impossible.
चितिश्चेत्यमिति द्वेधा वस्तु सर्वैर्विभावितम्‌ ।
तत्र चेत्यं चिता भास्यं स्वप्रभा चितिरस्तु ते ॥ ४३ ॥
citiś cetyaṁ iti dvedhā vastu sarvair vibhāvitaṁ ।
tatra cetyaṁ citā bhāsyaṁ sva-prabhā citir astu te ॥ 43 ॥

citiḥ — consciousness, cetyaṁ — object, iti — thus, dvedhā — twofold, vastu — entity, sarvaiḥ — by all, vibhāvitaṁ — conceived, tatra — there, cetyaṁ — object, citā — by consciousness, bhāsyaṁ — is illumined, sva-prabhā — self-luminous, citiḥ — consciousness, astu — is, te — to you.
Consciousness and object are conceived as twofold entities by all. There, the object is illumined by consciousness, and consciousness is self-luminous to you.
यथाऽऽलोकभातमपि वस्तु तद्भिन्नमस्ति वै ।
एवं चिता भासितं तु चेत्यमस्तु पृथग्विधम्‌ ॥ ४४ ॥
yathā'āloka-bhātam api vastu tad-bhinnaṁ asti vai ।
evaṁ citā bhāsitaṁ tu cetyaṁ astu pṛthag-vidham ॥ 44 ॥

yathā — just as, āloka-bhātam — illumined by light, api — even, vastu — object, tad-bhinnaṁ — separate from it, asti — is, vai — indeed, evaṁ — thus, citā — by consciousness, bhāsitaṁ — illumined, tu — but, cetyaṁ — object, astu — is, pṛthag-vidham — distinct.
Just as an object illumined by light is indeed separate from it, thus, the object illumined by consciousness is distinct.
चेत्यं चिदात्मकमिति नानुभूतिं समारुहेत्‌ ।
अथ च प्रागभिहितं जनकेन महात्मना ॥ ४५ ॥
cetyaṁ cid-ātmakam iti nānubhūtiṁ samāruhet ।
atha ca prāg abhihitaṁ janakena mahātmanā ॥ 45 ॥

cetyaṁ — object, cid-ātmakam — of the nature of consciousness, iti — thus, na — not, anubhūtiṁ — experience, samāruhet — can reach, atha — moreover, ca — and, prāk — previously, abhihitaṁ — said, janakena — by Janaka, mahātmanā — the great soul.
The object being of the nature of consciousness is not an experience. Moreover, it was previously said by the great soul, Janaka.

सङ्कल्पवर्जनादेव निर्विकल्पं मनो भवेत्‌ ।
तदेव निर्विकल्पं स्याज्ज्ञानं संसारनाशनम्‌ ॥ ४६ ॥
saṅkalpa-varjanād eva nirvikalpaṁ mano bhavet ।
tad eva nirvikalpaṁ syāt jñānaṁ saṁsāra-nāśanam ॥ 46 ॥

saṅkalpa-varjanāt — by abandonment of thoughts, eva — indeed, nirvikalpaṁ — without duality, manaḥ — mind, bhavet — becomes, tad — that, eva — indeed, nirvikalpaṁ — without duality, syāt — becomes, jñānaṁ — knowledge, saṁsāra-nāśanam — destroyer of worldly existence.
By abandonment of thoughts, the mind indeed becomes without duality. That same non-dual state becomes the knowledge that destroys worldly existence.
तदेव ह्यात्मनो रूपमित्युक्तं तत्‌ कथं भवेत्‌ ।
आत्मनो हि मनः प्रोक्तं करणं ज्ञानकर्मणि ॥ ४७ ॥
tad eva hy ātmano rūpam ity-uktaṁ tat kathaṁ bhavet ।
ātmano hi manaḥ proktaṁ karaṇaṁ jñāna-karmaṇi ॥ 47 ॥

tad — that, eva — indeed, hi — for, ātmanaḥ — of the self, rūpam — form, iti — thus, uktaṁ — said, tat — that, kathaṁ — how, bhavet — would be, ātmanaḥ — of the self, hi — indeed, manaḥ — mind, proktaṁ — is said, karaṇaṁ — instrument, jñāna-karmaṇi — in knowledge and action.
That is indeed said to be the form of the self. How would that be? For the mind is indeed said to be the instrument of the self in knowledge and action.
मनो यद्यात्मनो न स्याद्विशिष्येत जडात्‌ कथम्‌ ।
मनो जडाद्विशेषः स्यादात्मनो भगवन्ननु ॥ ४८ ॥
mano yady ātmano na syāt viśiṣyeta jaḍāt katham ।
mano jaḍāt viśeṣaḥ syāt ātmano bhagavan anu ॥ 48 ॥

manaḥ — mind, yadi — if, ātmanaḥ — of the self, na — not, syāt — is, viśiṣyeta — distinguished, jaḍāt — from the inert, katham — how, manaḥ — mind, jaḍāt — from the inert, viśeṣaḥ — difference, syāt — would be, ātmanaḥ — of the self, bhagavan — O Lord, anu — indeed.
If the mind is not of the self, how would it be distinguished from the inert? O Lord, indeed, the mind's difference from the inert is due to the self.
मनसैव हि बन्धः स्यान्मोक्षो वाऽप्यात्मनः स्फुटम्‌ ।
सविकल्पं मनो बन्धो मोक्षः स्यान्निर्विकल्पकम्‌ ॥ ४९ ॥
manasaiva hi bandhaḥ syān mokṣaḥ vā api ātmanaḥ sphuṭam ।
sa-vikalpaṁ mano bandhaḥ mokṣaḥ syāt nirvikalpakaṁ ॥ 49 ॥

manasā — by the mind, eva — indeed, hi — for, bandhaḥ — bondage, syāt — is, mokṣaḥ — liberation, vā — or, api — also, ātmanaḥ — of the self, sphuṭam — clearly, sa-vikalpaṁ — with duality, manaḥ — mind, bandhaḥ — bondage, mokṣaḥ — liberation, syāt — is, nirvikalpakaṁ — without duality.
For indeed, bondage and liberation of the self are clearly by the mind. The mind with duality is bondage, and liberation is without duality.
तत्‌ कथं मन एवात्मा करणं हि मनः स्मृतम्‌ ।
निर्विकल्पस्य संसिद्धावपि द्वैतं तु शिष्यते ॥ ५० ॥
tat kathaṁ mana eva ātmā karaṇaṁ hi manaḥ smṛtam ।
nirvikalpasya saṁsiddhau api dvaitaṁ tu śiṣyate ॥ 50 ॥

tat — that, kathaṁ — how, manaḥ — mind, eva — indeed, ātmā — self, karaṇaṁ — instrument, hi — indeed, manaḥ — mind, smṛtam — is considered, nirvikalpasya — of the non-dual, saṁsiddhau — in perfection, api — even, dvaitaṁ — duality, tu — but, śiṣyate — remains.
How is the mind itself the self, when the mind is considered an instrument? Even in the perfection of the non-dual, duality remains.
अथापि लोके दृष्टोऽस्ति यस्य भ्रान्तिरसन्‌ हि सः ।
नहि भ्रान्तिरसत्या स्यात्तदद्वैतं कथं भवेत्‌ ॥ ५१ ॥
athāpi loke dṛṣṭo'sti yasya bhrāntir asan hi saḥ ।
nahi bhrāntiḥ asatyā syāt tad advaitaṁ kathaṁ bhavet ॥ 51 ॥

atha api — even if, loke — in the world, dṛṣṭaḥ — seen, asti — is, yasya — whose, bhrāntiḥ — delusion, asan — non-existent, hi — indeed, saḥ — he, nahi — not, bhrāntiḥ — delusion, asatyā — by falsehood, syāt — is, tad — that, advaitaṁ — non-duality, kathaṁ — how, bhavet — would be.
Even if seen in the world, one whose delusion is non-existent, indeed he, not by falsehood is delusion, how would that be non-duality?
अर्थक्रिया न क्वचिच्च दुष्टाऽसत्येन वस्तुना ।
सर्व हि जागतं वस्तु स्थिरमर्थक्रियाकरम्‌ ॥ ५२ ॥
artha-kriyā na kvacit ca duṣṭā asatyena vastunā ।
sarva hi jāgataṁ vastu sthiram artha-kriyā-karam ॥ 52 ॥

artha-kriyā — utility, na — not, kvacit — anywhere, ca — and, duṣṭā — corrupted, asatyena — by false, vastunā — object, sarva — all, hi — indeed, jāgataṁ — worldly, vastu — object, sthiram — stable, artha-kriyā-karam — utility-producing.
Utility is not corrupted anywhere by a false object. All worldly objects indeed are stable and utility-producing.
तदसत्यं कथं ब्रूहि यतोऽद्वैतं प्रसिद्धयति ।
सर्वं च भ्रान्तिविज्ञानं भ्रान्त्यभ्रान्तिभिदा कथम्‌ ॥ ५३ ॥
tad-asatyaṁ kathaṁ brūhi yato'advaitaṁ prasiddhayati ।
sarvaṁ ca bhrānti-vijñānaṁ bhrānti-abhrānti-bhidā katham ॥ 53 ॥

tat — that, asatyaṁ — false, kathaṁ — how, brūhi — tell, yataḥ — from where, advaitaṁ — non-duality, prasiddhayati — is established, sarvaṁ — all, ca — and, bhrānti-vijñānaṁ — delusive knowledge, bhrānti — delusion, abhrānti — non-delusion, bhidā — distinction, katham — how.
Tell, how is that falsehood established as non-duality? All delusive knowledge and the distinction between delusion and non-delusion, how is it?
भ्रान्तिः सर्वसमा वापि कथं स्याद्‌ ब्रूहि मे गुरो ।
सन्देह एष चिरतो हृदि मे परिवर्तते ॥ ५४ ॥
bhrāntiḥ sarva-samā vā api kathaṁ syāt brūhi me guro ।
sandeha eṣa cirataḥ hṛdi me parivartate ॥ 54 ॥

bhrāntiḥ — delusion, sarva-samā — all-pervading, vā — or, api — even, kathaṁ — how, syāt — would be, brūhi — tell, me — to me, guro — O teacher, sandehaḥ — doubt, eṣaḥ — this, cirataḥ — for a long time, hṛdi — in the heart, me — my, parivartate — revolves.
Tell me, O teacher, how can delusion be all-pervading? This doubt has been revolving in my heart for a long time.
इत्येवं प्रश्नमाकर्ण्य दत्तात्रेयः समस्तवित्‌ ।
साधुप्रश्नप्रहृष्टात्मा प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमे ॥ ५५ ॥
iti evaṁ praśnam ākarṇya dattātreyaḥ samasta-vit ।
sādhu-praśna-prahṛṣṭa-ātmā pravaktum upacakrame ॥ 55 ॥

iti — thus, evaṁ — this, praśnam — question, ākarṇya — hearing, dattātreyaḥ — Dattatreya, samasta-vit — all-knowing, sādhu-praśna — good question, prahṛṣṭa-ātmā — delighted, pravaktum — to speak, upacakrame — commenced.
Thus, hearing this question, the all-knowing Dattatreya, delighted by the good question, commenced to speak.
राम साधु त्वया पृष्टं प्रोक्तप्रायमिदं पुनः ।
यावन्न मनसस्तोषस्तावद्‌ भूयो विशोधयेत्‌ ॥ ५६ ॥
rāma sādhu tvayā pṛṣṭaṁ prokta-prāyam idaṁ punaḥ ।
yāvat na manasaḥ toṣaḥ tāvat bhūyaḥ viśodhayet ॥ 56 ॥

rāma — O Rāma, sādhu — well done, tvayā — by you, pṛṣṭaṁ — asked, prokta-prāyam — often said, idaṁ — this, punaḥ — again, yāvat — until, na — not, manasaḥ — of the mind, toṣaḥ — satisfaction, tāvat — until, bhūyaḥ — again, viśodhayet — should clarify.
O Rāma, well done, this question is often asked. Until the mind is satisfied, one should keep clarifying.
गुरूर्वापि कथं ब्रूयादपृष्टस्तन्मनोगतम्‌ ।
प्राणिनां हि बुद्धिभेदात्तर्कः पूथगवस्थितः ॥ ५७ ॥
gurur vā api kathaṁ brūyāt apṛṣṭaḥ tat manaḥ gatam ।
prāṇināṁ hi buddhi-bhedāt tarkaḥ pūthag avasthitaḥ ॥ 57 ॥

guruḥ — teacher, vā — or, api — even, kathaṁ — how, brūyāt — would say, apṛṣṭaḥ — unasked, tat — that, manaḥ gatam — in the mind, prāṇinām — of beings, hi — indeed, buddhi-bhedāt — due to differences in intellect, tarkaḥ — reasoning, pūthag — different, avasthitaḥ — established.
How would a teacher say what is in the mind if unasked? Indeed, due to differences in intellect, reasoning is established differently among beings.
अपृष्ट्वा स्वस्वाभिमतं कः सन्देहाद्विमुच्यते ।
प्रष्टुर्विद्या हि सुदृढा प्रश्नो बीजं निरूपणे ॥ ५८ ॥
apṛṣṭvā sva-sva-abhimataṁ kaḥ sandehāt vimucyate ।
praṣṭuḥ vidyā hi sudṛḍhā praśnaḥ bījaṁ nirūpaṇe ॥ 58 ॥

apṛṣṭvā — without asking, sva-sva-abhimataṁ — one's own opinion, kaḥ — who, sandehāt — from doubt, vimucyate — is freed, praṣṭuḥ — of the questioner, vidyā — knowledge, hi — indeed, sudṛḍhā — firm, praśnaḥ — question, bījaṁ — seed, nirūpaṇe — in clarification.
Without asking one's own opinion, who is freed from doubt? Indeed, the question is the seed of firm knowledge for the questioner in clarification.
अप्रष्टुर्नैव विद्या स्यात्‌ पृष्ट्वा विद्यात्ततो गुरुम्‌ ।
चितिरेकैव वैचित्र्याद्भासत इति सम्भवेत्‌ ॥ ५९ ॥
apraṣṭuḥ na eva vidyā syāt pṛṣṭvā vidyāt tato gurum ।
citiḥ ekā eva vaicitryāt bhāsata iti sambhavet ॥ 59 ॥

apraṣṭuḥ — without asking, na eva — not at all, vidyā — knowledge, syāt — would be, pṛṣṭvā — having asked, vidyāt — one would know, tataḥ — then, gurum — from the teacher, citiḥ — consciousness, ekā eva — one only, vaicitryāt — due to variety, bhāsata — appears, iti — thus, sambhavet — may be possible.
Without asking, knowledge would not be at all. Having asked, one would know from the teacher. Thus, consciousness, though one only, may appear due to variety.
एकरूपो यथादर्शः प्रतिबिम्बादनेकधा ।
पश्य स्वप्नविकल्पादौ मन एकं हि केवलम्‌ ॥ ६० ॥
eka-rūpaḥ yathā ādarśaḥ pratibimbāt anekadhā ।
paśya svapna-vikalpa-ādau mana ekaṁ hi kevalam ॥ 60 ॥

eka-rūpaḥ — of one form, yathā — just as, ādarśaḥ — mirror, pratibimbāt — from reflections, anekadhā — in many ways, paśya — see, svapna-vikalpa-ādau — in dream and imagination, manaḥ — mind, ekaṁ — one, hi — indeed, kevalam — only.
Just as a mirror of one form appears in many ways from reflections, see in dreams and imaginations, the mind is indeed one only.
द्रष्टृदर्शनदृश्यात्मवैचित्र्येण विभाति हि ।
एवं शुद्धैव सा संविद्विचित्राकारभासिनी ॥ ६१ ॥
draṣṭṛ-darśana-dṛśyātma-vaicitryeṇa vibhāti hi ।
evaṁ śuddhaiva sā saṁvid vicitrākāra-bhāsinī ॥ 61 ॥

draṣṭṛ — seer, darśana — seeing, dṛśya — seen, ātma — self, vaicitryeṇa — through diversity, vibhāti — shines, hi — indeed, evaṁ — thus, śuddha — pure, eva — indeed, sā — she, saṁvid — consciousness, vicitra — various, ākāra — forms, bhāsinī — illuminating.
Thus, consciousness shines through the diversity of seer, seeing, and seen. Indeed, she is pure and illuminates various forms.
चितिश्चेत्यमिति द्वेधा स्वप्नेऽपि हि विभासते ।
आलोकमन्तरा त्वन्धो भावं जानाति वै ननु ॥ ६२॥
Citiḥ-cetyam-iti-dvedhā-svapne-api-hi-vibhāsate ।
ālokaṁ-antarā-tu-andhaḥ-bhāvaṁ-jānāti-vai-nanu ॥ 62 ॥

citiḥ — consciousness, cetyaṁ — the perceived, iti — thus, dvedhā — duality, svapne — in dreams, api — even, hi — indeed, vibhāsate — appears, ālokam — light, antarā — without, tu — but, andhaḥ — blind, bhāvaṁ — existence, jānāti — knows, vai — indeed, nanu — surely.
Consciousness and the perceived appear as duality even in dreams. Without light, the blind surely do not know existence.
अन्धस्याभासमानं च रूपं भाति स्मृतौ किल ।
नैवं चितेरभाने किं कदा कुत्र विभासते ॥ ६३ ॥
Andhasya-abhāsamānaṁ-ca-rūpaṁ-bhāti-smṛtau-kila ।
na-evaṁ-citeḥ-abhāne-kiṁ-kadā-kutra-vibhāsate ॥ 63 ॥

andhasya — of the blind, abhāsamānaṁ — appearing, ca — and, rūpaṁ — form, bhāti — shines, smṛtau — in memory, kila — surely, na — not, evaṁ — thus, citeḥ — of consciousness, abhāne — in absence, kiṁ — what, kadā — when, kutra — where, vibhāsate — shines.
The form appearing to the blind shines only in memory. Without the light of consciousness, when and where does anything shine?
यथादर्शं विना किञ्चित्‌ प्रतिबिम्बं न भाति वै ।
आदर्शान्नातिरिक्तोऽतः प्रतिबिम्बो भवेद्यथा ॥ ६४ ॥
Yathā-ādarsaṁ-vinā-kiñcit-pratibimbaṁ-na-bhāti-vai ।
ādarsa-anna-atirikto-ataḥ-pratibimbo-bhavet-yathā ॥ 64 ॥

Just as without a mirror, no reflection shines, so too, from the mirror, the reflection is not separate.
एवं चितिमृते किञ्चिदतिरिक्तं न विद्यते ।
अत एव मनोऽप्यन्यत्‌ सर्वथा नास्ति वै चितेः ॥ ६५ ॥
Evaṁ-citiṁ-ṛte-kiñcid-atiriktaṁ-na-vidyate ।
ataḥ-eva-manaḥ-api-anyat-sarvathā-na-asti-vai-citeḥ ॥ 65 ॥

Thus, without consciousness, nothing separate is known. Therefore, the mind is not other than consciousness in any way.

कल्पितं कार्यसंसिद्धयै करणं केवलं मनः ॥ ६६ ॥
Yathā-svapne-manas-tadvat-jāgrati-api-manaḥ-nahi ।
kalpitaṁ-kārya-saṁsiddhyai-karaṇaṁ-kevalaṁ-manaḥ ॥ 66 ॥

yathā — just as, svapne — in dreams, manas — mind, tadvat — so too, jāgrati — in waking, api — even, manaḥ — mind, nahi — not, kalpitaṁ — imagined, kārya-saṁsiddhyai — for the completion of actions, karaṇaṁ — instrument, kevalaṁ — merely, manaḥ — mind.
Just as the mind is in dreams, so too in waking, the mind is not different. The mind is merely an instrument imagined for the completion of actions.
यथा स्वाप्नः कुठारः स्यात्‌ करणं तरुछेदने ।
राम क्रियाऽसत्यरूपा सत्यं तत्करणं कथम्‌ ॥ ६७ ॥
Yathā-svāpnaḥ-kuṭhāraḥ-syāt-karaṇaṁ-taru-chedane ।
rāma-kriyā-asatya-rūpā-satyaṁ-tat-karaṇaṁ-katham ॥ 67 ॥

Just as a dream axe is an instrument for cutting trees, O Rāma, actions are false forms; how can that instrument be true?
असता नरशृङ्गेण कः कदा सुविदारितः ।
तस्मान्नास्ति मनो राम चासत्‌ कार्यस्य कारणम्‌ ॥ ६८ ॥

tasmāt-na-asti-manaḥ-rāma-ca-asat-kāryasya-kāraṇam ॥ 68 ॥

Who has ever been well-cut by a man's horn, a false thing? Therefore, O Rāma, the mind, too, is not the cause of false action.

यथा तथा सर्वदापि मनो नास्ति क्रियाकरम्‌ ॥ ६९ ॥

In dreams, the mind is said to be the instrument for vision, action, and other activities. Just as in dreams, so always, the mind is not the doer of actions.
चिदात्मा केवलं स्वच्छस्वाच्छन्द्यान्मनआदिकम्‌ ।
परिकल्प्य व्यवहरेद् दुश्यद्रष्ट्रादिभेदतः ॥ ७० ॥
Cidātmā-kevalaṁ-svaccha-svāchandyāt-manaḥ-ādikam ।
parikalpya-vyavaharet-dṛśya-draṣṭṛ-ādi-bhedataḥ ॥ 70 ॥

शृणु भार्गव चित्तत्वं परिपूर्णमपि स्वयम्‌ ॥ ७१ ॥
Kvacit-kvacit-kevalaṁ-tu-nirvikalpa-ātmanā-sthitaḥ ।

आकाशश्च चिदात्मा च न विलक्षणतां गतौ ॥ ७२ ॥
Nākāśa-tulyaṁ-caitanyāt-svaprakāśam-ataḥ-sthitam ।
ākāśaś-ca-cidātmā-ca-na-vilakṣaṇatāṁ-gatau ॥ 72 ॥

Not like space, consciousness is self-illuminating, thus established. Space and the consciousness-self are not distinct from each other.

सर्वाधारोऽप्यसङ्गात्मा सर्वान्तरबहिर्भवः ॥ ७३ ॥

sarvādāraḥ-api-asaṅga-ātmā-sarva-antara-bahiḥ-bhavaḥ ॥ 73 ॥

वस्तुतश्चैतन्यपूर्ण आत्मैवाकाश उच्यते ॥ ७४ ॥
Viśeṣaḥ-tatra-caitanyam-ākāśe-tat-na-vidyate ।
vastutaḥ-caitanya-pūrṇaḥ-ātmā-eva-ākāśaḥ-ucyate ॥ 74 ॥

There is no distinction in consciousness and space; in reality, the self, full of consciousness, is indeed called space.
नह्यात्माकाशयोर्भेदो लेशतोऽपि हि विद्यते ।
य आकाशः स आत्मैव यश्चात्माकाश एव सः ॥ ७५ ॥
Na-hi-ātmā-ākāśayoḥ-bhedaḥ-leśataḥ-api-hi-vidyate ।

Indeed, there is no difference between the self and space, even a little. What is space is indeed the self; and what is the self is indeed space.

सौरालोकं यथोलूकस्तमोमात्रं प्रपश्यति ॥ ७६ ॥

The ignorant see the nature of the self as space, indeed, from delusion, just as an owl sees only darkness in sunlight.

But the wise see space as the essence of self-consciousness. The supreme consciousness, the supreme lord, pure and free in splendor.

Illuminates the self as limited in many ways, just as, O Rāma, one sees oneself in dreams in many ways, separately.

अनेकधाऽवभासोऽपि परिच्छिन्नदृशैव हि ॥ ७९ ॥

anekadhā-avabhāsaḥ-api-paricchinna-dṛśā-eva-hi ॥ 79 ॥

You illuminate through distinctions of humans, etc., thus indeed. Even the illumination in many ways is surely by limited vision.
स्वयं स्वदृष्टया पूर्णात्मरूपिण्येव परा चितिः ।
ऐन्द्रजालिक एकोऽपि स्वमात्मानमनेकधा ॥ ८० ॥
Svayam-sva-dṛṣṭyā-pūrṇa-ātma-rūpiṇy-eva-parā-citiḥ ।
aindra-jālika-ekaḥ-api-svam-ātmānam-anekadhā ॥ 80 ॥

svayam — oneself, sva-dṛṣṭyā — by own vision, pūrṇa-ātma-rūpiṇī — in the form of the complete self, eva — indeed, parā-citiḥ — supreme consciousness, aindra-jālikaḥ — magician, ekaḥ — one, api — even, svam — own, ātmānam — self, anekadhā — in many ways.
By one's own vision, the supreme consciousness is indeed in the form of the complete self. Even a magician, though one, sees oneself in many ways.

एक एव निर्विकार एवं सा परमा चितिः ॥ ८१ ॥
Bhāsayaṁs-tatra-draṣṭṛṇāṁ-sva-dṛṣṭyā-bhāsate-svayam ।

bhāsayan — illuminating, tatra — there, draṣṭṛṇām — of the seers, sva-dṛṣṭyā — by own vision, bhāsate — shines, svayam — itself, ekaḥ — one, eva — indeed, nirvikāra — changeless, evam — thus, sā — that, paramā — supreme, citiḥ — consciousness.
Illuminating there, the supreme consciousness shines by the vision of the seers, itself indeed one and changeless.

Even the pure, one form shines in many limited ways, covered by illusion.

māyā-āvaraṇam — illusion's cover, api — even, etat — this, paricchinna-dṛśaḥ — of limited vision, bhavet — becomes, yathā — as, indrajālikaḥ — magician, māyā-āvṛtaḥ — covered by illusion, ca — and, anya-dṛśaḥ — of different vision, bhavet — becomes.
This illusion's cover comes of limited vision, as a magician covered by illusion appears differently.

Illusion created by others, extremely difficult to overcome, even in the world, yogis, others adept in mantras, and magicians.

ācchāditaṁ — covered, sva-svātantryam — own freedom, prāpya — attaining, kiñcit — something, su-yuktitaḥ — with proper reasoning, durghaṭam — difficult, ghaṭayanti — they accomplish, eva — indeed, tataḥ — thus, na — not, etad — this, vicitra-tam — very surprising.

evaṁ — thus, para-citeḥ — of the supreme consciousness, svaccha — pure, svātantryāt — from freedom, sva-ātmano — of one's self, vapuḥ — form, anekadhā — in many ways, paricchinnaṁ — limited, bhāsitaṁ — shines, bhṛgu-nandana — O son of Bhṛgu.
Thus, O son of Bhṛgu, from the pure freedom of the supreme consciousness, the form of one's self shines in many limited ways.

Paricchedaḥ-abhimānasya-tu-eka-deśe-su-viśramaḥ ।

Limitation of ego is well established in one place, which is also famous as incompleteness, described as ignorance.

Atra-muhyanti-bahavaḥ-tārkikāḥ-paṇḍitā-api ।
