atra — here, muhyanti — are deluded, bahavaḥ — many, tārkikāḥ — logicians, paṇḍitāḥ — scholars, api — even, sva-ātmānam — own self, anudāhṛtya — not realizing, bahir-dṛṣṭitayā — with outward vision, sthiteḥ — being.
Here many logicians and scholars are deluded, not realizing their own self, being with outward vision.
गुरूपदिष्टं यत्‌ किञ्चित्‌ सद्वाऽप्यसदपीतरत्‌ ।
अनुदाहृत्य चात्मानं यावन्न ह्यवलोकयेत्‌ ॥ ८९ ॥
Guru-upadiṣṭaṁ-yat-kiñcit-sat-vā-api-asat-api-itarat ।
Anudāhṛtya-ca-ātmānam-yāvat-na-hi-avalokayet ॥ 89 ॥

guru-upadiṣṭaṁ — taught by the guru, yat-kiñcit — anything, sat-vā — true, api — also, asat-api — untrue, itarat — other, anudāhṛtya — not realizing, ca — and, ātmānam — own self, yāvat — until, na — not, hi — indeed, avalokayet — realizes.
Anything taught by the guru, whether true or untrue, one does not realize until they realize their own self.
तावन्न फलमाप्नोति परोक्षात्मतया श्रुतेः ।
अतो मयोक्तं राम त्वं सम्पश्यात्मनि सद्दृशा ॥ ९० ॥
Tāvat-na-phalam-āpnoti-parokṣātmatayā-śruteḥ ।
Ataḥ-mayā-uktaṁ-rāma-tvaṁ-sampaśya-ātmani-sad-dṛśā ॥ 90 ॥

tāvat — until then, na — not, phalam — fruit, āpnoti — obtains, parokṣātmatayā — by indirect knowledge, śruteḥ — from scripture, ataḥ — therefore, mayā — by me, uktam — said, rāma — O Rāma, tvam — you, sampaśya — see, ātmani — in self, sad-dṛśā — with true vision.
Until then, one does not obtain the fruit by indirect knowledge from scripture. Therefore, O Rāma, I have said, you see within yourself with true vision.
चितिर्या परमा देवी सर्वसामान्यरूपिणी ।
सा प्रकाशमयी यस्माज्जडव्यावृत्तरूपिणी ॥ ९१ ॥
Citiḥ-yā-paramā-devī-sarva-sāmānya-rūpiṇī ।
Sā-prakāśamayī-yasmāt-jaḍa-vyāvṛtta-rūpiṇī ॥ 91 ॥

citiḥ — consciousness, yā — which, paramā — supreme, devī — goddess, sarva-sāmānya-rūpiṇī — of the form of all common, sā — that, prakāśamayī — full of light, yasmāt — since, jaḍa-vyāvṛtta-rūpiṇī — of the form separate from inertness.
The supreme consciousness, which is the goddess of all common forms, is full of light and separate from inertness.
अतः स्वात्मनि विश्रान्तिस्त्वहन्ता पररूपिणी ।
जडाश्चिदात्मविश्रान्ताश्चिदात्मनि विभासतः ॥ ९२ ॥
Ataḥ-sva-ātmani-viśrāntiḥ-tu-ahantā-para-rūpiṇī ।
jaḍāḥ-cid-ātma-viśrāntāḥ-cid-ātmani-vibhāsataḥ ॥ 92 ॥

ataḥ — therefore, sva-ātmani — in own self, viśrāntiḥ — rest, tu — indeed, ahantā — ego, para-rūpiṇī — in another form, jaḍāḥ — inert, cid-ātma — consciousness self, viśrāntāḥ — rested, cid-ātmani — in the self of consciousness, vibhāsataḥ — shines.
Therefore, the rest in one's own self is indeed the ego in another form. The inert rested in the consciousness self shines in the self of consciousness.
न स्वरूपे स्वतो भान्ति तस्मान्न स्वात्मविश्रमः ।
चितेस्तु केवलं स्वस्मिन्ननन्यपेक्षया सदा ॥ ९३ ॥
Na-svarūpe-svato-bhānti-tasmāt-na-sva-ātma-viśramaḥ ।
Citeḥ-tu-kevalaṁ-svasmin-ananya-apekṣayā-sadā ॥ 93 ॥

na — not, svarūpe — in own form, svato — by itself, bhānti — shines, tasmāt — therefore, na — not, sva-ātma-viśramaḥ — rest in own self, citeḥ — of consciousness, tu — indeed, kevalaṁ — only, svasmin — in self, ananya-apekṣayā — without any dependence, sadā — always.
Not shining in its own form by itself, therefore, there is no rest in the own self. The consciousness indeed only rests in itself always without any dependence.
भासमानत्वतः स्वस्मिन्‌ विश्रान्तिरुपपद्यते ।
पूर्णाहन्ता परा सेयं या जडेषु न विद्यते ॥ ९४ ॥
Bhāsamānatvataḥ-svasmin-viśrāntiḥ-upapadyate ।
Pūrṇa-ahantā-parā-sā-iyam-yā-jaḍeṣu-na-vidyate ॥ 94 ॥

bhāsamānatvataḥ — due to shining, svasmin — in self, viśrāntiḥ — rest, upapadyate — occurs, pūrṇa-ahantā — complete ego, parā — supreme, sā — that, iyam — this, yā — which, jaḍeṣu — in inert, na — not, vidyate — exists.
Due to shining in itself, rest occurs. This supreme complete ego, which does not exist in the inert, is this.
व्यावृत्तिस्पर्शहीनेयं परिच्छेदविवर्जनात्‌ ।
सर्वमस्यां यतः संस्थमादर्शे नगरं यथा ॥ ९५ ॥
Vyāvṛtti-sparśa-hīnā-iyam-pariccheda-vivarjanāt ।
Sarvam-asyām-yataḥ-saṁstham-ādarśe-nagaraṁ-yathā ॥ 95 ॥

vyāvṛtti-sparśa-hīnā — without touch of distinction, iyam — this, pariccheda-vivarjanāt — due to absence of limitation, sarvam — everything, asyām — in this, yataḥ — since, saṁstham — established, ādarśe — in a mirror, nagaraṁ — city, yathā — like.
Without touch of distinction, due to absence of limitation, everything is established in this, like a city in a mirror.
व्यावृत्तिर्वा परिच्छेदः कथं केन हि सम्भवेत्‌ ।
एवं पूर्णस्वरूपायाः पूर्ण यत्स्फुरणं स्थितम्‌ ॥ ९६ ॥
Vyāvṛttiḥ-vā-paricchedaḥ-kathaṁ-kena-hi-sambhavet ।
Evaṁ-pūrṇa-svarūpāyāḥ-pūrṇa-yat-sphuraṇaṁ-sthitam ॥ 96 ॥

vyāvṛttiḥ — distinction, vā — or, paricchedaḥ — limitation, kathaṁ — how, kena — by whom, hi — indeed, sambhavet — occurs, evaṁ — thus, pūrṇa-svarūpāyāḥ — of the complete form, pūrṇa — complete, yat — which, sphuraṇam — shining, sthitam — established.
How can distinction or limitation occur, indeed, by whom? Thus, the complete form's complete shining is established.
तदेव स्वात्मविश्रान्तिः पूर्णाहन्ता च कथ्यते ।
अखण्डैकरसं ह्येतदेतावद्‌ राम वै भवेत्‌ ॥ ९७ ॥
Tad-eva-sva-ātma-viśrāntiḥ-pūrṇa-ahantā-ca-kathyate ।
Akhaṇḍa-eka-rasaṁ-hi-etat-etāvat-rāma-vai-bhavet ॥ 97 ॥

tad — that, eva — indeed, sva-ātma-viśrāntiḥ — rest in own self, pūrṇa-ahantā — complete ego, ca — and, kathyate — is said, akhaṇḍa — unbroken, eka-rasaṁ — one essence, hi — indeed, etat — this, etāvat — as much, rāma — O Rāma, vai — indeed, bhavet — becomes.
That indeed is said to be rest in one's own self and complete ego. This unbroken one essence indeed becomes as much, O Rāma.
निरूपणे बहुविधमिव तत्‌ प्रतिभासते ।
एतावदेव स्वातन्त्र्यं यतः शक्तिर्हि तन्मयी ॥ ९८ ॥
Nirūpaṇe-bahuvidham-iva-tat-pratibhāsate ।
Etāvat-eva-svātantryaṁ-yataḥ-śaktiḥ-hi-tanmāyī ॥ 98 ॥

nirūpaṇe — in description, bahuvidham — many forms, iva — like, tat — that, pratibhāsate — appears, etāvat — as much, eva — indeed, svātantryaṁ — freedom, yataḥ — since, śaktiḥ — power, hi — indeed, tanmāyī — of that.
In description, that appears in many forms, as much indeed is the freedom, since the power is that indeed.
प्रकाशस्तेजसो यद्वदौष्ण्यं चैवापृथक्‌ स्थितम्‌ ।
एवं स्वातन्त्र्यविश्रान्तिसहितैकरसात्मिका ॥ ९९ ॥
Prakāśaḥ-tejasaḥ-yadvat-auṣṇyaṁ-ca-eva-apṛthak-sthitam ।
Evaṁ-svātantrya-viśrānti-sahita-eka-rasa-ātmikā ॥ 99 ॥

prakāśaḥ — light, tejasaḥ — of fire, yadvat — just as, auṣṇyam — heat, ca — and, eva — indeed, apṛthak-sthitam — inseparably existing, evaṁ — thus, svātantrya — freedom, viśrānti — rest, sahita — together, eka-rasa-ātmikā — of one essence.
Just as light and heat of fire exist inseparably, thus freedom and rest together are of one essence.
इयमेव हि मायाख्या शक्तिः परमदुर्घटा ।
आदर्शवद्यत्स्वरूपे चिदेकरसरूपिणी ॥ १०० ॥
Iyam-eva-hi-māyā-ākhyā-śaktiḥ-parama-durghaṭā ।
Ādarśavat-yat-svarūpe-cit-eka-rasa-rūpiṇī ॥ 100 ॥

iyam — this, eva — indeed, hi — indeed, māyā-ākhyā — called illusion, śaktiḥ — power, parama-durghaṭā — extremely difficult, ādarśavat — like a mirror, yat — which, svarūpe — in form, cit — consciousness, eka-rasa-rūpiṇī — of one essence.
This indeed is the power called illusion, extremely difficult, which in form is like a mirror, of one essence with consciousness.
सत्यप्यनेकवैचित्र्याभासनेन विभासते ।
तथा भासनकालेऽपि स्वरूपादनिवर्तनम्‌ ॥ १०१ ॥
satya-api-aneka-vaicitrya-abhāsanena vibhāsate ।
tathā bhāsana-kāle-api svarūpāt-anivartanam ॥ 101 ॥

satya — true, api — even, aneka — many, vaicitrya — variations, abhāsanena — by shining, vibhāsate — appears, tathā — similarly, bhāsana-kāle — during shining, api — also, svarūpāt — from true form, anivartanam — no deviation.
Even though appearing in many variations, the true form shines. Similarly, during shining, there is no deviation from the true form.
परिच्छेदावभासो यः सोऽनात्माभास उच्यते ।
साऽविद्या जडशक्तिः सा शून्यं प्रकृतिरेव च ॥ १०२ ॥
pariccheda-abhāsah yah sah-anātma-abhāsah ucyate ।
sā-avidyā jaḍa-śaktih sā śūnyam prakṛtih eva ca ॥ 102 ॥

pariccheda-abhāsah — appearance of limitation, yah — which, sah — that, anātma-abhāsah — appearance of the non-self, ucyate — is said, sā — that, avidyā — ignorance, jaḍa-śaktih — inert power, sā — that, śūnyam — void, prakṛtih — nature, eva — indeed, ca — and.
The appearance of limitation, which is said to be the appearance of the non-self, that is ignorance, the inert power, the void, and nature.
अत्यन्ताभाव आकाशस्तमः प्रथमसर्गकः ।
सर्व तदेव सम्प्रोक्तं परिच्छेदनमादिमम्‌ ॥ १०३ ॥
atyanta-abhāva ākāśaḥ-tamah prathama-sargakah ।
sarva tad-eva samproktam paricchedanam-ādimam ॥ 103 ॥

atyanta-abhāva — complete non-existence, ākāśaḥ — space, tamah — darkness, prathama-sargakah — first creation, sarva — all, tad-eva — that indeed, samproktam — said, paricchedanam-ādimam — primary limitation.
Complete non-existence, space, darkness, the first creation, all that indeed is said to be the primary limitation.
राम यः परिपूर्णात्मा विश्रमो वै समास्थितः ।
तस्यैकदेशताभ्रान्तिकृतमाकाशभासनम्‌ ॥ १०४ ॥
rāma yah paripūrṇa-ātmā viśramah vai samāsthitah ।
Tasya-eka-deśatā-bhrānti-kṛtam-ākāśa-bhāsanam ॥ 104 ॥

rāma — O Rāma, yah — which, paripūrṇa-ātmā — complete self, viśramah — rest, vai — indeed, samāsthitah — established, tasya — of that, eka-deśatā-bhrānti — misconception of partiality, kṛtam — created, ākāśa-bhāsanam — appearance of space.
O Rāma, the complete self, indeed, rests established. The misconception of partiality creates the appearance of space.
अतः आत्मप्रदेशो य आत्माभिमतिवर्जितः ।
आकाशः स हि सम्प्रोक्तः स हि संसारकारणम्‌ ॥ १०५ ॥
atah ātma-pradeśo yah ātma-abhimati-varjitah ।
ākāśaḥ sah hi samproktah sah hi saṁsāra-kāraṇam ॥ 105 ॥

atah — therefore, ātma-pradeśo — space of the self, yah — which, ātma-abhimati-varjitah — devoid of self-conception, ākāśaḥ — space, sah — that, hi — indeed, samproktah — is said, sah — that, hi — indeed, saṁsāra-kāraṇam — cause of samsara.
Therefore, the space of the self, which is devoid of self-conception, is said to be space. Indeed, that is the cause of samsara.
एष एव भवेद्‌ भेदः पशुदृष्टयेकगोचरः ।
राम सूक्ष्मदृशा पश्य य आकाशस्त्वयेक्ष्यते ॥ १०६ ॥
eṣa eva bhaved bhedaḥ paśu-dṛṣṭi-ekagoçarah ।
rāma sūkṣma-dṛṣā paśya yah ākāśaḥ tvayā īkṣyate ॥ 106 ॥

eṣa — this, eva — indeed, bhaved — would be, bhedaḥ — distinction, paśu-dṛṣṭi-ekagoçarah — visible to the limited vision, rāma — O Rāma, sūkṣma-dṛṣā — with subtle vision, paśya — see, yah — which, ākāśaḥ — space, tvayā — by you, īkṣyate — seen.
This indeed would be the distinction visible to the limited vision. O Rāma, with subtle vision, see the space that is seen by you.
तत्रत्यजीवराशीनामात्मा चैतन्यमेव सः ।
यथाऽन्यदेहेष्वाकाशो भासते यः सदा तव ॥ १०७ ॥
tatratya-jīva-rāśīnām-ātmā caitanyam-eva sah ।
yathā-anyadeheṣu-ākāśaḥ bhāsate yah sadā tava ॥ 107 ॥

tatratya-jīva-rāśīnām — of the collection of beings there, ātmā — self, caitanyam-eva — pure consciousness, sah — that, yathā — as, anyadeheṣu — in other bodies, ākāśaḥ — space, bhāsate — appears, yah — which, sadā — always, tava — your.
The self of the collection of beings there is pure consciousness, as the space appears in other bodies, which is always your own.
स एव तेषामात्मा स्याच्चिदानन्दघनात्मकः ।
एवं स्वकल्पिताकाशग्रस्तं यच्चिद्वपुः स्थितम्‌ ॥ १०८ ॥
sa eva teṣām ātmā syāt cid-ānanda-ghana-ātmakaḥ ।
evaṁ sva-kalpitā-ākāśa-grastam yat-cid-vapuḥ sthitam ॥ 108 ॥

saḥ — that, eva — indeed, teṣām — of them, ātmā — self, syāt — would be, cid-ānanda-ghana-ātmakaḥ — of the nature of dense consciousness and bliss, evaṁ — thus, sva-kalpitā-ākāśa — self-created space, grastam — pervaded, yat — which, cid-vapuḥ — form of consciousness, sthitam — remains.
That indeed would be their self, of the nature of dense consciousness and bliss. Thus, the form of consciousness remains pervaded by self-created space.
तदेव मन इत्युक्तमात्मैव नहि चेतरत्‌ ।
तत्रावरणमुख्यत्वात्‌ प्रमाणं मन उच्यते ॥ १०९ ॥
tat-eva manaḥ-iti-uktam-ātmā-eva nahi-cetarat ।
Tatra-āvaraṇa-mukhya-tvāt-pramāṇam-manaḥ-ucyate ॥ 109 ॥

tat — that, eva — indeed, manaḥ — mind, iti — thus, uktam — said, ātmā — self, eva — indeed, nahi — not, cetarat — otherwise, tatra — there, āvaraṇa-mukhya-tvāt — due to primary nature of covering, pramāṇam — proof, manaḥ — mind, ucyate — is called.
That indeed is called the mind, said to be the self, not otherwise. There, due to the primary nature of covering, the mind is called proof.
आवृतप्राधान्यतस्तु प्रमाता जीव उच्यते ।
एवमाकाशावृतोऽपि चिदात्मा भूय एव तु ॥ ११० ॥
āvrta-prādhānya-taḥ-tu pramātā jīvaḥ ucyate ।
evam-ākāśa-āvrtaḥ-api cid-ātmā bhūyaḥ eva tu ॥ 110 ॥

āvrta-prādhānya-taḥ — due to the primary nature of covering, tu — indeed, pramātā — knower, jīvaḥ — individual self, ucyate — is called, evam — thus, ākāśa-āvrtaḥ — covered by space, api — also, cid-ātmā — consciousness-self, bhūyaḥ — again, eva — indeed, tu — but.
Due to the primary nature of covering, the knower is called the individual self. Thus, even though covered by space, the consciousness-self is indeed again.
आकाशे कोमलेऽत्यन्तशिथिले निर्घनेऽमले ।
कठिनश्लिष्टघनतामालिन्यानां प्रकल्पनैः ॥ १११ ॥
ākāśe komale-atyanta-śithile nirghane-amale ।
kaṭhina-śliṣṭa-ghana-tāmālinyānām prakalpanaiḥ ॥ 111 ॥

ākāśe — in space, komale — soft, atyanta — extremely, śithile — loose, nirghane — non-dense, amale — pure, kaṭhina-śliṣṭa — hard and attached, ghana-tāmālinyānām — dense and impure, prakalpanaiḥ — by imaginations.
In the soft, extremely loose, non-dense, pure space, through imaginations of hard and attached, dense and impure.
भूतान्याभास्य देहात्मा देहेनापि समावृतः ।
कुम्भोदरगतो दीप उदरं व्याप्य भासते ॥ ११२ ॥
bhūtāni-ābhāsya dehātmā dehena-api samāvṛtaḥ ।
kumbha-udara-gataḥ dīpaḥ udaraṁ vyāpya bhāsate ॥ 112 ॥

bhūtāni — elements, ābhāsya — reflecting, dehātmā — embodied self, dehena — by the body, api — also, samāvṛtaḥ — covered, kumbha-udara-gataḥ — placed inside a pot, dīpaḥ — lamp, udaraṁ — inside, vyāpya — pervading, bhāsate — shines.
Reflecting elements, the embodied self, also covered by the body, shines like a lamp placed inside a pot, pervading the inside.
एवमेष शरीरान्तरवभासनमात्रकः ।
आस्ते गूढप्रदीपात्मा तदन्तर्मात्रभासनः ॥ ११३ ॥
evam-eṣa śarīra-antara-vabhāsana-mātrakaḥ ।
āste gūḍha-pradīpa-ātmā tad-antar-mātra-bhāsanaḥ ॥ 113 ॥

evam — thus, eṣaḥ — this, śarīra-antara-vabhāsana-mātrakaḥ — only reflecting the inner body, āste — remains, gūḍha-pradīpa-ātmā — like a hidden lamp, tat-antar-mātra-bhāsanaḥ — only illuminating the inside.
Thus, this only reflecting the inner body remains, like a hidden lamp, only illuminating the inside.
दीपप्रभा घटच्छिद्राद्यथा निर्याति वै बहिः ।
एवमक्षद्वारमुखाद्‌ भूयो निर्याति वै चितिः ॥ ११४ ॥
dīpa-prabhā ghaṭa-chidra-at-yathā niryāti vai bahiḥ ।
evam-akṣa-dvāra-mukhāt bhūyaḥ niryāti vai citiḥ ॥ 114 ॥

dīpa-prabhā — lamp's light, ghaṭa-chidra — through the pot's hole, yathā — as, niryāti — goes out, vai — indeed, bahiḥ — outside, evam — thus, akṣa-dvāra-mukhāt — through the openings of the senses, bhūyaḥ — again, niryāti — goes out, vai — indeed, citiḥ — consciousness.
As the lamp's light goes out through the pot's hole, indeed, thus, consciousness goes out again through the openings of the senses.
निर्याणं तु चितेर्नास्ति पुर्णत्वादक्रियत्वतः ।
स्वात्मावरणमाकाशं स्फूर्त्तिशक्तिश्चिदात्मनः ॥ ११५ ॥
niryāṇam tu citeḥ nāsti purnatvāt-akriyatvataḥ ।
svātma-āvaraṇam-ākāśam sphūrti-śaktiḥ-cidātmanah ॥ 115 ॥

niryāṇam — going out, tu — indeed, citeḥ — of consciousness, nāsti — does not exist, purnatvāt — due to completeness, akriyatvataḥ — due to non-action, svātma-āvaraṇam — self-covering, ākāśam — space, sphūrti-śaktiḥ — power of manifestation, cidātmanah — of consciousness-self.
Indeed, going out of consciousness does not exist due to its completeness and non-action. The self-covering space, the power of manifestation, is of the consciousness-self.
यावन्निवारयेत्तावद्‌ निर्याणं प्रविभासते ।
मनोव्यापार एष स्यात्‌ स्फूर्त्यापहतिरावृतेः ॥ ९१६ ॥
yāvat-nivārayet-tāvat niryāṇam pravibhāsate ।
mano-vyāpāra eṣa syāt sphūrtyā-apahati-āvṛteḥ ॥ 116 ॥

yāvat — as long as, nivārayet — one restrains, tāvat — until then, niryāṇam — going out, pravibhāsate — appears, mano-vyāpāraḥ — mental activity, eṣaḥ — this, syāt — would be, sphūrtyā — by manifestation, apahati — removal, āvṛteḥ — of the covering.
As long as one restrains, until then, the going out appears. This would be mental activity, the removal of the covering by manifestation.
तस्माद्राम मनो नान्यदात्मैव मन उच्यते ।
चला चितिर्मनोनाम्नी निश्चलात्मस्वरूपिणी ॥ ११७ ॥
tasmāt rāma manaḥ na anyat ātmā eva manaḥ ucyate ।
calā citiḥ mano-nāmnī niścala-ātma-svarūpiṇī ॥ 117 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, rāma — O Rāma, manaḥ — mind, na anyat — not different, ātmā eva — indeed the self, manaḥ ucyate — is called the mind, calā — moving, citiḥ — consciousness, mano-nāmnī — named as mind, niścala — unmoving, ātma-svarūpiṇī — in the form of the self.
Therefore, O Rāma, the mind is not different, indeed the self is called the mind. The moving consciousness named as mind, in the form of the unmoving self.
आवृत्त्यभिहतिः स्फूर्त्या चलनं राम वै चितेः ।
एतदेव विकल्पः स्याद्‌ विकल्पपरिवर्जने ॥ ११८ ॥
āvṛtti-abhiḥatih sphūrtyā calanam rāma vai citeḥ ।
etat-eva vikalpaḥ syāt vikalpa-parivarjane ॥ 118 ॥

āvṛtti — covering, abhihatiḥ — removal, sphūrtyā — by manifestation, calanam — movement, rāma — O Rāma, vai — indeed, citeḥ — of consciousness, etat-eva — this indeed, vikalpaḥ — imagination, syāt — would be, vikalpa-parivarjane — in the absence of imagination.
The removal of the covering by manifestation, indeed the movement of consciousness, O Rāma, this indeed would be imagination, in the absence of imagination.
निर्विकल्पं पूर्णरूपं विज्ञानं मुक्तिनामकम्‌ ।
राम त्यजात्र सन्देहं विकल्पस्य विवर्जने ॥ ११९ ॥
nirvikalpam pūrṇa-rūpam vijñānam mukti-nāmakam ।
rāma tyaja atra sandeham vikalpasya vivarjane ॥ 119 ॥

nirvikalpam — free from imagination, pūrṇa-rūpam — complete form, vijñānam — knowledge, mukti-nāmakam — called liberation, rāma — O Rāma, tyaja — abandon, atra — here, sandeham — doubt, vikalpasya — of imagination, vivarjane — in the absence.
Free from imagination, the complete form of knowledge, called liberation. O Rāma, abandon doubt here, in the absence of imagination.
अप्यावरणशेषः स्यादिति नास्त्येव चावृतिः ।
आवृतिर्नहि सत्याऽस्ति यतः स्वेनैव कल्पिता ॥ १२० ॥
api-āvaraṇa-śeṣaḥ syāt-iti nāsti-eva ca-āvṛtiḥ ।
āvṛtiḥ-na-hi satyā-asti yataḥ svena-eva kalpitā ॥ 120 ॥

api — even, āvaraṇa-śeṣaḥ — remaining covering, syāt — would be, iti — thus, nāsti — does not exist, eva — indeed, ca — and, āvṛtiḥ — covering, na — not, hi — indeed, satyā — true, asti — is, yataḥ — because, svena — by oneself, eva — indeed, kalpitā — imagined.
Even the remaining covering would not exist, thus indeed, the covering is not true, because it is indeed imagined by oneself.
यथा मनोरथे बद्धः केनचिच्छत्रुणा स्वयम्‌ ।
ताड्यमानस्तर्ज्यमानो यावत्‌ सङ्कल्पवर्जनम्‌ ॥ १२१ ॥
yathā manorathe baddhaḥ kenacich-chatruṇā svayam ।
tāḍyamānaḥ tarjyamāno yāvat saṅkalpa-varjanam ॥ 121 ॥

yathā — as, manorathe — in a fantasy, baddhaḥ — bound, kenacit — by some, chatruṇā — enemy, svayam — oneself, tāḍyamānaḥ — being beaten, tarjyamānaḥ — being threatened, yāvat — until, saṅkalpa-varjanam — imagination ceases.
As in a fantasy, bound by some enemy, oneself being beaten and threatened, until imagination ceases.
कुर्यात्तावत्ताडनं वा तर्जनं वापि लीयते ।
कि तत्र शिष्यते बन्धस्तथाऽत्रापि विभावय ॥ १२२ ॥
kuryāt-tāvat-tāḍanam vā tarjanam vā api līyate ।
ki tatra śiṣyate bandhaḥ tathā atra api vibhāvaya ॥ 122 ॥

kuryāt — does, tāvat — until then, tāḍanam — beating, vā — or, tarjanam — threatening, vā — or, api — also, līyate — ceases, ki — what, tatra — there, śiṣyate — remains, bandhaḥ — bondage, tathā — similarly, atra — here, api — also, vibhāvaya — consider.
Until then, the beating or threatening ceases; what remains there of bondage? Similarly, consider here also.
अनादिकालाद्रामात्र बन्धो नास्त्येव कस्यचित्‌ ।
जडात्मभ्रान्तिमुत्सृज्य कोऽयं बन्धो विचारय ॥ १२३ ॥
anādi-kāla-ād-rāma-atra bandhaḥ nāsti-eva kasyacit ।
jaḍa-ātma-bhrāntim utsṛjya kaḥ ayam bandhaḥ vicāraya ॥ 123 ॥

anādi — beginningless, kāla — time, ād — from, rāma — O Rāma, atra — here, bandhaḥ — bondage, nāsti — does not exist, eva — indeed, kasyacit — of anyone, jaḍa-ātma-bhrāntim — delusion of a material self, utsṛjya — giving up, kaḥ — what, ayam — this, bandhaḥ — bondage, vicāraya — consider.
From beginningless time, O Rāma, here bondage does not exist for anyone. Giving up the delusion of a material self, consider what is this bondage.
एष एव महाबन्धो बन्धसत्यत्वनिश्चयः ।
मृषा भीतस्य बालस्य यक्षग्रह इव स्थितः ॥ १२४ ॥
eṣa eva mahā-bandho bandha-satyatva-niścayaḥ ।
mṛṣā bhītasya bālasya yakṣa-graha iva sthitaḥ ॥ 124 ॥

eṣaḥ — this, eva — indeed, mahā-bandhaḥ — great bondage, bandha-satyatva-niścayaḥ — certainty of bondage's reality, mṛṣā — false, bhītasya — of the frightened, bālasya — child, yakṣa-graha — demon possession, iva — like, sthitaḥ — situated.
This indeed is the great bondage, the certainty of bondage's reality. Like the false demon possession of a frightened child, it is situated.
यावद्‌ बन्धभ्रान्तिमेनां नोत्सृजेद्‌ बुद्धिमानपि ।
न तावत्‌ संसृतेर्मुक्तो भवेत्‌ क्वापि महोद्यमैः ॥ १२५ ॥
yāvat bandha-bhrāntim-enāṁ notsṛjed buddhi-mān-api ।
na tāvat saṁsṛteḥ mukto bhavet kvāpi mahā-udyamaiḥ ॥ 125 ॥

yāvat — as long as, bandha-bhrāntim — delusion of bondage, enām — this, na utsṛjet — does not give up, buddhi-mān — wise, api — even, na — not, tāvat — until then, saṁsṛteḥ — from transmigration, muktaḥ — liberated, bhavet — would be, kva-api — anywhere, mahā-udyamaiḥ — by great efforts.
As long as this delusion of bondage is not given up, even a wise person is not liberated from transmigration anywhere, despite great efforts.
कोऽयं बन्धः कथं वा स्यान्निर्मलस्य चिदात्मनः ।
प्रतिबिम्बात्मकैः स्वात्मादर्शान्तःप्रविभावितैः ॥ १२६ ॥
kaḥ ayam bandhaḥ kathaṁ vā syāt nirmalasya cid-ātmanaḥ ।
pratibimba-ātmakaiḥ sva-ātma-ādarsa-antaḥ-pravibhāvitaiḥ ॥ 126 ॥

kaḥ — what, ayam — this, bandhaḥ — bondage, kathaṁ — how, vā — or, syāt — would be, nirmalasya — of the pure, cid-ātmanaḥ — consciousness-self, pratibimba-ātmakaiḥ — by reflections, sva-ātma-ādarsa — in the mirror of one's own self, antaḥ-pravibhāvitaiḥ — conceived internally.
What is this bondage, or how would it exist for the pure consciousness-self, conceived internally by reflections in the mirror of one's own self?
बन्धो यदि तदादर्शप्रतिबिम्बाग्निरादहेत्‌ ।
बन्धस्य सत्यताबुद्धिर्मनसोऽस्तित्वनिश्चयः ॥ १२७ ॥
bandho yadi tat-ādarsa-pratibimba-agniḥ-ādhet ।
bandhasya satyatā-buddhiḥ manasaḥ-asti-tva-niścayaḥ ॥ 127 ॥

bandhaḥ — bondage, yadi — if, tat — that, ādarsa — mirror, pratibimba — reflection, agniḥ — fire, ādhet — would burn, bandhasya — of bondage, satyatā-buddhiḥ — belief in reality, manasaḥ — of the mind, asti-tva-niścayaḥ — certainty of existence.
If bondage were like a fire reflection in a mirror that would burn, then belief in the reality of bondage and the certainty of the mind's existence would be true.
एतद्‌ द्वयमृते नास्ति बन्धः कस्यापि कुत्रचित्‌ ।
यावदेतद्‌ द्वयमलं सद्विचारमहाजलैः ॥ १२८ ॥
etad dvayam-ṛte nāsti bandhaḥ kasyāpi kutracit ।
yāvat-etad dvayam-alam sad-vicāra-mahā-jalaiḥ ॥ 128 ॥

etad — this, dvayam — two things, ṛte — without, nāsti — does not exist, bandhaḥ — bondage, kasyāpi — of anyone, kutracit — anywhere, yāvat — as long as, etad — this, dvayam — two things, alam — sufficiently, sad-vicāra — true reflection, mahā-jalaiḥ — by great waters.
Without these two things, bondage does not exist for anyone anywhere. As long as these two things are sufficiently washed away by the great waters of true reflection.
नोन्मार्जितं तावदिह तस्य संसारनाशने ।
अहं वा ब्रह्यदेवो वा विष्णुर्वापि च शङ्कुर: ॥ १२९ ॥
no unmārjitam tāvat-iha tasya saṁsāra-nāśane ।
ahaṁ vā brahma-devaḥ vā viṣṇuḥ vā api ca śaṁkuraḥ ॥ 129 ॥

no — not, unmārjitam — washed away, tāvat — until then, iha — here, tasya — of that, saṁsāra-nāśane — in the destruction of transmigration, ahaṁ — I, vā — or, brahma-devaḥ — Brahma, vā — or, viṣṇuḥ — Vishnu, vā — or, api — also, ca — and, śaṁkuraḥ — Shankara.
Until then, without being washed away, in the destruction of transmigration, neither I, nor Brahma, nor Vishnu, nor Shankara.
विद्यात्मिका वा त्रिपुरा नैव शक्ताः कथञ्चन ।
तस्माद्राम द्वयं चैतत्‌ परित्यज्य सुखी भव ॥ १३० ॥
vidyā-ātmikā vā tripurā na eva śaktāḥ kathañcana ।
tasmāt rāma dvayam etat parityajya sukhī bhava ॥ 130 ॥

vidyā-ātmikā — embodiment of knowledge, vā — or, tripurā — Tripura, na — not, eva — indeed, śaktāḥ — capable, kathañcana — by any means, tasmāt — therefore, rāma — O Rāma, dvayam — the two, etat — this, parityajya — giving up, sukhī bhava — be happy.
Neither the embodiment of knowledge nor Tripura is capable by any means. Therefore, O Rāma, giving up these two, be happy.
तस्माद्राम निर्विकल्परूपे मनसि संस्थिते ।
आत्ममात्रत्वतस्तस्य द्वैतं न परिशिष्यते ॥ १३१ ॥
tasmāt rāma nirvikalpa-rūpe manasi saṁsthite ।
ātma-mātratvataḥ tasya dvaitaṁ na pariśiṣyate ॥ 131 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, rāma — O Rāma, nirvikalpa-rūpe — in the form of non-duality, manasi — in the mind, saṁsthite — established, ātma-mātratvataḥ — by the nature of the self alone, tasya — of that, dvaitam — duality, na — not, pariśiṣyate — remains.
Therefore, O Rāma, in the mind established in the form of non-duality, by the nature of the self alone, duality does not remain.
इदं तदितिरूपेण भासनान्यन्मनो नहि ।
इदमादिपरित्यागे भासनात्मैव शिष्यते ॥ १३२ ॥
idaṁ tad iti rūpeṇa bhāsanāt yan manaḥ na hi ।
idam-ādi-parityāge bhāsanātmaiva śiṣyate ॥ 132 ॥

idaṁ — this, tad — that, iti — thus, rūpeṇa — in the form, bhāsanāt — from shining, yan — that, manaḥ — mind, na hi — not indeed, idam-ādi-parityāge — in giving up "this" and "that", bhāsanātmā — the essence of shining, eva — indeed, śiṣyate — remains.
From the mind not shining in the form of "this" and "that," in giving up "this" and "that," the essence of shining alone remains.
रज्जुसर्पपरिभ्रान्तिः सत्याभिमतवस्तुनि ।
रज्जुरूपे हि सर्पस्य भासिनीति विनिश्चयः ॥ १३३ ॥
rajju-sarpa-paribhrāntiḥ satya-abhimata-vastuni ।
rajju-rūpe hi sarpasya bhāsinīti viniścayaḥ ॥ 133 ॥

rajju — rope, sarpa — snake, paribhrāntiḥ — confusion, satya — true, abhimata — considered, vastuni — in the object, rajju-rūpe — in the form of the rope, hi — indeed, sarpasya — of the snake, bhāsinī — appears, iti — thus, viniścayaḥ — certainty.
The confusion of the rope and snake, considered true, in the form of the rope, indeed, the snake appears; thus, it is certain.
तत्र सर्पस्य बाधेऽपि रज्ज्वालम्बनहेतुतः ।
चिद्रूपादात्मनोऽन्यत्तु रज्जुज्ञानं स्थितं भवेत्‌ ॥ १३४ ॥
tatra sarpasya bādhe api rajju-ālambana-hetutaḥ ।
cid-rūpād ātmanaḥ anyat tu rajju-jñānaṁ sthitaṁ bhavet ॥ 134 ॥

tatra — there, sarpasya — of the snake, bādhe — in the negation, api — even, rajju — rope, ālambana — support, hetutaḥ — because of, cit-rūpād — from the form of consciousness, ātmanaḥ — of the self, anyat — other, tu — but, rajju-jñānam — knowledge of the rope, sthitam — established, bhavet — would be.
There, even in the negation of the snake, because of the support of the rope, from the form of consciousness, but other than the self, the knowledge of the rope would be established.
सापि रज्जुश्चिति यदा स्वप्नदृष्टान्तकल्पिता ।
रज्जुबाधे हि तज्ज्ञानं कथं शिष्येत्‌ किमाश्रयम्‌ ॥ १३५ ॥
sā api rajjuḥ citi yadā svapna-dṛṣṭānta-kalpitā ।
rajju-bādhe hi tat-jñānaṁ kathaṁ śiṣyet kim-āśrayam ॥ 135 ॥

sā — that, api — also, rajjuḥ — rope, citi — consciousness, yadā — when, svapna-dṛṣṭānta-kalpitā — imagined as a dream example, rajju-bādhe — in the negation of the rope, hi — indeed, tat-jñānam — that knowledge, katham — how, śiṣyet — would remain, kim-āśrayam — with what support.
When the rope itself is imagined as a dream example of consciousness, in the negation of the rope, indeed, how would that knowledge remain, with what support?
तस्माद्‌ दृश्यस्य बाधे तु तज्ज्ञानं केवला हि दृक्‌ ।
चिदात्मानतिरिक्तत्वाद्‌ द्वैतं तेन कथं भवेत्‌ ॥ १३६ ॥
tasmād dṛśyasya bādhe tu tat-jñānaṁ kevalā hi dṛk ।
cid-ātma-anatiriktatvād dvaitaṁ tena kathaṁ bhavet ॥ 136 ॥

tasmād — therefore, dṛśyasya — of the visible, bādhe — in the negation, tu — but, tat-jñānam — that knowledge, kevalā — only, hi — indeed, dṛk — seeing, cid-ātma — consciousness-self, anatiriktatvāt — because of non-separation, dvaitam — duality, tena — by that, katham — how, bhavet — would be.
Therefore, in the negation of the visible, that knowledge only remains as seeing. Because of non-separation from the consciousness-self, by that, how would there be duality?
अर्थक्रिया हि संदृष्टा स्वप्नवस्तुषु सुस्थिरा ।
स्वाप्नवस्तु स्थिरमिति स्वप्ने सर्वैर्विभावितम्‌ ॥ १३७ ॥
artha-kriyā hi sandṛṣṭā svapna-vastuṣu susthirā ।
svāpna-vastu sthiram iti svapne sarvaiḥ vibhāvitam ॥ 137 ॥

artha-kriyā — practical activity, hi — indeed, sandṛṣṭā — seen, svapna-vastuṣu — in dream objects, susthirā — stable, svāpna-vastu — dream objects, sthiram — stable, iti — thus, svapne — in a dream, sarvaiḥ — by all, vibhāvitam — considered.
Indeed, practical activity is seen as stable in dream objects. Dream objects are considered stable by all in a dream.
एतावानेव भेदः स्यात्‌ स्वप्नजाग्रद्विभासयोः ।
जाग्रति स्वप्नमिथ्यात्वनिंश्चयो भवति ध्रुवम्‌ ॥ १३८ ॥
etāvān eva bhedaḥ syāt svapna-jāgrat-vibhāsayoḥ ।
jāgrati svapna-mithyātva-niścayaḥ bhavati dhruvam ॥ 138 ॥

etāvān — this much, eva — indeed, bhedaḥ — difference, syāt — would be, svapna — dream, jāgrat — waking, vibhāsayoḥ — in the perceptions, jāgrati — in waking, svapna-mithyātva — falseness of the dream, niścayaḥ — certainty, bhavati — becomes, dhruvam — definite.
This much indeed is the difference in the perceptions of dream and waking: In waking, the certainty of the dream's falseness becomes definite.
स्वप्ने न जायते जाग्रन्मिथ्यात्वस्य विनिर्णयः ।
नैतावतैव सत्यत्वं जाग्रद्व्यवहृतेर्भवेत्‌ ॥ १३९ ॥
svapne na jāyate jāgrat-mithyā-tvasya viniścayaḥ ।
na etāvat eva satyatvaṁ jāgrat-vyavahṛteḥ bhavet ॥ 139 ॥

svapne — in a dream, na — not, jāyate — arises, jāgrat — waking, mithyā-tvasya — falseness, viniścayaḥ — certainty, na — not, etāvat — this much, eva — indeed, satyatvam — reality, jāgrat-vyavahṛteḥ — of waking activity, bhavet — would be.
In a dream, the certainty of the waking's falseness does not arise. This much alone would not determine the reality of waking activity.
यथा जाग्रति वस्तूनां स्थिरतार्थक्रियापि च ।
दृश्यते किं तथा स्वप्ने दृश्यते नहि वा वद ॥ १४० ॥
yathā jāgrati vastu-nāṁ sthiratā-artha-kriyā api ca ।
dṛśyate kiṁ tathā svapne dṛśyate nahi vā vada ॥ 140 ॥

yathā — as, jāgrati — in waking, vastu-nāṁ — of objects, sthiratā — stability, artha-kriyā — practical activity, api — also, ca — and, dṛśyate — is seen, kiṁ — what, tathā — thus, svapne — in a dream, dṛśyate — is seen, nahi — not, vā — or, vada — tell.
As in waking, the stability and practical activity of objects are seen, is it seen thus in a dream or not? Tell.

अर्थक्रियाकरा वापि स्थिरा वा भान्ति तत्समम्‌ ॥ ९४१ ॥
na svapne jāgarā bhāvāḥ svāpnā vā naiva jāgare ।
artha-kriyā-karā vā api sthirā vā bhānti tat-samam ॥ 141 ॥

na — not, svapne — in a dream, jāgarā — waking, bhāvāḥ — states, svāpnā — dream, vā — or, na — not, eva — indeed, jāgare — in waking, artha-kriyā-karā — causing practical activity, vā — or, api — also, sthirā — stable, vā — or, bhānti — appear, tat-samam — similarly.
In a dream, waking states do not appear, and dream states do not appear in waking. Practical activity or stability also do not appear similarly.
विभावय सूक्ष्मदृशा को भेदोऽतीतस्वप्नयोः ।
पश्यैन्द्रजालिककृते स्थैर्यमर्थक्रियामपि ॥ १४२ ॥
vibhāvaya sūkṣma-dṛśā ko bhedo 'tīta-svapnayoḥ ।
paśya-indrajāla-kṛte sthairyām artha-kriyām api ॥ 142 ॥

Consider with subtle vision, what is the difference between past and dream? See the stability and practical activity created by magic.

सत्यासत्यविभागो वै प्राकृतैर्विदितो नहि ॥ १४३ ॥
kiṁ tāvataiva tat satyam aindrajālika-nirmitam ।

What, then, is only true, created by magic? The distinction between true and false is not known by ordinary people.
अत एव मोहितास्ते प्रोचुः सत्यं हि जागतम्‌ ।
कदाप्यभावासंस्पृष्टं सत्यं राम प्रचक्षते ॥ १४४ ॥
ata eva mohitās te procuḥ satyaṁ hi jāgatam ।
kadā api abhāva-asaṁspṛṣṭaṁ satyaṁ rāma pracakṣate ॥ 144 ॥

ata eva — therefore, mohitāḥ — deluded, te — they, procuḥ — say, satyam — true, hi — indeed, jāgatam — the world, kadā api — at any time, abhāva-asaṁspṛṣṭam — untouched by non-existence, satyam — true, rāma — O Rama, pracakṣate — declare.
Therefore, the deluded ones say the world is true. O Rama, they declare it to be true, untouched by non-existence at any time.
अभावः स्यादभानाद्वै त्वभानं न चितेः क्वचित्‌ ।
अभानमचितामस्ति ह्यनेकत्वावभासतः ॥ १४५ ॥
abhāvaḥ syāt abhānāt vai tu abhānaṁ na citeḥ kvacit ।
abhānam acitām asti hi anekatva-avabhāsataḥ ॥ 145 ॥

Non-existence would be from non-appearance, indeed, but non-appearance is never of consciousness anywhere. Non-appearance is of the insentient, indeed, from the appearance of multiplicity.
परस्पराभावभासा अचिद्भावा हि सर्वथा ।
चिदभानं कदा कुत्र स्याद्‌ राम प्रविचारय ॥ १४६ ॥
paraspara-abhāva-bhāsāḥ acit-bhāvāḥ hi sarvathā ।
cit-abhānaṁ kadā kutra syāt rāma pravicāraya ॥ 146 ॥

paraspara-abhāva-bhāsāḥ — appearing as mutual non-existence, acit-bhāvāḥ — insentient states, hi — indeed, sarvathā — always, cit-abhānam — non-appearance of consciousness, kadā — when, kutra — where, syāt — would be, rāma — O Rama, pravicāraya — consider.
Insentient states always appear as mutual non-existence. O Rama, consider when and where the non-appearance of consciousness would be.
यदा चितिर्न भायाद्वै तदा भायात्‌ कथं वद ।
न भायाद्वा कथं भायादभाने यदि तद्द्वयोः ॥ १४७ ॥
yadā citir na bhāyād vai tadā bhāyāt kathaṁ vada ।
na bhāyād vā kathaṁ bhāyāt abhāne yadi tad-dvayoḥ ॥ 147 ॥

yadā — when, citir — consciousness, na bhāyād — does not appear, vai — indeed, tadā — then, bhāyāt — would appear, kathaṁ — how, vada — tell, na bhāyād — does not appear, vā — or, kathaṁ — how, bhāyāt — would appear, abhāne — in non-appearance, yadi — if, tad-dvayoḥ — of the two.
When consciousness does not appear, then how would it appear? Tell. If it does not appear, how would it appear in non-appearance of the two?
राम भायादेव चितिस्तस्मात्‌ सत्यैव सा चितिः ।
राम सत्यासत्यभेदं शृणु संक्षेपतो ब्रुवे ॥ १४८ ॥
rāma bhāyāt eva citis tasmāt satya eva sā citiḥ ।
rāma satya-asatya-bhedaṁ śṛṇu saṅkṣepato bruve ॥ 148 ॥

rāma — O Rama, bhāyāt — appears, eva — indeed, citis — consciousness, tasmāt — therefore, satya — true, eva — indeed, sā — it, citiḥ — consciousness, rāma — O Rama, satya-asatya-bhedaṁ — the distinction between true and false, śṛṇu — listen, saṅkṣepato — briefly, bruve — I tell.
O Rama, consciousness indeed appears; therefore, it is true. O Rama, listen, I briefly tell the distinction between true and false.
अन्यानपेक्षभासं स्यात्‌ सत्यमन्यदसत्यकम्‌ ।
अन्यथा रज्जुसर्पाद्यमपि सत्यं भवेन्ननु ॥ १४९ ॥
anyān-apekṣa-bhāsaṁ syāt satyam anyat asatyakam ।
anyathā rajju-sarpa-ādyam api satyaṁ bhavet nanu ॥ 149 ॥

What appears independently would be true; other things would be false. Otherwise, the rope-snake and the like would also be true, indeed.
बाधो ह्यभावविज्ञानं तद्भावेऽपि हि सम्भवेत्‌ ।
अभावे भावविज्ञानमपि सम्भवति स्फुटम्‌ ॥ १५० ॥
bādho hi abhāva-vijñānaṁ tad-bhāve api hi sambhavet ।
abhāve bhāva-vijñānam api sambhavati sphuṭam ॥ 150 ॥

bādho — negation, hi — indeed, abhāva-vijñānaṁ — knowledge of non-existence, tad-bhāve — in its existence, api — also, hi — indeed, sambhavet — would happen, abhāve — in non-existence, bhāva-vijñānam — knowledge of existence, api — also, sambhavati — happens, sphuṭam — clearly.
Negation, indeed, is knowledge of non-existence, and it would happen in its existence. In non-existence, knowledge of existence also happens clearly.
ततो न बाधितं सत्यमसत्यं बाधितं भवेत्‌ ।
इति पक्षो न युक्तः स्यात्‌ सर्वथा व्यभिचारतः ॥ १५१ ॥
tato na bādhitaṁ satyam asatyam bādhitaṁ bhavet ।
iti pakṣo na yuktaḥ syāt sarvathā vyabhicārataḥ ॥ 151 ॥

Therefore, the view that what is not negated is true and what is negated is false is not reasonable due to inconsistency in all ways.
चितोऽभाने न किञ्चित्‌ स्यान्न स्यात्तदपि सर्वथा ।
तस्माद्यश्चिन्न भातीति वदेत्‌ तार्किकसत्खरः ॥ १५२ ॥
cito 'bhāne na kiñcit syān na syāt tad api sarvathā ।
tasmād yaḥ cit na bhātīti vadet tārkika-satkharaḥ ॥ 152 ॥

cito — of consciousness, abhāne — in non-appearance, na kiñcit — nothing, syāt — would be, na syāt — would not be, tad api — that also, sarvathā — in all ways, tasmād — therefore, yaḥ — who, cit — consciousness, na bhāti — does not appear, iti — thus, vadet — would say, tārkika-satkharaḥ — logician mule.
In the non-appearance of consciousness, nothing would be, and that also would not be in all ways. Therefore, the logician mule who would say that consciousness does not appear...
स ब्रूयान्नाहमस्मीति तत्र केन किमुच्यते ।
यस्यात्मनि स्यात्‌ सन्देहो भानाभावेन सर्वदा ॥ १५३ ॥
sa brūyān na aham asmi iti tatra kena kim ucyate ।
yasya ātmani syāt sandehaḥ bhāna-abhāvena sarvadā ॥ 153 ॥

He would say, "I am not." Thus, there, by whom, what is said? Whose doubt in the self would always be by the non-appearance of consciousness?

तदा गण्डशिलाऽप्येषाऽप्यन्यमोहं विनाशयेत्‌ ॥ १५४ ॥
so 'nyeṣāṁ nāśayet mohaṁ nipuṇaiḥ tarka-gumphanair ।
tadā gaṇḍa-śilā api eṣā api anya-mohaṁ vināśayet ॥ 154 ॥

He would destroy the delusion of others by skillful arguments. Then, this rock would also destroy another's delusion.

सर्वमेव हि विज्ञानं भ्रान्तिरेव न संशयः ॥ १५५ ॥
tasmād artha-kriyā-bhāsa-mātreṇa nahi satyatā ।
sarvam eva hi vijñānaṁ bhrāntiḥ eva na saṁśayaḥ ॥ 155 ॥

Therefore, by the mere appearance of practical activity, there is not truth. All knowledge indeed is delusion, no doubt.

यथा हि बाधविज्ञानात्‌ पूर्वं भ्रान्तिर्भवेत्तथा ॥ १५६ ॥
apareyaṁ mahā-bhrāntiḥ teṣu abhrāntatva-niścayaḥ ।
yathā hi bādha-vijñānāt pūrvaṁ bhrāntiḥ bhavet tathā ॥ 156 ॥

This great delusion in them is the certainty of non-delusion. Indeed, as delusion would first be from the knowledge of negation, thus.

यथा च रजतज्ञानं शुक्तिज्ञानाद्‌ भ्रमात्मकम्‌ ॥ १५७ ॥
sarva-jāgata-vijñānaṁ abhrāntiḥ iva hi sthitam ।
yathā ca rajata-jñānaṁ śukti-jñānāt bhrama-ātmakam ॥ 157 ॥

All worldly knowledge is established as if non-delusion. Indeed, as the knowledge of silver from the knowledge of shell is of the nature of delusion.

नभोनीलभ्रमः सर्वसमानो भासते तथा ॥ १५८ ॥
evaṁ cida-ātma-vijñānāt sarvaṁ jñānaṁ bhrama-ātmakam ।
nabhaḥ-nīla-bhramaḥ sarva-samānaḥ bhāsate tathā ॥ 158 ॥

evaṁ — thus, cida-ātma-vijñānāt — from the knowledge of the consciousness self, sarvaṁ — all, jñānaṁ — knowledge, bhrama-ātmakam — of the nature of delusion, nabhaḥ-nīla-bhramaḥ — delusion of the blue sky, sarva-samānaḥ — similar to all, bhāsate — appears, tathā — thus.
Thus, from the knowledge of the consciousness self, all knowledge is of the nature of delusion. The delusion of the blue sky appears similarly to all.
जागतो भ्रम एष स्यात्‌ सर्वेषां दोषहेतुतः ।
अभ्रान्तिः शुद्धविज्ञानं यच्चिदात्मतया स्थितम्‌ ॥ १५९ ॥
jāgataḥ bhrama eṣa syāt sarveṣāṁ doṣa-hetutaḥ ।
abhrāntiḥ śuddha-vijñānaṁ yat cida-ātmatayā sthitam ॥ 159 ॥

jāgataḥ — of the waking state, bhramaḥ — delusion, eṣaḥ — this, syāt — would be, sarveṣāṁ — of all, doṣa-hetutaḥ — cause of defects, abhrāntiḥ — non-delusion, śuddha-vijñānaṁ — pure knowledge, yat — which, cida-ātmatayā — as the consciousness self, sthitam — established.
This delusion of the waking state would be the cause of defects for all. Non-delusion, pure knowledge, is established as the consciousness self.
एवमेतत्त्वया पृष्टं प्रोक्तं युक्त्यनुसङ्गतम्‌ ।
सन्देहमत्र सन्त्यज्य राम प्रोक्तं विनिश्चिनु ॥ १६० ॥
evam etat tvayā pṛṣṭaṁ proktaṁ yukti-anusaṅgatam ।
sandeham atra santyajya rāma proktaṁ viniścinu ॥ 160 ॥

evam — thus, etat — this, tvayā — by you, pṛṣṭam — asked, proktam — spoken, yukti-anusaṅgatam — consistent with reason, sandeham — doubt, atra — here, santyajya — abandoning, rāma — O Rama, proktam — spoken, viniścinu — determine.
Thus, this which was asked by you has been spoken, consistent with reason. O Rama, abandon doubt here and determine what has been spoken.
कथ मुक्ते व्यवहृतिरिति पृष्टं पुरा तु यत्‌ ।
तत्ते प्रवक्ष्यामि राम शृणु सम्यक्‌ समाहितः ॥ १६१ ॥
katha mukte vyavahṛtir iti pṛṣṭaṁ purā tu yat ।
tatte pravakṣyāmi rāma śṛṇu samyak samāhitaḥ ॥ 161 ॥

katha — how, mukte — for the liberated, vyavahṛtiḥ — conduct, iti — thus, pṛṣṭam — was asked, purā — before, tu — indeed, yat — which, tat — that, te — to you, pravakṣyāmi — I will explain, rāma — O Rama, śṛṇu — listen, samyak — attentively, samāhitaḥ — with concentration.
How is the conduct of the liberated? This was asked before. I will explain that to you, O Rama. Listen attentively with concentration.

प्रारब्धोपनतैर्भोगैः खिद्यमानाः क्षणे क्षणे ॥ १६२ ॥
muktā hi jñānino loke hy uttama-adhama-madhyamāḥ ।
prārabdho-panatair bhogaiḥ khidyamānāḥ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe ॥ 162 ॥

muktāḥ — the liberated, hi — indeed, jñāninaḥ — the wise, loke — in the world, hi — indeed, uttama-adhama-madhyamāḥ — best, worst, and middling, prārabdha-upanataiḥ — by experiences due to past karma, bhogaiḥ — by enjoyments, khidyamānāḥ — being afflicted, kṣaṇe kṣaṇe — moment by moment.
The liberated wise in the world are of three types: best, worst, and middling. They are afflicted moment by moment by experiences due to past karma.

ये तु प्रारब्धसंप्राप्तान्‌ भुञ्जाना अपि नो विदुः ॥ १६३ ॥
svarūpa-jñās tu ye rāma te manda-jñāninaḥ smṛtāḥ ।
ye tu prārabdha-saṁprāptān bhuñjānā api no viduḥ ॥ 163 ॥

svarūpa-jñāḥ — those who know their true nature, tu — indeed, ye — who, rāma — O Rama, te — they, manda-jñāninaḥ — dull-witted, smṛtāḥ — are considered, ye — who, tu — indeed, prārabdha-saṁprāptān — what comes from past karma, bhuñjānāḥ — experiencing, api — even, naḥ viduḥ — do not know.
Those who know their true nature, O Rama, are considered dull-witted if they do not recognize what comes from past karma even while experiencing it.
मधुक्षीबा रसमिव मध्यास्ते ज्ञानिनः स्मृताः ।
ये तु प्रारब्धकोटीनां फलैरपि विचित्रितैः ॥ १६४ ॥
madhu-kṣībā rasam iva madhyās te jñāninaḥ smṛtāḥ ।
ye tu prārabdha-koṭīnām phalair api vicitritaiḥ ॥ 164 ॥

madhu-kṣībāḥ — like intoxicated by honey, rasam — taste, iva — like, madhyāḥ — middling, te — they, jñāninaḥ — wise, smṛtāḥ — are considered, ye — who, tu — indeed, prārabdha-koṭīnām — of numerous past actions, phalaiḥ — by fruits, api — even, vicitritaiḥ — by varied.
The middling wise are considered like those intoxicated by the taste of honey. They, too, are influenced by the varied fruits of numerous past actions.
न स्वस्थितेः प्रच्यवन्ते नोद्विजन्त्यापदां गणैः ।
न विस्मयन्ति चाश्चर्यैर्न हृष्यन्ति महासुखैः ॥ १६५ ॥
na svasthiteḥ pracyavante nodvijanty āpadāṁ gaṇaiḥ ।
na vismayanti cāścaryair na hṛṣyanti mahā-sukhaiḥ ॥ 165 ॥

na — not, svasthiteḥ — from their true nature, pracyavante — they deviate, na — not, udvijanti — they are perturbed, āpadāṁ gaṇaiḥ — by groups of calamities, na — not, vismayanti — they are amazed, ca — and, āścaryaiḥ — by wonders, na — not, hṛṣyanti — they rejoice, mahā-sukhaiḥ — in great pleasures.
They do not deviate from their true nature, nor are they perturbed by groups of calamities. They are neither amazed by wonders nor do they rejoice in great pleasures.
अन्तःशान्ता बहिर्लोकसमास्ते ज्ञानिषूत्तमाः ।
एवं बुद्धिविभेदेन ज्ञानपाकविभेदतः ॥ १६६ ॥
antaḥ-śāntā bahiḥ-loka-samās te jñāniṣu uttamāḥ ।
evaṁ buddhi-vibhedena jñāna-pāka-vibhedataḥ ॥ 166 ॥

antaḥ-śāntāḥ — inwardly peaceful, bahiḥ-loka-samāḥ — outwardly ordinary, te — they, jñāniṣu — among the wise, uttamāḥ — best, evaṁ — thus, buddhi-vibhedena — by difference in intellect, jñāna-pāka-vibhedataḥ — by difference in maturity of knowledge.
The best among the wise are inwardly peaceful and outwardly ordinary. Thus, by the difference in intellect and maturity of knowledge...
प्रारब्धशेषमाहात्म्याद्‌ व्यवहारा विचित्रिताः ।
मधुमत्तादिवत्तेषां व्यवहारोऽपि सम्भवेत्‌ ॥ १६७ ॥
prārabdha-śeṣa-māhātmyād vyavahārā vicitritāḥ ।
madhu-mattā-divat teṣāṁ vyavahāraḥ api sambhavet ॥ 167 ॥

prārabdha-śeṣa-māhātmyāt — due to the grandeur of remaining prārabdha (past karma), vyavahārāḥ — conduct, vicitritāḥ — varied, madhu-mattā-divat — like one intoxicated by honey, teṣāṁ — their, vyavahāraḥ — conduct, api — also, sambhavet — may happen.
Due to the grandeur of remaining prārabdha, their conduct is varied. Their conduct may happen like that of one intoxicated by honey.

colophon.en: Thus ends the eighteenth chapter named "Knowledge Section" in the revered Tripura Rahasya.

lines.text: इति दत्तात्रेयमुखाच्छ्रुत्वा भार्गवनन्दनः ।
भूयः पप्रच्छ मुक्तानां व्यवहारक्रमं क्रमात्‌ ॥ १ ॥
iti dattātreya-mukhāc chrutvā bhārgava-nandanaḥ ।
bhūyaḥ papraccha muktānāṁ vyavahāra-kramaṁ kramāt ॥ 1 ॥

iti — thus, dattātreya-mukhāt — from the mouth of Dattatreya, śrutvā — hearing, bhārgava-nandanaḥ — the son of Bhrigu, bhūyaḥ — again, papraccha — asked, muktānām — of the liberated, vyavahāra-kramam — conduct and works, kramāt — gradually.
Thus, having heard from the mouth of Dattatreya, the son of Bhrigu again asked about the conduct and works of the liberated, gradually.
भगवन्‌ भूय एतन्मे विस्तरेण निरूपय ।
यथा बुद्धिविभेदेन ज्ञानपाकविचित्रता ॥ २ ॥
bhagavan bhūya etan me vistareṇa nirūpaya ।
yathā buddhi-vibhedena jñāna-pāka-vicitratā ॥ 2 ॥

bhagavan — O Lord, bhūyaḥ — again, etat — this, me — to me, vistareṇa — in detail, nirūpaya — explain, yathā — as, buddhi-vibhedena — by difference in intellect, jñāna-pāka-vicitratā — varied ripeness of knowledge.
O Lord, please explain to me in detail how the varied ripeness of knowledge arises due to differences in intellect.
ज्ञानं त्वेकविधं स्वात्ममात्रभानात्मकं ननु ।
उपेयं च तदेव स्याद्यन्मोक्षस्तत्प्रथात्मकः ॥ ३ ॥
jñānaṁ tv eka-vidhaṁ svātma-mātra-bhānātmakaṁ nanu ।
upeyaṁ ca tad eva syād yan mokṣas tat-prathātmakaḥ ॥ 3 ॥

jñānam — knowledge, tu — indeed, eka-vidham — of one kind, svātma-mātra-bhāna-ātmakam — consisting of the awareness of one's self alone, nanu — isn't it, upeyam — goal, ca — and, tat — that, eva — indeed, syāt — should be, yat — which, mokṣaḥ — liberation, tat-prathātmakaḥ — consisting of its manifestation.
Knowledge is indeed of one kind, consisting of the awareness of one's self alone. Isn't that the goal that which consists of its manifestation known as liberation?
तत्‌ कथं बुद्धिभेदेन पाकभेदसमाश्रयम्‌ ।
साधनान्यपि भिद्यन्तेऽथवा नेति तदीरय ॥ ४ ॥
tat kathaṁ buddhi-bhedena pāka-bheda-samāśrayam ।
sādhanāny api bhidyante 'thavā neti tad īraya ॥ 4 ॥

tat — that, katham — how, buddhi-bhedena — by difference in intellect, pāka-bheda-samāśrayam — depending on differences in ripeness, sādhanāni — practices, api — also, bhidyante — differ, athavā — or, na — not, iti — thus, tad — that, īraya — explain.
How, then, can there be dependence on differences in ripeness by the difference in intellect? Do practices differ or not? Explain that.
इति पृष्टः पुनस्तेन दत्तात्रेयो दयानिधिः ।
विस्तरेण तमेवार्थं प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमे ॥ ५ ॥
iti pṛṣṭaḥ punas tena dattātreyo dayānidhiḥ ।
vistareṇa tam eva arthaṁ pravaktum upacakrame ॥ 5 ॥

iti — thus, pṛṣṭaḥ — asked, punaḥ — again, tena — by him, dattātreyaḥ — Dattatreya, dayā-nidhiḥ — ocean of compassion, vistareṇa — in detail, tam — that, eva — indeed, arthaṁ — matter, pravaktum — to explain, upacakrame — began.
Thus asked again by him, Dattatreya, the ocean of compassion, began to explain that matter in detail.
शृणु राम प्रवक्ष्यामि रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम्‌ ।
साधने न विभेदोऽस्ति ज्ञानं न चित्रसाधनम्‌ ॥ ६ ॥
śṛṇu rāma pravakṣyāmi rahasyaṁ hy etad uttamam ।
sādhane na vibhedo 'sti jñānaṁ na citra-sādhanam ॥ 6 ॥

śṛṇu — listen, rāma — O Rama, pravakṣyāmi — I will explain, rahasyam — secret, hi — indeed, etat — this, uttamam — supreme, sādhane — in practice, na — not, vibhedaḥ — difference, asti — is, jñānam — knowledge, na — not, citra-sādhanam — various practices.
Listen, O Rama, I will explain this supreme secret. There is no difference in practice, and knowledge is not achieved through various practices.
तारतम्यात्‌ साधनानां फलप्राप्तिर्विभेदिता ।
पूर्णे तु साधने ज्ञानमनायासेन सिद्धयति ॥ ७ ॥
tāratamyāt sādhanānāṁ phala-prāptir vibheditā ।
pūrṇe tu sādhane jñānam anāyāsena siddhyati ॥ 7 ॥

tāratamyāt — by the gradation, sādhanānām — of practices, phala-prāptiḥ — attainment of fruit, vibheditā — difference, pūrṇe — complete, tu — indeed, sādhane — practice, jñānam — knowledge, anāyāsena — effortlessly, siddhyati — is attained.
The attainment of fruit varies by the gradation of practices. When the practice is complete, knowledge is effortlessly attained.
अपूर्तितारतम्येन त्वया सात्वायासापेक्षणाद्भवेत्‌ ।
वस्तुतः साधनं किञ्चिद्‌ ज्ञाने नैवोपयुज्यते ॥ ८ ॥
apūrti-tāratamyena tvayā sāt vāyāsāpekṣaṇād bhavet ।
vastutaḥ sādhanam kiñcid jñāne naiva upayujyate ॥ 8 ॥

apūrti-tāratamyena — by the incompleteness of gradation, tvayā — by you, sāt — effort, vāyāsāpekṣaṇāt — requiring, bhavet — may be, vastutaḥ — essentially, sādhanam — practice, kiñcit — anything, jñāne — in knowledge, naiva — not at all, upayujyate — is utilized.
By the incompleteness of gradation, effort may be required. Essentially, no practice is utilized in knowledge.
ज्ञानं क्वचिन्नैव साध्यं सिद्धत्वात्तु स्वभावतः ।
चैतन्यमेव विज्ञानं तत्‌ सदा स्वप्रकाशकम्‌ ॥ ९ ॥
jñānaṁ kvacin naiva sādhyaṁ siddhatvāt tu svabhāvataḥ ।
caitanyam eva vijñānaṁ tat sadā sva-prakāśakam ॥ 9 ॥

jñānam — knowledge, kvacit — anywhere, naiva — not at all, sādhyaṁ — achievable, siddhatvāt — due to being accomplished, tu — indeed, svabhāvataḥ — by nature, caitanyam — consciousness, eva — indeed, vijñānam — knowledge, tat — that, sadā — always, sva-prakāśakam — self-luminous.
Knowledge is not achievable anywhere, as it is accomplished by nature. Consciousness itself is knowledge, always self-luminous.
तत्र का साधनापेक्षा नित्यभानस्वरूपके ।
चैतन्यं निहितं चित्तकरण्डेऽतिसुनिर्मले ॥ १० ॥
tatra kā sādhanā-apekṣā nitya-bhāna-svarūpake ।
caitanyam nihitaṁ citta-karaṇḍe 'ti-sunirmale ॥ 10 ॥

tatra — there, kā — what, sādhanā-apekṣā — need for practice, nitya-bhāna-svarūpake — in the eternally luminous nature, caitanyam — consciousness, nihitam — placed, citta-karaṇḍe — in the casket of the mind, ati-sunirmale — very pure.
What need is there for practice for the eternally luminous nature? Consciousness is placed in the very pure casket of the mind.
अनन्तवासनापङ्कमग्नं नैवोपलक्ष्यते ।
निरोधसलिलैः सम्यग्‌ वासनापङ्कमार्जने ॥ ११ ॥
ananta-vāsanā-paṅka-magnaṁ naiva upalakṣyate ।
nirodha-salilaiḥ samyag vāsanā-paṅka-mārjane ॥ 11 ॥

ananta-vāsanā-paṅka-magnam — submerged in the mire of infinite impressions, naiva — not at all, upalakṣyate — perceived, nirodha-salilaiḥ — by the waters of restraint, samyak — properly, vāsanā-paṅka-mārjane — in the cleansing of the mire of impressions.
Submerged in the mire of infinite impressions, it is not perceived. By the waters of restraint, the mire of impressions is properly cleansed.
विचारशितयन्त्रेण यत्नाच्चित्तकरण्डके ।
चिरात्‌ संघटिते राम सुयुक्त्योद्‌घाटिते ततः ॥ १२ ॥
vicāra-śita-yantrena yatnāc citta-karaṇḍake ।
cirāt saṁghaṭite rāma su-yuktya udghāṭite tataḥ ॥ 12 ॥

vicāra-śita-yantrena — by the sharp instrument of inquiry, yatnāt — with effort, citta-karaṇḍake — in the casket of the mind, cirāt — after a long time, saṁghaṭite — assembled, rāma — O Rama, su-yuktyā — by proper reasoning, udghāṭite — opened, tataḥ — then.
By the sharp instrument of inquiry and with effort, in the casket of the mind, after a long time, assembled, O Rama, by proper reasoning, it is then opened.
भासमानं तु मणिवच्चैतन्यमुपलभ्यते ।
राम तस्माद्‌ वासनानां निरासे साधनं स्मृतम्‌ ॥ १३ ॥
bhāsamānaṁ tu maṇivat caitanyam upalabhyate ।
rāma tasmād vāsanānāṁ nirāse sādhanaṁ smṛtam ॥ 13 ॥

bhāsamānam — shining, tu — indeed, maṇivat — like a jewel, caitanyam — consciousness, upalabhyate — is perceived, rāma — O Rama, tasmāt — therefore, vāsanānāṁ — of impressions, nirāse — in the removal, sādhanaṁ — practice, smṛtam — is remembered.
Shining like a jewel, consciousness is perceived. Therefore, O Rama, practice is remembered in the removal of impressions alone.
वासना ल्पाधिक्यभावाद्‌ बुद्धिस्तु विविधा भवेत्‌ ।
यस्य यावद्‌ वासनौघो बुद्धिमाच्छाद्य संस्थितः ॥ १४ ॥
vāsanālpa-adhikya-bhāvād buddhis tu vividhā bhavet ।
yasya yāvad vāsanaugho buddhim āchādya saṁsthitaḥ ॥ 14 ॥

vāsanā-alpa-adhikya-bhāvāt — due to the presence of few or many impressions, buddhiḥ — intellect, tu — indeed, vividhā — varied, bhavet — becomes, yasya — whose, yāvat — as much, vāsanaughaḥ — flow of impressions, buddhim — intellect, āchādya — covering, saṁsthitaḥ — remains.
Due to the presence of few or many impressions, the intellect becomes varied. As much as the flow of impressions covers the intellect, it remains.
साधनापेक्षणं तस्य तावदेव भृगूद्वह ।
वासना विविधाः प्रोक्तास्तत्र मुख्या वदामि ते ॥ १५ ॥
sādhana-apekṣaṇaṁ tasya tāvad eva bhṛgūd-vaha ।
vāsanā vividhāḥ proktās tatra mukhyā vadāmi te ॥ 15 ॥

sādhana-apekṣaṇam — need for practice, tasya — his, tāvat — as much, eva — indeed, bhṛgūdvaha — O son of Bhrigu, vāsanāḥ — impressions, vividhāḥ — varied, proktāḥ — are said, tatra — there, mukhyā — chief, vadāmi — I will tell, te — to you.
The need for practice is as much as for the impressions covering one’s intellect, O son of Bhrigu. Varied impressions are said to be there; I will tell you the chief ones.
अपराधकर्मकामभेदेन त्रिविधा हि सा ।
अश्रद्धैवापराधः स्याद्‌ मुख्यः स्वात्मविनारनः ॥ १६ ॥
aparādha-karma-kāma-bhedena tri-vidhā hi sā ।
aśraddhā eva aparādhaḥ syād mukhyaḥ svātma-vināśanaḥ ॥ 16 ॥

aparādha-karma-kāma-bhedena — by the distinction of fault, action, and desire, tri-vidhā — threefold, hi — indeed, sā — that, aśraddhā — lack of faith, eva — indeed, aparādhaḥ — fault, syāt — may be, mukhyaḥ — chief, svātma-vināśanaḥ — destroying one's self.
By the distinction of fault, action, and desire, that is threefold. Lack of faith is indeed the chief fault, destroying one's self.
विपरीतग्रहश्चापि ह्यपराधस्तु पौरुषः ।
प्रायः कलासु कुशला अपराधवशान्ननु ॥ १७ ॥
viparīta-grahaś ca api hy aparādhas tu pauruṣaḥ ।
prāyaḥ kalāsu kuśalā aparādha-vaśān na nū ॥ 17 ॥

viparīta-grahaḥ — wrong perception, ca — and, api — even, hi — indeed, aparādhaḥ — fault, tu — indeed, pauruṣaḥ — of man, prāyaḥ — mostly, kalāsu — in the arts, kuśalāḥ — skilled, aparādha-vaśāt — due to fault, na — not, nu — indeed.
Wrong perception is also indeed a fault of man. Mostly skilled in the arts also, not indeed free, due to fault.
सत्सङ्गशास्त्रयोगैश्च परं तत्वं हि नो विदुः ।
निर्विशेषं परं तत्त्वं नास्ति नैव च सम्भवेत्‌ ॥ १८ ॥
sat-saṅga-śāstra-yogaiś ca paraṁ tattvaṁ hi no viduḥ ।
nirviśeṣaṁ paraṁ tattvaṁ nāsti naiva ca sambhavet ॥ 18 ॥

sat-saṅga-śāstra-yogaiḥ — by association with the good and scriptures, ca — and, paraṁ tattvam — the supreme truth, hi — indeed, naḥ viduḥ — they do not know, nirviśeṣam — without distinction, paraṁ tattvam — the supreme truth, na asti — is not, na eva — not indeed, ca — and, sambhavet — can be.
By association with the good and scriptures, one does not know the supreme truth. The supreme truth which is without distinction does not exist, nor indeed comes into being.
अस्ति तन्नैव विज्ञातं शक्यते केनचित्‌ क्वचित्‌ ।
ज्ञात्वापि परमं तत्त्वं नैतत्तत्वं परं भवेत्‌ ॥ १९ ॥
asti tat na eva vijñātaṁ śakyate kena cit kvacit ।
jñātvā api paraṁ tattvaṁ na etat tattvam paraṁ bhavet ॥ 19 ॥

asti — is, tat — that, na — not, eva — indeed, vijñātam — known, śakyate — possible, kena cit — by anyone, kvacit — anywhere, jñātvā — having known, api — even, paraṁ tattvam — the supreme truth, na — not, etat — this, tattvam — truth, param — supreme, bhavet — becomes.
It is not known by anyone, anywhere. Even having known the supreme truth, this truth does not become supreme.
एतज्ज्ञानात्‌ कथं मोक्ष इत्यादि बहुधा स्थितः ।
विपरीतग्रहो वापि चैतत्संशय एव वा ॥ २० ॥
etaj-jñānāt kathaṁ mokṣa ityādi bahudhā sthitaḥ ।
viparīta-graho vā api caitat-saṁśaya eva vā ॥ 20 ॥

etaj-jñānāt — from this knowledge, katham — how, mokṣaḥ — liberation, iti — thus, ādi — and so on, bahudhā — in many ways, sthitaḥ — exists, viparīta-grahaḥ — wrong perception, vā — or, api — even, ca — and, etat-saṁśayaḥ — this doubt, eva — indeed, vā — or.
From this knowledge, how can liberation arise, and so on, this debate exists in many ways? It is either wrong perception or indeed could be doubt.
अपराधः पौरुषस्तु वासनाद्या प्रकीर्तिता ।
शास्त्रविद्यासु कुशलाः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥ २१ ॥
aparādhaḥ pauruṣas tu vāsanādyā prakīrtitā ।
śāstra-vidyāsu kuśalāḥ śataśo’tha sahasraśaḥ ॥ 21 ॥

aparādhaḥ — fault, pauruṣaḥ — of man, tu — indeed, vāsanā-ādyā — starting with impressions, prakīrtitā — proclaimed, śāstra-vidyāsu — in scriptural knowledge, kuśalāḥ — skilled, śataśaḥ — hundreds, atha — and, sahasraśaḥ — thousands.
Indeed, the fault of man, starting with impressions, is proclaimed here. Hundreds and thousands are skilled in scriptural knowledge.
अनया विहता राम संसृतिं समुपागताः ।
पुरा दृष्कृतसंस्कारवशाद्‌ बुद्धौ तु यत्‌ स्थितम्‌ ॥ २२ ॥
anayā vihatā rāma saṁsṛtiṁ samupāgatāḥ ।
purā duṣkṛta-saṁskāra-vaśād buddhau tu yat sthitam ॥ 22 ॥

anayā — by this, vihatāḥ — obstructed, rāma — O Rama, saṁsṛtim — cycle of existence, samupāgatāḥ — attained, purā — previously, duṣkṛta-saṁskāra-vaśāt — by the force of bad impressions, buddhau — in the intellect, tu — indeed, yat — what, sthitam — remains.
O Rama, obstructed by this, they have attained the cycle of existence, previously driven by the force of bad impressions that remain in the intellect.
मालिन्यमुपदेशस्य ग्रहणप्रतिबन्धकम्‌ ।
येनाचार्यैः सम्यगुक्तमपि नो गृह्यते खलु ॥ २३ ॥
mālīnyam upadeśasya grahaṇa-pratibandhakam ।
yenācāryaiḥ samyag uktam api no gṛhyate khalu ॥ 23 ॥

mālīnyam — impurity, upadeśasya — of teaching, grahaṇa-pratibandhakam — obstruction to acceptance, yena — by which, ācāryaiḥ — by teachers, samyak uktam api — even if correctly taught, no gṛhyate — not accepted, khalu — indeed.
The impurity of teaching is an obstruction to acceptance. By which, even if correctly taught by teachers, it is not accepted, indeed.
सा कर्मवासना प्रोक्ता दुर्जेयापि निरोधतः ।
कामः कर्तव्यशेषः स्यादनन्तो बहुशाखकः ॥ २४ ॥
sā karma-vāsanā proktā durjeyā api nirodhataḥ ।
kāmaḥ kartavya-śeṣaḥ syād ananto bahu-śākhakaḥ ॥ 24 ॥

sā — that, karma-vāsanā — impression of actions, proktā — is said, durjeyā api — difficult to overcome, nirodhataḥ — by restraint, kāmaḥ — desire, kartavya-śeṣaḥ — residual duty, syāt — may be, anantaḥ — endless, bahu-śākhakaḥ — with many branches.
The impression of actions is said to be difficult to overcome by restraint. Desire, with residual duty, may be endless with many branches.
रामाम्भोधौ तरङ्गाणां संख्यां कुर्याद्धि कश्चन ।
पार्थिवानामणुनां वा तथा तारागणस्य वा ॥ २५ ॥
rāmāmbhodhau taraṅgāṇāṁ saṁkhyāṁ kuryād dhi kaścana ।
pārthivānām aṇūnāṁ vā tathā tārā-gaṇasya vā ॥ 25 ॥

rāma-ambhodhau — in the ocean of Rama, taraṅgāṇām — of waves, saṁkhyām — count, kuryāt — may do, hi — indeed, kaścana — someone, pārthivānām — of atoms, aṇūnām — of particles, vā — or, tathā — likewise, tārā-gaṇasya — of the stars, vā — or.
Indeed, someone may count the waves in the ocean of Rama, the particles of earth, or the stars.
एकस्यापि हि कामानां संख्यातुं नैव शक्यते ।
इयं राम तृतीया ते संप्रोक्ता कामवासना ॥ २६ ॥
ekasya api hi kāmānāṁ saṁkhyātuṁ naiva śakyate ।
iyaṁ rāma tṛtīyā te saṁproktā kāma-vāsanā ॥ 26 ॥

ekasya api — even of one, hi — indeed, kāmānām — of desires, saṁkhyātum — to count, na eva — not indeed, śakyate — possible, iyaṁ — this, rāma — O Rama, tṛtīyā — third, te — to you, saṁproktā — said, kāma-vāsanā — impression of desire.
But indeed, even the desires of one person cannot be counted. This, O Rama, is the third fault, impression of desire said to you.
आकाशादपि विस्तीर्णा ह्यचला भूधरादपि ।
आशापिशाची प्रोक्तेयं राम या कामवासना ॥ २७ ॥
ākāśād api vistīrṇā hy acalā bhū-dharād api ।
āśā-piśācī prokteyaṁ rāma yā kāma-vāsanā ॥ 27 ॥

ākāśāt api — even than the sky, vistīrṇā — more expansive, hi — indeed, acalā — more immovable, bhū-dharāt api — even than the mountain, āśā-piśācī — demon of hope, proktā — said, iyam — this, rāma — O Rama, yā — which, kāma-vāsanā — impression of desire.
More expansive than the sky, more immovable than the mountain, this demon of hope, O Rama, which is the impression of desire.
अनयैव हि सर्वोऽयं लोक उन्मत्तवत्‌ स्थितः ।
येन दन्दह्यमानोऽयं लोक आक्रन्दते सदा ॥ २८ ॥
anayā eva hi sarvaḥ ayaṁ lokaḥ unmatta-vat sthitaḥ ।
yena dandahyamānaḥ ayaṁ lokaḥ ākrandate sadā ॥ 28 ॥

anayā — by this, eva — indeed, hi — indeed, sarvaḥ — all, ayaṁ — this, lokaḥ — world, unmatta-vat — like a madman, sthitaḥ — is situated, yena — by which, dandahyamānaḥ — burning, ayaṁ — this, lokaḥ — world, ākrandate — cries out, sadā — always.
Indeed, by this, all this world is situated like a madman. Burning by which, this world always cries out.
केऽपि लोके धन्यतमा महामन्त्रसमाश्रयात्‌ ।
विनिर्मुक्तास्तया भान्ति नराः सर्वाङ्गशोतलाः ॥ २९ ॥
ke’pi loke dhanyatamā mahā-mantra-samāśrayāt ।
vinirmuktāḥ tayā bhānti narāḥ sarva-aṅga-śītalaḥ ॥ 29 ॥

ke api — some, loke — in the world, dhanyatamāḥ — most fortunate, mahā-mantra-samāśrayāt — by the refuge of the great mantra, vinirmuktāḥ — liberated, tayā — by that, bhānti — shine, narāḥ — people, sarva-aṅga-śītalaḥ — cool in all their limbs.
Some in the world, the most fortunate, by the refuge of the great mantra, are liberated. They shine, their limbs cool in all respects.
एताभिस्तिसुभी राम वासनाभिर्यतो मनः ।
समाक्रान्तमतो नूनं तत्तत्त्वं नावभासते ॥ ३० ॥
etābhiḥ tisubhiḥ rāma vāsanābhiḥ yataḥ manaḥ ।
samākrāntam ato nūnaṁ tat-tattvaṁ na avabhāsate ॥ 30 ॥

etābhiḥ — by these, tisubhiḥ — three, rāma — O Rama, vāsanābhiḥ — by impressions, yataḥ — since, manaḥ — the mind, samākrāntam — overwhelmed, ataḥ — therefore, nūnam — indeed, tat-tattvaṁ — that truth, na avabhāsate — does not shine.
By these three impressions in the mind (fault, action, desire), O Rama, since the mind is overwhelmed, therefore, indeed, that truth does not shine.
अतः सर्वसाधनस्य वासनानाशनं फलम्‌ ।
तत्राद्या ह्यपराधत्वनिश्चयाद्‌ विनिवर्तते ॥ ३१ ॥
ataḥ sarva-sādhanasya vāsanā-nāśanaṁ phalam ।
tatra ādyā hi aparādhatva-niścayāt vinivartate ॥ 31 ॥

ataḥ — therefore, sarva-sādhanasya — of all practices, vāsanā-nāśanam — destruction of impressions, phalam — the result, tatra — there, ādyā — the first, hi — indeed, aparādhatva-niścayāt — by certainty of fault, vinivartate — is removed.
Therefore, the destruction of impressions is the result of all practices. The first is indeed removed by the certainty of fault.
द्वितीया जन्मनैकेन निवर्ततापि जन्मभिः ।
ऐश्वरेण प्रसादेन नान्यथा कोटियुक्तिभिः ॥ ३२ ॥
dvitīyā janmanā ekena nivartate api janmabhiḥ ।
aiśvareṇa prasādena na anyathā koṭi-yuktibhiḥ ॥ 32 ॥

dvitīyā — the second, janmanā ekena — by one birth, nivartate — is removed, api — even, janmabhiḥ — by births, aiśvareṇa prasādena — by the grace of the Lord, na anyathā — not otherwise, koṭi-yuktibhiḥ — by millions of efforts.
The second is removed by one birth, even by many births, by the grace of the Lord, not otherwise, even by millions of efforts.
तृतीया विनिवर्तेत वैराग्यादिसुसाधनैः ।
दोषदृष्टयैव वैराग्यं भवेन्नैवान्यथा क्वचित्‌ ॥ ३३ ॥
tṛtīyā vinivarteta vairāgya-ādi-su-sādhanaiḥ ।
doṣa-dṛṣṭyā eva vairāgyaṁ bhavet na eva anyathā kvacit ॥ 33 ॥

tṛtīyā — the third, vinivarteta — is removed, vairāgya-ādi-su-sādhanaiḥ — by proper practices like detachment, doṣa-dṛṣṭyā — by seeing the fault, eva — indeed, vairāgyaṁ — detachment, bhavet — is, na — not, eva — indeed, anyathā — otherwise, kvacit — ever.
The third is removed by proper practices like detachment. Detachment indeed arises by seeing the fault, not otherwise, ever.
प्रोक्तानां वासनानां वै स्वल्पानल्पविभेदतः ।
तस्याश्चाल्पानल्पभावापेक्षा भवति भार्गव ॥ ३४ ॥
proktānāṁ vāsanānāṁ vai svalpa-analpa-vibhedataḥ ।
tasyāḥ ca alpa-analpa-bhāva-apekṣā bhavati bhārgava ॥ 34 ॥

proktānām — of the said, vāsanānām — impressions, vai — indeed, svalpa-analpa-vibhedataḥ — by distinction of small and great, tasyāḥ — of that, ca — and, alpa-analpa-bhāva-apekṣā — expectation of small and great state, bhavati — arises, bhārgava — O Bhargava.
Indeed, among these, by the distinction of small and great impressions, the expectation of small and great state arises, O Bhargava.
तत्राद्यं सर्वमूलं स्यान्मुमुक्षुत्वं न चेतरत्‌ ।
मुमुक्षामन्तरा यत्तु श्रवणं मननादिकम्‌ ॥ ३५ ॥
tatra ādyam sarva-mūlaṁ syāt mumukṣutvaṁ na cetarat ।
mumukṣā-mantarā yat tu śravaṇaṁ mananādikam ॥ 35 ॥

tatra — there, ādyam — the first, sarva-mūlam — the root of all, syāt — may be, mumukṣutvam — desire for liberation, na — not, cetarat — otherwise, mumukṣā-mantarā — without desire for liberation, yat — which, tu — but, śravaṇam — hearing, mananā-ādikam — reflection, etc.
There, the first, the root of all, is the desire for liberation, not otherwise. Without the desire for liberation, hearing, reflection, etc., are not effective.
न मुख्यफलसंयुक्तं केवलं शिल्पवद्‌ भवेत्‌ ।
न शिल्पज्ञानमात्रेण प्राप्यते परमं पदम्‌ ॥ ३६ ॥
na mukhya-phala-saṁyuktaṁ kevalaṁ śilpa-vad bhavet ।
na śilpa-jñāna-mātreṇa prāpyate paramaṁ padam ॥ 36 ॥

na — not, mukhya-phala-saṁyuktam — connected with main fruit, kevalam — only, śilpa-vat — like a craft, bhavet — becomes, na — not, śilpa-jñāna-mātreṇa — by mere knowledge of the craft, prāpyate — is attained, paramam padam — the supreme state.
Not connected with the main fruit, it becomes only like a craft. The supreme state is not attained by mere knowledge of the craft.
मुमुक्षामन्तरा यैस्तु श्रुतं सम्यग्‌ विचारितम्‌ ।
शवालङ्कारवत्‌ सर्वं तेषां व्यर्थं भवेत्‌ खलु ॥ ३७ ॥
mumukṣā-mantarā yaiḥ tu śrutaṁ samyak vicāritam ।
śavālaṅkāra-vat sarvaṁ teṣāṁ vyarthaṁ bhavet khalu ॥ 37 ॥

mumukṣā-mantarā — without desire for liberation, yaiḥ — by whom, tu — but, śrutam — heard, samyak vicāritam — properly reflected, śava-ālaṅkāra-vat — like the decoration of a corpse, sarvam — all, teṣām — of them, vyartham — in vain, bhavet — becomes, khalu — indeed.
Without the desire for liberation, by whom it is heard and properly reflected upon, all becomes in vain, like the decoration of a corpse.
व्यर्था सापि भवेन्मन्दा मुमुक्षा राम सर्वथा ।
यथा फलश्रुतेरिच्छा सामान्या न फलावहा ॥ ३८ ॥
vyarthā sā api bhavet mandā mumukṣā rāma sarvathā ।
yathā phala-śruteḥ icchā sāmānyā na phala-āvahā ॥ 38 ॥

vyarthā — in vain, sā api — that too, bhavet — becomes, mandā — weak, mumukṣā — desire for liberation, rāma — O Rama, sarvathā — in all respects, yathā — like, phala-śruteḥ — of hearing of fruit, icchā — desire, sāmānyā — ordinary, na phala-āvahā — does not bring fruit.
In all respects, weak desire for liberation becomes in vain, O Rama, like the ordinary desire from hearing of fruit, does not bring fruit.
फलश्रुत्युत्तरोद्भूता नेच्छा कर्मफलावहा ।
फलश्रुत्या कस्य नाम न स्यात्‌ सा जीवधर्मिणः ॥ ३९ ॥
phala-śruti-uttara-udbhūtā na icchā karma-phala-āvahā ।
phala-śrutyā kasya nāma na syāt sā jīva-dharmiṇaḥ ॥ 39 ॥

phala-śruti-uttara-udbhūtā — arising after hearing of fruit, na icchā — not the desire, karma-phala-āvahā — brings the fruit of action, phala-śrutyā — by hearing of fruit, kasya nāma — whose indeed, na syāt — would not be, sā — that, jīva-dharmiṇaḥ — of the living being.
The desire arising after hearing of fruit does not bring the fruit of action. By hearing of fruit, who indeed, doesn’t have the desire for fruit, among living beings.
तस्मादापातरूपाया मुमुक्षाया न वै फलम्‌ ।
यथा मुमुक्षा तीव्रा स्यात्तथा तस्याऽचिरं फलम्‌ ॥ ४० ॥
tasmāt āpāta-rūpāyāḥ mumukṣāyāḥ na vai phalam ।
yathā mumukṣā tīvra syāt tathā tasyāḥ aciram phalam ॥ 40 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, āpāta-rūpāyāḥ — superficial, mumukṣāyāḥ — of desire for liberation, na vai phalam — no indeed fruit, yathā — as, mumukṣā — desire for liberation, tīvra — intense, syāt — may be, tathā — thus, tasyāḥ — of that, aciram phalam — quick fruit.
Therefore, from this superficial desire for liberation, there is indeed no fruit. As the desire for liberation may be intense, thus its fruit is quick.
मुमुक्षा या मुख्यतमा सा साधनगणेष्वलम्‌ ।
प्रवृत्तिमुत्पादयेद्‌ वै सा हि तत्परतोच्यते ॥ ४१ ॥
mumukṣā yā mukhyatamā sā sādhanagaṇeṣu alam ।
pravṛttiṁ utpādayed vai sā hi tatparatā ucyate ॥ 41 ॥

mumukṣā — desire for liberation, yā — which, mukhyatamā — most important, sā — that, sādhanagaṇeṣu — among the practices, alam — sufficient, pravṛttiṁ — engagement, utpādayed — produces, vai — indeed, sā — that, hi — indeed, tatparatā — dedication, ucyate — is said.
The desire for liberation, which is most important, is sufficient among the practices. It indeed produces engagement and is said to be dedication.
यथा सुदग्धसर्वाङ्गो न शीतान्यदपेक्षते ।
तथा यदा विमुक्त्यन्यन्नापेक्षेत हि सर्वथा ॥ ४२ ॥
yathā sudagdha-sarvāṅgo na śītaṁ anyat apekṣate ।
tathā yadā vimukti anyat na apekṣeta hi sarvathā ॥ 42 ॥

yathā — as, sudagdha-sarvāṅgaḥ — one whose entire body is severely burnt, na — not, śītam — coolness, anyat — anything else, apekṣate — needs, tathā — so, yadā — when, vimuktiḥ — liberation, anyat — anything else, na — not, apekṣeta — needs, hi — indeed, sarvathā — in every way.
As one whose entire body is severely burnt does not need coolness or anything else (seeing that it is vain), so when one desires liberation, they do not need anything else indeed in every way.
सा मुमुक्षा भवेत्तीव्रा समर्था फलसाधने ।
एषा विमुक्तेरन्यत्र दोषदृष्ट्यैव जायते ॥ ४३ ॥
sā mumukṣā bhavet tīvra samarthā phala-sādhane ।
eṣā vimukteḥ anyatra doṣa-dṛṣṭyā eva jāyate ॥ 43 ॥

sā — that, mumukṣā — desire for liberation, bhavet — becomes, tīvra — intense, samarthā — capable, phala-sādhane — in achieving the goal, eṣā — this, vimukteḥ — of liberation, anyatra — otherwise, doṣa-dṛṣṭyā — by seeing faults, eva — indeed, jāyate — arises.
That desire for liberation becomes intense and capable of achieving the goal. This arises by seeing faults otherwise.
तीव्रवैराग्यमुखतः क्रमेण तीव्रतामियात्‌ ।
दोषदृष्ट्या हि वैराग्यं विषयप्रीतिनाशनम्‌ ॥ ४४ ॥
tīvravairāgya-mukhataḥ krameṇa tīvratām iyāt ।
doṣadṛṣṭyā hi vairāgyaṁ viṣaya-prīti-nāśanam ॥ 44 ॥

tīvravairāgya — intense detachment, mukhataḥ — from the face, krameṇa — gradually, tīvratām — intensity, iyāt — attains, doṣadṛṣṭyā — by seeing faults, hi — indeed, vairāgyaṁ — detachment, viṣaya-prīti-nāśanam — the destruction of attachment to objects.
From the face of intense detachment, it gradually attains intensity. Indeed, detachment arises by seeing faults, which destroys attachment to objects.
वैराग्येण मुमुक्षुत्वं तीव्रं तत्परतोदयम्‌ ।
तत्परत्वं साधनेषु प्रवृत्तिरतितीव्रतः ॥ ४५ ॥
vairāgyeṇa mumukṣutvaṁ tīvraṁ tatparatā udayam ।
tatparatvaṁ sādhanṣu pravṛttiḥ atitīvrataḥ ॥ 45 ॥

vairāgyeṇa — by detachment, mumukṣutvam — desire for liberation, tīvram — intense, tatparatā — dedication, udayam — arises, tatparatvam — dedication, sādhanṣu — in practices, pravṛttiḥ — engagement, atitīvrataḥ — extreme intensity.
By detachment, the desire for liberation becomes intense. Dedication arises, and with that dedication, engagement in practices is of extreme intensity.
अतितीव्रप्रकृत्यैव द्रुतं फलमवाप्नुयात्‌ ।
इति दत्तात्रेयवचो निशम्य भार्गवः पुनः ॥ ४६ ॥
atitīvraprakṛtyā eva drutam phalam avāpnuyāt ।
iti dattātreya-vaco niśamya bhārgavaḥ punaḥ ॥ 46 ॥

atitīvraprakṛtyā — by the nature of extreme intensity, eva — indeed, drutam — quickly, phalam — fruit, avāpnuyāt — attains, iti — thus, dattātreya-vacaḥ — the words of Dattatreya, niśamya — hearing, bhārgavaḥ — Bhargava, punaḥ — again.
By the nature of extreme intensity, one quickly attains the fruit. Hearing thus the words of Dattatreya, Bhargava again.
पप्रच्छ सन्दिग्धमनाः संशयं सुमहत्तरम्‌ ।
भगवन्‌ भवता प्रोक्तं सत्सङ्गो मूलकारणम्‌ ॥ ४७ ॥
papraccha sandigdha-manāḥ saṁśayaṁ su-mahattaram ।
bhagavan bhavatā proktam satsango mūla-kāraṇam ॥ 47 ॥

papraccha — asked, sandigdha-manāḥ — with a doubtful mind, saṁśayam — doubt, su-mahattaram — very great, bhagavan — O Lord, bhavatā — by you, proktam — said, satsangaḥ — association with the good, mūla-kāraṇam — main cause.
He asked, with a doubtful mind, a very great doubt, "O Lord, you have said that association with the good is the main cause.
ईश्वरानुग्रहश्चापि दोषदृष्टिरपीति च ।
किमादिकारणं मुख्यं तत्प्राप्तिर्वा कथं भवेत्‌ ॥ ४८ ॥
īśvara-anugrahaḥ ca api doṣa-dṛṣṭiḥ api iti ca ।
kim-ādi-kāraṇaṁ mukhyaṁ tat-prāptiḥ vā katham bhavet ॥ 48 ॥

īśvara-anugrahaḥ — grace of the Lord, ca — and, api — also, doṣa-dṛṣṭiḥ — seeing faults, api — also, iti — thus, ca — and, kim — what, ādi-kāraṇam — primary cause, mukhyam — main, tat-prāptiḥ — attaining that, vā — or, katham — how, bhavet — may be.
The grace of the Lord, and also seeing faults, thus, what is the primary main cause, and how may one attain that?
नहि निष्कारणं किञ्चिद्‌ भवेदिति हि निश्चयः ।
तत्‌ कथं स्याद्विना हेतोरेतन्मे वद विस्तरात्‌ ॥ ४९ ॥
na hi niṣkāraṇam kiñcit bhavet iti hi niścayaḥ ।
tat katham syāt vinā hetoḥ etan me vada vistarāt ॥ 49 ॥

na hi — indeed not, niṣkāraṇam — without cause, kiñcit — anything, bhavet — may be, iti — thus, hi — indeed, niścayaḥ — certainty, tat — that, katham — how, syāt — may be, vinā hetoḥ — without a cause, etan — this, me — to me, vada — tell, vistarāt — in detail.
Indeed, there is nothing without a cause, that is the certainty. So how may this happen without a cause? Tell me this in detail.
इति पृष्टः प्राह रामं दत्तात्रेयो दयानिधिः ।
भार्गव शृणु ते वक्ष्ये श्रेयसः परमोद्भवम्‌ ॥ ५० ॥
iti pṛṣṭaḥ prāha rāmaṁ dattātreyo dayā-nidhiḥ ।
bhārgava śṛṇu te vakṣye śreyasaḥ param-udbhavam ॥ 50 ॥

iti — thus, pṛṣṭaḥ — asked, prāha — said, rāmaṁ — to Rama, dattātreyaḥ — Dattatreya, dayā-nidhiḥ — ocean of compassion, bhārgava — O Bhargava, śṛṇu — listen, te — to you, vakṣye — I will tell, śreyasaḥ — of the supreme good, param-udbhavam — the supreme source.
Thus asked, Dattatreya, the ocean of compassion, said to Rama, "O Bhargava, listen, I will tell you the supreme source of the supreme good."
परा सा या चितिर्देवी स्वस्वातन्त्र्यस्य वैभवात्‌ ।
स्वात्मन्येव जगच्चित्रं दर्पणप्रतिबिम्बवत्‌ ॥ ५१ ॥
parā sā yā citiḥ devī sva-svātantryasya vaibhavāt ।
svātmani eva jagat-citraṁ darpaṇa-pratibimbavat ॥ 51 ॥

parā — supreme, sā — that, yā — which, citiḥ — consciousness, devī — goddess, sva-svātantryasya — of her own freedom, vaibhavāt — by the power, svātmani — in herself, eva — indeed, jagat-citram — the picture of the world, darpaṇa-pratibimbavat — like a reflection in a mirror.
The supreme consciousness, which is the goddess, by the power of her own freedom, reflects the picture of the world in herself, like a reflection in a mirror.
सैव हैरण्यगर्भाख्यां तनुमास्थाय वै परा ।
अनाद्यज्ञानसंच्छन्नजीवानां हितकाम्यया ॥ ५२ ॥
sā eva hiraṇya-garbha-ākhyāṁ tanum āsthāya vai parā ।
anādi-ajñāna-saṁcchanna-jīvānāṁ hita-kāmyayā ॥ 52 ॥

sā — she, eva — indeed, hiraṇya-garbha-ākhyāṁ — called Hiranyagarbha, tanum — body, āsthāya — assuming, vai — indeed, parā — supreme, anādi-ajñāna — beginningless ignorance, saṁcchanna — covered, jīvānām — of the beings, hita-kāmyayā — for the desire of welfare.
She, indeed, assuming the body called Hiranyagarbha, the supreme one, for the desire of welfare of beings covered by beginningless ignorance.
उन्मेषयदागमाब्धिं सर्वकामप्रपूरणम्‌ ।
तत्र जीवाः स्वभावेन विचित्रकामवासनाः ॥ ५३ ॥
unmeṣayad āgama-abdhim sarva-kāma-prapūraṇam ।
tatra jīvāḥ sva-bhāvena vicitra-kāma-vāsanāḥ ॥ 53 ॥

unmeṣayad — illuminating, āgama-abdhim — the ocean of scriptures, sarva-kāma-prapūraṇam — fulfilling all desires, tatra — there, jīvāḥ — beings, sva-bhāvena — by their nature, vicitra — various, kāma-vāsanāḥ — desires and tendencies.
Illuminating the ocean of scriptures, fulfilling all desires, there, beings, by their nature, have various desires and tendencies.
कथं तेषां शुभं भूयादेवं चिन्तापरायणः ।
असृजत्‌ काम्यकर्माणि फलचित्राणि सर्वशः ॥ ५४ ॥
kathaṁ teṣām śubhaṁ bhūyāt evaṁ cintā-parāyaṇaḥ ।
asṛjat kāmya-karmāṇi phala-citrāṇi sarvaśaḥ ॥ 54 ॥

kathaṁ — how, teṣām — for them, śubham — good, bhūyāt — may be, evaṁ — thus, cintā-parāyaṇaḥ — contemplating, asṛjat — created, kāmya-karmāṇi — actions for desires, phala-citrāṇi — various fruits, sarvaśaḥ — in every way.
Contemplating how there may be good for them, he created actions for desires with various fruits in every way.
सदसद्वापि हि जनः करोत्येव स्वभावतः ।
तथा च केनापि कर्मपरिपाकवशेन तु ॥ ५५ ॥
sadasad-vā api hi janaḥ karoti eva svabhāvataḥ ।
tathā ca kenāpi karma-paripāka-vaśena tu ॥ 55 ॥

sada-sad-vā — good or bad, api — also, hi — indeed, janaḥ — person, karoti — does, eva — indeed, svabhāvataḥ — by nature, tathā — so, ca — and, kenāpi — by some, karma-paripāka-vaśena — by the result of actions, tu — indeed.
A person does good or bad by nature. So, by some, that is due to attachment to the result of actions, indeed.
भ्रमन्‌ योनिविभेदेषु मानुष्यमुपसङ्गतः ।
कामनावशतः काम्ये कर्मण्यभिमुखो भवेत्‌ ॥ ५६ ॥
bhraman yoni-vibhedeṣu mānuṣyam upasaṅgataḥ ।
kāmanā-vaśataḥ kāmye karmaṇi abhimukho bhavet ॥ 56 ॥

bhraman — wandering, yoni-vibhedeṣu — in various births, mānuṣyam — human birth, upasaṅgataḥ — attaining, kāmanā-vaśataḥ — under the influence of desires, kāmye — for desires, karmaṇi — actions, abhimukhaḥ — inclined, bhavet — becomes.
Wandering in various births, attaining human birth, under the influence of desires, one becomes inclined to actions for desires.
कामनाया विशेषेण यदेश्वरपरो भवेत्‌ ।
तदैश्वराणि शास्त्राणि प्रसङ्गादवलोकयेत्‌ ॥ ५७ ॥
kāmanāyā viśeṣeṇa yad eśvara-paraḥ bhavet ।
tadā eśvarāṇi śāstrāṇi prasaṅgāt avalokayet ॥ 57 ॥

kāmanāyā — of desires, viśeṣeṇa — especially, yad — when, eśvara-paraḥ — devoted to the Lord, bhavet — becomes, tadā — then, eśvarāṇi — divine, śāstrāṇi — scriptures, prasaṅgāt — by association, avalokayet — looks into.
Especially, when one becomes devoted to the Lord due to desires, then, by association, one looks into the divine scriptures.
काम्यकर्मफलश्रुत्या प्रवृत्तः काम्यकर्मणि ।
विहतस्तत्फलाप्राप्त्या वैगुण्यात्‌ सूक्ष्मकर्मणः ॥ ५८ ॥
kāmya-karma-phala-śrutyā pravṛttaḥ kāmya-karmaṇi ।
vihatasta phala-aprāptya vai-guṇyāt sūkṣma-karmaṇaḥ ॥ 58 ॥

kāmya-karma-phala-śrutyā — by hearing the fruits of actions for desires, pravṛttaḥ — engaged, kāmya-karmaṇi — in actions for desires, vihataḥ — obstructed, tat-phala-aprāptya — due to not attaining the fruits, vai-guṇyāt — due to imperfection, sūkṣma-karmaṇaḥ — of subtle actions.
By hearing the fruits of actions for desires, engaged in actions for desires, obstructed due to not attaining the fruits, due to imperfection of subtle actions.
कर्तव्यजिज्ञासयैव कञ्चित्‌ सत्पुरुषं व्रजेत्‌ ।
तत्प्रसङ्गवशात्‌ क्वापि माहात्म्यं शृणुयात्‌ क्वचित्‌ ॥ ५९ ॥
kartavya-jijñāsayā eva kañcit sat-puruṣaṁ vrajet ।
tat-prasaṅga-vaśāt kvāpi māhātmyaṁ śṛṇuyāt kvacit ॥ 59 ॥

kartavya-jijñāsayā — by curiosity about duty, eva — indeed, kañcit — some, sat-puruṣaṁ — noble person, vrajet — approaches, tat-prasaṅga-vaśāt — by association with him, kvāpi — somewhere, māhātmyaṁ — greatness, śṛṇuyāt — hears, kvacit — sometimes.
By curiosity about duty, one indeed approaches some noble person, and by association with him, sometimes hears about greatness.
महेश्वरस्य च ततः प्राक्पुण्यपरिपाकतः ।
तस्य प्रसादने भूयात्‌ प्रवृत्तिरपि भार्गव ॥ ६० ॥
maheśvarasya ca tataḥ prāk-puṇya-paripākataḥ ।
tasya prasādane bhūyāt pravṛttiḥ api bhārgava ॥ 60 ॥

maheśvarasya — of the great Lord, ca — and, tataḥ — then, prāk-puṇya-paripākataḥ — by the maturation of previous merits, tasya — his, prasādane — in pleasing, bhūyāt — may be, pravṛttiḥ — engagement, api — also, bhārgava — O Bhargava.
Of the great Lord, then, by the maturation of previous merits, his engagement in pleasing the Lord may also be, O Bhargava.
तस्मात्‌ प्राक्पुण्यपाकेन सत्सङ्गमभिगम्य तु ।
प्राप्नोति श्रेयःसोपानपङ्क्तिमत्यन्तदुर्लभाम्‌ ॥ ६१ ॥
tasmāt prāk-puṇya-pākena sat-saṅgam abhigamya tu ।
prāpnoti śreyaḥ-sopāna-paṅktim atyanta-durlabhām ॥ 61 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, prāk-puṇya-pākena — by the maturation of previous merits, sat-saṅgam — association with the good, abhigamya — attaining, tu — indeed, prāpnoti — attains, śreyaḥ-sopāna-paṅktim — the series of steps leading to the supreme good, atyanta-durlabhām — extremely rare.
Therefore, by the maturation of previous merits, attaining association with the good, one attains the series of steps leading to the supreme good, which is extremely rare.
प्रायः सत्सङ्गमूलैव श्रेयःप्राप्तिरुदोरिता ।
क्वचिदुत्कृष्टपुण्येन चोत्कृष्टतपसापि वा ॥ ६२ ॥
prāyaḥ sat-saṅga-mūlā eva śreyaḥ-prāptir udīritā ।
