kvacit utkṛṣṭa-puṇyena ca utkṛṣṭa-tapasā api vā ॥ 62 ॥

prāyaḥ — mostly, sat-saṅga-mūlā — rooted in association with the good, eva — indeed, śreyaḥ-prāptiḥ — attainment of the supreme good, udīritā — stated, kvacit — sometimes, utkṛṣṭa-puṇyena — by excellent merits, ca — and, utkṛṣṭa-tapasā — by excellent austerities, api — also, vā — or.
Mostly, the attainment of the supreme good is stated to be rooted in association with the good, and sometimes by excellent merits or by excellent austerities.
श्रेयः प्राप्नोति सहसा ह्याकाशफलपातवत्‌ ।
तस्मात्‌ कारणवैचित्र्याच्छ्रेयःप्राप्तिविचित्रता ॥ ६३ ॥
śreyaḥ prāpnoti sahasā hy-ākāśa-phala-pāta-vat ।
tasmāt kāraṇa-vaicitryāt śreyaḥ-prāpti-vicitratā ॥ 63 ॥

śreyaḥ — supreme good, prāpnoti — attains, sahasā — suddenly, hy — indeed, ākāśa-phala-pāta-vat — like the fall of a fruit from the sky, tasmāt — therefore, kāraṇa-vaicitryāt — due to the variety of causes, śreyaḥ-prāpti-vicitratā — the variety of attaining the supreme good.
One attains the supreme good suddenly, like the fall of a fruit from the sky. Therefore, due to the variety of causes, there is a variety in the attainment of the supreme good.
तथा च बुद्धिभेदेन वासनातारतम्यतः ।
साधनानां तारतम्याद्‌ विचित्रा ज्ञानिनां स्थितिः ॥ ६४ ॥
tathā ca buddhi-bhedena vāsanā-tāratamyataḥ ।
sādhanānāṁ tāratamyād vicitrā jñānināṁ sthitiḥ ॥ 64 ॥

tathā — similarly, ca — and, buddhi-bhedena — by the difference in intelligence, vāsanā-tāratamyataḥ — by the gradation of tendencies, sādhanānāṁ — of practices, tāratamyāt — by the gradation, vicitrā — varied, jñānināṁ — of the wise, sthitiḥ — state.
Similarly, by the difference in intelligence, by the gradation of tendencies, and by the gradation of practices, the state of the wise is varied.
स्वभावाद्यस्य वै बुद्धेर्वासना विरला भवेत्‌ ।
तस्याल्पसाधनेनैव ज्ञानसिद्धिर्भवेदलम्‌ ॥ ६५ ॥
svabhāvād yasya vai buddher vāsanā viralā bhavet ।
tasyālpa-sādhanena eva jñāna-siddhir bhaved alam ॥ 65 ॥

svabhāvāt — by nature, yasya — whose, vai — indeed, buddheḥ — of intelligence, vāsanā — tendencies, viralā — sparse, bhavet — are, tasya — his, alpa-sādhanena — with little practice, eva — indeed, jñāna-siddhiḥ — attainment of knowledge, bhavet — happens, alam — enough.
By nature, whose intelligence has sparse tendencies, for him, indeed, with little practice, the attainment of knowledge happens enough.
यस्य स्वभावात्‌ संशुद्धं वासना नहि लेशतः ।
तस्य स्वल्पनिमित्तेन भवेज्ज्ञानं महत्तरम्‌ ॥ ६६ ॥
yasya svabhāvāt saṁśuddhaṁ vāsanā na hi leśataḥ ।
tasya svalpa-nimittena bhavet jñānaṁ mahattaram ॥ 66 ॥

yasya — whose, svabhāvāt — by nature, saṁśuddham — pure, vāsanā — tendencies, na hi — not, leśataḥ — at all, tasya — his, svalpa-nimittena — with little cause, bhavet — happens, jñānam — knowledge, mahattaram — great.
Whose intelligence is pure by nature and has no tendencies at all, for him, with little cause, great knowledge happens.
यस्य स्वभावादत्यन्तवासनानिबिडं मनः ।
तस्य ज्ञानं जातमपि समाच्छादितकल्पकम्‌ ॥ ६७ ॥
yasya svabhāvād atyanta-vāsanā-nibiḍaṁ manaḥ ।
tasya jñānaṁ jātam api samācchādita-kalpam ॥ 67 ॥

yasya — whose, svabhāvāt — by nature, atyanta — extremely, vāsanā-nibiḍam — full of tendencies, manaḥ — mind, tasya — his, jñānam — knowledge, jātam api — even though arisen, samācchādita-kalpam — appears to be covered.
Whose mind is extremely full of tendencies by nature, for him, even though knowledge arises, it appears to be covered.
तेनैव साधितं भूयश्चिरादभ्येति पुर्णताम्‌ ।
अत एव ज्ञानिना तु दृश्यते विविधा स्थितिः ॥ ६८ ॥
tena eva sādhitaṁ bhūyaś cirād abhyeti pūrṇatām ।
ata eva jñāninā tu dṛśyate vividhā sthitiḥ ॥ 68 ॥

tena — by that, eva — indeed, sādhitam — achieved, bhūyaḥ — again, cirāt — after a long time, abhyeti — attains, pūrṇatām — completeness, ataḥ eva — therefore, jñāninā — of the wise, tu — indeed, dṛśyate — is seen, vividhā — varied, sthitiḥ — state.
By that, indeed, achieved again, after a long time, attains completeness. Therefore, the state of the wise is seen to be varied.
चित्तपाकविभेदेन स्थितिभेदो भृगूद्वह ।
तस्माद्‌ बुद्धौ वासनाभिस्त्वावृत्तेस्तारतम्यतः ॥ ६९ ॥
citta-pāka-vibhedena sthiti-bhedo bhṛgūdvaha ।
tasmād buddhau vāsanābhiḥ tu āvṛtteḥ tāratamyataḥ ॥ 69 ॥

citta-pāka-vibhedena — by the difference in the maturity of the mind, sthiti-bhedaḥ — difference in state, bhṛgūdvaha — O descendant of Bhrigu, tasmāt — therefore, buddhau — in intelligence, vāsanābhiḥ — by tendencies, tu — indeed, āvṛtteḥ — due to covering, tāratamyataḥ — by gradation.
By the difference in the maturity of the mind, O descendant of Bhrigu, the difference in state is seen. Therefore, due to the gradation of covering by tendencies in intelligence.
ज्ञानं भिन्नं लक्ष्यते हि स्थितिभेदस्तथा भवेत्‌ ।
राम पश्य स्थितेर्भेदं ज्ञानिनां तु परस्परम्‌ ॥ ७० ॥
jñānaṁ bhinnaṁ lakṣyate hi sthiti-bhedaḥ tathā bhavet ।
rāma paśya sthiti-bhedaṁ jñānināṁ tu parasparam ॥ 70 ॥

jñānam — knowledge, bhinnam — different, lakṣyate — is observed, hi — indeed, sthiti-bhedaḥ — difference in state, tathā — similarly, bhavet — is, rāma — O Rama, paśya — see, sthiti-bhedam — difference in state, jñāninām — of the wise, tu — indeed, parasparam — among each other.
Knowledge is observed to be different, indeed, similarly, the difference in state is. O Rama, see the difference in state among the wise.
ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेशानां स्वभावज्ञानिनस्तु ते ।
तेषां पश्य स्थितेर्भेदं स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः ॥ ७१ ॥
brahma-viṣṇu-maheśānāṁ svabhāva-jñāninas tu te ।
teṣāṁ paśya sthiti-bhedaṁ svabhāva-prabhavaiḥ guṇaiḥ ॥ 71 ॥

brahma-viṣṇu-maheśānām — of Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesha, svabhāva-jñāninaḥ — knowing their nature, tu — indeed, te — they, teṣām — their, paśya — see, sthiti-bhedam — difference in state, svabhāva-prabhavaiḥ — by the qualities born of their nature, guṇaiḥ — by qualities.
Indeed, those who know their nature, such as Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesha, see their difference in state by the qualities born of their nature.
नैषां ज्ञानस्य मालिन्यं वक्तुं शक्यं कथञ्चन ।
स्वभावगुणमाहात्म्यं भिन्नमेव तथापि हि ॥ ७२ ॥
naiṣāṁ jñānasya mālinyaṁ vaktuṁ śakyaṁ kathañcana ।
svabhāva-guṇa-māhātmyaṁ bhinnam eva tathāpi hi ॥ 72 ॥

naiṣām — of their, jñānasya — of knowledge, mālinyam — impurity, vaktum — to say, śakyaṁ — is possible, kathañcana — in any way, svabhāva-guṇa-māhātmyaṁ — greatness of qualities born of nature, bhinnam — different, eva — indeed, tathāpi — still, hi — indeed.
In any way, it is not possible to say that their knowledge has impurity. The greatness of qualities born of nature is indeed different still.
यथा ज्ञानिशरीरं तु गौरं न श्यामतां व्रजेत्‌ ।
एवं चित्तस्वभावोऽपि नान्यभावं प्रपद्यते ॥ ७३ ॥
yathā jñāni-śarīraṁ tu gauraṁ na śyāmatāṁ vrajet ।
evaṁ citta-svabhāvaḥ api na anya-bhāvaṁ prapadyate ॥ 73 ॥

yathā — just as, jñāni-śarīram — the body of the wise, tu — indeed, gauram — fair, na — not, śyāmatām — dark, vrajet — becomes, evaṁ — similarly, citta-svabhāvaḥ — nature of the mind, api — also, na — not, anya-bhāvam — another state, prapadyate — assumes.
Just as the body of the wise, being fair, does not become dark, similarly, the nature of the mind also does not assume another state.
अस्मान्‌ राम तथा पश्य ज्ञानिनोऽत्रिसुतान्‌ स्थितान्‌ ।
दुर्वाससं चन्द्रमसं मां च भिन्नस्थितिं गतम्‌ ॥ ७४ ॥
asmān rāma tathā paśya jñāninaḥ atri-sutān sthitān ।
durvāsasaṁ candrama-saṁ māṁ ca bhinna-sthitiṁ gatam ॥ 74 ॥

asmān — us, rāma — O Rama, tathā — similarly, paśya — see, jñāninaḥ — wise, atri-sutān — sons of Atri, sthitān — situated, durvāsasaṁ — Durvasa, candrama-saṁ — Chandra, māṁ — me, ca — and, bhinna-sthitim — different states, gatam — attained.
O Rama, similarly, see us, the wise sons of Atri, such as Durvasa, Chandra, and me, having attained different states.
क्रोधिनं कामिनं त्यक्तसर्वलिङ्गपरिग्रहम्‌ ।
वसिष्ठं पश्य कर्मिष्ठं सनकादींश्च न्यासिनः ॥ ७५ ॥
krodhinaṁ kāminaṁ tyakta-sarva-liṅga-parigraham ।
vasiṣṭhaṁ paśya karma-iṣṭhaṁ sanakādīn ca nyāsinaḥ ॥ 75 ॥

krodhinam — angry, kāminam — desirous, tyakta-sarva-liṅga-parigraham — renouncing all marks of identity, vasiṣṭham — Vasistha, paśya — see, karma-iṣṭham — engaged in duties, sanaka-ādīn — such as Sanaka, ca — and, nyāsinaḥ — renunciates.
See Vasistha, engaged in duties, and such renunciates as Sanaka, who are angry, desirous, and renounce all marks of identity.
नारदं भक्तिसंमग्नं कवयन्तं च भार्गवम्‌ ।
दैत्यपक्षसंश्रयिणं गुरुं देवसमाश्रयम्‌ ॥ ७६ ॥
nāradaṁ bhakti-saṁmagnaṁ kavayantaṁ ca bhārgavam ।
daitya-pakṣa-saṁśrayiṇaṁ guruṁ deva-saṁāśrayam ॥ 76 ॥

nāradaṁ — Narada, bhakti-saṁmagnam — absorbed in devotion, kavayantaṁ — praising, ca — and, bhārgavam — Bhrigu, daitya-pakṣa-saṁśrayiṇam — residing with the demon party, gurum — preceptor, deva-saṁāśrayam — resorting to the gods.
See Narada, absorbed in devotion, praising, and Bhrigu, residing with the demon party, the preceptor resorting to the gods.
वाग्मिनं च व्यासमपि शास्त्रनिर्माणतत्परम्‌ ।
जनकं पश्य राजानं भरतं त्यागिनं तथा ॥ ७७ ॥
vāgminaṁ ca vyāsam api śāstra-nirmāṇa-tatparam ।
janakaṁ paśya rājānaṁ bharataṁ tyāginaṁ tathā ॥ 77 ॥

vāgminam — eloquent, ca — and, vyāsam — Vyasa, api — also, śāstra-nirmāṇa-tatparam — dedicated to scripture creation, janakam — Janaka, paśya — see, rājānam — king, bharatam — Bharata, tyāginam — renunciant, tathā — also.
See Vyasa, eloquent and dedicated to scripture creation, and also king Janaka, and Bharata, the renunciant.
भिन्नस्थितीन्‌ स्वभावेन ज्ञानिनः पश्य चापरान्‌ ।
रहस्यं ते प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणु भार्गवनन्दन ॥ ७८ ॥
bhinna-sthitīn svabhāvena jñāninaḥ paśya ca aparān ।
rahasyaṁ te pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu bhārgava-nandana ॥ 78 ॥

bhinna-sthitīn — different states, svabhāvena — by nature, jñāninaḥ — wise, paśya — see, ca — and, aparān — others, rahasyam — secret, te — to you, pravakṣyāmi — I will tell, śṛṇu — listen, bhārgava-nandana — O son of Bhargava.
See the different states of the wise by nature, and also others. I will tell you the secret, listen, O son of Bhargava.
त्रिविधा या वासनोक्ता द्वितीया तत्र या भवेत्‌ ।
कर्मजा मूढतारूपा सा सर्वेभ्यो महत्तरा ॥ ७९ ॥
trividhā yā vāsanoktā dvitīyā tatra yā bhavet ।
karma-jā mūḍhatā-rūpā sā sarvebhyo mahattarā ॥ 79 ॥

trividhā — threefold, yā — which, vāsanā uktā — tendencies are said, dvitīyā — second, tatra — there, yā — which, bhavet — is, karma-jā — born of actions, mūḍhatā-rūpā — in the form of delusion, sā — that, sarvebhyaḥ — among all, mahattarā — greater.
The threefold tendencies which are said previously, the second among them is born of actions, in the form of delusion, that is greater among all.
येषां तल्लेशकश्चित्ते नास्ति मेधाविनस्तु ते ।
अपराधविहीनानां तेषां कामादिवासनाः ॥ ८० ॥
yeṣāṁ tal leśakaś citte nāsti medhāvinas tu te ।
aparādha-vihīnānāṁ teṣāṁ kāma-ādi-vāsanāḥ ॥ 80 ॥

yeṣām — whose, tal — that, leśakaḥ — trace, citte — in the mind, nāsti — is not, medhāvinaḥ — intelligent, tu — indeed, te — they, aparādha-vihīnānām — free from fault, teṣām — their, kāma-ādi-vāsanāḥ — tendencies of desire and others.
Whose mind has no trace of that, indeed they are intelligent, free from fault, their tendencies of desire and others are gone.
अभ्यासेनाविलीनाश्च ज्ञानस्याप्रतिबन्धिकाः ।
ततो वैराग्यादिकं तु न तेषामुपयुज्यते ॥ ८१ ॥
abhyāsena avilīnāś ca jñānasya apratibandhikāḥ ।
tato vairāgyādikaṁ tu na teṣām upayujyate ॥ 81 ॥

abhyāsena — by practice, avilīnāḥ — not dissolved, ca — and, jñānasya — of knowledge, apratibandhikāḥ — without obstacles, tataḥ — therefore, vairāgyādikam — dispassion and others, tu — indeed, na — not, teṣām — for them, upayujyate — is required.
By practice, those who have knowledge without obstacles, for them, dispassion and others are not required.
न वा भूयोऽपि मननं समाधिश्चोपयुज्यते ।
सकृच्छ्रणमात्रेण मननं ध्यानमेव च ॥ ८२ ॥
na vā bhūyo api mananaṁ samādhiś ca upayujyate ।
sakṛt śravaṇa-mātreṇa mananaṁ dhyānam eva ca ॥ 82 ॥

na — not, vā — or, bhūyaḥ api — again, mananaṁ — contemplation, samādhiḥ ca — and meditation, upayujyate — is required, sakṛt — once, śravaṇa-mātreṇa — by mere hearing, mananaṁ — contemplation, dhyānam — meditation, eva ca — and also.
For them, again, neither contemplation nor meditation is required. By mere hearing once, contemplation and meditation occur.
तत्काल ईषत्‌ संप्राप्य ज्ञातासन्दिग्धतत्पदाः ।
भवन्ति जीवन्मुक्तास्ते जनकप्रमुखा इव ॥ ८३ ॥
tatkāla īṣat saṁprāpya jñātā sandigdha tat-padāḥ ।
bhavanti jīvanmuktāḥ te janaka-pramukhā iva ॥ 83 ॥

tatkāle — at that time, īṣat — slightly, saṁprāpya — having attained, jñātāḥ — known, asandigdha — without doubt, tat-padāḥ — the supreme state, bhavanti — become, jīvanmuktāḥ — liberated while living, te — they, janaka-pramukhāḥ — like Janaka and others, iva — like.
At that time, having slightly attained, they become liberated while living, knowing the supreme state without doubt, like Janaka and others.
विपरीताभ्यासवशान्नैव तैः क्षपिताः खलु ।
कामादिवासनाः सम्यक्‌ सूक्ष्मा निर्मलबुद्धिभिः ॥ ८४ ॥
viparīta-abhyāsa-vaśāt na eva taiḥ kṣapitāḥ khalu ।
kāmādi-vāsanāḥ samyak sūkṣmā nirmala-buddhibhiḥ ॥ 84 ॥

viparīta-abhyāsa-vaśāt — by contrary practice, na eva — indeed not, taiḥ — by them, kṣapitāḥ — destroyed, khalu — indeed, kāma-ādi-vāsanāḥ — tendencies of desire and others, samyak — completely, sūkṣmāḥ — subtle, nirmala-buddhibhiḥ — by pure-minded ones.
By contrary practice, indeed, they have not destroyed the tendencies of desire and others completely, which are subtle, by pure-minded ones.
अतस्तैस्तत्पदे ज्ञाते चापि पूर्वस्थितास्तु ताः ।
कामादिवासनाः प्राग्वत्‌ प्रवर्तन्ते निरन्तरम्‌ ॥ ८५ ॥
ataḥ taiḥ tat-pade jñāte ca api pūrva-sthitāḥ tu tāḥ ।
kāma-ādi-vāsanāḥ prāgvat pravartante nirantaram ॥ 85 ॥

ataḥ — therefore, taiḥ — by them, tat-pade — in that state, jñāte — known, ca api — even, pūrva-sthitāḥ — previously existing, tu — but, tāḥ — they, kāma-ādi-vāsanāḥ — tendencies of desire and others, prāgvat — as before, pravartante — continue, nirantaram — continuously.
Therefore, by them, even in that liberated state known, the previously existing tendencies of desire and others continue as before, continuously.
न ताभिरीषद्वा बुद्धेस्तेषां लेपो भवेत्‌ क्वचित्‌ ।
विद्वद्भिस्ते हि संप्रोक्ता मुक्ताश्च बहुमानसाः ॥ ८६ ॥
na tābhiḥ īṣat vā buddheḥ teṣāṁ lepaḥ bhavet kvacit ।
vidvadbhiḥ te hi saṁproktā muktāḥ ca bahumānasāḥ ॥ 86 ॥

na — not, tābhiḥ — by them, īṣat vā — even a little, buddheḥ — of intellect, teṣāṁ — their, lepaḥ — taint, bhavet — becomes, kvacit — anywhere, vidvadbhiḥ — by the wise, te — they, hi — indeed, saṁproktāḥ — called, muktāḥ — liberated, ca — and, bahumānasāḥ — highly regarded.
But, there is not even a little taint on their intellect by them (tendencies). Indeed, they are called liberated and highly regarded by the wise.
राम कर्मवासनाभिरतिमूढं तु यन्मनः ।
तस्य ज्ञानं नैव भवेत्‌ शिवोदितमपि क्वचित्‌ ॥ ८७ ॥
rāma karma-vāsanābhiḥ ati-mūḍhaṁ tu yat manaḥ ।
tasya jñānaṁ na eva bhavet śiva-uditam api kvacit ॥ 87 ॥

rāma — O Rama, karma-vāsanābhiḥ — by tendencies of actions, ati-mūḍham — very deluded, tu — indeed, yat — which, manaḥ — mind, tasya — of that, jñānam — knowledge, na — not, eva — indeed, bhavet — becomes, śiva-uditam — spoken by Shiva, api — even, kvacit — anywhere.
O Rama, indeed, the mind which is very deluded by tendencies of actions, for this mind knowledge does not come anywhere, even if spoken by Shiva.
दृढापराधयुक्तानामपि न स्यात्‌ कथञ्चन ।
यस्यापराधरूपापि कर्मरूपापि वासना ॥ ८८ ॥
dṛḍha-aparādha-yuktānām api na syāt kathañcana ।
yasya aparādha-rūpā api karma-rūpā api vāsanā ॥ 88 ॥

dṛḍha-aparādha-yuktānām — connected with strong offenses, api — even, na — not, syāt — becomes, kathañcana — in any way, yasya — whose, aparādha-rūpā — in the form of offenses, api — also, karma-rūpā — in the form of actions, api — also, vāsanā — tendencies.
Connected with strong offenses, to them knowledge does not come in any way, whose tendencies are in the form of offenses and actions.
स्वल्पा कामात्मकाश्चापि बहुलास्तस्य भार्गव ।
बहुलश्रवणैस्तद्वद्‌ मननैश्च समाधिभिः ॥ ८९ ॥
svalpāḥ kāma-ātmakaḥ ca api bahulāḥ tasya bhārgava ।
bahula-śravaṇaiḥ tadvat mananaiḥ ca samādhibhiḥ ॥ 89 ॥

svalpāḥ — small, kāma-ātmakāḥ — desire-oriented, ca — and, api — also, bahulāḥ — abundant, tasya — his, bhārgava — O descendant of Bhrigu, bahula-śravaṇaiḥ — by abundant hearing, tadvat — similarly, mananaiḥ — by contemplation, ca — and, samādhibhiḥ — by meditations.
O descendant of Bhrigu, his small tendencies, even if desire-oriented, become abundant by abundant hearing, and similarly by contemplation and meditations.
चिरकालेन विज्ञानं बहुक्लेशेन जायते ।
तस्य व्यवहृतिः स्वल्पा तत्राभ्यासप्रकर्षतः ॥ ९० ॥
cira-kālena vijñānaṁ bahu-kleśena jāyate ।
tasya vyavahṛtiḥ svalpā tatra abhyāsa-prakarṣataḥ ॥ 90 ॥

cira-kālena — over a long time, vijñānam — knowledge, bahu-kleśena — with great difficulty, jāyate — arises, tasya — his, vyavahṛtiḥ — practice, svalpā — small, tatra — there, abhyāsa-prakarṣataḥ — by the intensity of practice.
Knowledge arises over a long time with great difficulty; but his practice is small there by due to the intensity of practice.
मनो यदि भवेन्नष्टप्रायं निर्वासनत्वतः ।
ज्ञानिनस्त्वीदृशाः प्रोक्ता मध्यमा नष्टमानसाः ॥ ९१ ॥
mano yadi bhavet naṣṭa-prāyaṁ nir-vāsanatvataḥ ।
jñāninaḥ tu īdṛśāḥ proktā madhyamāḥ naṣṭa-mānasāḥ ॥ 91 ॥

mano — mind, yadi — if, bhavet — becomes, naṣṭa-prāyam — almost destroyed, nir-vāsanatvataḥ — due to absence of tendencies, jñāninaḥ — of the knowledgeable ones, tu — indeed, īdṛśāḥ — such, proktāḥ — are called, madhyamāḥ — middle, naṣṭa-mānasāḥ — whose mind is destroyed.
If the mind becomes almost destroyed due to the absence of tendencies, indeed, such knowledgeable ones are called middle, whose mind is destroyed.
तेषामेव तु केषाञ्चिदभ्यासस्याप्रकर्षतः ।
वासनाविरलं यस्मादनष्टं मानसं भवेत्‌ ॥ ९२ ॥
teṣām eva tu keṣāñcit abhyāsasya aprakarṣataḥ ।
vāsanā-viralaṁ yasmāt anaṣṭaṁ mānasaṁ bhavet ॥ 92 ॥

teṣām — of them, eva — indeed, tu — but, keṣāñcit — some, abhyāsasya — of practice, aprakarṣataḥ — due to lack of intensity, vāsanā-viralam — with sparse tendencies, yasmāt — for which, anaṣṭam — not destroyed, mānasam — mind, bhavet — becomes.
Indeed, for some of them, due to lack of intensity in practice, the mind, with sparse tendencies, does not become destroyed.
समनस्कास्तु ते प्रोक्ता मन्दज्ञानयुतास्तु वै ।
केवलज्ञानिनस्त्वेते जीवन्मुक्तास्तथेतरे ॥ ९३ ॥
samanaskāḥ tu te proktā manda-jñāna-yutāḥ tu vai ।
kevala-jñāninaḥ tu ete jīvan-muktāḥ tathā itare ॥ 93 ॥

samanaskāḥ — having a mind, tu — but, te — they, proktāḥ — are called, manda-jñāna-yutāḥ — possessing dull knowledge, tu — but, vai — indeed, kevala-jñāninaḥ — possessing only knowledge, tu — indeed, ete — these, jīvan-muktāḥ — liberated while living, tathā — as well, itare — others.
But they are called those possessing dull knowledge, still having a mind, indeed, only those possessing only knowledge are liberated while living, as well as others.
केवलज्ञानिनो दृष्टदुःखभाजो भवन्ति हि ।
प्रारब्धतन्त्रास्ते प्रोक्ता देहान्ते मुक्तिभागिनः ॥ ९४ ॥
kevala-jñāninaḥ dṛṣṭa-duḥkha-bhājaḥ bhavanti hi ।
prārabdha-tantrāḥ te proktā deha-ante mukti-bhāginaḥ ॥ 94 ॥

kevala-jñāninaḥ — those possessing only knowledge, dṛṣṭa-duḥkha-bhājaḥ — experiencing visible suffering, bhavanti — become, hi — indeed, prārabdha-tantrāḥ — bound by prarabdha karma, te — they, proktāḥ — are called, deha-ante — at the end of the body, mukti-bhāginaḥ — having liberation.
Indeed, those possessing only knowledge, experiencing visible suffering, become bound by prarabdha karma, they are called having liberation at the end of the body.
ये नष्टमानसाः प्रोक्तास्तैः प्रारब्धं पराकृतम्‌ ।
मनोभूमौ तु प्रारब्धबीजं भोगाङ्कुरं भवेत्‌ ॥ ९५ ॥
ye naṣṭa-mānasāḥ proktās taiḥ prārabdhaṁ parākṛtam ।
mano-bhūmau tu prārabdha-bījaṁ bhoga-aṅkuraṁ bhavet ॥ 95 ॥

ye — those, naṣṭa-mānasāḥ — whose mind is destroyed, proktāḥ — are said, taiḥ — by them, prārabdham — prarabdha karma, parākṛtam — transcended, mano-bhūmau — in the field of the mind, tu — indeed, prārabdha-bījam — seed of prarabdha karma, bhoga-aṅkuraṁ — sprout of experience, bhavet — becomes.
Those whose mind is destroyed are said to have transcended prarabdha karma. In the field of the mind, the seed of prarabdha karma becomes the sprout of experience.
मनोभूमेरभावेन तत्‌ प्रारब्धं तु कालतः ।
कुमूलस्थं बीजमिव विनश्येन्नप्टशक्तिकम्‌ ॥ ९६ ॥
mano-bhūmeḥ abhāvena tat prārabdham tu kālataḥ ।
ku-mūlastham bījam iva vinaśyet anapṭa-śaktikam ॥ 96 ॥

mano-bhūmeḥ — of the field of the mind, abhāvena — due to absence, tat — that, prārabdham — prarabdha karma, tu — indeed, kālataḥ — over time, ku-mūlastham — rootless, bījam — seed, iva — like, vinaśyet — perishes, anapṭa-śaktikam — without potency.
Due to the absence of the field of the mind, that prarabdha karma, over time, perishes like a rootless seed without potency.
यथात्यन्तसुमेधावी युगपद्दश पञ्च च ।
कार्याणि कुरूते क्वापि भवेदस्खलितोऽपि च ॥ ९७ ॥
yathā atyanta-sumedhāvī yugapad daśa pañca ca ।
kāryāṇi kurute kvāpi bhavet askhalitaḥ api ca ॥ 97 ॥

yathā — as, atyanta-sumedhāvī — exceedingly intelligent, yugapad — simultaneously, daśa — ten, pañca ca — and five, kāryāṇi — actions, kurute — does, kvāpi — somewhere, bhavet — becomes, askhalitaḥ — without faltering, api ca — and also.
Just as an exceedingly intelligent person can simultaneously perform ten or five actions somewhere without faltering.
भूय एवंविधा दृष्टाः क्रियानैपुण्यसंश्रयाः ।
यथा गच्छन्‌ वदन्‌ कुर्वन्‌ युगपल्लक्ष्यते जनः ॥ ९८ ॥
bhūya evaṁ-vidhā dṛṣṭāḥ kriyā-naipuṇya-saṁśrayāḥ ।
yathā gacchan vadan kurvan yugapad lakṣyate janaḥ ॥ 98 ॥

bhūyaḥ — moreover, evaṁ-vidhāḥ — such, dṛṣṭāḥ — seen, kriyā-naipuṇya-saṁśrayāḥ — endowed with skill in action, yathā — as, gacchan — walking, vadan — speaking, kurvan — doing, yugapad — simultaneously, lakṣyate — is seen, janaḥ — a person.
Moreover, such people are seen endowed with skill in action, performing multiple activities simultaneously like walking, speaking, and doing.
तत्र चैकेन मनसा कथं स्यात्‌ त्रिविधा क्रिया ।
अध्येतृणां बहूनां च युगपल्लक्षयेद्‌ गुरुः ॥ ९९ ॥
tatra ca ekena manasā kathaṁ syāt trividhā kriyā ।
adhyetṛṇāṁ bahūnāṁ ca yugapad lakṣayet guruḥ ॥ 99 ॥

tatra — there, ca — and, ekena manasā — with one mind, katham — how, syāt — be, trividhā kriyā — threefold action, adhyetṛṇām — of students, bahūnām — many, ca — and, yugapad — simultaneously, lakṣayet — observes, guruḥ — the teacher.
In this case, with one mind, how can there be threefold action? And how does the teacher observe the many students simultaneously?
अपभ्रंशानुच्चरितं वर्णभेदव्यवस्थितम्‌ ।
राम यस्ते हतः शत्रुरर्जुनो हैहयाधिपः ॥ १०० ॥
apabhraṁśa-anucaritāṁ varṇa-bheda-vyavasthitam ।
rāma yaḥ te hataḥ śatruḥ arjunaḥ haihaya-ādhipaḥ ॥ 100 ॥

apabhraṁśa — improper pronunciation, anucaritām — those who follow, varṇa-bheda-vyavasthitam — established in the distinction of letters, rāma — O Rama, yaḥ — who, te — your, hataḥ — slain, śatruḥ — enemy, arjunaḥ — Arjuna, haihaya-ādhipaḥ — the lord of the Haihayas.
O Rama, who was your enemy, Arjuna, the lord of the Haihayas, who improperly followed the distinction of letters and was established in their differentiation, was slain.
सहस्रवाहुर्युगपद्‌ हेतिभिर्वहुभिः पृथक्‌ ।
अयुध्यदस्खलन्‌ क्वापि मेधावी दृष्ट एव ते ॥ १०१ ॥
sahasra-vāhur yugapad hetibhiḥ bahubhiḥ pṛthak ।
ayudhyat askhalan kvāpi medhāvī dṛṣṭa eva te ॥ 101 ॥

sahasra-vāhuḥ — with a thousand arms, yugapad — simultaneously, hetibhiḥ — with weapons, bahubhiḥ — many, pṛthak — separately, ayudhyat — fought, askhalan — without faltering, kvāpi — anywhere, medhāvī — wise, dṛṣṭaḥ — seen, eva — indeed, te — by you.
With a thousand arms, he fought simultaneously with many weapons separately, without faltering anywhere, indeed seen by you, the wise one.
तेषां मनो बहुविधं भूत्वा तत्तत्क्रमानुगम्‌ ।
यथा कार्य बहुविधं साधयेत्तद्वदेव हि ॥ १०२ ॥
teṣāṁ mano bahu-vidhaṁ bhūtvā tat-tat kramānugam ।
yathā kāryaṁ bahu-vidhaṁ sādhayet tadvat eva hi ॥ 102 ॥

teṣām — their, mano — mind, bahu-vidham — multifaceted, bhūtvā — becoming, tat-tat — respective, krama-anugam — following the sequence, yathā — as, kāryam — action, bahu-vidham — many kinds, sādhayet — accomplish, tadvat — likewise, eva — indeed, hi — surely.
Their mind, becoming multifaceted, following the respective sequence, accomplishes many kinds of actions, likewise indeed, surely.
उत्तमज्ञानिनामात्मदृष्टिर्बाह्यगतापि च ।
अविरुद्धा सर्वदा स्याद्येषां ते बहुमानसाः ॥ १०३ ॥
uttama-jñāninām ātma-dṛṣṭiḥ bāhya-gatā api ca ।
aviruddhā sarvadā syāt yeṣāṁ te bahu-mānasāḥ ॥ 103 ॥

uttama-jñāninām — of the highest knowers, ātma-dṛṣṭiḥ — self-perception, bāhya-gatā — externally directed, api — even, ca — and, aviruddhā — undisturbed, sarvadā — always, syāt — is, yeṣām — whose, te — they, bahu-mānasāḥ — having many minds.
Similarly, the highest knowers' of self-perception, even when externally directed, always remains undisturbed; they are said to have many minds.
तत्‌ प्रारब्धं मनोभूमौ भवेदङ्कुरितं पृथक्‌ ।
भवेद्‌ ज्ञानाग्निना दग्धं भूतं भूतं पुनः पुनः ॥ १०४ ॥
tat prārabdham mano-bhūmau bhavet aṅkuritam pṛthak ।
bhavet jñāna-agninā dagdham bhūtaṁ bhūtaṁ punaḥ punaḥ ॥ 104 ॥

tat — that, prārabdham — prarabdha karma, mano-bhūmau — in the field of the mind, bhavet — becomes, aṅkuritam — sprouted, pṛthak — separately, bhavet — becomes, jñāna-agninā — by the fire of knowledge, dagdham — burnt, bhūtaṁ bhūtaṁ — each time, punaḥ punaḥ — again and again.
That prarabdha karma, sprouted separately in the field of the mind, becomes burnt by the fire of knowledge each time, again and again.
प्रारब्धबीजाङ्कुरः स्यात्‌ सुखदुःखसमागमः ।
तद्विमर्शः फलं प्रोक्तं कुतो दग्धाङ्कुरे फलम्‌ ॥ १०५ ॥
prārabdha-bīja-aṅkuraḥ syāt sukha-duḥkha-samāgamaḥ ।
tat-vimarśaḥ phalaṁ proktaṁ kuto dagdha-aṅkure phalam ॥ 105 ॥

prārabdha-bīja-aṅkuraḥ — sprout of prarabdha seed, syāt — becomes, sukha-duḥkha-samāgamaḥ — union of pleasure and pain, tat-vimarśaḥ — reflection on that, phalam — fruit, proktam — is said, kuto — wherefrom, dagdha-aṅkure — burnt sprout, phalam — fruit.
The sprout of the prarabdha seed has a union of pleasure and pain; reflection on that is said to be the fruit. Wherefrom does the fruit come from a burnt sprout?
आहृतैरनुसन्धानैस्तेषां व्यवहृतिर्भवेत्‌ ।
यथा प्रौढो हि बालेन सह खेलन्‌ हि दृश्यते ॥ १०६ ॥
āhṛtaiḥ anusandhānaiḥ teṣāṁ vyavahṛtiḥ bhavet ।
yathā prauḍhaḥ hi bālena saha khelan hi dṛśyate ॥ 106 ॥

āhṛtaiḥ — by gathered insights, anusandhānaiḥ — through recollections, teṣām — their, vyavahṛtiḥ — interaction, bhavet — becomes, yathā — as, prauḍhaḥ — mature, hi — indeed, bālena — with a child, saha — together, khelan — playing, hi — indeed, dṛśyate — is seen.
Their interaction becomes through gathered insights and recollections, just as a mature person is seen playing with a child.
हृष्टो विषण्णश्च शिलागजादीनां विनाशने ।
एवं हृष्यन्ति सीदन्ति कार्येषु बहुमानसाः ॥ १०७ ॥
hṛṣṭaḥ viṣaṇṇaḥ ca śilā-gaja-ādīnāṁ vināśane ।
evaṁ hṛṣyanti sīdanti kāryeṣu bahu-mānasāḥ ॥ 107 ॥

hṛṣṭaḥ — pleased, viṣaṇṇaḥ — distressed, ca — and, śilā-gaja-ādīnāṁ — of stone and elephant, vināśane — in destruction, evaṁ — thus, hṛṣyanti — rejoice, sīdanti — and grieve, kāryeṣu — in actions, bahu-mānasāḥ — those with many minds.
Like an elephant is pleased or distressed in the destruction of stone by the elephant, thus they rejoice and grieve in actions, those with many minds.
यथाऽन्यकार्यसक्तस्य हर्षोद्वेगौ न चान्तरौ ।
एवं तेषां व्यवहृतौ समा सर्वत्र संस्थितिः ॥ १०८ ॥
yathā anya-kārya-saktasya harṣa-udvegau na ca antarau ।
evaṁ teṣāṁ vyavahṛtau samā sarvatra saṁsthitiḥ ॥ 108 ॥

yathā — as, anya-kārya-saktasya — of one engaged in actions, harṣa-udvegau — joy and agitation, na ca — not, antarau — internally, evaṁ — thus, teṣām — their, vyavahṛtau — in conduct, samā — equal, sarvatra — everywhere, saṁsthitiḥ — stability.
As there is no internal joy or agitation for the one engaged in particular action, thus their conduct is equal and stable everywhere.
मेधाविनां ज्ञानिनां तु वासनानाशहेतवे ।
विरुद्धवासनाभ्यासनिरोधादेरभावतः ॥ १०९ ॥
medhāvināṁ jñānināṁ tu vāsanā-nāśa-hetave ।
Viruddha-vāsanā-abhyāsa-nirodha-ādi-abhāvataḥ ॥ 109 ॥

medhāvināṁ — of the intelligent, jñānināṁ — of the knowledgeable, tu — but, vāsanā-nāśa-hetave — for the destruction of tendencies, viruddha-vāsanā-abhyāsa-nirodha-ādi — by the practice of opposing tendencies, abhāvataḥ — due to absence.
For the intelligent and knowledgeable ones, due to the absence of the practice of opposing tendencies, the destruction of tendencies occurs.
अनुवृत्तिर्भवेत्‌ पूर्ववासनाऽनाशहेतुतः ।
अतः केचित्‌ कर्मनिष्ठाः कामिनः क्रोधिनोऽपरे ॥ ११० ॥
anuvṛttiḥ bhavet pūrva-vāsanā-anāśa-hetutaḥ ।
ataḥ kecit karma-niṣṭhāḥ kāminaḥ krodhinaḥ apare ॥ 110 ॥

anuvṛttiḥ — continuation, bhavet — becomes, pūrva-vāsanā-anāśa-hetutaḥ — due to the absence of destruction of previous tendencies, ataḥ — thus, kecit — some, karma-niṣṭhāḥ — devoted to actions, kāminaḥ — desirous, krodhinaḥ — angry, apare — others.
Due to the absence of destruction of previous tendencies, the continuation becomes thus; some are devoted to actions, others are desirous and angry.
उत्तमनज्ञानिनो भान्ति विविधाचारतत्पराः ।
समनस्कस्तत्र यो वै मन्दज्ञानी निरूपितः ॥ १११ ॥
uttama-an-jñānino bhānti vividha-ācāra-tatparāḥ ।
samanaskaḥ tatra yo vai manda-jñānī nirūpitaḥ ॥ 111 ॥

uttama-an-jñāninaḥ — highest and knowledgable ones, bhānti — shine, vividha-ācāra-tatparāḥ — devoted to various practices, samanaskaḥ — one with a steady mind, tatra — there, yo — who, vai — indeed, manda-jñānī — slow-witted, nirūpitaḥ — described.
The highest and knowledgeable ones shine, devoted to various practices. There, indeed, the one with a steady mind is described as a slow-witted person.
तेनापि वेद्यमखिलमसत्यत्वेन निश्चितम्‌ ।
स्वरूपवित्तौ नो किञ्चिद्भासते हि समाधिषु ॥ ११२ ॥
tena api vedyam akhilam asatyatvena niścitam ।
svarūpa-vittau no kiñcid bhāsate hi samādhiṣu ॥ 112 ॥

tena api — by him also, vedyam — knowledge, akhilam — all, asatyatvena — as false, niścitam — determined, svarūpa-vittau — in self-realization, no kiñcid — nothing at all, bhāsate — shines, hi — indeed, samādhiṣu — in samadhis.
By him also, all knowledge is determined as false. In self-realization, nothing at all shines in samadhis.
समाधिर्वै स्वरूपस्य विमर्शो नान्य उच्यते ।
निर्विकल्पस्वरूपं तु सर्वाश्रयतया सदा ॥ ११३ ॥
samādhir vai svarūpasya vimarśo nānya ucyate ।
nirvikalpa-svarūpaṁ tu sarvāśrayatayā sadā ॥ 113 ॥

samādhiḥ — samadhi, vai — indeed, svarūpasya — of the true nature, vimarśaḥ — reflection, na anya — not another, ucyate — is said, nirvikalpa-svarūpam — the state of non-duality, tu — indeed, sarvāśrayatayā — as the foundation of all, sadā — always.
Samadhi is indeed the reflection of the true nature; nothing else is said to be so. The state of non-duality, as the foundation of all, always.
स्फुरत्येव हि सर्वेषां तदस्फूर्तौ न किञ्चन ।
तथा विकल्पविकलं स्फुरेत्‌ प्रोक्तदशासु च ॥ ११४ ॥
sphurati eva hi sarveṣāṁ tad asphūrtau na kiñcana ।
tathā vikalpa-vikalaṁ sphuret prokta-daśāsu ca ॥ 114 ॥

sphurati — shines, eva — indeed, hi — certainly, sarveṣām — of all, tad — that, asphūrtau — in non-shining, na kiñcana — nothing at all, tathā — likewise, vikalpa-vikalam — free from thoughts, sphuret — shines, prokta-daśāsu — in the stated states, ca — and.
It certainly shines in all, and in non-shining, there is nothing at all. Likewise, it shines free from thoughts in the stated states.
तावता नहि सर्वेषां समाधिः स्याद्धि भार्गव ।
ये तद्वि मर्शसंयुक्ताः स तेषामेव संस्मृतः ॥ ११५ ॥
tāvatā nahi sarveṣāṁ samādhiḥ syād dhi bhārgava ।
ye tad vimarśa-saṁyuktāḥ sa teṣām eva saṁsmṛtaḥ ॥ 115 ॥

tāvatā — by that much, nahi — not, sarveṣām — of all, samādhiḥ — samadhi, syāt — is, hi — indeed, bhārgava — O Bhargava, ye — those, tad vimarśa-saṁyuktāḥ — connected with that reflection, sa — that, teṣām — of them, eva — indeed, saṁsmṛtaḥ — is remembered.
By that much, samadhi is not achieved by all, indeed, O Bhargava. But, only those who are connected with that reflection are remembered.
व्यवहारपरा वित्तिरपि वेद्यविवर्जिता ।
विदितं नाभसं नैल्यं यथा भूयोऽवलोकने ॥ ११६ ॥
vyavahāra-parā vittir api vedya-vivarjitā ।
viditaṁ nābhasaṁ nailyaṁ yathā bhūyo'valokane ॥ 116 ॥

vyavahāra-parā — engrossed in worldly dealings, vittiḥ — consciousness, api — even, vedya-vivarjitā — devoid of knowables, viditam — known, nābhasaṁ — to the sky, nailyaṁ — blueness, yathā — as, bhūyaḥ — again, avalokane — in seeing.
Even the consciousness engrossed in worldly dealings is devoid of knowables, known as the sky's blueness is seen again.
असत्यत्वेन विज्ञातं न वित्तिस्तेन संयुता ।
अन्यथा नैव भेदः स्यात्तत्त्वातत्वविभासयोः ॥ ११७ ॥
asatyatvena vijñātam na vittiḥ tena saṁyutā ।
anyathā naiva bhedaḥ syāt tattva-atattva-vibhāsayoḥ ॥ 117 ॥

asatyatvena — as false, vijñātam — known, na vittiḥ — consciousness, tena saṁyutā — connected with that, anyathā — otherwise, naiva — not, bhedaḥ — difference, syāt — would be, tattva-atattva-vibhāsayoḥ — between truth and untruth.
Known as false, the consciousness is not connected with that; otherwise, there would be no difference between truth and untruth.
तथाऽसत्यगृहोतस्य वेद्यस्य नहि वेदने ।
सम्बन्धः कुत्रचिद्वा स्याज्ज्ञानिनामत एव हि ॥ ११८ ॥
tathā asatya-gṛha-utasya vedyasya nahi vedane ।
sambandhaḥ kutracid vā syāt jñāninām ata eva hi ॥ 118 ॥

tathā — likewise, asatya-gṛha-utasya — grasping the unreal, vedyasya — of the knowable, nahi vedane — not in knowledge, sambandhaḥ — connection, kutracit vā — somewhere, syāt — would be, jñāninām — of the wise, ata eva — thus indeed, hi — certainly.
Likewise, grasping the unreal, there is no connection in knowledge somewhere; thus indeed, it is certainly stated for the wise.
वेद्यहीना भवेद्वित्तिर्बाधितस्य विभासनात्‌ ।
अमनस्कस्य सुतरां यतः सा चोन्मनी दशा ॥ ११९ ॥
vedya-hīnā bhavet vittiḥ bādhitasya vibhāsanāt ।
amanaskasya sutarāṁ yataḥ sā ca unmanī daśā ॥ 119 ॥

vedya-hīnā — devoid of knowables, bhavet — becomes, vittiḥ — consciousness, bādhitasya — of the negated, vibhāsanāt — due to shining, amanaskasya — of the mindless, sutarāṁ — especially, yataḥ — because, sā — that, ca — and, unmanī daśā — state of unmani.
Consciousness becomes devoid of knowables due to the shining of the negated, especially of the mindless, because that is the state of unmani.
मनो वै निश्चलं यत्र तदुक्तं चोन्मनी दशा ।
मनसश्चलनं तत्‌ स्यात्‌ सत्यवेद्यस्य सङ्गतिः ॥ १२० ॥
mano vai niścalaṁ yatra tad uktaṁ ca unmanī daśā ।
manasaś calanaṁ tat syāt satya-vedyasya saṅgatiḥ ॥ 120 ॥

mano — mind, vai — indeed, niścalaṁ — still, yatra — where, tat — that, uktam — said, ca — and, unmanī daśā — state of unmani, manasaś — of the mind, calanaṁ — movement, tat — that, syāt — would be, satya-vedyasya — of the true knowable, saṅgatiḥ — connection.
Where the mind is still, that is said to be the state of unmani; the movement of the mind would be the connection with the true knowable.
उत्तमज्ञानिनश्चैते दशे युगपदास्थिते ।
स सर्वदा व्युत्थितश्च समाधिस्थश्च भार्गव ॥ १२१॥
uttama-jñāninaś ca ete daśe yugapad āsthitā ।
saḥ sarvadā vyutthitaś ca samādhi-sthaś ca bhārgava ॥ 121 ॥

uttama-jñāninaḥ — of the highest wise ones, ca — and, ete — these, daśe — states, yugapad — simultaneously, āsthitā — established, saḥ — he, sarvadā — always, vyutthitaḥ — active, ca — and, samādhi-sthaḥ — in samadhi, ca — and, bhārgava — O Bhargava.
These states are simultaneously established in the highest wise ones; he is always both active and in samadhi, O Bhargava.
तस्मात्तस्यापि वेद्येन रहिता वित्तिरास्थिता ।
एवमेतद्धि संप्रोक्तं पृष्टं यद्यत्‌ पुरा त्वया ॥ १२२ ॥
tasmāt tasya api vedyena rahitā vittiḥ āsthitā ।
evam etad dhi saṁproktaṁ pṛṣṭaṁ yad yat purā tvayā ॥ 122 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, tasya api — even of him, vedyena — by the knowable, rahitā — devoid, vittiḥ — consciousness, āsthitā — established, evam — thus, etad — this, hi — indeed, saṁproktaṁ — has been said, pṛṣṭaṁ — asked, yad yat — whatever, purā — before, tvayā — by you.
Therefore, even his consciousness is established devoid of the knowable; thus, this has been said as asked by you before.

colophon.en: Thus ends the nineteenth chapter named "Discussion on the Distinction of States of Knowledge" in the revered Tripura Rahasya.

lines.text: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि पुरा वृत्तं शृणुष्व तत्‌ ।
पुरा ब्रह्मसभामध्ये सत्यलोकेऽतिपावने ॥ १ ॥
atra te vartayiṣyāmi purā vṛttaṁ śṛṇuṣva tat ।
purā brahmasabhāmadhye satyaloke' tipāvane ॥ 1 ॥

atra te — here to you, vartayiṣyāmi — I will narrate, purā vṛttaṁ — what happened in ancient times, śṛṇuṣva — listen, tat — that, purā — long ago, brahmasabhāmadhye — in the assembly of Brahma, satyaloke — in the highest realm, atipāvane — very pure.
Here, I will narrate to you what happened in ancient times. Listen, long ago, in the assembly of Brahma, in the very pure highest realm.
ज्ञानप्रसङ्गः समभूत्‌ सूक्ष्मात्सूक्ष्मविमर्शनः ।
सनकाद्या वसिष्ठश्च पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः ॥ २ ॥
jñānaprasaṅgaḥ samabhūt sūkṣmātsūkṣmavimarśanaḥ ।
sanakādyā vasiṣṭhaśca pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ ॥ 2 ॥

jñānaprasaṅgaḥ — a discussion of knowledge, samabhūt — took place, sūkṣmātsūkṣmavimarśanaḥ — subtle and deeper deliberation, sanakādyā — Sanaka and others, vasiṣṭhaḥ ca — and Vasistha, pulastyaḥ — Pulastya, pulahaḥ — Pulaha, kratuḥ — Kratu.
A discussion of knowledge took place, with subtle and deeper deliberation. Present were Sanaka and others, Vasistha, Pulastya, Pulaha, and Kratu.
भृगुरत्रिरङ्गिराश्च प्रचेता नारदस्तथा ।
च्यवनो वामदेवश्च विश्वामित्रोऽथ गौतमः ॥ ३ ॥
bhṛgur atrir aṅgirāś ca pracetā nāradas tathā ।
cyavano vāmadevaś ca viśvāmitro' tha gautamaḥ ॥ 3 ॥

bhṛguḥ — Bhrigu, atriḥ — Atri, aṅgirāḥ ca — and Angiras, pracetā — Praceta, nāradaḥ tathā — and Narada, cyavanaḥ — Cyavana, vāmadevaḥ ca — and Vamadeva, viśvāmitraḥ — Visvamitra, atha — also, gautamaḥ — Gautama.
Present were Bhrigu, Atri, Angiras, Praceta, Narada, Cyavana, Vamadeva, Visvamitra, and Gautama.
शुक्रः पराशरो व्यासः कण्वः काश्यप एव च ।
दक्षः सुमन्तुः शङ्खश्च लिखितो देवलोऽपि च ॥ ४ ॥
śukraḥ parāśaro vyāsaḥ kaṇvaḥ kāśyapa eva ca ।
dakṣaḥ sumantuḥ śaṅkhaś ca likhito devalo' pi ca ॥ 4 ॥

śukraḥ — Sukra, parāśaraḥ — Parashara, vyāsaḥ — Vyasa, kaṇvaḥ — Kanva, kāśyapaḥ eva ca — and Kashyapa, dakṣaḥ — Daksha, sumantuḥ — Sumantu, śaṅkhaḥ ca — and Shankha, likhitaḥ — Likhita, devalaḥ api ca — and Devala.
Present were Sukra, Parashara, Vyasa, Kanva, Kashyapa, Daksha, Sumantu, Shankha, Likhita, and Devala.
एवमन्ये ऋषिगणा राजर्षिप्रवरा अपि ।
सर्वे समुदितास्तत्र ब्रह्मसत्रे महत्तरे ॥ ५ ॥
evam anye ṛṣigaṇā rājarṣipravarā api ।
sarve samuditās tatra brahmasatre mahattare ॥ 5 ॥

evam — thus, anye — others, ṛṣigaṇā — groups of sages, rājarṣipravarā api — and best among royal sages, sarve — all, samuditāḥ — gathered, tatra — there, brahmasatre — in the great assembly of Brahma, mahattare — in the grand.
Thus, other groups of sages and the best among royal sages all gathered there in the grand assembly of Brahma.
मोमांसां चक्रुरत्युच्चैः सूक्ष्मात्सूक्ष्मनिरूपणैः ।
ब्रह्माणं तत्र पप्रच्छुरृषयः सर्व एव ते ॥ ६ ॥
momāṁsāṁ cakrur atyuccaiḥ sūkṣmāt sūkṣmanirūpaṇaiḥ ।
brahmāṇaṁ tatra papracchur ṛṣayaḥ sarva eva te ॥ 6 ॥

momāṁsāṁ — deliberation, cakruḥ — performed, atyuccaiḥ — very intensely, sūkṣmāt — subtle, sūkṣmanirūpaṇaiḥ — with subtle explanations, brahmāṇaṁ — to Brahma, tatra — there, papracchuḥ — asked, ṛṣayaḥ — sages, sarva eva te — all of them.
The deliberation was performed very intensely, with subtle explanations. The sages there asked Brahma.
भगवन्‌ ज्ञानिनो लोके वयं ज्ञातपरावराः ।
तेषां नो विविधा भाति स्थितिः प्रकृतिभेदतः ॥ ७ ॥
bhagavan jñānino loke vayaṁ jñātaparāvarāḥ ।
teṣāṁ no vividhā bhāti sthitiḥ prakṛtibhedataḥ ॥ 7 ॥

bhagavan — O Lord, jñāninaḥ — the enlightened ones, loke — in the world, vayaṁ — we, jñātaparāvarāḥ — knowers of the highest and the lowest, teṣāṁ — their, no — our, vividhā — various, bhāti — appear, sthitiḥ — states, prakṛtibhedataḥ — due to differences in nature.
O Lord, we knowers of the highest and the lowest in the world see various states of the enlightened ones due to differences in nature.
केचित्‌ सदा समाधिस्था केचिन्मीमांसने रताः ।
अपरे भक्तिनिर्मग्नाश्चाव्ये कर्मसमाश्रयाः ॥ ८ ॥
kecit sadā samādhisthā kecin mīmāṁsane ratāḥ ।
apare bhaktinirmagnāś cā' 'vye karmasamāśrayāḥ ॥ 8 ॥

kecit — some, sadā — always, samādhisthāḥ — absorbed in samadhi, kecit — some, mīmāṁsane ratāḥ — engaged in deliberation, apare — others, bhaktinirmagnāḥ — immersed in devotion, ca — and, avyekarmasamāśrayāḥ — resting on imperishable actions.
Some are always absorbed in samadhi, some are engaged in deliberation, others are immersed in devotion, and others still rest on imperishable actions.
व्यवहारपरास्त्वेके बहिर्मुखनरा इव ।
तेषु श्रेयान्‌ हि कतम एतन्नो वक्तुमर्हसि ॥ ९ ॥
vyavahāraparās tveke bahirmukhanarā iva ।
teṣu śreyān hi katama etan no vaktum arhasi ॥ 9 ॥

vyavahāraparāḥ — engrossed in worldly dealings, tu eke — but some, bahirmukhanarāḥ iva — like outward-facing men, teṣu — among them, śreyān — better, hi — indeed, katama — which, etan — this, no — to us, vaktum arhasi — you should tell.
But some are engrossed in worldly dealings, like outward-facing men. Among them, who is better? This you should tell us.
स्वस्वपक्षं वयं विद्मः श्रेयांसमिति वै विधे ।
इति पृष्टोऽवदद्‌ ब्रह्मा मत्वाऽनाश्वस्तमानसान्‌ ॥ १० ॥
svasvapakṣaṁ vayaṁ vidmaḥ śreyāṁsam iti vai vidhe ।
iti pṛṣṭo' vadad brahmā matvā' nāśvastamānasān ॥ 10 ॥

svasvapakṣaṁ — our own standpoint, vayaṁ — we, vidmaḥ — know, śreyāṁsam — better, iti — thus, vai — indeed, vidhe — O Lord, iti — thus, pṛṣṭaḥ — asked, avadad — said, brahmā — Brahma, matvā — thinking, anāśvastamānasān — unsettled minds.
We know our own standpoint to be better, O Lord. Thus asked, Brahma said, thinking of their unsettled minds.
मुनीन्द्रा नाहमप्येतद्वेद्मि सर्वात्मना ततः ।
जानीयादिममर्थं तु सर्वज्ञः परमेश्वरः ॥ ११ ॥
munīndrā nāham apy etad vedmi sarvātmanā tataḥ ।
jānīyād imam arthaṁ tu sarvajñaḥ parameśvaraḥ ॥ 11 ॥

munīndrāḥ — O great sages, na aham — I do not, api etad — even this, vedmi — know, sarvātmanā — entirely, tataḥ — therefore, jānīyāt — would know, imam arthaṁ — this matter, tu — indeed, sarvajñaḥ — the omniscient, parameśvaraḥ — Supreme Lord.
O great sages, I do not know this entirely. Therefore, the omniscient Supreme Lord would know this matter.
तत्र यामोऽथ संप्रष्टुमित्युक्त्वा तत्र तैर्ययौ ।
सङ्गम्य देवदेवेशं विष्णुनाभिसमागतम्‌ ॥ १२ ॥
tatra yāmo' tha saṁpraṣṭum ity uktvā tatra tair yayau ।
saṅgamya devadeveśaṁ viṣṇunābhisamāgatam ॥ 12 ॥

tatra — there, yāmaḥ — let us go, atha — then, saṁpraṣṭum — to ask, iti — thus, uktvā — having said, tatra — there, taiḥ — with them, yayau — he went, saṅgamya — meeting, devadeveśaṁ — the Lord of Lords, viṣṇunā — with Vishnu, abhisamāgatam — united.
Let us go there to ask, thus having said, he went there with them, meeting the Lord of Lords, they united with Vishnu.
पप्रच्छ ऋषिमुख्यानां प्रश्नं तं लोकसृड्‌ विधिः ।
प्रश्नं निशम्य च शिवो ज्ञात्वा विधिमनोगतम्‌ ॥ १३ ॥
papraccha ṛṣimukhyānāṁ praśnaṁ taṁ lokasṛḍ vidhiḥ ।
praśnaṁ niśamya ca śivo jñātvā vidhimanogatam ॥ 13 ॥

papraccha — asked, ṛṣimukhyānāṁ — of the chief sages, praśnaṁ — question, taṁ — that, lokasṛḍ — creator of the world, vidhiḥ — Brahma, praśnaṁ — question, niśamya — having heard, ca — and, śivaḥ — Shiva, jñātvā — knowing, vidhi-mano-gatam — the intention of Brahma's mind.
Brahma, the creator of the world, asked that question of the chief sages. Having heard the question, Shiva, knowing the intention of Brahma's mind.
मत्वाऽनाश्वस्तमनस ऋषीन्‌ देवो व्यचिन्तयत्‌ ।
किञ्चिदुक्तं मयाऽत्रापि व्यर्थमेव भवेन्ननु ॥ १४ ॥
matvā' nāśvastamanasa ṛṣīn devo vyacintayat ।
kiñcid uktaṁ mayā' trapiva vyartham eva bhaven nanu ॥ 14 ॥

matvā — thinking, anāśvastamanasaḥ — unsettled minds, ṛṣīn — of the sages, devaḥ — the god, vyacintayat — thought, kiñcit — something, uktam — said, mayā — by me, atra api — even here, vyartham — useless, eva — indeed, bhavet — would be, nanu — certainly.
Thinking of the unsettled minds of the sages, the god thought, "Even if I say something here, it would indeed be useless."
स्वपक्षत्वेन जानीयुरृषयोऽश्रद्धया युताः ।
इति मत्वा प्रत्युवाच देवदेवो महेश्वरः ॥ १५ ॥
svapakṣatvena jānīyur ṛṣayo' śraddhayā yutāḥ ।
iti matvā pratyuvāca devadevo maheśvaraḥ ॥ 15 ॥

svapakṣatvena — due to their own standpoint, jānīyuḥ — would know, ṛṣayaḥ — sages, aśraddhayā yutāḥ — filled with disbelief, iti — thus, matvā — thinking, pratyuvāca — replied, devadevaḥ — the Lord of Lords, maheśvaraḥ — Maheshwara.
Thinking that the sages, filled with disbelief, would know due to their own standpoint, Maheshwara, the Lord of Lords, replied.
शृणुध्वं मुनयो नाहमप्येतद्वेद्मि सुस्फुटम्‌ ।
अतो विद्यां भगवतीं ध्यायामः परमेश्वरीम्‌ ॥ १६ ॥
śṛṇudhvaṁ munayo nāham apy etad vedmi susphuṭam ।
ato vidyāṁ bhagavatīṁ dhyāyāmaḥ parameśvarīm ॥ 16 ॥

śṛṇudhvaṁ — listen, munayaḥ — O sages, na aham api — I do not even, etad — this, vedmi — know, susphuṭam — clearly, ataḥ — therefore, vidyām — knowledge, bhagavatīm — the divine, dhyāyāmaḥ — let us meditate, parameśvarīm — Supreme Goddess.
Listen, O sages, I do not even know this clearly. Therefore, let us meditate on the divine knowledge, the Supreme Goddess.
तत्प्रसादान्निगूढार्थमपि विद्मस्ततः परम्‌ ।
इत्युक्ता मुनयः सर्वे विधिविष्णुशिवैः सह ॥ १७ ॥
tatprasādān nigūḍhārtham api vidmas tataḥ param ।
ityuktā munayaḥ sarve vidhiviṣṇuśivaiḥ saha ॥ 17 ॥

tatprasādāt — by her grace, nigūḍhārtham — hidden meaning, api — even, vidmaḥ — we know, tataḥ param — thereafter, iti uktā — thus spoken, munayaḥ — sages, sarve — all, vidhiviṣṇuśivaiḥ saha — with Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva.
By her grace, we will know even the hidden meaning thereafter. Thus spoken, all the sages, along with Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva.
दध्युर्विद्यां महेशानीं त्रिपुरां चिच्छरीरिणीम्‌ ।
एवं सर्वैरभिध्याता त्रिपुरां चिच्छरीरिणीम् ॥ १८ ॥
dadhyur vidyāṁ maheśānīṁ tripurāṁ ciccharīriṇīm ।
evaṁ sarvair abhidhyātā tripurāṁ ciccharīriṇīm ॥ 18 ॥

dadhyuḥ — meditated, vidyām — on the knowledge, maheśānīm — of Maheshani, tripurām — Tripura, ciccharīriṇīm — embodying consciousness, evaṁ — thus, sarvaiḥ — by all, abhidhyātā — meditated upon, tripurām — Tripura, ciccharīriṇīm — embodying consciousness.
They meditated on the knowledge of Maheshani, Tripura, embodying consciousness. Thus, all meditated upon Tripura, embodying consciousness.
आविरासीच्चिदाकाशमयी शब्दमयी परा ।
अभवद्‌ मेघगम्भीरनिःस्वनो गगनाङ्गणे ॥ १९ ॥
āvirāsīc cidākāśamayī śabdamayī parā ।
abhavad meghagambhīraniḥsvano gaganāṅgaṇe ॥ 19 ॥

āvirāsīt — appeared, cidākāśamayī — composed of consciousness and space, śabdamayī — composed of sound, parā — the Supreme, abhavat — there was, meghagambhīraniḥsvanaḥ — deep sound like that of thunder, gaganāṅgaṇe — in the sky.
The Supreme, composed of consciousness and space, composed of sound, appeared. There was a deep sound like that of thunder in the sky.
वदन्त्वृषिगणाः किं वो ध्याता तद्‌ द्रुतमीहितम्‌ ।
मत्पराणां हि केषाञ्चिन्न हीयेताभिवाञ्छितम्‌ ॥ २० ॥
vadantv ṛṣigaṇāḥ kiṁ vo dhyātā tad drutam īhitam ।
matparāṇāṁ hi keṣāñcin na hīyetābhivāñchitam ॥ 20 ॥

vadantu — let speak, ṛṣigaṇāḥ — the sages, kiṁ — what, vaḥ — your, dhyātā — meditated, tad — that, drutam — quickly, īhitam — desired, matparāṇāṁ — of my devotees, hi — indeed, keṣāñcit — of some, na hīyeta — not fail, abhivāñchitam — desire.
Let the sages speak, what did you meditate upon and quickly desire? Indeed, for some of my devotees, the desired does not fail.
इति श्रुत्वा परां वाणीं प्रणेमुर्मुनिपुङ्गवाः ।
ब्रह्मादयोऽपि तदनु तुष्टवुर्विविधैः स्तवैः ॥ २१ ॥
iti śrutvā parāṁ vāṇīṁ praṇemur munipuṅgavāḥ ।
brahmādayo'pi tadanu tuṣṭavur vividhaḥ stavaiḥ ॥ 21 ॥

iti — thus, śrutvā — having heard, parām — supreme, vāṇīm — words, praṇemuḥ — bowed down, munipuṅgavāḥ — best of sages, brahmādayaḥ — Brahma and others, api — also, tadanu — then, tuṣṭavuḥ — praised, vividhaḥ — various, stavaiḥ — hymns.
Having heard the supreme words, the best of sages bowed down. Then, Brahma and others praised with various hymns.
अथ प्रोचुरृषिगणा विद्यां तां त्रिपुरेश्वरीम्‌ ।
नमस्तुभ्यं महेशानि श्रीविद्ये त्रिपुरेश्वरि ॥ २२ ॥
atha procur ṛṣigaṇā vidyāṁ tāṁ tripureśvarīm ।
namas tubhyaṁ maheśāni śrīvidye tripureśvari ॥ 22 ॥

atha — then, procuḥ — spoke, ṛṣigaṇāḥ — group of sages, vidyām — knowledge, tām — that, tripureśvarīm — of Tripureshwari, namas — salutation, tubhyam — to you, maheśāni — O great Goddess, śrīvidye — O sacred knowledge, tripureśvari — O ruler of Tripura.
Then the group of sages spoke that knowledge of Tripureshwari. Salutation to you, O great Goddess, O sacred knowledge, O ruler of Tripura.
अशेषोत्पादयित्री त्वं स्थापयित्री निजात्मनि ।
विलापयित्री सर्वस्य परमेश्वरि ते नमः ॥ २३ ॥
aśeṣotpādayitrī tvaṁ sthāpayitrī nijātmani ।
vilāpayitrī sarvasya parameśvari te namaḥ ॥ 23 ॥

aśeṣotpādayitrī — creator of all, tvam — you, sthāpayitrī — sustainer, nijātmani — in oneself, vilāpayitrī — dissolver, sarvasya — of all, parameśvari — O Supreme Goddess, te — to you, namaḥ — salutation.
You are the creator of all, sustainer in oneself, dissolver of all, O Supreme Goddess, salutation to you.
अनूतना सर्वदाऽसि यतो नास्ति जनिस्तव ।
नवात्मिका सदा त्वं वै यतो नास्ति जरा तव ॥ २४ ॥
anūtanā sarvadā'si yato nāsti janis tava ।
navātmikā sadā tvaṁ vai yato nāsti jarā tava ॥ 24 ॥

anūtanā — ever new, sarvadā — always, asi — you are, yataḥ — because, na asti — there is no, janis — birth, tava — for you, navātmikā — ever fresh, sadā — always, tvam — you, vai — indeed, yataḥ — because, na asti — there is no, jarā — old age, tava — for you.
You are ever new because there is no birth for you. You are ever fresh because there is no old age for you.
सर्वाऽसि सर्वसाराऽसि सर्वज्ञा सर्वहर्षिणी ।
असर्वाऽसर्वगाऽसाराऽसर्वज्ञाऽसर्वहर्षिणी ॥ २५ ॥
sarvā'si sarvasārā'si sarvajñā sarvahārṣinī ।
asarvā'sarvagā'sārā'sarvajñā'sarvahārṣinī ॥ 25 ॥

sarvā — all, asi — you are, sarvasārā — essence of all, asi — you are, sarvajñā — omniscient, sarvahārṣinī — delighting all, asarvā — not all, asarvagā — not going everywhere, asārā — without essence, asarvajñā — not omniscient, asarvahārṣinī — not delighting all.
You are all, the essence of all, omniscient, delighting all. You are not all, not going everywhere, without essence, not omniscient, not delighting all.
देवि भूयो नमस्तुभ्यं पुरस्तात्‌ पृष्ठतोऽपि च ।
अधस्तादूर्ध्वतः पार्श्वे सर्वतस्ते नमो नमः ॥ २६ ॥
devi bhūyo namas tubhyaṁ purastāt pṛṣṭhato'pi ca ।
adhastād ūrdhvataḥ pārśve sarvatas te namo namaḥ ॥ 26 ॥

devi — O Goddess, bhūyaḥ — again, namas tubhyam — salutation to you, purastāt — in front, pṛṣṭhataḥ — behind, api — also, ca — and, adhastāt — below, ūrdhvataḥ — above, pārśve — at the sides, sarvataḥ — in all directions, te — to you, namo namaḥ — repeated salutations.
O Goddess, again salutation to you in front, behind, below, above, at the sides, in all directions, repeated salutations to you.
ब्रूहि यत्तेऽपरं रूपमैश्वर्यं ज्ञानमेव च ।
फलं तत्साधनं मुख्यं साधकं सिद्धमेव च ॥ २७ ॥
brūhi yat te'paraṁ rūpam aiśvaryaṁ jñānam eva ca ।
phalaṁ tat sādhanam mukhyaṁ sādhakaṁ siddham eva ca ॥ 27 ॥

brūhi — tell, yat — what, te — your, aparam — other, rūpam — form, aiśvaryam — power, jñānam — knowledge, eva — indeed, ca — and, phalam — result, tat — that, sādhanam — means, mukhyam — primary, sādhakam — practitioner, siddham — perfected, eva — indeed, ca — and.
Tell what your other form, power, and knowledge are. The result, means, primary practitioner, and perfected one.
सिद्धेस्तु परमां काष्ठां सिद्धेषूत्तममेव च ।
देव्येतत्‌ क्रमतो ब्रूहि भूयस्तुभ्यं नमो नमः ॥ २८ ॥
siddhes tu paramāṁ kāṣṭhāṁ siddheṣūttamam eva ca ।
devy etat kramato brūhi bhūyas tubhyaṁ namo namaḥ ॥ 28 ॥

siddheḥ — of perfection, tu — but, paramām — supreme, kāṣṭhām — state, siddheṣu — among the perfected ones, uttamam — best, eva — indeed, ca — and, devi — O Goddess, etat — this, kramataḥ — in sequence, brūhi — tell, bhūyaḥ — again, tubhyam — to you, namo namaḥ — repeated salutations.
Tell the supreme state of perfection and the best among the perfected ones, O Goddess. Again, repeated salutations to you.
इत्यापृष्टा महाविद्या प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमे ।
दयमाना ऋषिगणे स्पष्टार्थं परमं वचः ॥ २९ ॥
ityāpṛṣṭā mahāvidyā pravaktum upacakrame ।
dayamānā ṛṣigaṇe spaṣṭārthaṁ paramaṁ vacaḥ ॥ 29 ॥

iti — thus, āpṛṣṭā — asked, mahāvidyā — great knowledge, pravaktum — to explain, upacakrame — began, dayamānā — being compassionate, ṛṣigaṇe — to the group of sages, spaṣṭārtham — clear meaning, paramam — supreme, vacaḥ — words.
Thus asked, the great knowledge began to explain, being compassionate to the group of sages, with clear meaning and supreme words.
शृणुध्वमृषयः सर्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि क्रमेण तत्‌ ।
अमृतं ह्यागमाम्भोधेः समुद्धृत्य ददामि वः ॥ ३० ॥
śṛṇudhvam ṛṣayaḥ sarvaṁ pravakṣyāmi krameṇa tat ।
amṛtaṁ hy āgamāmbhodheḥ samuddhṛtya dadāmi vaḥ ॥ 30 ॥

śṛṇudhvam — listen, ṛṣayaḥ — O sages, sarvam — all, pravakṣyāmi — I will explain, krameṇa — in sequence, tat — that, amṛtam — nectar, hi — indeed, āgamāmbhodheḥ — from the ocean of scriptures, samuddhṛtya — having extracted, dadāmi — I give, vaḥ — to you.
Listen, O sages, I will explain everything in sequence. I give you the nectar extracted from the ocean of scriptures.
यत्र सर्वं जगदिदं दर्पणप्रतिबिम्बवत्‌ ।
उत्पन्नं च स्थितं लीनं सर्वेषां भासते सदा ॥ ३१ ॥
yatra sarvaṁ jagad idaṁ darpaṇa-pratibimba-vat ।
utpannaṁ ca sthitaṁ līnaṁ sarveṣāṁ bhāsate sadā ॥ 31 ॥

yatra — where, sarvam — all, jagat — world, idam — this, darpaṇa-pratibimba-vat — like a reflection in a mirror, utpannam — arisen, ca — and, sthitam — situated, līnam — dissolved, sarveṣām — for all, bhāsate — shines, sadā — always.
Where all this world, like a reflection in a mirror, arises, is situated, and dissolves, always shines for all.
यदेव जगदाकारं भासतेऽविदितात्मनाम्‌ ।
यद्योगिनां निर्विकल्पं विभात्यात्मनि केवलम्‌ ॥ ३२ ॥
yad eva jagad-ākāraṁ bhāsate 'viditātmanām ।
yad yogināṁ nirvikalpaṁ vibhāty ātmani kevalam ॥ 32 ॥

yat — which, eva — indeed, jagat-ākāram — world-like form, bhāsate — shines, avidita-ātmanām — for those unaware of the Self, yat — which, yoginām — for yogis, nirvikalpam — without distinction, vibhāti — shines, ātmani — in the Self, kevalam — alone.
Which indeed shines as the world-like form for those unaware of the Self, which shines without distinction for yogis in the Self alone.
गम्भीरस्तिमिताम्भोधिरिव निश्चलभासनम्‌ ।
यत्‌ सुभक्तैरतिशयप्रीत्या कैतववर्जनात्‌ ॥ ३३ ॥
gambhīra-stimitāmbhodhir iva niścalabhāsanam ।
yat subhaktair atiśayaprītyā kaitavavarjanāt ॥ 33 ॥

gambhīra — deep, stimita-ambhodhiḥ — still ocean, iva — like, niścala-bhāsanam — unshaken illumination, yat — which, subhaktaiḥ — by great devotees, atiśaya-prītyā — with great love, kaitava-varjanāt — free from deceit.
Which is like the deep, still ocean, unshaken illumination, which is worshipped by great devotees with great love, free from deceit.
स्वभावस्य स्वरसतो ज्ञात्वापि स्वाद्वयं पदम्‌ ।
विभेदभावमाहृत्य सेव्यतेऽत्यन्ततत्परैः ॥ ३४ ॥
svabhāvasya svarasato jñātvāpi svādvayaṁ padam ।
vibhedabhāvam āhṛtya sevyate 'tyanta-tatparaiḥ ॥ 34 ॥

svabhāvasya — of nature, svarasataḥ — naturally, jñātvā — knowing, api — even, svādvayam — sweet, padam — place, vibheda-bhāvam — with a sense of differentiation, āhṛtya — bringing, sevyate — is worshipped, atyanta-tatparaiḥ — by those extremely devoted.
Knowing naturally the sweet place of nature, even with a sense of differentiation, it is worshipped by those extremely devoted.
अक्षान्तकरणादीनां प्राणसूत्रं यदान्तरम्‌ ।
यदभाने न किञ्चित्‌ स्याद्यच्छास्त्रैरभिलक्षितम्‌ ॥ ३५ ॥
akṣāntakaraṇādīnāṁ prāṇasūtraṁ yadāntaram ।
yad abhāne na kiñcit syād yac chāstrair abhilakṣitam ॥ 35 ॥

akṣa-anta-karaṇa-ādīnāṁ — of senses and inner faculties, prāṇa-sūtram — the thread of life, yat-āntaram — what is within, yat — which, abhāne — in the absence, na — not, kiñcit — anything, syāt — would be, yat — which, śāstraiḥ — by scriptures, abhilakṣitam — indicated.
The thread of life within the senses and inner faculties, in the absence of which there would be nothing, as indicated by the scriptures.
परा सा प्रतिभा देव्याः परं रूपं ममेरितम्‌ ।
ब्रह्माण्डानामनेकानां बहिरूर्ध्वे सुधाम्बुधौ ॥ ३६ ॥
parā sā pratibhā devyāḥ paraṁ rūpaṁ mameritam ।
brahmāṇḍānām anekānāṁ bahir ūrdhve sudhāmbudhau ॥ 36 ॥

parā — supreme, sā — that, pratibhā — brilliance, devyāḥ — of the goddess, param — supreme, rūpam — form, mama — my, īritam — spoken, brahmāṇḍānām — of universes, anekānām — many, bahih-ūrdhve — beyond and above, sudhā-ambudhau — in the ocean of nectar.
The supreme brilliance of the goddess, the supreme form, spoken by me, beyond and above many universes, in the ocean of nectar.
मणिद्वीपे नीपवने चिन्तामणिसुमन्दिरे ।
पञ्चब्रह्ममये मञ्चे रूपं त्रैपुरसुन्दरम्‌ ॥ ३७ ॥
maṇidvīpe nīpavane cintāmaṇi-sumandire ।
pañcabrahmamaye mañce rūpaṁ traipurasundaram ॥ 37 ॥

maṇi-dvīpe — in the island of jewels, nīpa-vane — in the kadamba forest, cintāmaṇi-sumandire — in the gem mansion, pañcabrahmamaye — composed of five Brahmas, mañce — on the throne, rūpam — form, traipura-sundaram — of Tripurasundari.
In the island of jewels, in the kadamba forest, in the gem mansion, on the throne composed of five Brahmas, is the form of Tripurasundari.
अनादिमिथुनं यत्तदपराख्यमृषीश्वराः ।
तथा सदाशिवेशानौ विधिविष्णुत्रिलोचनाः ॥ ३८ ॥
anādi-mithunaṁ yat tad aparākhyam ṛṣīśvarāḥ ।
tathā sadāśiveśānau vidhi-viṣṇu-trilocanāḥ ॥ 38 ॥

anādi-mithunam — beginningless pair, yat — which, tat — that, aparākhyam — called Aparā, ṛṣīśvarāḥ — O lords of sages, tathā — and, sadāśiva-īśānau — Sadashiva and Ishana, vidhi-viṣṇu-trilocanāḥ — Brahma, Vishnu, and three-eyed Shiva.
The beginningless pair called Aparā, O lords of sages, and Sadashiva and Ishana, Brahma, Vishnu, and three-eyed Shiva.
गणेशस्कन्ददिक्पालाः शक्तयो गणदेवताः ।
यातुधानाः सुरा नागा यक्षकिम्पुरुषादयः ॥ ३९ ॥
gaṇeśa-skanda-dik-pālāḥ śaktayo gaṇa-devatāḥ ।
yātudhānāḥ surā nāgā yakṣa-kimpuruṣādayaḥ ॥ 39 ॥

gaṇeśa-skanda-dik-pālāḥ — Ganesha, Skanda, and the guardians of directions, śaktayaḥ — powers, gaṇa-devatāḥ — the hosts of deities, yātudhānāḥ — demons, surāḥ — gods, nāgāḥ — serpents, yakṣa-kimpuruṣa-ādayaḥ — yakshas, kimpurushas, etc.
Ganesha, Skanda, the guardians of directions, the powers, the hosts of deities, demons, gods, serpents, yakshas, kimpurushas, and others.
पूज्याः सर्वा मम तनूरपराः परिकीर्तिताः ।
मम मायाविमूढास्तु मां न जानन्ति सर्वतः ॥ ४० ॥
pūjyāḥ sarvā mama tanūḥ aparāḥ parikīrtitāḥ ।
mama māyā-vimūḍhās tu māṁ na jānanti sarvataḥ ॥ 40 ॥

pūjyāḥ — worshipped, sarvāḥ — all, mama — my, tanūḥ — forms, aparāḥ — called Aparā, parikīrtitāḥ — are said, mama — my, māyā-vimūḍhāḥ — deluded by illusion, tu — but, mām — me, na jānanti — do not know, sarvataḥ — everywhere.
All my forms called Aparā are said to be worshipped. But deluded by my illusion, they do not know me everywhere.
पूजिताऽहमेव सर्वैर्ददामि फलमीहितम्‌ ।
न मत्तोऽन्या काचिदस्ति पूज्या वा फलदायिनी ॥ ४१ ॥
pūjitā'ham eva sarvair dadāmi phalam īhitam ।
na matto'nyā kācid asti pūjyā vā phaladāyinī ॥ 41 ॥

pūjitā — worshipped, aham — I, eva — indeed, sarvaiḥ — by all, dadāmi — give, phalam — result, īhitam — desired, na — not, mattaḥ — from me, anyā — other, kācit — any, asti — is, pūjyā — worthy of worship, vā — or, phaladāyinī — bestower of fruits.
I alone, being worshipped by all, give the desired result. There is no one else other than me who is worthy of worship or a bestower of fruits.
यथा यो मां भावयति फलं मत्‌ प्राप्नुयात्तथा ।
ममैश्वर्यमृषिगणा अपरिच्छिन्नमीरितम्‌ ॥ ४२ ॥
yathā yo māṁ bhāvayati phalaṁ mat prāpnuyāt tathā ।
mama aiśvaryam ṛṣigaṇā aparicchinnam īritam ॥ 42 ॥

yathā — as, yo — whoever, māṁ — me, bhāvayati — meditates upon, phalam — result, mat — my, prāpnuyāt — obtains, tathā — thus, mama — my, aiśvaryam — power, ṛṣigaṇāḥ — O group of sages, aparicchinnam — infinite, īritam — declared.
As one meditates upon me, one obtains my result. My power, O group of sages, is declared as infinite.
अनपेक्ष्यैव यत्किञ्चिद्‌ अहमद्वयचिन्मयी ।
स्फुराम्यनन्तजगदाकारेण ऋषिपुङ्गवाः ॥ ४३ ॥
anapekṣyaiva yat kiñcid aham advaya-cinmayī ।
sphurāmy ananta-jagad-ākāreṇa ṛṣipuṅgavāḥ ॥ 43 ॥

anapekṣya — without depending, eva — indeed, yat kiñcit — whatever, aham — I, advaya — non-dual, cinmayī — consciousness, sphurāmi — manifest, ananta-jagad-ākāreṇa — in the form of infinite worlds, ṛṣipuṅgavāḥ — O best of sages.
Without depending on anything, I, the non-dual consciousness, manifest as the infinite worlds, O best of sages.
तथा स्फुरन्त्यपि सदा नात्येम्यद्वैतचिद्वपुः ।
एतन्मे मुख्यमैश्वर्यं दुर्घटार्थविभावनम्‌ ॥ ४४ ॥
tathā sphuranti api sadā na atyemi advaita-cid-vapuḥ ।
etan me mukhyam aiśvaryam durghaṭārtha-vibhāvanam ॥ 44 ॥

tathā — thus, sphuranti — manifest, api — even, sadā — always, na atyemi — do not leave, advaita-cid-vapuḥ — non-dual consciousness form, etat — this, me — my, mukhyam — primary, aiśvaryam — power, durghaṭārtha — difficult-to-comprehend, vibhāvanam — visualization.
Thus, even though manifesting always, I do not leave the form of non-dual consciousness. This is my primary power, the difficult-to-comprehend visualization.
ममैश्वर्यं तु ऋषयः पश्यध्वं सूक्ष्मया दृशा ।
सर्वाश्रया सर्वगता चाप्यहं केवला स्थिता ॥ ४५ ॥
mama aiśvaryam tu ṛṣayaḥ paśyadhvaṁ sūkṣmayā dṛśā ।
sarvāśrayā sarvagatā ca api ahaṁ kevalā sthitā ॥ 45 ॥

mama — my, aiśvaryam — power, tu — indeed, ṛṣayaḥ — O sages, paśyadhvam — see, sūkṣmayā — subtle, dṛśā — vision, sarva-āśrayā — support of all, sarvagatā — pervading all, ca — and, api — also, aham — I, kevalā — alone, sthitā — remaining.
O sages, see my power with subtle vision. I am the support of all, pervading all, and remain alone.
स्वमायया स्वमज्ञात्वा संसरन्ती चिरादहम्‌ ।
भूयो विदित्वा स्वात्मानं गुरोः शिष्यपदं गता ॥ ४६ ॥
sva-māyayā svam ajñātvā saṁsaranti cirād aham ।
bhūyo viditvā sva-ātmānaṁ guroḥ śiṣya-padaṁ gatā ॥ 46 ॥

sva-māyayā — by my own illusion, svam — myself, ajñātvā — not knowing, saṁsaranti — wandering, cirāt — for a long time, aham — I, bhūyaḥ — again, viditvā — knowing, sva-ātmānam — my own self, guroḥ — of the guru, śiṣya-padam — the state of disciple, gatā — attained.
By my own illusion, not knowing myself, I have wandered for a long time. Knowing my own self again, I have attained the state of a disciple of the guru.
नित्यमुक्ता पुनर्मुक्ता भूयो भूयो भवाम्यहम्‌ ।
निरूपादानसम्भारं सृजामि जगदीदृशम्‌ ॥ ४७ ॥
nitya-muktā punar-muktā bhūyo bhūyo bhavāmy aham ।
nirūpādāna-sambhāraṁ sṛjāmi jagad īdṛśam ॥ 47 ॥

nitya-muktā — always liberated, punaḥ-muktā — liberated again, bhūyaḥ bhūyaḥ — again and again, bhavāmi — become, aham — I, nirūpādāna-sambhāram — without material cause, sṛjāmi — create, jagat — world, īdṛśam — like this.
Always liberated, I become liberated again and again. I create this world without material cause.
इत्यादि सन्ति बहुधा ममैश्वर्यपरम्पराः ।
न तद्‌ गणयितुं शक्यं सहस्रवदनेन वा ॥ ४८ ॥
ityādi santi bahudhā mama aiśvarya-paramparāḥ ।
na tat gaṇayituṁ śakyaṁ sahasra-vadanena vā ॥ 48 ॥

iti-ādi — such as these, santi — are, bahudhā — many, mama — my, aiśvarya-paramparāḥ — series of powers, na — not, tat — that, gaṇayitum — to count, śakyam — possible, sahasra-vadanena — with a thousand mouths, vā — or.
Such as these, there are many series of my powers. It is not possible to count them even with a thousand mouths.
शृण्वन्तु संग्रहाद्‌ वक्ष्ये मदैश्वर्यस्य लेशतः ।
जगद्यात्रा विचित्रेयं सर्वतः संप्रसारिता ॥ ४९ ॥
śṛṇvantu saṅgrahād vakṣye mad-aiśvaryasya leśataḥ ।
jagad-yātrā vicitreyaṁ sarvataḥ saṁprasāritā ॥ 49 ॥

śṛṇvantu — listen, saṅgrahāt — in brief, vakṣye — I will explain, mat-aiśvaryasya — my power, leśataḥ — in part, jagad-yātrā — the journey of the world, vicitrā — varied, iyam — this, sarvataḥ — everywhere, saṁprasāritā — spread.
Listen, I will briefly explain my power in part. This varied journey of the world is spread everywhere.
मम ज्ञानं बहुविधं द्वैताद्वैतादिभेदतः ।
परापरविभेदाच्च बहुधा चापि तत्फलम्‌ ॥ ५० ॥
mama jñānaṁ bahuvidhaṁ dvaita-advaita-ādi-bhedataḥ ।
para-apara-vibhedāt ca bahudhā ca api tat-phalam ॥ 50 ॥

mama — my, jñānam — knowledge, bahuvidham — of various kinds, dvaita-advaita-ādi-bhedataḥ — from distinctions like duality and non-duality, para-apara-vibhedāt — from distinctions of higher and lower, ca — and, bahudhā — in many ways, api — also, tat-phalam — its results.
My knowledge is of various kinds, from distinctions like duality and non-duality, and from distinctions of higher and lower. Its results are also varied in many ways.
द्वैतज्ञानं तु विविधं द्वितीयालम्बनं यतः ।
ध्यानमेव तु तत्प्रोक्तं स्वप्नराज्यादिसम्मितम्‌ ॥ ५१ ॥
dvaita-jñānaṁ tu vividhaṁ dvitīya-ālambanaṁ yataḥ ।
dhyānam eva tu tat proktaṁ svapna-rājya-ādi-sammitam ॥ 51 ॥

dvaita-jñānam — knowledge of duality, tu — indeed, vividham — various, dvitīya-ālambanam — depending on the second, yataḥ — because, dhyānam — meditation, eva — indeed, tu — but, tat — that, proktam — said, svapna-rājya-ādi-sammitam — similar to dream realms.
Knowledge of duality is indeed various, depending on the second. It is said that meditation on it is similar to dream realms.
तच्चापि सफलं ज्ञेयं नियत्या नियतं यतः ।
अपरं चापि विविधं तत्र मुख्यं तदेव हि ॥ ५२ ॥
tat ca api saphalam jñeyaṁ niyatyā niyataṁ yataḥ ।
aparaṁ ca api vividhaṁ tatra mukhyam tad eva hi ॥ 52 ॥

tat — that, ca — and, api — also, saphalam — fruitful, jñeyam — to be known, niyatyā — by regulation, niyatam — fixed, yataḥ — because, aparam — another, ca — and, api — also, vividham — varied, tatra — there, mukhyam — main, tat — that, eva — indeed, hi — surely.
That is also fruitful, to be known by regulation, because it is fixed. Another is also varied, and the main one is indeed that.
प्रोक्तमुख्यापरमय ध्यानं मुख्यफलक्रमम्‌ ।
अद्वैतविज्ञानमेव परविज्ञानमीरितम्‌ ॥ ५३ ॥
prokta-mukhya-aparamaya dhyānaṁ mukhya-phala-kramam ।
advaita-vijñānam eva para-vijñānam īritam ॥ 53 ॥

prokta — said, mukhya-aparamaya — main and secondary, dhyānam — meditation, mukhya-phala-kramam — primary result sequence, advaita-vijñānam — non-dual knowledge, eva — indeed, para-vijñānam — higher knowledge, īritam — declared.
The said meditation of main and secondary, the primary result sequence, is indeed the non-dual knowledge, declared as higher knowledge.
मामनाराध्य परमां चिरं विद्यां तु श्रीमतीम्‌ ।
कथं प्राप्येत परमां विद्यामद्वैतसंज्ञिकाम्‌ ॥ ५४ ॥
mām anārādhya paramāṁ ciraṁ vidyāṁ tu śrīmatīm ।
kathaṁ prāpyeta paramāṁ vidyām advaita-saṁjñikām ॥ 54 ॥

mām — me, anārādhya — not worshipping, paramām — supreme, ciraṁ — for long, vidyām — knowledge, tu — but, śrīmatīm — glorious, kathaṁ — how, prāpyeta — can be attained, paramām — supreme, vidyām — knowledge, advaita-saṁjñikām — called non-dual.
Without worshipping me, the supreme, for a long time, how can the supreme glorious knowledge called non-dual be attained?
तदेवाद्वैतविज्ञानं केवला या परा चितिः ।
तस्याः शुद्धदशामर्शो द्वैतामर्शाभिभावकः ॥ ५५ ॥
tad eva advaita-vijñānam kevalā yā parā citiḥ ।
tasyāḥ śuddha-daśāmarśaḥ dvaita-āmarśa-abhibhāvakaḥ ॥ 55 ॥

tad — that, eva — indeed, advaita-vijñānam — non-dual knowledge, kevalā — alone, yā — which, parā — supreme, citiḥ — consciousness, tasyāḥ — of that, śuddha-daśāmarśaḥ — pure state realization, dvaita-āmarśa — duality realization, abhibhāvakaḥ — overpowering.
That non-dual knowledge is indeed the supreme consciousness alone, whose pure state realization overpowers duality realization.
चित्तं यदा स्वमात्मानं केवलं ह्यभिसम्पतेत्‌ ।
तदेवानुविभातं स्याद्‌ विज्ञानमृषिसत्तमाः ॥ ५६ ॥
cittaṁ yadā svam ātmānaṁ kevalaṁ hy abhisampatet ।
tad eva anuvibhātaṁ syāt vijñānam ṛṣi-sattamāḥ ॥ 56 ॥

cittam — mind, yadā — when, svam — own, ātmānam — self, kevalam — alone, hi — indeed, abhisampatet — attains, tad — that, eva — indeed, anuvibhātam — illuminated, syāt — would be, vijñānam — knowledge, ṛṣi-sattamāḥ — O best of sages.
When the mind attains its own self alone, it indeed becomes illuminated knowledge, O best of sages.
श्रुतितो युक्तितो वापि केवलात्मविभासनम्‌ ।
देहाद्यात्मावभासस्य नाशनं ज्ञानमुच्यते ॥ ५७ ॥
śrutito yuktito vā api kevala-ātma-vibhāsanam ।
deha-ādi-ātma-avabhāsasya nāśanam jñānam ucyate ॥ 57 ॥

śrutitaḥ — from scripture, yuktitaḥ — from reasoning, vā — or, api — also, kevala-ātma-vibhāsanam — illumination of the pure self, deha-ādi-ātma-avabhāsasya — of the appearance of body and such as self, nāśanam — destruction, jñānam — knowledge, ucyate — is called.
The illumination of the pure self from scripture or reasoning, and the destruction of the appearance of body and such as self, is called knowledge.
तदेव भवति ज्ञानं यज्ज्ञानेन तु किञ्चन ।
भासमानमपि क्वापि न विभायात्‌ कथञ्चन ॥ ५८ ॥
tad eva bhavati jñānaṁ yad jñānena tu kiñcana ।
bhāsamānam api kvāpi na vibhāyāt kathañcana ॥ 58 ॥

tad — that, eva — indeed, bhavati — becomes, jñānam — knowledge, yat — which, jñānena — by knowledge, tu — but, kiñcana — anything, bhāsamānam — shining, api — even, kvāpi — anywhere, na — not, vibhāyāt — appears, kathañcana — in any way.
That indeed becomes knowledge by which anything, even though shining anywhere, does not appear in any way.
तदेवाद्वैतविज्ञानं यद्विज्ञानेन किञ्चन ।
अविज्ञातं नैव भवेत्‌ कदाचिल्लेशतोऽपि च ॥ ५९ ॥
tad eva advaita-vijñānam yad vijñānena kiñcana ।
avijñātam naiva bhavet kadācit leśataḥ api ca ॥ 59 ॥

tad — that, eva — indeed, advaita-vijñānam — non-dual knowledge, yad — which, vijñānena — by knowledge, kiñcana — anything, avijñātam — unknown, na — not, eva — indeed, bhavet — would be, kadācit — at any time, leśataḥ — even a little, api — also, ca — and.
That indeed is non-dual knowledge by which anything would not be unknown at any time, even a little.
सर्वविज्ञानात्मरूपं यद्विज्ञानं भवेत्‌ खलु ।
तदेवाद्वैतविज्ञानं परमं तापसोत्तमाः ॥ ६० ॥
sarva-vijñāna-ātma-rūpaṁ yad vijñānaṁ bhavet khalu ।
tad eva advaita-vijñānam paramaṁ tāpasottamāḥ ॥ 60 ॥

sarva-vijñāna-ātma-rūpam — the essence of all knowledge, yad — which, vijñānam — knowledge, bhavet — would be, khalu — indeed, tad — that, eva — indeed, advaita-vijñānam — non-dual knowledge, paramam — supreme, tāpasa-uttamāḥ — O best of ascetics.
The essence of all knowledge, which would be knowledge indeed, that is indeed non-dual knowledge, the supreme, O best of ascetics.
जाते यादृशविज्ञाने संशयाश्चिचरसम्भृताः ।
वायुनेवाभ्रजालानि विलीयन्ते परं हि तत्‌ ॥ ६१ ॥
jāte yādṛśa-vijñāne saṁśayāḥ cicarasambhṛtāḥ ।
vāyuneva-abhrājālāni vilīyante paraṁ hi tat ॥ 61 ॥

jāte — arising, yādṛśa — such, vijñāne — knowledge, saṁśayāḥ — doubts, cicarasambhṛtāḥ — gathered from ignorance, vāyuneva — like wind, abhrājālāni — clouds, vilīyante — dissolve, paraṁ — supreme, hi — indeed, tat — that.
When such knowledge arises, doubts gathered from ignorance dissolve like clouds by the wind. Indeed, that is supreme.
कामादिवासनाः सर्वा यस्मिन्‌ सन्ति न किञ्चन ।
स्युर्भग्नदंष्ट्राहिरिव तद्विज्ञानं परं स्मृतम्‌ ॥ ६२ ॥
kāmādi-vāsanāḥ sarvā yasmin santi na kiñcana ।
syuḥ bhagna-daṁṣṭrāhih iva tad-vijñānam paraṁ smṛtam ॥ 62 ॥

kāmādi — of desires, vāsanāḥ — impressions, sarvā — all, yasmin — in which, santi — are, na — not, kiñcana — anything, syuḥ — become, bhagna-daṁṣṭrāhih — like a toothless snake, iva — like, tad-vijñānam — that knowledge, paraṁ — supreme, smṛtam — remembered.
All impressions of desires in which nothing remains are like a toothless snake. That knowledge is remembered as supreme.
विज्ञानस्य फलं सर्वदुःखानां विलयो भवेत्‌ ।
अत्यन्ताभयसंप्राप्तिर्मोक्ष इत्युच्यते फलम्‌ ॥ ६३ ॥
vijñānasya phalaṁ sarva-duḥkhānāṁ vilayo bhavet ।
atyanta-abhaya-saṁprāptiḥ mokṣa iti ucyate phalam ॥ 63 ॥

vijñānasya — of knowledge, phalam — result, sarva-duḥkhānām — of all sufferings, vilayaḥ — dissolution, bhavet — would be, atyanta-abhaya-saṁprāptiḥ — attainment of complete fearlessness, mokṣaḥ — liberation, iti — thus, ucyate — is called, phalam — result.
The result of knowledge is the dissolution of all sufferings. The attainment of complete fearlessness is called liberation.
भयं द्वितीयसङ्कल्पादद्वैते विदिते दृढम्‌ ।
कुतः स्याद्‌ द्वैतसङ्कल्पस्तमः सूर्योदये यथा ॥ ६४ ॥
bhayaṁ dvitīya-saṅkalpāt advāite vidite dṛḍham ।
kutaḥ syāt dvaita-saṅkalpaḥ tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā ॥ 64 ॥

bhayam — fear, dvitīya-saṅkalpāt — from the conception of duality, advāite — in non-duality, vidite — known, dṛḍham — firmly, kutaḥ — where, syāt — would be, dvaita-saṅkalpaḥ — conception of duality, tamaḥ — darkness, sūryodaye — at sunrise, yathā — like.
Fear arises from the conception of duality. Where would be the conception of duality when non-duality is firmly known, like darkness at sunrise?
ऋषयो न भयं क्वापि द्वैतसङ्कुल्पवर्जने ।
अतो यत्फलमन्यत्‌ स्यात्तद्भयं सर्वथा भवेत्‌ ॥ ६५ ॥
ṛṣayo na bhayaṁ kvāpi dvaita-saṅkalpa-varjane ।
ato yat phalam anyat syāt tad bhayaṁ sarvathā bhavet ॥ 65 ॥

ṛṣayaḥ — sages, na — not, bhayam — fear, kvāpi — anywhere, dvaita-saṅkalpa-varjane — in the absence of duality conception, ataḥ — therefore, yat phalam — whatever result, anyat — other, syāt — would be, tad bhayam — that fear, sarvathā — in every way, bhavet — would be.
Sages do not have fear anywhere in the absence of the conception of duality. Therefore, whatever other result would be, that fear would be in every way.
अन्तवत्तु द्वितीयं स्याद्‌ भूयो लोके समीक्षणात्‌ ।
सान्ते भयं सर्वथैवाभयं तस्मात्‌ कुतो भवेत्‌ ॥ ६६ ॥
antavat tu dvitīyaṁ syād bhūyo loke samīkṣaṇāt ।
sānte bhayam sarvathā eva abhayaṁ tasmāt kuto bhavet ॥ 66 ॥

antavat — finite, tu — indeed, dvitīyam — second, syāt — would be, bhūyaḥ — more, loke — in the world, samīkṣaṇāt — from observation, sānte — finite, bhayam — fear, sarvathā — in every way, eva — indeed, abhayaṁ — fearlessness, tasmāt — therefore, kuto — where, bhavet — would be.
The second is indeed finite, observed more in the world. In every way, finite fear exists. Therefore, where would be fearlessness?
संयोगो विप्रयोगान्तः सर्वथैव विभावितः ।
फलयोगोऽपि तस्माद्धि विनश्येदिति निश्चयः ॥ ६७ ॥
saṁyogaḥ viprayoga-antaḥ sarvathā eva vibhāvitaḥ ।
phala-yogaḥ api tasmāt hi vinaśyet iti niścayaḥ ॥ 67 ॥

saṁyogaḥ — union, viprayoga-antaḥ — ending in separation, sarvathā — in every way, eva — indeed, vibhāvitaḥ — considered, phala-yogaḥ — result union, api — also, tasmāt — therefore, hi — indeed, vinaśyet — perishes, iti — thus, niścayaḥ — certain.
Union ends in separation in every way. Result union also perishes. Thus, it is certain.
यावदन्यत्‌ फलं प्रोक्तं भयं तावत्प्रकीर्तितम्‌ ।
तदेवाभयरूपं तु फलं सर्वे प्रचक्षते ॥ ६८ ॥
yāvat anyat phalaṁ proktaṁ bhayaṁ tāvat prakīrtitam ।
tat eva abhaya-rūpaṁ tu phalaṁ sarve pracakṣate ॥ 68 ॥

yāvat — as long as, anyat — other, phalam — result, proktam — stated, bhayam — fear, tāvat — as much, prakīrtitam — described, tat — that, eva — indeed, abhaya-rūpam — in the form of fearlessness, tu — but, phalam — result, sarve — all, pracakṣate — declare.
As long as other results are stated, fear is described as much. But that result, in the form of fearlessness, is declared by all.
यदात्मनोऽनन्यदेव फलं मोक्षः प्रकीर्तितः ।
ज्ञाता ज्ञानं ज्ञेयमपि फलं चैकं यदा भवेत्‌ ॥ ६९ ॥
yad ātmanaḥ ananya-deva phalaṁ mokṣaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ।
jñātā jñānaṁ jñeyam api phalaṁ ca ekam yadā bhavet ॥ 69 ॥

yad — when, ātmanaḥ — of self, ananya-deva — non-other, phalam — result, mokṣaḥ — liberation, prakīrtitaḥ — declared, jñātā — knower, jñānam — knowledge, jñeyam — object of knowledge, api — also, phalam — result, ca — and, ekam — one, yadā — when, bhavet — becomes.
When the result of the self, non-other, is declared as liberation, and when the knower, knowledge, and object of knowledge also become one.
तदा हि परमो मोक्षः सर्वभीतिविवर्जितः ।
ज्ञानं विकल्पसङ्कल्पहानं मौढ्यविवर्जितम्‌ ॥ ७० ॥
tadā hi paramaḥ mokṣaḥ sarva-bhīti-vivarjitaḥ ।
jñānaṁ vikalpa-saṅkalpa-hānaṁ mauḍhya-vivarjitam ॥ 70 ॥

tadā — then, hi — indeed, paramaḥ — supreme, mokṣaḥ — liberation, sarva-bhīti-vivarjitaḥ — devoid of all fear, jñānam — knowledge, vikalpa-saṅkalpa-hānam — free from doubts and deliberations, mauḍhya-vivarjitam — devoid of ignorance.
Then indeed is the supreme liberation, devoid of all fear. Knowledge free from doubts and deliberations, devoid of ignorance.
ज्ञातुः स्वच्छात्मरूपं तदादावनुपलक्षितम्‌ ।
उपलक्षक एवातो गुरुः शास्त्रं च नेतरत्‌ ॥ ७१ ॥
jñātuḥ svaccha-ātma-rūpaṁ tadā adau anupalakṣitam ।
upalakṣaka eva ataḥ guruḥ śāstraṁ ca na itarat ॥ 71 ॥

jñātuḥ — of the knower, svaccha-ātma-rūpam — clear self-nature, tadā — then, adau — initially, anupalakṣitam — not perceived, upalakṣakaḥ — perceiver, eva — indeed, ataḥ — therefore, guruḥ — teacher, śāstram — scripture, ca — and, na — not, itarat — otherwise.
The clear self-nature of the knower is initially not perceived. Therefore, the teacher and scripture are perceivers, not otherwise.
एतदेव हि विज्ञेयस्वरूपमभिधीयते ।
ज्ञातृज्ञानज्ञेयगतो यावद्‌ भेदोऽवभासते ॥ ७२ ॥
etad eva hi vijñeya-svarūpam abhidhīyate ।
jñātṛ-jñāna-jñeya-gato yāvat bhedaḥ avabhāsate ॥ 72 ॥

etad — this, eva — indeed, hi — surely, vijñeya-svarūpam — the nature of what is to be known, abhidhīyate — is said, jñātṛ-jñāna-jñeya-gataḥ — concerning the knower, knowledge, and the known, yāvat — as long as, bhedaḥ — difference, avabhāsate — appears.
This indeed is said to be the nature of what is to be known, as long as the difference between the knower, knowledge, and the known appears.
तावज्ज्ञाता ज्ञानमपि ज्ञेयं वा न भवेत्‌ क्वचित्‌ ।
यदा भेदो विगलितो ज्ञात्रादीनां मिथः स्थितः ॥ ७३ ॥
tāvat jñātā jñānam api jñeyam vā na bhavet kvacit ।
yadā bhedaḥ vigalitaḥ jñātrādīnām mithaḥ sthitaḥ ॥ 73 ॥

tāvat — as long, jñātā — knower, jñānam — knowledge, api — also, jñeyam — the known, vā — or, na — not, bhavet — would be, kvacit — anywhere, yadā — when, bhedaḥ — difference, vigalitaḥ — dissolved, jñātrādīnām — among knower, knowledge, and the known, mithaḥ — mutually, sthitaḥ — established.
As long as the difference among the knower, knowledge, and the known appears, there is no knower, knowledge, or the known. When the difference is dissolved, they are mutually established.
तदा ज्ञात्रादिसम्पत्तिरेतदेव फलं स्मृतम्‌ ।
ज्ञात्रादिफलपर्यन्तं न भेदो वस्तुतो भवेत्‌ ॥ ७४ ॥
tadā jñātrādi-sampattiḥ etad eva phalaṁ smṛtam ।
jñātrādi-phala-paryantam na bhedaḥ vastutaḥ bhavet ॥ 74 ॥

tadā — then, jñātrādi-sampattiḥ — attainment of knower, knowledge, and the known, etad — this, eva — indeed, phalam — result, smṛtam — remembered, jñātrādi-phala-paryantam — up to the result of knower, knowledge, and the known, na — not, bhedaḥ — difference, vastutaḥ — in reality, bhavet — would be.
Then, the attainment of the knower, knowledge, and the known is indeed remembered as this result. Up to the result of the knower, knowledge, and the known, in reality, there is no difference.
व्यवहारप्रसिद्धयर्थं भेदस्तत्र प्रकल्पितः ।
अतोऽपूर्वं लभ्यमत्र फलं नास्त्येव किञ्चन ॥ ७५ ॥
vyavahāra-prasiddhi-artham bhedaḥ tatra prakalpitaḥ ।
ataḥ apūrvaṁ labhyam atra phalaṁ na asti eva kiñcana ॥ 75 ॥

vyavahāra-prasiddhi-artham — for the sake of worldly conduct, bhedaḥ — difference, tatra — there, prakalpitaḥ — assumed, ataḥ — therefore, apūrvam — unprecedented, labhyam — to be obtained, atra — here, phalam — result, na asti — does not exist, eva — indeed, kiñcana — anything.
For the sake of worldly conduct, the difference is assumed there. Therefore, there is no unprecedented result to be obtained here.
आत्मैव मायया ज्ञातृज्ञानज्ञेयफलात्मना ।
यावद्भाति भवेत्तावत्‌ संसारो ह्यचलोपमः ॥ ७६ ॥
ātmā eva māyayā jñātṛ-jñāna-jñeya-phala-ātmanā ।
yāvat bhāti bhavet tāvat saṁsāraḥ hi acala-upamaḥ ॥ 76 ॥

ātmā — self, eva — indeed, māyayā — by illusion, jñātṛ-jñāna-jñeya-phala-ātmanā — as knower, knowledge, and known, yāvat — as long as, bhāti — appears, bhavet — would be, tāvat — so long, saṁsāraḥ — worldly existence, hi — indeed, acala-upamaḥ — like a mountain.
The self indeed appears as knower, knowledge, and known by illusion. As long as it appears, worldly existence would be like a mountain.
यदा कथञ्चिदेतत्तु भायाद्‌ भेदविवर्जितम्‌ ।
संसारो विलयं यायाच्छिन्नाभ्रमिव वायुना ॥ ७७ ॥
yadā kathañcit etat tu bhāyāt bheda-vivarjitam ।
saṁsāraḥ vilayaṁ yāyāt chinna-abhram iva vāyunā ॥ 77 ॥

yadā — when, kathañcit — somehow, etat — this, tu — but, bhāyāt — appears, bheda-vivarjitam — free from difference, saṁsāraḥ — worldly existence, vilayaṁ yāyāt — would dissolve, chinna-abhram — cut clouds, iva — like, vāyunā — by wind.
When somehow this appears free from difference, worldly existence would dissolve like cut clouds by the wind.
एवंविधमहामोक्षे तत्परत्वं हि साधनम्‌ ।
तत्परत्वे तु संपूर्णे नान्यत्‌ साधनमिष्यते ॥ ७८ ॥
evaṁ-vidha-mahā-mokṣe tatparatvaṁ hi sādhanam ।
