tatparatve tu sampūrṇe na anyat sādhanam iṣyate ॥ 78 ॥

evaṁ-vidha-mahā-mokṣe — in such great liberation, tatparatvam — devotion to that, hi — indeed, sādhanam — means, tatparatve — in devotion to that, tu — but, sampūrṇe — complete, na — not, anyat — other, sādhanam — means, iṣyate — is desired.
For such great liberation, devotion to that is indeed the means. In complete devotion to that, no other means is desired.
अपूर्णे तत्परत्वे तु किं सहस्रसुसाधनैः ।
तस्मात्तात्पर्यमेव स्यान्मुख्यं मोक्षस्य साधनम्‌ ॥ ७९ ॥
apūrṇe tatparatve tu kiṁ sahasra-su-sādhanaiḥ ।
tasmāt tatparyam eva syāt mukhyaṁ mokṣasya sādhanam ॥ 79 ॥

apūrṇe — incomplete, tatparatve — in devotion to that, tu — but, kiṁ — what, sahasra-su-sādhanaiḥ — with thousands of good means, tasmāt — therefore, tatparyam — devotion to that, eva — indeed, syāt — would be, mukhyam — main, mokṣasya — of liberation, sādhanam — means.
In incomplete devotion to that, what use are thousands of good means? Therefore, devotion to that is indeed the main means of liberation.
तात्पर्यं सर्वेथैतत्तु साधयामीति संस्थितिः ।
यस्तात्पर्येण संयुक्तः स्वंथा मुक्त एव सः ॥ ८० ॥
tātparyaṁ sarvathā etat tu sādhayāmi iti saṁsthitiḥ ।
yaḥ tātparyeṇa saṁyuktaḥ svaṁthā mukta eva saḥ ॥ 80 ॥

tātparyam — devotion to that, sarvathā — in every way, etat — this, tu — but, sādhayāmi — I accomplish, iti — thus, saṁsthitiḥ — state, yaḥ — who, tātparyeṇa — with devotion to that, saṁyuktaḥ — connected, svamthā — by nature, mukta — liberated, eva — indeed, saḥ — he.
In every way, the state of "I accomplish this" with devotion to that. Who is connected with devotion to that is indeed liberated by nature.
दिनैर्मासैर्वत्सरैर्वा मुक्तः स्याद्वाऽन्यजन्मनि ।
बुद्धिनैर्मल्यभेदेन चिरशीघ्रव्यवस्थितिः ॥ ८१ ॥
dinaiḥ māsaiḥ vatsaraiḥ vā muktaḥ syāt vā anya-janmani ।
buddhi-nairmalya-bhedena cira-śīghra-vyavasthitiḥ ॥ 81 ॥

dinaiḥ — by days, māsaiḥ — by months, vatsaraiḥ — by years, vā — or, muktaḥ — liberated, syāt — may be, vā — or, anya-janmani — in another birth, buddhi-nairmalya-bhedena — by the purity of intellect, cira-śīghra-vyavasthitiḥ — in a short or long duration.
Liberation may come in days, months, years, or another birth, depending on the purity of intellect and the duration involved, whether short or long.
बुद्धौ तु बहवो दोषाः सन्ति सर्वार्थनाशनाः ।
यैर्जनाः सततं त्वेवं पच्यन्ते घोरसंसृतौ ॥ ८२ ॥
buddhau tu bahavo doṣāḥ santi sarva-artha-nāśanāḥ ।
yair janāḥ satataṁ tu evam pacyante ghora-saṁsṛtau ॥ 82 ॥

buddhau — in the intellect, tu — indeed, bahavaḥ — many, doṣāḥ — faults, santi — exist, sarva-artha-nāśanāḥ — destructive of all meanings, yaiḥ — by which, janāḥ — people, satatam — constantly, tu — indeed, evam — thus, pacyante — are tormented, ghora-saṁsṛtau — in the terrible cycle of existence.
In the intellect, indeed, there are many faults destructive of all meanings, by which people are constantly tormented in the terrible cycle of existence.
तत्राद्यः स्यादनाश्वासो द्वितीयः कामवासना ।
तृतीयो जाड्यता प्रोक्ता त्रिधैवं दोषसंग्रहः ॥ ८३ ॥
tatrādyaḥ syāt anāśvāsaḥ dvitīyaḥ kāma-vāsanā ।
tṛtīyaḥ jāḍyatā proktā tri-dhā evaṁ doṣa-saṁgrahaḥ ॥ 83 ॥

tatra — among them, ādyaḥ — the first, syāt — is, anāśvāsaḥ — lack of faith, dvitīyaḥ — the second, kāma-vāsanā — desire tendencies, tṛtīyaḥ — the third, jāḍyatā — dullness, proktā — is said, tri-dhā — in three ways, evam — thus, doṣa-saṁgrahaḥ — collection of faults.
Among them, the first is lack of faith, the second is desire tendencies, and the third is dullness; thus, the collection of faults is said to be of three types.
द्विविधः स्यादनाश्वासः संशयश्च विपर्ययः ।
मोक्षोऽस्ति नास्ति वेत्याद्यः संशयः समुदाहृतः ॥ ८४ ॥
dvividhaḥ syāt anāśvāsaḥ saṁśayaś ca viparyayaḥ ।
mokṣaḥ asti nāsti vā iti ādyah saṁśayah samudāhṛtaḥ ॥ 84 ॥

dvividhaḥ — of two kinds, syāt — is, anāśvāsaḥ — lack of faith, saṁśayaḥ — doubt, ca — and, viparyayaḥ — misconception, mokṣaḥ — liberation, asti — exists, nāsti — does not exist, vā — or, iti — thus, ādyah — first, saṁśayah — doubt, samudāhṛtaḥ — is said.
Lack of faith is of two kinds: doubt and misconception. The first doubt is whether liberation exists or not.
नास्त्येव मोक्ष इत्याद्यो भवेदत्र विपर्ययः ।
एतद्द्वयं तु तात्पर्ये मुख्यं स्यात्‌ प्रतिबन्धकम्‌ ॥ ८५ ॥
nāsti eva mokṣaḥ iti ādyah bhavet atra viparyayaḥ ।
etat dvayam tu tātparye mukhyam syāt pratibandhakam ॥ 85 ॥

nāsti — does not exist, eva — indeed, mokṣaḥ — liberation, iti — thus, ādyah — first, bhavet — would be, atra — here, viparyayaḥ — misconception, etat dvayam — these two, tu — indeed, tātparye — in devotion, mukhyam — primary, syāt — is, pratibandhakam — obstructive.
The first misconception here is that liberation does not exist. These two, doubt and misconception, are the primary obstacles in devotion.
विपरीतनिश्चयेन नश्येदेतद्‌ द्वयं क्रमात्‌ ।
अत्रोपायो मुख्यतमो मूलच्छेदो न चापरः ॥ ८६ ॥
viparīta-niścayena naśyet etad dvayam kramāt ।
atra upāyo mukhyatamo mūla-chedah na ca aparah ॥ 86 ॥

viparīta — contrary, niścayena — by determination, naśyet — would destroy, etad dvayam — these two, kramāt — gradually, atra — here, upāyaḥ — means, mukhyatamaḥ — primary, mūla-chedah — root cutting, na — not, ca — and, aparah — another.
These two, doubt and misconception, would gradually be destroyed by contrary determination. The primary means here is cutting the root, and there is no other.
अनाश्वासस्य मूलं तु विरुद्धतर्कचिन्तनम्‌ ।
तत्परित्यज्य सत्तर्कावर्तनस्य प्रसाधने ॥ ८७ ॥
anāśvāsasya mūlam tu viruddha-tarka-cintanam ।
tat parityajya sat-tarka-āvartanasya prasādhane ॥ 87 ॥

anāśvāsasya — of lack of faith, mūlam — root, tu — indeed, viruddha-tarka-cintanam — contrary reasoning, tat — that, parityajya — abandoning, sat-tarka-āvartanasya — of correct reasoning, prasādhane — in establishment.
The root of lack of faith is contrary reasoning. Abandoning that and establishing correct reasoning.
विपरीतो निश्चयः स्याद्‌ मूलच्छेदनपूर्वकः ।
ततः श्रद्धासमुदयादनाश्वासः प्रणश्यति ॥ ८८ ॥
viparītaḥ niścayaḥ syāt mūla-chedana-pūrvakaḥ ।
tataḥ śraddhā-samudayāt anāśvāsaḥ praṇaśyati ॥ 88 ॥

viparītaḥ — contrary, niścayaḥ — determination, syāt — would be, mūla-chedana-pūrvakaḥ — preceded by root cutting, tataḥ — then, śraddhā-samudayāt — by the rise of faith, anāśvāsaḥ — lack of faith, praṇaśyati — is destroyed.
Contrary determination, preceded by root cutting, then by the rise of faith, destroys lack of faith.
कामादिवासना बुद्धेः श्रवणे प्रतिबन्धिका ।
कामादिवासनाविष्टा बुद्धिर्नैव प्रवर्तते ॥ ८९ ॥
kāma-ādi-vāsanā buddhēḥ śravaṇē pratibandhikā ।
kāma-ādi-vāsanā-viṣṭā buddhiḥ na eva pravartate ॥ 89 ॥

kāma-ādi-vāsanā — desire and other tendencies, buddhēḥ — of intellect, śravaṇē — in hearing, pratibandhikā — obstructive, kāma-ādi-vāsanā-viṣṭā — filled with desire and other tendencies, buddhiḥ — intellect, na — not, eva — indeed, pravartate — functions.
Desire and other tendencies in the intellect obstruct hearing. An intellect filled with desire and other tendencies indeed does not function.
लोकेऽपि कामी काम्यस्य सदा ध्यानैकतत्परः ।
पुरःस्थितं न पश्येच्च श्रोत्रोक्तं शृणुयान्न च ॥ ९० ॥
lokē api kāmī kāmyasya sadā dhyāna-eka-tatparaḥ ।
puraḥ-sthitam na paśyēt ca śrotra-uktam śṛṇuyāt na ca ॥ 90 ॥

lokē — in the world, api — even, kāmī — desirous person, kāmyasya — of the desired, sadā — always, dhyāna-eka-tatparaḥ — focused in meditation, puraḥ-sthitam — placed before, na paśyēt — does not see, ca — and, śrotra-uktam — spoken in hearing, śṛṇuyāt — hears, na — not, ca — and.
In the world, even a desirous person always focused on the desired does not see what is placed before and does not hear what is spoken in hearing.
कमादिवासितस्यैवं श्रुतं चाश्रुतसम्मितम्‌ ।
कामादिवासनां तस्माज्जयेद्‌ वैराग्यसम्पदा ॥ ९१ ॥
kāmādi-vāsitasya evaṁ śrutam ca aśruta-sammitam ।
kāmādi-vāsanām tasmāt jayet vairāgya-sampadā ॥ 91 ॥

kāmādi-vāsitasya — filled with desire and others, evam — thus, śrutam — heard, ca — and, aśruta-sammitam — like unheard, kāmādi-vāsanām — desire and other tendencies, tasmāt — therefore, jayet — conquer, vairāgya-sampadā — by the wealth of dispassion.
Thus, for one filled with desire and others, the heard is like the unheard. Therefore, conquer desire and other tendencies by the wealth of dispassion.
सन्ति कामक्रोधमुखा वासनास्तु सहस्रशः ।
तत्र कामो मूलभूतस्तन्नाशे नहि किञ्चन ॥ ९२ ॥
santi kāma-krodha-mukhā vāsanāstu sahasraśaḥ ।
tatra kāmo mūla-bhūtaḥ tan-nāśe nahi kiñcana ॥ 92 ॥

santi — there are, kāma-krodha-mukhā — desire, anger, and others, vāsanāstu — tendencies, sahasraśaḥ — thousands, tatra — among them, kāmaḥ — desire, mūla-bhūtaḥ — fundamental, tan-nāśe — in its destruction, nahi — not, kiñcana — anything.
There are thousands of tendencies like desire, anger, and others. Among them, desire is fundamental; in its destruction, nothing remains.
ततो वैराग्यसंयोगाद्‌ नाशयेत्‌ कामवासनाम्‌ ।
आशा हि कामः संप्रोक्त एतन्मे स्यादिति स्थिता ॥ ९३ ॥
tato vairāgya-saṁyogād nāśayet kāma-vāsanām ।
āśā hi kāmaḥ samprokta etan-me syāt iti sthitā ॥ 93 ॥

tataḥ — therefore, vairāgya-saṁyogāt — by the connection with dispassion, nāśayet — destroy, kāma-vāsanām — desire tendencies, āśā — hope, hi — indeed, kāmaḥ — desire, samprokta — is said, etat-me syāt — this should be mine, iti — thus, sthitā — situated.
Therefore, by the connection with dispassion, destroy the desire tendencies. Hope, indeed, is said to be desire, situated as "this should be mine."
शव्येषु स्थूलभूता सा सूक्ष्माऽशक्येषु संस्थिता ।
दृढवैराग्ययोगेन सर्वां तां प्रविनाशयेत्‌ ॥ ९४ ॥
śavyeṣu sthūla-bhūtā sā sūkṣmā aśakyeṣu saṁsthitā ।
dṛḍha-vairāgya-yogena sarvāṁ tāṁ pravināśayet ॥ 94 ॥

śavyeṣu — in the possible, sthūla-bhūtā — gross, sā — that, sūkṣmā — subtle, aśakyeṣu — in the impossible, saṁsthitā — situated, dṛḍha-vairāgya-yogena — by the practice of firm dispassion, sarvāṁ — all, tāṁ — them, pravināśayet — should destroy.
In the possible, it is gross, and in the impossible, it is subtle. By the practice of firm dispassion, one should destroy all of them.
तत्र मूलं काम्यदोषपरामर्शः प्रतिक्षणम्‌ ।
वैमुख्यं विषयेभ्यश्च वासना नाशयेदिति ॥ ९५ ॥
tatra mūlaṁ kāmya-doṣa-parāmarśaḥ prati-kṣaṇam ।
vai-mukhyaṁ viṣayebhyaśca vāsanā nāśayet iti ॥ 95 ॥

tatra — there, mūlam — root, kāmya-doṣa-parāmarśaḥ — contemplation of the faults of desires, prati-kṣaṇam — every moment, vai-mukhyaṁ — disinterest, viṣayebhyaḥ — in the objects, ca — and, vāsanā — tendencies, nāśayet — destroy, iti — thus.
There, the root is the contemplation of the faults of desires every moment. Disinterest in the objects and destroying the tendencies, thus.
यस्तृतीयो बुद्धिदोषो जाड्यरूपो व्यवस्थितः ।
असाध्यः सोऽभ्यासमुखैः सर्वथा ऋषिसत्तमाः ॥ ९६ ॥
yaḥ tṛtīyaḥ buddhi-doṣaḥ jāḍya-rūpaḥ vyavasthitaḥ ।
asādhyaḥ saḥ abhyāsa-mukhaiḥ sarvathā ṛṣi-sattamāḥ ॥ 96 ॥

yaḥ — which, tṛtīyaḥ — third, buddhi-doṣaḥ — intellect fault, jāḍya-rūpaḥ — in the form of dullness, vyavasthitaḥ — situated, asādhyaḥ — incurable, saḥ — that, abhyāsa-mukhaiḥ — by practices, sarvathā — in every way, ṛṣi-sattamāḥ — O best of sages.
The third intellect fault, which is situated in the form of dullness, is incurable by practices in every way, O best of sages.
येन तात्पर्यतश्चापि श्रुतं बुद्धिमनारुहेत्‌ ।
तज्जाड्यं हि महान्‌ दोषः पुरुषार्थविनाशनः ॥ ९७ ॥
yena tātparyataḥ ca api śrutam buddhiṁ anāruhet ।
tat jāḍyaṁ hi mahān doṣaḥ puruṣārtha-vināśanaḥ ॥ 97 ॥

yena — by which, tātparyataḥ — by devotion, ca — and, api — even, śrutam — heard, buddhiṁ — intellect, anāruhet — does not rise, tat — that, jāḍyaṁ — dullness, hi — indeed, mahān — great, doṣaḥ — fault, puruṣārtha-vināśanaḥ — destroyer of purpose.
By which even heard with devotion, the intellect does not rise, that dullness is indeed a great fault, destroyer of purpose.
तत्रात्मदेवतासेवामृते नान्यद्धि कारणम्‌ ।
सेवायास्तारतम्येन जाड्यं तस्य हराम्यहम्‌ ॥ ९८ ॥
tatra ātma-devatā-sevā-mṛte na anyat dhi kāraṇam ।
sevāyāḥ tārātamyena jāḍyaṁ tasya harāmy aham ॥ 98 ॥

tatra — there, ātma-devatā-sevā — service to the self-god, mṛte — except, na — not, anyat — another, dhi — indeed, kāraṇam — cause, sevāyāḥ — of service, tārātamyena — by gradation, jāḍyaṁ — dullness, tasya — its, harāmi — remove, aham — I.
There, except for service to the self-god, there is no other cause. By the gradation of service, I remove its dullness.
जाड्याल्पानल्पभावेन सद्यो वा परजन्मनि ।
भवेत्तस्य फलप्राप्तिर्जाड्यसंयुक्तचेतसः ॥ ९९ ॥
jāḍya-alpa-analpa-bhāvena sadyaḥ vā para-janmani ।
bhavet tasya phala-prāptiḥ jāḍya-saṁyukta-cetasaḥ ॥ 99 ॥

jāḍya — dullness, alpa — little, analpa — great, bhāvena — by nature, sadyaḥ — immediately, vā — or, para-janmani — in another birth, bhavet — would be, tasya — its, phala-prāptiḥ — attainment of result, jāḍya-saṁyukta-cetasaḥ — of one with dull intellect.
By nature, whether little or great dullness, immediately or in another birth, the attainment of its result would be of one with dull intellect.
सर्वसाधनसम्पत्तिर्ममैव प्रणिधानतः ।
उपयाति च यो भक्त्या सर्वदा मामकैतवात्‌ ॥ १०० ॥
sarva-sādhana-sampattiḥ mama eva praṇidhānataḥ ।
upayāti ca yaḥ bhaktyā sarvadā mama kaitavāt ॥ 100 ॥

sarva-sādhana-sampattiḥ — all the wealth of practices, mama — my, eva — indeed, praṇidhānataḥ — by devotion, upayāti — attains, ca — and, yaḥ — who, bhaktyā — by devotion, sarvadā — always, mama — my, kaitavāt — without deceit.
All the wealth of practices, by my devotion indeed, attains; and who is always by devotion without deceit, attains to me.
स साधनप्रत्यनीकं विधूयाशु कृती भवेत्‌ ।
यस्तु मामीश्वरीं सर्वबुद्धिप्रसरकारिणीम्‌ ॥ १०१ ॥
sa sādhanapratyanīkaṁ vidhūyāśu kṛtī bhavet ।
yastu māmīśvarīṁ sarvabuddhiprasarakāriṇīm ॥ 101 ॥

sa — he, sādhanapratyanīkam — obstacles to practice, vidhūya — having removed, āśu — quickly, kṛtī — successful, bhavet — becomes, yastu — who, mām — me, īśvarīm — the Lord, sarvabuddhiprasarakāriṇīm — the one who expands all intellects.
He who quickly removes obstacles to practice becomes successful; the one who honors me, the Lord, who expands all intellects.
अनादृत्य साधनैकपरः स्याद्‌ मूढभावतः ।
पदे पदे विहन्येत फलं प्राप्येत वा न वा ॥ १०२ ॥
anādṛtya sādhanikaḥ syād mūḍhabhāvataḥ ।
pade pade vihanyeta phalaṁ prāpyeta vā na vā ॥ 102 ॥

anādṛtya — neglecting, sādhanikaḥ — only focused on practice, syāt — may be, mūḍhabhāvataḥ — due to ignorance, pade pade — at every step, vihanyeta — obstructed, phalaṁ — fruit, prāpyeta — may attain, vā — or, na vā — or not.
Neglecting, if one is only focused on practice due to ignorance, he may be obstructed at every step and may or may not attain the fruit.
तस्मात्तु ऋषयो मुख्यं तात्पर्यं साधनं भवेत्‌ ।
एवं तात्पर्यवानेव साधकः परमः स्मृतः ॥ १०३ ॥
tasmāttu ṛṣayo mukhyaṁ tātparyaṁ sādhanam bhavet ।
evaṁ tātparyavāneva sādhakaḥ paramaḥ smṛtaḥ ॥ 103 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, tu — but, ṛṣayaḥ — sages, mukhyam — primary, tātparyam — intention, sādhanam — practice, bhavet — should be, evaṁ — thus, tātparyavān — one with intention, eva — only, sādhakaḥ — practitioner, paramaḥ — supreme, smṛtaḥ — is remembered.
Therefore, sages, primary intention should be the practice. Thus, one with intention is remembered as the supreme practitioner.
तत्र मद्भक्तियुक्तस्तु साधकः सर्वपूजितः ।
सिद्धिरात्मव्यवसितिर्देहानात्मत्वभावना ॥ १०४ ॥
tatra madbhaktiyuktastu sādhakaḥ sarvapūjitaḥ ।
siddhirātmavyavasitirdehānātmatvabhāvanā ॥ 104 ॥

tatra — there, madbhaktiyuktaḥ — endowed with my devotion, tu — indeed, sādhakaḥ — practitioner, sarvapūjitaḥ — respected by all, siddhiḥ — accomplishment, ātma-vyavasitiḥ — self-realization, deha-anātmatva-bhāvanā — the thought of the body not being the self.
There, the practitioner endowed with my devotion is respected by all. Accomplishment is self-realization and the thought that the body is not the self.
आत्मत्वभावनं नूनं शरीरादिषु संस्थितम्‌ ।
तदभावनमात्रं तु सिद्धिर्मौढ्यविवर्जितम्‌ ॥ १०५ ॥
ātmatvabhāvanaṁ nūnaṁ śarīrādiṣu saṁsthitam ।
tadabhāvanamātraṁ tu siddhirmauḍhyavivarjitam ॥ 105 ॥

ātmatva-bhāvanaṁ — the thought of selfhood, nūnaṁ — certainly, śarīra-ādiṣu — in the body, etc., saṁsthitam — situated, tad-abhāvanam-ātram — merely its negation, tu — but, siddhiḥ — accomplishment, mauḍhya-vivarjitam — free from ignorance.
The thought of selfhood is certainly situated in the body, etc. Its mere negation is accomplishment free from ignorance.
आत्मा व्यवसितः सर्वैरपि नो केवलात्मना ।
अत एव तु सम्प्राप्ता महानर्थपरम्परा ॥ १०६ ॥
ātmā vyavasitaḥ sarvairapi no kevalātmanā ।
ata eva tu samprāptā mahānarthaparamparā ॥ 106 ॥

ātmā — self, vyavasitaḥ — determined, sarvaiḥ — by all, api — also, no — not, kevalātmanā — as the pure self, ataḥ — therefore, eva — indeed, tu — but, samprāptā — attained, mahānartha-paramparā — great series of misfortunes.
The self is determined by all, but not as the pure self. Therefore, indeed, a great series of misfortunes is attained.
तस्मात्‌ केवलचिन्मात्रं यद्‌ देहाद्यवभासकम्‌ ।
तन्मात्रात्मव्यवसितिः सर्वसंशयनादिनी ॥ १०७ ॥
tasmāt kevalacinmātraṁ yad dehādyavabhāsakam ।
tanmātrātma-vyavasitiḥ sarva-saṁśayanādinī ॥ 107 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, kevala-cinmātram — pure consciousness, yad — which, deha-ādi-avabhāsakam — illuminates the body, etc., tan-mātra-ātma-vyavasitiḥ — determination as the pure self, sarva-saṁśaya-nādinī — removing all doubts.
Therefore, pure consciousness which illuminates the body, etc., determining this as the pure self, removes all doubts.
सिद्धिरित्युच्यते प्राज्ञैर्नातः सिद्धिरनन्तरा ।
सिद्धयः खेचरत्वाद्या अणिमाद्यास्तथैव च ॥ १०८ ॥
siddhirityucyate prājñairnātaḥ siddhiranantarā ।
siddhayaḥ khecaratvādyā aṇimādyāstathaiva ca ॥ 108 ॥

siddhiḥ — accomplishment, iti — thus, ucyate — is said, prājñaiḥ — by the wise, na — not, ataḥ — than this, siddhiḥ — accomplishment, anantarā — other, siddhayaḥ — accomplishments, khecaratva-ādyāḥ — such as the ability to move in the sky, aṇimā-ādyāḥ — and others like becoming small, tathā — also, eva — indeed, ca — and.
Accomplishment is this, thus said by the wise; not any other accomplishment than this. Accomplishments like the ability to move in the sky, becoming small, and others, indeed.
आत्मविज्ञानसिद्धेस्तु कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम्‌ ।
ताः सर्वास्तु परिच्छिन्नाः सिद्धयो देशकालतः ॥ १०९ ॥
ātma-vijñāna-siddhestu kalāṁ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm ।
tāḥ sarvāstu paricchinnāḥ siddhayo deśakālataḥ ॥ 109 ॥

ātma-vijñāna-siddheḥ — of self-knowledge accomplishment, tu — but, kalām — part, na arhanti — do not deserve, ṣoḍaśīm — sixteenth, tāḥ — those, sarvāḥ — all, tu — but, paricchinnāḥ — limited, siddhayaḥ — accomplishments, deśa-kālataḥ — by space and time.
Self-knowledge accomplishment does not deserve even a sixteenth part of those. All those accomplishments are limited by space and time.
इयं स्यादपरिच्छिन्नाः स्वात्मविद्या शिवात्मिका ।
स्वात्मविद्यासाधनेषु ताः सर्वाः सुप्रतिष्ठिताः ॥ ११० ॥
iyaṁ syād aparicchinnāḥ svātma-vidyā śivātmikā ।
svātma-vidyā-sādhaneṣu tāḥ sarvāḥ supratiṣṭhitāḥ ॥ 110 ॥

iyaṁ — this, syāt — should be, aparicchinnāḥ — unlimited, svātma-vidyā — self-knowledge, śivātmikā — auspicious nature, svātma-vidyā-sādhaneṣu — in the practices of self-knowledge, tāḥ — those, sarvāḥ — all, supratiṣṭhitāḥ — well established.
This should be unlimited self-knowledge of auspicious nature. Only those are all well established in the practices of self-knowledge.
आत्मविद्याविधावेतास्त्वन्तरायप्रयोजकाः ।
किं ताभिरिन्द्रजालात्मसिद्धितुल्याभिरीहितम्‌ ॥ १११ ॥
ātma-vidyā-vidhāv etās tv antarāya-prayojakāḥ ।
kiṁ tābhir indrajāla-ātma-siddhi-tulyābhir īhitam ॥ 111 ॥

ātma-vidyā-vidhau — in the practice of self-knowledge, etāḥ — these, tu — but, antarāya-prayojakāḥ — obstacles, kiṁ — what, tābhiḥ — with those, indra-jāla-ātma-siddhi-tulyābhiḥ — like magical accomplishments, īhitam — desired.
These are obstacles in the practice of self-knowledge. What is desired with those like magical accomplishments?
यस्य साक्षाद्‌ ब्रह्मपदमपि स्यात्तृणसम्मितम्‌ ।
कियन्त्येताः सिद्धयो वै कालक्षपणहेतवः ॥ ११२ ॥
yasya sākṣād brahma-padam api syāt tṛṇa-sammitam ।
kiyanty etāḥ siddhayo vai kāla-kṣapaṇa-hetavaḥ ॥ 112 ॥

yasya — whose, sākṣāt — directly, brahma-padam — the state of Brahman, api — even, syāt — may be, tṛṇa-sammitam — equivalent to straw, kiyantyaḥ — how many, etāḥ — these, siddhayaḥ — accomplishments, vai — indeed, kāla-kṣapaṇa-hetavaḥ — causes of wasting time.
For one whose state of Brahman is directly equivalent to straw, how many of these accomplishments are indeed causes of wasting time?
तस्मात्‌ सिद्धिर्नेतरा स्यादात्मविज्ञानसिद्धितः ।
ययाऽत्यन्तशोकनाशो भवेदानन्दसान्द्रता ॥ ११३ ॥
tasmāt siddhir netarā syād ātma-vijñāna-siddhitaḥ ।
yayā atyanta-śoka-nāśo bhavet ānanda-sāndrata ॥ 113 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, siddhiḥ — accomplishment, na itarā — not otherwise, syāt — should be, ātma-vijñāna-siddhitaḥ — from self-knowledge accomplishment, yayā — by which, atyanta-śoka-nāśaḥ — complete destruction of sorrow, bhavet — happens, ānanda-sāndrata — full of bliss.
Therefore, accomplishment should be from self-knowledge, not otherwise. By which the complete destruction of sorrow happens and is full of bliss.
सैव सिद्धिर्नेतरा तु मृत्युग्रासविमोचिनी ।
इयमात्मज्ञानसिद्धिर्विविधाभ्यासभेदतः ॥ ११४ ॥
saiva siddhir netarā tu mṛtyu-grāsa-vimocinī ।
iyam ātma-jñāna-siddhir vividha-abhyāsa-bhedataḥ ॥ 114 ॥

sā eva — that only, siddhiḥ — accomplishment, na itarā — not otherwise, tu — but, mṛtyu-grāsa-vimocinī — freeing from the grasp of death, iyam — this, ātma-jñāna-siddhiḥ — self-knowledge accomplishment, vividha-abhyāsa-bhedataḥ — by different kinds of practices.
That only is the accomplishment, not otherwise, freeing from the grasp of death. This self-knowledge accomplishment is by different kinds of practices.
बुद्धिनैर्मल्यभेदाच्च परिपाकविभेदतः ।
संक्षेपतस्तु त्रिविधा चोत्तमा मध्यमाऽधमा ॥ ११५ ॥
buddhi-nairmalya-bhedāc ca paripāka-vibhedataḥ ।
saṁkṣepatas tu trividha ca uttamā madhyamā adhamā ॥ 115 ॥

buddhi-nairmalya-bhedāt — by the difference in the purity of intellect, ca — and, paripāka-vibhedataḥ — by the difference in ripening, saṁkṣepataḥ — briefly, tu — but, trividha — threefold, ca — and, uttamā — best, madhyamā — medium, adhamā — inferior.
Briefly, by the difference in the purity of intellect and the difference in ripening, there are threefold: best, medium, and inferior.
लोके द्विजानामुषयः पठितश्रुतिसम्मिता ।
मेधया च महाभ्यासाद्‌ व्यापारशतसंकुला ॥ ११६ ॥
loke dvijānām uṣayaḥ paṭhita-śruti-sammitā ।
medhayā ca mahā-abhyāsāt vyāpāra-śata-saṅkulā ॥ 116 ॥

loke — in the world, dvijānām — of the twice-born, uṣayaḥ — activities, paṭhita-śruti-sammitā — reciting the Vedas, medhayā — by intellect, ca — and, mahā-abhyāsāt — by great practice, vyāpāra-śata-saṅkulā — involved in hundreds of activities.
In the world, the activities of the twice-born are reciting the Vedas, by intellect, and by great practice, are involved in hundreds of activities.
अप्यस्खलितवर्णा या पठिता श्रुतिरूत्तमा ।
समाहितस्य व्यापारेऽसमाहितस्य चान्यदा ॥ ११७ ॥
api askhalita-varṇā yā paṭhitā śruti uttamā ।
samāhitasya vyāpāre asamāhitasya ca anyadā ॥ 117 ॥

api — even, askhalita-varṇā — with unbroken letters, yā — which, paṭhitā — recited, śrutiḥ — Vedic knowledge, uttamā — best, samāhitasya — of the concentrated, vyāpāre — in activities, asamāhitasya — of the unconcentrated, ca — and, anyadā — at another time.
Even the Vedic knowledge, recited with unbroken letters, is best, for the concentrated one in activities than of the unconcentrated one.
पूर्ववद्याऽप्यस्खलिता पठिता मध्यमा श्रुतिः ।
या सदा ह्यनुसन्धानयोगादेव भवेत्तथा ॥ ११८ ॥
pūrvavat api askhalitā paṭhitā madhyamā śrutiḥ ।
yā sadā hi anusandhāna-yogāt eva bhavet tathā ॥ 118 ॥

pūrvavat — like before, api — even, askhalitā — with unbroken letters, paṭhitā — recited, madhyamā — medium, śrutiḥ — Vedic knowledge, yā — which, sadā — always, hi — indeed, anusandhāna-yogāt — by the practice of investigation, eva — only, bhavet — becomes, tathā — thus.
Even like before, recited with unbroken letters, Vedic knowledge, for the medium one, who is always studied thus only by the practice of investigation.
पठिता श्रुतिरत्यन्तास्खलिता त्वधमा हि सा ।
एवमेवात्मविज्ञानसिद्धिरक्ता त्रिधर्षयः ॥ ११९ ॥
paṭhitā śrutiḥ atyanta askhalitā tu adhamā hi sā ।
evam eva ātma-vijñāna-siddhiḥ tridhā ṛṣayaḥ ॥ 119 ॥

paṭhitā — recited, śrutiḥ — Vedic knowledge, atyanta — extremely, askhalitā — with unbroken letters, tu — but, adhamā — inferior, hi — indeed, sā — that, evam eva — thus only, ātma-vijñāna-siddhiḥ — self-knowledge accomplishment, tridhā — threefold, ṛṣayaḥ — sages.
The Vedic knowledge, recited extremely with unbroken letters, is indeed not grasped, for the inferior. Thus only, the self-knowledge accomplishment is threefold, O sages.
या महाव्यवहारेषु प्रतिसन्धानवर्जने ।
अन्यदा तद्वर्जने वा सर्वदा प्रतिसन्धितः ॥ १२० ॥
yā mahā-vyavahāreṣu pratisandhāna-varjane ।
anyadā tad-varjane vā sarvadā pratisandhitaḥ ॥ 120 ॥

yā — which, mahā-vyavahāreṣu — in great activities, pratisandhāna-varjane — without interruption, anyadā — at another time, tad-varjane — with that interruption, vā — or, sarvadā — always, pratisandhitaḥ — united.
When taking up great activities, one may be engaged without interruption, or at another time, with some interruption, however, is always united.
अन्यूनाधिकभावा स्यात्सोत्तमा मध्यमाऽधमा ।
अत्रोत्तमैव संसिद्धेः परा काष्ठा निरूपिता ॥ १२१ ॥
anyūnādikabhāvā syāt sottamā madhyamā adhamā ।
atrottamaiva saṁsiddheḥ parā kāṣṭhā nirūpitā ॥ 121 ॥

anyūna-adikabhāvā — less and more states, syāt — may be, uttamā — best, madhyamā — medium, adhamā — inferior, atra — here, uttamā — best, eva — only, saṁsiddheḥ — of accomplishment, parā — supreme, kāṣṭhā — limit, nirūpitā — designated.
Depending on that, there may be states of less and more: best, medium, and inferior. Here, only the best is designated as the supreme limit of accomplishment.
स्वप्नादिष्वप्यवस्थासु यदा स्यात्परमा स्थितिः ।
विचारक्षणतुल्येव सिद्धिः सा परमोत्तमा ॥ १२२ ॥
svapnādiṣv apy avasthāsu yadā syāt paramā sthitiḥ ।
vicārakṣaṇatulyā eva siddhiḥ sā paramottamā ॥ 122 ॥

svapna-ādiṣu — in dreams, etc., api — even, avasthāsu — in states, yadā — when, syāt — may be, paramā — supreme, sthitiḥ — state, vicāra-kṣaṇa-tulyā — equal to a moment of contemplation, eva — only, siddhiḥ — accomplishment, sā — that, paramottamā — supreme.
When there is a supreme state even in dreams and other states, that accomplishment, equal to a moment of contemplation, is supreme.
सर्वत्र व्यवहारेषु यत्नात्‌ संस्कारबोधतः ।
यदा प्रवृत्तिः सिद्धेः सा परा काष्ठा समीरिता ॥ १२३ ॥
sarvatra vyavahāreṣu yatnāt saṁskāra-bodhataḥ ।
yadā pravṛttiḥ siddheḥ sā parā kāṣṭhā samīritā ॥ 123 ॥

sarvatra — everywhere, vyavahāreṣu — in activities, yatnāt — with effort, saṁskāra-bodhataḥ — through awareness of impressions, yadā — when, pravṛttiḥ — engagement, siddheḥ — of accomplishment, sā — that, parā — supreme, kāṣṭhā — limit, samīritā — is declared.
When engagement in all activities, with effort through awareness of impressions, is declared as the supreme limit of accomplishment.
अयत्नेनैव परमे स्थितिः संवेदनात्मनि ।
अव्याहता यदा सिद्धिस्तदा काष्ठां समागता ॥ १२४ ॥
ayatnenaiva parame sthitiḥ saṁvedanātmani ।
avyāhatā yadā siddhis tadā kāṣṭhāṁ samāgatā ॥ 124 ॥

ayatnena — without effort, eva — only, parame — supreme, sthitiḥ — state, saṁvedana-ātmani — in the sensitive self, avyāhatā — uninterrupted, yadā — when, siddhiḥ — accomplishment, tadā — then, kāṣṭhām — limit, samāgatā — reached.
When the supreme state in the sensitive self is without effort and uninterrupted, then accomplishment has reached its limit.
व्यवहारपरो भावान्‌ पश्चन्नपि न पश्यति ।
द्वैतं तदा हि सा सिद्धिः पूर्णतामभिसङ्गता ॥ १२५ ॥
vyavahāraparo bhāvān paścann api na paśyati ।
dvaitaṁ tadā hi sā siddhiḥ pūrṇatām abhisaṅgatā ॥ 125 ॥

vyavahāra-paro — engaged in activities, bhāvān — states, paśyan — seeing, api — even, na paśyati — does not see, dvaitam — duality, tadā — then, hi — indeed, sā — that, siddhiḥ — accomplishment, pūrṇatām — completeness, abhisaṅgatā — has attained.
When engaged in activities, one sees that state but does not see duality, then that accomplishment has attained completeness.
जागरादौ व्यवहरन्नपि निद्रितवद्‌ यदा ।
स्थितिस्तदा हि सा सिद्धिः पूर्णतामभिसङ्गता ॥ १२६ ॥
jāgarādau vyavaharann api nidritavad yadā ।
sthitis tadā hi sā siddhiḥ pūrṇatām abhisaṅgatā ॥ 126 ॥

jāgara-ādau — in waking, etc., vyavaharan — acting, api — even, nidrita-vat — like sleeping, yadā — when, sthitiḥ — state, tadā — then, hi — indeed, sā — that, siddhiḥ — accomplishment, pūrṇatām — completeness, abhisaṅgatā — has attained.
When one acts in waking, etc., like sleeping, then that state of accomplishment has attained completeness.
एवं सिद्धिमनुप्राप्तः सिद्धेषूत्तम उच्यते ।
व्यवहारपरो नित्यं न समाधिं विमुञ्चति ॥ १२७ ॥
evaṁ siddhim anuprāptaḥ siddheṣu uttama ucyate ।
vyavahāra-paro nityaṁ na samādhiṁ vimuñcati ॥ 127 ॥

evaṁ — thus, siddhim — accomplishment, anuprāptaḥ — having attained, siddheṣu — among the accomplished, uttama — best, ucyate — is called, vyavahāra-paro — engaged in activities, nityaṁ — always, na — does not, samādhim — meditation, vimuñcati — abandon.
Thus, having attained accomplishment, he is called the best among the accomplished. Always engaged in activities, he does not abandon meditation.
कदाचिदपि मेधावी स सिद्धेषूत्तमो मतः ।
ज्ञानिनां विविधानां च स्थितिं जानाति सर्वदा ॥ १२८ ॥
kadācit api medhāvī sa siddheṣu uttamaḥ mataḥ ।
jñānināṁ vividhānāṁ ca sthitiṁ jānāti sarvadā ॥ 128 ॥

kadācit — sometimes, api — even, medhāvī — wise, saḥ — he, siddheṣu — among the accomplished, uttamaḥ — best, mataḥ — considered, jñāninām — of the wise, vividhānām — various, ca — and, sthitim — state, jānāti — knows, sarvadā — always.
Sometimes even the wise are considered the best among the accomplished. He always knows the various states of the wise.
स्वानुभूत्या स्वान्तरेव स सिद्धेषूत्तमो मतः ।
संशयो वापि कामो वा यस्य नास्त्येव लेशतः ॥ १२९ ॥
svānubhūtyā svāntareva sa siddheṣu uttamaḥ mataḥ ।
saṁśayo vā api kāmo vā yasya na asti eva leśataḥ ॥ 129 ॥

svānubhūtyā — by self-experience, svāntare — within oneself, eva — only, saḥ — he, siddheṣu — among the accomplished, uttamaḥ — best, mataḥ — considered, saṁśayaḥ — doubt, vā — or, api — even, kāmaḥ — desire, vā — or, yasya — whose, na — not, asti — is, eva — indeed, leśataḥ — even a trace.
By self-experience alone, he is considered the best among the accomplished. He has no trace of doubt or desire.
निर्भयो व्यवहारेषु स सिद्धेषूत्तमो मतः ।
सर्व सुखञ्च दुःखञ्च व्यवहारञ्च जागतम्‌ ॥ १३० ॥
nirbhayo vyavahāreṣu sa siddheṣu uttamaḥ mataḥ ।
sarva sukhaṁ ca duḥkhaṁ ca vyavahāraṁ ca jāgatam ॥ 130 ॥

nirbhayaḥ — fearless, vyavahāreṣu — in activities, saḥ — he, siddheṣu — among the accomplished, uttamaḥ — best, mataḥ — considered, sarvam — all, sukham — happiness, ca — and, duḥkham — sorrow, ca — and, vyavahāram — activity, ca — and, jāgatam — worldly.
Fearless in activities, he is considered the best among the accomplished. He knows all happiness, sorrow, and worldly activities.
स्वात्मन्येवाभिजानाति स सिद्धेषूत्तमो मतः ।
अत्यन्तं बद्धमात्मानं मुक्तं चापि प्रपश्यति ॥ १३१ ॥
svātmany eva abhijānāti sa siddheṣu uttamaḥ mataḥ ।
atyantaṁ baddham ātmānaṁ muktaṁ ca api prapaśyati ॥ 131 ॥

svātmany — in oneself, eva — only, abhijānāti — knows, saḥ — he, siddheṣu — among the accomplished, uttamaḥ — best, mataḥ — considered, atyantam — extremely, baddham — bound, ātmānam — self, muktam — liberated, ca — and, api — also, prapaśyati — sees.
Knowing in oneself, he is considered the best among the accomplished. He sees the self as both extremely bound and liberated.
यः स्वात्मनि तु सर्वात्मा स सिद्धेषूत्तमो मतः ।
यः पश्यन्‌ बन्धजालानि सर्वदा स्वात्मनि स्फुटम्‌ ॥ १३२ ॥
yaḥ svātmani tu sarvātmā sa siddheṣu uttamaḥ mataḥ ।
yaḥ paśyan bandha-jālāni sarvadā svātmani sphuṭam ॥ 132 ॥

yaḥ — who, svātmani — in oneself, tu — but, sarvātmā — all souls, saḥ — he, siddheṣu — among the accomplished, uttamaḥ — best, mataḥ — considered, yaḥ — who, paśyan — seeing, bandha-jālāni — webs of bondage, sarvadā — always, svātmani — in oneself, sphuṭam — clearly.
He who sees all souls in oneself is considered the best among the accomplished. He always sees the webs of bondage clearly in oneself.
मोक्षं नपेक्षते क्वापि स सिद्धेषूत्तमो मतः ।
सिद्धोत्तमोऽहमेवेह न भेदस्त्वावयोः क्वचित्‌ ॥ १३३ ॥
mokṣaṁ na apekṣate kvāpi sa siddheṣu uttamaḥ mataḥ ।
siddha-uttamaḥ aham eva iha na bhedaḥ tu āvayoḥ kvacit ॥ 133 ॥

mokṣam — liberation, na — not, apekṣate — expects, kvāpi — anywhere, saḥ — he, siddheṣu — among the accomplished, uttamaḥ — best, mataḥ — considered, siddha-uttamaḥ — best of the accomplished, aham — I, eva — only, iha — here, na — not, bhedaḥ — difference, tu — but, āvayoḥ — between us, kvacit — anywhere.
He who does not expect liberation anywhere is considered the best among the accomplished. I am the best of the accomplished here, and there is no difference between me and him anywhere.
एतद्व ऋषयः प्रोक्तं सुस्पष्टमनुयुक्तया ।
एतन्मयोक्तं विज्ञाय न क्वचित्‌ परिमुह्यति ॥ १३४ ॥
etad vai ṛṣayaḥ proktaṁ suspaṣṭam anuyuktayā ।
etad maya uktam vijñāya na kvacit parimuhyati ॥ 134 ॥

etad — this, vai — indeed, ṛṣayaḥ — sages, proktam — said, suspaṣṭam — clearly, anuyuktayā — by reasoning, etad — this, mayā — by me, uktam — spoken, vijñāya — knowing, na — not, kvacit — anywhere, parimuhyati — deluded.
Indeed, sages have clearly said this with reasoning. Knowing this spoken by me, one is not deluded anywhere.
इत्युक्त्वा सा परा विद्या विरराम भृगूद्वह ।
श्रुत्वैतदृषयः सर्व सन्देहमपहाय च ॥ १३५ ॥
ity uktvā sā parā vidyā virarāma bhṛgūdvaha ।
śrutvā etad ṛṣayaḥ sarve saṁdeham apahāya ca ॥ 135 ॥

iti — thus, uktvā — having said, sā — that, parā — supreme, vidyā — knowledge, virarāma — ceased, bhṛgūdvaha — O descendant of Bhṛgu, śrutvā — having heard, etad — this, ṛṣayaḥ — sages, sarve — all, saṁdeham — doubt, apahāya — removing, ca — and.
Thus, having said this, the supreme knowledge ceased, O descendant of Bhṛgu. Having heard this, all the sages removed their doubts.
नत्वा शिवादीन्‌ लोकेशान्‌ जग्मुः स्वं स्वं निवेशनम्‌ ।
विद्यागीता मयैषा ते प्रोक्ता पापौघनाशिनी ॥ १३६ ॥
natvā śiva-ādīn lokeśān jagmuḥ svaṁ svaṁ niveśanam ।
vidyā-gītā mayā eṣā te proktā pāpa-ogha-nāśinī ॥ 136 ॥

natvā — having bowed, śiva-ādīn — to Shiva and others, lokeśān — lords of the world, jagmuḥ — went, svaṁ svaṁ — each to their own, niveśanam — abode, vidyā-gītā — the Song of Knowledge, mayā — by me, eṣā — this, te — to you, proktā — spoken, pāpa-ogha-nāśinī — destroyer of the multitude of sins.
Having bowed to Shiva and the other lords of the world, they went each to their own abode. This Song of Knowledge, destroyer of the multitude of sins, has been spoken to you by me.
श्रुता विचारिता सम्यक्‌ स्वात्मसाम्राज्यदायिनी ।
विद्यागीताऽत्युत्तमेयं साक्षाद्विद्यानिरूपिता ॥ १३७ ॥
śrutā vicāritā samyak svātma-sāmrājya-dāyinī ।
vidyā-gītā atyuttama iyam sākṣāt vidyā-nirūpitā ॥ 137 ॥

śrutā — heard, vicāritā — considered, samyak — properly, svātma-sāmrājya-dāyinī — bestower of self-sovereignty, vidyā-gītā — Song of Knowledge, atyuttamā — very excellent, iyam — this, sākṣāt — directly, vidyā-nirūpitā — described knowledge.
Heard and properly considered, this very excellent Song of Knowledge, bestower of self-sovereignty, is directly described as knowledge.
पठतां प्रत्यहं प्रीता ज्ञानं दिशति सा स्वयम्‌ ।
संसारतिमिराम्भोधौ मज्जतां तरणिर्भवेत्‌ ॥ १३८ ॥
paṭhatāṁ pratyahaṁ prītā jñānaṁ diśati sā svayam ।
saṁsāra-timira-ambhodhau majjatāṁ taraṇiḥ bhavet ॥ 138 ॥

paṭhatām — for those who read, pratyaham — daily, prītā — pleased, jñānam — knowledge, diśati — bestows, sā — that, svayam — herself, saṁsāra-timira-ambhodhau — in the ocean of worldly darkness, majjatām — for those sinking, taraṇiḥ — boat, bhavet — becomes.
For those who read daily, pleased, she bestows knowledge herself. In the ocean of worldly darkness, she becomes a boat for those who are sinking.

colophon.en: Thus ends the twentieth chapter named "The Conclusion of the Songs of Knowledge" in the revered Tripura Rahasya.

lines.text: श्रुत्वेत्थं भार्गवो रामो दत्तात्रेयमुनीरितम्‌ ।
अविद्याजालविभ्रान्तेर्मुक्तप्रायो बभूव ह ॥ १ ॥
śrutvetthaṁ bhārgavo rāmo dattātreya-munīritam ।
avidyā-jāla-vibhrānter mukta-prāyo babhūva ha ॥ 1 ॥

śrutvā — having heard, itthaṁ — thus, bhārgavaḥ — descendant of Bhṛgu (Rama), rāmaḥ — Rama, dattātreya-muni — Dattatreya sage, īritam — spoken, avidyā — ignorance, jāla — net, vibhrānteḥ — delusion, mukta-prāyaḥ — nearly liberated, babhūva — became, ha — indeed.
Having heard thus, Rama, the descendant of Bhṛgu, who was deluded by the net of ignorance, became nearly liberated after listening to the sage Dattatreya.
पुनः पप्रच्छात्रिसुतं किञ्चिन्नत्वा सुभक्तितः ।
भगवन्‌ ब्रूहि विज्ञानसाधनं सुविनिश्चितम्‌ ॥ २ ॥
punaḥ papracchātrisutaṁ kiñcin natvā subhaktitaḥ ।
bhagavan brūhi vijñāna-sādhanaṁ suvinishchitam ॥ 2 ॥

punaḥ — again, papraccha — asked, atrisutaṁ — Atri’s son (Dattatreya), kiñcit — something, natvā — having bowed, subhaktitaḥ — with devotion, bhagavan — O Lord, brūhi — tell, vijñāna-sādhanam — the means to knowledge, suvinishchitam — well ascertained.
Again, he asked Atri's son, having bowed with devotion, "O Lord, tell me the well-ascertained means to knowledge."
सारभूतं च सुलभं यत्‌ साक्षात्‌ फलदायकम्‌ ।
ज्ञानिनां लक्षणं चापि येन ज्ञास्यामि तान्‌ द्रुतम्‌ ॥ ३ ॥
sāra-bhūtaṁ ca sulabhaṁ yat sākṣāt phala-dāyakam ।
jñānināṁ lakṣaṇaṁ ca api yena jñāsyāmi tān drutam ॥ 3 ॥

sāra-bhūtam — essential, ca — and, sulabham — easy, yat — which, sākṣāt — directly, phala-dāyakam — fruit-giving, jñāninām — of the wise, lakṣaṇam — characteristics, ca — and, api — also, yena — by which, jñāsyāmi — I will know, tān — them, drutam — quickly.
Tell me the essential, easy, and directly fruit-giving means, and the characteristics of the wise by which I will quickly know them.
ज्ञानिनां देहसंयोगे वियोगे च स्थितिं तथा ।
व्यवहारं कुर्वतां चाप्यनासक्तं मनः कथम्‌ ॥ ४ ॥
jñānināṁ deha-saṁyoge viyoge ca sthitiṁ tathā ।
vyavahāraṁ kurvatāṁ ca api anāsaktaṁ manaḥ katham ॥ 4 ॥

jñāninām — of the wise, deha-saṁyoge — in union with the body, viyoge — in separation, ca — and, sthitiṁ — state, tathā — as well as, vyavahāraṁ — conduct, kurvatām — of those acting, ca — and, api — also, anāsaktam — unattached, manaḥ — mind, katham — how.
How do the wise maintain their state in union and separation from the body, and how do they conduct themselves with an unattached mind?
एतत्‌ सर्व सुकृपया स्पष्टं मे वक्तुमर्हसि ।
एवमत्रिसुतः पृष्टो जमदग्निसुतेन वै ॥ ५ ॥
etat sarva su-kṛpayā spaṣṭaṁ me vaktum arhasi ।
evam atri-sutaḥ pṛṣṭo jamadagni-sutena vai ॥ 5 ॥

etat — this, sarva — all, su-kṛpayā — with great kindness, spaṣṭam — clearly, me — to me, vaktum — to tell, arhasi — you should, evam — thus, atri-sutaḥ — Atri’s son, pṛṣṭaḥ — asked, jamadagni-sutena — by Jamadagni’s son (Rama), vai — indeed.
With great kindness, please clearly tell me all this. Thus, Atri's son was asked by Jamadagni's son.
सन्तुष्टः प्राह करुणासिन्धुः सम्बोध्य भार्गवम्‌ ।
शृणु राम प्रवक्ष्यामि रहस्यं ज्ञानसाधनम्‌ ॥ ६ ॥
santuṣṭaḥ prāha karuṇā-sindhuḥ sambodhya bhārgavam ।
śṛṇu rāma pravakṣyāmi rahasyaṁ jñāna-sādhanam ॥ 6 ॥

santuṣṭaḥ — pleased, prāha — said, karuṇā-sindhuḥ — ocean of compassion, sambodhya — addressing, bhārgavam — to Bhārgava (Rama), śṛṇu — listen, rāma — Rama, pravakṣyāmi — I will tell, rahasyam — secret, jñāna-sādhanam — means to knowledge.
Pleased, the ocean of compassion addressed Bhārgava (Rama) and said, "Listen, Rama, I will tell you the secret means to knowledge."
ज्ञानस्य साधनं मुख्यं देवतानुग्रहः परः ।
यः सर्वभावतः स्वात्मदेवतामुपसङ्गतः ॥ ७ ॥
jñānasya sādhanaṁ mukhyaṁ devatānugrahaḥ paraḥ ।
yaḥ sarva-bhāvataḥ svātma-devatām upasaṅgataḥ ॥ 7 ॥

jñānasya — of knowledge, sādhanaṁ — means, mukhyam — principal, devatānugrahaḥ — grace of the deity, paraḥ — supreme, yaḥ — who, sarva-bhāvataḥ — with all emotions, svātma-devatām — own deity, upasaṅgataḥ — approaching.
The principal means to knowledge is the supreme grace of the deity, which is approached with all emotions as one's own deity.
तस्य ज्ञानं सुसुलभं भवतीति विनिश्चयः ।
एतत्‌ सर्वोत्तमं राम प्रोक्तं ज्ञानस्य साधनम्‌ ॥ ८ ॥
tasya jñānaṁ susulabhaṁ bhavati iti viniścayaḥ ।
etat sarvottamaṁ rāma proktaṁ jñānasya sādhanam ॥ 8 ॥

tasya — his, jñānam — knowledge, susulabham — very easy, bhavati — becomes, iti — thus, viniścayaḥ — certainty, etat — this, sarvottamam — highest, rāma — Rama, proktam — stated, jñānasya — of knowledge, sādhanam — means.
It is certain that for him, knowledge becomes very easy. This is stated as the highest means to knowledge, Rama.
अन्यानपेक्षमेतत्त्‌ फलसंसाधने क्षमम्‌ ।
एतद्विहायान्यदत्र न सम्यक्‌ फलदं भवेत्‌ ॥ ९ ॥
anyānapekṣam etat phala-saṁsādhane kṣamam ।
etad vihāya anyad atra na samyak phala-daṁ bhavet ॥ 9 ॥

anyānapekṣam — independent of others, etat — this, phala-saṁsādhane — in achieving results, kṣamam — capable, etat — this, vihāya — without, anyat — other, atra — here, na — not, samyak — properly, phala-dam — fruit-giving, bhavet — can be.
This is capable of achieving results independently of others. Without this, nothing else here can properly give fruit.
शृण्वत्र कारणं राम सकारणमिदं भवेत्‌ ।
विज्ञानं केवलचितिर्या सर्वस्यावभासिका ॥ १० ॥
śṛṇv atra kāraṇaṁ rāma sakāraṇam idaṁ bhavet ।
vijñānaṁ kevala-citiḥ yā sarvasya avabhāsikā ॥ 10 ॥

śṛṇu — listen, atra — here, kāraṇam — reason, rāma — Rama, sakāraṇam — with reason, idam — this, bhavet — is, vijñānam — knowledge, kevala-citiḥ — pure consciousness, yā — which, sarvasya — of everything, avabhāsikā — illuminator.
Listen here to the reason, Rama. This is with reason. Knowledge, which is pure consciousness, illuminates everything.
तस्यावभासरूपायाः कल्पितावरणं तु यत्‌ ।
विचारातु तदपोहेन तत्स्वरूपोपलक्षणम्‌ ॥ ११ ॥
tasya avabhāsa-rūpāyāḥ kalpita-āvaraṇaṁ tu yat ।
vicārāt tu tat-apohena tat-svarūpa-upalakṣaṇam ॥ 11 ॥

tasya — its, avabhāsa-rūpāyāḥ — of the nature of illumination, kalpita-āvaraṇam — imagined covering, tu — but, yat — which, vicārāt — by inquiry, tu — but, tat — that, apohena — by removal, tat-svarūpa — its true nature, upalakṣaṇam — realization.
The imagined covering of its illuminating nature, but by inquiry and removal, leads to the realization of its true nature.
तच्चान्येषां बहिर्भावतत्पराणां सुदुर्लभम्‌ ।
भक्तानामन्यपरताहानेन तत्परत्वतः ॥ १२ ॥
tat ca anyeṣāṁ bahir-bhāva-tatparāṇāṁ sudurlabham ।
bhaktānām anya-paratā-hānena tat-paratvataḥ ॥ 12 ॥

tat — that, ca — and, anyeṣām — for others, bahir-bhāva-tatparāṇām — focused on external things, sudurlabham — very difficult, bhaktānām — for devotees, anya-paratā-hānena — by abandoning otherness, tat-paratvataḥ — due to devotion.
And that is very difficult for others who are focused on external things, but for devotees who abandon otherness and focus on devotion, it becomes easy.
सुलभं शीघ्रसम्प्राप्यं भवत्येव सुनिश्चितम्‌ ।
देवतातत्परस्त्वेवं भूत्वा स्वल्पान्यसाधनः ॥ १३ ॥
sulabhaṁ śīghra-samprāpyaṁ bhavati eva su-niścitam ।
devatā-tatparaḥ evam bhūtvā svalpa-anya-sādhanaḥ ॥ 13 ॥

sulabham — easy, śīghra-samprāpyam — quickly attainable, bhavati — becomes, eva — indeed, su-niścitam — well ascertained, devatā-tatparaḥ — devoted to the deity, evam — thus, bhūtvā — becoming, svalpa-anya-sādhanaḥ — little other means.
Indeed, it is well ascertained that for one devoted to the deity, it becomes easy and quickly attainable, requiring little other means.
ज्ञात्वा कथञ्चिदात्मानमन्यान्‌ प्रति निरूपयेत्‌ ।
निरूपयन्‌ सदा राम समावेशं समाप्नुयात्‌ ॥ १४ ॥
jñātvā kathaṁcid ātmānam anyān prati nirūpayet ।
nirūpayan sadā rāma samāveśaṁ samāpnuyāt ॥ 14 ॥

jñātvā — knowing, kathaṁcid — somehow, ātmānam — oneself, anyān — others, prati — towards, nirūpayet — should describe, nirūpayan — describing, sadā — always, rāma — Rama, samāveśam — absorption, samāpnuyāt — attains.
Knowing oneself somehow, one should describe it to others. Describing it always, Rama, one attains absorption.
एवं निरूपणाद्यैस्तु समवेशे दृढे सति ।
शिवतामाप्य तच्चित्तं हर्षोद्वेगविवर्जितम्‌ ॥ १५ ॥
evaṁ nirūpaṇādyaistu samāveśe dṛḍhe sati ।
śivatām āpya tat-cittaṁ harṣa-udvega-vivarjitam ॥ 15 ॥

evaṁ — thus, nirūpaṇādyaḥ — through description, tu — and, samāveśe — in absorption, dṛḍhe — firm, sati — being, śivatām — state of Shiva, āpya — attaining, tat-cittaṁ — that mind, harṣa-udvega-vivarjitam — free from joy and sorrow.
Thus, through description and firm absorption, attaining the state of Shiva, the mind becomes free from joy and sorrow.
यत्र यतर व्रजति तत्‌ सर्वं तच्छिवसात्कृतम्‌ ।
करोत्युत्तमविज्ञानी जीवन्मुक्तपदस्थितः ॥ १६ ॥
yatra yatra vrajati tat sarvaṁ tat śiva-sāt-kṛtam ।
karoti uttama-vijñānī jīvan-mukta-pada-sthitaḥ ॥ 16 ॥

yatra yatra — wherever, vrajati — goes, tat — that, sarvam — all, tat — that, śiva-sāt-kṛtam — consecrated to Shiva, karoti — does, uttama-vijñānī — highest knower, jīvan-mukta-pada-sthitaḥ — established in the state of liberation.
Wherever he goes, all that is consecrated to Shiva. The highest knower, established in the state of liberation, does this.
तस्मात्‌ सुभक्तियोगेनान्येभ्यो भूयो निरूपणम्‌ ।
श्रेष्ठं साधनमेतत्तु नान्यदेतत्समं भवेत्‌ ॥ १७ ॥
tasmāt su-bhakti-yogena anyebhyo bhūyo nirūpaṇam ।
śreṣṭhaṁ sādhanam etat tu na anyat etat-samam bhavet ॥ 17 ॥

tasmāt — therefore, su-bhakti-yogena — with great devotion, anyebhyaḥ — to others, bhūyaḥ — again, nirūpaṇam — explanation, śreṣṭham — best, sādhanam — means, etat — this, tu — but, na — not, anyat — other, etat-samam — equal to this, bhavet — can be.
Therefore, with great devotion, explain this again to others. This is the best means; there is no other equal to this.
भक्त्या निरूपणसम न भवेदन्यसाधनम्‌ ।
ज्ञानिनां लक्षणं राम दुर्विज्ञेयं भवेत्‌ खलु ॥ १८ ॥
bhaktyā nirūpaṇa-samam na bhavet anya-sādhanam ।
jñānināṁ lakṣaṇaṁ rāma durvijñeyaṁ bhavet khalu ॥ 18 ॥

bhaktyā — with devotion, nirūpaṇa-samam — equal to explanation, na bhavet — there is not, anya-sādhanam — other means, jñāninām — of the wise, lakṣaṇam — characteristics, rāma — Rama, durvijñeyam — difficult to understand, bhavet — is, khalu — indeed.
With devotion, there is no other means equal to explanation. The characteristics of the wise, Rama, are indeed difficult to understand.
यतः सर्वान्तरं तत्तु नेत्रवागाद्यगोचरम्‌ ।
न निरूपयितुं शक्यं लिक्षितुं वाऽपरैः क्वचित्‌ ॥ १९ ॥
yataḥ sarvāntaram tat tu netra-vāk-ādya-gocaram ।
na nirūpayitum śakyaṁ likhitum vā aparaiḥ kvacit ॥ 19 ॥

yataḥ — because, sarva-āntaram — all inner, tat — that, tu — but, netra-vāk-ādya — eye, speech, etc., gocaram — perceptible, na — not, nirūpayitum — to describe, śakyam — possible, likhitum — to write, vā — or, aparaiḥ — by others, kvacit — anywhere.
Because it is all inner and not perceptible to the eye, speech, etc., it is not possible to describe or write it anywhere by others.
यथा शास्त्रज्ञता लोके त्वन्यैर्न ज्ञायते क्वचित्‌ ।
देहवस्त्रभूषणाद्यैरेवमन्यैर्न वेद्यते ॥ २० ॥
yathā śāstra-jñatā loke tu anyaiḥ na jñāyate kvacit ।
deha-vastra-bhūṣaṇa-ādyaiḥ evam anyaiḥ na vedyate ॥ 20 ॥

yathā — as, śāstra-jñatā — knowledge of scriptures, loke — in the world, tu — but, anyaiḥ — by others, na jñāyate — not known, kvacit — anywhere, deha-vastra-bhūṣaṇa-ādyaiḥ — by body, clothes, ornaments, etc., evam — thus, anyaiḥ — by others, na vedyate — not known.
As the knowledge of scriptures is not known by others in the world through body, clothes, ornaments, etc., similarly, it is not known by others.
विद्वत्ता हि स्वसंवित्तिमात्रवेद्या न चान्यथा ।
यथा संस्वादितरसरसज्ञत्वं हि भार्गव ॥ २१ ॥
vidvattā hi sva-saṁvitti-mātra-vedyā na ca anyathā ।
yathā saṁsvādita-rasa-rasa-jñatvaṁ hi bhārgava ॥ 21 ॥

vidvattā — wisdom, hi — indeed, sva-saṁvitti-mātra — only by self-awareness, vedyā — known, na — not, ca — and, anyathā — otherwise, yathā — just as, saṁsvādita — tasted, rasa — flavor, rasa-jñatvaṁ — knowledge of flavor, hi — indeed, bhārgava — O Bhārgava.
Wisdom is known only by self-awareness and not otherwise, just as the knowledge of flavor is known by tasting it, O Bhārgava.
तथापि चतुरैर्विद्यावद्भिस्तद्भाषणादिभिः ।
वेद्यते हि यथा स्वस्य मार्ग: सुक्ष्मपिपीलकैः ॥ २२ ॥
tathāpi caturair vidyāvadbhis tad bhāṣaṇādibhiḥ ।
vedyate hi yathā svasya mārgaḥ sukṣma-pipīlakaiḥ ॥ 22 ॥

tathāpi — still, caturaiḥ — by the wise, vidyāvadbhiḥ — by the learned, tat — that, bhāṣaṇādibhiḥ — by their speech, vedyate — is known, hi — indeed, yathā — just as, svasya — one's own, mārgaḥ — path, sukṣma-pipīlakaiḥ — by tiny ants.
Still, by the wise and learned, it is known by their speech, just as the path is known by tiny ants.
सन्ति स्थूललक्षणानि त्वनेकान्तानि तानि तु ।
सूक्ष्मलक्ष्माणि चान्यानि दुर्विज्ञेयानि वै परैः ॥ २३ ॥
santi sthūla-lakṣaṇāni tu anekāntāni tāni tu ।
sūkṣma-lakṣmāṇi ca anyāni durvijñeyāni vai paraiḥ ॥ 23 ॥

santi — there are, sthūla-lakṣaṇāni — gross characteristics, tu — but, anekāntāni — many-sided, tāni — those, tu — but, sūkṣma-lakṣmāṇi — subtle characteristics, ca — and, anyāni — others, durvijñeyāni — difficult to comprehend, vai — indeed, paraiḥ — by others.
There are gross characteristics that are many-sided, but the subtle characteristics are difficult to comprehend by others.
निरूपणं भाषणं च साधनाभिनयस्तथा ।
ज्ञानिनामिव चान्यैस्तु कर्तु शक्यो हि लक्ष्यते ॥ २४ ॥
nirūpaṇaṁ bhāṣaṇaṁ ca sādhana-abhinayaḥ tathā ।
jñāninām iva ca anyaiḥ tu kartuḥ śakyaḥ hi lakṣyate ॥ 24 ॥

nirūpaṇam — description, bhāṣaṇam — speech, ca — and, sādhana-abhinayaḥ — demonstration of practice, tathā — thus, jñāninām — of the wise, iva — like, ca — and, anyaiḥ — by others, tu — but, kartuḥ — to do, śakyaḥ — possible, hi — indeed, lakṣyate — is seen.
The description, speech, and demonstration of practice, like the wise, are seen to be possible by others as well.
अनिर्मलान्तःकरणैरभ्यस्तं ज्ञानसाधनम्‌ ।
स्थिरीभवति यत्तेषां लक्षणं तत्‌ प्रकीर्तितम्‌ ॥ २५ ॥
anirmala-antaḥkaraṇaiḥ abhyastam jñāna-sādhanam ।
sthirībhavati yat teṣāṁ lakṣaṇaṁ tat prakīrtitam ॥ 25 ॥

anirmala-antaḥkaraṇaiḥ — by impure-hearted ones, abhyastam — practiced, jñāna-sādhanam — means to knowledge, sthirībhavati — becomes firm, yat — which, teṣām — for them, lakṣaṇam — characteristic, tat — that, prakīrtitam — is stated.
The means to knowledge, practiced by those with impure hearts, becomes firm for them. This is stated as their characteristic.
यस्य मानावमानौ च लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ ।
नेषद्विशेषितुं शक्तौ विद्यात्‌ तं ज्ञानिषूत्तमम्‌ ॥ २६ ॥
yasya mānā-avamānau ca lābhālābhau jayājayau ।
na iṣat-viśeṣituṁ śaktau vidyāt taṁ jñāniṣu uttamam ॥ 26 ॥

yasya — whose, mānā-avamānau — honor and dishonor, ca — and, lābhālābhau — gain and loss, jayājayau — victory and defeat, na — not, iṣat-viśeṣituṁ — slightly distinguishable, śaktau — are able, vidyāt — know, taṁ — him, jñāniṣu — among the wise, uttamam — highest.
Know him as the highest among the wise, for whom honor and dishonor, gain and loss, victory and defeat are not slightly distinguishable.
स्वात्मानुभववार्तासु पृष्टो गृढार्थमप्युत ।
असन्दिग्धः प्रतिवदेद्‌ झटिति ज्ञानिषूत्तमः ॥ २७ ॥
svātmānubhava-vārtāsu pṛṣṭo gṛhārtham api uta ।
asandigdhaḥ prativadet jhaṭiti jñāniṣu uttamaḥ ॥ 27 ॥

svātmānubhava-vārtāsu — in self-experiences, pṛṣṭaḥ — asked, gṛhārtham — hidden meaning, api — also, uta — certainly, asandigdhaḥ — without doubt, prativadet — replies, jhaṭiti — instantly, jñāniṣu — among the wise, uttamaḥ — highest.
The highest among the wise is he who, when asked about self-experiences, replies instantly and without doubt, even with hidden meanings.
यस्योत्साहो भवेद्‌ ज्ञानवार्तास्वतितरां किल ।
निरूपणे ह्यवैमुख्यं ज्ञानिनो लक्षणं हि तत्‌ ॥ २८ ॥
yasya utsāho bhaved jñāna-vārtāsu atitarāṁ kila ।
nirūpaṇe hi avaimukhyam jñāninaḥ lakṣaṇam hi tat ॥ 28 ॥

yasya — whose, utsāhaḥ — enthusiasm, bhavet — is, jñāna-vārtāsu — in discussions of knowledge, atitarām — extremely, kila — indeed, nirūpaṇe — in explaining, hi — indeed, avaimukhyam — not avoiding, jñāninaḥ — of the wise, lakṣaṇam — characteristic, hi — indeed, tat — that.
The characteristic of the wise is the one who has extreme enthusiasm in discussions of knowledge and does not avoid explaining it.
अनारम्भः स्वभावेन सन्तोषः शुचिचित्तता ।
महापत्स्वपि शान्तात्मा स भवेज्ज्ञानिषूत्तमः ॥ २९ ॥
anārambhaḥ svabhāvena santoṣaḥ śuci-cittatā ।
mahāpat-su api śānta-ātmā sa bhavet jñāniṣu uttamaḥ ॥ 29 ॥

anārambhaḥ — non-initiation, svabhāvena — by nature, santoṣaḥ — contentment, śuci-cittatā — purity of mind, mahāpat-su — in great calamities, api — even, śānta-ātmā — peaceful mind, saḥ — he, bhavet — is, jñāniṣu — among the wise, uttamaḥ — highest.
He is the highest among the wise who, by nature, does not initiate actions, is content, has a pure mind, and remains peaceful even in great calamities.
एतदादीनि लक्ष्माणि भार्गवोत्तम ज्ञानिनाम्‌ ।
स्वात्मनस्तु परीक्षायां सुस्थिराणि न संशय: ॥ ३० ॥
etad-ādīni lakṣmāṇi bhārgava-uttama jñāninām ।
svātmanastu parīkṣāyāṁ susthirāṇi na saṁśayaḥ ॥ 30 ॥

etad-ādīni — such as these, lakṣmāṇi — characteristics, bhārgava-uttama — O best of Bhārgava, jñāninām — of the wise, svātmanastu — in self-examination, parīkṣāyām — in examination, susthirāṇi — stable, na saṁśayaḥ — no doubt.
Such characteristics, O best of Bhārgava, are stable in the self-examination of the wise, without a doubt.
साधकस्तु सदा स्वात्मपरीक्षातत्परो भवेत्‌ ।
यथा परीक्षणेऽन्यस्य निपुणः संप्रवर्तते ॥ ३१ ॥
sādhakaḥ tu sadā svātma-parīkṣā-tatparaḥ bhavet ।
yathā parīkṣaṇe anyasya nipuṇaḥ sampravartate ॥ 31 ॥

sādhakaḥ — the seeker, tu — indeed, sadā — always, svātma-parīkṣā-tatparaḥ — dedicated to self-examination, bhavet — should be, yathā — as, parīkṣaṇe — in examining, anyasya — of others, nipuṇaḥ — skilled, sampravartate — engages.
The seeker should always be dedicated to self-examination, just as he skillfully engages in examining others.
तथा परीक्षन्‌ स्वात्मानं सिद्धिं न कथमाप्नुयात्‌ ।
यदाऽन्यगुणदोषाणामविचारणतत्परः ॥ ३२ ॥
tathā parīkṣan svātmānam siddhiṁ na katham āpnuyāt ।
yadā anya-guṇa-doṣāṇām avicāraṇa-tatparaḥ ॥ 32 ॥

tathā — thus, parīkṣan — examining, svātmānam — oneself, siddhim — attainment, na — not, katham — how, āpnuyāt — attain, yadā — when, anya-guṇa-doṣāṇām — of others' virtues and faults, avicāraṇa-tatparaḥ — dedicated to non-examination.
Thus, examining oneself, how can one not attain success? When dedicated to non-examination of others' virtues and faults.
स्वीयानां गुणदोषाणां विचारपरमो भवेत्‌ ।
तदा सर्वसाधनानां प्राप्त्या सिद्धिमुपैष्यति ॥ ३३ ॥
svīyānām guṇa-doṣāṇām vicāra-paramo bhavet ।
tadā sarva-sādhanānām prāptyā siddhim upaiṣyati ॥ 33 ॥

svīyānām — of one's own, guṇa-doṣāṇām — virtues and faults, vicāra-paramaḥ — dedicated to examination, bhavet — should be, tadā — then, sarva-sādhanānām — all means, prāptyā — by attainment, siddhim — success, upaiṣyati — attains.
When one is dedicated to examining one's own virtues and faults, then by attaining all means, one attains success.
एवं प्रोक्तानि लक्ष्माणि ज्ञानिनां भृगुनन्दन ।
स्वात्मनस्तु परीक्षायामुपयुक्तानि सर्वथा ॥ ३४ ॥
evaṁ proktāni lakṣmāṇi jñāninām bhṛgu-nandana ।
svātmanastu parīkṣāyām upayuktāni sarvathā ॥ 34 ॥

evaṁ — thus, proktāni — stated, lakṣmāṇi — characteristics, jñāninām — of the wise, bhṛgu-nandana — O son of Bhṛgu, svātmanastu — in self-examination, parīkṣāyām — in examination, upayuktāni — useful, sarvathā — always.
Thus, O son of Bhṛgu, the stated characteristics of the wise are always useful in self-examination.
अन्येषां तु परीक्षायामनेकान्तान्यमूनि तु ।
यतो ये ज्ञानिनोऽत्यन्तशुद्धस्वान्ता भृगूद्वह ॥ ३५ ॥
anyeṣāṁ tu parīkṣāyām anekāntāni amūni tu ।
yataḥ ye jñāninaḥ atyanta-śuddha-svāntā bhṛgu-udvaha ॥ 35 ॥

anyeṣām — of others, tu — but, parīkṣāyām — in examination, anekāntāni — many-sided, amūni — these, tu — but, yataḥ — because, ye — who, jñāninaḥ — wise, atyanta-śuddha-svāntā — extremely pure-hearted, bhṛgu-udvaha — O best of Bhṛgu.
But in the examination of others, these are many-sided. Because the wise who are extremely pure-hearted, O best of Bhṛgu.
तेषामापातसंसिद्धसाधनैः सिद्धिरास्थिता ।
अतः पूर्ववासनानुरोधव्यापारतत्पराः ॥ ३६ ॥
teṣām āpāta-saṁsiddha-sādhanais siddhiḥ āsthitā ।
ataḥ pūrva-vāsanā-anurodha-vyāpāra-tatparāḥ ॥ 36 ॥

teṣām — of them, āpāta-saṁsiddha-sādhanais — by seemingly perfect means, siddhiḥ — success, āsthitā — established, ataḥ — therefore, pūrva-vāsanā-anurodha — following past tendencies, vyāpāra-tatparāḥ — engaged in activities.
Their success is established by seemingly perfect means. Therefore, they follow past tendencies and engage in activities.
कथं परीक्षणीयास्ते सामान्यव्यवहारिणः ।
ज्ञानिनस्तु तत्परीक्षां कुर्युरभ्यासवैभवात्‌ ॥ ३७ ॥
kathaṁ parīkṣaṇīyāste sāmānya-vyavahāriṇaḥ ।
jñāninaḥ tu tat-parīkṣām kuryuḥ abhyāsa-vaibhavāt ॥ 37 ॥

katham — how, parīkṣaṇīyāḥ — to be examined, te — they, sāmānya-vyavahāriṇaḥ — ordinary conduct, jñāninaḥ — wise, tu — but, tat-parīkṣām — their examination, kuryuḥ — do, abhyāsa-vaibhavāt — by the power of practice.
How can they, with ordinary conduct, be examined? But the wise do their examination by the power of practice.
आपातदर्शनादेव यथा रत्नपरीक्षकाः ।
मन्दज्ञानवतां देहसंस्था मूढसमैव हि ॥ ३८ ॥
āpāta-darśanāt eva yathā ratna-parīkṣakāḥ ।
manda-jñānavatāṁ deha-saṁsthā mūḍha-samaiḥ hi ॥ 38 ॥

āpāta-darśanāt — by superficial observation, eva — indeed, yathā — like, ratna-parīkṣakāḥ — jewel examiners, manda-jñānavatām — of the dull-witted, deha-saṁsthā — those with body consciousness, mūḍha-samaiḥ — like fools, hi — indeed.
Like jewel examiners by superficial observation, those with body consciousness are like fools to the dull-witted.
यतो न तेषां सहजसमाधिप्राप्तिरस्ति हि ।
यावद्‌ विमर्शनपरास्तावत्ते पूर्णरूपिणः ॥ ३९ ॥
yataḥ na teṣām sahaja-samādhi-prāptir asti hi ।
yāvat vimarśana-parāḥ tāvat te pūrṇa-rūpiṇaḥ ॥ 39 ॥

yataḥ — because, na — not, teṣām — their, sahaja-samādhi-prāptiḥ — attainment of natural meditation, asti — is, hi — indeed, yāvat — as long as, vimarśana-parāḥ — engaged in inquiry, tāvat — as long as, te — they, pūrṇa-rūpiṇaḥ — full in form.
Because they do not attain natural meditation, as long as they are engaged in inquiry, they remain full in form.
यदा विचारविमुखास्तदा देहमयत्वतः ।
सुखदुःखजुषोऽत्यन्तं पशुतुल्यतया स्थिताः ॥ ४० ॥
yadā vicāra-vimukhāḥ tadā deha-mayatvataḥ ।
sukha-duḥkha-juṣaḥ atyantaṁ paśu-tulyatayā sthitāḥ ॥ 40 ॥

yadā — when, vicāra-vimukhāḥ — turned away from inquiry, tadā — then, deha-mayatvataḥ — due to body consciousness, sukha-duḥkha-juṣaḥ — experiencing pleasure and pain, atyantaṁ — extremely, paśu-tulyatayā — like animals, sthitāḥ — situated.
When turned away from inquiry, then due to body consciousness, experiencing pleasure and pain, they remain extremely like animals.
मध्ये मध्ये पूर्णदशासादनान्निर्वृता अपि ।
तेषां या सा पशुदशा सद्विमर्शान्तरालगा ॥ ४१ ॥
madhye madhye pūrṇa-daśā-āsādanān nirvṛtā api ।
teṣāṁ yā sā paśu-daśā sad-vimarśa-antarālagā ॥ 41 ॥

madhye — in between, madhye — in between, pūrṇa-daśā — state of completeness, āsādanāt — due to attaining, nirvṛtā — satisfied, api — even, teṣām — of them, yā — which, sā — that, paśu-daśā — animal-like state, sad-vimarśa — true reflection, antarālagā — intervening.
Even though they attain satisfaction intermittently by reaching a state of completeness, their animal-like state lies between true reflections.
न बन्धनाय भवति दग्धरज्जुरिव स्थिता ।
लाक्षारसैर्यदा वस्त्रप्रान्तयुग्मं सुरञ्जितम्‌ ॥ ४२ ॥
na bandhanāya bhavati dagdha-rajjuḥ iva sthitā ।
lākṣā-rasaiḥ yadā vastra-prānta-yugmaṁ surañjitam ॥ 42 ॥

na — not, bandhanāya — for bondage, bhavati — becomes, dagdha-rajjuḥ — burnt rope, iva — like, sthitā — situated, lākṣā-rasaiḥ — with lac dye, yadā — when, vastra-prānta-yugmam — edges of the cloth, surañjitam — decorated.
Like a burnt rope does not bind, when the edges of the cloth are dyed with lac, it appears decorated.
व्याप्त्या वासोमध्यमपि सर्व लाक्षारुणं भवेत्‌ ।
एवं तस्य व्यवहृतिश्चिदामर्शनमध्यगा ॥ ४३ ॥
vyāptyā vāso-madhyam api sarva lākṣā-aruṇaṁ bhavet ।
evaṁ tasya vyavahṛtiḥ cid-āmarśana-madhyagā ॥ 43 ॥

vyāptyā — by spreading, vāsaḥ-madhyam — middle of the cloth, api — also, sarva — entirely, lākṣā-aruṇam — dyed red, bhavet — becomes, evaṁ — thus, tasya — his, vyavahṛtiḥ — activity, cid-āmarśana — in the midst of consciousness, madhyagā — centered.
By spreading, even the middle of the cloth becomes entirely dyed red. Thus, his activity is centered in the midst of consciousness.
चिद्रूपात्मैकतां याता न ततो बन्धनाय सा ।
मध्यविज्ञानिनां देहसंयोगो नास्ति सर्वथा ॥ ४४ ॥
cid-rūpa-ātmaikatāṁ yātā na tato bandhanāya sā ।
madhya-vijñānināṁ deha-saṁyogaḥ nāsti sarvathā ॥ 44 ॥

cid-rūpa — of the form of consciousness, ātma-ikatām — unity of the self, yātā — attained, na — not, tataḥ — from that, bandhanāya — for bondage, sā — she, madhya-vijñāninām — of the middle-wise, deha-saṁyogaḥ — association with the body, nāsti — is not, sarvathā — at all.
Having attained unity with the form of consciousness, she does not become bound. The association with the body does not exist for the middle-wise at all.
देहात्मत्वग्रहो देहसंयोगः प्रोच्यते बुधैः ।
स नास्ति मध्यविज्ञानवतो राम कदाचन ॥ ४५ ॥
deha-ātmatva-grahaḥ deha-saṁyogaḥ procyate budhaiḥ ।
saḥ nāsti madhya-vijñāna-vataḥ rāma kadācana ॥ 45 ॥

deha-ātmatva-grahaḥ — identification with the body, deha-saṁyogaḥ — association with the body, procyate — is said, budhaiḥ — by the wise, saḥ — that, nāsti — does not exist, madhya-vijñāna-vataḥ — for the middle-wise, rāma — O Rāma, kadācana — ever.
Identification with the body is said to be association with the body by the wise. That does not exist for the middle-wise ever, O Rāma.
अभ्यासातिशयात्तस्य मनो लीनं हि सर्वदा ।
सदा समाहितस्वान्तो व्यवहारो न तस्य हि ॥ ४६ ॥
abhyāsa-atiśayāt tasya mano līnaṁ hi sarvadā ।
sadā samāhita-svāntaḥ vyavahāraḥ na tasya hi ॥ 46 ॥

abhyāsa-atiśayāt — by excessive practice, tasya — his, manaḥ — mind, līnaṁ — absorbed, hi — indeed, sarvadā — always, sadā — always, samāhita-svāntaḥ — composed mind, vyavahāraḥ — activity, na — not, tasya — his, hi — indeed.
By excessive practice, his mind is always absorbed. His activity is not there, as his mind is always composed.
यो देहयात्रानिर्वाहः सोऽपि तस्य युषुप्तिवत्‌ ।
यथा कश्चित्‌ सुषुप्तिस्थो वासनामात्रतः क्वचित्‌ ॥ ४७ ॥
yo deha-yātrā-nirvāhaḥ saḥ api tasya yuṣupti-vat ।
yathā kaścit suṣupti-stho vāsanā-mātrataḥ kvacit ॥ 47 ॥

yaḥ — which, deha-yātrā-nirvāhaḥ — maintaining the body, saḥ — that, api — even, tasya — his, yuṣupti-vat — like deep sleep, yathā — as, kaścit — someone, suṣupti-sthaḥ — in deep sleep, vāsanā-mātrataḥ — only by tendencies, kvacit — sometimes.
Even the maintenance of his body is like deep sleep. Just as someone in deep sleep sometimes acts only by tendencies.
किञ्चिदुक्त्वा च कृत्वा च न पश्चाद्वेद किञ्चन ।
यथा च मदिरामत्तो वदन्‌ कुर्वन्न वेद वै ॥ ४८ ॥
kiñcid uktvā ca kṛtvā ca na paścāt veda kiñcana ।
yathā ca madirā-matto vadann kurvann veda vai ॥ 48 ॥

kiñcit — something, uktvā — saying, ca — and, kṛtvā — doing, ca — and, na — not, paścāt — afterwards, veda — knows, kiñcana — anything, yathā — as, ca — and, madirā-mattaḥ — drunk, vadann — speaking, kurvann — doing, veda — knows, vai — indeed.
Saying or doing something, he does not know anything afterwards, just as a drunk person does not know what he speaks or does.
एवमेष महायोगी लोकयात्राबहिर्गत ।
किञ्चित्‌ कदाचित्‌ कुर्वश्च न विजानाति तत्पुनः ॥ ४९ ॥
evam eṣa mahā-yogī loka-yātrā-bahirgata ।
kiñcit kadācit kurvaś ca na vijānāti tat punaḥ ॥ 49 ॥

evam — thus, eṣaḥ — this, mahā-yogī — great yogi, loka-yātrā-bahirgataḥ — beyond worldly activities, kiñcit — something, kadācit — sometimes, kurvan — doing, ca — and, na — not, vijānāti — knows, tat — that, punaḥ — again.
Thus, this great yogi, beyond worldly activities, sometimes does something but does not know it again.
प्रारब्धवासनाभ्यां तु स देहो निर्वहेत्‌ सदा ।
यस्तूत्तमः सुविज्ञानी देहस्तस्यापि नास्ति हि ॥ ५० ॥
prārabdha-vāsanābhyāṁ tu sa deho nirvahet sadā ।
yaḥ tu uttamaḥ su-vijñānī dehaḥ tasya api na asti hi ॥ 50 ॥

prārabdha-vāsanābhyām — by past tendencies, tu — but, saḥ — that, dehaḥ — body, nirvahet — functions, sadā — always, yaḥ — who, tu — but, uttamaḥ — highest, su-vijñānī — wise, dehaḥ — body, tasya — his, api — even, na — not, asti — is, hi — indeed.
But the body always functions by past tendencies. For the highest wise one, even the body does not exist.
व्यवहारं करोत्येष रथसारथिवत्‌ स्थित ।
यथा रथेन व्यापारं कुर्वन्‌ न रथदेहकः ॥ ५१ ॥
vyavahāraṁ karoti eṣaḥ ratha-sārathi-vat sthita ।
yathā rathena vyāpāraṁ kurvan na ratha-dehakaḥ ॥ 51 ॥

vyavahāram — activity, karoti — does, eṣaḥ — he, ratha-sārathi-vat — like a charioteer, sthitaḥ — situated, yathā — as, rathena — with a chariot, vyāpāram — action, kurvan — doing, na — not, ratha-dehakaḥ — body of the chariot.
He performs activities like a charioteer, situated as if with a chariot, doing actions but not being the body of the chariot.
सारथिः स्यादेवमेव देहव्यापारतत्परः ।
न देही नापि व्यापारी शुद्धसंवेदनात्मकः ॥ ५२ ॥
sārathiḥ syāt evam eva deha-vyāpāra-tat-paraḥ ।
na dehī na api vyāpārī śuddha-saṁvedana-ātmakaḥ ॥ 52 ॥

sārathiḥ — charioteer, syāt — would be, evam eva — just so, deha-vyāpāra-tat-paraḥ — engaged in body activities, na — not, dehī — body, na api — nor, vyāpārī — actor, śuddha-saṁvedana-ātmakaḥ — of pure consciousness.
Just so, the charioteer would be engaged in body activities, not the body nor the actor, but of pure consciousness.
अन्तरत्यच्छसुस्वान्तो बहिर्व्यवहरत्यसौ ।
यथा स्त्रीवेषितो नाट्ये द्वैरूप्यमुपसङ्गतः ॥ ५३ ॥
antar-atyaccha-susvāntaḥ bahiḥ vyavaharati asau ।
yathā strī-veṣitaḥ nāṭye dvai-rūpyam upasaṅgataḥ ॥ 53 ॥

antar-atyaccha-susvāntaḥ — inner pure mind, bahiḥ — externally, vyavaharati — acts, asau — he, yathā — as, strī-veṣitaḥ — dressed as a woman, nāṭye — in a play, dvai-rūpyam — dual role, upasaṅgataḥ — assuming.
With an inner pure mind, he acts externally as one dressed as a woman in a play, assuming a dual role.
यथा क्रीडन्‌ कुमारेण प्रौढस्तद्दोषवर्जितः ।
एवमेष जगत्क्रीडातत्परो निर्मलाशयः ॥ ५४ ॥
yathā krīḍan kumāreṇa prauḍhaḥ tad-doṣa-varjitaḥ ।
evam eṣa jagat-krīḍā-tat-paraḥ nirmala-āśayaḥ ॥ 54 ॥

yathā — as, krīḍan — playing, kumāreṇa — with a child, prauḍhaḥ — adult, tad-doṣa-varjitaḥ — free from that fault, evam — thus, eṣa — this, jagat-krīḍā-tat-paraḥ — engaged in the play of the world, nirmala-āśayaḥ — pure-hearted.
As an adult playing with a child is free from being a child, thus, this one engaged in the play of the world is pure-hearted.
मध्यज्ञानी निरोधस्य प्रकर्षेणाचलस्थितिः ।
अचलस्थितिरेतस्य विचारस्य प्रकर्षतः ॥ ५५ ॥
madhya-jñānī nirodhasya prakarṣeṇa acala-sthitiḥ ।
