kim asti ki nāsti loke ko'tyantāsambhavī bhavet ।
etāvad uktvā nṛpate mocaya drutam agrajam ॥ 106 ॥

kim — what, asti — exists, ki — what, nāsti — does not exist, loke — in the world, kaḥ — who, atyantāsambhavī — absolutely impossible, bhavet — may be, etāvat — thus, uktvā — having said, nṛpate — O king, mocaya — release, drutam — quickly, agrajam — elder brother
What exists and what does not exist in the world? Who may be absolutely impossible? Having said thus, O king, I’ll release the elder brother quickly.
दृगस्ति नास्ति वै दृश्यं व्यवहारो ह्यसम्भवी ।
उक्तमेतद्‌ ब्रह्मरक्षो मुञ्च मद्‌भ्रातरं द्रुतम्‌ ॥ १०७ ॥
dṛg asti nāsti vai dṛśyaṁ vyavahāro hy asambhavī ।
uktam etad brahmarakṣo muñca mad bhrātaraṁ drutam ॥ 107 ॥

dṛk — seer, asti — exists, nāsti — does not exist, vai — indeed, dṛśyam — the seen, vyavahāraḥ — transactions of the world, hi — indeed, asambhavī — impossible, uktam — said, etad — this, brahmarakṣaḥ — O Brahma Rakshasa, muñca — release, mad — my, bhrātaram — brother, drutam — quickly
The seer exists, indeed the seen does not exist. The transactions of the world are indeed impossible. This is said. O Brahma Rakshasa, release my brother quickly.
श्रुत्वैतदथ सन्तुष्टो मुमोच ब्रह्मराक्षसः ।
रुक्माङ्गदं ततः पश्चादभवद्‌ ब्राह्मणो हि सः ॥ १०८ ॥
śrutvaitad atha santuṣṭo mumoca brahmarākṣasaḥ ।
rukmāṅgadaṁ tataḥ paścād abhavad brāhmaṇo hi saḥ ॥ 108 ॥

śrutvā — having heard, etat — this, atha — then, santuṣṭaḥ — satisfied, mumoca — released, brahmarākṣasaḥ — Brahma Rakshasa, rukmāṅgadam — Rukmangada, tataḥ — then, paścāt — afterwards, abhavat — became, brāhmaṇaḥ — a Brahmin, hi — indeed, saḥ — he
Having heard this, the Brahma Rakshasa, satisfied, released Rukmangada. Then afterwards, he indeed became a Brahmin.
तेजस्विनं तपोमूर्तिं दृष्ट्वा ब्राह्मणरूपिणम्‌ ।
पप्रच्छतू राजसुतौ को भवानिति शङ्कितौ ॥ १०९ ॥
tejasvinaṁ tapo-mūrtiṁ dṛṣṭvā brāhmaṇa-rūpiṇam ।
papracchatu rājasutau ko bhavān iti śaṅkitau ॥ 109 ॥

tejasvinam — radiant one, tapaḥ-mūrtim — embodiment of penance, dṛṣṭvā — seeing, brāhmaṇa-rūpiṇam — in the form of a Brahmin, papracchatu — asked, rājasutau — the princes, kaḥ — who, bhavān — you, iti — thus, śaṅkitau — with doubt
Seeing the radiant embodiment of penance in the form of a Brahmin, the princes asked with doubt, "Who are you?"
अथ प्राह ब्राह्मणाग्रयः स्वं वृत्तं वै यथातथम्‌ ।
अहं पुरा ब्राह्मणस्तु मगधेष्वभिविश्रुतः ॥ ११० ॥
atha prāha brāhmaṇāgrayaḥ svaṁ vṛttaṁ vai yathā-tatham ।
ahaṁ purā brāhmaṇas tu magadheṣv abhiviśrutaḥ ॥ 110 ॥

atha — then, prāha — said, brāhmaṇāgrayaḥ — the foremost Brahmin, svam — his own, vṛttam — story, vai — indeed, yathā-tatham — as it was, aham — I, purā — formerly, brāhmaṇaḥ — Brahmin, tu — but, magadheṣu — in Magadha, abhiviśrutaḥ — well-known
Then the foremost Brahmin told his own story as it was. "I was formerly a Brahmin, well-known in Magadha."
वसुमानिति विख्यातः सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः ।
सभासु निर्जिता भूयो मया विद्याभिमानिना ॥ १११ ॥
vasumān iti vikhyātaḥ sarvaśāstra-viśāradaḥ ।
sabhāsu nirjitā bhūyo mayā vidyābhimāninā ॥ 111 ॥

vasumān — Vasuman, iti — thus, vikhyātaḥ — famous, sarvaśāstra — all scriptures, viśāradaḥ — expert, sabhāsu — in assemblies, nirjitā — defeated, bhūyaḥ — again, mayā — by me, vidyā — knowledge, abhimāninā — proud
"Famous as Vasuman, expert in all scriptures, I defeated many in assemblies, again and again, proud of my knowledge."
विद्वांसः शतशो विप्रास्ततोऽत्यन्तसुगर्वितः ।
कदाचिद्‌ मगधेशस्य सभायामष्टकं मुनिम्‌ ॥ ११२ ॥
vidvāṁsaḥ śataśo viprās tato'tyanta-sugarvitaḥ ।
kadācid magadheśasya sabhāyām aṣṭakaṁ munim ॥ 112 ॥

vidvāṁsaḥ — scholars, śataśaḥ — by hundreds, viprāḥ — Brahmins, tataḥ — then, atyanta — extremely, sugarvitaḥ — proud, kadācit — once, magadheśasya — of the king of Magadha, sabhāyām — in the assembly, aṣṭakam — Ashtaka, munim — sage
"Scholars by the hundreds, Brahmins, then I became extremely proud. Once, in the assembly of the king of Magadha, a sage named Ashtaka..."
परावरज्ञं संशान्तं वादार्थी सङ्गतोऽभवम्‌ ।
शुष्कतर्कैकनिपुण आत्मविद्याविचारणे ॥ ११३ ॥
parāvarajñaṁ saṁśāntaṁ vādarī saṅgato'bhavam ।
śuṣkatarkaika-nipuṇa ātmavidyāvicāraṇe ॥ 113 ॥

parāvara-jñam — knower of the higher and lower, saṁśāntam — completely tranquil, vādarī — for debate, saṅgataḥ — met, abhavam — became, śuṣka-tarka — dry logic, eka-nipuṇa — solely skilled, ātmavidyā — self-knowledge, vicāraṇe — inquiring
"Knower of the higher and lower, completely tranquil, for debate, I met him. Skilled solely in dry logic, inquiring into self-knowledge."
ततो मया स आक्षिप्तः केवलं तर्कयुक्तिभिः ।
समाधानवचस्तस्य बह्वागमसुबृंहितम्‌ ॥ ११४ ॥
tato mayā sa ākṣiptaḥ kevalaṁ tarka-yuktibhiḥ ।
samādhāna-vacas tasya bahv-āgama-subṛṁhitam ॥ 114 ॥

tataḥ — then, mayā — by me, saḥ — he, ākṣiptaḥ — challenged, kevalam — only, tarka-yuktibhiḥ — by logical arguments, samādhāna-vacaḥ — words of resolution, tasya — his, bahu — many, āgama — scriptures, subṛṁhitam — well-supported
"Then I challenged him only with logical arguments. His words of resolution were well-supported by many scriptures."
दूषयित्वा तर्कजालैरधिक्षेपपरोऽभवम्‌ ।
अधिक्षिप्तोऽपि बहुधा मया राजसभागतः ॥ ११५ ॥
dūṣayitvā tarka-jālair adhikṣepa-paro'bhavam ।
adhikṣipto'pi bahudhā mayā rājasabhāgataḥ ॥ 115 ॥

dūṣayitvā — criticizing, tarka-jālaiḥ — by webs of logic, adhikṣepa-paraḥ — focused on insults, abhavam — became, adhikṣiptaḥ — insulted, api — even, bahudhā — many times, mayā — by me, rājasabhā-gataḥ — assembly of the king
"Criticizing with webs of logic, I became focused on insults. Even insulted many times by me, in the assembly of the king."
शान्तस्तूष्णीं बभूवाथ शिष्यस्तस्य महात्मनः ।
काश्यपो मां क्रोधवशाच्छशाप नृपसंसदि ॥ ११६ ॥
śāntas tūṣṇīṁ babhūvātha śiṣyas tasya mahātmanaḥ ।
kāśyapo māṁ krodhavaśāc chaśāpa nṛpa-saṁsadi ॥ 116 ॥

śāntaḥ — calm, tūṣṇīm — silent, babhūva — became, atha — then, śiṣyaḥ — disciple, tasya — his, mahātmanaḥ — great soul, kāśyapaḥ — Kashyapa, mām — me, krodhavaśāt — out of anger, śaśāpa — cursed, nṛpa-saṁsadi — in the assembly of the king
"He was calm and silent. Then his disciple, the great soul Kashyapa, cursed me out of anger, in the assembly of the king."
आचार्य मेऽधिक्षिपसि त्वमस्थाने द्विजाधम ।
यतस्तस्माच्चिरं कालं ब्रह्मरक्षो भविष्यसि ॥ ११७ ॥
ācārya me'dhikṣipasi tvam asthāne dvijādham ।
yataḥ tasmāc ciraṁ kālaṁ brahmarakṣo bhaviṣyasi ॥ 117 ॥

ācārya — teacher, me — my, adhikṣipasi — you insult, tvam — you, asthāne — inappropriately, dvija-adham — lowest of the twice-born, yataḥ — since, tasmāt — therefore, ciraṁ kālam — for a long time, brahma-rakṣaḥ — Brahma Rakshasa, bhaviṣyasi — you will become
"Teacher, you insult my teacher inappropriately, lowest of the twice-born. Since therefore, for a long time, you will become a Brahma Rakshasa."
शप्त एवमहं तेन भीतोऽत्यन्तं तदा मुनिम्‌ ।
वेपमानः प्रणम्याशु चाष्टकं शरणं गतः ॥ ११८ ॥
śapta evam ahaṁ tena bhīto'tyantaṁ tadā munim ।
vepamānaḥ praṇamyāśu cāṣṭakaṁ śaraṇaṁ gataḥ ॥ 118 ॥

śaptaḥ — cursed, evam — thus, aham — I, tena — by him, bhītaḥ — frightened, atyantam — greatly, tadā — then, munim — sage, vepamānaḥ — trembling, praṇamya — bowing, āśu — quickly, cāṣṭakam — Ashtaka, śaraṇam — refuge, gataḥ — took
"Cursed thus by him, greatly frightened, then I, trembling, bowing, quickly took refuge in the sage Ashtaka."
मयि सोऽथ दयां चक्रे विरोधिन्यपि शान्तधीः ।
शापस्यान्तं ददौ मह्यं तन्मे निग्दतः शृणु ॥ ११९ ॥
mayi so'tha dayāṁ cakre virodhini api śāntadhīḥ ।
śāpasya antaṁ dadau mahyaṁ tan me nigdataḥ śṛṇu ॥ 119 ॥

mayi — to me, saḥ — he, atha — then, dayām — compassion, cakre — did, virodhini — to the opponent, api — even, śānta-dhīḥ — calm-minded, śāpasya — curse's, antam — end, dadau — gave, mahyam — to me, tat — that, me — my, nigdataḥ — attentively, śṛṇu — listen
"To me, then he showed compassion, even to the opponent, the calm-minded. He gave an end to the curse for me. Listen attentively to that."
प्रश्नांस्त्वया मयि कृतान्‌ प्रतयुक्तांश्च मया हि तान्‌ ।
स्थापितान्‌ केवलैस्तर्कैर्यदेकः प्रतिवक्ष्यति ॥ १२० ॥
praśnān tvayā mayi kṛtān pratiyuktāṁś ca mayā hi tān ।
sthāpitān kevalais tarkair yad ekaḥ prativakṣyati ॥ 120 ॥

praśnān — questions, tvayā — by you, mayi — to me, kṛtān — made, pratiyuktān — answered, ca — and, mayā — by me, hi — indeed, tān — those, sthāpitān — established, kevalaiḥ — solely, tarkaiḥ — by logic, yat — what, ekaḥ — one, prativakṣyati — will answer
"The questions made by you to me, and answered by me indeed, those established solely by logic, when that one will answer."
कश्चिद्‌ विद्वांस्तदा शापाद्विमुक्तस्त्वं भविष्यसि ।
तच्छापादद्य ते मुक्तश्चिराय नृपनन्दन ॥ १२१ ॥
kaścid vidvāṁs tadā śāpād vimuktas tvaṁ bhaviṣyasi ।
tacchāpād adya te muktaś cirāya nṛpanandana ॥ 121 ॥

kaścit — some, vidvān — wise one, tadā — then, śāpāt — from curse, vimuktaḥ — liberated, tvaṁ — you, bhaviṣyasi — will be, tac-chāpāt — from that curse, adya — today, te — your, muktaḥ — freed, cirāya — for a long time, nṛpanandana — O prince
"Some wise one will liberate you from the curse then. Today you are freed from that curse after a long time, O prince."
तत्त्वां मन्ये महात्मानं ज्ञातज्ञेयं नृषूत्तमम्‌ ।
इत्युक्तस्तेन विप्रेण विस्मितोऽभून्नृपात्मजः ॥ १२२ ॥
tattvāṁ manye mahātmānaṁ jñātajñeyaṁ nṛṣūttamam ।
ity uktas tena vipreṇa vismito'bhūn nṛpātmajaḥ ॥ 122 ॥

tat — that, tvām — you, manye — I consider, mahātmānam — great soul, jñāta-jñeyam — knower of the known, nṛṣūttamam — best among men, iti — thus, uktas — spoken, tena — by him, vipreṇa — by the Brahmin, vismitaḥ — astonished, abhūt — became, nṛpātmajaḥ — the prince
"That, you I consider a great soul, knower of the known, best among men.” Thus spoken by him, the Brahmin, the prince became astonished.
ततो भूयो नृपसुतोऽनुयुक्तस्तेन सर्वशः ।
वसुमन्तं बोधयित्वा सम्यक्‌ प्रागात्‌ पुरं स्वकम्‌ ॥ १२३ ॥
tato bhūyo nṛpasuto'nuyuktas tena sarvaśaḥ ।
vasumantaṁ bodhayitvā samyak prāgāt puraṁ svakam ॥ 123 ॥

tataḥ — then, bhūyaḥ — again, nṛpasutaḥ — the prince, anuyuktaḥ — questioned, tena — by him, sarvaśaḥ — entirely, vasumantam — Vasuman, bodhayitvā — enlightening, samyak — completely, prāgāt — went, puram — city, svakam — his own
Then again the prince, questioned entirely by him, enlightening Vasuman completely, went to his own city.
प्रणम्य वसुमन्तं तं सहितो भ्रातृसैनिकैः ।
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं यत्पृष्टं भार्गव त्वया ॥ १२४ ॥
praṇamya vasumantaṁ taṁ sahito bhrātṛ-sainikaiḥ ।
etat te sarvam ākhyātaṁ yat pṛṣṭaṁ bhārgava tvayā ॥ 124 ॥

praṇamya — bowing, vasumantam — Vasuman, tam — him, sahitaḥ — accompanied, bhrātṛ-sainikaiḥ — by brothers and soldiers, etat — this, te — to you, sarvam — all, ākhyātam — told, yat — what, pṛṣṭam — asked, bhārgava — O Bhargava, tvayā — by you
Bowing to Vasuman, accompanied by brothers and soldiers, this all is told to you, what was asked by you, O Bhargava.

colophon.en: Thus ends the twenty-first chapter named "The Story of the Demon" in the esteemed Tripura Rahasya.

lines.text: श्रुत्वैवं राक्षसकथां रामो भृगुकुलोद्वहः ।
पुनः पप्रच्छावधूतकुलेशं प्रश्रयाश्रयः ॥ १ ॥
śrutvā evaṁ rākṣasa-kathāṁ rāmo bhṛgukula-udvahaḥ
punaḥ papraccha avadhūta-kuleśaṁ praśraya-āśrayaḥ ॥ 1 ॥

śrutvā - having heard, evaṁ - thus, rākṣasa-kathām - the story of the Rakshasa, rāmaḥ - Rama, bhṛgukula-udvahaḥ - scion of Bhrigu's clan, punaḥ - again, papraccha - asked, avadhūta-kuleśam - lord of the avadhutas, praśraya-āśrayaḥ - with humility
Having heard the story of the Rakshasa, Rama, the scion of Bhrigu's clan, with humility, asked the lord of the avadhutas again.
भगवन्‌ किं तेन पृष्टं शापमुक्तद्विजेन वै ।
हेमाङ्गदेन किं प्रोक्तमेतन्मे कृपया वद ॥ २ ॥
bhagavan kiṁ tena pṛṣṭaṁ śāpa-mukta-dvijena vai
hemāṅgadena kiṁ proktam etan me kṛpayā vada ॥ 2 ॥

bhagavan - O Lord, kim - what, tena - by him, pṛṣṭam - asked, śāpa-mukta-dvijena - by the curse-freed Brahmin, vai - indeed, hemāṅgadena - by Hemangada, kim - what, proktam - spoken, etat - this, me - to me, kṛpayā - kindly, vada - tell
O Lord, what was asked by the curse-freed Brahmin, and what did Hemangada say? Kindly tell this to me.
कौतुक्यत्यन्तमत्राहं न तदल्पं भवेत्‌ क्वचित्‌ ।
इति पृष्टः पुनः प्राह दत्तात्रेयो दयापरः ॥ ३ ॥
kautukya-atyantam-atra-ahaṁ na-tad-alpam-bhavet-kvacit
iti-pṛṣṭaḥ-punaḥ-prāha-dattātreyo-dayā-paraḥ ॥ 3 ॥

kautukya - curiosity, atyantam - greatly, atra - here, aham - I, na - not, tad - that, alpam - small, bhavet - may be, kvacit - ever, iti - thus, pṛṣṭaḥ - asked, punaḥ - again, prāha - said, dattātreyaḥ - Dattatreya, dayā-paraḥ - compassionate
I am greatly curious about this, and it is not a small matter. Thus asked again, compassionate Dattatreya said.
राम तत्ते प्रवक्ष्यामि महार्थं तत्प्रभाषितम्‌ ।
ततः पप्रच्छ वसुमान्‌ हेमाङ्गदमुपस्थितम्‌ ॥ ४ ॥
rāma tat te pravakṣyāmi mahārthaṁ tat prabhāṣitam
tataḥ papraccha vasumān hemāṅgadam upasthitam ॥ 4 ॥

rāma - O Rama, tat - that, te - to you, pravakṣyāmi - I will tell, mahārtham - great meaning, tat - that, prabhāṣitam - spoken, tataḥ - then, papraccha - asked, vasumān - Vasuman, hemāṅgadam - Hemangada, upasthitam - present
O Rama, I will tell you that which was spoken with great meaning. Then Vasuman asked Hemangada, who was present.
राजपुत्र किञ्चिदहं पृच्छामि त्वं समीरय ।
अहमष्टकयोगीशात्‌ तदज्ञासिषमादितः ॥ ५ ॥
rājaputra kiñcid ahaṁ pṛcchāmi tvaṁ samīraya
aham aṣṭaka-yogīśāt tad ajñāsiṣam āditaḥ ॥ 5 ॥
rājaputra - O prince, kiñcid - something, aham - I, pṛcchāmi - ask, tvam - you, samīraya - answer, aham - I, aṣṭaka-yogīśāt - from the yogi Ashtaka, tat - that, ajñāsiṣam - learned, āditaḥ - at first
O prince, I ask you something, you answer. I learned that at first from the yogi Ashtaka.
भूयस्त्वदुक्त्या च सम्यग्‌ विदितं परमं पदम्‌ ।
किन्तु ते ज्ञाततत्वस्य कथं स्थितिरियं भवेत्‌ ॥ ६ ॥
bhūyas tvad-uktyā ca samyag viditaṁ paramaṁ padam
kintu te jñāta-tattvasya kathaṁ sthitir iyaṁ bhavet ॥ 6 ॥

bhūyaḥ - again, tvad-uktyā - by your words, ca - and, samyak - completely, viditam - known, paramam - supreme, padam - state, kintu - but, te - your, jñāta-tattvasya - of the knower of truth, katham - how, sthitiḥ - state, iyam - this, bhavet - may be
Again, by your words, the supreme state is completely known. But how is the state of the knower of truth?
कथं ज्ञातसुविज्ञेयो व्यवहारपरायणः ।
ध्वान्तप्रकाशयोर्यद्वत्‌ स्थितिरेकत्र सम्भवेत्‌ ॥ ७ ॥
kathaṁ jñāta-su-vijñeyo vyavahāra-parāyaṇaḥ
dhvānta-prakāśayor yadvat sthitir ekatra sambhavet ॥ 7 ॥

katham - how, jñāta-su-vijñeyaḥ - well known to the knower, vyavahāra-parāyaṇaḥ - dedicated to actions, dhvānta-prakāśayoḥ - of darkness and light, yadvat - as, sthitiḥ - state, ekatra - together, sambhavet - can be
How can the state of the well-known, of the knower, be dedicated to actions, be like the state of darkness and light together?
एतन्मे राजतनय ब्रूहि सम्यग्‌ यथास्थितम्‌ ।
इत्यापृष्टः प्राह हेमाङ्गदस्तं ब्राह्मणोत्तमम्‌ ॥ ८ ॥
etan me rājatanaya brūhi samyag yathāsthitam
ity āpṛṣṭaḥ prāha hemāṅgadas taṁ brāhmaṇottamam ॥ 8 ॥

etat - this, me - to me, rājatanaya - O prince, brūhi - tell, samyak - correctly, yathāsthitam - as it is, iti - thus, āpṛṣṭaḥ - asked, prāha - said, hemāṅgadaḥ - Hemangada, tam - to him, brāhmaṇottamam - best of Brahmins
O prince, tell this to me correctly as it is. Thus asked, Hemangada said to him, the best of Brahmins.
ब्रह्मन्‌ ते भ्रान्तिरद्यापि न सम्यक्‌ प्रविनाशिता ।
व्यवहारेण किं ज्ञानं बाध्यते स्वात्मसम्भवम्‌ ॥ ९ ॥
brahman te bhrāntir adyāpi na samyak pravināśitā
vyavahāreṇa kiṁ jñānaṁ bādhyate svātmasambhavam ॥ 9 ॥

brahman - O Brahmin, te - your, bhrāntiḥ - delusion, adyāpi - even now, na - not, samyak - completely, pravināśitā - destroyed, vyavahāreṇa - by actions, kim - what, jñānam - knowledge, bādhyate - is obstructed, svātmasambhavam - self-existent
O Brahmin, your delusion is even now not completely destroyed. By actions, how is knowledge, which is self-existent, obstructed?
व्यवहारवशाद्‌ ज्ञानं बाध्यते चेत्‌ ततः कथम्‌ ।
पुरुषार्थस्य लाभः स्यात्‌ स्वाप्तज्ञानसमेन वै ॥ १० ॥
vyavahāravaśād jñānaṁ bādhyate cet tataḥ katham
puruṣārthasya lābhaḥ syāt svāpta-jñāna-samena vai ॥ 10 ॥

vyavahāra-vaśāt - by actions, jñānam - knowledge, bādhyate - is obstructed, cet - if, tataḥ - then, katham - how, puruṣārthasya - of human goals, lābhaḥ - gain, syāt - may be, svāpta-jñāna-samena - with sleep-like knowledge, vai - indeed
If knowledge is obstructed by actions, then how is the gain of human goals possible by sleep-like knowledge?
सर्वोऽपि व्यवहारोऽयं जानमाश्रित्य सम्भवेत्‌ ।
तज्ज्ञानं बाध्यते तेन कथं तन्मे समीरय ॥ ११ ॥
sarvo'pi vyavahāro'yaṁ jñānam āśritya sambhavet
tat jñānaṁ bādhyate tena kathaṁ tan me samīraya ॥ 11 ॥

sarvaḥ - all, api - even, vyavahāraḥ - actions, ayam - this, jñānam - knowledge, āśritya - relying on, sambhavet - may be, tat - that, jñānam - knowledge, bādhyate - obstructed, tena - by that, katham - how, tat - that, me - to me, samīraya - explain
All actions, even this, may rely on knowledge. How is that knowledge obstructed by that? Explain this to me.
ज्ञानं तदेव हि भवेद्‌ यत्रेदं भासते जगत्‌ ।
सङ्कल्पाद्‌ व्यवहारो हि ज्ञाने सर्वः प्रकाशते ॥ १२ ॥
jñānaṁ tadeva hi bhaved yatra idaṁ bhāsate jagat
saṅkalpād vyavahāro hi jñāne sarvaḥ prakāśate ॥ 12 ॥

jñānam - knowledge, tat - that, eva - indeed, hi - indeed, bhavet - may be, yatra - where, idam - this, bhāsate - shines, jagat - world, saṅkalpāt - by resolve, vyavahāraḥ - actions, hi - indeed, jñāne - in knowledge, sarvaḥ - all, prakāśate - shines
Knowledge is indeed where this world shines. By resolve, all actions indeed shine in knowledge.
असङ्कल्पेन तद्रूपमनुलक्ष्य धिया सकृत्‌ ।
कृतार्थो बन्धनिर्मुक्तो भवतीति सुनिश्चयः ॥ १३ ॥
asaṅkalpena tad rūpam anulakṣya dhiyā sakṛt
kṛtārtho bandha-nirmukto bhavati iti su-niścayaḥ ॥ 13 ॥

asaṅkalpena - without resolve, tat - that, rūpam - form, anulakṣya - observing, dhiyā - by intellect, sakṛt - once, kṛtārthaḥ - accomplished, bandha-nirmuktaḥ - free from bondage, bhavati - becomes, iti - thus, su-niścayaḥ - well-determined
Without resolve, observing that form by intellect once, one becomes accomplished, free from bondage. Thus, it is well-determined.
तस्माद्‌ ब्रह्मन्न ते प्रश्नः सम्मतोऽयं सुबुद्धिभिः ।
पुनस्तं प्राह वसुमान्‌ नृपसूनुं महाशयम्‌ ॥ १४ ॥
tasmād brahman na te praśnaḥ sammato'yaṁ subuddhibhiḥ
punas taṁ prāha vasumān nṛpasūnuṁ mahāśayam ॥ 14 ॥

tasmāt - therefore, brahman - O Brahmin, na - not, te - your, praśnaḥ - question, sammataḥ - approved, ayam - this, subuddhibhiḥ - by the wise, punaḥ - again, tam - to him, prāha - said, vasumān - Vasuman, nṛpasūnum - to the prince, mahāśayam - O great one
Therefore, O Brahmin, your question is not approved by the wise. Again, Vasuman said to the prince, "O great one."
सत्यं राजकुमारैतद्‌ मयापीत्थं सुनिश्चितम्‌ ।
स्वरूपं निर्विकल्पं हि संवेदनमिहोच्यते ॥ १५ ॥
satyaṁ rājakumāra etad mayā api ittham su-niścitam
svarūpaṁ nirvikalpaṁ hi saṁvedanam iha ucyate ॥ 15 ॥

satyam - truth, rājakumāra - O prince, etad - this, mayā - by me, api - also, ittham - thus, su-niścitam - well-determined, svarūpam - true nature, nirvikalpam - without thoughts, hi - indeed, saṁvedanam - awareness, iha - here, ucyate - is said
Truth, O prince, this is also well-determined by me. True nature is indeed awareness without thoughts, as it is said here.
सविकल्पत्वमापन्ने पुनर्भ्रान्तिः कुतो नहि ।
विकल्प एव हि भ्रान्तिर्यथा रज्जौ भुजङ्गमः ॥ १६ ॥
savikalpatvam āpanne punar bhrāntiḥ kuto nahi
vikalpa eva hi bhrāntiḥ yathā rajjau bhujangamaḥ ॥ 16 ॥

savikalpatvam - with alternatives, āpanne - having attained, punaḥ - again, bhrāntiḥ - delusion, kutaḥ - where, nahi - not, vikalpaḥ - alternative, eva - indeed, hi - indeed, bhrāntiḥ - delusion, yathā - like, rajjau - in the rope, bhujangamaḥ - snake
With thoughts, having attained, where is not delusion again? Indeed, thoughts are delusion, like a snake in the rope.
शृणु ब्रह्मन्‌ न जानासि भ्रमाभ्रमविनिर्णयम्‌ ।
गगनं नीलमाभाति गगनं जानतामपि ॥ १७ ॥
śṛṇu brahman na jānāsi bhramābhrama-vinirṇayam
gaganaṁ nīlam ābhāti gaganaṁ jānātām api ॥ 17 ॥

śṛṇu - listen, brahman - O Brahmin, na - not, jānāsi - you know, bhrama-abhrama-vinirṇayam - distinction between delusion and non-delusion, gaganam - sky, nīlam - blue, ābhāti - appears, gaganam - sky, jānātām - to those who know, api - even
Listen, O Brahmin, you do not know the distinction between delusion and non-delusion. The sky appears blue even to those who know.
व्यवहारं च कुर्वन्ति नीलं नभ इति क्वचित्‌ ।
तावतैव तु तज्ज्ञानं न भ्रान्तिरभिधीयते ॥ १८ ॥
vyavahāraṁ ca kurvanti nīlaṁ nabha iti kvacit
tāvataiva tu tat-jñānaṁ na bhrāntiḥ abhidhīyate ॥ 18 ॥

vyavahāram - actions, ca - and, kurvanti - they do, nīlam - blue, nabha - sky, iti - thus, kvacit - sometimes, tāvata - by that, eva - indeed, tu - but, tat-jñānam - that knowledge, na - not, bhrāntiḥ - delusion, abhidhīyate - is called
They sometimes act saying the sky is blue. But by that knowledge, it is not called delusion.
अतत्त्वज्ञे हि सा भ्रान्तिस्तत्त्वज्ञे सा प्रमैव हि ।
हतप्रामाण्यजीवं तज्ज्ञानं मृतमहाहिवत्‌ ॥ १९ ॥
atattvajñe hi sā bhrāntiḥ tattvajñe sā pramaiva hi
hataprāmāṇya-jīvam tat-jñānam mṛta-mahāhivat ॥ 19 ॥
To the ignorant, however, that is delusion; to the knower of truth, that is indeed true knowledge. That knowledge is like a dead great snake without authority or living.
दर्पणप्रतिबिम्बस्य व्यवहारः समो भवेत्‌ ।
अभिज्ञस्यानभिज्ञस्य चाप्यतोऽस्ति भिदा तयोः ॥ २० ॥
darpaṇa-pratibimbasya vyavahāraḥ samo bhavet
abhijñasya anabhijñasya ca api ataḥ asti bhidā tayoḥ ॥ 20 ॥

darpaṇa-pratibimbasya - of the reflection in the mirror, vyavahāraḥ - action, samaḥ - same, bhavet - may be, abhijñasya - of the knowledgeable, anabhijñasya - of the ignorant, ca - and, api - also, ataḥ - therefore, asti - there is, bhidā - difference, tayoḥ - between them
The action of the reflection in the mirror may be the same for the knowledgeable and the ignorant. But therefore, there is a difference between them.
ज्ञस्य प्रमैव तज्ज्ञानमज्ञस्य तु भ्रमात्मकम्‌ ।
ज्ञानिनां ज्ञानमेव स्यात्‌ सर्वोऽपि व्यवहारकः ॥ २१ ॥
jñasya pramaiva tajjñānam ajñasya tu bhramātmakam
jñānināṁ jñānameva syāt sarvo'pi vyavahārakaḥ ॥ 21 ॥

jñasya - for the wise, pramā - true knowledge, eva - indeed, tat - that, jñānam - knowledge, ajñasya - for the ignorant, tu - but, bhramātmakam - delusion, jñāninām - for the wise, jñānam - knowledge, eva - indeed, syāt - may be, sarvaḥ - all, api - even, vyavahārakaḥ - worldly transactions
For the wise, that knowledge is indeed true knowledge; but for the ignorant, it is delusion. For the wise, knowledge is indeed worldly transactions in all aspects.
दर्पणप्रतिबिम्बानां व्यवहारेण सम्मितः ।
अभिज्ञानामतो भूयो नहि भ्रान्तेः समुद्भवः ॥ २२ ॥
darpaṇa-pratibimbānāṁ vyavahāreṇa sammitah
abhijñānām ato bhūyo nahi bhrānteḥ samudbhavaḥ ॥ 22 ॥

darpaṇa-pratibimbānām - of mirror reflections, vyavahāreṇa - by transaction, sammitah - equal, abhijñānām - for the knowledgeable, ataḥ - therefore, bhūyaḥ - again, nahi - not, bhrānteḥ - of delusion, samudbhavaḥ - arising
By seeing the worldly transactions, as mirror reflections, they are equal for the knowledgeable. Therefore, again, there is no arising of delusion.
केवलाज्ञानजनितं ज्ञानेन विनिवर्तते ।
दोषेण जनितं कस्माद्विलीयेद्‌ ज्ञानमात्रतः ॥ २३ ॥
kevala-ajñāna-janitaṁ jñānena vinivartate
doṣeṇa janitaṁ kasmād vilīyed jñānamātrataḥ ॥ 23 ॥

kevala - only, ajñāna - ignorance, janitam - born, jñānena - by knowledge, vinivartate - is removed, doṣeṇa - by fault, janitam - born, kasmāt - why, vilīyet - dissolves, jñānamātrataḥ - by mere knowledge
That born of ignorance is only removed by knowledge. Why does the fault-born ignorance dissolve by mere knowledge?
अत एव तैमिरिकः पश्येद्‌ जानन्नपि द्वयम्‌ ।
जगदाभास एषस्तु कर्मदोषसमुद्भवः ॥ २४ ॥
ata eva taimirikaḥ paśyed jānannapi dvayam
jagadābhāsa eṣastu karmadoṣa-samudbhavaḥ ॥ 24 ॥

ataḥ - therefore, eva - indeed, taimirikaḥ - the one with defective sight, paśyet - sees, jānannapi - even knowing, dvayam - duality, jagadābhāsaḥ - world appearance, eṣaḥ - this, tu - but, karma-doṣa-samudbhavaḥ - arising from the fault of action
Therefore, indeed, the one with defective sight sees duality even when knowing. This world appearance arises from the fault of action.
तस्मादाकर्मविलयं व्यवहारो न लीयते ।
समाप्ते कर्मणि ततः शिष्येदद्वयचिन्मयम्‌ ॥ २५ ॥
tasmād akarma-vilayaṁ vyavahāro na līyate
samāpte karmaṇi tataḥ śiṣyed advaya-cinmayam ॥ 25 ॥

tasmāt - therefore, akarma - non-action, vilayam - dissolution, vyavahāraḥ - worldly transactions, na - not, līyate - dissolves, samāpte - completed, karmaṇi - action, tataḥ - then, śiṣyet - remains, advaya-cinmayam - non-dual consciousness
Therefore, worldly transactions do not dissolve into non-action. When action is completed, non-dual consciousness remains.
तस्मान्नास्त्येव विज्ञानां कदापि भ्रान्तिसम्भवः ।
इति श्रुत्वा पुनर्विप्रः पप्रच्छ नृपनन्दनम्‌ ॥ २६ ॥
tasmān nāsty eva vijñānāṁ kadāpi bhrānti-sambhavaḥ
iti śrutvā punar vipraḥ papraccha nṛpanandanam ॥ 26 ॥

tasmāt - therefore, na asti - does not exist, eva - indeed, vijñānām - for the wise, kadāpi - ever, bhrānti-sambhavaḥ - occurrence of delusion, iti - thus, śrutvā - hearing, punaḥ - again, vipraḥ - the Brahmin, papraccha - asked, nṛpanandanam - the prince
Therefore, there is no occurrence of delusion for the wise. Thus, hearing this, the Brahmin again asked the prince.
अहो नृपात्मज कथं ज्ञानिनां कर्म सम्भवेत्‌ ।
ज्ञानाग्निसंस्पर्शनेऽपि कर्मतूलः कथं स्थितः ॥ २७ ॥
aho nṛpātmaja kathaṁ jñānināṁ karma sambhavet
jñānāgni-saṁsparśane'pi karma-tūlaḥ kathaṁ sthitaḥ ॥ 27 ॥

aho - O, nṛpātmaja - prince, katham - how, jñāninām - for the wise, karma - action, sambhavet - may be, jñāna-agni - fire of knowledge, saṁsparśane - in contact, api - even, karma-tūlaḥ - action as cotton, katham - how, sthitaḥ - remains
O prince, how may action arise for the wise? Even in contact with the fire of knowledge, how does action as cotton remain?
अथाह हेमाङ्गदोऽपि विप्रं तं नृपनन्दनः ।
ब्रह्मन्‌ शृणु प्रवक्ष्यामि त्रिविधं कर्म ज्ञानिनाम्‌ ॥ २८ ॥
athāha hemāṅgado'pi vipraṁ taṁ nṛpanandanaḥ
brahman śṛṇu pravakṣyāmi trividaṁ karma jñāninām ॥ 28 ॥

atha - then, āha - said, hemāṅgadaḥ - Hemangada, api - also, vipram - to the Brahmin, tam - him, nṛpanandanaḥ - prince, brahman - O Brahmin, śṛṇu - listen, pravakṣyāmi - I will explain, trividaṁ - threefold, karma - action, jñāninām - of the wise
Then Hemangada, the prince, said to the Brahmin, "O Brahmin, listen, I will explain the threefold action of the wise."
सर्वेषां च समानं स्यादपक्वं पक्वमेव च ।
हतोदितं चेति तत्र नश्येद्‌ ज्ञानादमध्यमम्‌ ॥ २९ ॥
sarveṣāṁ ca samānaṁ syād apakvaṁ pakvameva ca
hato-uditaṁ ca iti tatra naśyed jñānād amadhyamam ॥ 29 ॥

sarveṣām - for all, ca - and, samānam - same, syāt - may be, apakvam - unripe, pakvam - ripe, eva - indeed, ca - and, hato-uditaṁ - destroyed and arisen, ca - and, iti - thus, tatra - there, naśyet - destroyed, jñānāt - by knowledge, amadhyamam - not mediocre
For all, the actions may be unripe and ripe. Destroyed and arisen, thus there, all are destroyed by knowledge, which is superior.
कर्मणां पाचकः कालो नियत्या नियतः स्थितः ।
कालेन पाचितप्रायं पक्वं कर्म समीरितम्‌ ॥ ३० ॥
karmaṇāṁ pācakaḥ kālo niyatya niyataḥ sthitaḥ
kālena pācita-prāyaṁ pakvaṁ karma samīritam ॥ 30 ॥

karmaṇām - of actions, pācakaḥ - cook, kālaḥ - time, niyatya - determined, niyataḥ - fixed, sthitaḥ - established, kālena - by time, pācita-prāyam - mostly cooked, pakvam - ripe, karma - action, samīritam - mentioned
The cook of actions is time, which is determined and fixed. By time, those that are mostly cooked are mentioned as ripened action.
अपाचितमपक्वं स्याद्‌ ज्ञानोत्पत्तेरनन्तरम्‌ ।
कृतं हतोदितं विद्धि ज्ञानाद्धतसमुद्भवात्‌ ॥ ३१ ॥
apācitam apakvaṁ syād jñānotpatter anantaram
kṛtaṁ hato-uditaṁ viddhi jñānād hata-samudbhavāt ॥ 31 ॥

apācitam - uncooked, apakvam - unripe, syāt - may be, jñāna-utpatteḥ - arising of knowledge, anantaram - afterwards, kṛtam - done, hato-uditaṁ - destroyed and arisen, viddhi - know, jñānāt - by knowledge, hata-samudbhavāt - arisen from destruction
Uncooked, unripe action may be after the arising of knowledge. Know that these are done, destroyed, by arising of knowledge, arisen from the destruction (of ignorance).
तत्र पक्वं तु यत्‌ कर्म तदारब्धमितीर्यते ।
आवेगं मुक्तशरवत्तिष्ठत्येव फलप्रदम्‌ ॥ ३२ ॥
tatra pakvaṁ tu yat karma tad ārabdham itīryate
āvegaṁ mukta-śara-vat tiṣṭhaty eva phala-pradam ॥ 32 ॥

tatra - there, pakvam - ripe, tu - indeed, yat - what, karma - action, tat - that, ārabdham - commenced, iti - thus, īryate - is said, āvegam - with force, mukta-śara-vat - like a released arrow, tiṣṭhati - stands, eva - indeed, phala-pradam - fruit-bearing
There, indeed, the ripe action that is commenced, thus it is said, stands with force like a released arrow, bearing fruit.
तन्मूलको जगद्भासो ज्ञानस्य तारतम्यतः ।
स्थितोऽपि भ्रान्तितुल्योऽपि न भ्रान्तिः फलभेदतः ॥ ३३ ॥
tan-mūlako jagad-bhāso jñānasya tāratamyataḥ
sthito'pi bhrānti-tulyaḥ api na bhrāntiḥ phala-bhedataḥ ॥ 33 ॥

tat-mūlakaḥ - rooted in that, jagad-bhāsaḥ - world appearance, jñānasya - of knowledge, tāratamyataḥ - by precedence, sthitaḥ - established, api - even, bhrānti-tulyaḥ - like delusion, na - not, bhrāntiḥ - delusion, phala-bhedataḥ - by difference in result
Rooted in that, the world appearance by precedence of knowledge, is established, even like delusion, but not delusion due to a difference in result.
जनयेत्‌ तत्कालफलं मन्दज्ञानवतां स्फुटम्‌ ।
मध्यानामस्फुटं तच्च ज्ञानिनां फलभासनम्‌ ॥ ३४ ॥
janayet tatkāla-phalaṁ manda-jñānavatāṁ sphuṭam
madhyānām asphuṭaṁ tac ca jñānināṁ phala-bhāsanam ॥ 34 ॥

janayet - generates, tatkāla - immediate, phalam - fruit, manda-jñānavatām - of those with intoxicated knowledge, sphuṭam - clear, madhyānām - of the middling, asphuṭam - unclear, tat - that, ca - and, jñāninām - of the wise, phala-bhāsanam - fruit appearance
It generates immediate fruit, clear to those with intoxicated knowledge, and unclear to the middling. That fruit appearance is clear for the wise.
उत्तमानां तु तत्कालफलं च स्पष्टभासनम्‌ ।
शशशृङ्गसमं ब्रह्मन्‌ नहि तत्फलमुच्यते ॥ ३५ ॥
uttamānāṁ tu tatkāla-phalaṁ ca spaṣṭa-bhāsanam
śaśa-śṛṅga-samaṁ brahman nahi tat phalam ucyate ॥ 35 ॥

uttamānām - of the highest, tu - indeed, tatkāla - immediate, phalam - fruit, ca - and, spaṣṭa-bhāsanam - clear appearance, śaśa-śṛṅga-samam - like the horn of a hare, brahman - O Brahmin, nahi - not, tat - that, phalam - fruit, ucyate - is said
For the highest, indeed, the immediate fruit has a clear appearance. O Brahmin, that fruit is not said to be, like the horn of a hare.
अज्ञानिनां कर्मफलं पुष्टं पूर्वानुसन्धितः ।
पूर्वापरानुसन्धानात्‌ पोषितं तत्फलं तु तैः ॥ ३६ ॥
ajñānināṁ karma-phalaṁ puṣṭaṁ pūrvānusandhitaḥ
pūrvāpara-anusandhānāt poṣitaṁ tat-phalaṁ tu taiḥ ॥ 36 ॥

ajñāninām - of the ignorant, karma-phalam - fruit of action, puṣṭam - nourished, pūrva-anusandhitaḥ - based on the past, pūrva-apara-anusandhānāt - from past and future connection, poṣitam - nourished, tat - that, phalam - fruit, tu - but, taiḥ - by them
For the ignorant, the fruit of action is nourished based on the past. From past and future connection, that fruit is nourished by them.
ज्ञानिनां फलसन्धानं छिन्नमात्मानुसन्धितः ।
अतो न पुष्टं मन्दानामारब्धजनितं फलम्‌ ॥ ३७ ॥
jñānināṁ phala-sandhānaṁ chinnam ātmā-anusandhitaḥ
ataḥ na puṣṭam mandānām ārabdha-janitaṁ phalam ॥ 37 ॥

jñāninām - of the wise, phala-sandhānam - connection with fruit, chinnam - cut off, ātmā-anusandhitaḥ - connected to the self, ataḥ - therefore, na - not, puṣṭam - nourished, mandānām - of the intoxicated, ārabdha-janitam - generated by action, phalam - fruit
For the wise, the connection with fruit is cut off, once connected to the self. Therefore, the fruit generated by action is not nourished for the intoxicated.
मध्यानां ज्ञानिनां तच्च फलं मन्दसुषुप्तिषु ।
मशकादिकृतं दुःखमिव तत्‌ सूक्ष्मतां गतम्‌ ॥ ३८ ॥
madhyānāṁ jñānināṁ tac ca phalaṁ manda-suṣuptiṣu
maśaka-ādikṛtaṁ duḥkham iva tat sūkṣmatāṁ gatam ॥ 38 ॥

madhyānām - of the middling, jñāninām - of the wise, tat - that, ca - and, phalam - fruit, manda-suṣuptiṣu - in light sleep, maśaka-ādikṛtam - caused by a mosquito, duḥkham - pain, iva - like, tat - that, sūkṣmatām - subtlety, gatam - attained
For the middling wise, that fruit is like the pain caused by a mosquito in light sleep, attaining subtlety.
उत्तमज्ञानिनां तत्तु फलं पूर्णमपि स्थितम्‌ ।
दग्धरज्जुरिव भवेत्‌ स्थितात्मज्ञानवैभवात्‌ ॥ ३९ ॥
uttama-jñānināṁ tat tu phalaṁ pūrṇam api sthitam
dagdha-rajjur iva bhavet sthita-ātma-jñāna-vaibhavāt ॥ 39 ॥

uttama-jñāninām - of the highest wise, tat - that, tu - but, phalam - fruit, pūrṇam - complete, api - even, sthitam - established, dagdha-rajjuh - burnt rope, iva - like, bhavet - may be, sthita-ātma-jñāna-vaibhavāt - by the glory of established self-knowledge
For the highest wise, that fruit, even if complete, is like a burnt rope, due to the glory of established self-knowledge.
यथा नाटकवृत्तेषु नरो वेषान्तरं गतः ।
हृष्यन्‌ विषीदंश्च भूयो नान्तर्विकृतिमाप्नुयात्‌ ॥ ४० ॥
yathā nāṭaka-vṛtteṣu naro veṣāntaraṁ gataḥ
hṛṣyan viṣīdan ca bhūyo na antarvikṛtim āpnuyāt ॥ 40 ॥

yathā - as, nāṭaka-vṛtteṣu - in the course of a play, naraḥ - a man, veṣāntaram - different costumes, gataḥ - taken, hṛṣyan - rejoicing, viṣīdan - lamenting, ca - and, bhūyaḥ - again, na - not, antarvikṛtim - internal change, āpnuyāt - attains
As in the course of a play, a man taking different costumes, rejoicing and lamenting again, does not attain internal change.
एवमेष स्थितज्ञानी सुपूर्णफलसङ्गतः ।
न फलैः स्पृश्यते तस्मात्तत्फलं शशशृङ्गवत्‌ ॥ ४१ ॥
evameṣa sthita-jñānī supūrṇa-phala-saṅgataḥ
na phalaiḥ spṛśyate tasmāt tat-phalaṁ śaśa-śṛṅgavat ॥ 41 ॥

evam - thus, eṣaḥ - this, sthita-jñānī - stable in knowledge, supūrṇa-phala-saṅgataḥ - full of results, na - not, phalaiḥ - by fruits, spṛśyate - is touched, tasmāt - therefore, tat-phalam - those fruits, śaśa-śṛṅgavat - like the horn of a hare
Thus, this one stable in knowledge, full of results, is not touched by fruits. Therefore, those fruits are like the horn of a hare.
अज्ञानिभिस्तु शुद्धात्मा नोपलक्षित एव हि ।
अतो देहात्मभूतास्ते दृश्यसत्यविमर्शनाः ॥ ४२ ॥
ajñānibhiḥ tu śuddhātmā na upalakṣita eva hi
ataḥ dehātma-bhūtāḥ te dṛśya-satya-vimarśanāḥ ॥ 42 ॥

ajñānibhiḥ - by the ignorant, tu - but, śuddhātmā - pure self, na - not, upalakṣita - perceived, eva - indeed, hi - certainly, ataḥ - therefore, deha-ātma-bhūtāḥ - considering the body as the self, te - they, dṛśya-satya-vimarśanāḥ - discerning the visible as true
But by the ignorant, the pure self is not perceived. Therefore, they consider the body as the self, discerning the visible as true.
मन्दज्ञानिभिरात्मा तु विदितः शुद्धचिन्मयः ।
जगच्चासत्यतो दृष्टं तथाप्यभ्यासमान्द्यतः ॥ ४३ ॥
manda-jñānibhiḥ ātmā tu viditaḥ śuddha-cinmayaḥ
jagat ca asatyataḥ dṛṣṭaṁ tathā api abhyāsa-māndyataḥ ॥ 43 ॥

manda-jñānibhiḥ - by the intoxicated in knowledge, ātmā - the self, tu - but, viditaḥ - known, śuddha-cinmayaḥ - pure consciousness, jagat - world, ca - and, asatyataḥ - as unreal, dṛṣṭam - seen, tathā - thus, api - even, abhyāsa-māndyataḥ - due to weak practice
By the intoxicated in knowledge, the self is known as pure consciousness. The world is seen as unreal, but even thus, due to weak practice...
प्राग्वासनाहृतज्ञानास्ते देहात्मप्रभासनम्‌ ।
जगतः सत्यताभासं मध्ये मध्ये समाययुः ॥ ४४ ॥
prāg-vāsanā-hṛta-jñānās te dehātma-prabhāsanam
jagataḥ satyatā-bhāsaṁ madhye madhye samāyayuḥ ॥ 44 ॥

prāk - previous, vāsanā - impressions, hṛta - taken from, jñānāḥ - knowledge, te - they, deha-ātma-prabhāsanam - considering the body as self, jagataḥ - of the world, satyatā-bhāsam - appearance of reality, madhye madhye - in between, samāyayuḥ - come
Taken from previous impressions, their knowledge, considering the body as self, in between, come to the appearance of the world's reality.
भूयो ज्ञानवासनया विधुन्वन्त्यसतीं दृशम्‌ ।
वासनैवं सत्यमिथ्याज्ञानयोश्च परस्परम्‌ ॥ ४५ ॥
bhūyo jñāna-vāsanayā vidhunvanti asatīm dṛśam
vāsanā evam satya-mithyā-jñānayoḥ ca parasparam ॥ 45 ॥

bhūyaḥ - again, jñāna-vāsanayā - by the impression of knowledge, vidhunvanti - shake off, asatīm - unreal, dṛśam - perception, vāsanā - impression, evam - thus, satya-mithyā-jñānayoḥ - of true and false knowledge, ca - and, parasparam - mutually
Again, by the impression of knowledge, they shake off the unreal perception. Thus, mutually, the impressions of true and false knowledge...
मिलिता मन्दज्ञानिनामतो मध्ये फलं स्फुटम्‌ ।
समेऽपि वासने चैते नहि तुल्ये महीसुर ॥ ४६ ॥
miltā manda-jñāninām ataḥ madhye phalaṁ sphuṭam
same api vāsane ca ete nahi tulye mahīsura ॥ 46 ॥

miltā - combined, manda-jñāninām - of the intoxicated in knowledge, ataḥ - thus, madhye - in between, phalam - fruit, sphuṭam - clear, same - equal, api - even, vāsane - impressions, ca - and, ete - these, nahi - not, tulye - equal, mahīsura - O best of sages
Combined, of the intoxicated in knowledge, thus, in between, the fruit is clear. Even if the opposing impressions are equal, these are not equal, O best of sages.
सत्यज्ञानवासनया बाध्यते वासनाऽपरा ।
न च मिथ्यावासनया बाध्यते सत्यवासना ॥ ४७ ॥
satya-jñāna-vāsanayā bādhyate vāsanā aparā
na ca mithyā-vāsanayā bādhyate satya-vāsanā ॥ 47 ॥

satya-jñāna-vāsanayā - by the impression of true knowledge, bādhyate - is obstructed, vāsanā - impression, aparā - other, na - not, ca - and, mithyā-vāsanayā - by the impression of false knowledge, bādhyate - obstructed, satya-vāsanā - true impression
By the impression of true knowledge, the other impression is obstructed. And by the impression of false knowledge, the true impression is not obstructed.
मिथ्यावासनयाविष्टो विस्मृतः केवलां पराम्‌ ।
ततो मिथ्यावासनां तु विनिश्चित्य भ्रमात्मिकाम्‌ ॥ ४८ ॥
mithyā-vāsanayā āviṣṭo vismṛtaḥ kevalāṁ parām
tato mithyā-vāsanāṁ tu viniścitya bhrama-ātmikām ॥ 48 ॥

mithyā-vāsanayā - by the impression of false knowledge, āviṣṭaḥ - occupied, vismṛtaḥ - forgotten, kevalām - only, parām - supreme, tataḥ - then, mithyā-vāsanām - false impression, tu - but, viniścitya - deciding, bhrama-ātmikām - of delusion
Occupied by the impression of false knowledge, one has forgotten the supreme only. Then deciding that false impression as of delusion...
विधूय वासनां सत्यामुपैति ब्राह्मणोत्तम ।
ततो न बाधिता सत्यवासना भवति क्वचित्‌ ॥ ४९ ॥
vidhūya vāsanāṁ satyām upaiti brāhmaṇa-uttama
tato na bādhitā satya-vāsanā bhavati kvacit ॥ 49 ॥

vidhūya - shaking off, vāsanām - impression, satyām - true, upaiti - attains, brāhmaṇa-uttama - O best of Brahmins, tataḥ - then, na - not, bādhitā - obstructed, satya-vāsanā - true impression, bhavati - becomes, kvacit - ever
Shaking off the false impression, one attains the true. Then the true impression is not obstructed ever, O best of Brahmins.
मध्यमस्य विस्मृतिर्नो न मिथ्याज्ञानमेव च ।
अविस्मृतस्येच्छयैव मिथ्याज्ञानं क्वचिद्भवेत्‌ ॥ ५० ॥
madhyamasya vismṛtir no na mithyā-jñānam eva ca
avismṛtasya icchayā eva mithyā-jñānam kvacit bhavet ॥ 50 ॥

madhyamasya - of the middling, vismṛtiḥ - forgetfulness, no - not, na - not, mithyā-jñānam - false knowledge, eva - also, ca - and, avismṛtasya - of the non-forgetter, icchayā - by desire, eva - indeed, mithyā-jñānam - false knowledge, kvacit - sometimes, bhavet - may be
For the middling, forgetfulness is not there, nor false knowledge. For the non-forgetter, by desire, the false knowledge sometimes may arise.
सिद्धस्यैषा स्थितिः प्रोक्ता साधकस्योच्यते शृणु ।
यथा यथा तत्परः स्यात्तथाऽविस्मृतिरुच्छ्रिता ॥ ५१ ॥
siddhasya eṣā sthitiḥ proktā sādhakasya ucyate śṛṇu
yathā yathā tat-paraḥ syāt tathā avismṛtiḥ ucchritā ॥ 51 ॥

siddhasya - of the accomplished, eṣā - this, sthitiḥ - state, proktā - said, sādhakasya - of the aspirant, ucyate - is said, śṛṇu - listen, yathā yathā - as much as, tat-paraḥ - focused on that, syāt - may be, tathā - so, avismṛtiḥ - non-forgetfulness, ucchritā - elevated
This state of the accomplished is said of the aspirant, it is said, listen: as much as one is focused on that, so non-forgetfulness is elevated.
पूर्णस्य विस्मृतिर्नास्ति मिथ्याज्ञानं प्रयत्नतः ।
उत्तमस्य पुनर्ब्रह्मन्‌ समाधिव्यवहारयोः ॥ ५२ ॥
pūrṇasya vismṛtiḥ na asti mithyā-jñānam prayatnataḥ
uttamasya punaḥ brahman samādhi-vyavahārayoḥ ॥ 52 ॥

pūrṇasya - for the complete, vismṛtiḥ - forgetfulness, na - not, asti - is, mithyā-jñānam - false knowledge, prayatnataḥ - by effort, uttamasya - for the highest, punaḥ - again, brahman - O Brahmin, samādhi-vyavahārayoḥ - in samadhi and transaction
For the complete accomplished one, forgetfulness of that is not; false knowledge is removed by effort. For the highest, again, O Brahmin, either in samadhi and worldly transactions...
न भेदो लेशतोऽप्यस्ति यतोऽविस्मरणं सदा ।
यः समाधिपरो मध्यस्तस्य याऽविस्मृतिः स्थिता ॥ ५३ ॥
na bhedo leśataḥ api asti yataḥ avismaraṇaṁ sadā
yaḥ samādhi-paraḥ madhyaḥ tasya yā avismṛtiḥ sthitā ॥ 53 ॥

na - not, bhedaḥ - difference, leśataḥ - even a little, api - also, asti - is, yataḥ - where, avismaraṇam - non-forgetfulness, sadā - always, yaḥ - who, samādhi-paraḥ - focused on samadhi, madhyaḥ - middling, tasya - his, yā - which, avismṛtiḥ - non-forgetfulness, sthitā - established
There is not even a little difference where non-forgetfulness (of that state) is always. For the middling, who is focused on samadhi, his non-forgetfulness is established.
सेषन्म्लाना भवेन्मिथ्याज्ञानभूमिषु भूसुर ।
यस्तूत्तमोऽपि स्वाच्छन्द्यात्‌ प्रारब्धवशतोऽपि वा ॥ ५४ ॥
seṣan-mlānā bhavet mithyā-jñāna-bhūmiṣu bhūsura
yaḥ tu uttamaḥ api svācchandyāt prārabdha-vaśataḥ api vā ॥ 54 ॥

seṣan-mlānā - slightly faded, bhavet - may be, mithyā-jñāna-bhūmiṣu - in the ground of false knowledge, bhūsura - O best of sages, yaḥ - who, tu - but, uttamaḥ - highest, api - even, svācchandyāt - by free will, prārabdha-vaśataḥ - by destiny, api - also, vā - or
It may be slightly faded and may be situated in the ground of false knowledge, O best of sages. Even the highest, due to free will or by destiny...
समाध्यतत्परो भूयात्‌ तस्याम्लानैव चास्मृतिः ।
वस्तुतः शृणु भूदेव मध्यमोत्तमज्ञानिनाम्‌ ॥ ५५ ॥
samādhi-tat-paraḥ bhūyāt tasya amlānā eva ca asmr̥tiḥ
vastutaḥ śṛṇu bhūdeva madhyama-uttama-jñāninām ॥ 55 ॥

samādhi-tat-paraḥ - focused on samadhi, bhūyāt - may be, tasya - his, amlānā - negligent, eva - indeed, ca - and, asmr̥tiḥ - forgetfulness, vastutaḥ - actually, śṛṇu - listen, bhūdeva - O best of sages, madhyama - middling, uttama - highest, jñāninām - of the wise
Even focused on samadhi, his forgetfulness may arise if negligent indeed. Actually, listen, O best of sages, about the middling and the highest of the wise.
कर्म नैवास्ति यत्किञ्चिद्यतस्ते पुर्णतां गताः ।
संविदात्मातिरिक्तं यन्न ते पश्यन्ति किञ्चन ॥ ५६ ॥
karma naiva asti yat kiñcit yataḥ te pūrṇatāṁ gatāḥ ।
saṁvid-ātma-atiriktaṁ yat na te paśyanti kiñcana ॥ 56 ॥

karma - action, na - not, eva - indeed, asti - is, yat - what, kiñcit - anything, yataḥ - because, te - they, pūrṇatāṁ gatāḥ - have attained completeness, saṁvid-ātma-atiriktaṁ - beyond the self of consciousness, yat - which, na - not, te - they, paśyanti - see, kiñcana - anything
There is indeed no action at all because they have attained completeness. Beyond the self of consciousness, they see nothing.
कर्म शेषं कथं शिष्येद्यतः सर्वं चिदग्निना ।
भस्मीकृतमतस्तेषां न किञ्चित्‌ परिशिष्यते ॥ ५७ ॥
karma śeṣaṁ kathaṁ śiṣyed yataḥ sarvaṁ cid-agni-nā ।
bhasmī-kṛtam atas teṣāṁ na kiñcit pariśiṣyate ॥ 57 ॥

karma - action, śeṣam - residue, katham - how, śiṣyet - remains, yataḥ - because, sarvam - all, cit-agni-nā - by the fire of consciousness, bhasmī-kṛtam - turned to ashes, ataḥ - therefore, teṣām - their, na - not, kiñcit - anything, pariśiṣyate - remains
How can any residue of action remain, because all is turned to ashes by the fire of consciousness? Therefore, nothing remains of theirs.
ऐन्द्रजालिककर्मेव त्वितरैरेव दृश्यते ।
शृणु ब्रह्मन्‌ रहस्यं ते प्रवक्ष्यामि समासतः ॥ ५८ ॥
aindra-jālika-karma iva tu itaraiḥ eva dṛśyate ।
śṛṇu brahman rahasyaṁ te pravakṣyāmi samāsataḥ ॥ 58 ॥

aindra-jālika-karma - magic-like action, iva - as, tu - but, itaraiḥ - by others, eva - indeed, dṛśyate - is seen, śṛṇu - listen, brahman - O Brahmin, rahasyam - secret, te - to you, pravakṣyāmi - I will explain, samāsataḥ - briefly
Like a magic show, the actions are seen only by others. Listen, O Brahmin, I will briefly explain the secret to you.
शिवस्य यादृशी सैव ज्ञानिनां दृष्टिरुच्यते ।
नास्ति भेदो लेशतोऽपि सत्यमेतन्न संशयः ॥ ५९ ॥
śivasya yādṛśī saiva jñānināṁ dṛṣṭiḥ ucyate ।
na asti bhedaḥ leśataḥ api satyam etan na saṁśayaḥ ॥ 59 ॥

śivasya - of Shiva, yādṛśī - such as, sā - that, eva - indeed, jñāninām - of the wise, dṛṣṭiḥ - vision, ucyate - is said, na asti - there is not, bhedaḥ - difference, leśataḥ - slightest, api - even, satyam - truth, etan - this, na - not, saṁśayaḥ - doubt
The vision of the wise is said to be like that of Shiva. There is not even the slightest difference; this is the truth without a doubt.
तस्मान्न किञ्चित्‌ कर्मापि ज्ञानिनामनुवर्तते ।
इति श्रुत्वा स वसुमान्‌ हेमाङ्गदनिरूपितम्‌ ॥ ६० ॥
tasmān na kiñcit karmāpi jñāninām anuvartate ।
iti śrutvā sa vasumān hemāṅgada-nirūpitam ॥ 60 ॥

tasmāt - therefore, na - not, kiñcit - anything, karma - action, api - even, jñāninām - of the wise, anuvartate - follows, iti - thus, śrutvā - hearing, sa - he, vasumān - Vasuman, hemāṅgada-nirūpitam - explained by Hemangada
Therefore, no action follows the wise. Thus, hearing this, Vasuman, as explained by Hemangada...
सर्वसन्देहनिर्मुक्तो विज्ञानविशदाशयः ।
पूजितो राजपुत्राद्यैः स्वं स्थानं प्रत्यपद्यत ॥ ६१ ॥
sarva-sandeha-nirmukto vijñāna-viśadāśayaḥ ।
pūjito rājaputrādyaiḥ svaṁ sthānaṁ pratyapadyata ॥ 61 ॥

sarva-sandeha-nirmuktaḥ - free from all doubts, vijñāna-viśada-āśayaḥ - with a clear mind of knowledge, pūjitaḥ - honored, rājaputra-ādyaiḥ - by princes and others, svam - his, sthānam - place, pratyapadyata - returned
Free from all doubts, with a clear mind of knowledge, honored by princes and others, he returned to his place.
प्राप्तौ स्वनगरं राजपुत्रावपि ततः परम्‌ ।
एवं श्रुत्वा पुना रामः पप्रच्छात्रिसुतं मुनिम्‌ ॥ ६२ ॥
prāptau sva-nagaraṁ rājaputrāv api tataḥ param ।
evaṁ śrutvā punā rāmaḥ papraccha atri-sutaṁ munim ॥ 62 ॥

prāptau - having reached, sva-nagaram - their city, rājaputrāv - the two princes, api - also, tataḥ - then, param - further, evam - thus, śrutvā - hearing, punāḥ - again, rāmaḥ - Rama, papraccha - asked, atri-sutam - Atri's son, munim - sage
Having reached their city, the two princes also then lived further, thus hearing, Rama again asked the sage, Atri's son.
श्रुतमेतद्धि विज्ञानं गुरो त्वन्मुखनिर्गतम्‌ ।
विनष्टो मम सन्देहो विदितं तन्महत्पदम्‌ ॥ ६३ ॥
śrutam etad dhi vijñānaṁ guro tvan-mukha-nirgatam ।
vinaṣṭo mama sandehaḥ viditaṁ tan mahat-padam ॥ 63 ॥

śrutam - heard, etat - this, hi - indeed, vijñānam - knowledge, guro - O guru, tvan-mukha-nirgatam - emanating from your mouth, vinaṣṭaḥ - destroyed, mama - my, sandehaḥ - doubt, viditam - known, tat - that, mahat-padam - great state
This knowledge indeed heard, O guru, emanating from your mouth, has destroyed my doubt and made known that great state.
सर्वानुस्यूतसंवित्तिमात्रात्मा भाति सर्वत: ।
तथापि भवता प्रोक्तमादितः सर्वमेव तु ॥ ६४ ॥
sarva-anusyūta-saṁvitti-mātra-ātmā bhāti sarvataḥ ।
tathāpi bhavatā proktam āditaḥ sarvam eva tu ॥ 64 ॥

sarva - all, anusyūta - pervaded, saṁvitti - consciousness, mātra - only, ātmā - self, bhāti - shines, sarvataḥ - everywhere, tathāpi - even so, bhavatā - by you, proktam - said, āditaḥ - from the beginning, sarvam - all, eva - indeed, tu - but
The self, pervaded by consciousness, shines everywhere. Even so, all was said by you from the beginning.
संक्षेपेण पुनर्ब्रूहि विज्ञानं सारवत्तरम्‌ ।
यावद्धारयितव्यं मे गुरो सर्वात्मना मया ॥ ६५ ॥
saṁkṣepeṇa punar brūhi vijñānaṁ sāra-vattaram ।
yāvat dhārayitavyaṁ me guro sarva-ātmanā mayā ॥ 65 ॥

saṁkṣepeṇa - briefly, punaḥ - again, brūhi - tell, vijñānam - knowledge, sāra-vattaram - most essential, yāvat - as long as, dhārayitavyam - to be retained, me - by me, guro - O guru, sarva-ātmanā - with all my heart, mayā - by me
Briefly, again, tell the most essential knowledge, as long as it is to be retained by me, O guru, with all my heart.
इत्यापृष्टः स रामेण पुनः प्राहात्रिनन्दनः ।
शृणु राम प्रवक्ष्यामि सर्वसारतमं पुनः ॥ ६६ ॥
ityā-pṛṣṭaḥ sa rāmeṇa punaḥ prāha atri-nandanaḥ ।
śṛṇu rāma pravakṣyāmi sarva-sāratamaṁ punaḥ ॥ 66 ॥

iti - thus, āpṛṣṭaḥ - asked, saḥ - he, rāmeṇa - by Rama, punaḥ - again, prāha - said, atri-nandanaḥ - Atri's son, śṛṇu - listen, rāma - O Rama, pravakṣyāmi - I will explain, sarva-sāratamam - most essential, punaḥ - again
Thus asked by Rama, again, Atri's son said, "Listen, O Rama, I will explain the most essential again."
या चितिः परमेशानी पूर्णाहन्तामयी परा ।
सा स्वातन्त्र्याभिधमायाशक्तिमाहात्म्यतः सदा ॥ ६७ ॥
yā citiḥ parameśānī pūrṇā-ahantāmayī parā ।
sā svātantrya-abhidhamāyā-śakti-mahātmyataḥ sadā ॥ 67 ॥

yā - which, citiḥ - consciousness, parameśānī - supreme goddess, pūrṇā - complete, ahantāmayī - filled with the sense of 'I', parā - supreme, sā - that, svātantrya - freedom, abhidhamāyā - known as māyā, śakti - power, mahātmyataḥ - from greatness, sadā - always
Which consciousness, the supreme goddess, complete, filled with the sense of 'I', that supreme, always known as the māyā power, from her greatness...
जगदाभासयेद्‌ नूनं दुर्घटैकविधायिनः ।
प्रतिबिम्बवदादर्शे तत्प्रकारं शृणु क्रमात्‌ ॥ ६८ ॥
jagadābhāsayed nūnaṁ durghaṭaika-vidhāyinaḥ ।
pratibimba-vat-ādarśe tat-prakāraṁ śṛṇu kramāt ॥ 68 ॥

jagat - world, ābhāsayet - manifests, nūnam - indeed, durghaṭa - difficult, eka-vidhāyinaḥ - unique creator, pratibimba-vat - like a reflection, ādarśe - in a mirror, tat-prakāram - that method, śṛṇu - listen, kramāt - in order
The world indeed manifests from the unique creator. Like a reflection in a mirror, listen to that method in order.
या सा परा चितिः पूर्णा पूर्णाहंभावबृंहिता ।
स्वातन्त्र्यवशतः स्वात्मरूपं द्वेधाऽवभासयत्‌ ॥ ६९ ॥
yā sā parā citiḥ pūrṇā pūrṇa-ahaṁbhāva-bṛṁhitā ।
svātantrya-vaśataḥ sva-ātma-rūpaṁ dvedhā avabhāsayat ॥ 69 ॥

yā - which, sā - that, parā - supreme, citiḥ - consciousness, pūrṇā - complete, pūrṇa-ahaṁbhāva-bṛṁhitā - expanded with complete sense of 'I', svātantrya-vaśataḥ - by the power of freedom, sva-ātma-rūpam - own form, dvedhā - in two ways, avabhāsayat - shines
That supreme consciousness, complete, expanded with the complete sense of 'I', by the power of freedom, shines in its own form in two ways.
तत्रैकांशेऽप्यहंभावोऽपूर्ण आभासितो यदा ।
तदा द्वितीयभागस्तदहंभावविनिर्गतः ॥ ७० ॥
tatra eka-aṁśe api ahaṁbhāvaḥ apūrṇa ābhāsitaḥ yadā ।
tadā dvitīya-bhāgaḥ tad-ahaṁbhāva-vinirgataḥ ॥ 70 ॥

tatra - there, eka-aṁśe - in one part, api - even, ahaṁbhāvaḥ - sense of 'I', apūrṇa - incomplete, ābhāsitaḥ - manifested, yadā - when, tadā - then, dvitīya-bhāgaḥ - second part, tad-ahaṁbhāva-vinirgataḥ - separated from that sense of 'I'
There, even in one part, when the sense of 'I' is manifested incompletely, then the second part is separated from that sense of 'I'.
बाह्यमव्यक्तमभवत्‌ तद्दृष्ट्यैव भृगूद्वह ।
अपूर्णाहंभावयुत एष प्रोक्तः सदाशिवः ॥ ७१ ॥
bāhyam avyaktaṁ abhavat tat-dṛṣṭyā eva bhṛgūdvaha ।
apūrṇa-ahaṁbhāva-yuta eṣaḥ proktaḥ sadāśivaḥ ॥ 71 ॥

bāhyam - external, avyaktaṁ - unmanifest, abhavat - became, tat-dṛṣṭyā - by that view, eva - indeed, bhṛgūdvaha - O descendant of Bhrigu, apūrṇa-ahaṁbhāva-yuta - associated with incomplete sense of 'I', eṣaḥ - this, proktaḥ - is said, sadāśivaḥ - Sadashiva
That view became the external unmanifest, indeed, O descendant of Bhrigu. But the one associated with incomplete sense of 'I', this is said to be Sadashiva.
स तमव्यक्तभागं तु पश्यन्‌ भिन्नमपि स्वतः ।
अहमेतदित्यभेदाद्‌ अनुसन्धिपरः सदा ॥ ७२ ॥
sa tam avyakta-bhāgaṁ tu paśyan bhinnam api svataḥ ।
aham etad iti abhedāt anusandhi-paraḥ sadā ॥ 72 ॥

sa - he, tam - that, avyakta-bhāgam - unmanifest part, tu - but, paśyan - seeing, bhinnam - different, api - even, svataḥ - from himself, aham etad - I am this, iti - thus, abhedāt - from non-difference, anusandhi-paraḥ - intent on contemplating, sadā - always
He, seeing that unmanifest part as different even from himself, "I am this," thus always knowing by intent on contemplating with non-difference.
स एव भूयः स्वातन्त्र्यात्‌ सिसृक्षुर्विविधं जगत्‌ ।
अव्यक्तमात्मनो देहमेतदेवाहमास्थितः ॥ ७३ ॥
sa eva bhūyaḥ svātantryāt sisṛkṣur vividhaṁ jagat ।
avyaktaṁ ātmanaḥ deham etad eva aham āsthitaḥ ॥ 73 ॥

saḥ - he, eva - indeed, bhūyaḥ - again, svātantryāt - by freedom, sisṛkṣuḥ - desiring to create, vividham - various, jagat - world, avyaktaṁ - unmanifest, ātmanaḥ - of the self, deham - body, etat - this, eva - indeed, aham - I, āsthitaḥ - occupied
He indeed, again, by freedom, desiring to create the various worlds, occupied the unmanifest body of the self as "I".
इत्येवमनुसन्धानपर ईश्वर आबभौ ।
अव्यक्तमभिमानेनाविष्ट ईश्वर एव तु ॥ ७४ ॥
iti evam anusandhāna-para īśvara ābabhau ।
avyaktam abhimanena āviṣṭa īśvara eva tu ॥ 74 ॥

iti - thus, evam - so, anusandhāna-para - intent on contemplating, īśvaraḥ - the lord, ābabhau - manifested, avyaktaṁ - unmanifest, abhimanena - with identification, āviṣṭaḥ - occupied, īśvaraḥ - the lord, eva - indeed, tu - but
Thus, so intent on contemplating, the lord manifested. Occupied the unmanifest identification, indeed the lord.
त्रिधा समभवद्‌ रूद्रहरिद्रुहिणरूपतः ।
द्रष्टृदृश्यमहाराशिसमुदायावभासकाः ॥ ७५ ॥
tridhā samabhavad rūdra-hari-druhiṇa-rūpataḥ ।
draṣṭṛ-dṛśya-mahā-rāśi-samudāya-avabhāsakāḥ ॥ 75 ॥

tridhā - threefold, samabhavat - became, rūdra-hari-druhiṇa-rūpataḥ - in the forms of Rudra, Hari, and Brahma, draṣṭṛ-dṛśya-mahā-rāśi - vast seer and seen, samudāya - aggregation, avabhāsakāḥ - manifesting
He became threefold, in the forms of Rudra, Hari, and Brahma, manifesting the vast aggregation of the seer and the seen.
विधयो विविधा आसंस्तथा तद्रूपसंस्थिताः ।
बहवो हरयोऽप्यासंस्तत्संहारपरायणाः ॥ ७६ ॥
vidhayo vividhā āsan tathā tat-rūpa-saṁsthitāḥ ।
bahavo harayo api āsan tat-saṁhāra-parāyaṇāḥ ॥ 76 ॥

vidhayaḥ - forms, vividhā - various, āsan - became, tathā - so, tat-rūpa-saṁsthitāḥ - established in those forms, bahavaḥ - many, harayaḥ - Hari (forms of Vishnu), api - also, āsan - became, tat-saṁhāra-parāyaṇāḥ - intent on destruction
Various forms became established in those forms. Many forms of Hari also became intent on destruction.
अनेकशोऽभवन्‌ रुद्रा एवमेष जगद्विधिः ।
एवंविधं जगत्तत्त्वं दर्पणप्रतिबिम्बवत्‌ ॥ ७७ ॥
anekaśo'bhavan rudrā evam eṣa jagad-vidhiḥ ।
evaṁ-vidhaṁ jagat-tattvaṁ darpaṇa-pratibimba-vat ॥ 77 ॥

anekaśaḥ - numerous, abhavan - became, rudrāḥ - forms of Rudra, evam - thus, eṣa - this, jagat-vidhiḥ - world order, evaṁ-vidham - thus, jagat-tattvam - world essence, darpaṇa-pratibimba-vat - like the reflection in a mirror
Numerous forms of Rudra thus became. This world order, thus, the world essence, is like the reflection in a mirror.
भासते केवलं राम नहि जातं तु किञ्चन ।
परा चितिः प्रपूर्णाहंभावरूपैव सर्वदा ॥ ७८ ॥
bhāsate kevalaṁ rāma nahi jātaṁ tu kiñcana ।
parā citiḥ prapūrṇa-ahaṁ-bhāva-rūpa eva sarvadā ॥ 78 ॥

bhāsate - shines, kevalam - only, rāma - O Rama, nahi - not, jātaṁ - born, tu - but, kiñcana - anything, parā - supreme, citiḥ - consciousness, prapūrṇa-ahaṁ-bhāva-rūpā - in the form of complete 'I', eva - indeed, sarvadā - always
It shines only, O Rama, not anything born/appears. The supreme consciousness, indeed always in the form of complete 'I'.
स्थिताप्यनेका सम्पूर्णाहंभावपरिबृहिता ।
यथा त्वं राम सर्वस्मिन्‌ देहेऽहंभावबृहितः ॥ ७९ ॥
sthitā api anekā sampūrṇa-ahaṁ-bhāva-paribṛhitā ।
yathā tvaṁ rāma sarvasmin dehe ahaṁ-bhāva-bṛhitaḥ ॥ 79 ॥

sthitā - established, api - also, anekā - numerous, sampūrṇa-ahaṁ-bhāva-paribṛhitā - enveloped in the complete sense of 'I', yathā - as, tvam - you, rāma - O Rama, sarvasmin - in all, dehe - bodies, ahaṁ-bhāva-bṛhitaḥ - filled with the sense of 'I'
Established, also numerous, enveloped in the complete sense of 'I'. As you, O Rama, filled with the sense of 'I' in all bodies.
पृथग्‌ नेत्राद्यहंभावैरपि तत्तत्क्रियापरः ।
एवमेव परा संवित्‌ पूर्णाहन्तासमाश्रया ॥ ८० ॥
pṛthak netra-ādya-ahaṁ-bhāvaiḥ api tat-tat-kriyā-paraḥ ।
evam eva parā saṁvit pūrṇa-ahantā-samāśrayā ॥ 80 ॥

pṛthak - different, netra-ādya - eyes, etc., ahaṁ-bhāvaiḥ - senses of 'I', api - also, tat-tat - various, kriyā-paraḥ - engaged in actions, evam - thus, eva - indeed, parā - supreme, saṁvit - consciousness, pūrṇa-ahantā-samāśrayā - resting in complete 'I'
Different eyes and other senses of 'I', also engaged in various actions. Thus indeed, the supreme consciousness rests in the complete 'I', everywhere.
सदाशिवादिस्तम्बान्ताऽपूर्णाहन्ताश्रयापि वै ।
वस्तुतः सैव परमा चितिरेवं हि भासिनी ॥ ८१ ॥
sadāśiva-ādi-stamba-antā-apūrṇa-ahantā-āśrayā api vai ।
vastutaḥ sā eva paramā citiḥ evam hi bhāsinī ॥ 81 ॥

sadāśiva-ādi - from Sadashiva onwards, stamba-antā - to a blade of grass, apūrṇa-ahantā-āśrayā - resting in incomplete sense of 'I', api - also, vai - indeed, vastutaḥ - truly, sā - she, eva - indeed, paramā - supreme, citiḥ - consciousness, evam - thus, hi - indeed, bhāsinī - shining
From Sadashiva onwards to a blade of grass, even resting in the incomplete sense of 'I', truly, she indeed is the supreme consciousness, shining thus.
देहाहंभावरूपस्त्वं स्वतो रूपरसादिकम्‌ ।
ग्रहीतुमसमर्थोऽपि चाक्षतादात्म्यमेत्य तु ॥ ८२ ॥
deha-ahaṁbhāva-rūpas tvaṁ svato rūpa-rasa-adikam ।
grahītum-asamarthaḥ api ca-akṣata-ādātmyam-etya tu ॥ 82 ॥

deha-ahaṁbhāva-rūpaḥ - form of bodily 'I', tvam - you, svato - by yourself, rūpa-rasa-adikam - form, taste, etc., grahītum - to grasp, asamarthaḥ - incapable, api - even, ca - and, akṣata-ādātmyam - identity with consciousness, etya - attaining, tu - but
The form of bodily 'I', you, by yourself, are incapable of grasping form, taste, etc., but it is by attaining identity with consciousness.
सर्वं गृह्णासि सततमेवं देवः सदाशिवः ।
स्वतः सर्वाभेदमयो ब्रह्मादिस्तम्बराशिषु ॥ ८३ ॥
sarvaṁ gṛhṇāsi satatam evam devaḥ sadāśivaḥ ।
svataḥ sarva-abhedamayo brahma-ādi-stamba-rāśiṣu ॥ 83 ॥

sarvam - everything, gṛhṇāsi - you grasp, satatam - always, evam - thus, devaḥ - lord, sadāśivaḥ - Sadashiva, svataḥ - by yourself, sarva-abhedamayaḥ - full of non-difference with everything, brahma-ādi - from Brahma onwards, stamba-rāśiṣu - to a blade of grass
You grasp everything always, thus, O lord Sadashiva, by yourself, full of non-difference with everything, from Brahma to a blade of grass.
अन्तस्तादात्म्यमापन्नो जानाति च करोति च ।
यथा ते निर्विकल्पं तु रूपं सर्वाश्रयं हि सत्‌ ॥ ८४ ॥
antastādātmyam āpanno jānāti ca karoti ca ।
yathā te nirvikalpaṁ tu rūpaṁ sarvāśrayaṁ hi sat ॥ 84 ॥

antas - within, tādātmyam - identity, āpannaḥ - attaining, jānāti - knows, ca - and, karoti - does, ca - and, yathā - as, te - your, nirvikalpam - without difference, tu - but, rūpam - form, sarva-āśrayam - basis of all, hi - indeed, sat - being
Attaining identity within, he knows and does. Just as your form, indeed, is without difference, the basis of all being.
न किञ्चिदपि जानाति करोति च भृगूद्वह ।
एवमेव परा संवित्‌ सर्वलोकसमाश्रया ॥ ८५ ॥
na kiñcid api jānāti karoti ca bhṛgūdvaha ।
evam eva parā saṁvit sarva-loka-samāśrayā ॥ 85 ॥

na - not, kiñcit - anything, api - even, jānāti - knows, karoti - does, ca - and, bhṛgūdvaha - O descendant of Bhrigu, evam - thus, eva - indeed, parā - supreme, saṁvit - consciousness, sarva-loka-samāśrayā - basis of all worlds
But also, does not know or do anything, O descendant of Bhrigu, thus indeed, the supreme consciousness is the basis of all worlds.
भेदलेशमपि क्वापि न जानाति करोति च ।
एतावज्जागतं सर्वं तस्यामेवावभासते ॥ ८६ ॥
bhedaleśam api kvāpi na jānāti karoti ca ।
etāvat-jāgataṁ sarvaṁ tasyām evāvabhāsate ॥ 86 ॥

bheda-leśam - slightest difference, api - even, kvāpi - anywhere, na - not, jānāti - knows, karoti - does, ca - and, etāvat - thus, jāgatam - world, sarvam - all, tasyām - in her, eva - indeed, avabhāsate - shines
Not knowing or doing even the slightest difference anywhere, thus, all the world shines in her indeed.
तत्स्वातन्त्र्यात्‌ प्रभूतं च दर्पणप्रतिबिम्बवत्‌ ।
जगतो भासनं सर्वं तस्या एवावभासनम्‌ ॥ ८७ ॥
tat-svātantryāt prabhūtaṁ ca darpaṇa-pratibimba-vat ।
jagato bhāsanaṁ sarvaṁ tasyā eva avabhāsanam ॥ 87 ॥

tat-svātantryāt - by her freedom, prabhūtam - manifested, ca - and, darpaṇa-pratibimba-vat - like a mirror reflection, jagataḥ - of the world, bhāsanam - shining, sarvam - all, tasyāḥ - her, eva - indeed, avabhāsanam - reflection
By her freedom, manifested and like a mirror reflection, the shining of the world, all, indeed, is her reflection.
यथादर्शाभास एव प्रतिबिम्बावभासनम्‌ ।
अत्र त्वमहमन्ये च द्रष्टारो दृङ्मयाः खलु ॥ ८८ ॥
yathā ādarśa-ābhāsa eva pratibimba-avabhāsanam ।
atra tvam-aham-anyāḥ ca draṣṭāraḥ dṛṅ-mayāḥ khalu ॥ 88 ॥

yathā - like, ādarśa-ābhāsa - mirror reflection, eva - indeed, pratibimba-avabhāsanam - reflection, atra - here, tvam - you, aham - I, anye - others, ca - and, draṣṭāraḥ - seers, dṛṅ-mayāḥ - consisting of reflections, khalu - indeed
Like a mirror reflection, indeed, here you, I, and others, the seers, are indeed consisting of reflection.
दृश्यासंमेलने शुद्धचितिरेव न चेतरत्‌ ।
घटादिदर्पणो यद्वद् घटादीनामसङ्गमे ॥ ८९ ॥
dṛśya-asaṁmelane śuddha-citiḥ eva na ca itarat ।
ghaṭādi-darpaṇaḥ yadvat ghaṭādīnām asaṅgame ॥ 89 ॥

dṛśya-asaṁmelane - in the meeting of the seen, śuddha-citiḥ - pure consciousness, eva - indeed, na - not, ca - and, itarat - otherwise, ghaṭa-ādi - pot and others, darpaṇaḥ - mirror, yadvat - like, ghaṭādīnām - of the pots, asaṅgame - non-connection
In the meeting of the seen objects, pure consciousness is indeed, otherwise not affected. Like the non-connection of the mirror, with pots and others.
शुद्धदर्पणमात्रः स्याद्विभेदः प्रतिबिम्बतः ।
एवं विकल्पसम्भूतदृश्याभासप्रमार्जने ॥ ९० ॥
śuddha-darpaṇa-mātraḥ syād vibhedaḥ pratibimbataḥ ।
evaṁ vikalpa-sambhūta-dṛśya-ābhāsa-pramārjane ॥ 90 ॥

śuddha-darpaṇa-mātraḥ - mere pure mirror, syāt - may be, vibhedaḥ - distinction, pratibimbataḥ - by reflection, evaṁ - thus, vikalpa-sambhūta - arising from imagination, dṛśya-ābhāsa - appearance of the seen, pramārjane - in erasing
Just as pure mirror, may be the mere distinction is of reflections. Thus, in erasing the appearance of the seen arising from imagination...
शेषिता परमा संविदद्वितीयस्वरूपिणी ।
महानन्दघना चैषा दुःखलेशविवर्जनात्‌ ॥ ९१ ॥
śeṣitā paramā saṁvid advitīya-svarūpiṇī ।
mahānanda-ghanā ca eṣā duḥkha-leśa-vivarjanāt ॥ 91 ॥

śeṣitā - remaining, paramā - supreme, saṁvid - consciousness, advitīya-svarūpiṇī - with a non-dual nature, mahānanda-ghanā - full of great bliss, ca - and, eṣā - this, duḥkha-leśa-vivarjanāt - from the absence of the slightest sorrow
Remaining as supreme consciousness with a non-dual nature, full of great bliss, and from the absence of the slightest sorrow.
सर्वानन्दघनाकारा यतः सर्वैरभीप्सिता ।
सुखमात्मस्वरूपं स्यात्‌ सर्वैर्यस्मादभीप्सितम्‌ ॥ ९२ ॥
sarva-ānanda-ghana-ākārā yataḥ sarvaiḥ abhīpsitā ।
sukham ātma-svarūpaṁ syāt sarvaiḥ yasmāt abhīpsitam ॥ 92 ॥

sarva-ānanda-ghana-ākārā - form of all condensed bliss, yataḥ - because, sarvaiḥ - by all, abhīpsitā - desired, sukham - happiness, ātma-svarūpam - self-nature, syāt - may be, sarvaiḥ - by all, yasmāt - because, abhīpsitam - desired
Because it is the form of all condensed bliss and is desired by all, happiness may be the self-nature, because it is desired by all.
यदर्थो देहादिभावो यन्न कस्यापि नेप्सितम्‌ ।
यस्यैव लेशो विषयानन्द इत्यभिधीयते ॥ ९३ ॥
yad-arthaḥ deha-ādi-bhāvaḥ yat na kasyāpi nepsitam ।
yasya eva leśaḥ viṣayānandaḥ iti abhidhīyate ॥ 93 ॥

yat-arthaḥ - for the sake of which, deha-ādi-bhāvaḥ - bodily existence, yat - which, na - not, kasyāpi - by anyone, nepsitam - desired, yasya - whose, eva - indeed, leśaḥ - a trace, viṣayānandaḥ - pleasure from objects, iti - thus, abhidhīyate - is called
For the sake of which bodily existence, which is not desired by anyone, a trace of whose existence is indeed called pleasure from objects.
स एव भारहानादौ सुषुप्तौ चावभासते ।
चिदेव स्पृहणीयत्वादानन्द इति प्रोच्यते ॥ ९४ ॥
sa eva bhāra-hānādau suṣuptau ca avabhāsate ।
cit eva spṛhaṇīyatvāt ānanda iti procyate ॥ 94 ॥

saḥ - that, eva - indeed, bhāra-hāna-ādau - in the loss of burden, suṣuptau - in deep sleep, ca - and, avabhāsate - shines, cit - consciousness, eva - indeed, spṛhaṇīyatvāt - from desirability, ānandaḥ - bliss, iti - thus, procyate - is called
That (supreme consciousness) indeed shines in the loss of burden and in deep sleep. Consciousness indeed is called bliss from desirability.
मूढा नहि विजानन्ति स्वात्मभूतं महासुखम्‌ ।
विभिन्नमभिजानन्ति व्यञ्जकानां विभेदतः ॥ ९५ ॥
mūḍhā na hi vijānanti svātma-bhūtaṁ mahā-sukham ।
vibhinnam abhijānanti vyañjakānāṁ vibhedataḥ ॥ 95 ॥

mūḍhāḥ - the deluded, na - not, hi - indeed, vijānanti - know, svātma-bhūtam - self-nature, mahā-sukham - great bliss, vibhinnam - different, abhijānanti - perceive, vyañjakānām - of the expressions, vibhedataḥ - by difference
The deluded do not know the self-nature of great bliss. They perceive differences by the difference of expressions.
यथा हि दर्पणे भावा भासमाना निमित्ततः ।
यावद्दर्पणविज्ञानं भिन्ना एव विभान्ति वै ॥ ९६ ॥
yathā hi darpaṇe bhāvā bhāsamānā nimittataḥ ।
yāvat darpaṇa-vijñānaṁ bhinnā eva vibhānti vai ॥ 96 ॥

yathā - as, hi - indeed, darpaṇe - in the mirror, bhāvāḥ - objects, bhāsamānāḥ - appearing, nimittataḥ - by cause, yāvat - as long as, darpaṇa-vijñānam - knowledge of the mirror, bhinnāḥ - different, eva - indeed, vibhānti - shine, vai - indeed
As indeed, objects appearing in the mirror, their cause, as long as the knowledge of the mirror is there, it indeed shines as different.
विदिते प्रतिबिम्बत्वे भासमानं च पुर्ववत्‌ ।
न दर्पणाद्‌ भिन्नमस्ति त्वादर्शः शुद्ध एव हि ॥ ९७ ॥
vidite pratibimbatve bhāsamānaṁ ca purva-vat ।
na darpaṇāt bhinnam asti tu ādarśaḥ śuddha eva hi ॥ 97 ॥

vidite - when known, pratibimbatve - as reflection, bhāsamānam - appearing, ca - and, purva-vat - as before, na - not, darpaṇāt - from the mirror, bhinnam - different, asti - is, tu - but, ādarśaḥ - mirror, śuddhaḥ - pure, eva - indeed, hi - certainly
When known as reflection, though appearing as before, is not considered different from the mirror, the mirror is indeed pure.
एव विदिततत्त्वस्य जगदेतावदीदृशम्‌ ।
भासमानमपि स्वात्ममात्रमेव न चेतरत्‌ ॥ ९८ ॥
eva vidita-tattvasya jagat etāvat īdṛśam ।
bhāsamānam api svātma-mātram eva na ca itarat ॥ 98 ॥

eva - thus, vidita-tattvasya - to the one who knows the truth, jagat - world, etāvat - so much, īdṛśam - like this, bhāsamānam - appearing, api - even, svātma-mātram - only the self, eva - indeed, na - not, ca - and, itarat - otherwise
Thus, to the one who knows the truth, the world appears like this, everything is only the self, indeed, not otherwise.
घटादिकं मृदि यथा हेम्नि यद्वद्विभूषणम्‌ ।
प्रतिमाश्च यथा शैले जगदेवं चिदात्मनि ॥ ९९ ॥
ghaṭādikaṁ mṛdi yathā hemni yadvat vibhūṣaṇam ।
pratimāś ca yathā śaile jagat evaṁ cid-ātmani ॥ 99 ॥

ghaṭādikam - pots and others, mṛdi - in clay, yathā - as, hemni - in gold, yadvat - just as, vibhūṣaṇam - ornament, pratimāḥ - images, ca - and, yathā - as, śaile - in stone, jagat - world, evam - thus, cit-ātmani - in the self of consciousness
As pots and others in clay, just as ornaments in gold, and images in stone, thus the world is in the self of consciousness.
जगन्नास्त्येवेति दृष्टिरपूर्णैव भृगूद्वह ।
नास्तीति विपरीतो हि निश्चयो नैव सिद्धयति ॥ १०० ॥
jagan na asti eva iti dṛṣṭiḥ apūrṇā eva bhṛgūdvaha ।
na asti iti viparītaḥ hi niścayaḥ na eva siddhayati ॥ 100 ॥

jagat - world, na - not, asti - is, eva - indeed, iti - thus, dṛṣṭiḥ - vision, apūrṇā - incomplete, eva - indeed, bhṛgūdvaha - O descendant of Bhrigu, na - not, asti - is, iti - thus, viparītaḥ - opposite, hi - indeed, niścayaḥ - determination, na - not, eva - indeed, siddhayati - accomplishes
The vision that the world does not exist indeed is incomplete, O descendant of Bhrigu. The determination, indeed, the opposite of it does not exist, does not accomplish too.
साधकात्मजगद्‌दृष्टेर्भूयः सम्भवतः स्फुटम्‌ ।
नास्तीति शापमात्रेण कथं स्याज्जगतो लयः ॥ १०१ ॥
sādhaka-ātma-jagad-dṛṣṭeḥ bhūyaḥ sambhavataḥ sphuṭam ।
na asti iti śāpa-mātreṇa kathaṁ syāt jagataḥ layaḥ ॥ 101 ॥

sādhaka-ātma-jagad-dṛṣṭeḥ - from the perception of the aspirant, bhūyaḥ - again, sambhavataḥ - arising, sphuṭam - clearly, na asti - not is, iti - thus, śāpa-mātreṇa - by mere curse, katham - how, syāt - can be, jagataḥ - of the world, layaḥ - dissolution
From the perception of the aspirant, the world clearly arising again, how can the world be dissolved by mere curse, saying it does not exist?
आदर्शनगरं सर्वमस्त्यादर्शस्वभावतः ।
एवं जगच्चिदात्मैकरूपं सत्यमुदीरितम्‌ ॥ १०२ ॥
ādarśa-nagaraṁ sarvam asti ādarśa-svabhāvataḥ ।
evaṁ jagat cid-ātma-eka-rūpaṁ satyam udīritam ॥ 102 ॥

ādarśa-nagaram - city of reflections, sarvam - all, asti - is, ādarśa-svabhāvataḥ - by the nature of a mirror, evaṁ - thus, jagat - world, cid-ātma - consciousness-self, eka-rūpam - one form, satyam - truth, udīritam - declared
All is like a city of reflections, existing by the nature of a mirror. Thus, the world is declared to be one form with the consciousness-self, the truth.
पूर्णविज्ञानमेतत्‌ स्यात्‌ सङ्कोचपरिवर्जनात्‌ ।
दृगेव दृश्यतां प्राप्तं स्वमाहात्म्यप्रकर्षतः ॥ १०३ ॥
pūrṇa-vijñānam etat syāt saṅkoca-parivarjanāt ।
dṛk-eva dṛśyatāṁ prāptaṁ sva-māhātmya-prakarṣataḥ ॥ 103 ॥

pūrṇa-vijñānam - complete knowledge, etat - this, syāt - may be, saṅkoca-parivarjanāt - by elimination of contraction, dṛk-eva - seer itself, dṛśyatām - seen, prāptam - attained, sva-māhātmya-prakarṣataḥ - by the greatness of its own glory
This may be complete knowledge by eliminating contraction. This seer itself, attained seen (seeing seer-seen separately), by the greatness of its own glory.
यथादर्शो नगरतामेष शास्त्रार्थसंग्रहः ।
न बन्धोऽस्ति न मोक्षोऽस्ति साधकः साधनं च न ॥ १०४ ॥
yathā-ādārśaḥ nagaratām-eṣa śāstra-artha-saṁgrahaḥ ।
na bandhaḥ asti na mokṣaḥ asti sādhakaḥ sādhanam ca na ॥ 104 ॥

yathā - as, ādārśaḥ - mirror, nagaratām - city-like, eṣa - this, śāstra-artha-saṁgrahaḥ - essence of scripture, na - not, bandhaḥ - bondage, asti - is, na - not, mokṣaḥ - liberation, asti - is, sādhakaḥ - aspirant, sādhanam - means, ca - and, na - not
As the mirror has the reflection of a city, this is the essence of scripture. There is no bondage, no liberation, no aspirant, and no means.
अखण्डाद्वयचिच्छक्तिस्त्रिपुरैवावभासिनी ।
सैवाविद्या च विद्या च बन्धो मोक्षश्च साधनम्‌ ॥ १०५ ॥
akhaṇḍa-advaya-cit-śaktiḥ tripurā eva avabhāsinī ।
sā eva avidyā ca vidyā ca bandhaḥ mokṣaḥ ca sādhanam ॥ 105 ॥

akhaṇḍa-advaya-cit-śaktiḥ - unbroken non-dual consciousness power, tripurā - Tripura, eva - indeed, avabhāsinī - shining, sā - she, eva - indeed, avidyā - ignorance, ca - and, vidyā - knowledge, ca - and, bandhaḥ - bondage, mokṣaḥ - liberation, ca - and, sādhanam - means
The unbroken non-dual consciousness power, Tripura, indeed, shining, she indeed is ignorance and knowledge, bondage and liberation, and the means.
एतावदेव विज्ञेयं नान्यद्‌ भार्गव विद्यते ।
एतत्तेऽभिहितं राम विज्ञानक्रममादितः ॥ १०६ ॥
etāvad-eva vijñeyam nānyad bhārgava vidyate ।
etat te abhihitam rāma vijñāna-kramam āditaḥ ॥ 106 ॥

etāvat - this much, eva - indeed, vijñeyam - to be known, na - not, anyat - other, bhārgava - O descendant of Bhrigu, vidyate - exists, etat - this, te - to you, abhihitam - has been told, rāma - O Rama, vijñāna-kramam - the process of knowledge, āditaḥ - from the beginning
This much indeed is to be known; nothing else exists, O descendant of Bhrigu. This has been told to you, O Rama, the process of knowledge from the beginning.
एतत्‌ सुविज्ञाय जनो भूयः क्वापि न शोचति ।
नारदैष ज्ञानखण्डः सूपपत्त्युपलब्धिकः ॥ १०७ ॥
etat su-vijñāya janaḥ bhūyaḥ kvāpi na śocati ।
nārada eṣa jñāna-khaṇḍaḥ su-upapatti-upalabdhikaḥ ॥ 107 ॥

etat - this, su-vijñāya - knowing well, janaḥ - a person, bhūyaḥ - further, kvāpi - anywhere, na - not, śocati - grieves, nārada - O Narada, eṣaḥ - this, jñāna-khaṇḍaḥ - piece of knowledge, su-upapatti-upalabdhikaḥ - obtained by proper reasoning
Knowing this well, a person further does not grieve anywhere. O Narada, this piece of knowledge is obtained by proper reasoning.
श्रुतो न नाशयेत्‌ कस्य मोहमज्ञान सम्भवम्‌ ।
श्रुत्वाप्येतद्‌ यस्य मोहो न शान्तिं प्राप्नुयात्‌ क्वचित्‌ ॥ १०८ ॥
śrutaḥ na nāśayet kasya moham ajñāna-sambhavam ।
śrutvā api etat yasya mohaḥ na śāntiṁ prāpnuyāt kvacit ॥ 108 ॥

śrutaḥ - heard, na - not, nāśayet - destroy, kasya - whose, moham - delusion, ajñāna-sambhavam - arising from ignorance, śrutvā - hearing, api - even, etat - this, yasya - whose, mohaḥ - delusion, na - not, śāntim - peace, prāpnuyāt - may attain, kvacit - anywhere
Heard, if it does not destroy whose delusion arising from ignorance. Even after hearing this, whose delusion exists, he may not attain peace anywhere.
स शैलपुरुषो लोके केन ज्ञानं पुनर्भवेत्‌ ।
सकृदेव श्रुतं ह्येतद्विज्ञानं जनयेद्‌ दृढम्‌ ॥ १०९ ॥
sa śaila-puruṣo loke kena jñānaṁ punar bhavet ।
sakṛt eva śrutaṁ hi etad vijñānaṁ janayet dṛḍham ॥ 109 ॥

saḥ - that, śaila-puruṣaḥ - mountain-like man, loke - in the world, kena - by what, jñānam - knowledge, punar - again, bhavet - may be, sakṛt - once, eva - indeed, śrutam - heard, hi - indeed, etat - this, vijñānam - knowledge, janayet - may become, dṛḍham - firm
That mountain-like man in the world, by this knowledge, how can he be born again? Once heard indeed, this knowledge may become firm.
द्विधा त्रिधा वा मन्दस्य ज्ञातं न जनयेत्‌ कथम्‌ ।
एतत्‌ पापौघशमनं श्रुतं विज्ञानदं मतम्‌ ॥ ११० ॥
dvidhā tridhā vā mandasya jñātaṁ na janayet katham ।
etat pāpa-ogha-śamanam śrutam vijñāna-dam matam ॥ 110 ॥

dvidhā - in two ways, tridhā - in three ways, vā - or, mandasya - of the dull, jñātam - known, na - not, janayet - may generate, katham - how, etat - this, pāpa-ogha-śamanam - destroyer of the flood of sins, śrutam - heard, vijñāna-dam - giver of knowledge, matam - considered
In two or three ways, for the dull, knowledge may not be generated. This destroyer of the flood of sins, heard, is considered the giver of knowledge.
लिखितं दृष्टिदोषघ्नं पूजितं चित्तशोधनम्‌ ।
मूढतानाशनं चैतत्‌ सर्वदा परिशीलितम्‌ ॥ १११ ॥
likhitam dṛṣṭi-doṣa-ghnam pūjitam citta-śodhanam ।
mūḍhatā-nāśanam ca etat sarvadā pariśīlitam ॥ 111 ॥

likhitam - written, dṛṣṭi-doṣa-ghnam - destroyer of fault perception, pūjitam - revered, citta-śodhanam - purifier of mind, mūḍhatā-nāśanam - destroyer of delusion, ca - and, etat - this, sarvadā - always, pariśīlitam - practiced
Written words, these are destroyer of fault perception, revered, purifier of the mind, destroyer of delusion, this should always be practiced.
सर्वात्मभूतं यद्रूपं विचार्यावगतं स्फुटम्‌ ।
मुक्तिः स्यादन्यथा बन्धः सा भवेत्‌ त्रिपुरैव ह्रीम्‌ ॥ ११२ ॥
sarvātma-bhūtaṁ yad-rūpaṁ vicāryā avagataṁ sphuṭam ।
muktiḥ syāt anyathā bandhaḥ sā bhavet tripura eva hrīm ॥ 112 ॥

sarva-ātma-bhūtam - all-soul-prevading, yad-rūpam - whose form, vicāryā - by consideration, avagatam - understood, sphuṭam - clearly, muktiḥ - liberation, syāt - may be, anyathā - otherwise, bandhaḥ - bondage, sā - she, bhavet - may be, tripurā - Tripura, eva - indeed, hrīm - hrim (mantra)
Whose form is all-soul-prevading, clearly understood by consideration, liberation is attained. Otherwise, it may be bondage. She indeed is Tripura, hrim.

colophon.dev: इति श्रीमदितिहासोत्तमे त्रिपुरारहस्ये द्वादशसाहस्यां संहितायां ज्ञानखण्डे द्वाविंशोऽध्यायः ।
colophon.en: Thus ends the twenty-second chapter named "The Compilation of Adventures" in the esteemed Tripura Rahasya.
